title: The best pad for hand waxing I've used.
text:
This is a very durable pad and it features a closed cell foam that won't absorb very much wax. This is a big plus because there is very little product waste and when it's finally time to wash the pad, there's much less wax to remove saving time and water. It fits very nicely in the traditional size wax can.

The best way to use this pad is pat or press the wax rather than wipe wax onto the pad. This allows one to put down an extremely thin layer of wax. This avoids overloading the pad and buffing is a breeze. Using this method one standard 16x16 MF towel is enough for my truck.

title: Finish Kare 425 get the job done.
text:
I have been using this product for a couple of weeks and the results have been excellent. While most sprays will give a good result with painted metal surfaces, a plastic tonneau cover is another issue. It builds up a lot of static quickly and it makes getting rid of dust very difficult. Finish Kare 425 has done a much better job than other sprays have. To get the best results use a good microfiber towel and a spray bottle that produces a very fine mist. I didn't like the 31oz spray bottle that Finish Kare supplies so I used one of my own.

I haven't given this product 5 stars because I haven't been using it that long but if my experience with the product continues to be good, I'll update the review and upgrade the rating.

title: What more could you ask for?
text:
I have just started using Finish Kare products, specifically I started with Finish Kare's synthetic paste wax even though it is actually a finishing sealant. (Finish Kare 1000P Hi-Temp Paste Wax [[ASIN:B002NZL6M6 15oz Finish Kare 1000P Hi Temp]] They sell 1000p for boats but it works wonderfully on cars as well. This is a dynamite product because it is both easy to apply and buff off plus because it's for boats which see a much more difficult environment than most cars, one can expect a much longer period of protection than typical car waxes give. If you're looking for one wax to protect your ride, you really can't go wrong with the 1000P. It also produces a beautiful shine though some might claim that it doesn't have the depth and wet look that many carnauba waxes give.

To see if I could get the depth of shine and wet look, I was eager to purchase some of Finish Kare's 2685 Pink Paste Wax. It's made from #1 Brazilian carnauba plus some reinforcing resins to give the wax more durability, especially it's resistance to burn-off from heat. In what has to be one of the sweetest deals I've seen in a long time, you can get three cans of the 2685 for the price of one. If you apply this wax properly, you'll be fixed practically for life.

I applied one coat to my Ranger this afternoon and it couldn't have been easier. I did the entire truck including wheels and tonneau cover in about an hour. I applied this wax during a very humid day (like we have anything else in GA at this time of year) and it went on smoothly and it hazed in about 5 minutes. On other waxes, I've had a hard time getting them off if they sat too long but the 2685 buffed right off with a cotton towel. Normally, I have to use microfiber to remove sealants and waxes and on many days, static becomes a problem but not so with cotton. It's just my opinion but with a cotton towel, you don't remove any of the newly applied product. Another possible advantage is that this wax (like 1000p) doesn't stain exterior vinyl. In my experience all I had to do was use a soft bristle brush to remove the dry residue. NOTE: I keep my vinyl in pretty good condition and you may have a different experience if your vinyl has weathered so test and test again.

Note that neither 1000p nor 2685 have any cleaning properties. If your paint has corrosion, stains or other problems, you'll need a cleaner wax or a polish to fix the paint. Finish Kare make some products that will help you here: Finish Kare 215 One Step Cleaner & Surface Sealant ([[ASIN:B002NQXLP0 Finish Kare Cleaner Surface Sealant]] but once your paint is good you can add a couple of coats of 1000P to keep the paint protected.

Since neither 1000p nor 2685 have any cleaners in them, they can be layered. I had three coats of 1000p on my ride before I added the 2685 today. Tomorrow, I'll add another coat.

Finish Kare, like to many other companies is very spare with information about how to use their products in the most effective way and the stores that sell Finish Kare products just mouth the basic superficial marketing hype without going into the nitty gritty. So after perusing the forum where these product have been discussed, figure about 24 hours for each layer to cure before another layer can be applied. If you don't leave enough time between coats, you risk taking off the first coat with the second one. The current thinking is that it takes about 3 days for 1000p to cure completely and I'd guess a similar time for 2685.

I would have given this product 5 stars except durability is a critical feature of a wax and I haven't had time to test the durability of either 1000p or 2685 yet. I'll update when I know more.

title: It's OK, but missing important features
text:
I liked the wide bands that hold the mask on because they're more comfortable than elastic. Also, the idea to make the band loop around your neck to hold the mask when it's not on your face is great. There are three things I fault this mask for.

First, there's no wire over the bridge of the nose to hold the mask tight against the nose and face in order to stop your exhale from fogging up your glasses and to stop the mask from pushing up into your eyes.

Second, there's a place to insert a PM2.5 filter, but the cavity is so large, the filter can drift around in that area. There's nothing to hold the filter in place in front of your nose and mouth except friction.

Third, since the air can come in around the filter, it does: this makes the filter useless anyway. The mask needs a pocket for the filter, and air should not be able to go through the mask anywhere except through the filter.

Without the filter, this mask would catch some of the droplets you exhale, but it will not protect you from the COVID-19 virus, according to Medical News Today.

If you don't care about the filter, this mask is better than a bandanna because it has that loop to hold the mask when it's off your face.

I bought this for small 3 to 10 gallon aquariums knowing it was too long. It's simple however to cut the tubes it comes with (it's a lot for small aquarium needs) and make it very compact. I flush mount the pickup bell (shortest possible. How it's pictured here) for the 3 gallon, and have custom cut the remaining tubes to fit my other tanks, set so the pump is just under. Simply swap out the small tubes. Use xtra care and always wet the rubber sealing ring. I hard wired a power supply to it, but the correct plug in power supply is in others comments on here. It cleans well and so nice not having a time limit from draining water. Always lots of debri in the sock. I love it for water changes too. Much easier than starting a reg siphon. I've never used batteries, but the power seems pretty good. Primes and starts as soon as the pump gets below the water. I've lifted it back up with just the shortened bell under and it kept pumping. Not tons of power but I have shrimp and other tiny critters so it's actually just right for avoiding them. Gets the poo. Bottom line.

Update: The youtube hacks for more suction work. Eliminate the slots on the pickup bell. Normal siphon vacs don't have them so why does this need them? It doesn't. Some use tape. I wouldn't. Tape + water can fail, and the ashesive could be poisonous. Best way is to shorten it. Cut it off at the base of the slots and sand smooth. An added bonus is it's even more compact. title: You pay for what you get.
text:
Overall this tablet is pretty nice, and for the price you'll be pretty happy.
Let's start with the bad stuff:
- The back of the tablet is entirely metal which helps dissipate heat, but also makes the tablet quite slippery.
- It only has 2GB of RAM, which when running more than 2 or 3 apps at a time can really make it slow down.
- It only has 32GB of Internal Storage, which is hardly anything for a Windows Tablet. You WILL need a MicroSD Card.
- The speaker quality is very bad; the speakers are very quiet and don't have a very clear sound.
- (Something you should and probably do expect) The cameras are an afterthought. They'll get the job done for taking notes or Video Chatting, but don't expect much more.
- Wi-Fi is only 2.4Ghz, No 5Ghz band. It is also not that strong and doesn't go very far from the router.
Pros:
- A very nice looking 1080p IPS Display.
- Very responsive Touch Screen, no input delay.
- Overall smooth performance when surfing the web or using the tablet in general.
- Good battery life when running 50% brightness.

Overall Thoughts:
For $80, you're getting a very nice looking tablet with a beautiful display. The thing I use the tablet for most and for what I recommend it most for is media streaming(YouTube, Netflix, Hulu, etc..). The Intel Atom z8350 is not the fastest processor, but it is capable of playing YouTube at 1080p 60FPS with no lag as long as you use Microsoft Edge(because it's hardware-accelerated). If you are into Video Editing, Gaming, or any kind of task that requires the tablet to render something, don't waste your money, this tablet is not made for that and you will be disappointed.
Overall a good buy.

Always, ALWAYS, seek medical attention first...

title: Fabulous!
text: I bought Blue Magic's Petroleum Jelly on a whim, and I'm glad I did. I've heard of this product from them before but found it for the first time at my local hair supply store in NYC. I used it as a sealant for my 4C natural hair after washing, deep conditioning, and then moisturizing it with hot water and aloe vera gel. What's most interesting about this product is that it's not really a grease, but it's too shiny, too oily, and too smooth to pass off as petroleum jelly, it's also too white in color to even pass off as something like Vaseline, which is an off-yellow color. I was skeptical at first as to how my hair would respond to this because this product is very in-between, and also odd, in many ways. It's scented but its scent is barely there, like there's a slight floral smell, but it's really hard to detect it, sometimes you smell it, sometimes you don't. Using this as a grease on your hair makes you feel like you're using what I'd call a "clean" grease, where it doesn't have the heavy coloring, fragrance, and oils like their original blue or green Blue Magic, it's just petroleum jelly infused with aloe vera, safflower oil, and vitamin E. To my surprise, this product worked just like those greases. It's not too heavy, but it's not too light either. It held my two-strand twists together very beautifully. It actually gave my style a slicker and smoother look to it, and my hair was so moisturized. This is advertised as being like an all-purpose petroleum jelly where you can also use it on your body, hands, lips, etc. but I think you're better off just using straight up Vaseline; I just don't think it quite works in the same way because, again, it's just way too shiny, oily, and greasy for that, but as a sealant on moist/wet hair? Fabulous. I wouldn't go out of my way to just buy this product, but if I go back to the shop to get my favorite products and I so happen to see it's in stock still, sure, I'll grab it!

title: Dissolves easily and quickly.
text:
This will be my fourth brand of marine collagen that I've tried. I'm looking to improve the health of my skin and hair which are very dry, and hoping to find some relief from my joint pain due to arthritis. So far with some of the powdered marine collagens that I've tried, I've experienced faster hair and nail growth but not much else.
I am still testing out this Nuton Collagen Peptide so I can't say how well it has been working just yet. I've only had it for four days now. I can say that it does not have a bad odor nor a harsh flavor. It dissolves easily and quickly into my morning tea. I don't even need to stir it!
According to the description, this is type 1 collagen from wild-caught Pacific Ocean Paddock and Red Snapper from a sustainable and traceable supply chain. I think Nuton also offers beef collagen but I do not eat cow so I've only tried marine collagen.
As of now, the reason I knock off one star is because of how small the container is. This container is 5oz and approximately 13 servings which doesn't even get you through half a month. But, I know that this brand of collagen is fairly new so I'm wondering if the company plans to offer this supplement in a larger tub in the future once they receive feedback or sales begin to increase. That's just my guess and if I end up loving this powder, I'll be begging them to make a larger tub with at least a month's worth because I drink marine collagen everyday. It often takes a while for my body to notice benefits from new supplements so hopefully I'll be able to fully assess how this new brand does by the end of 13 days. I'll be sure to update if I notice any big pros or cons.
I also want to say that I was in contact with the company before and after I made my purchase and they are really nice to do business with. They are prompt and courteous and they let me know that they are a small, family business and that this is a new brand of collagen. It makes me happy to help out a new, small business.

title: Failed on first use
text:
We just received the Ivation Quad-Point massager to replace our Zillion ZMA-13 massager that broke in under a year. We were so disappointed in Zillion we decided to try another company. From what we understood, we were buying a new product (the Ivation), but it arrived in an old, beat-up box, so perhaps we got a damaged unit. However, we tried it out immediately once UPS dropped it off. We placed it in a wing-back reading chair, turned it on, leaned back (as if sitting into the chair) on it, and it came to a dead stop. We thought we had a faulty power connection, so reconnected the plugs, repeated, and again the machine came to a dead stop, turning itself off. Next we lay the machine flat on the floor, turned it on, and with outstretched palms pressed down on the massage face. With less pressure than our bodies could impose on it, the massager came to a complete stop and turned itself off. Each time before it shut itself down we could hear the motor grounding to a halt.

We're giving the product two stars instead of one because we just don't know if the pressure sensitivity is an engineered safety feature (a poor one, if so), or if we got a defective unit. In any case, the massager is going back and we're done looking at portable massage units.

title: An Outstanding Insect Guard and Sunscreen Product
text:
Avon SKIN-SO-SOFT Bug Guard is a must have during the summer. Before I bought this, I did quite a bit of research to find the best mosquito/fly/nat repellent, since I'd be in Haiti for three days, I wanted something to protect me, yet something that was safe. Avon Skin-So-Soft was my choice for three reasons: 1) I also needed sunscreen and because this has sun protection in it as well as repellent, it took care of two things in one; 2) Of all the natural repellents on Amazon, this product had the most reviews as well as costumer satisfaction; and 3) I did not want DEET or really any other chemical that would have a pungent oder or harmful substance in it.
During my entire stay in Haiti, I did not receive one mosquito or even an insect bite, while wearing this Avon product. It is very much like sun screen, however, it is not sticky, and it has a nice smell to it, almost like a citrus smell but not too strong. The sun screen protection also proved to work out really well, and although I did tan a little, I didn't get burned. Overall, this product is absolutely amazing, and I would definitely buy it again when I run out!

title: My initial impression
text:
As a mother of two, I want to make sure to keep my body the best it can be, which includes the muscles 'down there' (haha!)
I had been considering kegel balls for some time, but was trying to wait for a good deal, so when I saw these, I decided to take the plunge.

Stupidly, I did not think about the fact that I use the Nuva-ring birth control. When I asked my doctor, she said that it can be removed for X amount of time, but I'm not super comfortable with that, so I am going to wait until my '3 months off' to use these. I thought that I could still give my initial impressions though!

Firstly, these come in a cute little bag that not only will keep them cleaner between uses, but will also make it way more discreet to store. I appriciate that things like that were considered and included.

I noticed no odor from these, which was something I was concerned about. I would still suggest washing them before using them, with either a specific sex-toy spray, or a very mild detergent and rinsing thoroughly.

The one 'con' that I see at this point (Which I will update once I've used them) is that there are no directions included in the packaging. Of all products that are considered self-explanatory, this is one that I would still read the directions on! Also, considering that my birth control may be considered a contraindication for these balls, I'd of really appreciated a manual with that information in it. I feel like this could be considered a medical aid, so the lack of information caused me to dock a star.

title: Purple Cushion Is Pure Gold
text:
This has far exceeded my expectations. While the price for a cushion seems high, I have been more than pleased with how this has eased my lower back pain -- in fact, I just ordered a second one. I've used it on three different chairs in the house, and in both front seats in my Toyota. It's a substantial, nicely heavy cushion with Purple's unique design: built to ease back pain while making a more than comfortable cushion device.

There was a slight icky smell on arrival - but I left it in the garage for 24 hours, then put it in its sleeve and it's been fine ever since. The sleeve has two handles for easy carrying, and one side has a non-slip finish so it doesn't slide around. It also slips off for washing.

My wife and I have shopped for a new mattress, and we've considered the Purple, so we learned a bit about them, which is why I bought this cushion. They're not for everybody, we were told -- but for me it's been flawless. It's far from memory foam, but has its own sophisticated 'semi-rubbery' feel that provides great support.

I heartily recommend, and see no problems.

I am not too sure how I feel about these. This is great in theory and I love that this pack provides six sets (12 pegs) in the various sizes. I found that this size pack would be most applicable to most of my shoes, so I would not pick the larger sizes unless your heels are thicker overall.

Tip: As soon as the original tip breaks, do not keep walking on them until you replace them! I found that some of my shoes that had broken off continued to flatten the nail and now I cannot get the original nail out in order to replace the tip. My fault!

After I pulled out the original peg on a shoe, I found that when I inserted a new tip, it would not stay in. It slips and falls out so incredibly easily. I measured the nail of the new and old, and they are the same thickness/size so it is not that the nail is smaller. I am not sure why they won't stay in. I might try to super glue the edge of the plastic to the bottom of the heel while avoiding the nail so that I can replace again if needed.

Pulling the nails out are also incredibly difficult. Even for those that are not flattened out, they are stuck in there so well that it takes an awful lot of effort and time to get the old nails out.

Great concept, but not sure if it is worth the headaches to do it this way instead of just taking them to a cobbler.

You would think that if they really wanted people to buy their products over here in the US they would be able to get someone to translate directions for use. I had to ask other customers what they did and how to use the products. As best I can tell you this is what you do:

#2, apply black face mask to your face, avoid eyes and mouth etc. I tried to get an even coat but still ended up having some areas that were thicker than the rest. These are by far and away THE BEST compression socks we own, and between hubby and me, that's alot of compression socks! I actually came back to Amazon today to get at least one more pair. This particular ad says "not currently available", but there is a new ad (the link above), exact same sock, from the same seller, but the price is now $42 a pair, a $22 INCREASE & MORE THAN DOUBLE THE $19.95 I paid a few months ago! For me, $20 was plenty high, thus the reason I didn't dare buy more than one pair, being unfamiliar with them. Turns out they are wonderful socks, but, nonetheless, I can't pay $42! I know I'm in for LOTS of time spent looking for a satisfactory substitute, staring at ad pictures, trying to tell how wide the upper band is compared to these. That is the number one reason I love these socks. The upper band is wider than I have ever seen on any compression sock and SO COMFORTABLE. I have very stocky legs (hubby says I'm built for plowing.....yea, he's a real funny guy!), and my other compression socks can get very uncomfortable, even painful, by day's end, binding at the top when the edema is bad. The compression on these (20-30) is greater than the 15-20 I typically wear, but they are SO comfortable overall, the higher level isn't even noticeable, never painful. At the same time, that added compression definitely helps with the edema on those particularly problematic days. The fabric is considerably heavier/thicker than my other socks but doesn't make my feet uncomfortably warm or sweaty.
I think it's terrible when sellers decide to price a medical item so high that it becomes out of reach for many. Of what benefit can a health-related item be if a large portion of the population who need it cannot afford it? My 3 star rating is based on that issue - a price that more than doubled, from $20 to $42, in the span of a few months. THE SOCK ITSELF IS A 5 STAR ITEM if you can pay the price.

title: Must have, but you must know how to use it.
text:
My wife bought me this for my contact lenses and I was curious and a bit worried based on the reviews I've read. I waited to write a review until I used it in several scenarios. The package I received had 2 large bottles and 1 "TSA friendly" 3oz bottle plus 2 of the lens holders. I wear Air Optic Multifocals, a "open a new pack once a month" disposable.

From the picture you will notice that the lid is red and there is a red/orange warning label around it. This is to make sure it stands out to you because you cannot use this like you use normal lens solution. This is a special formula and special holding container that you put your lenses in overnight and it cleans them with a "bubbling" action, which really does bubble away. The hitch is that you have to have the lenses in for a recommended period of time so the solution neutralizes. You cannot do a quick soak or put them in for a couple of hours...once they are in you are committed.

So first things first, this stuff is absolutely fantastic at doing exactly what it advertises. If you leave it in overnight (they say 6 and a half hours, but it really needs more like 8), your lenses feel as fresh at the end of the month as they do at the start. This was really key to me because for the first 2 1/2 years of wearing lenses, the end of the month for new lenses was something I really looked forward to because my lenses bothered my eyes more and more over the course of the month. This fixed that - they feel as good on day 30 as day 1. I won't live without this product again.

However, you need to know that it does not replace regular lens solution. You need regular solution for the quick soak, the popping out a lens to clean it, etc. This is a better cleaner, not a new solution. Though my eye doctor's office didn't really do a good job of covering this in the "consult" I paid for, my personal take is you need a product like Clear Care for routine cleaning, you need regular lens solution for short soaks and those times where you take lenses in and out, and you need a good rewetting solution for those days where lenses are being annoying. This is part of a total solution.

If you don't pay attention to which bottle you grab, or you ignore the warnings, you will pay a hefty price. I accidentally grabbed this when cleaning a lens real quick one day instead of my regular solution, which was totally my fault - I was inattentive. The bottle is covered in more warnings than you can ever imagine and those warnings don't understate the consequences...but I rinsed my lens and popped it back in my eye. The pain was easily in the top 10 pain moments of my life, and the irritation and soreness lasted for a couple of days. They are dead serious, you have to let them soak.

The other thing to know is I don't recommend for travel unless you can give long soak times. I travel on business a lot, and frequently end up taking people out to dinner/entertaining, followed by getting up early. Despite the bottle recommendations on soak time, I've let it run an hour past and still experienced anywhere from mild to heavy burning. The heavy burning was after 7.5 hours of soak on my most recent business trip, and it was about 50% of the pain felt in the "rinsed and put back in" incident. There seems to be some variables in the soak time, and at home I tend to soak at least 8 hours without problems. For future business trips, I'll just take the regular holders and regular solution.

In summary, I consider this stuff a must-have, but it has a specific purpose and role. It is not a jack of all trades, it has a job. That job extends the life of your lenses and completely improves their comfort, but understand the limitations and whatever you do, do NOT underestimate the warnings.

title: Takes a bit of patience to use, but it does work pretty well
text:
First thing you need to do is actually look through the manual. The device is not as user friendly as it could be, so you kind of need to sit down and learn a little bit about it.

If you just insert the batteries and start randomly trying to take readings, you'll get a lot of connection errors. If you're going to use the "press it against your skin" method, it works a lot better if you wash your hands (which the manual tells you to do) and whatever part of your body you press the large electrode against. Dry/oily skin prevents it from sensing the electrical pulses from your heart. Washing moistens the area and will give you good readings, (but you don't want dripping wet hands.)

The screen resolution is adequate for a casual view of the waveforms, but to REALLY examine them you need to upload the readings to your computer (usb cable provided. Download the Viewer program from their website - don't bother using the disc). Connection to my PC was straightforward. Plug in the USB, turn the Device on, and open the Viewer. Click on "Import Device Data." (It will tell you to create an ID. See the manual.)

Using the ECG Viewer program you can click on any part of the waveform and a larger view appears in a lower window. I did end up using Microsoft's built in Magnifier to make the whole Viewer program larger, which helped a great deal. You can see and count every block on the strip which is useful for a more thorough analysis, as readings are time-based in milli-seconds. It's not just the shape of the waveforms, but also the space between them that's useful for diagnostic info. Watch some youtube ECG videos made for nurses/students, if you want to learn more. It's not that hard to learn how to interpret a readout. You'll catch on after watching 3 or 4 videos. I find it quite fascinating myself, the ingenuity of being able to tell how well your heart is functioning just by reading electrical impulses.

Like most companies, they give you the usual disclaimers about not relying solely on this or diagnosing yourself, to keep the lawyers happy. But this little gadget can indeed tell you enough about your heart (after you learn how to read it) to make an informed decision to see a cardiologist, but of course you should have regular physical exams anyway when you're middle aged. It's not some devious plot to make you give doctors your money. Things really do go wrong with our bodies after a number of decades go by, especially if you smoke, drink, don't exercise, and don't eat right.

It's also not a bad idea to pick up a digital blood pressure device. They are fairly cheap and easy to use. Omron seems to be the top brand, but there are plenty of choices. Read reviews.

It takes only a few minutes a day to collect readings, which you can store on your smartphone and show your doctor. The readings you take at home can actually be more accurate than at the doctor's office, as you're at a more rested state at home, as opposed to fighting traffic on the drive over there, or rushing to be on time.

Sadly, this ECG monitor doesn't have Smartphone storage, but if nothing else, you can email readings to your doctor, or email them to yourself and pull them up on an ipad to show him.

title: Good Value and Solid Doses. Novelty factor (2 flavors) is a bonus
text:
Performix has been around the supplement game for a while. Most recognize them via their "Terra" bead technology.

Anyways, I was in the market for a pre workout that would fit my criteria: (300mg caffeine), pump focused (no need to add in bulk ingredients) and of course a good value. My criteria is pretty basic. In this day and age there are so many to choose from. What ended up swaying me over was the novelty factor of 2 flavors.

Ingredients/Profile wise ION v2x is pretty standard. I do like the different types of caffeine which gives instant/prolonged release energy coupled with teacrine as an added bonus. for pumps, there's a solid dose of citrulline malate and agmatine. Again, the blend is nothing special, but when you factor in the cost and being able to switch up the flavors it makes this an attractive option. Flavors/taste is really up to the individual but they both are tasty to me. Definitely favors the candy taste vs the fruit taste for the respective flavor. As others have noted, it does come in a metal tin and each flavor is in a ziplock baggie. It is slightly cumbersome to put it back in the container, so I just leave the two baggies out.

Overall, if you want a preworkout with tried and true ingredients, you should consider this. the dual flavors (or 3 if you mix) allows you to change things up .

title: Do you want to add a JAW workout into your routine?
text:
I bought 3 boxes of Venture Bars. I've been a big fan of Controlled Labs for a while now and figured they couldn't go wrong with these bars.

Flavors - Flavors are pretty subjective but 2/3 flavors were pretty spot on (Almond Coconut/Chocolate PB Fudge). The cookie dough one tasted more chocolate chip than cookie dough. With that being said I enjoyed all 3 flavors.

Macros - These bars aren't a MRP but also aren't so small that they don't satisfy you either. These macros fit the usual protein bars made with IMO. So in short, these bars don't have too many filler ingredients.

Texture - This is where things get weird. I ordered my bars around the time these came out so they should have be pretty fresh. These bars are hard!!! All 3 flavors. They even bent my permanent retainer when I chewed on them the first time. It would take me almost 20 minutes to eat an entire bar...these bars are almost impossible to chew thoroughly. As far as the fillings (nuts/chocolate chips) - I'd say they were pretty liberal in putting those in which is a plus, but back to the texture.... they recommend microwaving it (w/o wrapper) for 10 seconds.

I did that and boy did it make a big difference but then it turned from a 5x5 chewing session into a 5x100 chewing session. It was like taffy. It was soft but became chewier. lol.

So in short, if you want to take your time eating bars, then try these out. I'll find some way to eat the remaining 30+ bars I have left

title: Hot Topic: Green Tea Weight Loss
text:
Green Tea Weight Loss
---------------------
The possibility that green tea helps with weight loss has been a recent hot topic in the media.

What is the potential role of tea in helping maintain healthy weight? Unsweetened, tea, both black and green has with or without milk no sodium, no sugar, little or no fat and virtually no kilojoules, yet tea is a satisfying, aromatic beverage. This makes tea an ideal choice for a weight control plan that is part of a healthy lifestyle, especially when substituting for other sugar sweetened beverages.
Another factor to potentially maintain a healthy weight is that regular tea contains caffeine which has been shown to increase energy expenditure (number of kilojoules burned)(17,18). In a study, published in the Journal of Nutrition, consumption of 3-4 servings of oolong tea was shown to increase energy expenditure and the rate of fat breakdown. In addition, subjects drinking tea spent energy at a 3% faster rate and burnt about 70 more kilojoules a day than those consuming water (48).

Some emerging research on energy expenditure conducted with tea and tea extracts has suggested that increases in metabolism and rate of fat breakdown may not be solely due to caffeine in the tea. One study measuring the effect of green tea extract on energy expenditure in people showed that drinking either caffeinated water or tea extract significantly increased the number of kilojoules burned, but in addition the rate of fat breakdown was significantly higher for participants drinking tea extract than those drinking the caffeinated water(49).
In a second study researchers looked at group of flavonoids in tea and its effect on weight loss and body fat. They found significant weight loss and a significant reduction in total body fat in the people drinking tea flavonoids (equal to 3-4 cups of tea per day) when compared to participants drinking the placebo (66 ).
While this is active area of research; the preliminary evidence suggests the tea drinking can increase energy expenditure and fat burning. However, there are no conclusive studies that tea drinking has beneficial effects on weight loss. Still, tea is a satisfying, low kilojoule beverage that can be substituted for sweetened beverages and is a delicious alternative to plain water in a healthy weight management plan.

Green tea may benefit some more than others
--------------------------------------------
At the recent International Research Conference on Food, Nutrition and Cancer sponsored by the American Institute for Cancer Research (AICR), scientists presented new evidence about phytochemicals in green tea that may help prevent normal cells from developing into cancer and spreading.
Yet people may wonder if drinking green tea is worthwhile, because the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) refused to allow a health claim for green tea on labels this summer.
Although more evidence is needed to justify a strong statement about green tea's ability to lower the risk of cancer, it is not a bad idea to include this beverage in a healthful, mostly plant-based diet.
Black tea is the most frequently consumed tea in the U.S., but green tea contains far higher levels of the phytochemical EGCG. Both oolong and black teas, including the common orange pekoe, lose some of their EGCG as they are processed. However, green tea leaves are steamed or baked before they can oxidize, so their EGCG levels remain high.
Since it is a powerful antioxidant, EGCG may help prevent both heart disease and cancer. It helps to stabilize highly reactive molecules known as free radicals that can damage blood vessels and increase the risk of heart disease, or alter the DNA in our genes, promoting cancerous changes. In addition, EGCG may protect against cancer development by increasing the self-destruction of cancer cells and by affecting enzymes and the signals between cells, slowing the growth and multiplication of cancer cells.
Related content
* Scientists find how green tea fights cancer
* Green tea doesn't lower cancer risk, says FDA
But while the evidence of EGCG's ability to deter cancer is quite strong in laboratory studies, population studies show much less consistent benefits. The inconsistent population evidence is one of the primary reasons that the FDA recently refused to approve a health claim on the labels of products with green tea that would link its consumption with lower cancer risk.
Benefits some more than others
In the FDA's view, the effectiveness of foods in laboratory studies is merely background material. Consistent evidence among populations is key to supporting health claims. However, researchers point out that the laboratory studies, which are overwhelmingly positive about the health effects of EGCG, are necessary to explain the results of population studies. Without them, we would not know what EGCG is or what it can do.
Furthermore, inconsistent results from population studies do not mean that there is no benefit to drinking green tea. Human studies show that the antioxidant capacity of the blood does increase about an hour after drinking green tea.
Other studies show that markers of DNA damage decrease after drinking even black tea or decaf green tea, both of which contain less EGCG than regular green tea.
The differences in health impact that are seen among green tea drinkers in population studies may mean that green tea benefits some people more than others. Genetic variations, varying exposures to risk-producing substances like tobacco, or different diets could all help explain the differences seen in these studies.
One study, for example, suggests that tea and soy may produce contrary benefits. Eating one of these foods may decrease the potential benefits from the other one.
Drinking massive amounts of green tea will never be able to save us from the ill effects of overeating a poorly balanced diet and living a sedentary lifestyle.
Eating a mostly plant-based diet, maintaining a healthy weight, keeping physically active and avoiding tobacco are the most effective steps we can take to lower our cancer risk. However, for those of us who would like to do a little more to reduce the risk of cancer, replacing three or four cups of coffee or soda per day with green tea is a reasonable step that may bring a variety of health benefits.

title: All About Pu Er Tea
text:
All About Pu Er Tea

The most famous tea from Yunnan is Puer. Yunnan also produces green tea, jasmine tea, and black tea. Yunnan province is in south west China and the origin of tea can be traced there. There are a number of trees in Yunnan that can be dated back more that 2000 years. The rain forests of Yunnan are rich in diversity, a majority of the flowers that we grow in the US can be traced back to Yunnan.

Yunnan began to process tea in the Three Kingdoms period (220-360). Allegedly, at this time Zhu Ge Liang from Sichuan, a clever tactician, encouraged the Yunnan people to cultivate tea to improve their lives. Still, Yunnan people call Zhu Ge Liang their tea god. He is still prayed to in the south of Yunnan where he conquered more that 2000 years ago. This is the area of Xichuanbanna and the six famous mountains. At the heart of Yunnan's south west is the city of Puer, the base of the province's ancient tea market, and from where "puer tea" derives its name. (The city Simao in 2007 changed its name to Puer, and should not be confused with the ancient city). From Puer city, tea was distributed to Tibet, and South East Asia on "tea horse trading roads." The rough terrain of Yunnan demanded efficiently packed tea, so compressed cakes of tea were wrapped and tied into stacks of seven and enclosed into a bamboo shell. For this reason, certain puer cakes are commonly labled "Qi Zi Bing" or literally Seven Piece Cake. Carrying tea though the humid rain forest over the long, hard trading routes may have encouraged natural fermentation.

oldcake.jpgPeople enjoy and collecting puer tea for three main reasons including enjoyment of the tea, overall health benefits and the investment potential. It became popular outside of the traditional markets of Tibet and Mongolia, where for many years it was exchanged for horses, when it became sought after in Hong Kong for its health benefits, and for its mysterious quality of slow, natural fermentation, that causes it to improve with age. During the Cultural Revolution a lot of the old cakes were destroyed increasing the rareness of aged puer. In 1973, a process was invented to create fermented puer in about 60 days.

Now the popularity of puer has spread from Hong Kong and Guangzhou, to Taiwan, Beijing, Shanghai and South East Asia. The popularity of puer has even started to spread to the US and Europe. All puer tea starts out the same. The basic ingredient is called mao cha. Mao cha is harvested and allowed to dry in the sun. Yunnan is the only tea growing province in China that has a lot of high altitude sunshine and blue skies. One of the side affects of all this sunshine is some very large leaf tea plants.

All tea originated in Yunnan, but you might be surprised to know that the tea plants are called Camellia Sinesis Assamica. The reason is that9 picking big leaf tea tree.jpg when the British found the variety of tea growing in India they named it Assamica and believed that it was wild, but it had actually been planted along the old Silk Road that ran from Yunnan and Burma into Assam. Even though the origin issue has been cleared up, the ancient tea trees in Yunnan have kept the inaccurate name.

A lot of puer produced is said to be made from wild tea trees, but this is not the case. Wild tea trees are known to make people pretty sick sometimes, and what is called "wild" by puer makers is in fact old tea trees that have been cultivated, and are usually over a hundred years old. The age of the tree can be determined by measuring the trunk. Trees have very often been cut back drastically to increase yield, and more bushes are being planted at break neck speed. Planting tea is helpful to the the environment in Yunnan that has suffered from the burning of forests to plant sugar cane. Sugar, though a profitable short term crop, quickly depletes the mountain soil and erosion can quickly wear away the topsoil from whole mountain sides.
Harvesting and Making Puer Tea

The quality of the mao cha the most important factor in making puer. The ideal mao cha is two leaves and one bud. Farmers typically bring their mao cha to towns and villages where it is purchased by local buyers and sorted and then purchased by puer producers. Although relatively large 18 mao cha ready to sell to producer.jpgareas may be favorite places for certain producers to buy their mao cha, the cultivation is done by small farmers. Since puer has become more popular, many farmers are cutting their old trees to create bushes which have a better yield, so the number of old trees is decreasing every year. Most commercial puer is a blend of mao cha from different areas and there are some producers that will reveal the areas in Yunnan where the mao cha originated. These kinds of details enhance the value of the tea over time, and we try to supply this information whenever we can. The tea grows in high mountain areas and the mao cha is brought now to the villages in the valley once a week to be sold. The process hasn't changed for centuries.

There are two general types of puer, shu (black, cooked) and sheng (green, raw). The raw or sheng (green) puer is made from mao cha this is lightly steamed and pressed into cakes. It is the sheng puer that demonstrates the miracle of puer. It slowly changes over time through a natural fermentation process. The microbes present in the mao cha that are not destroyed during sun drying work their magic and over 8 to 10 years raw puer tea is transformed to cooked, green to black. It is the sheng that is most valuable over time and starts to reach is full maturity after around thirty years. Puer teas are elemental and mysteriously dark, fermented teas which are robust, earthy, rich and grounding. Puer is often a favorite tea of the truly dedicated tea drinker. This aged tea usually begins with a variety of leaf from exceptionally broad-leaved tea trees. This tea either left loose or compressed into cakes is then permitted to retain barely enough moisture content that the tea continues to ferment slowly over time. For this reason, puer is best stored open so that oxygen can continue to refine the tea.

Shu puer, or cooked/black puer is more complicated. In 1973, because of a shortage of old cakes caused by the destruction of all things old during the Cultural Revolution, a process was developed for uniformly speeding up the aging process. This process has been well guarded in the past but is relatively simple, but not without skill. Large piles of maocha are wetted and then covered with a large canvass cloth, creating a kind of composting effect. The water drains of as does some of the natural moisture through the weight of the pile. Inside of the pile heat is produced. The pile becomes a rich environment for the grow of microbes that thrive in the tea leaves of the Yunnan rain forest. The skill comes into play when the pile needs to be turned. The turning needs to come at the right time, and there are clumps of growth that occur at the bottom of the heap and must be broken up and evenly distributed throughout the pile. When to turn and the attention paid to the details of turning are critical, so that the pile adds a pleasant fragrance to the tea. A poor level of skill turns the heap into an unkempt barnyard smell, flatteringly called `earthy' in the West, and `old house smell' in China. After the the tea is cooked it is sorted for grade, and then lightly steeped and pressed into cakes, bricks, etc.

Puer is separated into ten grades determined by leaf size, with the largest being tenth grade. In understanding about grades, it is wrong to 13 old big leaf tree.jpgassume that the 1st grade is the best grade for puer. There is only an incidental correlation between the grade of the puer and the quality of an individual cake. For example, some of the most sought after tea is made from maocha that is larger than tenth grade tea. It is always a question of taste. Of course if a lot of expensive buds are used in a cake, it will drive the price up, even if it is not considered a good candidate for aging. So don't be strictly guided by the grade, think also about the uniformity and tightness of compression and the overall flavor achieved by the cake's mao cha blend.

It used to be that the old government factories blended by just throwing maocha from the surrounding mountains all in together in a kind of random way. Now there are some companies that blend for a mixture of qualities that are associated with different growing areas for creating a well rounded cake, taking sweet maocha, and blending with fragrant maocha for example. There are also rumors about starters for cooking, like bread starters, and maocha that comes from some mythical place. Puer companies try to keep a tight lid on these trade secrets, and all of this secrecy has given puer a mythical reputation. However puer is magical in and of itself, without all of the hyperbole. It is a simple tea made by ancient peoples from ancient trees and bushes that has remarkable qualities.

Puer is famed for its health benefits and is consumed daily in the South of China, and in Southeast Asia by older Asians that are looking to maintain their health. The French are currently doing research on the affects of drinking puer with maintaining a healthy level of cholesterol. It is said to be helpful for digestive and metabolism problems.
Judging a Puer Cake's Quality

39 tea cake indentation.jpgWhen shopping for puer here are some very general guidelines. Look the cake over to see if the leaves are uniform through the cake, and pay attention to the compression of the cake; it should not be too tight, or too loose. title: Weight Loss Benefits of Green Tea!
text:
Weight Loss Benefits of Green Tea
=================================

If you drink green tea you can-
* Lower Cholesterol
* Increase Thermogenesis (the body's rate of burning calories)
* Enhance fat oxidation

Burns Fat Naturally
Green tea contains high concentrations of catechin polyphenols. These compounds work with other chemicals to intensify levels of fat oxidation and thermogenesis, where heat is created in the body by burning fuels such as fat. Drinking Japanese green tea regularly will increase your metabolism and help burn fat safely and naturally.

Lowers cholesterol and increases energy expenditure
Green tea also causes carbohydrates to be released slowly, preventing sharp increases in blood-insulin levels. This promotes the burning of fat.
The thermogenic effect was originally attributed to its caffeine content. However, green tea stimulates brown fat thermogenesis far greater than a comparable amount of pure caffeine. It appears that the catechin-polyphenols, in particular epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), and caffeine that naturally occur in green tea work synergistically to stimulate thermogenesis and augment and prolong sympathetic stimulation of thermogenesis. It has been shown to increase 24-hour energy expenditure and fat oxidation (caffeine only increases metabolism during the time you take it).

Weight is gained as excess sugars and fats are stored in the body as fat cells. Green tea catechins can help prevent obesity by inhibiting the movement of glucose in fat cells. Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) has been found to be especially effective. There is now good evidence that green tea catechins are related to reductions in body fat.
EGCG is a powerful antioxidant with positive qualities but a balanced diet and exercise, lots of it, are of paramount importance to any weight reduction program.

Green Tea and Weight Loss
=========================
by: Kathryn O'Neill

There's recently been a LOT in the weight loss news concerning green tea.
Green tea's weight loss effects have been causing more and more people to start sipping the ancient Chinese or Japanese brew.

But just how does green tea help you lose weight? And does it really work or is it all just hype? This article gives you the real facts about drinking green tea to lose weight.
Advantages of Drinking Green Tea for Weight Loss:

1) Green tea revs up your metabolism

A study reported on in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, found that green tea extract resulted in a significant increase in energy expenditure (a metabolism `boost').
The researchers also concluded that that over a 24-hour period, green tea extract increases the metabolic rate by 4%. These effects are probably due to the high concentrations of catechin polyphenols found in green tea. These work to help intensify levels of fat oxidation and thermogenesis (the rate at which your body burns calories).

2) Green tea inhibits fat absorption and helps glucose regulation
Experts tell us that the catechins in green tea help to inhibit the movement of glucose into fat cells. Green tea may also act as al glucose regulator. It helps to slow the rise in blood sugar after a meal. This prevents high insulin spikes (lots of insulin promotes fat storage) and the subsequent fat storage.

3) Green tea may help reduce appetite
Scientists at the University of Chicago found that green tea caused rats to lose up to 21 percent of their body weight. Rats injected with a green tea extract lost their appetites and consumed up to 60 percent less food after seven days of daily injections. This may have something to do with the blood sugar regulating effects of green tea.

4) Green tea can help you save calories on your morning brew.
We are a nation hooked on our java. Be it the regular double-cream, double-sugar standard or that mocha, dappa, frappucinno, the calories we ingest just to get our morning caffeine is wreaking havoc on our waistlines.

If you want to save mega-calories in the morning but still get your caffeine fix, try substituting green tea for coffee. Or have a green tea in the afternoon instead of that 700 calorie mocha-chillate dream. You'll definitely notice the difference in your waistline after a few weeks.

So there are 4 ways that green tea can help you with weight loss. But how much do you actually have to drink to get these amazing metabolism boosting effects?

Experts vary but the general consensus seems to be that 3 - 5 cups of green tea per day is optimal. Doing this can help you burn an extra 70 calories per day which amounts to 7 pounds per year. Pretty good for not exercising or cutting calories, right?
However, 3 - 5 cups can be a lot for some people, so you might also want to consider green tea extract, green tea pills or a green tea patch.

Disadvantages of Drinking Green Tea For Weight Loss:
#1) Green tea is not a magic bullet
While some people will tell you that green tea is the be-all-end-all for weight loss success, I think the keyword here is balance. You're not going to eat 5000 calories a day, drink a cup of green tea and make it all go away - it just isn't going to happen. A healthy diet and increased exercise will go a long way in helping you lose weight and keep it off.
#2) Be cautious of the caffeine if you have health problems
For some people that have heart troubles, high blood pressure or stimulant sensitivities, the caffeine in green tea may not be the best idea. If you're worried about the caffeine from green tea, try taking green tea extract. Most green tea extract is made from decaffeinated green tea so you can still get the weight loss benefits without the caffeine.
If you think the caffeine may be a problem, make sure to consult your doctor before starting green tea for weight loss. Also make sure to consult your doctor before starting green tea if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

*** Bottom Line ***: Green tea helps you with weight loss by boosting your metabolic rate, regulating your blood sugar, suppressing your appetite and giving you something else besides that high calorie, high sugar coffee beverage to drink in the morning. While it's not the magic bullet, it can definitely give you a boost in weight loss and in your overall health!

Green tea may benefit some more than others
-------------------------------------------
At the recent International Research Conference on Food, Nutrition and Cancer sponsored by the American Institute for Cancer Research (AICR), scientists presented new evidence about phytochemicals in green tea that may help prevent normal cells from developing into cancer and spreading.
Yet people may wonder if drinking green tea is worthwhile, because the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) refused to allow a health claim for green tea on labels this summer.
Although more evidence is needed to justify a strong statement about green tea's ability to lower the risk of cancer, it is not a bad idea to include this beverage in a healthful, mostly plant-based diet.
Black tea is the most frequently consumed tea in the U.S., but green tea contains far higher levels of the phytochemical EGCG. Both oolong and black teas, including the common orange pekoe, lose some of their EGCG as they are processed. However, green tea leaves are steamed or baked before they can oxidize, so their EGCG levels remain high.
Since it is a powerful antioxidant, EGCG may help prevent both heart disease and cancer. It helps to stabilize highly reactive molecules known as free radicals that can damage blood vessels and increase the risk of heart disease, or alter the DNA in our genes, promoting cancerous changes. In addition, EGCG may protect against cancer development by increasing the self-destruction of cancer cells and by affecting enzymes and the signals between cells, slowing the growth and multiplication of cancer cells.
Related content
* Scientists find how green tea fights cancer
* Green tea doesn't lower cancer risk, says FDA
But while the evidence of EGCG's ability to deter cancer is quite strong in laboratory studies, population studies show much less consistent benefits. The inconsistent population evidence is one of the primary reasons that the FDA recently refused to approve a health claim on the labels of products with green tea that would link its consumption with lower cancer risk.
Benefits some more than others
In the FDA's view, the effectiveness of foods in laboratory studies is merely background material. Consistent evidence among populations is key to supporting health claims. However, researchers point out that the laboratory studies, which are overwhelmingly positive about the health effects of EGCG, are necessary to explain the results of population studies. Without them, we would not know what EGCG is or what it can do.
Furthermore, inconsistent results from population studies do not mean that there is no benefit to drinking green tea. Human studies show that the antioxidant capacity of the blood does increase about an hour after drinking green tea.
Other studies show that markers of DNA damage decrease after drinking even black tea or decaf green tea, both of which contain less EGCG than regular green tea.
The differences in health impact that are seen among green tea drinkers in population studies may mean that green tea benefits some people more than others. Genetic variations, varying exposures to risk-producing substances like tobacco, or different diets could all help explain the differences seen in these studies.
One study, for example, suggests that tea and soy may produce contrary benefits. Eating one of these foods may decrease the potential benefits from the other one.
Drinking massive amounts of green tea will never be able to save us from the ill effects of overeating a poorly balanced diet and living a sedentary lifestyle.
Eating a mostly plant-based diet, maintaining a healthy weight, keeping physically active and avoiding tobacco are the most effective steps we can take to lower our cancer risk. However, for those of us who would like to do a little more to reduce the risk of cancer, replacing three or four cups of coffee or soda per day with green tea is a reasonable step that may bring a variety of health benefits.

April 7, 2008 -- An antioxidant in green tea may be a powerful weapon against breast cancer.
A new study shows the green tea antioxidant EGCG (epigallocatechin-3-gallate) significantly slowed breast cancer growth in female mice.

Previous studies have suggested that this antioxidant may protect against breast cancer and other cancers, but this research has been limited, and the mechanism behind these effects isn't clear.
Researchers say the results suggest that green tea's anticancer effects may be largely because of its high content of EGCG, which helps the body's cells from becoming damaged and aging prematurely.
Behind Green Tea's Anticancer Effect
In the study, presented this week at the Experimental Biology 2008 conference, researchers examined the effects of the green tea antioxidant on several indicators of breast cancer growth in laboratory mice.
One group of the female mice was fed a solution of the antioxidant in water for five weeks while the other received regular drinking water. During the second week of the study, researchers injected both groups with breast cancer cells.
At the end of the study, researchers measured tumor size, weight, and density as well as VEGF protein levels associated with tumor growth.
The results showed that treatment with the green tea antioxidant decreased tumor size by 66% and weight by 68% compared with the control group. Mice fed the antioxidant also had significantly lower density of small blood vessels within tumors and VEGF protein levels.
Researcher Jian-Wei Gu, of the University of Mississippi Medical Center in Jackson, says the green tea antioxidant may work against breast cancer by suppressing blood vessel growth in breast tumors as well as slowing the proliferation and migration of breast cancer cells.

Mechanism for green tea's anti-cancer action revealed
17-May-2005
Related topics: Research, Phytochemicals, plant extracts, Cancer risk reduction
Green tea appears to protect against cancer by affecting a 'promiscuous' protein that pharmaceutical experts are already targeting in their work on anti-cancer drugs, according to new research.
The study, by PhD student Christine Palermo at the University of Rochester Medical Center, reveals a potential new mechanism to explain the tea, and particularly its active compounds' action against cancer.
While many studies suggest that green tea protects people against some forms of cancer, such as breast and liver cancer, exactly how it does so has been difficult to pinpoint.
"It's important to find out the source of green tea's protective effects," said toxicologist Thomas A Gasiewicz, whose work on the harmful effects of dioxin led the Rochester group to explore the protective effects of green tea.
"What is exciting here is that a completely new mechanism has been found that very well could be responsible for its protective effects, and that could help us find a compound that is much more potent."
Palermo, Gasiewicz, and current undergraduate Claire Westlake discovered that a chaperone protein known as HSP90 is involved in conferring green tea's protective effects. Other researchers have shown that many cancer cells have an increase in the level of HSP90 compared to healthy cells, and that when HSP90 is blocked, levels of proteins that make cancer cells grow drop.
Drug makers are currently working on ways to block HSP90, which is known as a promiscuous chaperone protein because it binds to many different cells and receptors in the body. It turns out that those researchers are trying to duplicate what green tea does naturally. Gasiewicz says green tea might modulate HSP-90 in a way that researchers have not seen before.
Gasiewicz and his group have shown how dioxin and other substances like cigarette smoke manipulate a major cancer-causing molecule, the aryl hydrocarbon (AH) receptor, which frequently plays a role in turning on genes that are oftentimes harmful.
Two years ago the team discovered that AH activity is inhibited by a chemical found in white and green teas, epigallocatechingallate or EGCG, now being produced and marketed as a supplement by DSM.
"We initially hypothesized that EGCG would work in the same way as other AH antagonists, by binding directly to it. We were completely surprised that this isn't the case," said Gasiewicz, whose work was funded by the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences and the American Institute for Cancer Research.
Instead, the team found that EGCG binds to HSP90, a protein that helps other proteins stay stable, serving the same role as a tail on a kite. When the two bind, HSP90 no longer turns on the AH receptor, stopping the cascade of events that would lead to the activation of several harmful genes.
Another potential mechanism for green tea's action was outlined recently by a team at the University of Wisconsin and Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland, Ohio. The found that green tea polyphenols reduce levels of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) in prostate tumour cells in a mouse model for human prostate cancer. Increased levels of IGF-1 are associated with higher risk of several cancers, such as prostate, breast, lung and colon.
Meanwhile, researchers at Kyushu University in Japan reported last year that EGCG appears to inhibit tumour cell growth by binding to a receptor on cells called the 67-kDa laminin receptor. A variety of tumours produce abnormally high levels of 67 LR, and the receptor is thought to be involved in the spread of cancers through the body.

Is Green Tea Really an Anti-Cancer Miracle?
Talk to your doctor about green tea.

By Gale Maleskey, MS, RD
Registered Dietitian
About the Author
July 23, 2009

Change Text Size A | A | A
If you've had cancer, or a precancerous condition, it's time to talk with your doctor about using green tea extract. More and more research is showing that green tea extract can slow the progression of cancer. It doesn't work for all cancers, but it seems to have a significant effect on some types. Its effect may even depend on genetic markers and hormone sensitivities associated with your type of cancer.

Some of the cancers that green tea can face down include prostate, esophageal, bladder, cervical, pancreatic, ovarian, lymphoma and leukemia. Green tea is also active against human papilloma virus (HPV) a sexually transmitted virus associated with cervical and anal cancer and warts.

(Since green tea can also apparently neutralize some chemotherapy treatments, such as Velcade, used for multiple myeloma and mantel cell lymphoma, it's important that you consult with your doctor if you are undergoing treatment.)

The most recent study, by researchers at Louisiana State University, found that men scheduled for a radical prostatectomy due to cancer who took a green tea extract had a significant reduction in the markers predictive of prostate cancer progression. In some men, the drop was more than 30%! The reductions were in biochemicals that either stimulate cancer growth or indicate continued cancer growth. The men took a total of 1.3 grams of tea polyphenols, equivalent to about 12 cups of green tea. (McLarty, J, et al. Cancer Prev Res. 2009 June 19.) [E Pub ahead of print.]

Even though this was a small study, other evidence suggests that green tea can take on cancer. One study found that men with high-grade prostate intraepithelial neoplasia -- cellular changes that often lead to cancer -- who took green tea catechins 200 mg three times daily for a year, had a reduced risk of progression to prostate cancer. (Bettuzzi S, et al. Cancer Res .2006;66:1234-40.)

Polyphenols (catechins, such as EGCG) in tea appear to protect cells from DNA damage that can promote cancer. Animal research suggests that the EGCG in green tea may prevent new blood vessel growth in tumors, inhibit tumor cell proliferation, and induce death in cancer cells in at least two different ways.

The Anti-Aging Bottom Line: Green tea extract can be an important part of an anti-cancer arsenal. For general prevention, we recommend about 450 mg a day of a standardized green tea extract. Unlike brewed tea and non-standardized green tea extracts, our formula provides consistently high amounts of green tea's most active constituents. If you're being treated for cancer, it's best to talk with your doctor about dosage.

title: Huangshan Mao Feng Tea, one of China's ten most famous green teas
text:
Huangshan Mao Feng Tea, one of China's ten most famous green teas

Huangshan Mao Feng Tea, one of China's ten most famous green teas, was first produced in 1875 during The Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) in the area around Huangshan Mountain. The area features ideal growing climate for the tea. The tea trees are grown at altitudes of over 700 meters, and the fertile soil, cool air, and adequate rain make the tea leaves large and strong which gives Huangshan Mao Feng tea its long lasting aroma. What distinguishes Huangshan Mao Feng Tea from other Mao Feng Teas is the color of its leaves. The tea liquor is jade green in color and has a light flowery fragrance.
Huangshan Mao Feng Tea's name derives from its appearance and its growing location. The leaves look like the tongues of birds covered with silvery floss. In Chinese, "Mao" means fluffy, and "Feng" means mountain peaks. Although it is not a scented tea, it has many properties similar to scented tea. The tea liquor has an apricot flavor, and a fragrance like magnolias. No apricot trees or magnolias grow in the area, so it is unknown how Huangshan Mao Feng gets its unique flavors. There is however wild peach trees that grow in close proximity to the tea plants, and that may be the cause. Huangshan Mao Feng Tea drinkers say that the first brewing is fragrant, the second brewing is sweet, and the third brewing is strong. The tea tastes clean and refreshing, and lasts a long time on the tongue.
The techniques and production of Huangshan Mao Feng Tea are unique. The leaves are picked in when still buds with one unfolding leaf. The leaves when processed are yellow-green and covered with silvery hair. The best Huangshan Mao Feng Tea is picked early in the year in what is called pre Qingming picking, which is in early April. After picking, the tea leaves are spread out thinly in the sunlight to allow the leaves to wither. The freshly withered leaves are then pan fried in large woks over an open fire. The pan frying prevents the tea leaves from fermenting (oxidizing). While the tea leaves are being pan fried, they are rolled, which causes the leaves to twist, and curl. The production techniques strive to preserve the natural flavor of the fresh leaves, so that that flavor may be released during brewing.
There is an ancient Chinese legend surrounding the origins of Huangshan Mao Feng Tea. It is said that young scholar and a beautiful woman who worked in a tea plantation were madly in love. One day a local landowner saw the woman and wanting her for his own, seized her and forced her to become her concubine. The woman escaped only to find that the landowner had killed the young scholar. When she found this out, she immediately went to his grave which was located high on a mountainside. She wept uncontrollably until she became the rain, and the young scholar became a tea tree. It is said this is why the area where the tea trees grows is cloudy and humid all year. The tea orchards growing on the mountain slopes near Huangshan Mountain are beautiful any time of the year, but the best time to visit it is when the girls are out among the tea trees picking the fresh buds. It is a particularly beautiful scene. Visitors to the area at this time are able to go out among the tea trees and help in the harvesting of this wonderful tea.

title: Has no taste (which is great), blends fairly smoothly, and is totally natural with no additives
text:
I was very pleased to see a high quality, grass-fed, non-GMO protein powder with no flavor. My family likes to mix our protein powder with all sorts of things (fruit, cinnamon, ground flax seeds, etc., and prefer to taste those ingredients vs. artificially flavored elements of protein powder). The protein grams/serving is pretty average (16G/3 TBLSPN).

Upon opening the package, I noticed there was no smell at all. That boded well for the powder having no taste. That was true – there was no taste at all. I blended this with half a banana, coconut milk, blueberries, and flax seeds.

It blended pretty well – there was no powder left on the sides of the nutribullet blending cup. The top of the smoothie was pretty ‘frothy’ – it happened two out of four times I used the powder. Not sure if it’s because of the powder, but can’t think of what else it could be because everything else is my standard ingredients for every single smoothie I make.

As for the texture, the powder seemed to be slightly gritty in the smoothie. It wasn’t enough to make me not want to drink it, or to not buy it again, but I’ve had powders that blend completely – to the point where you wouldn’t know they were there at all. The second time I made a smoothie with the Wild Whey, I blended it for about 30 seconds longer than I usually would, just to make sure it fully blended the powder. It didn’t seem to make a difference.

So the bottom line – 4 stars because the protein grams/serving are slightly low, and the texture was a bit more gritty than I really like.

However, it is rare to find a high quality, truly grass-fed, non-GMO protein powder. When you look at the ingredients in most protein powders on the market they are full of additives and artificial ingredients. So kudos to Wild Whey for making a totally natural product that tastes good and is good for the body.

* I received the protein powder for evaluation and review

title: big, bold cobalt bottle of lemon essential oil - great
text:
The Radha lemon essential oil is wonderful – a big bottle of very strong smelling lemon oil (not a sweet lemon, but a very ‘true’ lemon scent). I use a LOT of lemon oil for making homemade dish soap and cleaners, so the big 4 oz bottle is great. You don’t need many drops to get the effect.

Lemon essential oil cuts grease really well, and leaves a really clean scent. I stopped using commercial cleaners a few years ago and it makes a huge difference – dishes are cleaner, laundry smells better, and my skin is less itchy (recipe below for dish soap). I also use lemon oil a lot to clean my oven – nothing else seems to be able to get it looking that clean.

The radha bottles are a trademark cobalt blue, protecting the essential oils from light and UV rays which can deteriorate the liquid inside – this extends the life of the oil and keeps it more potent. Their droppers are always high quality, also.

Ingredients
• 1 ¾ cups boiling water
• 1 Tbsp borax (I've used this for the past 2 years and it lasts forever: [[ASIN:B00AZ6IH68 Mule Team Borax and Arm & Hammer Super Washing Soda Variety Pack]])
• 1 Tbsp grated soap (I use nonscented Ivory)
• 15-20 drops 100% pure essential oils

Directions
1. Heat water to boiling.
2. Combine borax and grated bar soap in a medium bowl. Pour hot water over the mixture. Whisk until the grated soap is completely melted.
3. Allow mixture to cool on the countertop for 6-8 hours, stirring occasionally. Dish soap will gel upon standing.
4. Transfer to a squirt bottle, and add essential oils (if using). Shake well to combine

* I received the radha essential oil for evaluation and review

title: Bottle of 300 Vitamin C 500mg/Rose Hips 5mg Unflavored USA Packaged Tablets
text:
I like taking about a gram (1000 mg) of Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) as a daily supplement. For me it seems to help ward off colds plus keep me healthier as I age. This is a Vitamin C 500mg small tablet that has in addition 5mg of Rose Hips with no added sugar or flavorings. The tablets are small and easy to swallow with a slightly acidic ascorbic acid taste. These are not for chewing. The label does not say where the ascorbic acid and rose hips are sourced from but does say "Blended and Packaged & Lab Tested in the USA". That gives me a secure feeling that this is a product to trust. I am willing to pay a premium for that.
I won't risk taking foreign sourced drugs generally as I have read too many horror stories of adulteration with awful stuff. The ingredients do appear to be sourced from outside the USA however. That would drop a half star but since there are no halves, I'll default to 5.

This bottle comes double sealed and the tablet size is seen in my pictures. I liked the convenience of the flip top to open cap on this bottle.

I do note that these have a recommended Serving Size of 1 a day for a 500mg dosing. That means the bottle will go almost a year at 1 a day; even with me taking 2 a day there are 150 days worth at a great value. Supplements such as this are best taken with a meal I believe as that improves absorption.

As always check with your Healthcare Provider whenever beginning a new Supplement/Nutraceutical/or OTC Drug as there are many possible drug interactions that need to be considered.

I Recommend these Carlyle Store Vitamin C 500mg | 300 Tablets | Ascorbic Acid with Rose Hips | Vegetarian, Non-GMO, and Gluten Free Supplement | High Potency Formula | by Carlyle. These will be a great daily Vitamin C Supplement for me and are a great value.

title: Good quality shaving brush
text:
I own three shaving brushes, none of them truly top-quality. Of the three, I like this one the most.

The handle is wood. Although the marketing tells us the wood is "Tasmanian timber," and it may well be, it appears nondescript to me, light brown without any distinguishing features. It has a thin metal ring surrounding the hole where the bristles enter the handle. It's not a stunning handle but it's certainly nice enough. The varnish on the bottom of mine looked like it had touched something before it had dried completely, so it's rough, which is unfortunate but I can live with it.

What I like is that the boar bristles are higher quality than those in my other two brushes. The tips are softer, and there are more bristles bound into the handle. As a result, it does a better job of making lather, and it feels softer on my face. I haven't noticed any bristles coming loose while I'm lathering my face, which is a problem with one of my other brushes.

title: Quell is an overpriced tens unit with horrible overpriced electrode pads that will cost you more than a cable bill each month.
text:
Way too pricey. Quell claims these last 2 weeks a piece. I'm not seeing it. I wipe my leg with alcohol, and place on my leg without touching the pads with my fingers. The problem is that because of the curve of the leg, the pads have a tough time staying stuck, but instead naturally they start to curl at the edges. The strap doesn't really do much to remedy this problem. The pads still don't remain tight to the leg... which causes a burning sensation because the current isn't distributed properly.

Quell's remedy to this is to not fix their crappy electrodes, but to instead try to up-sell you on their more expensive sports electrodes. What they should be doing is offering a refund and fixing their product to work simply like they claim in their advertising. It's not like I'm the only one complaining about this. It's a very common complaint.

Honestly, I think this company is ripping people off. I don't believe for a second their "86% of users experience pain relief" claims. Just look through the comments on their Facebook pages / ads or here on Amazon and you'll see this number doesn't comply with actual reviews. I wore the device for 4 weeks and all I did was waste time, burn my legs and spent over $300. Since I purchased the Quell on eBay, I can't return it. The reason I purchased it on eBay was to save money. I figured with an "86%" success rate, the odds were in my favor lol.

What really irritates me is why Quell charges $250 for an overpriced tens unit that fits in a strap. They claim it's special technology but that's utter BS. It's a wearable tens unit for your leg. I can see them charging maybe $80 for this, but how they justify charging 10x the cost of my very good $30 tens unit that's actually more powerful, I have no idea.

And why they must charge $30 for 2 crappy electrode pads that barely last a week, when the pads for my tens unit only cost a small fraction of this price. They are the same exact thing basically, except the Quell pads are placed on a piece of paper with 2 snaps attached. How that justifies a 3x cost increase is beyond me. You'd think that a larger venture like Quell with national ad campaigns would be getting great deals with their bulk purchasing power... compared to a small company selling tens units strictly on Amazon.
