title: Fast, Effective (seriously) Do your heels a favor !!!!
text:
I had purchased the battery run version of this and used it from time to time. But when i used it I would use it after using and callous scrubber and a scraper, then a smaller scraper and yes, really, sandpaper !The battery version of this was mainly to smooth the skin after all other efforts were done. This was all time consuming and annoying to say the least. The battery version was "ok" for smoothing and frankly if you had bad heels etc. it would work but I would work for a long time, usually giving up and doing more later that day and it did not really do much. So, thanks to the wonderful folks who answered my questions I decided to give this a try. it came today. Turned it on (about a 6 ft. cord) and proceed to work on my heels. Wow, I fell in love with this thing. The battery version would slow down and even stop if pressure was put on it. And yes, I know you don't want to put too much pressure because you don't want to take skin off, but heck, you need to put "some" pressure if you have callus' or bad heels. For those that want just touching up then the battery version will work. For us with serious problems ... well.. we need this thing!! I stopped after a bit because I did not want to take off too much until I got the hang of this Emjoi but will go back this evening to do more. And I think one more go round will pretty much take care of my heel problem. Not sure how often I will have to do it. That will come with time. But this is so much more easier than anything else I have used (sandpaper included) and loads faster. This is honestly well worth the money. Oh yes, I think it is actually quieter than the battery version too. I might keep the battery version to take on trips though in case touch ups needed But to be honest this Power Emjoi just flat out does the job for me.

OH, also, don't always go in the same direction. Changing direction will ensure you are getting a really all around smooth surface. And, don't hold the pedi in the same place too long of course, Besides getting an uneven filing down area you might wind up taking off too much skin in one place. So move it around !

Update: 6/11 Because of the condition of my heels I found I had to use the Emjoi Power about 2 times a day for the last few days. I determined rather than try and undue everything in one go (that would have taken quite some time) By doing some every day I made sure I wasn't taking off too much skin etc. Bottom line my heels were bad enough that doing it in just one time would not have really worked well. So, do some everyday and in a few days you'll be happy. Woke up this morning and rubbed my heels (don't laugh) because previously the jaggedness of my heels would scratch my other leg, get caught in my nightgown etc. Yep not nice. This morning.. my heels are "smoooooooth" ! Just don't rush it, little bit a few times a day until your heels get where you want them. From there as I said I'll see how often I have to touch them up.

title: Best brush for applying beard oils (wet or dry)
text:
I'm new to the world that is the almighty and powerful BEARD! Mine isn't yet a full beard, but a very full goatee; the rest is still trying to catch up. I learned of CanYouHandlebar from the Punisher Life website - they have a Punisher Life version of their beard oil. I instead went to the CYHB full website to check out their full line, and bought several products to try. In a word...WOW! I never knew anything about beard care, but now that I do, I'll never be caught without it.

I bought a few things: Wisdom and Honor in the stainless steel 1oz flasks; one ounce of Temperance in the amber bottle; this horse hair beard brush; and Wisdom in "dry" oil (beard butter). Every product is absolutely amazing. No greasy residues, no pungent odors, and no allergy issues (though make sure you check to make sure you're not allergic to the ingredients - all natural doesn't mean no allergies). In fact, the scents remind me of an old world rustic outdoor setting (Initiative), or - with both Wisdom and Honor - of sitting by a fireplace in an aged leather chair smoking a tobacco pipe while reading theology surrounded by dusty tomes and jamming to Mozart. Class and sophistication come to mind without being pretentious.

In short, these are impeccable beard care products that are all natural, soothing, and smell great. Your spouse will thank you for it. But get good combs, too. I have Kent 20T and 87T hand-made varieties and believe me a quality comb makes a huge difference.

These oils wiped out beard dandruff, dry and itchy skin, and this brush helps to stimulate blood flow to the follicles to promote a healthy and lusterful beard. Do your beard a favor...get CanYouHandlebar products. You won't be let down.

title: Well worth the money
text:
I have had one of these for several years now. I like it so much I gave one to a friend. It is on 24/7. I never turn it off. Sometimes lint and dust in the air gets sucked up into the intake part. You can tell when this happens because you will not feel any air come out when you hold your hand next to it. When this happens, I unplug it and use toothpicks to reach inside the narrow vents to unclog them but I suppose a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment would work just as well.
You can tell it is working because there is a burning smell, like you get when you are ironing clothes. That is the smell of the little buggers in the air getting fried. You can buy replacement bulbs for $15 from Target when yours burns out.
I am using this in a big bathroom that even with an exhaust fan used to get mildewy every few months from 5 people taking hot showers and steaming up the place. Since I have been using it, there has been no mildew on the ceiling or walls at all.
I plan to buy a couple to put away for when this one finally dies in case the company stops making it.

title: Sweetener Comparison Chart  by R. McClintick
text:
For your information I've been using sweeteners for over 30 years. The Stevita is my preferred method of sweetening coffee, tea, kool aid, and food. This product has been used in my home for the last 3 years, and I love it. The comparison chart shares some of my discoveries and feelings about the products I've used.

Stevita-Pkts. for 1.5 cups of cold liquid- .75-1; pkts. for 1.5 cups hot liquid- 2; after taste rating from low=0.1 to high=5- 0.1, and finally problems- The ease of use is a little harder with humid weather, but rice in the storage container eliminates the problem. There are zero carb. grams, less than any of the other sweeteners listed here.

Sweet'n Low (pink generic packs also)-Pkts. for 1.5 cups of cold liquid- .75-1; pkts. for 1.5 cups hot liquid- 2; after taste rating from low=0.1 to high=5- 4.3, and finally problems- the strong aftertaste is problematic for many, and with baking always remember to add fluid to compensate for sugar moisture lost (and this may also be the case with all the other sweeteners).

Equal(generic's also)-Pkts. for 1.5 cups of cold liquid- 1.5-2; pkts. for 1.5 cups hot liquid- 4; after taste rating from low=0.1 to high=5-3.8, and finally problems- hot food and drinks require more sweetener packets and they may also increase the aftertaste.

Truvia-Pkts. for 1.5 cups of cold liquid- 1.5-2; pkts. for 1.5 cups hot liquid- 4; after taste rating from low=0.1 to high=5-1.8, and finally problems- the carb content with each packet of sweetener is about 3 grams, one teaspoon of sugar has about 4 grams of carb.

Splenda(generic's also)-Pkts. for 1.5 cups of cold liquid- 2-3 ; pkts. for 1.5 cups hot liquid- 6; after taste rating from low=0.1 to high=5- 0.8, and finally problems- total carb is less than one gram per packet, but for hot drinks I use 6 packets of it.

Please remember these are my personal takes on the sweeteners, there is more info online about chemical composition and health concerns with use.

So because of the differences in cost, flavor, and ease of use my choice is Stevita.

title: Good Product that Could Be a Great One
text:
I got this as a replacement for a post-workout drink I currently use that I'm having trouble finding.

The Bad:
This is about 1/3 more expensive at just over $1 a serving, but I figured I'd give it a shot, even though I feel that the labeling is inadequate.
As a low-carb person, I always check the carb counts on things I purchase. This doesn't list carbs at all, but after reading the ingredients, I assumed it to be either 0, or at least very low, but with the inclusion of tart cherry extract, I would have liked to have that listed, just for my own peace of mind. Tart cherry juice can have a boatload of carbs, so I hope to find out how much this includes at some point.
The flavor (fruit punch) is almost non-existent. The sweetness is at a perfect level (my other product is super-sweet (in a bad way), the level on this is good. After working out, the last thing I want is something that is sickeningly sweet.
When putting this in cold water, there is residue on the bottom of the bottle that doesn't seem to want to dissolve, so you constantly have to shake the bottle to get it stirred up.

The Good:

I like that this includes vitamin C, which is always a benefit for low-carb folks, since citrus fruits are off limits.
I also like that it includes some electrolytes, although the levels are really low (6%, 4%, and 2% daily allowance of Magnesium, Sodium, and Potassium, respectively. You lose these in your sweat during exercise, so I would have liked more.
The BCAA (branched chain amino acids) level is on par with other brands, including my usual one at 7g.
I mentioned tart cherry as a bad thing above, but it's actually quite healthful. There's some data that shows muscle recovery is faster when this is in your diet, it includes a lot of antioxidants and vitamins and minerals as well.

All-in-all, I'll continue to use this, at least until I find out the carb level. If it's high, I'll have to discontinue using it, or maybe cut the serving size down to reduce the level. For those who don't worry about carbs in their diet, I think this is a great product, worthy of 5 stars, but for the lack of carb information, I had to drop a star.

title: My new favorite brand!
text:
Anyone who knows anything about ttc(trying to conceive) or is ttc, you will know how quickly tests add up. Finding cheaper options is always there, but you are worried about the accuracy. So when given the chance to try these I of course took it. Upon arrival I was very pleased with them. I loved that the packaging was simple yet effective. I of course took them out right away to "test" them. For starters I love that it came with a box for storage when not in use. Each test is labeled very simple, yet noticeable. They are marked very differently from each other and should cause no concern about a mix up. Each test is wrapped individually, which you want. The test strips are pretty thin, which you can expect with any dip stick style test. This particular set comes with 50 LH strips(ovulation) and 20 HCG strips (pregnancy). For anyone who may have not used these, I will explain a little. You simply collect a small amount of urine in a cup and dip these into it. The strips are have a "max" line mark to which you do not dip past. Very easy, and even easier is that there's an illustration showing this on each test strip package should you forget.

Getting into a little more details of each, I'll start with the LH(ovulation) strips. These show you when your LH surges, which is usually 12-48 hours before ovulation. Average is 36 hours. Giving you a better idea of when to bd(baby dance). On a normal cycle you ovulate 14 days after the first day of your last cycle, however most people are not average. That's where these tests come in handy. Depending on the length of your cycle will determine when you should begin testing with LH strips. Sadly this set doesn't come with a testing chart, so I will post them for help.
Cycle 21 days.......start testing on cycle day 5
Cycle 22 days.......start testing on cycle day 6
Cycle 23 days......start testing on cycle day 7
So on and so forth. If your cycles 30 days you test on day 14. If your cycle is irregular, start testing based on the shorted cycle you had. These are not like pregnancy test and should not be taken first thing in the morning. Most recommending testing between the hours of 10am-8pm. Although most get the best results after 12pm. For these to read positive the line must be as dark or darker than the control line. Most women will always see a line, so please be sure you check the darkness to insure a correct positive. After getting a positive you can quit testing as you know your LH has surged and ovulation is pending.

Now onto the HCG(pregnancy) ones. These are much more simple to use and really have no line watching of time frames. These particular test ring in at 25miu, which is the lower normal for most store bought test. They are actually a bit more sensitive than some more expensive tests. These should be used with first morning urine as it tends to be more concentrated, however feel free to test anytime should you want. As most know a line is a line regardless of the darkness. If you get a line on these you know there's a baby on the way.

I have tried both tests and have had excellent results. I am always worried about evaps and these have yet to have one. Even after sitting and drying for some time the strip remained completely white. While both of these are recommended to not read past 10 minutes, I have noticed that the LH strips do take a bit to finish running. I usually read it at 10 minutes exactly for the true reading. I have tried many different brands tests and these definitely rank in the top. The best part is the price is so low for such a generous amount. If taken correctly these could last a few months. Unless of course your like myself and take way too many. I love these tests and I'm so glad I was able to try them out. I will be recommending them to my friends and family. I will also be reordering these should I need more in the future although I'm hoping to get my positive HCG with these soon. Happy testing, baby making, bright positives, and good vibes ladies.

title: Another weapon in your arsenal against fish parasites.
text:
Fenbendazole is a good weapon for an aquarists to have in his or her arsenal. This medication will treat a variety of internal parasites from your fish.

As a previous reviewer has stated, thorough treatment is required when fighting some of the more persistent internal parasites, like roundworms. Start the treatment as soon as you suspect internal parasites. Your chances, the fish chances, are much better if you start the treatment while they are still eating. If you wait until after they stop eating, then you are limited to medicating the water in the tank. The best way is to also mix fenbendazole with the fish food and feed it to the fish in conjunction with treating the water.

The fish will be more likely to accept the medication if you mix it with frozen food. You can thaw frozen shrimp and soak it in fenbendazole. For added efficiency, you can use a binder like Seachem focus to help draw the medication into the food. You can also try mixing with flakes, but the flakes will get soggy and messy.

The main value of this medication to me is its use as a preventative. I feed this to newly-acquired fish. Basically, I make the assumption that the new fish are infected and treat accordingly. This medication will not harm the fish and it will clear away internal parasites that may be hitching a ride on your new fish. In this manner, in the event that the fish are exposed to a stressor later on, at least they will not succumb to intestinal worms. Even if the fish do get stressed, if there are no low-level camallanus worm infection in any of the fish in the tank, they will not get infected.

Some hobbyists use canine de-wormer on their fish. However, this is not an expensive product and you will be better off simply using the fenbendazole that is already packaged for use with tropical fish. This will save you from having to buy canine tablets and having to ground it into a fine powder.

title: Good, tight holding sock clips
text:
I have used several types of sock clips for my work (thin cotton) socks. These are good clips and I would give a 5-star rating except they are difficult to get my socks clipped into the device. It takes me longer than with other clips. I have had no problems with sock becoming loose in the wash or dryer, and this is with quite thin socks.

DETAILS:

My favorite clip is [[ASIN:B003E6DK4U SockPro Sock Holders Red]]. You can get them in various colors and they are simple to put your socks into them and I have had very minimal loose socks after many (~15) washes with each clip. You just pull the ends through the socks and it is almost a one hand operation once you get used to it. I have not liked [[ASIN:B00I001GKU 10 Pcs Mix Color Socks Stockings Hose Clip Holder Organizer Rack Laundry Supplies]] as well. They grip the socks much looser than the ones I recommend and I am loosing socks 15-20% of the time.

I have also used [[ASIN:B000QOHCFQ 24 SockLocks, Colors May Vary]] with good success. They are a harder plastic where the ones I recommend are softer and more flexible. I thought that the SockLocks would not hold up well to the hot wash and may become brittle. They seem quite flimsy; however they have worked well through at least 10 wash/dry cycles and given the price they may be a better purchase than the SockPro item.

These SockStar clips are even tighter holding than the other clips I have used. They are thicker plastic and seem well made. I like the color on them and think they will hold up well. I have only used a few clips through 2 wash/dry cycles, so I do not know the longer term reliability, but I expect that it will be fine. If you have had problems with other sock clips loosing grip in the wash, then I would suggest these. They take me a bit longer to get my socks clipped is the only negative I have. I may be a little stingy in taking off a star...

title: It works, but could be better! Here's how to make it last longer!!
text:
These work very well. So, why only 4 stars? Well, as some have pointed out, they become very difficult to blow through after a fairly short time in use. Some have suggested placing some cotton balls in the blow end, removing them when the unit begins to clog up. That’s a good idea, as the way this actually works is 2 fold.

It has both a paper fiber air filter, similar in appearance to the automotive air cleaner filters of yesteryear, and after the smoke passes through that, it is then passed through activated charcoal. From my experiments with making my own filters, I can attest to the fact that it’s the paper filter that actually removes the visible smoke (resin), as filters I’ve made that used activated charcoal only, even when constructed to route the smoke efficiently & evenly through all of the charcoal, don’t remove visible smoke, at all.

So, it would seem that the charcoal is there only to remove smell and possibly any drug elements, such as THC, or nicotine. So, by placing the cotton balls in the blow end, they begin to absorb most of the resin, which is what is making the smoke visible, preventing most of it from getting to the internal paper filter. But, even this method will eventually clog the paper filter element within the unit.

There is a solution to this. I take a bottle of 99.9% Iso Alcohol and place it in a deep kettle of water - water as hot as I can get it from my tap, to heat the alcohol up. WARNING - NEVER USE FLAME OR THE STOVE TO HEAT ALCOHOL, UNLESS YOU LIKE SERIOUS BURNS!

After the alcohol has had time to become heated, it is then poured slowly, a bit at a time, into the SmokeBuddy. As it will take some time to break through the resin, it won’t take much to fill the unit to the top. At first, it will just sit there. But in a minute, it will begin to flow out the bottom, and it will have a ton of resin in it.

I do this over a large bowl. I pour about 8 ounces through the unit. I also use a paper towel to dry off any spilled alcohol at the rim, so I can put my mouth on it and blow the alcohol through. But, it’s important not to do this too soon, as the heated alcohol, being allowed to flow slowly, will absorb more resin then blowing it through. The blowing helps clear out the last of the alcohol, and I only do it after each pour stops running out the bottom, to clear it out for the next pour. You can’t pour in too much at a time due to how slowly it flows through. Try not to overflow it.

Once this has been done, leave the unit all day to dry out the alcohol. Blowing through it from time to time will help. If you desperately need to use it before it dries completely, you can, but I try to avoid it. When it’s finished, it will flow almost as well as it did when new, and so far, I’ve not yet been able to use one up to the point that I can’t re-clean it. I’d have given it 5 stars, if the maker had cared enough to make it out of metal, and so that you can unscrew the top to change the paper filter & even replace the charcoal, when needed.

Instead, they’ve elected to have us contribute more to pollution, as people will be throwing these plastic bodied units into the trash when they no longer work. As I said, they should have made them out of metal. They would cost more, but they would last forever, with only the filter elements being repurchased and replaced as needed. Far better for the environment & for the customer. There are just WAY too many disposable items being made and sold these days.

text: I became convinced of the healing benefits of silver solution after I applied it to a nasty cut that wasn't looking great. Everything cleared right up. Now I like to keep a supply on hand and, except for mosquito bites, for which I use lavender essential oil, it's done a consistently excellent job at keeping infections under control. It's very effective. Taking it internally in small doses regularly will do you do harm, however, larger doses should be avoided. Silver can turn the skin gray if overused, and that side effect isn't reversible. I do take it internally in small doses for my general health - about five sprays under my tongue once or twice a day and I feel great about it. It can be difficult to find and I think this is a good price. I'm glad to have found it.

Since the main ingredient is identical, I compared this to two products; name brand Benadryl and my usual generic brand. I'm impressed that it comes in at about half the price of Benadryl brand, so if you prefer name brand, over the counter medications, you should definitely consider this. However, I found it was two and a half times the cost of the generic brand I usually use. Sadly, I'll finish this box, but I won't be buying it again. title: You have to add your own stickers (provided) and they don't hold a lot of pills.
text:
I take a lot of supplements, and am always on the hunt for pill holders and will hold them all. Sadly this don't work for me. Each container is really quite small. It would work if you're just using it for your meds and a couple of vitamins, but it's not for me.

I did have some other issues with it:

There are two sets, presumably one is for night and the other for day, but they’re identical. There’s no way to tell them apart without trying to see through the container or removing one to check. It's very easy to get them confused, especially in the dim light of morning or after a long day. That's not a good thing.

Having two separate containers means that when you pack them there's a good chance they'll get separated. I don’t want to muck about with that sort of thing when I travel. I want things as streamlined as possible.

It's a bit fiddly - you have to completely remove the day you want to use and then open the top, but I suppose this does stop them from opening accidentally.

Finally, each day container is labeled, but it's on the side that's hidden from view. The manufacturer seems to have realized this oversight too late, so they provide little stickers you can add to the top to label the days. Really? It's a sleek and attractive pill case, that now has printed white stickers stuck on it that are hard to get lined up and straight. Plus, I'm really not sure how long they'll stay on.

They're pretty, they’re better at stopping your pills from scattering, and I like that they're colorful, but there are issues I can't overlook. They just don't work for me on so many levels.

title: Earthy, bitter taste. Doesn't dissolve in water, best added to diet in other ways.
text:
I very much hope this works for me, because it addresses almost every issue that I see as a concern. I tasted the dry powder first, and was surprised to find it herbal and earthy. The bitter taste came after I added it to hot water and some tea. It remained suspended in the water for the most part, but I wouldn't say it completely dissolved. It was easy to drink, even thought bitter isn't my favorite flavor. I think it would be nice to add to soups, vegetable dishes, and smoothies, rather than teas, just because of my personal taste. The measurements are given in grams and, since I'm American, a virtually useless guideline for me. I use a light half teaspoon per dose and hope that's on track.

I find that so many typically recommended supplements have done me little good, so I'm always willing to try something more unusual. Bearing this in mind, I feel comfortable recommending this.

title: Very pleased with this product!
text:
I'm a bit suspicious of mysterious green powders I'm supposed to consume. I never know what to expect when it comes to taste. However, I'm trying to introduce new sources of harder to find nutrients into my diet and I've read a lot of good things about astragalus root.

I think you usually need to take a new nutrient for a while before you can gauge its effectiveness, so I can't speak here to the health benefits of astragalus root. If it does what people claim, it will do me a great deal of good. I CAN speak to how this product tastes.

I have to cut down on my carb intake so, while I'd love to have a smoothie everyday, I just can't. So I have to make the ones I do have count. Since the bag is small and the dosage is one scoop I thought this bag wouldn't last long at all. Turns out the scoop is also small! I'm pleased with how long I think I will take me to finish the bag. Also, adding the powder didn't seem to alter the taste of my smoothie at all. It blended in smoothly without any lumps and really just vanished into the mix. I didn't even notice a change in color.

I have to say I'm very pleased with this product. It's a bit high in price, but using it as I do makes it worth the cost. I'm also glad I can say I can keep my precious smoothies tasting as good as they do, but now they're even better for me. I can recommend this product without hesitation.

text:
MUST DO TIP: There are a lot of complaints about the wax not sticking or going on. You MUST remove all traces of oil from the glasses first. The best way to do this is to use the pre-moistened glasses wipes that you can get from pretty much anywhere. If you don't have those, use water and a dry paper towel. title: Not effective, definitely not worth it
text:
I was cautiously optimistic about using DMSO to help with soreness and injuries from running and the occasional injuries from weights. Some of the reviews I've read from multiple sources cite this product as a virtual miracle for these types of uses claiming to significantly reduce pain/inflammation in a short amount of time. My experience has been the exact opposite - it didn't provide any relief at all for my hamstrings/knees or trapezium - in fact the soreness continued to worsen the way it would have if I'd done nothing at all.

The smell is a whole other issue - I'd been prepared so was expecting something pretty bad. If the product had relieved the symptoms as intended I would say it was a fair trade, maybe. But after the initial uses, I did a short 20 minute workout and 5 minutes later stopped in my tracks thinking, "holy crap, what is that smell?" It wasn't sweat, it smelled like garlic mixed with a little petroleum. It was coming out of my pores and the infamous taste was there too. I have serious doubts that this could be healthy/ok to have absorbed into your body.
The bottom line is that it didn't work for me and my body was much better served by using a muscle rub.

title: Works well and includes replacement blades!
text: This razor is similar to the lower end models of so-called "name brand" rotary shavers.  It gives a pretty good shave and fits well in my hand. The 90 minute battery power is great (I haven't run out of power yet but that's the spec) and means one full charge prior to travel will do it.  Worst case it's a usb charge so typically I am set up for that on the road anyway. And I can see the remaining battery power on the display when I turn it on.  (You can lock the on/off button, btw, by pressing and holding it down for a few seconds.)  For the price it's a great razor to leave in my travel kit so I don't have to take a more expensive model with me. (Because who hasn't left something in a hotel room?)  The only negatives: it does not have a built-in sideburn trimmer which I really like. None of them are the greatest cutters but they are useful for a quick clean-up. And there's no travel bag but I have some bags from other devices that I'll co-opt for this one. One huge positive that helps to offset the negatives: it comes with a replacement cutter (with three rotary blades).  It's never clear with generic brands where one can buy replacement blades, and sometimes it's less expensive to just buy a new razor. They included the first replacement blades so in my mind that doubles the useful life of the product.  That's a great feature that every non-name brand razor manufacturer should include.  It truly differentiates this product from its many generic competitors.

title: Failure to charge after 2 months of use spoils an otherwise good product
text:
Until this stopped recharging, It was a 4-star item; knowing this might be a problem I deferred review. At this point, it won't charge and is dead. So, let me review both pre- and post-death.
If you like ultrasonic toothbrushes, this is great. Motor is strong, brushhead movement is less than a rotary, but on par with other top-end ultrasonic toothbrushes. The ultrasonic motion really foams up during use, which is different than a rotary. Body is solid, good heft and feel in the hand. I really like the brushheads - connection to the body is solid, with no 'wobble'. Overall, if you prefer ultrasonic to rotary, this is a solid 4-stars.
Until... it comes to recharge. Arrived fully charged and didn't begin to slow for 3 weeks - which is a great charge life. I plugged it in and recharged overnight. This charge lasted two weeks. Another overnight, lasted about a week. After that, needed overnight just to turn on. At this point, even plugged in, it won't power on. Recharge is essential feature, with this failing in 2 months, I can't give it more than 2-stars.
I'm not the only buyer who reported this same behavior, so it isn't a one-off problem. Fix the battery issue and it would be a solid 4-stars.

title: Oily, Greasy and Heavy!

I had received a sample Argan oil of another brand to try and really loved how soft it made my hair feel. When the bottle ran out, I came to Amazon to look for a replacement. I thought to give a try when I saw the high ratings received on this Organic Moroocan Argan Oil. I start the process with freshly washed wet hair. I placed a few drops of oil onto my palm and spread it around my palm. First of all, the oil felt thick and greasy on my palm. I thought it might feel different once it’s absorb in so I continue with my routine. Starting from the ends of my hair and running my palms up to half way from scalp. Unfortunately, it felt nothing like the other brand I had used. Once dried, my hair didn’t feel soft like the other brand did, instead it made my hair feel heavy, greasy and I looked like I haven’t washed my hair in months! I had to shampoo my hair a couple of times the next day to get rid of the greasy feel.

Since this is a brand new bottle, I didn’t want to be wasteful so I tried it on my face on another evening. I placed two drops of oil on my palm and massaged it onto my face and neck. After 30 minutes, my face still felt oily!

Not sure if this is how cold pressed, unrefined argan oil is supposed to feel but I am NOT a fan!

title: Newbie Review
text:
I am a noob to all this oil stuff, so I'm going to write my review in my plain terms and update as I learn.
2/4 Update- Overnight went alright. Both held water all night long and then some, both were turned on to the bottom, which shows as full speed on the dial dots but it still goes 1/4 way further, so I had it on 3/4 of the way. I can't sleep with any lights on, and I put a small face cloth in front of the blue light switch. I woke up in the middle of the night and could see from the light coming out that it wasn't blowing upwards, it was blowing out and then just falling back down and my dresser around it was damp. I adjusted the white spout and turned down the speed and it seemed to have helped. The white top spout piece might not have been in the right place and it might have been keeping it from blowing all the way. It is now working fine. Second thing to note is that the piece that blows the mist, where is sits in the bottom of the tank, turned a little brown. I tried to rub it off thinking it was from the water, but it's almost as if it's stained. The other unit does not have this.

2/3 The item does not come in a sealed package, just an unmarked box, tab closed, item in a plastic bag. It was clean and appeared unused so it seemed fine.
There is not a special dispenser spot for the essential oils, you fill it up with water just like a humidifier and drip some of the oil in it before putting it back on the base.
You will up the tank with water, drop some oil in it, close it, put the tank back on the base. You'll hear the base fill up. Then plug it in and use the turn dial to set how hard you want it blowing. I was surprised it blows cold (whatever temp the water you put in was), I thought for some reason it warmed it. I used room temperature distilled water.
The light can be turned off with the switch on the back.
You don't have to unplug it to turn it off, the dial can be turned to off.

title: Finally, a quality made denture bath!
text:
While searching online and in stores for a denture bath, I've not found what most of us call, a "quality" made product. I believe that I have now found it with this one! (can we say, "hooray!")

Many commenters have posted how "flimsy" or "leaky" others baths are. Both of which I have experienced first hand with the denture bath that the prosthodontist provided me with. My wife complained that there was water all over the bathroom countertop every time I used the denture bath (nightly). It got to the point where I was monitoring the amount of water, carefully placing the bath on the counter and I know for a fact, I did not spill any water. Sure enough, it became obvious that I did get a leaky one. I decided it was time to find a new one. Like I said before, I looked online and in stores. I simply wasn't comfortable with the ones I've seen or read about. That is, until I came across this one.

Granted, we're not talking about major dollars or to some, a rather insignificant item, but for those us with a denture, it's important that we find something which will suit our needs and be worry-free. When I received the bath, I was pleased to see how well made it was. In addition, the plastic is not "flimsy" or thinly made. The basket inside is also rigid and feels, to me at least, to be quality made. I am now able to place my denture in the bath, add warm water and place my denture cleaner tablet without any concerns. I believe you'd find the same experience. As other commenters have stated, you cannot properly seat the lid unless the basket is in place. It's easy to clean and easy to put back.

PROS: Quality made, more rigid plastic (not flimsy), intuitive, easy to use and clean
CONS: None noted

title: Best sleeping mask I have had so far.
text:
I was looking for a sleeping mask that I could use on an upcoming international trip. I have trouble sleeping when it is not totally dark, so sleeping when travelling in a plane, train or other mode of transportation has always been difficult. I wanted to find a sleeping mask that was both comfortable to wear and blocked out all light.

I ordered the Seedling's 3D Contoured Cup Sleeping Mask and it has really hit the mark on what I was looking for.

Good:
1. Comfortable to wear. It is not flat. Cushion runs around the outer edge of the mask so it does not touch any part of your eyes.
2. Blocking light. I tested wearing the mask during the daytime and to my surprise there was no light seepage. It was totally dark. Since the mask has contoured cups around your eyes you can open them while wearing to confirm no light was coming in.
3. Material. The mask feels like it made out of some neoprene/spandex material. It is smooth against the skin.
4. Bonus. It comes with a bonus silk mask and ear plugs.

Bad:
1. Nothing to note. Although one suggestion I would make is to include a carrying case for the mask instead of the bonus silk mask. Since I plan to use the mask when I travel, I have to figure out how to protect it in my baggage when not being used.

Overall I would highly recommend this sleeping mask.

title: OMG! Perfect to keep my medical patch on...and dry.
text:
(Read last paragraph for proper application.)
I’ve tried about every brand and type of adhesive bandage out there to keep my prescription estrogen patch on. And keep it dry when I shower. Finally success with this product! I’ve included a photo. I’ve had this adhesive film over my patch for 4 days so far, and have showered and the patch is still in place and dry. It’s not bulky, and it doesn’t lose its adhesive quality like all the other things I’ve tried. I haven’t tried to remove it yet since I don’t change patches but every 7 days, but I’ve read others saying it was easy to remove.
BE SURE YOU DON’T REMOVE THE “OUTER” EDGE COVERING “UNTIL” THE PATCH IS STUCK IN PLACE. That outer edge keeps acts like a picture frame that keeps a canvas from wrinkling (and in this case, prevents it sticking to itself.) Once the inner portion is stuck to your skin, there is a cut in the framed outer edge that allows you to peel it off in a long strip.

I decided to MOVE my patch to a different spot, and discovered the clear adhesive film is easy and painless to pull off. Then I applied my medical patch with a NEW clear adhesive film to a new spot. All went extremely well. You cannot re-use the clear adhesive film; use a new one when you need to reapply.

I love this adhesive film!

title: Easy to use, healthful product from grass fed beef
text: I do not normally buy gelatin. I make my own grass fed bone broth for its collagen and gelatin and really enjoy it. However, in some circumstances such as changing from burning glucose to burning ketones, it is necessary to measure protein levels precisely, which is impossible in a home-made product. As a result, I bought this beef gelatin to use in my morning "bulletproof coffee" which requires either collagen or gelatin. I have to say that my coffee is much more enjoyable because this product has only a very mild almost indiscernible taste. As always with any gelatin product, follow the instructions. Some gelatin must be exposed to cold water before hot water is added or it will clump and not gel. Some gelatin requires only hot water. This gelatin requires the two step process. I have not used it for jelly and probably never will. But I enjoy it in my coffee, especially when I can be confident that I am using a product from grass fed beef.

text: This product is  exactly the same as the Welledia 1800ML diffuser and $6 less in price, I bought both at the same time and was very surprised to see the same product besides the name Welledia below the front knob the led color above the knob is green and blue on the Newstyle and both turn red and shut down when empty. Both products work good as a essential oil diffuser and love the fact you can turn the light on and off. Both have variable adjustment of amount of water vapor output but find fan does not change speed as you increase the amount of mist which can be so much it tends to sink down like a cloud instead of rising. You can play with the output knob to get your desired flow. This just shows how powerful the ultrasonic plate is. These two products (being identical) are both heads above the Young Living diffuser which I had to replace due to failure at less than half the price . I highly recommend these two products but save some money by buying the Newstyle brand. One came in a fancy box and the other came in a plane box. Both hold the same amount of water even though I have not measured either, the dimensions are the same and hold enough water to last 6-18 hours depending on the flow rate. I love the fact you can add the oils and water, put the cap on and shake it to mix the oils before placing it on the diffuser plate. No, the led above the knob cannot be turned off but a piece of electrical tape over it does the trick. UPDATE, TO USE BEST AS AN ESSENTIAL OIL DIFFUSER, PUT OILS DIRECTLY IN THE BASE AFTER IT HAS WATER IN IT NOT IN THE TANK. This will concentrate the oil diffusion better into the air and when the oils have been diffused will keep working as a humidifier. Add more oils as needed to the base water but MAKE SURE you turn off machine before you lift tank off to do this or splashing of water will occur.

Other than that, the mask is fully adjustable, blocks 100% external light, and material is very pleasant.

The speakers are fully adjustable and once properly placed for your ears, they can get surprisingly loud. The speakers themselves are wrapped in foam so you do not feel them if you are like me and a side sleeper.

With volume at full, my wife did not hear any sound bleed from the headphones which was another pleasant surprise.

Have not tried using the 'call' function yet and doubt I will. However, if I ever do I will update this review.

Overall, super great bargain for under $10. Very comfortable and adjustable. Surprisingly superior sound with adequate volume. Very easy to setup and use. title: Accurate and Can Save Lives!
text:
I once was a juror on a drunken driving case and the judge actually said, "I want to make it clear. It is not illegal to drink and drive; it is illegal to drive drunk or impaired". Well, it doesn't take much alcohol to get you legally drunk or impaired.

This tiny little device (2" X 3" X 0.5") is a complex breathalyzer that uses your iPhone for results! It only takes less than a minute to `pair' with your iPhone (you must download the free BACtrack app. It will ask for credit card info, but is not charged).
First thing to do is set the settings to your gender and weight for accuracy. Note that females have fewer enzymes to break down alcohol and certain races have even less. Check Wikipedia or GOOGLE for this information.

Open the app, and when it says `take a reading', a clock appears and gives you one minute to prepare. Simply `BLOW NOW!' by taking a steady deep blow into the analyzer while watching the eight blue bars fill up - then you stop. There is a slight `click'. The test results are shown on your phone via a large number, such as 0.004 (which means it is likely you are very sober). Click 'OK' and you are shown a `graph' that indicate the times between `blows' and your alcohol level. 0.08 is legally drunk and you should test again in fifteen minutes.

There is also an option to get a "Dose-Specific Effect" of your alcohol level with suggestions. It is also very important to wait at least fifteen (15) minutes to test after your last drink, cigarette or food consumption.
You can `tag' a drink for future use in the computer storage, like a beer, glass of wine, liquor, etc. You can add a photo of that time period (although this would be more appropriate if you were at a party sharing the device and getting a shot of a 0.18% drinker looks like. The device does come with three plastic washable mouthpieces. There is a tab for notes. There is also a `share' button which lets you share your results on Facebook, text it, or tweet it. Now come on! Close out the program and your entire previous tests are stored. There is a system called `Zeroline' which estimates how long it will take your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) to return to 0.00% based on your last test result.

My results the first time:
I enter `Male' and `195 pounds' at 8:00pm on an empty stomach; 4 ounces; Vodka with soda. This is a typical bar mix.
After one hour my BAC was 0.10. Over the legal limit. The second hour I drank a 2 oz. drink and waited an hour. My BAC was 0.065.

So 6 ounces of vodka on a fairly empty stomach with the `time to sobriety' (0.00%) would happen around 2:00am. This was interesting information. It's a pricey unit, but not anywhere near the over $10,000 it is estimated, to deal with being busted drunk driving. Drive safely!

title: Loving The Treatment Creams and Oil
text:
Just received this today and started using the treatment creams and the oil tonight and wanted to give my first impression.

There's a lot of stuff in here for just $20, especially considering that these same products in these same sizes go for a minimum of $4 a pop on the Nailtiques website. These are very small containers but I'm thinking they will last for at least a month, some possibly longer depending on how much is used each time. So far I've used the cuticle and skin gel, the nail moisturizer, the oil therapy and the hand conditioner. This would be a nice gift for someone who loves taking care of their nails.

Right off, the scent is quite nice, not overpowering. These are rich feeling but not greasy at all. They seem to sink right in and give relief for that dry feeling my hands and nails can sometimes get. I decided to use these first then I'll put on the protein tomorrow. My nails are not all that soft but they do have ridges and tend to split along those ridges. They also get very dry and tend to peel. This kit seems to be perfect, although, not sure I'll be using the foot cream much since most likely I will only get one application out of the tiny container.

Included in the boxes for both the protein and the oil is a very short guide which describes all of the products and directions for use along with suggestions and tips for specific uses. Otherwise, it's up to you how you use these. I applied the cuticle and skin gel first, then the nail moisturizer, then the oil and finished up with the hand cream. If you go to their website and look at the FAQ page, they state that the nail moisturizer promotes nail moisture and the oil seals it in. I just went to the website and read it over so that I had an idea of how to use these things for the best results.

Now, keep in mind, the formula 2 protein does have formaldehyde resin in it, which is what helps strengthen the nails, but if you have a problem with using anything with formaldehyde, you'll probably want to look at something else.

I've read so many good reviews of the Nailtiques products that I was willing to give this a shot. Only time will tell if it'll work for me or not.

These sleeves are completely opaque so they can help hide tattoos and disguise such skin imperfections as healed scars, psoriatic outbreaks, eczema, keratosis pilaris (my personal reason for wanting them), embarrassing keloids, birthmarks, vitiligo, freckles, moles, insect bites, and the redness and inflammation from allergic dermatitis. I can also see them being useful in blocking direct contact btwn dirty little kid fingernails and itchy, possibly open insect bites. And, while I'm throwing out supposition, what if they helped block out dangerous UV sun rays, or aided in blocking the transfer of the itchy effects of poison oak/ivy? Those are certainly questions worth asking this seller before purchasing, if those are the reasons you're interested in this product.

I'm not affiliated with, nor did I receive any compensation from this company in exchange for my review. It's just a great product that I'm delighted to have found. These sleeves have, in a sense, given me back my life after 20+ years of hiding! Thank you, Presadee!!!

title: My New Favorite Pillow!!!
text:
Finally, after years of buying the wrong pillow, I have found the right pillow for me. I just took my new Rejuvenation Milliet Pillow for side sleepers out of the box, and I can tell instantly that this will be the best pillow yet. I can't wait for bedtime tonight to give it an all night test. It is also pretty heavy, so I won't be "chasing" it around in my sleep. title: Experienced user found this worked some then caught my hair.
text:
I've spent much time trying this product out before reviewing and I've also tried the fo air curler secret. I watched videos and read the instructions and prepped my hair properly etc. it is essential you have no tangles and a very small section of hair.

My review on this curler.
Pros:
it curls in all directions- alternating, left or right. Simple to switch.
It has a great panel that shows you the temperature that is easily read.
It heats up quickly.
It is not that heavy on my opinion - I don't think the Conair secret one is either
It comes in different colors
It comes with multiple hair clips
It comes in a nice box
Fast shipping
Easy to adjust temp.
Will make a curl if it works right*** please see cons
Curls if done correctly will last a couple days

Cons-
It will accept a smaller section of hair than the conair secret

It has trapped at least 3 curl sections when doing the entire head. When the hair gets trapped on this one it seems much harder to remove and it ruins that piece of hair look wise. It even when you take very small sections and brush out all over and each time for each section, when it's trapped it sucks your hair in twists it excessively into a tight cord and is very hard to remove from the device- yes my hair got stuck but luckily I got it out each time before it burned off. It damaged my hair but I was able to fix it on these pieces with intense deep conditioning. Please know I read all the instructions and have experience using these. The conair one was easier to remove if it did get trapped but I did not like it bc it did not curl in all directions. I've tried to curl my hair with the osir after a hair cut, deep contioning and much more to see if that was my issue with the product. My stylist said my hair was in very good condition and I took small sections and brushed brush brushed it smooth. I was very sad that this product did not work for me bc I needed my hair done for a wedding. On the curls that come out without catching it looks really nice!- but after all the work I did trying to fix the pieces that always ended up getting caught and then looked horrible it was not worth using this for that. I don't feel like I could ever be confident that my entire head would come out. As I always had a few (in different locations each time) that made my hair look very very bad like lighting hit it with a severe hard tight twist- bc the machine keeps twisting for a bit even when it's caught. Eventually it stops but after that I still had to fight getting my hair out.

I wish this worked but it didn't for me. I have fine hair. I hope that you try these out bc they are incredible but this one in particular caught on me too much. Your hair might be different!

title: Took out 99% of my squeaks!
text:
I have been in my home for three years and have been living with squeaks the entire time. I finally got tired of it and ordered this kit. I would not recommend the kit without extra screws, because chances are you will need them and then have to reorder. I didn't use all of mine but if any more develop I can take care of them instantly.

I had several squeaks in my master bedroom, hallway, and a 2nd bedroom. The stud finder did not work for me at all. Anywhere I drilled it would not slide up and down so it felt like I always hit a stud. Im sure it works but for some reason it was not doing it for me. To find the studs I pulled the carpet back in the corners and found where the nails were hammered in. This shows where the studs are. I marked the nail holes with tape in a few different spots on top of the carpet, and then measured from there where the rest would be. This worked like a charm for me.

This method got rid of every squeak in my master bedroom except for one and for some reason it squeaks on the sub floor between two joists. When I replace the carpet this year I will look into it. It got out 100% of the squeaks in my 2nd bedroom, and 100% of them in my hall way. In the closet of my master bedroom it would squeak if you stepped anywhere withing a 24" square. I put one screw in the stud and it took care of the whole thing. That was awesome.

No damage to my carpet at all and it was very easy to do. If you have a hard time finding your studs just pull the carpet back in a corner and press it back in when you're done. I highly recommend this product.

text: Overall, this product makes me miss Drixoral even more than ever! I really wish they'd bring it back! The similarities and differences between this product, ALA-HIST PE, and Drixoral are as follows: (1) same antihistamine,  Dexbromfeniramine, but (2) different (less effective) decongestant (phenylephrine aka PE) as opposed to Drixoral's pseudoephedrine. Also, (3) Drixoral was one pill every 12 hours (and it lasted about 24 hrs for me), whereas the dose of this product is one pill every 4 hours; (4) this product makes me very drowsy, whereas Drixoral never did. (5) I could depend on Drixoral to start working in 20-30 minutes every time I had to take it, whereas this product is hit or miss -- sometimes it starts working in 20-30 mins, sometimes it doesn't ever start working. But even when it does work, it lasts less than 2 hrs for me. Finally, (6) this product is excessively overpriced, much more expensive than Drixoral was. All that said, I won't be wasting my money on this product anymore :(

title: Great air purifier for a small space
text:
I have had this small air purifier for a little over a week now. I have it located in a guest bathroom to help keep the air fresh and any odors at bay. So far I would have nothing to complain about with the unit.
The item arrived packaged in a small black box. It was secure and tidy packaging, and included a small page with information about the unit. The device itself is quite small. It is a matte black color with an orange/amber LED strip on it. The Light is the only immediate indication that the unit is powered on once plugged in, and there is no way to turn the light off. Unless the room is very dark, the light is not very bright, and in a dark room the light is not bright enough to be a night light or anything like that, so the light is not distracting in any way in my opinion.
It’s hard to quantifiably review the air purifying ability of the device. This unit does not have a fan and filter like larger more expensive units do designed to remove allergens and irritants from larger spaces. Those units often have the filter, as well as an ionization feature. This unit only filters by ionization, meaning it uses the electricity to negatively charge the air molecules, which then bind with irritants. When this bond is made, the particles should be too heavy, and thus fall to the ground. There is no noticeable smell or sound produced by this device, but I have no reason to doubt it is working.
Knowing what this purifier is for, I would recommend it for anyone looking for something similar. I would not encourage someone to get it expecting it to work magic in a very large space, but rather benefit a smaller area.

title: Decent, but you're paying for the name
text:
Ignore the comments from reviewers claiming the light is like an old fluorescent light. Sorry, but such comments can only be from people ignorant as to color temperatures or people who received a lamp with a defective ballast. As advertised, this light has a very natural light to it with more of a colder/bluish tint. If you like that, great. If you don't, buy another lamp. But don't claim that it has a harsh fluorescence or glare, or that it flickers, because those are factually untrue statements.

Overall, the lamp is decent quality, but the arm on mine has fallen down twice and I've really needed to tighten down the one-sided wing nut on the side to keep it up. I would have been willing to pay another $10-20 for a brushed steel map made in the USA with better quality on the adjustment arm.

One last thing: The lamp comes shipped in a large box with huge blocks of Styrofoam. Don't assume because this is a "full spectrum lamp" that the manufacturer cares in the slightest about the environment. They apparently don't.

title: Very good at odor elimination...but limited at air purifying + has a heavy plug.
text:
As others are no doubt smarter than me, I mistakingly purchased this to clean and purify air in a small-ish work office. Stale, perhaps moldy air was the norm, the GG1000 a hopeful solution to this uncomfortable dilemma.

By 'smarter than me,' I'm referring to an ignorance that the GG1000 could only sanitize versus operate akin to ionizers on HEPA. After weeks of use, the GG1000 did nothing to improve the air quality in the office. About to send it to the great waste bin in the sky, I gave it a second chance in my poorly ventilated, home kitchen. The same kitchen where cooking anything sends the odor seemingly across continents.

Eureka! What once was lost now is found. The GG1000 is a rockstar in this odor killing capacity, albeit a finicky one when it comes to being plugged into the wall. While said plug can rotate, the one is a tad unbalanced meaning older outlets might struggle with it (consider a multi-prong adapter for stability).

On the odor killing front, I can't believe how well this thing works. I don't believe it an overstatement to speculate 80+ percent of kitchen odors are now gone. It's a new experience to have a kitchen and apartment no longer smelling like yesterday's vegetables (curse you, broccoli!). GG1000, you da' man.

**UPDATE - DEC 2014**
Product started sounding like a highest pitch aircraft taking off, 24/7. Germ Guardian stands by their stuff, and - even if out of the 1 year warranty - offered me a replacement at half MSRP (to include shipping).

FYI: If you're looking for a good small office HEPA purifier: [[ASIN:B005NCB3HY Whirlpool Whispure Tower Air Purifier- HEPA Air Cleaner, APT40010R]].

title: this is my first experience with a somewhat sentient vacuum and I've actually enjoyed it. In the spirit of that enjoyment
text: So, this is my first experience with a somewhat sentient vacuum and I've actually enjoyed it.  The quick start instructions on the box and the app (there's an app that comes with it!!!) are a pretty good place to start if you're like me and hate having to put things together, follow diagrams, directions, etc.  The bot takes very little to assemble and there's a slight smell when in first use, but this can be expected of any new machine you bring into your home and can be remedied easily: my solution is to put dabs of essential oil (very, very little) on the filter and wham, new experience altogether.  There are a few drawbacks however: difficulties with sliding onto low, medium-thickness carpet, not being able to climb into a room elevated off the flat hardwood and what seems to be the bot's complete inability to find the docking station when told to dock in the app.  All in all, it works like a dream on hardwood and makes me feel grossed out by all the dirt, hair, etc., in the dirt cup because it's so effective (duh, Hoover!).  The dirt cup itself, however, is easy to find and empty, but seems to spill every single time I take the top off which is a minor drawback.  A great little bot which can get into low dirty places like under beds, tables and couches and makes the floor honestly feel cleaner after it's done doing a cycle.  I have spent many an evening running the bot with its Bluetooth in the app, and it responds almost instantly to walls and my directions on the keypad.  Cats are simultaneously fascinated and terrified which is entertaining in and of itself.  Excellent little gadget which has replaced most of my manual vacuuming.

Before I let my kids try any products I always taste test first and I have to say, I wasn't pleased by the taste. It had a weird after-taste so I don't blame my kids. Hopefully they can work on improving the taste and have it be more similar to the Berry taste on the other probiotics.

Our kids have taken probiotics for a few years now. Oddly enough, one of our children got an ear infection just prior to these arriving so we were interested to see if this would have any positive effect. Unfortunately it did not. This was our child's first ear infection and I wasn't expecting a miracle but we wanted to try these for a day or two before getting antibiotics. The doctor told us it was a pretty mild ear infection so we did give our child abx for the recommended course. It is advised not to use probiotics while on antibiotics.

After the antibiotics were done we continued to give these to our kids but they didn't like the taste of them. They normally take [[ASIN:B007XEPURO Ultimate Flora Kids Probiotic Supplement, Chewable Tablets Berry 30 ea]] made by the same company Renew Life (kids) and they love them.

The great thing is these are 10 Billion CFU with three strains (listed below).

Full ingredients: Bifidobacterium lactis, Lactobacillus acidophilus, Streptococcus salivarius K12, xylitol, inulin, sorbitol, natural orange flavor, magnesium stearate, silica, vegetable juice color, natural vanilla flavor, citric acid and ascorbic acid.

Overall, these are just OK. If they improve the flavor of these, I think my kids would be more into taking them. We did not notice any issues with our kids going from 3 Billion to these 10 Billion.

title: Much Better Than Expected
text:
My husband is on his feet all the time and suffers from some foot pain as a result. He finds that shoes with more supportive arches tend to help alleviate this, so I had him try using these Makryn Adjustable Shoe Insoles in some of his shoes that have less support. He was a little skeptical at first because these insoles were not particularly thick like some of his gel cushioned arch support insoles. He used them nevertheless and added the medium size "soft support" self-adhesive arch pad. Note that the insoles come with six pairs of these additional peel-and-stick self adhesive support pads, with three "soft support" and three "normal support."

After wearing these Makryn Insoles in a pair of shoes that usually do not provide much support, he said that these arched inserts worked much better than he had expected. The insoles went in easily and stayed in place throughout the day. The size large fit his size 12 shoes perfectly. He had been concerned that the soft support pads might not hold, but they stayed in place as well. Best of all, he did not feel the same level of foot pain/discomfort that he usually experiences after being in those shoes all day. The only negative thing he noted was that he had to experiment with the placement of the self-adhesive pads several times before they felt right. All the same, given how well these have worked out, he's thinking about ordering an extra pair of these insoles for his other shoes so he doesn't have to switch these around.

title: Requires Some Trial And Error Adjustments, But Very Good
text:
I've been going on walks more often during these last few months. I think my health has improved, but my feet have started to hurt from all the miles I've covered. I decided to give these Barefoot Scientist So Jelly Pressure Relief Insole Grips a try. They come with 2 pairs (1 pair for the heel, 1 pair for the balls of the feet) of clear gel, shock absorbing inserts. Each of the inserts has a self adhesive side.

After removing the backing material, I stuck the inserts onto the insoles of my usual pair of walking shoes. After trying them out on a walk, I had to stop after a few minutes to adjust the placement of the inserts. The squishy balls of the front inserts just weren't hitting the right area of my feet. Luckily, I was still able to peel the inserts up and relocate them on my insoles. After another mile, I stopped once more to make another insert placement adjustment. The 3rd time was the charm and I finally got the inserts on the spots that worked best for me. I've had them in my walking shoes since and they've been working out very well in cushioning and relieving the pressure on my feet. I recommend using these, but you will likely have to make some adjustments to get them on the right spot for your needs.

title: Flavor A Little Sweet And Less Than 3 Weeks Worth Per Bottle, But Great Immunity Booster
text: I had heard about the potential benefits of zinc as a supplement even before the pandemic. I decided to try out this HIMMUNE Ionic Zinc Spray as a way of introducing some zinc into my daily life. I figured it could only help. Besides, the ingredients include Vitamin B5, which my body needs anyway. The zinc comes in a 30ml spray bottle that is a very handy size for keeping with me throughout the day. The label indicates that each bottle has 150 sprays which I  initially thought was a great value. Then I read the back label and found that, for adults 18+, they recommend 4 sprays 2 times per day, which breaks down to only about 19 daily doses. So in less than 3 weeks, I'll need to order another bottle. The spray itself is also a bit sweet and the flavor stays in my mouth for quite a while. The ingredients say that spearmint natural flavor is included, but all I really taste is the sweetener. Despite these issues, I feel better using this zinc immunity booster on a daily basis, especially with cold and flu season coming up coupled with the ongoing pandemic.

title: It's Hard to Eat Just One...
text:
These Digestive Advantage Probiotic Bites in Dark Chocolate are addictive! Ideally, you'd eat one of these after a meal or daily, as a supplement to your diet, to improve your gut flora and overall digestive health. I am an avid fan of pro-biotics, and also enjoy kombucha, yogurt, kefir, etc... which are delish, but not quite as simple to eat or as convenient as popping a chocolate into your mouth as you do with these bites. These Digestive Advantage Bites are the size of giant malt-balls, and are about 90% chocolate in my estimation- straight to the center of the bite, where you then encounter a small circle of chewier and slightly grainy textured probiotic/ chocolate mix, that is only slightly noticeable as being different from the rest of the chocolate, and which does not taste all that different from the rest of the bite either. The only reason i noticed was the texture, which is not unpleasant.

I had a hard time eating these just as a supplement, and ended up snarfing a bunch just at once, and they disappeared over a few days (actually, it wasn't just me- my family discovered them quickly), ...cuz it's chocolate- and a very melty high quality chocolate at that (these have a thin waxy coating which prevents them melting in your hand), and these are completely delish. If you don't already take probiotics, I highly recommend you try some form, because it truly makes you feel better inside over a longer term- less stomach issues and better digestion means your body runs more efficiently. These delicious Probiotic Bites are a great way to get the benefits of probiotics, without the nastiness of swallowing pills, and in a form that you can carry with you easily. Also, my kids will eat these in a heartbeat.

title: Great Taste, Refreshing, Easy to Dissolve, but Has Aspartame
text:
This Sport Go Electrolyte in Lemon Lime is very tasty. The directions recommend 2 scoops with the included scoop, added to 16 oz (500 ml) of water, for one serving size. I mixed a 1/2 serving size (1 scoop to 8 oz water) in the white ceramic mug shown in my pic, and stirred it with a spoon. It dissolved fairly quickly and evenly, making a slightly lemonade-type milky looking drink, which tasted very sweet to me. I put it in my water bottle and filled the rest of the bottle with plain water, to get 1/2 the recommended concentration, which was a better flavor for me, because I don't love sweet drinks- but, you can easily add the amount you want, which is convenient.

I compared this Sport Go to the leading-brand sports drink starting w "G" that I often have on hand. The G contained artificial colors and natural and artificial flavors, whereas the Sport Go had only natural flavors,but also contained aspartame (the blue pack sweetener on tables at restaurants). G contained 27.5 grams Total Carbs (22 grams in my 12 oz G bottle increased 1/4 to account for the 16 oz comparison) vs. Sport Go's 36 g. G contained 100 cal (80 cal x 1.25) vs. Sport Go's 150 cal. G had about 26g sugar (21g x 1.25) vs. Sport Go's 7g. Sport Go contains several other electrolyes and minerals missing from the G, however, including Magnesium and Calcium.

Overall, depending on what you are looking for, this Sport Go is a multi-mineral electrolyte drink that tastes great (diluted for me), and will provide a good supplement for your heavy sport activities, without unnecessary artificial colors or flavors. On the other hand, I am not a big fan of Aspartame.

title: About its features
text:
Caveat: I received this at a discount to evaluate and provide an unbiased review

I feel really badly to drop my rating from a five star (see below) to a 3 star, because the unit stopped working after about 3 months. Until then, it worked great - I was able to use it for close to 2 months without charging it. I really liked it. Unfortunately, it stopped working. May well be my fault, I may have been pressing the activation button too hard - I'm type A and noticed I was breaking pens because I pressed so hard. Even if that was the problem, I felt the unit should accommodate people like me. I asked the person who contacted me about their warrantee policy - she replied she didn't know since no one had ever told her it stopped working!

That said, the Beiwin Sonicare is a really nice product. It may not be right for everyone, but it has advantages over the two year-old Philips Sonicare that I had been using and possible disadvantages. For the record, I haven't checked Philips' subsequent products.

I prefer it to my two-year old Philips toothbrush. Some users may find it particularly useful, such as travelers and some people with hand/wrist disorders such as arthritis for reasons below.

The manufacturer, Beiwin, listed these features in their Sonic toothbrush:
- 3 brushing modes ( low, massage and high) with a two-minute timer.
- Sonic technology delivers up to 42,000 brush strokes per minute.
- Magnetic inductive charging provides 3.5 hours fast charging and stays charged for 60 days when brushing twice a day.

Pros

1. Wow, the charge is very impressive. I used it for a couple of weeks now and I haven't charged it once. As mentioned above, it should last a couple of months brushing 2x/day without charging. That's way more than my old brush.

2. It is more streamlined, more narrow and lighter in weight than the Philips I was using,

The base of the Beiwin Sonicare measures 1"L x 1"W, while the Philips Sonicare measures 1 5/16"L and 1 1/16" W.

3. I like the three brush mode settings. I tend to go with light setting.

4. I did "off the cuff" testing with three people, who thought that the vibration of the Beiwin seemed to be a bit less noticeable than my former one.

5. The charger is quite different than others I've used.

Instead of a cord, it takes a standard removable micro-usb cord. I find connecting the cord on my Philips toothbrush annoying as the charger keeps on itself. And it's easier to deal with if your dog chews the wire (unplugged).

The toothbrush charger sits on a very small base. Maybe the size of a Susan B Anthony half dollar. No problem sticking it in your wallet when you're on the road. The charger pulls the toothbrush to its base with magnets. I

6. The product is quite inexpensive.

Sidebar:

1. The shape of the bristle head is a bit rounder than the Philips, and the bristles have about the same amount of hardness. A review of the literature on toothbrush design by Hayasaki (cite below), which concluded that research suggests the shape of the head is not as important as the diameter of the filament - thinner filaments feel softer and more flexible, but thicker bristles clean more effectively. So both toothbrushes should equate in shape and hardness of the filaments, though users may prefer different shapes of the head.

Cons:

1. And this is a big con - it looks like they intend to sell the brushes as separate items at some point but currently Bewin doesn't seem to be providing them yet. I'll change my rating if I notice they are available.

There is no reference on this page as to what buyers are supposed to do, other than buying another set.

The brushes on my Philips toothbrush don't fit on the Bewin and I don't see a reference to what wethey currently they aren't selling

2. It doesn't include a travel case. Not a problem for me since the Philips case fits it fine.

3. It doesn't include a USB converter if you just want to plug it in.

4. As I mentioned, although it's not an issue for me, it is easier to wobble the toothbrush on its base.

Citation:

Hayasaki, H., Saitoh, I., Nakakura-Ohshima, K., Hanasaki, M., Nogami, Y., Nakajima, T., . . . Yamasaki, Y. (2014). Tooth brushing for oral prophylaxis. Japanese Dental Science Review, 50(3), 69-77. doi: 10.1016/j.jdsr.2014.04.001

title: A Good Harness For The Price!
text:
I like this harness very much, especially considering the price I paid for it. These harnesses can and do go for more than $50 regularly, so I was leery when I saw it up for $15 with free shipping, but it is the brand name listed and arrived in the box (and very quickly, to boot!).

Pros:

* Very affordable.
* This harness fits many sizes. I'm a plus size woman and I fit without a problem.
* It's very user friendly. I've used harnesses for years, and this one is simple to put on and operate.
* The leather is strong and seems quite sturdy, especially in comparison to the typical fabric these harnesses are made of.

Cons:

* The leather feels like it could become irritating if worn for too long.
* As with all nylon strap harnesses, the sides/back have a tendency to dig in to the skin.
* It only comes with one O-ring, which just seems kind of cheap to me. A set of 2-3 is typical.

All in all, it's a good harness for the price. It would be great for those just interested in trying it out and seeing if they enjoy this type of play.

title: Unimpressed
text:
All right, so I just received these today in the mail. I've had plantar fasciitis for a while now and it is definitely no fun, especially first thing in the morning. I saw these online, I figured, I'd give it a shot, they don't look too bad.
When I took them out of the box, this funky smell hit me... it was so strong, that my cats actually ran from it. There are no instructions in or on the box, what so ever about how long to wear, how to launder, nothing. However I was pleasantly surprised that there was actually a pair in the box and not just one.
The white part is made of pretty soft material so it feels pretty good on my feet. Now, the "unique memory foam with cooling gel" aka the blue part... that is mighty unimpressive. I was hoping to feel either the memory foam or the cooling gel part, but unfortunately I don't. The whole thing is barely over (if at all) 1 mm thick, I am not sure it has any effect on anything what so ever.
Having to walk with plantar fasciitis I know how important a good support with quite bit of cushion is! Well, these really don't provide much of that at all.
I read the rest of the reviews and most people complain about them being too small. I don't have that problem but I do have pretty small feet (size 5.5) so they are almost a bit too big for me but definitely not for someone with swollen or big feet. I guess having a few different sizes could help that issue.
I will wear them for a few days and come back with an update to see if my feet feel any different.
Update: I've been wearing these for quite a few days now, noticed no difference in my plantar fasciitis. However, if I wear them for a few hours, my heels start sweating in them (eww).
I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. If this review has helped you in any way, please click the YES button. Thank you.

title: Did the job...
text:
This worked very well on a fishing trip up to Wisconsin this June...and they were having a REALLY bad year for mosquitos. I'm pregnant and was looking for something that had the recommended amount of DEET or Picardin...this was the only thing I found that really fit the bill. I knew I would be wearing it every day while on vacation so wanted to avoid anything with too high a percentage of the repellent and this was perfect. It has a pleasant smell to it and both the insect repellent and the sunscreen worked well for me. I still got quite a tan...but I WAS sitting in a boat all day getting not only the full sun but also the reflection from the water...but I did not burn.

The bottle was a little smaller than I was expecting (don't know why...the size is listed right on there so it's not like it was advertised differently) so if you want this to be used by more than one person I would either get a bigger size or multiple bottles.

Only thing I disliked about it (and this is very minor) is that I did feel greasy at the end of the day and REALLY wanted to wash it all off immediately when coming in for the night...but didn't because it was impossible to keep the mosquitos out of the house and I didn't want bites while I was sleeping. I don't think this product is any worse than others in this respect...it just kept me from really "loving" it.

title: Great OT brushing protocol brushes
text:
When my autistic child was three, the OT suggested brushing. It's been a great tool over the years. Basically, before an event where you know the child has a lot of sensory triggers (like a school assembly) you spend 15 minutes brushing them. Down their arms - always away from the body wherever you brush them at - down their back, gentle pressure, you don't want to overstimulate them. As they got older, my child was able to take over the brushing. We kept a brush in the school office like you would medicine, but also they carried one with them. We kept one in the car. In every room of the house, eventually.
The brushes we used were just surgical brushes. The disposable kind the doctors scrub with and throw out.

These are nice. The same brush, but in a pretty color. Plus, you get EIGHT at once! Great price, pretty colors. Love this set!
