Utilities say "Flushable" personal wipes clog sewer systems

for the full story:
[...]

Next time you go to toss that "flushable" wipe in the toilet, you might want to consider a request from your sewer utility: Don't.

Sewer agencies across the country say the rapidly growing use of pre-moistened "personal" wipes -- used most often by potty-training toddlers and people seeking what's advertised as a more "thorough" cleaning than toilet paper -- are clogging pipes and jamming pumps.

Utilities struggling with aging infrastructure have wrestled for years with the problem of "ragging" -- when baby wipes, dental floss, paper towels and other items not designed for flushing entangle sewer pumps.
The latest menace, officials say, is that wipes and other products, including pop-off scrubbers on toilet-cleaning wands, are increasingly being marketed as "flushable." Even ever-thickening, super-soft toilet paper is worrisome because it takes longer to disintegrate, some say.

"Just because you can flush it doesn't mean you should," said I.J. Hudson, a spokesman for the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, which handles sewage for 1.8 million Maryland residents in Montgomery and Prince George's counties.

The result: Utility officials say crews needed for less preventable sewer maintenance and repairs are being deployed instead to patrol for wipes.

text:
I am a size a size 5.5 in women's shoes and I got these not because I have flat feet, but because I have very high arches and most shoes do not give enough arch support (especially not flats or sandals). These are AMAZING!

They were super easy to place after figuring out the best placement for me on a shoe's insole on my first pair. To do that, I stuck an unpeeled pair of these in a pair of flats and walked around until I got them to the right placement. I then carefully popped my foot out and placed each where they were when I pulled out. For every shoe after that (including some flat boots that would have been difficult to place if I'd done them first) I just used the first pair of flats as a template and put the inserts on the same spot of the insole as the ones in the first pair of flats are. It seems a little complex when written out, but it is honestly very simple when doing it.

I've put them in two pairs of boots and two pairs of flats, so far. I've used both the blue gels, one of the clear, and one of the tan fabric. I like the feel under my foot of the tan fabric one the most. They can slip a bit while wearing them (probably especially with it being summer) but they all work great for my needs and especially for the cost. I plan to keep some of these on hand from now on, for when I buy new shoes that need the support.

title: Very Small, Vibrates Handle More Than Face-Brush
text: This is very small, as to the part that washes your face and the vibration travels down the handle more than up to the face-brush. That wouldn't be so bad except that it takes so long to wash my face with this and it gets irritating to hold it because of the vibration. I've tried so many of these and this one just isn't usable except when turned off. That's ridiculous, so I'm giving it three stars for working as a non-electric unit, but it's not good as an electric, given all the options on the market. Good luck in your search.

title: Great Back Scrubber
text: This is another wonderful bath product that we've found is working very well. There used to be a lot more variation in quality, but with new level of competition out there, I'm finding that most products are really pretty good if not excellent. This is made of safe materials, so I found nothing wrong with it and nothing to concern me. It is also very easy to use and very easy to keep clean. In this case, we got a great back scrubber that rinses clean very very easily and is also pleasing on the skin. This back scrubber is wonderful and earned five stars through a couple of months of testing. Of course, I will update this review if we experience any kind of product failure, but so far I'm really happy with this. Good luck in your search.

title: Works Well Enough As A Backup, Not Great
text: This is a really nice little face washer for a person who needs a very gentle washer, but it doesn't do much exfoliating because the bristles are all very fine and soft. It is exactly as described and pictured and it is working very well so far. With this kind of item, it either matches the photos or it doesn't, and this one looks exactly like the photos, and then it either works or it doesn't, and this one works well enough, but the little balls under the surface don't really seem to do anything other than massage. I suppose they feel nice, but they don't increase the face washing ability of this, so I'm not really sure why they are there. More vibration settings are needed as well as some thicker bristles either on the other side of the unit or on the edge along the top or bottom of the main pad, to make this work better. The listing is accurate and we are satisfied with the performance of this item as a backup unit, but it isn't good enough to be the main one that I use or that anyone else is using. Power consumption is as stated and it is easy to use and easy to work with and we've had no problems with it after quite a while of use. We all basically reached the same conclusion that it needs a better design as to variation of bristles and then more vibration settings. It is very easy to hold, so that was good and that is why it gets four instead of three stars. Many are too hard to hold. This is easy to hold when it is wet and it doesn't become too slippery to keep in my hand. Good luck in your search.

title: Standard Wand Massager
text: This is a standard wand massager. It functions identically to nearly every one I've tried. It charges just like all the others, has about the same battery life, and has the same assortment of speeds. So on this one it really comes down to price. I say you should check the prices on the day you want to order and then order the cheapest of this style as they appear to all be the same. It works well, as you would expect, and is quieter than the old ones but not as quiet as people make it sound when they say "quiet". People can hear this if they are in the room. It's nowhere near silent. Still, it works well and sounds and functions exactly like most on the market right now. Good luck in your search. This is a worthy contender, if the price is right.

title: Tiny, For Kids, But Not Good Enough For Your Kids
text: This is very small, far too small for an adult, but it's also not very good. The cord to hang this in the shower is on the little loofah, making the loofah very uncomfortable to use. the other side is too small to use. It's sized for kids to early teens and is not good enough for anyone to use. This is a hard pass. Buy something else. Good luck in your search.

title: Excellent Telescoping Back Scratcher
text: This is a telescoping back scratcher. It is wonderful at what it does. The little metal finger-like protrusions on the hand-shaped end-piece, do an excellent job of scratching at all angles. The unit extends easily and retracts easily, but not so easing that it retracts while I'm using it. It is convenient to stand up in a pen-holder, alongside my pens, at my desk. I love it and it really does earn those five stars. Of course, with this type of metal design, you don't want to use it when wearing a knit sweater or anything made of delicate natural silk, but, for all other garments, it is as fabric-friendly as any I've found. Good luck finding what will work for your needs.

title: Works Just As Well As The More Expensive One, Excellent
text: This little hair dryer has turned out to be just as good as the name-brand model it replaced. It cost me half as much as the other, but, after months of use, I've found that it is doing a wonderful job, holding up very well, and seems to me to be just as good as the other. I highly recommend this item. It is a very good little dryer. Good luck finding what will work for your needs.

title: Thick, Comfortable & Get The Job Done
text: These gloves come in two varieties, the lined, which are a solid color, and the unlined, which are dual-tone, white with colorful fingertips. The lining on the lined version is exactly like the Mr. Clean gloves I've used for years. The unlined are exactly like the gloves I used to get many years ago from the same brand. Overall, given that Mr. Clean gloves have been my favorite for an exceptionally long time, these are equal to the task, equal in comfort and they get the job done equally well. With the lined version, if I am going to do something that will make me sweat a lot, it even has the same little flaw of a bit of the lining coming off on my hands, sort of like chalk, they are that similar. title: This is the top in quality for long chain bath sponges, among all I've tried.
text: The Niceshoes back loofah back scrubber, which is basically a long chain back sponge, is, for the record, the nice thick one you are looking for. These stretch enough to use comfortably for your back and everywhere else, but, thankfully, don't overstretch like so many brands that end up just hanging to the floor. These long, chain sponges are thickly packed (with a nice thick, closer weave netting / webbing having been used to make them) and are far superior to the cheap ones we've all bought and thrown away at some point. It is because of that thicker netting that these bounce back so well from stretching but are still such very effective back scrubbers. I highly recommend this product. I purchased from niceshoes and, after several months, I can say the product holds up and only needs to be thrown away and replaced due to germ concerns, not due to any failure of the product itself. Good luck finding what you need.

title: Great Product, Nice Alternative To Tins,
text:
Short version: These are great! What are you waiting for?

I am so happy Viter Energy created this as an alternative to the metal tins they sell. I love the tins but I also wanted some caffeine mints that I could easily carry around with me in my pocket or backpack, plus the tins can be a little loud when you're down to a few mints and it jingles, these are better for the office or a bag or purse so they don't make any noise. Also I tend to lose things easily so I have misplaced a few tins but with these if I lose a packet that's only 3 mints not a big deal. Plus if I ever don't want 3 mints at once I can always put the extra into one of my remaining tins, which now permanently stay in my cars and a few spots in the house. Having 3 mints in each packet also makes for a lot less packaging waste which is always good. I also like that they are 40mg. A lot of caffeine mints start at 60+ mg but sometimes I don't need that much, or if I do I would rather space them out which works great with the 40mg. I have read some reviews of the tins where people hate the taste but I think it's fine. You shouldn't expect it to taste just like a non-caffeinated mint but I have tried other brands that were so much worse. Maybe it's something about the Wintergreen flavor that really disguises the bitterness of the caffeine. This is a perfect offering in between the tins and the bulk bag. As far as effectiveness, these are definitely the same mints you get in the tins and all I can say is they work. In fact the few times I took them late in the day I stayed up way too late at night, so consider that a warning if you're not a regular coffee drinker. The box also tells you about the 2 founders and how the company came to be, how cool is that?! I can't really think of any complaints. One of the few products out there that does/is exactly what is claimed.

title: PVC hardens after a few weeks - supple when new, similar to latex, sizing correct
text:
Update - while the vinyl is still more durable and puncture resistant than latex, I'm going to have to ding this a solid 2 stars because of a couple of issues: 1) The PVC hardens after a few weeks, from exposure to grease or detergents, I don't know, but definitely not as supple. 2) The PVC is more slippery than latex. Still, we have had more than a few latex gloved ruined from goof-off or other solvents which the PVC is somewhat immune to, so there's definitely some advantages.

We used to use latex gloves for cleaning and dish washing, but they tend to be somewhat delicate, lasting only a week or 2, so we switched over to heavy nitrile gloves. These last far longer but the rubber is comparatively stiff and not nearly as comfortable as the latex. We also use "true blues" PVC gloves, but these are quite heavy vinyl so are really just for heavy cleaning tasks. When I first tried these on I was surprised as the feel was nearly identical to the latex gloves. Sizing is accurate.

If a toothbrush and toothpaste are a "10" in getting your teeth clean, these are perhaps a "6" However they have a huge advantage in being super easy to use - you could even use them while riding a bicycle!

They are textured fabric sleeves that fit over your finger. Since there are no bristles, they're not going to get stuff in between your teeth as a toothpick would. However, they're good at freshening your breath and getting "just brushed" feel to your teeth.

Also, they are soooo small. They come in a foil pouch and are very thin. You can keep a pair in your wallet and not even know they are there.

They're expensive enough I wouldn't use them everyday (I keep a toothbrush in my desk for daily use) but there are enough scenarios I could imagine them for - Freshen your breath and mouth just before important presentations, late night after clubbing, just before a date, after a meal on the road - times when you're not likely to have brought a toothbrush and toothpaste.

title: ❤️🖤💛💚Massage With Compression 💞 Great For Plantar Fasciitis💙🧡💜🤎
text:

The bottom massager is more pointy than smooth which for me, is the only sometimes negative aspect to this depending on how sensitive my feet are at the time. My husband who has Plantar Fasciitis loves the pointy bits.

The bottom rollers are big enough to cover the entire foot, including my husband's size 10 feet. Not all foot massagers are designed this way. Around the same time I ordered this, I also ordered a soft & plush foot rest style massager. It has massage rollers that are smaller, so it doesn't cover the entire foot but the rollers are smooth. No compression, but you can slide your feet into a little plush cave that is removable. That massager is about $100 less than this massager.

If I had to pick between the two, I'd pick this massager by Sharper Image. It is the best massager I've ever owned & I've owned quite a few over the years thanks to my husbands Plantar Fasciitis. This doesn't mean I don't love the other massager. I love them both. The other is more cozy time relaxing, this on the other hand while very relaxing, also offers much more therapeutic benefits. Even though massager means business, I will still fall into a light doze while using it.

This also has a heat function. It doesn't get very warm, but it is still nice; never too hot.

As advertised, you can flip this over for a vibrating foot rest. Personally, I really enjoy the versatility.

If you want something that looks nice, need some serious foot TLC, & can afford it, I see no reason why you wouldn't consider getting this. If you do want it & it's out of your price range (oh how I know that feeling I'm a full time Eco farmer), put it in your carts save for later & wait & hopefully a deal rolls around or you accumulate enough points on your amazon visa to get it free.

If this sounds like more massage action than you really need or want, you may want to check out the other foot massager I mentioned. Remember though, it doesn't cover the entire foot bed. I adjust my feet when I use it to get the rollers where I want them. Link: smile.amazon.com/dp/B09P4P3DB6

title: Fake
text:
Something is off about this essential oil (EO). First is the scent. I realize that our noses can be tricked, but the scent seems wrong to me. It is too strong & overly sweet or perfumy. Simply put, it smells fake.

There is an incredible amount of EO fraud online. Aside from my nose, there are a few other things about this EO that bug me:
1) No botanical name.
2) No Country Of Origin aka COO
3) No distillation method
4) No certifications

What they got right:
1) The bottle is amber glass with a standard screw cap. There is no euro/reducer top. A glass bulb dropper is included.

I ordered this to make my own milk soap. I've been making it for years using the cold process method. I usually buy 4 ounce bottles of EO's which gives me 4 batches of soap (when using one EO). I will not be using this brand. Brands I trust are NOW & Plant Therapy. Both have USDA Certified organic options. There are other brands as well, but those are the two that easily come to mind.

I'm not an EO expert, just a decades long user. I never use fragrances or perfumes. I have autoimmune disease & must be very careful about what I am exposed to. Should you buy this brand? I say "No" because there are other brands to choose from that seem much more on the up & up. But that is for you to decide.

title: Fake - "Vanilla"
text:
Fraud. This stuff is nothing but essential oil fraud. First off, there is no such thing as actual vanilla essential oil. 100% vanilla essential oil does not exist. Don't believe me? Research it & be enlightened. I thought this perhaps was an absolute. Upon arrival no information was on the boxes or the bottles. Another red flag for essential oil fraud which is incredibly common. A quality essential oil will provide the botanical name, extraction method, & country of origin (COO).

Without knowing any of the above, your nose would immediately alert you that this is fake. It smells nothing like vanilla. I work with whole, 100% pure organic vanilla beans every day. I can't even begin to describe what this fake garbage smells like. I assure you it's not vanilla.

Personally, I wouldn't order anything from this brand. If you want vanilla get an absolute or use the beans themselves. Unless you don't care & don't mind using whatever the heck this is. As a woman with endometriosis, avoiding toxins is high on my list of priorities. I want nothing to do with this.

title: No Scent
text: I don't use perfumes or fragrances. Instead I rely only on essential oils. Rose is one of mine & my husbands favorites, but it is rather costly. I cannot even smell a hint of rose in this roll on. I love the 2 ingredients & that it is USDA Certified Organic; that is part of why I ordered it. The other main reason is for the rose smell. Without the rose, I may as well just rub some organic MCT oil on me when I make my morning cuppa.

title: Ridiculously Narrow For Inserts, Make Great Cat Toys

title: I Like This Toothpaste BUT It Doesn't Treat Sensitivity As Advertised
text:
I ordered this because I'm currently using this brands whitening system & wanted a toothpaste that would help with sensitivity as well as remineralization. The thing is, it says nothing about desensitizing or hypersensitivity. I took off a star for that.

The title at the time of ordering & of my review:
"Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for Total Care | Prevents Cavities & Desensitizes Hypersensitivity | Vegan & Gluten-Free | Active Ingredients of Fluoride & Pentasodium Triphosphate"

I'm middle aged & have need to strengthen my enamel. I normally use Sensodyne for enamel repair. I like this toothpaste better than Sensodyne. I also use the generic "Act" remineralizing mouthwash at least twice a day. So far, I can't really say if any of it is actually helping.

Anyway, this toothpaste has a nice clean minty taste that isn't too strong & it doesn't have that crazy rabid dog foam. The price right now is about double what it was when I first looked at it. I'm not sure what the deal is there. I'd suggest keeping an eyeball on it & nab it when the price is a bit more realistic as it's not worth paying $10 for a 3.5oz tube of toothpaste.

title: I Don't Think These Are True Essential Oils
text:
I've been using essential oils (EO's) for nearly 2 decades. These EO's are highly suspect for several reasons. First, Peppermint is the first bottle I opened. It has a distinct acetone/alcohol undertone. Peppermint is pretty distinct with that strong sweet sharp crisp smell, this is weak & obviously doesn't smell correct if I think I'm sniffing a bottle of peppermint scented nail polish remover. Rosemary & Lemon smell okay, but Orange has almost no scent which is also odd as it's a pretty distinct scent. Okay, they are all rather distinct scents.

Now that I got the smell part out of the way, what about things like the COO (country of origin), distillation method, botanical name, where the product was manufactured etc.? None of that has been provided. Zip. Nada. Zero. It's pretty crazy considering the excessive amount of packaging used, yet on all that packaging they didn't list this relevant information? Most quality EO's will provide this type of info & they will typically smell like what they are supposed to smell like.

I guess for $7.50 at the time of my review (I didn't see a price when I ordered), I should have known. Who the heck gets 4 bottles of genuine unadulterated EO's for $1.88 each????

title: Pulls Threads
text: I really like the idea of a battery free/rechargeable free option for lint removal. While this does remove lint just fine, it also damages clothing. It catches in the threads & pulls them. The larger lint remover seems to do it much more so than the smaller one. It has pulled threads out of my yoga pants & my wool socks. My battery operated lint removers can cause damage as well. It is usually when the fabric isn't tight enough & a bit gets pulled into the blade head & it cuts a hole in the fabric. So far I'd say the battery operated lint removers cause far less damage. This seems faster & easier to use, but I'm not sure it's worth the risk on good clothing.

title: Seems Good
text:
I ordered this because my usual brand Pure Synergy Immune Health was out of stock. Immune Health is a supplement my husband takes daily as he is a upper manager in retail who works swing shifts & overnights. While this product seems okay, it doesn't provide full disclosure of ingredients like the Synergy brand. I expected more information to be on the packaging or the bottle. This doesn't arrive in a bottle, but in 6 blister pack sheets with 10 capsules per sheet. A product brochure is included in the box, but again, no additional info. about the ingredients, not even the type of capsule used. It does "guarantee 100% mushrooms" & that it is free from fillers, etc., so that should mean there are no other ingredients, however they should make it very clear as most supplements have a Other Ingredients section in the supplement facts. If this is truly 100% mushrooms, then under Other Ingredients it should say, "None". The brand also claims certified organic, but has no verification supporting this claim. I think a full disclosure of ingredients along with the verification seals to back up a products claims is a reasonable thing to expect from a supplement company. Even if that full disclosure simply means stating "none".

Regarding usage, it seems fine. However, I will be reordering Pure Synergy Immune Health when it's back in stock simply because it is a trusted brand. It really does seem to help the immune system stay healthy. Of course, you can always get sick no matter what you do. I run my own eco farm full time & one of the things I grow is elderberries. I harvest & dry these to make my own elderberry syrup which my husband also takes regularly along with the Immune Health. The Covid situation is the first time I've had to deal with the Pure Synergy Immune Health going out of stock on amazon (I subscribe & save to it). I've ordered other mushroom supplements for him several times when this happens. So far, they seem to have all been helpful. From what my husband & I can tell, this brand is no different then the others he's tried (not counting Synergy).

title: Palatable In Small Amounts
text:
I decided to take this because, you guessed it I'm stressed out beyond my wildest dreams. So far 2020 has been a rotten year & this is before Coronavirus stepped in. Since then, things for me have gotten progressively worse. Add to that I have Endometriosis. Ashwagandha is supposed to help with stress. So far, it's not working. My stress is bad.

I selected this brand for several reasons. It's supposed to be organic (however, it doesn't have the USDA Certified Organic seal), it's packaged in glass, it's not in capsule form & there are no fillers.

Directions say to use a teaspoon in whatever (smoothies, coffee, teas, tonics, milks, baking, etc). I decided to start with a 1/2 tsp. in my homemade mint hot cocoa. I could easily taste the Ashwagandha. It nearly ruined my cocoa. Even the copious amounts of mint I used weren't enough to disguise the taste. I decided to try again the following day but reduced it to 1/4 tsp. That worked.

I plan to keep taking this daily. I didn't expect instant results, so maybe it will help eventually. Time will tell.

title: Natural Lemon Toothpaste =D
text:
I really like this toothpaste. I've tried a heck of a lot of various natural toothpastes over the past 2 decades & thankfully have liked a heck of a lot of them. I decided to try this brands "The Freshest Mouth" Mild Spearmint & this Mojito "Healthy Teeth & Gum Care" toothpaste. Out of the two, I like this toothpaste much more. Don't get me wrong, I like the spearmint well enough, I just like this better.

Like many natural toothpastes, this doesn't have a ridiculous amount of foam. It doesn't feel abrasive at all. It also doesn't irritate the flesh inside of my mouth. I love the light lemony flavor as well.

If you like a strong flavored toothpaste you probably wont be happy with this. There are other natural brands that have a lot more essential oils. If you are looking for something mild, you are going to love this brand.

Overall, I am satisfied.

title: Great Stuff
text:
I've been taking collagen in my cuppa tea for nearly a decade. My go to brand is by Great Lakes in the green canister. The Cornucopia Institute did a test for heavy metals in collagen & all but two brands rated high (you can look it up for more info. it's always good to do your own research rather than blindly trust a review, LOL). I have seen such great results from taking collagen, that I don't plan to stop even knowing about the heavy metals. I also don't plan on not consuming organic cocoa or chocolate due to the heavy metals or rice (California organic rice rates the lowest).

Anyway, this collagen works exactly as expected. I hate the plastic container, but aside from that, it's fine. Flavorless, dissolves fine. I will even add it to hot cocoa, any hot beverage really. I use a hand held whisk/frother. It always turns out great.

The results I've enjoyed thanks to collagen are most noticeable to me in my hair. My hair is very long (past my bra) & straight. I get it cut once a year. I have hardly any splits. I am always complimented on my hair, told how beautiful it is. I see people stare at it. It's amazing. I'm middle aged! When I was half my age, my hair was constantly splitting & never beautiful. When I started eating better & organic, I did notice a big improvement, but the biggest & best improvement was once I started taking a little collagen powder in my hot cuppas every day.

Overall, I highly recommend collagen, this brand, or whatever brand you like - it works.

title: Drumstick Tree
text:
Morninga is a super healthy, nutrient loaded treat. If you like matcha tea &/or spinach, you'll probably love morninga. There are lots of ways to enjoy it, here are two of my favorites:

Yummy Latte:
1.5 C milk
1 tsp Moringa
1 tsp raw honey

Combine Moringa powder & maple syrup or honey in a mug just like you would for making matcha tea. If you want to use sugar cane, add a bit of milk or water to combine into a paste (again, just like matcha tea). Use a milk frother or a small saucepan to steam the milk until it bubbles. Add the milk to your mug and stir.

Nutritious Smoothie:
3/4 C water or milk
1 ripe banana broken up
2 large or 4 small leaves of kale or chard
1 tbsp your choice of nut butter
1 tbsp cacao powder
1 tsp moringa
1 date (optional) - if you want extra sweetness
1 C ice

Blend in a blender & enjoy!

title: Great For DIY Blends
text: I've pretty much stopped by green powder mixes/blends because they always have gums, stevia, &/or monk fruit.  Instead, I buy the ingredients I like & make up my own blends depending on what I want that day.  Some stuff I buy or grow fresh on my organic family farm depending on the time of year.  If there is enough surplus, I dry the extra greens, grind them into powder & store them in amber Ball mason jars in the freezer to use during the winter months.  I don't grow Noni fruit, so it is one of the items always on my buy list.  Noni powder doesn't add much in flavor, it's mostly for the health benefits.  You can mix it into just about any green juice or smoothie blend you like.  A really simple summer smoothie example is fresh peeled de-seeded cucumbers, fresh blueberries, noni powder, & coconut milk.  A super sweet ice cream like treat is frozen pineapple, frozen banana, coconut milk & noni powder.  I like to freeze it a bit & eat it when it's super hot out.  It's so refreshing & incredibly sweet.  For green blends spinach, kale, noni, blueberry, & maple syrup with vanilla whisked into cold water works for a quick nutritious pick me up.  The possibilities are endless.

title: I feel lucky
text:
I feel lucky to have found this series at all. Kudos to the publisher/distributor for keeping it alive. It's one of the best series ever written in the genre. A realistic (not falsely beautiful or endowed) young woman's journey without too much meanness, though she has a friend like that. Pretty realistic on that count too. The meanness isn't the main focus, the journey is, and it's a realistic journey with a lot to offer readers in terms of growing up sane and finding every part of yourself. Most relationship issues resolved, but also realistic there. There's some good horror and a lot of soul searching, a lot of tough romance. It's more about a girl finding her strengths and what calls to her . . . and going for it. Some good craft work included throughout the entire series.

Not as fond of the diary portions being chapter/book adjacent myself, synchronicity and all, but the info provided in the diary bits adds to the series overall--you can skip or skim the journaled "flashbacks" on the first read through (I did). When you want that much detail on every main character, you can go back and read the off rhythm diary entries.

Too bad it wasn't discovered by Hollywood/television, but the saga is sweeping and would require a lot of film locations. Just had to repurchase after giving first copy away to a young adult. Glad I could find this second copy at all, no less at a reasonable price. Thank you.

title: Type 3B/3C
text:
I have type 3B/C hair and thought that maybe this would help flatten my hair on blow-dry only weeks. Usually I flat iron, but I've been trying to give my hair a break from frying lately. I tested it on my normal heat setting (190C) and the hottest setting (230C) and neither worked well. I tried it with freshly blow dried hair and 2 day old blow dried hair. I tried small sections, pulling the hair taut against the sides of the bristle-plates; nope (plus the ends are left curly because they barely touched the plates).

The design of the iron is really high quality though. I was expecting something cheapy, but this really has a solid build and controls. It turned off on me and I didn't realize it; I don't care for the auto-shut off, I bet most curly girls don't. 45 minutes?! We're just getting halfway done lol.

One good point is that it didn't damage my hair. There is no way I'm trying it on air dried hair, it wouldn't do anything a blow dryer couldn't do. Overall, if there were some sort of clamping mechanism, it would be a much better item. Some sort of interlocking brush/hotplate combo would be amazing, and might even replace my flat iron! Until someone invents that, these brush straighteners are only for the straight-haired girls.

I've been using Oona for about a year now, and I endorse it to all of my friends!  (Maybe Oona should hire me for this!) The bag was not bubble wrapped, it was a tightly wrapped plastic bag taped closed (so much tape I had to cut it open) inside a bubble-pack envelope. The envelop was larger than the bag so it bounced around a bit during shipment. Nothing was broken, but as another reviewer stated, best to open these over a trash can. Lots of sparkly dust and little slivers.

I wiped each piece down with a damp sponge to remove the dust, and laid it out to dry. It's worth that little bit of effort to reveal the beautiful glow hidden under the dust!

title: Great pump for 32 ounce Hibiclens
text: This pump is a perfect fit for the 32 ounce Hibiclens bottle, and screws on top with no problem. Pump out the amount you need and was the germs away! It's definitely better than trying to pour out the soap. Do be aware, if you need a smaller amount, pump very gently and only part of the way down, because one pump gives you a LOT of product. The liquid squirts out pretty far-- I think this is just the nature of the Hibiclens and not the pump-- so cup your hand around the opening to avoid it squirting onto your arm. This is an inexpensive accessory that makes Hibiclens much easier and much more convenient to use-- and you can use it over and over each time you get a new bottle.

title: Trace minerals in a nearly tasteless solution

Well, I can’t say that my gut problems are entirely resolved. But I think this stuff is moving me in the right direction.

title: A wonderful red powder - high in antioxidants
text:
This lovely antioxidant blend contains pomegranate juice powder grape seed extract, tart cherry extract, blueberry powder, cranberry powder, raspberry powder and strawberry powder. Besides the fruit powders, this blend also includes superfoods such as açaí powder, turkey tail mushroom and cordyceps powder. It also includes a digestive blend which includes apple pectin, quinoa, buckwheat and chia seed powder. As a bonus, it also includes a probiotic blend. The manufacturer has wisely made sure that almost all the ingredients are organically sourced. It contains natural sugars and further sweetened with monk fruit extract.

My only gripe is that it already has 7 grams of sugar per scoop - personally, I don't understand why the manufacturer felt the necessity of adding the monk fruit (which doesn't really add much to sugar content,) to an already naturally sweet formula. I find it overly sweet and so have been using only 1/2 a scoop in my morning smoothie. Other than that, this is a great blend that I am really enjoying.

This maca which is light brown in color (there are also yellow and black macas) has a nice flavor and blends well in smoothies. I will absolutely buy again from this seller. Excellent product.

title: Good antioxidant and source of vitamin C

I found this on the web: “Camu camu is used for viral infections including herpes, cold sores, shingles, and the common cold. It is also used for eye conditions including cataracts and glaucoma. Other uses include treatment of asthma, “hardening of the arteries” (atherosclerosis), chronic fatigue syndrome, depression, gum disease (gingivitis), headaches, and osteoarthritis.”

Whether or not it treats any of these conditions, I do believe it’s a good natural source of vitamin C and bioflavonoids. It’s strong stuff, so go easy on it, otherwise your smoothie will be overly tangy.

title: Be Very Careful With This Herb
text:
Fadogia has been shown to raise testosterone levels significantly (at least in rat studies) and has been recommended by many for this purpose in humans. So, it likely will work in this regard, at least to a degree.

However, another study on rats found that fadogia in amounts similar to what is available in supplements caused damage in the testes, liver, and kidneys of rats, and there were signs of cell damage, including in lower doses that are more common in human supplement amounts.

I believe in supplements and take a lot of them, but I am also very careful with what I put in my body. The research on this herb is emerging and it is important to be very careful. I recommend caution. If you use it, I suggest a low dose (no more than one pill) and alternating use on-and-off.

title: Seems To Be Quality Inositol
text:
Inositol is a sugar alcohol once thought to be a B vitamin (it isn't actually a vitamin), but it does seem to have many benefits in the body. When I take it before bed, it really does help with sleep, and seems to also positively impact serotonin levels even into the next day.

It also may help with female fertility issues, and this product contains a ratio of two different types of inositol based on some studies related to that issue.

I took off a star, because while the description here does explain how to open the bottle lid and close it to keep the product fresh (I'm glad they made that clear), it doesn't mention anything about third-party testing, which I like to see when buying supplements. It does provide me with the sleep benefits of inositol, so it likely is pure.

title: Good Inositol Supplement
text:
Inositol is a sugar-alcohol and was once thought to be vitamin B8. However, it isn't actually a vitamin, but it is beneficial to the body, and is found along with choline in lecithin.

Inositol can help with sleep, mood, and may even with female fertility. This formula is of higher strength than others, but the pills are pretty big. It also includes some folic acid.

I take inositol before bed each night and it does seem to help me sleep longer, and stops me from waking up so much in the middle of the night.

I am taking off a star because I can't find references to third-party testing and the verbiage on their website is filled with spelling mistakes and grammar issues. While this doesn't necessarily indicate problems with the supplement, I like to see a company that seem fully reputable.

title: Good Source of Magnesium
text:
Magnesium is an important mineral, and many people are deficient in it. For this reason, magnesium can help with heart issues and even help with sleep. Some people even get relief from headaches or anxiety from taking it.

Magnesium comes in a variety of forms, and some are better absorbed and utilized by the body than others. Magnesium glycinate is one of the best forms, and the body seems to absorb more magnesium from this than other, cheaper forms (like magnesium oxide).

I have taken magnesium for many years and am healthier for it. I usually take it before bed as part of my nighttime supplements. The company seems to be quality and suggests that they are a supplier and as such, do their own testing and tracking.

title: Has A Lot Of Good Ingredients
text:
I use pre-workout formula before most workouts. I tend to look for a few things in a pre-workout, namely creatine, beta-alanine, and caffeine. These chemicals not only help me feel mental and physical energy, but also seem to have performance benefits. This formula contains all of these supplements.

It also has some other beneficial chemicals that I don't necessarily need in a pre-workout, but I like. These include betaine and taurine. I usually add taurine in my post-workout, but having it in a pre-workout is fine as well.

Some of the other ingredients may have various mental and physical benefits during a workout, including DMAE which can give me a mental lift.

So, I really like this pre-workout, and I have to say that it tastes pretty good. I recommend it!

title: Seems To Be A Good Astaxanthin Supplement
text:
I have taken astaxanthin for a few years, as an overall health supplement, but also specifically for skin health. It is indeed a powerful supplement, and one of the most potent carotenoids. It is derived from a type of algae, and is what makes both salmon and pink flamingos have their characteristic pink color.

This seems like good astaxanthin. The only reason I took off a star is I can't seem to find much about this company online. I like to check up on supplement companies to see what they are about in terms of history and quality control.

title: Decent Post Workout
text:
I like taking BCAAs and EAAs after a workout, to provide some protein replenishment after working out. Plus I like drinking something flavorful to hydrate myself.

This is an interesting formula. Not only does it contain essential amino acids, but it adds ashwagandha, and I'm not sure of the reason for that. Ashwagandha has a relaxing impact, but also may have a positive impact on testosterone, so I am not sure of the point of it.

Given my preferences for a post-workout, I add taurine powder to this.

The flavor is pretty decent, but I have very few standards with workout formulas, so I may not be the best person to ask on these things.

title: May Work But Is Pricey
text:
Based on some research, this supplement may work, over time, to increase mental stamina and clarity. The main ingredient is an extract of the cocoons of a type of moth! I am not going to lie, that is kind of wild, and I have taken almost every supplement under the sun. There is, however, some evidence it works. I personally haven't felt anything, but then again, I am already taking quite a few brain-enhancing supplements and my memory is already very sharp.

However, the price is really high, probably because we are dealing with something as time-consuming as collecting moth cocoons to get the main ingredient. If you want to give it a go, it may work, but the price is prohibitive in my opinion. Nonetheless, it's a pretty fascinating supplement.

title: Great Black Seed Oil
text:
Black cumin seed oil has a variety of benefits, and I have taken it for a little over a year. After taking it, I noticed a lot more drive and mental energy to get things done. This has been the best benefit of black seed oil for me. I take it regularly for a few weeks, and then take a few days off to make sure the effect doesn't go away.

This is an extract, which is standardized for the active ingredient, which explains why it is more expensive than other pills. It will, however, also be more effective than plain old black cumin seed oil, which doesn't have a set amount of the active ingredient guaranteed.

This is a good product, and the price is pretty good for the extract.

title: An Important Amino Acid
text:
I take taurine as part of my post-workout formula, in part because it helps balance out taking beta-alanine, which may deplete taurine (and beta-alanine is in my pre-workout).

But Taurine has its own benefits, including potentially protecting the heart, brain, and muscles. I also feel a good mental lift from taking taurine, and there is some evidence it can enhance athletic performance, which is why it is an ingredient in some pre-workout formulas.

I normally use taurine powder, but if you would prefer pills, this is a good option. However, in pill form, it ends up being much more expensive, gram for gram, than powder.

title: Potent Product From A Great Company
text:
I want to start by saying Liftmode is the real deal. They do extensive testing and are very transparent with their customers. If there is any company I trust to deliver a quality supplement, it is them.

This is a high potency icariin formula. It is 90% icariin which is a lot more concentrated than most horny goat weed supplements you'll ever find. And, you definitely pay for the potency! This is one expensive supplement. It may have an impact on testosterone levels and drive, although there isn't a lot of solid evidence confirming this. It may be worth a try if you are experiencing "manly" issues.

I personally haven't really felt anything from it, but my testosterone levels are just fine and I lift weights and exercise 5-6 times a week.

title: Two Nootropics In One Formula
text:
This formula contains two nootropic agents, i.e. chemicals that might have cognitive benefits. Both of them give me vivid dreams when taken at night, and I notice a subtle mental lift from both of them. Alpha-GPC is a form of choline that allows for the production of acetylcholine in the brain (be aware that too much acetylcholine can potentially cause depressive thoughts, so don't overdo it).

When taking this product, I do notice that lift. However, I am not sure if it's real or just a placebo effect.

Why? The price on this is really good for these two chemicals, since both are rather expensive. That concerns me a little, since if it's too good to be true, it might be the case! I will give them the benefit of the doubt, especially since the label says there is "third party testing." So if you want these two chemicals for a good price, give this a try.

title: Pretty Much Everything I Look For
text:
When I get a pre-workout, I like it to have creatine, beta-alanine, and caffeine. These are three elements that make me feel "ready to go" in terms of working out. The addition of glutamine, taurine, and citrulline is also cool, since I often put those in my "mid-workout" which I take partway through the workout when I do cardio and lift.

So this formula pretty much takes care of everything I need. The only thing I noticed is that the caffeine content is pretty high, and since I'm a big coffee drinker, it's just worth noting that your daily caffeine content can really shoot up if you combine this with coffee and aren't sensitized.

The taste is pretty good too. I look forward to it.

title: Potent Type Of Ginseng
text:
Ginseng may have a variety of benefits, including providing a feeling of increased energy and perhaps even helping with certain "male issues." I have taken it off and on since high school, and it seems to make me feel better when I took it even back then.

Ginseng is often rather expensive, and there are other ways to get many of the benefits of ginseng that are much cheaper options. However, ginseng is nonetheless a very renowned herb and known (at least in traditional medicine) to have a lot of supposed benefits.

This brand uses mature ginseng (so it has more time to develop nutrients) and also does extensive testing, which is always a good thing when considering which brand to go with.

title: Powerful Amino Acid
text:
N-acetyl cysteine has some potential lung and liver health benefits, and I have taken it fairly regularly for almost 10 years. Since it may raise glutathione levels in the body, it could potentially reverse the graying of hair as well, at least in theory.

NAC is best taken on an empty stomach, since it is an amino acid. And, I suggest not taking it before exercise, since it has antioxidant activity, and too much antioxidant activity during exercise can actually negate the benefits of exercise (you want some bodily stress to happen).

My main issue with this is the price. It's more expensive (as of now at least) than most other brands of NAC I have ever bought.

title: Comprehensive Formula
text:
This is a good formula that combines Vitamin D3 with multiple forms of Vitamin K.

Typically, Vitamin D and K2 are paired together, since both are important for bone health and calcium regulation in the body (to make sure calcium ends up in the bones and not inside your arteries).

However, this formula also contains K1, which helps with blood clotting. So, if you are on blood thinners, K1 might impact this. Nonetheless, K1 is still an essential nutrient and is present in green, leafy vegetables, so the amount here will not impact those who aren't on blood thinners as a life-saving necessity.

Be sure to take this pill with some type of fat or with a meal since both vitamins are fat-soluble. Also, this formula contains black pepper extract, which may increase the absorption of both vitamins. Be aware that black pepper extract can interact with certain drugs.

title: Good Eye Health Supplement
text:
This is a decent eye health supplement that is high in lutein, and reasonable in its zeaxanthin content (typically there is a lot less zeaxanthin than lutein when they are paired together in nature).

Both carotenoids are present in the eye and supplementing with lutein can help with overall eye health and possibly prevent certain eye diseases. There is a very little bit of bilberry extract in this, but not enough to do much.

The price is a little high for a lutein supplement, but it's not too bad. Overall, this is a good eye health formula. I recommend it, especially if you don't eat a lot of foods high in lutein (like kale).

title: Solid Post-Workout
text:
This is a good post-workout (or, for me, often a mid-workout formula). It contains branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) that are vegan, which isn't a big concern for me, but if you are concerned about that, then that's a plus. It also contains glutamine, and all the essential amino acids. Adding EAAs not only has been shown to help build muscle mass, but can help vegans get a more balanced amino acid profile.

The flavor is really good too! Even though I'm not vegan, this is a formula that anyone can appreciate and use.

title: Highly Absorbable Q10
text:
Co-Enzyme Q10 is an anti-aging nutrient I have taken for many years. It has been shown to help with heart health issues and other health concerns.

This formula contains co-enzyme Q10 paired with lecithin, which has been shown to help its absorption and utilization by the body. As such, it is a better way to get co-enzyme Q10, which can be difficult for the body to absorb and utilize. Note that this is not the ubiquinol form of Q10, which is ultimately the best-absorbed, but which is also very expensive.

So far, I have been very satisfied with this brand. I recommend this if you want a good form of Q10.

title: Good Plant-Based Protein Powder
text:
This is a decent plant-protein formula that tastes great and is fairly low in carbs, which is the main thing I look for in a protein powder, since I am on a low carb diet and stick to it.

I just mix it with a few tablespoons of half-and-half (yes I know this makes it non-vegan, so this could easily be duplicated by using some plant-based milk) and create a pudding-like mix. It is a high-protein, lower carb dessert for me.

My main issue with this is that I don't like consuming sugar if I don't have to, and from what I can tell this is sweetened with brown rice syrup and maltodextrin. While, yes, brown rice sugar is more natural than refined sugar, and it isn't high in fructose, it is still basically a fancy source of sugar. Overall, however, this is a good powder that is still relatively low in carbs.

title: A Powerful Nutrient For Your Liver And More
text:
Tudca, aka Tauroursodeoxycholic acid, is basically a water-soluble bile salt, which means it emulsifies fats (breaks them down into smaller units so lipase can work on them more effectively). So, it can help with fat digestion, especially for those with gall bladder issues, but it also has many other benefits.

Where Tudca shines is that because it is water-soluble, it can clean out the bile salts that can get backed up in the liver, which causes liver problems. It has also been shown to have anti-aging properties because it apparently can protect the endoplasmic reticulum of all cells, and thus have positive implications in preventing diabetes and even neurological diseases.

While I know that Staunch Labs produces workout-related supplements, the evidence that Tudca can help with muscle building is very slim, but some bodybuilders swear by it. I personally am not sure.

title: A Green Superfood
text:
Chlorella is an algae "super-food" and rich in all kinds of vitamins, minerals, and other nutrients. If you are looking for something "green" to take for overall health, this is a great option.

This brand seems good and the price is pretty reasonable for pills. It is much cheaper if you buy it in bulk and mix it with water, but that also tastes pretty bad. So, if you need chlorella pills, I recommend this.

title: A Good Probiotics Formula
text:
This is a good probiotic formula that contains probiotics (good bacteria), prebiotics (food for the good bacteria), and post-biotics (products produced by good bacteria). This makes this formula kind of unique, in that the inclusion of post-biotics is a new thing. To some degree, this may be a novelty, but there is some research that shows that for people who really can't tolerate probiotics, post-biotics may have benefits.

This is a solid formula in this regard, although the number of units (4 billion per pill) is a little low compared to other formulas, some of which go into the 10-50 billion. However, this range of CFUs is about right for the price.

title: My Daughter Likes Them
text:
This is a good probiotic for kids. It tastes good and what's important for me is that it includes a hefty dose of probiotics, at least for a chewable tablet: 5 billion CFU.

The formula also includes inulin, which is a good prebiotic, i.e. food for the good bacteria. I look for this when buying a probiotic.

For my 8-year old daughter, the real issue is taste, and she really does like the taste of this, so this product is a winner by my definition.

title: Seems To Be A Quality Mushroom Supplement
text:
This is a good mushroom blend that contains extracts of the fruiting body of various medicinal mushrooms. Lion's mane in particular may have nootropic benefits, and I have taken it at various times for that benefit.

That the company claims to third-party test is good because a lot of mushroom supplements don't contain a lot of the fruiting body and therefore are pretty worthless.

Finding information about this company was challenging since apparently "Nature's Nutrition" is the name of multiple companies. Their website is pretty boilerplate without going into many details about them, or how they test.

title: A Powerful Anti-Inflammation Supplement
text:
I have been a very active person since high school, and took up regularly running and working out when I was in my early 20s in the early 2000s. Since then, I have consistently run and lifted. Right now, I pretty much use the Stairmaster 4-5 times a week (burning about 700-1000 calories each time) and lifting 3 times a week. In the summer months, I run 50-75 miles a month.

I'm not saying this to brag, but to mention that I put my body through a lot, and at 41 I have no major (or minor) joint issue. I attribute this to a variety of things, including taking glucosamine and other supplements since my early 20s.

This formula is high in glucosamine sulfate (the sulfate form is more expensive but superior to glucosamine HCL) and also includes quite a few other major anti-inflammatory herbs and chemicals. It has standardized boswellia and turmeric, which will help with inflammation issues. I take both of these regularly.

The price is kind of high, but there are a lot of expensive ingredients in here.

title: High Potency, Time Release Probiotic
text:
I regularly take probiotics because of a lot of promising research that is coming out related to gut bacteria having a lot of benefits, digestive and even beyond.

This seems to be a really good product, with 11 billion CFUs of probiotics, and a guaranteed 4 billion by the expiration date. It has multiple strains and is timed release, probably to release them into the gut and avoid destruction in the stomach.

This "11 billion" amount was kind of confusing for me at first, since the label says "4 billion." However, if you look at the bottom of the back side, below the label, it explains it has 11 billion at the time of manufacture. It is kind of cool that they guarantee 4 billion until expiration. Most companies aren't that transparent.

title: Powerful Formula For A High Price
text:
This is a powerful formula for joint pain or other inflammatory problems. It contains a variety of ingredients that have been shown to positively impact joint health.

I like to take certain supplements to preventatively address joint issues, since at age 41, I work out and lift weights almost daily, and run anywhere from 70-100 miles a month in warmer weather. So far, I have avoided any joint issues, thanks in part to supplements like glucosamine sulfate, MSM, and some of the ones in this formula.

I like that it contains a form of turmeric that is readily absorbed and utilized. If you look up the research behind Turmipure gold, you'll see that it is absorbed a lot better compared to regular turmeric extract that is 95% Curcumin. I am guessing this is because it is complexed with lecithin, which should also help the other ingredients absorb better.

The inclusion of astaxanthin is good as well, and I take it regularly as an overall anti-aging supplement, as well as for skin health.

The main drawback I see is the price. It is pretty high, even if you were to buy the various ingredients separately.

title: A More Bioavailable Form Of Co-Enzyme Q10
text:
Co-enzyme Q10 has been shown to have multiple benefits, and I have taken it for many years as a general anti-aging supplement. This supplement is labeled ubidecarenone, which is basically a synonym for ubiquinone, the more common name for co-enzyme Q10. I admit I have never seen that chemical name used, so I had to look it up.

This is co-enzyme Q10 that is supposed to be absorbed better. I'm guessing this is because it is mixed with lecithin, which has been shown to enhance the absorption of co-enzyme Q10 and a variety of other chemicals. Since co-enzyme Q10 can often be challenging to absorb, this seems like a good formula.

title: Great Mask For The Price
text:
It may not be manly to admit, but I wear a sleep mask. I am pretty sensitive to light, and when I wear a mask, I sleep a lot better than if I don't wear one, especially in the morning hours. Research shows darkness is extremely helpful in promoting sleep and overall health (one study found sleeping with a street light outside raised cancer rates).

This mask is pretty standard. It's comfortable and covers most of my field of vision. It does the job pretty well for an amazing price when compared to some of the others I have purchased in the past.

So, if you want a nice mask that is comfortable and inexpensive, this is definitely a great option.

title: Beet Root Powder For A Good Price
text:
Beet root powder may have some health benefits, mainly due to the high nitrate content of beets. This gets converted into nitric oxide in the body, which dilates blood vessels, increasing blood flow. This may not only lower blood pressure, but also enhance exercise and athletic related activities.

Beet root is also rich in betaine, also known as trimethylglycine (TMG). It has been shown to have a variety of health benefits, including possibly helping with weight loss and muscle gain. I have taken it for years.

This powder seems highly concentrated and doesn't taste too bad; it has a kind of sweet and earthy taste, but I wouldn't call it amazing. It is worth trying before exercise, or just supplemented with a meal (I have put it in vegetable smoothies).

I haven't noticed any particular benefits from it, like increased endurance, but I also lift regularly and use other forms of pre-workout, so it might be hard for me to see a benefit.

So, if you're looking for beet root powder for a good price, check this out.

title: Good Probiotics
text: This is a decent probiotic formula, with over 5 billion organisms, and a mix of proven strains. The price is definitely reasonable for what you get. 5 billion is a pretty typical amount for this price range and should have an impact. If you have digestive tract issues or immune issues, this formula is likely to help. Pair it with some prebiotic product (such as inulin fiber or pectin, contained in apples) and you'll see even better results.

title: Good Vinegar Formula With Some Extras
text:
This is an apple cider vinegar formula with some extras that may slightly help you lose weight. For example, it contains lecithin, kelp, and apple pectin. Lecithin and apple pectin may help you digest fats better, theoretically ensuring that fat is used properly. Kelp contains iodine, which might positively impact metabolism if you have a deficiency.

I mainly like vinegar for the acetic acid content, which may have a positive impact on longevity. Unfortunately, this formula doesn't list the percent of acetic acid in the vinegar.

The main reason I knocked off a star is that the vinegar dose isn't as high because of the added extras.

title: Good Formula, But Label Online Is Inaccurate
text:
The label shown on the amazon page (as of 5/6/19) is double the dose that is on the actual bottle. It would take two pills to achieve the dose listed as one capsule on the amazon page scan of the label.

Otherwise, the formula is all right. It does have ingredients that will likely benefit eye health (like zinc, taurine, and lutein). The formula isn't balanced the way I would like. I would prefer more lutein, and less beta-carotene.

Also, be sure to take this formula with some fat or food, or else the lutein won't absorb, since it's fat soluble.

title: Good Joint Formula
text:
This isn't really a "yoga" formula per se, and more of a joint and mobility formula that may help keep your joints feeling good. It contains very small amounts of a few vitamins and minerals. The main ingredients are the "proprietary blend" which contains glucosamine sulfate (which is the good form of glucosamine - avoid the HCL version), MSM, and Chrondroitin and a few other nutrients that may help ease pain and strengthen joints. I have been taking many of these ingredients for years and it could be the reason at 40 I still am able to run 80+ miles a month pain free.

I am not a huge fan of these "blends." Just tell us how much of each ingredient is in there. I take glucosamine and MSM regularly and it would be nice to know! Also, it's hard to find out anything about this company. A lot of these supplement companies start up and are basically importers of Chinese ingredients (not bad per se, since most raw materials are made there these days). However, it would be nice to know more about the company.

So, overall 4 stars, and not 5 for the reasons I listed above.

title: Excellent protein for those who dont like thick shakes
text:
Well i have to say that Syntrax Nectar is a very unique protein for anyone who has been around the block. they are some of the best tasting (and unique) flavors around. It is a 100% Whey isolate with 0 carbs and 0 fat. It is fruit juice flavored (and some others) and very thin. It is the consistency of gatorade which is a plus because i like to sip it intra workout and its not heavy at all. 

The value is pretty good considering its an isolate, but i usually buy concentrate which is cheaper. I can deal with the lactose but if you cant this is lactose free.
Its around 25 dollars for 36 scoops at 34 grams of protein each so its not bad at all for an isolate

As for flavors, all of them are really good, I made all of them with 8 oz of water and some ice cubes. They taste like what they say they will and dont have a diet aftertaste which is nice. They do foam alot if you shake them but about 5 minutes of settling and they are fine. i have tried 13 flavors because of a variety pack i bought and here are my ratings.

Apple Ecstasy: 10/10, tasted just like a green apple air head. not very sour but nice and sweet. 

Caribbean Cooler: 7/10. This was good but i just dont like coconut. It tastes like a pina coolada which im not a huge fan of.

Crystal Sky: 7/10 I thought this would be the best, it is like a tropical punch but its very heavy on the pineapple and i thought it was too tangy. 

Fuzzy Navel: 9/10 This was a peach orange blend that tasted alot like tang with a little peach in it. it was very good 

Lemon Tea: 8/10 I thought this would be gross but it actually tasted like lemon tea. for anyone who likes arnold palmer it comes very close to that.

Pink Grapefruit: 9/10 It tastes just like what you would think, it was very good and very refreshing

Roadside Lemonade: 7/10 This did not taste like lemonade! it tasted like lemon meraunge(?) pie, but it was good if you dont think about it as lemonade

Strawberry Kiwi: 10/10 this was one of my favorites. it was mostly strawberry but it was still really good

Twisted Cherry: 7/10 This was good if you like cherry, it was a little artificial tasting but im not a huge cherry guy.

Cappuccino: 10/10 WOW this was really good. it tasted just like a dunkin donuts frappaccino. 

Chocolate truffle: 7/10 It was an average chocolate, a little too sweet for my taste

Vanilla Torte: 10/10 Second best Vanilla ever, to Muscle Milk but at 1/3 the calories. Amazing

Strawberry truffle: 8/10 it was a good creamy, sweet strawberry. tasted like strawberry shortcakes

All in all this is an awesome isolate for the price, and the unique flavors are all really good. i would recommend to anyone.

 Pros: 

Low Carbs/fat

Tastes Great

Decent Change To The Norm

Cons: Not That Cheap Compared To Others

title: Works well, easy to use
text:
I groom my dogs myself, and the feet is always the hardest part. I saw an advertisement for this, or something similar on Facebook ? and thought, hmm 🤔 that might make the feet part WAY easier.

So, I purchased off Amazon for the fast shipping, free returns etc. It arrived quickly, un-damaged and I let it sit for a bit. It’s not really grooming time yet anyways.

So this week I got the flu and during a brief period of wellness that allowed me sit on the couch instead of in bed, I decided to test it out. I was exhausted so I did the rear feet one day and front feet the next which my dog was fine with. She HATES getting her feet groomed.

It went really well. The tool works as described as you can see in the photos. It was a lot easier than my large clipper, safer and beats resorting to scissors which I usually do. Best part is my dog tolerated it quite well. She wasn’t thrilled, but there was minimal pulling away. It helped I think that the lowest speed was more than enough to do the job. It is quieter and perhaps has less vibration which I assume is what my dog is afraid of.

All in all, I am quite satisfied with the purchase and would definitely recommend. I can’t speak to longevity as it is a fresh purchase. I would guess it holds up well with time and I can always update if it breaks. Mine came pre-charged which was nice. I see many future grooming sessions with happy dogs and hopefully no foot related trembling from the pups.

The woman I talked to was very nice and explained that it must of been a bad batch of the product or that somehow it was damaged in shipping. I appreciate their customer service and would order another product from them, just not this specific product due to the citrus oils staining my brand new yoga mat. title: Great Deal On A Great Vitamin Combo
text:
If I could only supplement with two vitamins, they would be D3 and K2. D3 is so important for so many body functions, and is hard to get in the diet. It is lauded for immunity support and strong bones. The problem with D3 supplementation is the potential for the increased calcium absorption to end up as bone spurs, calcium deposits in blood vessels, and calcification in soft tissues. K2 is absolutely essential to take in tandem with D3 to ensure your not doing more harm than good. K2 will assist in placing calcium where it belongs in teeth and bone, and not in soft tissues.

I love this product not only for combining D3 with K2, but also including bioperine. Bioperine helps the body absorb certain things such as turmeric. While I'm not aware of its possible assistance in absorbing vitamins, I do use it every time I take turmeric, beet root, or other herbs. This product saves me money by combining three things I deem essential for my supplement regimen. Thus, it makes this product about one third the price as all these supplements combined.

I took these probiotics with me on vacation because it seems my body always gets thrown out of whack when I travel. I started them a couple weeks prior, though. I wanted to see if I could feel their effects that early. The first day I took them I actually felt my sinuses moving-like clearing! I think I may have been fighting off a cold or was having sinus troubles but I never actually got sick or any kind of sinus infection so...maybe the probiotics kept me from actually getting worse (?)...I don't really know but I am assuming they helped!

Vacation went fabulously and I feel the probiotics were a big part of that! I'm going to continue to take these beyond just for vacation, while I'm continuing to educate myself and healing this gut of mine! I'm seriously feeling REALLY GOOD and it's a consistent kind of good!

I'll have to do an "update" at some point though, as I've had a weird skin issue that could have come from my previous intakes of high carbs so....(eek) maybe probiotics and whole organic foods will be the KEY to healing!!!

My biggest advice (that I would also give to a best friend) is to always educate the self, pay attention to what OUR individual bodies respond best to, and maybe give these probiotics a try!

5 stars because I still feel these probiotics working on my sinuses and because I've been feeling constantly good physically, mentally and emotionally!

title: So far, very good
text:
I bought these because I had a HUGE bag of wonderful tasting heirloom garlic cloves that I couldn't possibly get through. So, I minced and froze them into very small ice cubes. I keep these in the freezer - it's fast and convenient and the flavor is good, even frozen.

When I removed the garlic from the ice cube tray, the tray reeked - I still haven't gotten the smell out of that. Now, the garlic small has easily seeped out of the plastic baggie and is permeating all the other frozen food. I didn't want garlic flavored ice cream! I moved the garlic as far away from sensitive items as I could, but it was still a problem.

I put the garlic in these bags a few weeks ago. I pulled out a bag of it yesterday and smelled - I couldn't smell anything. I was wondering if I might also use them to store nuts - if it keeps smells in, it might keep smells out, too. Nuts often pick up off smells along with garlic or onion smells.

My only criticism is that these are pretty small. These are smaller than a small sandwich baggie, I'm pretty sure. I had to use 3 or 4 of these just for the garlic. I just looked up the size of a sandwich baggie -it's 6.5 by 5.5. These are 5 x 6. While that doesn't seem that much smaller, coupled with the fact that they don't have a pleated bottom and that the material is very sturdy/firm, these just don't have the same amount of space I would have preferred.

UPDATE......
Finally someone answers!
Apparently what I thought was an expiration date is indeed a "Manufactured Date"...This is the response I was given. And Thank you.

"There is no "expiration date" on the Bonita V product. There is a "lot #" and a "MFD". MFD stands for Manufactured Date. Our Bonita V has Lot #609055 MFG: 01/17 (which means they are best used by 01/19) or later.

Many companies in the natural products industry have made the switch from printing "Best Before", "Best Used By" or "Expiration Date" on bottles of vitamins and supplements to printing "Manufacture" dates (MFG). The change was made in order to keep in compliance with the regulations set forth in the FDA’s Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP). The Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the agency that oversees the manufacture and labeling of dietary supplements, does not require an expiration date on dietary..."

title: Not actually worth it
text:
I had not brushed regularly in so long, and definitely didn't floss. Seemed I always had bleeding gums, and bad breath no matter what I did, and it was discouraging. I recalled years ago using a tool exactly like this with more success with regards to frequency of use, so I purchased it.

Yes, it is reusable and self contained, which I like a lot, and fits much better in the mouth than some of the other reusable ones. But there are a few downsides. For starters, it's made of plastic, and unless one feels like raveling which ever floss one prefers using (assuming one didn't want, or couldn't get the refill kind made for it), one doesn't have too many options. Next, it has to be wound pretty tightly, or else it pops off the fork prong thingies, and even then it could do that anyway. But tightly wound means it doesn't curve around the tooth as much, if at all, cleaning less surface area as just using ones fingers to hold the floss.

The biggest problem I had with this, was with the floss itself. One day, it caught between my back teeth and frayed. Thin filaments were stuck between my teeth, and I couldn't get it out. While driving it somehow dislogged, and got stuck at the top of my throat, back of the tongue - I had to pull over because it was making me gag, and I had to throw up trying to get it out... sorry about that. From then on, I decided to quickly find natural floss, as if I am going to swallow bits of string, I'd rather it not be plastic. Well, turns out virtually all floss found in stores is made from synthetic fiber... even the vegan kind. And a quick search on amazon will get you silk floss... sounds fancy until you remember that the silk worms don't survive the process. Thankfully, natural fibers for floss, that doesn't kill animals, is out there, so I tried it out, and somehow it's thicker, than this floss here, but doesn't get stuck between my teeth! Makes no sense!

Finally, I got a proper cleaning from the dentist, started brushing and flossing after each meal, took turmeric for inflammation (turns out I had gingivitis, ew), and an alcohol-free herbal mouth wash, and within a week my mouth was clean again all the time!! I finally felt effective, and decided to just use my fingers to hold the floss, like a big girl, and just like that I'm flossing all the time, without this gimmick!

text:
This product is well thought out and can be effective. I particularly like the high content and form of magnesium this product uses. The only issue I have is with the price. If you purchase the 10 night option, that is $5.00 a night for a potential night of sleep. That alone is enough to keep you awake. Don't get me wrong, a good night of sleep is worth that to me, but just knowing that I am dealing with a company that would use such an obscene markup just ruins it for me.

Nutrition is my business. I learned a long time ago to beware of companies that will only allow you to purchase a product from the by subscription, without giving you the opportunity to try it first. You can make a one time purchase on Amazon.

Also, beware of companies that will give you pat answers like, "We want you to take the product for an extended period of time because our product has a cumulative effect, and works better over time." That may be, but really they just want you on the hook for $100.00 a month.

Unless you are Elvis and have a ton of money to blow on a good night of sleep, I would steer clear. The pretense of taking the high road is obvious here. This is an incredibly overpriced product. I would love to know how much it actually costs to manufacture one 30 night supply of this.

* Hand strap doesn't apply pressure in the right place to limit hand/wrist movement.
* The way the metal brace is sewn into the wrist doesn't seem that it's going to last long.
* Length is too short to restrict wrist movement
* Straps on the inside of the wrist get in the way and snag your clothing, it would've been better if the straps were fastened to the top side of your hand
* Thumb hole opening is too small so it puts pressure on web area between your thumb and index finger. It should've had a larger opening closer to your wrist to accomodate your thumb joint rather than applying pressure to the joint itself

title: This works great!
text: I have a full growth pattern of hair but I still like a buzzed head. I went to a high end barber a few times and got a straight razor shave, but my hair returned so quickly my nice shiny bald head was gone in no time. I have so many little speed bumps on my scalp that I’d bleed profusely if shaved it myself with one of my Gillet face razor. Therefore I’ve been using my 00000 blade on my electric hair trimmer to get it as short as I can. It’s messy and a pain to clean up. THEN, an add for a competing brand of this razor showed up in my Instagram feed. I immediately went to my Amazon app and reviewed all of them. Reading mixed reviews about effectiveness and durability, I bought the cheapest one ($29.99) with the highest rating. I’ve only used it a few times so I can’t comment on durability. But, the first time I dry shaved. I didn’t want to test the “waterproof” claim but it worked well. The next time I jumped in the shower with it using plain water. It cut a bit closer. Tonight I thought I’d try it in the shower with my beard shaving soap and see if it got gooped up and didn’t work well. It worked fabulously. After a few laps around my head I’d simply hold it up to he shower head to blast it clean.  No matter the method, you do have to go back and forth and round and round to get your whole head nice and smooth. Other than that, this thing is fabulous. It rinses clean easily and charges quickly. I have a goatee without a mustache and it does a poor job of shaving my upper lip and nostril area so I just clean that up with my shave razor.  Anyhow, I am super pleased as this makes a previously nasty job to a painless and clean one.

And it occurs to me that if the tablet is on a stand, you can just turn it around so that the speaker faces you, making an amplifier unnecessary.

A stronger magnet would work better, as would a deeper undercut to allow you to rest it over a cover of some kind. (Don't most people have some sort of protective cover on their highly expensive tablets? Just wondering.)

You will actually get a better magnification of sound coming out of your speaker if you cup your hand behind it, than you do from this little plastic gizmo. No kidding. Try it.

A much more sensible choice would be a good set of earbuds.
