title: Super Effective At Getting Rid Of Buildup And Restoring My Hair Though The Fragrance Is So Strong It May Be A Put Off
text:
My dry hair has been misbehaving lately- it looks dull, feels rough and is unmanageable. I wash and condition every day using hard water and use at least three styling products daily. I’m scheduled to get my hair colored in five days and figured my hair looks lousy because my hair needs coloring and perhaps because I’ve tried a number of different shampoos lately instead of sticking with my usual products. As it turns out, however, I simply needed a good clarifying shampoo.

A clarifying shampoo is used to get rid of build up from hair products, minerals from hard water, chlorine, pool chemicals, oils, etc. This Organic Doctor charcoal clarifying shampoo is black, thick and has a strong scent. This shampoo has an emphasis on organic and natural ingredients and looks better than a lot of shampoos as it doesn’t have many common chemicals (e.g., SLS, phalates and parabens), but it does appear to still contain some chemicals such as fragrance. The scent smells heavy and masculine to me and I’m not crazy about it, but surprisingly my hair smells good after it’s rinsed and dried. And the strong scent doesn’t trigger my allergies or cause any irritation.

The first application didn’t lather much, but the second one created generous lather that I massaged through my hair and rinsed easily. My hair looks restored as it’s shiny and manageable again. It feels and looks healthy, and my color looks good. I had no idea my issues were due to the build up of things like minerals and hair care products. I’ll gladly endure the smell and use this once or twice a month to clarify (more often may affect my color) and swimmers and some others may benefit from using this more often. 4 stars.

title: High Quality Antioxidant Supplement That May Aid Digestion And Provide Other Benefits And Also Gives Me No Adverse Side Effects
text:
We steam globe artichokes once or twice a week, and I love them as they are low in calories and high in antioxidants and nutrients. They also really agree with my stomach and seem to aid my digestion. But they aren't the most convenient food to eat daily, so I decided to give Nature's Bounty Artichoke supplement a try as artichokes are known for being antioxidant rich and for being good for digestion. The dose is one capsule once or twice a day, preferably with a meal. I take a number of supplements, so I'm taking just one a day. I find these capsules digest easily, and I've had no allergic reaction or adverse effects. I don't get any burp-up icky taste like I get with some vitamins and supplements.

The bottle contains 100 capsules (3-month supply for me) each with 350 mg of Artichoke Extract (standardized to contain 2.2 % Cynarin, 7.7 mg). The capsules also contains rice flour, gelatin and less than 2% Silica and Vegetable Magnesium Stearate. This product is free of milk, lactose, soy, wheat, sugar, fish, sodium, yeast, gluten and preservatives, and have no artificial color, flavor or sweetener. I've read that the Cynarin in artichokes has lots of possible beneficial properties. Nature's Bounty states these Artichoke capsules support antioxidant health, which I believe based on the properties of fresh artichokes. WEB MD also says Cynarin MAY reduce heartburn, nausea, vomiting, gas and even lower cholesterol. But I've read it takes weeks or even months to get the full benefit, so I can't really evaluate these possibilities yet. But I do believe at a minimum taking these supplements provides antioxidants, and I wouldn't be surprised if this product also aids in digestion.

I've read people with ragweed and other plants allergies can be allergic to Cynarin (though I've had no reaction and have those allergies). Also, this supplement may not be suitable for people with bile duct obstruction or gallstones. So it's best to read-up and check with your doctor before taking this or any supplement. I found Web MD to be a good source of information on Cynarin. I like this supplement and will continue to take one a day, but I can't personally attest to health benefits so quickly. I trust the Nature's Bounty name and these appear to be high quality supplements Made in the USA that, at a minimum, supply antioxidants. They don't make me sick or trigger any negative reaction and may have other potential beneficial effects, so I give this Nature's Bounty Artichoke supplement 4 stars.

title: Not impressed
text:
This bag makes me a little crazy. Its a decent bag compared to some of the others which are just way too buly/expensive. There are four major problems with this item.

1) This bag is tall and thin. The machine at the bottom makes it so bottom heavy that the rest of the bag wants to flop forward. Most other bags are wider and not as tall, making the less liekly to flop or fall.
2) Problem #2 is the complete lack of any kind of pocket or mesh. Nothing to put an an extra feed bag in, or packets of santizer wipes or, well, anything at all. The criss cross things in the front are virtually useless. I tried putting some things in there, tightening it, and they were loose and unstable. Tightening the bungee too much makes the bag look ridiculous and cinched.
3) Problem #3 is that mesh pocket inside the bag for the machine. It's a job for the jaws of life getting the machine in and out of that obnoxiously small pocket. I know other reviewers have said similar things that it will stretch and whatnot. It really kind of doesnt. It does *a little*. But not much. It has absolutely zero stretch in the material. I used to only put the machine in the bag when we went places, but it took so much f*ing time to manhandle the machine into the pocket, and then break my finger tips trying to get it out later, that we just keep it in this bag at all times. In that respect it actually works out bc we hang the bag from hooks and it's portably convenient. So there's a star, I guess.
4) Problem #4, is that there is (was) no way to charge up the machine while it's in the bag. What if you're traveling a long distance, or will be out for most of the day? I have to pry the machine out of the pocket and stuff it back in for half an hour just to get it charged? No. I did that like an idiot the first couple of times, and then decided to just cut a very small hole in the mesh and it opened up into the perfect space for the cord to fit through. Apparently it was too hard for this company to consider that people might actually have the audacity to want to charge the machine while in the bag. (eyeroll). Easy to solve, but it just shouldn't have had to be that way.
5) Problem #5 is that the flap for the window doesnt have the option to stay open. My son gets feeds during the night and its so annoying to try and undo that velcro every time the the machine beeps, which is alot. Again, easily solvable with a safety pin, but it just shouldnt have to be that way.

Generally, the bag does what its designed to do but not one single other thing. The other star is for the the fabric being easily cleanable. A dry-ish sponge and some scrubbing and it gets off any splatters of formula.

Not impressed.

title: "Holy water" for my skin
text:
Glycerin is a well known moisturizer and used in most personal care and beauty products. If you search for some scholastic papers, it has healing properties too, while other moisturizers do not.

I brought one bottle last year but didn't figure out how to use it - how to get enough on the skin without breaking the bank. I was on the wrong track of trying to make body/face wash or body lotion. Then I realized the best and simplest way is to dilute and then spray with a fine "atomizer" on dry skin. I must have came across that many times but since they always add something to it like rose water, I wonder what they were trying to achieve. And that I wasn't comfortable leaving some chemicals on my skin, until I know it has healing properties.

For this product, I use 1 part glycerin to 9 part filtered water. It is by volume, teaspoons or buckets. You can apply like cologne or spray with a fine mist. After drying you will feel that your palm is slightly coated with a smooth, comfortable but not sticky layer. The exact concentration doesn't matter that much as the drying process is self adjusting. I bet this level of concentration beats the content in even the most moisturizing body wash or shampoo.

You can use up to 2 part glycerin to 8 part purified water without feeling sticky, but the presence of glycerin on the skin will be felt.

My hands wouldn't heal easily. I have to wear gloves when doing house work. But even washing hands after going to the bathroom will interrupt the healing. Nothing OTC can really stop the deterioration, until I have to go to the doctors for prescription steroid. I use Dove for body wash and Vaseline for body lotion. That won't stop the next cycle of outbreak - steroid.

Then I discovered corn huskers lotion. It worked miracles. It's $2 a bottle. But I am fed up to go to the only store that stock it. It was so simply that I made my own. Replace 4 part of water above with vodka (standard 40%) ! That is 1 part glycerin, 4 part vodka and 5 part of purified water. I think the alcohol in corn huskers lotion did the job. You can use 70% rubbing alcohol for first-aid but vodka is obviously food grade so I can handle anything without drying my hands completely first or wash them. Also, some people add vodka to make beauty products, so I'm not worried. You can vary the concentration to see if it works faster.

Other than my hands, I also have an occasionally outbreak that made my whole body extremely itchy. I have to see the doctor urgently and receive shots. Because it's the whole body or the whole legs, he can't give me potent steroids so I have a few days of can't do anything because of the itch, using the useless creams that he gave me. Dermatologists are only interested in plastic surgery so he wasn't keen on finding the cause of my problems. I think it's dryness on a small part of the limbs that caused it. For years I was afraid to go swimming, and banned myself from the hot tub. Dove body wash and the like won't work. I have to top it up with body lotion. If I was lazy a little bit, some minor skin problems will come up somewhere.

Now I just spray (1:9 glycerin) after bath after towel dry. It's almost free compared to lotions. But the effortless application is priceless.

There's more. I have dry feet. At the heel some dry skin peeled off but remained attached. I cannot grind it off with beauty stones. Lotions make it feel better but the dead skin are still there. But after just a few days of spraying glycerin, the problem vaporized. My feet were smoother than I can remember.

I sprayed my hair after towel dry too.

Nowadays I look for glycerin in shampoo and body wash. The ingredients are listed in the order of concentration I think. I look for pure soap made from vegetable oil and preferably olive, as they were for the royals. The difference is the amount of glycerin in it. The liquid form is made of potassium salt suitable for shampoo and body wash. The solid soap bar is made of sodium salt. But they are selling like gold, approaching $20 for a quad and $10 for a bar. Even if I use them, I still need to spray glycerin from time to time, or if just to feel soft, smooth and good. I may also find cheaper ones with less glycerin because I have plenty.

Just don't apply neat. High enough concentration can absorb moisture from your skin. Also, be sensible reading things from the Internet like this. My brain almost blew up. One person conjectured that if the atmosphere is dry enough, the glycerin will lost moisture to the air, and get moisture from your skin instead. Other than that it is totally wishful thinking, if that make any sense products containing glycerin would have carried a warning label - don't go to California after application.

title: Great color, horrible design
text:
The design of this case is so odd and poorly thought out. Did any real pump wearers test it? I can't imagine they did, because they would have caught this glaring flaw: While clipped horizontally to a waistband or belt, the clip is situated in the case so that the wearer must read/interact with the screen upside-down. WHAT?!?!?! Why would the designer think it was important for the people looking AT you to be able to read the screen right-side-up? The wearer is the important one here, not her/his audience. (And, no, there is no way to flip the clip around to the other side - it is either vertical or horizontal one-way only.) Since the integration with the Dexcom G5 just rolled out, I look at my pump frequently, as it now displays my CGM graph. Having an upside-down screen is even MORE annoying now that I rely on those quick glances to see how I'm doing.

Also, the clip needs teeth or something to actually hold it in place. My pump slips off of my waistband several times per day (and while sleeping), no matter what type of material my pants are made of. I have had too many slip-offs, with the only thing holding my pump to my body being the tubing to my infusion set (ummm... OUCH). I still keep the case on for its protection, but usually end up slipping the whole thing into my pocket because it's just so annoyingly-designed.

The only thing I like about it is the color. But, that's it.

I can't wait until I have more options for a case.

title: Lifesaver
text:
My Mom is on oxygen full time now and although her ears are not red, she said the tubing is bothering her ears. So for an immediate relief I took stuffing out of a dog toy and sewed it over the tubing where it hits her ears.

Then I ordered these. I googled it because I didnt know they had a product for this. I had read reviews that said they didnt stay on good and some people put a drop of glue on them to stay on.

So when we got them and she was putting them on, they kept popping off. Then I noticed she was putting them on with the opening pointing up, so every time she went to bend it on her ears it popped off. So I put them on with the opening pointing on and they stayed on.

After using them for several days they dont seem to come off anymore and she has no more soreness on her ears. So these really are a lifesaver!!

title: This looks like a great mixture for a multi-vitamin!
text:
Im pretty excited to try these. I had gastric bypass surgery in January of 2000. I never regretted having the surgery as I was 405 pounds the day of surgery and I lost over 200 pounds - it gave me my life back. But the one down side is that I am vitamin deficient in many areas.

My biggest problem was Iron, B12, and Protein. I became very anemic and it took me until last year to finally get all my blood work in the normal ranges. To do this I take a lot of vitamin supplements. In addition, Im on disability for fibromyalgia, so I take additional supplements for that.

Right now I take a daily multi-vitamin, Magnesium, Ester C, Iron, Vitamin B12, and Fibromyalgia Herbal Mix. This pill has all the same things a regular daily vitamin has, but it also has an herbal blend specifically designed for women, and it has an herbal blend for Immune Support. Im going to discontinue the Ester C as I start this and see if it has any negative effects. If it doesnt I will begin to eliminate other supplements to see if I can get down to just one type of pill a day.

I will continue to update my review as times passes.

title: Not accurate for dairy and..... bananas!
text:
We long had a suspicion that our daughter had a banana allergy. Obviously, we wanted to find out and use this test since we can just use hair samples and that's pretty simple and easy to do.

We collected the hair samples, scanned the QR code, recorded the information and mailed it out.

We received an email acknowledgement and a few days later the results.

It stated she was in the "Red" (high sensitivity) for dairy and all cheeses, which does not appear to be true since our kids drink a lot of milk, twice a day and our daughter eats cheese almost every day since she loves it.

Most importantly, we searched for Bananas and it showed she was completely in the clear for bananas.

So we gave her 1/4 of a banana with Benadryl in our other hand. She had no other foods since 12pm and we did this before dinner, so her stomach was clear of foods for probably 5+ hours.

Within 15 minutes her stomach hurt and she started feeling itchy. This was the same reaction we suspected over a year ago and thought it was probably the banana.

We gave her Benadryl and she was feeling better within 20 minutes.

I looked at the test results again and it said she was in the clear for Bananas but completely high/red for dairy and all cheeses listed.

For now, we cannot trust their results since we have real-life experience of the opposite.

Hope the manufacturer will contact me to re-verify results.

I can only give 1-star since I can't give lower.

title: I am going to have to return it
text:
I had a different brand that broke after a month but I loved that thing, so I began the search for a replacement. This fell in a comfortable price range but sadly is no good for me.
The head strap was not adjustable enough. Even let out as far as it will go it just felt too tight on my head. My head is not big but I do have thick hair.
As others have commented, the bridge area over your nose is very uncomfortable. With my old device I'd be asleep before the 15 minute cycle was even over. With this one,however, I kept having to readjust the mask to get the pressure off my nose, but then the mask was too high up on my eyes and more adjusting had to be done. I was ready to turn it off before the session was even complete.
I think in an attempt to cover the motor sounds the music coming through the mask is played too loudly. The melodies were fine for me but the white noise was too much. One is supposed to sound like a babbling brook but comes out sounding like people splashing their feet in a pool. The birds sound more like squawking than chirping. It was not relaxing. There may be an option to turn the sound off, I didn't try since I already knew I was unhappy with this mask,, and you can connect to your phone so you can play your own music if you choose.
I'll be returning and looking for another option.

title: Helps mood and concentration
text: My kids focus and mood are much improved when they take Omega 3s. (We are vegetarian and find these supplements beneficial). These are vegan, no fish oil and no heavy metals, especially important for kids. The serving is supposed to be 3 a day, and at that dose these are pretty expensive and honestly with their flavor it's hard to stomach eating that many. Fortunately, we find one a day is plenty. They taste kind of lemony, or kind of orangey, and also like algae. The algae smell and flavor is there, and it's not entirely pleasant. While my kids prefer gummies to tablets, these are not their favorite. They'll eat them, but they aren't excited about them. That said, these are pretty much the same as every other Omega 3 gummy on the market, we have yet to find one that tastes good.... so maybe that's just the nature of Omega 3s.

title: Doesn't cut grease

This cleaner also comes in a pretty small bottle for the price. It works to wipe down my kids eating table and art table, but for kitchen and bathroom cleaning it just doesn't cut it.

title: Hydrophobic
text: I wanted to use these pads as backup protection when I'm wearing a menstrual cup, and for that purpose they are almost okay, but they aren't very comfortable. They slide around a lot because they only have one snap and the outer fabric is slick. The inner fleece fabric is fairly hydrophobic. Liquid beads on the top and slides to the edges. When it does get absorbed, the top of the fleece stays wet rather than wicking moisture away from your skin, which isn't comfortable. There are also no washing instructions in the box. We used cloth diapers for both of our kids and these pads are pretty much just tiny cloth diapers, so I wash these how I washed those, but care instructions would be nice. Overall I'm disappointed and I would not recommend this product.

title: Small but festive
text: These Halloween decorations are okay, but they are smaller than I expected. It's enough to decorate an entry way or one wall or snacks table but that's about all. The shaped Mylar balloons in particular were quite little.  I got a spider (8" tall x 14" from leg tip to leg tip when deflated), a ghost with  pumpkin (a total of 11" x 13" with a 8" x 8" pumpkin and a 5" x " ghost), and 3 16" circular balloons (2 that are orange and say "Happy Halloween" with cute Halloween pictures, one black with a bloody skeleton that says "spooky"). So I got more than the 3 Mylar balloons promised in the product description, but they were much smaller than the product description indicated. I got 16 latex balloons, 4 each of white with a ghost face, orange with a scary jack o lantern face, black with a red scary face and clear with orange and black confetti. They look good but smell very strongly of turpentine. I got 6 tissue paper pom poms (some assembly required) with an 8" diameter. 2 each in orange black and white. There were also kits to make 12" long black and orange tissue paper tassels. Lastly there is a set of cardstock cutouts with images that spell out "Happy Halloween" and some black ribbon to string them on. Overall the decorations look cute, but honestly I was hoping for something better at this price.

I have had many many protein shakes over the last 10 years, and I can't say I recommend any of the protein powders that this company makes. When the best you can say about a product is "it's better than something that is undrinkable" that's not exactly a ringing endorsement. It comes in a deceptively large jar that is only half full. I'd recommend trying something else and skipping this product all together, but if you must try this particular variety of protein powder for some reason the vanilla is the best, then the chocolate, the strawberry is undrinkable.

title: Classic comfort
text: This is a classic rubber hot water bottle like I used to use as a kid. It stays warm for 5 hours and has a super soft velvety removable cover with a calming Galaxy print on it. The cover is really well made, and the bottle doesn't leak. The bottle has a nice wide mouth so you don't spill filling it up. It doesn't come with any instructions on how to use it, so here's what I do: boil a tea kettle full of water, remove it from the heat and let it stand for 5-10 minutes, pour into the hot water bottle, screw on plug. (Tap water isn't hot enough, and boiling water is so hot it will damage the bottle.) This provides the perfect amount of comforting heat for muscle aches, cramps, or chilly nights.

title: Disgusting Drink
text: This protein powder tastes terrible. When I first opened the bottle I was disappointed that it was only half full. Then I tasted it and I was glad that it was only half full. It tastes like carob flavored chalk. The flavor is so bad that even adding chocolate syrup to it doesn't save it. It still leaves a cloying gross aftertaste in your mouth. I tried it both with water and with soy milk and it was equally awful both ways. Don't torture yourself and buy something else. The taste is amazing...amazingly bad.

title: A very efficient little First Aid survival kit for those small emergencies when out and about.
text: Now that so many are finally emerging from the safety of their homes and exploring here and there, safety should be uppermost in their minds when it comes to things like hiking, camping, and even sports.  Having available a nifty little First Aid Kit like this one is smart.  It's stuffed with about 78 items for assorted mini emergencies, and is lightweight.  It's not a bad idea to keep it in the car just in case, or with any outdoor activity gear.  The kit contains almost anything a slightly injured person might need for a quick fix.  There's gauze and tape, band aids, antiseptic towelettes, safety pins, tweezers, and even a small Pocket Guide for First Aid.  (I wish it had a small pair of scissors, though I have a pair and will put them in the kit).  The almost cube-shaped bag or pouch is made of a sturdy cloth with zipper across the top and sides with two different ways to carry it, and about the size of a man's open palm.

(According to the GG bottle - 2,250 mg total for 3 capsules....a lot more!)  The literature here also mentions that this GG Tumeric is 1,100 mg per serving, see what I mean?  Doing some research, the consensus seems to be an average of 1,200 to 1,800 mg per day, or another opinion at about 500 to 2,000 mg per day....what to do?  This question arose because I've also started taking a homeopathic natural skin supplement formula that includes 300 mg of Tumeric per day.  All of them include the black pepper for better absorption.  I just don't want to overdose, so I'm sticking somewhere with the average.  Anyway, I think Tumeric is a very good way to help with osteoarthritis, high cholesterol, itchy skin, and it also helps the liver, and has good anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. I like this brush straightener very much!
I really didn't expect it to actually work, but it did. I will admit that I had no idea that the temperature was a celcius temperature, so I will make sure not to use it on the highest setting when I use again. It's perfect for a quick solution when you want your hair to look good. It did straighten my hair nicely - I have very fine hair, and it's wavy. This straightener did a great job of straightening fine long hair without much time involved.
My advice, if you're going to use this product- use a heat protectant as well as a "setting lotion" so the results last - same advice I'd give anyone using any heat styling product.
It was as simple as brushing my dry hair out to make sure there's no tangles, and using the brush to straighten my hair. You DO have to hold onto the end of your hair as you are pulling the length through the brush. This is so much easier than using a flat iron to straighten!
I've seen many people use a flat iron to touch up, which is probably what you would do if you have very curly or coarse hair.

title: Mr Clean Magic Eraser Healed My Broken Leg!
text:
Okay, not really ...but what even ARE these things?? I submit for your review, the following real-life (this time, True) scenarios:

A couple years ago I accidentally scraped my car's bumper along the edge of the garage door while sleepily coming home from work (more than once, DEEP). Cosmetic damage looked real ugly for about a year. I'm not sure where I heard about MR Clean Magic Erasers, maybe some online car repair/body work forum ...but WOW, after destroying a couple of these little sponges they actually worked out every single last visible scuff mark (aside from one or two spots you could still see if you looked super closely).

I have used them to remove black TAR from countertops. Successfully, and without much effort at all. After trying many other products, unsuccessfully.

The reason I got on the computer to leave this review, is because ten minutes ago I just used a TIIIIIIINY corner of a Mr Clean Magic Eraser to save my $150 sunglasses ...how did I damage them you ask? I dropped them into an old RUSTY wheelbarrow, and then an electric hand saw tumbled over them - soooo painfully dragging the lenses face-down across the rust and scratching them. Cried myself to sleep, woke up, and tried a Magic Eraser in the morning. Successfully, and without much effort at all. All birds on the property sang in unison.

I have been keeping these IN STOCK under my sink since 2014. Whenever I need to use one, I just cut off however much I think I need so I don't waste an entire sponge every time and they last FOREVER. Thanks for reading my review and have a great day.

title: Awkward fit; presses onto nose too much, making for a very uncomfortable fit
text:
I bought this eye mask for my occasional headaches and daytime naps.

WHAT I LIKE:
- the cord is quite long - 72" or 6 feet which is perfect if you fall asleep, so that it gives you enough leeway tossing and turning and not getting entangled with the cord
- the cord attaches to the mask magnetically - in case you DO get entangled, it easily snaps off (but it is also a big CON... read below)
- the material seems to be of high quality and it is padded, which feels very soft to the touch

WHAT I DISLIKE:
- the mask comes only in a box, not a pouch. I do not like stuff like this to be in a box that could get smashed, waterlogged or otherwise damaged. A dedicated pouch with a string as a hanger would be much more practical
- the temperature switch (on the cable) is very touch sensitive - this might be a defect of my particular eye mask: when I set it on HIGH, and I just lightly move the cord by the magnetic attachment, it will turn off entirely. So in order to not disrupt the heating, I have to set it on MEDIUM or LOW for it to work (because everyone moves around a bit....)

AND MY BIGGEST COMPLAINT:
- the mask stays on 15 minutes at a time, which in my opinion is a very short time - it should be longer!
- THE DESIGN IS WRONG! No matter how I shift the mask, the cutout shape for the nose is too small meaning the mask is sitting either mostly on the top of my eyes and I can peek from under the mask and see daylight (and my nose is nicely cleared), or I push it over my eyes, and then the mask and its padding pushes onto my (rather large, I admit) nose and sinuses and makes wearing it VERY UNCOMFORTABLE.
I have to say, my head is truly somewhat larger and so is my nose, so this discomfort might be due to the proportions of my face features, I don't know....

So all in all, mostly because of the awkward design and therefore the uncomfortable fit, I hardly ever use this mask.

title: made me sick
text: Hopefully whoever reads this review does their research on probiotics in general as I didn't do mine hence why I'm probably giving this such a poor review.  As you may already be aware, different brands have different strains of 'good bacteria', and cheaper brands especially can cause problems such as an upset stomach.  When I first started taking these at the minimum dose (only 1 a day, always with a meal) I would notice my appetite would go from relatively full to very hungry almost immediately, where as before my stomach would feel more empty over a much longer duration.  No big deal, I figured my body was trying to adjust.  Then around 6+/- days into taking these I started having a cramped stomach an hour or so after going out for a beer or two, possibly what could have triggered the stomach ache since I've heard some craft beers contain probiotics in the yeast (correct me if I'm wrong, I've also heard this is filtered out in the brewing process).  I did not take my probiotic the same day I drank and that night, I went to sleep hoping my stomach would feel better in the morning.  I got up around 1am and went to the bathroom, I could not go and wanted so bad to throw up but couldn't.  I was having cold sweats looking super flushed and almost passed out on the bathroom floor.  The stomach ache was so debilitating, it was VERY similar to the time my appendix ruptured, and I was afraid this time it could be something unrelated to the probiotics, like my spleen.  I didn't know what was going on at the time and stumbled into the other room to wake up my gf.  Slowly over the next 3 days I was able to go, only ate a bare minimum of 1 meal a day with water and a small cup of coffee which is very unusual for me as I always have a big appetite.  Finally I woke up today and things seem to be back to normal.  I read up on stomach aches and probiotic uses online and they say this is why it is so important to get the right brand (I heard Align at Costco is a good brand).  Several people who had this problem (who did not cite drinking) said these stomach pains lasted a week or more.  I find it hard to believe that just ~1L of beer could cause such a reaction but I guess it's possible this was due to the bacteria in the beer.  Anyway I am scared to take any more of these, so do your research especially if you drink.

text:
Beyond Tangy Tangerine's label claim says 1g sugar, 7g carbohydrates. The 6g of carbs must be from maltodextrin, which is in essence, a sugar as well, because it's off the charts on the glycemic index. When I take a serving of BTT, I get a sugar reaction, as if I just mowed down 5 chips a'hoy cookies. It's really uncanny. So, I honestly question the label claims. Maybe it's the maltodextrin that's causing a reaction, I'm not sure. But this product gives me bloat, like I said, worse than if I ate a gigantic pastry.

What I do know, is that while I'm sure this product has benefits, if you can digest it properly, for me, it causes awful digestive reactions. I have been taking Dr. Wallach's Ultimate Classic, which is basically the liquid form of this product for years with NO negative reactions... and that has 7.5g of sugar per serving! Also, I take Youngevity's "Rebound FX" product, which too has 7g of sugar per serving, and I digest that just fine. Something's funny with this product.

If I had to guess, it's the maltodextrin giving me a reaction. But, needless to say, I can't tolerate it. I will go back to Youngevity's Ultimate Classic, Colloidal Minerals, and I'll stay with Rebound FX. Beyond Tangy Tangerine is NOT for me. This was an extremely expensive failed experiment. I still have a container that's half full, that will unfortunately be going in the trash, or passed onto someone else.

title: Works good.  Just temper your expectations
text:
I actually own a previous model of this which is nowhere near as nice. I bought this one because the older model is stuck 3 states away, and I'm dealing with a minor foot issue.

Some things that stand out:

- the heating element. If this heats from cold water, I assume it would take forever. DO NOT expect it to do some miracle heating of cold or even cool water. Start with lukewarm water, warm enough that you can tolerate it but not "hot" if that makes sense. Then enable the heating element. I estimate it will take roughly 15-30 minutes to actually "heat" the water from this point, just to give you perspective. Plus your skin and vessels will thank you for the gradual heating.

- the vibration element. There's no real "massaging" here. It just vibrates. Good for the soles of your feet, yes. That's about all it'll really do for you. What irritated me is that the center separator has something in there that rattles a bit. Not a showstopper but it was annoying. (Yes, I removed the attachment piece.)

- The bubble element. I wasn't impressed. It's good to help the water heat up faster by introducing air into it, but you literally can't feel the bubbles at your feet with the vibration element enabled. Not nearly as dispersed or "awesome" as what the picture shows.

- Some of the nubs under foot feel higher than others. This is especially true near the pinky toe. A bit annoying, not a showstopper.

- I do like the separate compartment for storing the attachments.

- I also like the way the pour spout is designed. On the older model you could only go so high before water was spilling out the front. Here, it's small enough to pour out but not so large as to cause spilling.

- I did not use the rollers, I took them out.

- I use a tea tree soak and they dissolve nicely here. My feet are already looking and feeling much better after only a few days of sessions.

- There are four attachments, one a regular brush, which you can use to completely pedicure. I recommend following up with a foot lotion for the best results, or at least some cocoa butter lotion or coconut oil.

title: This Is The Only Review You Need To Read
text:
This review is the only one you need to read. Background: I am a retired marine mechanical engineer. I deal in the real world, what works and what does not. Cause and effect, efficiency, and production.

My coffee thermos is the brushed stainless steel Zojirushi. It holds 7 cups of water. The inside surface is uneven with the brushed surface. This makes any stain harder to remove, as a rough surface makes adherence easier, examples being paint, etc. Following the directions, I poured 2 ounces of S n C into the carafe. I saw that IMMEDIATELY the spot where the concentrate contacted the metal went clean and bright, with the stain coming off in sheets. I then added 2 cups of warm/hot tap water, approximately 125 deg. I swirled it around and waited for 3 minutes. The stain at eh bottom was gone, except for a few isolated spots. I used a soft bristle brush for about a minute to easily remove the remainder. I then emptied the jug, rinsed it and looked inside. The surface was clean and spotless, but there was a ring where the treatment solution reached its highest level. I then put in 1 ounces of concentrate and brushed the stained ring for less than a minute. All gone completely. The entire inside is like brand new. No evidence of stain anywhere.

Reflection: In retrospect, I could have filled the jug higher with another ounce of concentrate and that stain would have disappeared. Either way it is a personal choice.

Conclusion: The product works completely, efficiently, and as advertised. Period. Full Stop. No qualifiers. I will never use anything else. Why would I? The coffee stains were about 4 months old, when the coffee maker was purchased. I always clean the jug, the top and the filter tray with dishwashing soap and water by hand everyday.

Any other reports to the contrary are in my opinion, lies, or the results of persons too incompetent or arrogant to follow directions. It's that simple.

title: Great for reading in bed!
text: I use this lamp at my bedside either for reading books or with my Kindle Fire for reading and apps.  Before getting this lamp, I was content with using my overhead lighting to read in my room.  Since getting the Verilux lamp, I use either the lamp alone (particularly at night) or the overhead and Verilux lamp combined.  It also improves use of my Kindle Fire or other tablet/cell devices.  In any of these situations, using the Verilux lamp makes a clear difference in ease on the eyes so there is no eye strain or related headaches.  The contrast of a black and white text page is perfect.  The gooseneck of the lamp is adjustable to get just the right angle for your reading or craft work.  It does provide a good pool of light for these purposes as opposed to lighting up the room.  If you are reading at night it won't disturb a partner sleeping for example but is significantly higher quality than using a booklight.  Replacement bulbs are available currently priced at around $20.  A comparable product in desk/table top lamp is also available, though for the bedside or an armchair this floor lamp is just the right height.  I have also submitted pictures of what the lamp looks like in my room to show the height.  Most people think of a floor lamp as being taller than this is.  I wouldn't want it at a taller height for my purposes.  I have also added pictures of what text looks like under the light so check out customer images for those pictures.  I will absolutely continue using this light for reading and I suspect replace the bulb maybe once a year?  It could even last longer but $20/yr or so is very reasonable for good reading light.  Now that I am used to this, I couldn't go back to just my overhead lamp or a table lamp at my bedside. I will recommend this product to friends and family as well.

title: Great for plantar faciitis and restless leg syndrome!!!
text:
I got this foot massager mainly for my husband. He has plantar fasciritis and is supposed to roll the bottom of his feet on a tennis ball a couple times a day. This was the answer to our prayers. He comes home from work and takes off the dress shoes that causes his foot pain and can't wait to get his feet in the massager. The foot massager does deep tissue massaging, almost to the point it's uncomfortable but that's what he needsand wants to help his feet so it's perfect. I on the other hand have restless leg syndrome and a lot of the time the calves of my legs ache really bad. I had read on some of the reviews were people was putting the calves of their legs in the Foot massager and I thought why not! So I placed the massager on the couch, laid down and put my calves in it. I. set it to auto which is 15 minutes of different types of massage. I let it finish and for the rest of the night I had no pain in my legs! This is absolutely better than having to take ibuprofen all the time which didn't work as well as the massage. The unit runs nice and quiet and is a beautiful red color. It is quite large but that's OK, I just store it beside the couch or underneath my coffee table for easy access as we will be using this every day. As other said the remote is almost useless, by the time you have tried pushing buttons a few times you could have bent over and pushed the button. It did come very nicely packaged to keep it from getting damaged in shipment. Another wonderful feature is that the covers to the footbed so unzip so they can be washed! Well, enough reviewing, I'm gonna get a massage! Lol.
I would like to disclose that I did received this item for either a discounted price or for free to give an honest and unbiased opinion. I was not paid or compensated to give a rating or to even review the product. I give ratings based on my experience and the performance that I expect with a product. title: Wore these to the club. Saved my hearing.
text:
I’m getting old. Not physically or mentally (these are for my clubbing nights) but in terms of wisdom. I now know that most people in their 30s have lost a good amount of hearing due to loud situations. Concerts, parties, clubs, etc. I want to preserve my hearing for as long as I can cos I don’t wanna be that old dude that goes, “huh?” a hundred times a day.

I got these for loud karaoke, club, and bar environments where the boom and high shrill of treble from music is too much. These still let in a good amount of bass (which you feel) and treble, making the music still enjoyable but at a reduced, more sane level.

Rock musicians as they age tend to have better hearing than their classical counterparts. This, at first, makes no sense, but it’s true because rock and pop musicians use hearing protection a whole lot more than conductors and instrumentalists of classical music.

So wise up and start using protection unless you want hearing aids in your future. Those tiny hairs in your ear that allow you to listen can’t regenerate!

title: Great for Filing Down Damaged Toenail
text:
I use this to file down a thickened, damaged toenail. The glass file broke on my first use because it's very, very brittle. Luckily, it didn't result in small shards of glass everywhere, it just broke in half. It almost seems acrylic, but I think it is glass.

The main filing blocks are clearly labeled and easy to use. They're pretty big so easy to grip--I'm a man with medium sized hands so if it's easy for me, should be easy for most women. I can't attest to how long these will last, but the filing blocks are made of seemingly rigid foam. I'll report back if these break.

As for the surfaces of the filing block, they really are varied, unlike what some reviewers claim. So you do have different steps to do your nails in. What I use to file down my damaged big toe is soak in warm, epsom salt water (helps kill bacteria), and I dry off with a towel right before filing. After filing a bit off, I re-dip my feet into the soaking solution, and repeat this process. My toenail looks fairly normal, but you must also remember to be careful in filing, I suggest a circular motion because if you go too fast/hard/deep you might bleed.

title: For the price, pretty good for loud concerts and smaller ears
text:
I was torn between these and [[ASIN:B019M576XW Eargasm High Fidelity Earplugs]], but leaning towards Downbeats because they were half the price, and they seemed like they would be less noticeable in my ear. Thanks to a sale I got both these and Eargasms and decided to test them.

Basically, Downbeats muffled sound more than Eargasm earplugs did, but at loud volumes (like a concert) the muffle isn't that noticeable. Since I need earplugs that are clear at more normal volumes too (like a college lecture, background conversations in a large room), these muffled a bit too much to be helpful. It still wasn't a wasted purchase as I discovered these earplugs help with lessening noise when I need to fall asleep without muting too much (I still need to hear alarms, but I'm a very light sleeper), and the small size makes them comfortable for side sleeping.

I didn't have a problem with removal like some other reviews said as I couldn't stick the earplugs far enough into my ear for it to be an issue.

The picture is a size comparison of downbeats and the Eargasm high Fidelity earplugs (order is: Regular Eargasm plugs on the left, Downbeats in center, and smaller Eargasms on the right). The regular size Eargasm's middle flange is 1.5cm wide, and the Downbeat's smaller flange and the middle flange on the small Eargasm plug are both 1.3cm wide.

title: Not very responsive and the display is sleep-disrupting
text:
This machine works decently. You can cycle through the sounds (many of which are... bizarre? Who wants to go to sleep hearing someone eat? Yuck!) and you can use it as a nightlight.

However, the buttons on the front are atrocious. They're barely pressable - you can't tell whether you've hit the button and I've often found myself accidentally hitting it twice and having to tediously cycle through weird noises again. The power button is equally challenging. And, the lights! I've had to absolutely smack the thing to turn off the aggressively bright night light that comes ON at the slightest brush.

The real killer, though, is the display light. When you have the machine on, it constantly lights the display (showing what settings are chosen) in BRIGHT BLUE. This is widely reputed to be the worst light color to sleep near, and it certainly causes me to have difficulty relaxing. However if you press something over the display, like tape, you can't tell where the buttons are. And if you cover it with a pillow case you can't hear the sounds properly. Awful design.

The plastic cover makes the trimmer more ergonomic. The size, about 3.5 inches long, works for either fingernails or toenails, though it’s best to have designated clippers for your toes for sanitary reasons. The file on the bottom is nothing special.

To me, it’s a given that nail clippers will leave a bit of a rough edge. I always follow up my clipping with some filing to smooth things out. These clippers are no exception. title: An okay multivitamin with some extra stuff
text: I needed another multivitamin and found this one. I liked that it had Chlorophyll and CQ10. As well as a good amount of copper. Those are things I needed to help me get used to the high altitudes in the area that I moved to. I was not sure of the incredibly high level of B-12 or the high levels of Thiamine, Pantothenic Acid, Riboflavin, B-6 and Biotin that are in it. I know they are water soluble so when you take it whatever you do not need will be flushed away in your urine. But that seems like a waste. The Chromium Picolinate is pretty high too but it helps with my blood sugar so I did not worry about that. I also like the fruit and vegetable blend in it but it was only 5mgs worth. I really appreciate it when I can get a multivitamin that is made mostly from fruits and vegetables and does not have magnesium stearate or silica in it. It was strange to me that these are liquid vitamins in the capsule but that seems to make them absorb quicker. Since some of the ingredients were at high doses I took a capsule in the morning at breakfast and one at lunch. I thought that would also keep from having insomnia from the caffeine in the green tea leaf or the stimulation of the Panax Ginseng and Eleutherococcus Senticosus. The capsules are an ugly black color and they are a little oily on the outside. They are smaller than most of my other supplements so there was no problem swallowing them. The capsules are thinner than others too so they can be easily broken open. One broke open when I picked it up and I just swallowed both halves. While taking them I have had good energy and have been generally in a positive mood. I feel good. I think this is an okay multivitamin. The price is not bad for the ingredients you get. But I think most people will want a multivitamin that has more even amounts of each vitamin or mineral. However these levels of ingredients could be the specific combination that someone needs for their particular situation. So I would recommend it to them. title: A good combination of helpful ingredients.
text:
This is pretty good formula with 5 important ingredients that most people need to maintain great hair, skin and nails: Biotin, Keratin, MSM and Hyaluronic Acid and Collagen. Although the Biotin level is quite high which may cause a problem for some people overtime. I was surprised that it did not contain Vitamin A or or some kind of Retinol. I would think that would be included to help the skin. But this formula does contain a good mixture of other helpful ingredients like Fo-Ti and Alpha Lipoic Acid along with some I do not recognize like Nori Yaki and Wakame. I do appreciate that it is made with no GMO ingredients. I would like this formula better if it had a higher dose of calcium and if it did not have the substances listed in the “Other ingredients” section as I do not believe they are good for anyone. Also sometimes a pharmaceutical glaze on tablets like these does not allow the tablet to dissolve so the ingredients can be absorbed in the digestive tract so I crack it open with my teeth before swallowing it.
It’s difficult to measure results with a product like this. However, since I have been taking it my nails have been getting a little stronger, not breaking as easily. I do not notice anything yet with my hair and skin. The tablets do have distinct smell that you have to get past before you can get it down as well. Overall I think this formula could be of benefit to have regularly in your diet if you can get past all of the other non-beneficial things in it.

title: It’s an okay formula.
text:
I had needed more CQ10 and saw this product. It was packaged nicely so I thought I’d give it a try. When I received it and checked out the ingredients. The Coenzyme Q10 is the Ubidecarenone form which has to be broken down in the body to the Ubiquinol (CQ10). This is a problem for older people because the ability to break it down is declines with age. Fortunately I am not old enough that it’s a problem. The Vitamin E is d-alpha tocopheryl acetate which is okay but I’d rather have just simple d-alpha tocopheryl. I was disappointed to find listed in the “Other Ingredients” section on the label is polysorbate 80. This is chemical is used to help disperse the ingredients, keep the gel consistency and etc. But according to it’s own MSDS it May cause adverse reproductive effects, cancer and may affect our genetic material (mutagenic).
After seeing the polysorbate 80 in it I did not think I should take it.
Others may not mind these types of ingredients but I want to be vigilant in keeping myself healthy which includes watching what I put in my body. I did not mind the rest of the ingredients. The softgels swallowed easy enough even though they are larger than other supplements I take. And the manufacturer tried to think of a good mix of ingredients to help everything absorb better.
I would not recommend this product for everyone only really healthy individuals and I would not recommend taking it everyday. I would, however, instead encourage people to find a more natural, less harmful formula.

title: Safe, easy-to-use supplement for cold and flu season
text:

I find it is way more effective in fighting illness than pharmaceuticals, and it doesn't have any negative side effects or kill off the "good" bacteria in my gut. title: Healthy and convenient way to get your greens
text:
Years ago, I had someone extol the virtues of wheatgrass to me. I was a bit skeptical, because I thought it smelled kind of funny, and I was somewhat squeamish about adding something so green to my food and drink. However, given the opportunity to try it for free, I thought I'd give it a shot.

This Super Organics Organic Wheatgrass Powder makes it easy to get my greens. It is organic, non-GMO, vegan and packed with powerful nutrients. One serving (less than a teaspoon) of this powder contains 89% of an adult's daily recommended amount of Vitamin C, 77% Riboflavin (Vitamin B2), 42% Thiamin (B1) and significant amounts of 4 other vitamins. It's easy to digest. It doesn't taste or smell nearly as strong as I would have thought, and as long as you put it in something that is brightly colored, it doesn't make it look strange.

I figured that, since wheatgrass is made of the green stalks of young wheat, that people with gluten intolerance would not be able to consume it. However, when I checked online, I read that wheat- and barley-grass both lack the protein that makes people with gluten allergies sick. Check with your doctor to be sure, but I think it's safe.

This powder is very fine and is packed in a resealable pouch that stands up on your shelf. It comes with a cute little scoop for measuring. It does not need to be refrigerated, but should be stored in a cool, dry place.

If you are looking for a healthy super-food with a lot of nutrition in a small amount, this is a good choice. You can add it to smoothies, like I did, or make a "wheatgrass shot" with one scoop of powder to 2 ounces of water. How ever you choose to blend it, it's an easy way to eat your greens and get the nutrients they provide.

title: Good taste, fair texture, but sketchy nutritional value
text:
I was skeptical about this product at first. Most energy bars have the taste and texture of thick cardboard. The thought of trying to get a kid to eat one was not terribly appealing. But surprisingly, they were not bad.

The appearance is a plus. Each bar is individually packaged in bright green and blue plastic. This product looks like a cross between a nutty brownie (which may not appeal to some youngsters) and a candy bar. The taste isn't bad, either--like rich, dark, crunchy chocolate. It requires a bit of chewing--which, again, may be a turn-off for some kids. But it really satisfies and stays with you for a long time. It took two bars to stave my hunger, but I imagine a child would require only one to keep him/her happy.

They are not particularly healthy, though, in my opinion. I counted at least four kinds of sugar repeated early in the list of ingredients. At 130 mg of sodium per 1.26 oz bar, they seemed to have a pretty high salt content. There are vitamins and minerals added, but they appear to be of chemical rather than natural origin--which means they may not be readily digested and absorbed into the body. I was really disturbed to see silicon dioxide (basically sand, which has been linked to restless leg syndrome) included in the list of ingredients. And with the excito-toxin MSG frequently being listed these days as "natural flavor," I was more than a little suspicious about seeing that item as an ingredient.

If you are desperate for something to feed your kids on the go, these are okay. They are pretty solid, so I think these would work well in the glove box or under the seat as an emergency snack for the kiddos. Unlike a candy bar, they won't melt in the heat. But they seem to have only barely more nutritional value than a chocolate bar. You might be better off reaching for the trail mix or a bag of raw nuts, instead.

title: Finally a "Perfect" Meal Replacement/Energy Bar!
text:
Note: This review is for the Red Raspberry Perfect Food flavor. Sometimes reviews get listed on other flavors as well, so keep this in mind as not all the aspects will apply to other flavors

I've personally tried a lot of energy/meal replacement bars, and been let down by most of them. Typical bars are loaded with soy, refined sugar, and ingredients that are incomplete or simply harmful. In the Garden of Life bars I've finally found something that tastes great, fills me up, and is amazingly healthy. There are a lot of things to like about these bars, and very few not to:

A balance of Meal Necessities - The bars include 40g of (good) Carbs for quick energy, 6g of Protein for sustained energy, and 6g of good fats for a satisfied feeling after eating. It's important to understand that the fats and carbs in this bar are for the most part completely good for you, they are not empty carbs or bad fats that are typically avoided in diets. The result is a nice satisfied feeling after eating one.

Provides 5g of fiber per bar - Most people don't get enough fiber, and definitely not the quality fiber in these bars. 3g of that fiber is soluble, the best kind. It's very rare to find this in a bar, and a great way to add needed fiber to your diet.

All the benefits of a green drink, in a portable and tasty format - While those green foods drinks are great for you, I personally can't stomach them, and don't have the time to mix and drink them all day. These bars are made from exactly the same thing as GOL's Perfect Food and Super Seed Mixes, giving you all the healthy fruits, veggies, sprouted grains and sprouted nuts, sweetened with honey and put in a convenient portable format.

Sweetened with Honey, NOT sugar - One of my biggest complaints with energy bars is that they're usually loaded with sugar, which gives a temporary rush of energy, and then a crash, tweaking out you insulin levels in a way that is not healthy. The GOL bars are different in that while they are roughly 20% sugar, the only sweetener used is Honey, which is a complex sugar that doesn't affect your body negatively the way refined sugars do.

Probiotics in the Bar - Garden of Life is known for their probiotics, and they have included some in the bar, to give you not only a balanced nutrition supply, but also some helpful bacteria to digest it with.

Finally, possibly most important of all, Taste! - The taste is a lightly sweet, pleasantly textured faint raspberry flavor. Biting into the bar is a satisfying feeling; it is soft but there is a "bulk" to it. There isn't a gooey or crunchy feeling like other bars, and no nasty chemical taste.

There are a lot of things to like about these bars, and very few not to. Try one out - you'll be pleasantly surprised at how great a meal bar can be!

title: Getting Back to Relaxing My Back
text:
I to have purchased this to replace and old Panasonic EP790 Shiatsu Massage chair.
My old chair had a drive belt wore out and I can't find that part.
I think its about 18 years old and if definitely got my moneys worth out of it, using it almost every day.
I'm going to try and find a belt and am still going to keep it as the motors and gears are still good, or maybe find someone looking for the motors. The front cushion is almost worn through.

This new chair is whisper quiet, I think the posting about a noisy chair is less than accurate or they got a defective unit. This chair seems to make less noise than my old one.

It has about the same footprint as my old one, maybe a little bigger and fits nicely into small spaces.

My new chair has many more choices for massage type which I like.
It doesn't seem to work the neck as good as my older unit.
I haven't played with the settings on manual yet and can probably get more intensity on upper areas, also the upper massage may improve as the padding gets broke in.
I like that the new chair provides lateral massage movement, where the old chair just ran up and down.
The massage range has been increased and reaches lower on my back, very nice.
The massage heads seem more like real hands.
The motorized recline and leg lift feature is nice as well.

The big difference is the leg massage.
It applies pressure squeezing the legs and then stretching them by pulling on them.
I'm thinking that its going to help with leg blood circulation.
It takes a bit getting use to this new feature.
My friend loved the leg massage and thought it was the best part.

The delivery was curb side and on time.
The back legs have rollers just tip it back and roll.
Its not easy lifting from the front to roll, it takes 2 people.
It was crated well and now I have a lot of cardboard to recycle.

Now all I have to do is pay for this, LOL.
I used my Amazon Store Card and got 1 year same as cash + free shipping.
That helped and with out that I mostly likely would not have made this purchase.
A great deal.

title: IMCO Super Triplex
text: I just got my IMCO Super Triplex lighter today and I couldn't be happier with it. It is very simple to operate, the design is very cool and it lights on the first strike every time. It is nickel plated steel and has a ten year warranty. I got the Super model because it has a slide to adjust how much airflow reaches the flame while the standard and slimline models just have open slots for air that cannot be closed. I was concerned that there would be some fluid loss when I was not using the lighter if I could not close the air slots but the "snuffer" portion of the cap actually forms a seal around the wick when closed so I think the other models would be fine and the adjustable airflow does not make a huge difference in operation. The only negative thing I could say is it seems like it will chew through flints really fast! I have been striking it a lot more than I normally would just checking it out and showing it off but I have already worn the flint down half way in one day! It has a very aggressive spark, which is a plus in that it will always light on the first strike regardless of any weather but I would order a few packs of flints with it if you like to play with your new toys as much as I do.

title: Save yourself $50 and go with a different brand
text:
I bought this product for my wife for Christmas, and have been thoroughly disappointed in it. HoMedics claim that this foot spa's "Heatboost Technology" will warm up water in minutes. This may be true, but what they fail to mention is that you have to have one of the two massage settings running in order to activate the heater. If you were hoping to pre-heat it, or maybe just soak your feet in some warm water, you are out of luck.
My second issue with this foot spa - it is LOUD. As in, hear it on the other side of the house, through 3 walls loud. My wife ran this while we were watching TV together, and I had to turn the TV up over 3/4 of it's volume in order to hear dialogue. And again, it won't heat water unless one of the massage settings are on.
Finally, for as much as I paid for this, I expected to get some more/higher quality features. I'm talking powered rollers, jets from multiple angles. I should have paid a bit more attention when ordering, but it is natural to assume that a $70 foot spa would have more features than a $20 version from Wal-Mart, right? Well, assumptions got the better of me this time.

Bottom line, if you want quality, look elsewhere. If you are willing to put up with the problems I outlined here, save yourself $50 and buy the same thing with a different label at Wal-Mart.

title: i get stuff and play
text:
5/28/17 purchased one of these used, actually two Healthy Line mats: 1) the small red amethyst pad ~36" x 18" with photon lights and 2) this large reversible mat. i like both of them. really only have issues with a damaged index finger, as far as pain goes. but i have a body that doesn't handle heat well. my core, once heated, retains heat: it doesn't cool down properly, so i got these pads to poke at the problem in an attempt to work with it and resolve it, or at least better understand it. in the meantime, infrared heat is good for the body.

turns out that i am okay with heat applied to just one side of my body, provided the other side is exposed to a cool space, whether it is the front side, or the backside. it turns out that the problem is when my entire body is surrounded by heat when it warms up, and that is when i find myself in trouble. am also experimenting with various chi machines, which impose a very active form of passive exercise on the entire body. the small fir pad with photon lights (which combines near infrared heat with far infrared heat) sits on a massage table where i use a Sun Ancon Chi Machine SM-330. that is kind of interesting, because it combines three things while just relaxing on the table: the significant passive movement imposed on the body by the chi machine with both far and near infrared heat, all at the same time, so i am more interested in that result than simply laying on the big mat with only far infrared heat going on.

so far, my experiences have been good. the big mat is laying on a chaise lounge where i often sit during waking hours. i first used the mat with the jade and toumaline stones side up, and have now turned it over with the amethyst side up. will be using both mats daily and will update results. i update reviews regularly.

title: Updated -- It does work but has a strong odor and an edge that is a little sharp for using on the face
text:
I got this yesterday and tried it this am. It came well packaged. In an a outer envelope then a nicer bubble wrap envelop. It has a little ziploc plastic case you can keep it in if you like. It is very silicon feeling texture and a little squishy. It reminds me of mini flatten silicone fake boob. Honestly that's what I initially thought of when i pulled it out and started touching it. It has a edge to it I am not crazy about where its sealed. So you will have to be careful around your eyes. I don't have the OG product this is based on so I can't compare it to that. But it does take very little makeup and it is very very easy to clean. Im not crazy about the finish it leaves on your face its seems a little streaky. I used my toothbrush foundation brush because I like the finish it gives over top of it. I do like it but I don't love it. And I would take away another half star and make it 3.5 if I could because it stinks. It has a terrible smell I'm leaving the storage pouch it comes with open as I'm hoping the product smell will fade in time. But it is really really smelly almost to the point where I wasn't going to use it. If you have a sensitivity to smells you will not like this.

Update 11-6-2017
So I ended up placing it next to my kitchen sink (no pouch) for about a month a few times a week I would wash it with warm soap and water. After about a month only if I held it directly under my nose would I get that chemical smell. I don't know if it was from the pouch it came in or the actual product. But it does fade over time. Now there is zero smell. I still don't use this right next to my eyes because to me the edges seem a bit sharp. How i use this product is to actually place the foundation on my face then I use one of those toothbrush style face brushes to distribute it evenly across my face. So my brush doesn't get as gunked up as quickly with product and I don't have to get foundation on my fingers either. It saves the amount of foundation I use. My foundation lasts probably twice as long now as it did before.

title: Inverness Quality!
text:
This review is for Inverness 24k Gold Plated 3mm piercing earrings in Rose/October. However I should mention that I have a number of pairs of 14k Inverness Piercing Earrings in many birthstone colors including Amethyst, Auqamarine, Emerald, Ruby, and Blue Topaz, & Sapphire. In my opinion Inverness makes the best quality piercing earrings on the planet. Besides the birthstone piercing earrings, I have a number of other designs as well, and a couple of months my daughter had her ears pierced with the October Rose color flower earrings, which are perfect for a 6 year-old's first pair of pierced earrings. She now also has a pair of Inverness Rainbow Flower earrings as well which she switched to after her Rose ones had been in for over 6 weeks.
When it came time to pierce my daughter's ears, I would not have trusted them to any other piercing system than Inverness, as not only are their earrings second to none when it comes to quality, but the same can be said for their piercing system & piercing instruments. My daughter actually smiled throughout the piercing.

Now, about the earrings - These Inverness Piercing Earrings, such as the 3mm Birthstone Post Earrings are extremely well-made with the strong posts that are honed to a sharp surgical point which not only adds to the ease of the piercing, but they are covered in the ear the Inverness Patented Safety Clutch, which is sort of a bell-shaped earring back, that safely covers the point of the post end and cannot by easily removed by little hands.

As an adult who at this point has no need to continue to wear piercing earrings, I actually prefer to wear many styles of Inverness Piercing Earrings, and the birthstones are some of my very favorites. I'm sure that there are many adults who had their ears pierced years ago, who still have their Inverness Piercing Earrings in their jewelry boxes, and more importantly still wear them. They are that good.

title: Verilux Brushed Brass Lamp-Inferior Warranty Service
text:
I was disappointed with both the quality of this lamp after 5 months of very light use and the attitude of the company when trying to fix or replace the lamp. A $200 lamp should not break after 5 months in the first place, especially when it is just standing in one spot with no adjustments being made. I am the only person living in the house, so I know that no one damaged it.

The fixture that allows the lamp shade component that can be adjusted up and down failed, causing the shade portion to just dangle from the pole after I turned it on one evening. When I was finally able to contact customer service after figuring out their hours of service and waiting on hold for 20 minutes, I was told I certainly could send it back at MY cost and "Please enclose a check for $25 for return shipping as well." So it would cost me $25 to ship it and $25 to have it returned $50, in addition to the 50 mile trip to town to ship it, another $25. So I get to pay $75 to return this 5 month old $200 lamp with a 3 year warranty. Some warranty! I was extremely frustrated to say the least. I don't often have a need to return things, but the companies that I deal with normally stand behind their products and take responsibility by providing excellent customer service and product satisfaction. Verilux is certainly not one of those companies.

Fortunately, Amazon came to my rescue. However, I won't be buying Verilux products anymore. The box the lamp came in says that these are manufactured in China - so perhaps the parts are being cheaply made.

Thank you, Amazon! You will continue to my favorite online shopping site!

title: Not impressed
text:
Before buying this watched the “You Tube” videos/ reviews. I have below shoulder length, poker straight, fine hair thanks to being of Eastern European descent. It doesn’t take well to holding a curl despite thickening spray, mousse, etc. In the past have use a Revlon curling iron (with a clip) which actually curled and a Calista Perfect Styler brush style curling iron. Not sure why but the Calista Perfect Styler gave volume that lasted. Had been the ONLY thing that has so far but that was 7 years ago.
Bought this as needed a bigger barrel due to longer hair and retractable bristles as have gotten hair tangled in past. The retractable bristles are okay. They still have tangled several times though. Even at the hottest setting—-410F this will produce a very loose wave at most and it will last no more than 20 minutes if I’m lucky. I’ve used it only 3 times now using very small strands of hair, keeping in for about 20-30 seconds, retract. Little “flip.” Doesn’t last anyway. So disappointed as had really high hopes for this.
May work well (not sure) as straightener or on someone blessed with thicker, wavy hair but for me, even at highest heat- no results. Doesn’t even do the trick of polishing ends and giving any volume by flipping under when just used as brush curling iron to turn under ends (not using retractable feature).
Gave 2 stars as has a larger barrel (not easy to find, retractable bristles can be helpful. Really wanted this to work like Perfect Styler used to but unfortunately didn’t. Not sure why. Heats up quickly, auto off. No real risk of burning fingers or skin. If they come out with an “improved model” with higher heat, maybe ceramic, infrared barrel I would be willing to test. I will keep as won’t return something I have already used on my hair, though only 3 times and hair was clean with volumizing shampoo and thickening spray.

Update: Decided to give tus one more try and carefully watched videos. title: Am I crazy?
text:
I don’t understand the positive reviews. I hit “buy” after reading so many glowing reviews from other healthcare workers…

The stock images of the product and even in the description don’t even match the design of what I received and what other reviewers are showing. The instructions in the description don’t even make sense because of this factor!

The first I wore it was underneath my scrub top at work and I about died from overheating and sweating while doing my basic tasks which are not very physical. After an hour or so I had to take it off because I was afraid that by how much it was digging into my arm pits that I was about to have broken skin. No matter how I adjusted it, positioned it at bra line or lower around my ribs toward my waist, it stretched and rolled up every time. I felt no real support nor correction. It felt way too stretchy for any such effect. I could wrap the strap’s completely around myself with little difference.

I thought that perhaps I should be wearing it over a top to help, but this lovely ballet pink would look heinous and unprofessional over my black uniform. It’s a pretty color in general, but I don’t get it being the only color.

I am 5’2” and currently a fluffy 180 supporting 36H breasts. Because I wear large to extra large tops as to not be strangled, I went with the Large / XL for my curves. Now I will acknowledge I DO struggle with properly fitting bras because I am short between my bra line to shoulders, as my frame is proportioned well, but to a smaller petite scale. I have a true mesomorph frame for hips and shoulders being equally broad, but condensed for a small person. My straps slip no matter how small my band size, and my shoulders are adequately broad in relation to my ribcage. I’ve been blessed with gigantic high ones, to the dismay of any bra, dress, and shirt designer.

I was giving the benefit of the doubt that perhaps I should have went with the Small / Medium (although I am NOT) and with consideration of my top struggles…

That was until I came back and noticed the images vs the item. Unacceptable.

title: High quality product, but not for everyone
text:
As I'm getting older, I wanted to have a boost in my fertility when starting to try. After some research, I decided to try cassava. I took 4-6 capsules daily starting in July until October. There were immediate results from taking it: first ovulation, I was far more crampy than usual. First period was also harder than usual. I pressed on. Around ovulation in October, I was crampy and one day got so dizzy that I collapsed. It turned out I was having ovarian cysts and that month the cyst hemorrhaged. Obviously I stopped taking the cassava immediately. It took about two months for my body to stop producing the cysts.

Clearly this is a high quality product with pure cassava. The company has excellent customer service, and if you are going to choose taking cassava, I would recommend this product.

That being said, if you feel bad or funny taking the cassava, trust your body and stop taking it. It's my own fault that it got as bad as it did with me. I kept saying to myself something doesn't feel right after a month of taking it, but I didn't stop to really think through what was different from the previous month (this was the only new factor).

title: It Works But...
text:
I have been plagued with a degenerative condition of my cervical vertebrae for many years. It's mostly and admittedly due to bad posture. I have tried for years to find a pillow that would provide proper support for a restful sleep but never found one. I decided to try a different approach and seek out a neck brace that might do the trick. I reviewed many and from customer feedback didn't think many would really help and be comfortable which was a key criteria. I saw this product and based on its design it seem to hold great promise.

I've been using it now for several weeks. I wear it at night when I sleep and when I spend time at my work station on my computer. Overall this product does help relieve my neck pain which was the primary objective. However, I was disappointed with the overall comfort for two reasons:
1) the material for the strap and the way it's constructed is scratchy and irritates my skin after wearing it for awhile. If some other type of material (e,g, neoprene) was used that was softer without any exposed sewed seams that might make it more comfortable.
2) the brace that's on the back of your neck has tourmaline inside to produce heat to relieve pain. I found the level of heat to be way too much for me and in fact I think it's unnecessary for me (but fine for someone else). What I've done to diminish the heat and add comfort to the back of my neck is use a small wash cloth between my neck and the brace. That seems to do the trick and enables me to wear it throughout the night.

I also sometimes find that the strap in the front of my neck may sometimes rest on my adam's apple and feel uncomfortable so I have to adjust it. Perhaps a design modification would address that.

All in all it has been a big plus in relieving my neck pain and I'm satisfied about that The other issues are not a major impediment and I'll deal with it. Design changes hopefully could solve these issues.

Also wish they would have/could have made it compatible with Android devices also... there are as many, if not more, Android owners/users as there are Apple these days I believe.

You do need to blow through it once a month even if you don't need it as you have to keep the collector moist so that it works next time. Company says the BACtrack should work and last for 5 years.

Will have to see how easy this is to use under actual conditions it is needed for. Will have to test it more over time to know.

Can't deny the fact that if it saves one arrest or one life it is well worth the cost and trouble to use it.
