text:
This is one of a few ozone generators we purchased to protect against coronavirus.

This one (for the fridge) was primarily to protect against infectious disease that might be attached to fresh foods that we can't exactly wash with bleach or sanitizing wipes.

The fact that everything that is fungible and exposed to air in the fridge started to last FOREVER after installing this device was an unintended result, but it does do exactly what it claims to.

We've had grapes that usually last a week, two at the most, last perfectly well without mold or discoloration for more than a month in the fridge with this running. Ginger, celery, tomatoes - same thing.

This works so well it almost makes you wonder, but the food tastes just as if it were fresh (although maybe just a touch dry-ish on the surface from being exposed in the fridge for the better part of a month).

CAVEAT: This thing takes 4 D cells to work, and don't even think about trying to run it on anything less than alkaline batteries because if you do, you'll be replacing batteries every few days. Alkalines last a lot longer (like around a month) so that's the (only) way to go with this device.

title: Excellent cleaning, disinfection program for contact lenses.
text:
I use soft contacts and tend to build up deposits on the lenses within 7-10 days. I was recently turned on to this product and can say after using for several weeks that it does break up the deposits and leave the lenses like new/fresh.

Two bottles of solution and a lens cleaning apparatus/vial is included in the package, making the overall value excellent.

It's quite easy to use. The lenses are placed inside color-coded and marked (for R/L) baskets. The baskets are snapped closed. The baskets are inserted into a vial which has been filled to a line with the solution. Over the course of several hours the solution works on breaking up deposits and thoroughly disinfecting the lenses. During the process the solution is neutralized to saline water. When the process is completed, the lenses are ready to roll.

Wish I had started using this product years ago, would have saved me $$ from prematurely throwing out lenses with build up.

Recommended for ease of use and effectiveness.

text:
Recently bought this for a long plane flight. I had a couple non-inflatable ones I bought long ago but they were too bulky in the back of the neck, pushed my head forward too much. Went to a few stores and tried a few different neck pillows and was unimpressed with most of them. I saw this one at Target for $14.99 and decided to check it out.

Brought it home and played around with different inflation pressures and found that fully inflated was best for my long neck. Tried it out sitting in the easy chair and it was comfortable on the back of my neck even fully inflated. I used a 21" duffle bag for my carry on and it fit into the end zipper pocket a-ok when it was deflated. It inflates/deflates easily, and it's not hard to get it to be at different inflation levels. Be sure to have the inflation nozzle side down when you use it as the poly fill is on the opposite side.

About the only annoying thing is that my neck did get hot enough to sweat wearing this after a couple hours, but I'm a 'sweater' anyways. It would be nice if the material was something that was more breathable though. The super long "do not remove" tag is a little annoying too, you probably want to remove it before taking it on a flight.

I plan on keeping it next to the easy chair for naps from now on and will update my review if need be.

The full part number on the box on mine was TS45NR12.

Update: Never really used it for the easy chair so decided to store it in my carry-on bag so that I wouldn't lose it. On a recent trip had an issue where the internal valve wouldn't stay closed when first inflating it, it's supposed hold the air in as you are inflating it. So I had to inflate it and then quickly put the cover on it. However after using it on the first leg of the flight it started working correctly again after that. I'm going to try storing it partially inflated and see if that helps, or maybe you just need to moisten the area where the valve seals after its been stored. I'm going to leave a note on it to remind myself to check its functionality before the next trip as that was a little frustrating to deal with sitting in the airline seat.

title: Excellent foot stool
text:
Drive Medical Bariatric Heavy Duty Foot Stool #13037-1

This is a strong, stable, and safe, foot stool. They are so good, I own four of them. Drive Medical and Design is a major manufacturer of medical equipment and supplies for hospitals and other medical facilities, and if this stool is any indication, they make first-rate products. Next time you're in a hospital or doctor's office, look around and chances are you'll see this brand of stand. I'm 6/4 and 270 lbs., and this thing doesn't flex even a little, when I step on it.

Dimensions: 11" x 14" tread, 9" height. The legs/feet flare out slightly for a depth of 14" and width of 16.5", for outstanding stability. Absolutely rock solid and non-tipping, even if you stand on the outer edge. According to my postal scale, the stool weighs 6 lbs.; it doesn't feel heavy at all. (This is the size & weight of MY stools; slightly different from Amazon's description.)

The stool has large slip-resistant rubber feet on 1" chrome-plated steel legs. The tread is thick, ribbed, slip-resistant rubber that has stuck well on my stools, and the welded cross-braced frame is so strong, the stool is rated at an impressive 500 lbs. Drive Medical makes a lighter (5 lb.) stool, the model #13030-1, but it lacks the cross-bracing and is rated at [only] 300 lbs. For just a few dollars more, get this excellent cross-braced unit for the safest foot stool available.

Between the standard chrome plated and the "silver vein" models of this foot stool, the latter is more attractive and looks more expensive.

Con: if you have persistent ants coming in from outside that keep coming you might want to consider getting this product AND placing some poison they take back to the nest, or putting ant bait outside. I have a small child so I am not placing poison in our common spaces. I’ll keep buying this I guess, just wanted to give an update.

Original review: Ants crawled in through a hole under our bathtub faucet. I have been spraying the ants and the areas they travel in for three days with this spray. The spray suffocated the ants immediately and I later washed them down the drain. Learned to be careful and ventilate the room, and continued to spray often. Over 3 days and the bottle is halfway empty, but the ants have stopped coming! Yay! When we tried the another product, liquid ant bait, the ants kept coming for at least a month. I prefer this! Caution, ventilation is best as being to close to the spray can make you cough and feel irritated in respiratory system. I recommend 2-4 quick sprays and then leave the room.

title: Great larger size for dexterity issues!
text:
First off, the packaging is adorable. The box is so cute that it'd make a great little gift or stocking stuffer. Each piece, the long rectangle and hexagon are wrapped separately so as to split up and give them as gifts is also an option.

I have used these kinds of buffers for years. My favorite part is the last step...the shine. It leaves an unbelievable gloss to your nail.

There have been a few reviews stating these are larger than most and it is a little different trying to file your nails but I do not find that to be the case at all. In fact, I have arthritis in my hands at the tender age of 41 and I happen to love these oversized buffers. When I use the small ones my hands cramp up and my arthritis starts hurting. I am a nail junkie and these work great and I don't have any complaints whatsoever. I will not go back to the small buffers after using these.

Again, I think this would be a great gift idea especially for an older person with dexterity issues.

I rely on other customer reviews and feel it is very important to give honest feedback. I did purchase these at a slight discount but that does not affect my review. These work great for me and that is how I base my review. So if you are happy with your current small buffers maybe you wouldn't want to jump on these but for me, I am thrilled with the larger size since not only is it easier for me to use but I'll also get more use out of them since each space is larger than what I used to use.

I do like to sanitize these after each use by putting a little rubbing alcohol on the sides, just using my finger. I think this also prolongs the use, removing any remaining debris.

I would purchase these again in a heartbeat for myself as well as for a gift.

title: Almost No Scent
text:
I'm a shower kinda gal, but that means I don't use the luxury, nice-smelling products available for baths. These sounded like they would add a little decadence to mundane showers. Good theory. Too bad it didn't work.

I admit to using only one of these so far, the lavender one. It is not supposed to get TOO wet so I put it in the front corner of my shower. In that location, it didn't get wet enough to work. So I put it in a back corner. There is got some water, and more if I turned. I could tell it was working because there was a lavender colored stream of product going down the drain. And I could hear it fizzing. But I couldn't smell it. Even when I bent down close to it, it had almost no scent, certainly not the steamy spa effect. My shower is glass enclosed, so it's not like all the scent was escaping through an open door or light shower curtain.

Although this is a nice idea, and would have been good for a gift if it worked, for me it was a bust.

title: Lovely Scent and Refills are Available (Just not here in July 2020)
text:
I love the scent of this lemon leaf and thyme spray. It's refreshing and not floral, not cloyingly sweet. I also really like the simple aluminum (recyclable) bottle that comes with a simple plastic (not recyclable) trigger in the starter kit. The scent contains essential oils, but there is no list of ingredients so I don't know what else is in there. Probably a lot of water. The scent is not quite as strong as I would like for a big room, nor does it last as long, but the pros outweigh the cons.

The aluminum cans are supposed to be refillable, but I couldn't find any refills on Amazon at the time of this review. However, I could find them on the company's product page. I think you could probably find a DIY recipe for making your own, but I doubt I could make anything that smells as nice as this lemon leaf and thyme combination.

title: Good Ingredients
text:
I liked the taste of the chocolate bar quite a bit. The ginger-nutmeg one was okay but not as flavorful to me even though I love both ginger and nutmeg. Those bars seemed too sweet to me, perhaps too much monk fruit concentrate for my tastes? There are no artificial sweeteners, which is a plus. And the ingredients are stellar. Lots of whole nuts and seeds mixed in with the other ingredients. These are relatively small bars with only two grams of sugar but six grams of protein. There are 13 grams of carbs but ten of those grams are fiber, leaving 3 grams of net carbs.

You can get this information by reading the box but you can't get most of it by reading the product page because ingredients aren't listed and only some of the nutritional information is there. The individual bars do not have nutritional or ingredient lists either. That information is confined to labels on the larger box these bars come in. I'm vacillating between e3 and 4 stars, but going with 4 because the ingredients, once you find the list, are really good.

title: Sturdy, Practical, Not Fancy
text:
If you want a permanent or semi-permanent journal for any reason, but you don't want it to be covered in butterflies or skulls, this is a very nice, sturdy journal. The paper is an ivory color, tending toward a bit yellow, and the markings are a medium rusty brown. There is "Date Page" at the top of each page, which you can use or ignore, depending on how you want to use the journal. It is lined, and the top and bottom lines are a little bit darker than the ones between, with tiny marks that can be used for paragraph or column/tab guides.

The book doesn't lie completely flat when you open it, but it's still easy enough to write, but you might need to anchor the page with your wrist as you write. The paper is matte so it accepts a variety of inks.

This isn't the type of journal where you can rip out a page or two and expect it to go unnoticed, so if you use this to write nefarious plans that you don't want seen or reveal that you sneaked out 4 times this week, you're gonna have to swallow the whole book.

The ribbon is a nice touch, but not quite nice enough. It's quite thin, but it's also not quite long enough. I want a ribbon I can pull out of the book and mark my new place without having to open to the old page, and this isn't long enough. Still, it's a nice, sturdy book. Whether it is a good value, you'll have to judge for yourself. There is no current price listed at the time this review is being written.

title: Chewable DGL in general is great but this product is in gel-caps, NOT in the form of chewable tabs
text:
Most people have to deal with the annoyance of hyperacidity and burning stomach, and for some people it's not an occasional occurrence but a chronic thing. Usually what people do to deal with burning stomach or heartburn is to take antacids like Tums, Tagamet or Prilosec. All of these medications work by reducing the stomach acidity.

Tums contain alkaline ingredients like calcium carbonate that directly neutralizes the HCL acid in the stomach for a short period of time (because obviously then the stomach produces more). Tagamet and Zantac work by blocking the H2 histamine receptors, which regulate the acid production on the stomach. They provide a long lasting reduction in stomach acidity, because they lower the production of acid instead of acting on the acid itself. Prilosec and similar drugs belong to the class of the proton pump inhibitors, which again works by reducing the production of acid by the stomach, in a long lasting, and more aggressive way.

One problem that people (including often doctors) don't understand is that when people experience heartburn or burning stomach, it's often not caused by an actual excess of acidity in the stomach, but by a damage of the layer of mucus that protects the stomach lining. The stomach is designed to have a very high acidity, both to digest foods and to protect against pathogens that can be ingested with the food, because most are killed by the highly acidic environment of the stomach. Acids damage tissues so normally there is a layer of acid-resistant mucus that creates a buffer between the acid inside the stomach and the stomach itself. As long as this barrier is in place everything is good.

The mucus production, however, can be reduced by several different factors, like use of aspirin and similar NSAIDs, stress, steroid drugs, etc. If the protective mucus is reduced, the stomach lining will become vulnerable to the corrosive action of the stomach acids, which will create burning, pain, etc.

It seems clear that the best approach is to increase the production of protective mucus, rather than reducing the stomach acidity, yet all the official therapies focus on reducing the stomach acidity. This, by the way, is a terrible idea (unless it's a legitimate case of hyperclorridia or excessive stomach acid) because not only does it make you more vulnerable to food borne pathogens, but it can contribute to an overgrowth of H. Pylori, if that's already an issue for you. Helicobacter Pylori is a bacteria commonly found in the stomach that can overcolonize lead to stomach ulcers. H Pylori prevents a less acidic environment, and it can actually reduce the ph of the stomach acid. So, if you are taking anything to reduce stomach acid, you are actually doing H Pylori a favor, for which it will repay you with some excruciating ulcers.

Additionally, reducing stomach acid also impairs your digestion and assimilation of vitamins and nutrients. Vitamin B12, for instance, requires a certain acidity for it to be absorbed. Same thing for iron and many others.

The only thing that is known to increase the production of the protective stomach mucus is licorice, which DGL is made from. (By the way, I am talking about REAL licorice, not the fake "licorice" flavored candies that are actually flavored with anise and bear no resemblance to real licorice.)

Why not just take licorice, you might be asking. Since licorice can increase blood pressure (which for some people is a concern), DGL is licorice that has the blood pressure raising chemical removed to provide a 100% safe supplement.

When I got this brand of DGL, upon opening the seal and taking out the pills I immediately noticed a problem: they are not chewable tabs like I was used to, they are gel-caps made to be swallowed. If you read online, almost all the sources mention the fact that DGL licorice extract needs to come in touch with saliva to be really effective. Apparently there is something in the enzymes from the saliva that has a synergic effect with DGL.

I've not been able to find a proper clinical trial to support this claim about the need of saliva enzymes for DGL to be effective, so I will take it with a grain of salt, even though there seems to be a universal consensus about this fact.

I do seem to notice, however, that this kind of DGL is less effective than the chewable tabs I was used to, so there might be something to it.

At the same time I'm considering the possibility that my mind is playing tricks and is making me feel like this product is less effective because I know that it should be less effective. Because of this, and because it's a very good supplement (no fillers, no extra ingredients) I don't want to penalize this product too much and I decided to give it 4 stars. If I'm gonna find some hard evidence of the saliva theory I will lower the rating accordingly.

If this product doesn't help, then I highly recommend you try the chewable DGL, which is what I normally use, and find quite effective.

title: You were warned.
text:
This review is for the: Redecker Bath Brush with Removable Untreated Beechwood Handle with Tampico bristles.

Cons:

Let me count the ways I dislike this brush:

1) The head is so big that you can’t brush your back with any pressure (physics below for us nerds).
(I modified the head to make it smaller because of this problem- see pic)
2) The wood is completely unfinished and will begin the slow unpleasant task of rotting the first time you use it.
3) The head will fall off the handle the first time you use it and the only way to keep it on is to glue it on. So
the idea of using it as a back brush AND a hand brush is ridiculous.
4) Another ridiculous idea: the natural bristles. Again, the rotting starts with your first shower. Do you really
want to soak this in bleach weekly?
5) I have $12 back brushes bought in Walgreens or CVS that outperform this brush in every way. See the
picture. (Unfortunately, I have not been able to find a decent brush on Amazon that isn’t too short).

Pros:
If you want a really elegant brush to hang on your wall, one that reflects the best brush-making traditions of 1900, and is made in Germany no less, this IS the brush for you! Enjoy!

Physics for the nerds: Let’s say, in the awkward position of scrubbing your back, you can press the brush against the back with 3 pounds of force. If you are using a 2” diameter round drugstore brush head, that’s about 3 square inches of brush (pi r squared). So you can apply a pressure of 3/3 or 1 psi of pressure to your back with the brush. Now take this monster. Let’s say it has an area of about 7 square inches. Now you can only apply a pressure of 3/7 psi to your back. Now if you’re buying this stiff brush, you want a good scrub, right? NOT with this brush.

title: I purchased the product with great expectation for these reasons
text: I'm using my wife's name as I logged in via her account. I purchased Kokoro cream for treatment of an enlarged prostate (and elevated PSA). Progesterone cream has been shown, in studies and anecdotally, to help with enlargement of the prostate, by preventing conversion of testosterone to DHT and countering estradiol levels in men.  I purchased the product with great expectation for these reasons.  However, upon receiving my product I discovered it contained lecithin (from soy). Men with BPH should avoid soy products.  I was disappointed.  The other ingredients are very good and the progesterone is supposedly sourced naturally. There is much to like about the product but due to its having one ingredient derived from soy, I am not using it. I purchased another progesterone cream.  The Kokoro cream now sits unused, a waste of (IIRC) $24 or $25.  Because of the soy I would not recommend this product. Men should search for other natural progesterone creams.  Look for Roger Mason's book on prostate cancer for helpful information w.r.t. progesterone cream.

title: Best alternative to gloves!!!!
text:
Several years ago, I was talking with my personal trainer at the gym about how my hands were getting calloused from all of the free weight work I had been doing. He had suggested gloves but, I explained, I had tried gloved in the past and didn't like them. Most gloves add too much bulk to whatever I'm gripping and actually make it so that my forearms get fatigued. I also don't like the fact that gloves start to develop an odor quickly since they get sweaty from my workout and from living in my gym bag. Unless I wanted to have several pairs of gloves that got switched in and out of rotation, I would have to wash my sole pair of gloves nearly nightly.

The guy using the weight bench next to me overheard this conversation and offered to let me try his Lynx. I LOVED THEM! They add almost no bulk at all to barbells and dumbbells, they create an amazing amount of grip and they can be washed in just a few seconds in the sink at the gym.

The only problem I have with them (and why I'm on Amazon today... to order another pair) is that you have to be careful about setting them down somewhere and forgetting them. My Lynx were in as good a shape after five years of using them as they were when I bought them. Had I not lost them last week at the gym, they probably would have lasted another five years or more.

title: Excellent, convenient, durable water ozonator
text:
I've owned this SOTA model for decades. It still works well and I still use it for every drop of water I drink. All it takes is 5 minutes of ozone treatment per gallon to not only kill all pathogens, but energize the water and sparkle up its taste as well (there are also 10 minute and higher time settings on the unit) .

I am a bit of a purist. I first steam distill a gallon of tap water using the top-of-the-line H2O Labs steam distiller (shown below); and then I use the SOTA ozonator as a final measure of purification. As I mention in my review of the H2O Labs steam distiller, if you saw and smelled the crud that's left over at the bottom of the distillation chamber after one cycle, you'd never go back to drinking tap water again.

One often hears about the contamination of a municipal water supply, as in Flint, Michigan (2014); or just yesterday (June 21, 2019), the dangerous E Coli outbreak in the entire water supply of Long Beach, Long Island. If any of the residents of these cities had an ozonator or water distiller on hand, the contamination threat would be completely eliminated.

In any event, it's best to take full control of water purification matters with these devices. And it's gratifying to know that the water so treated is cleansed of all contaminants and pathogens.

title: Keeping you on the right side of funky
text:
We are avid outdoorsy folks and therefore, pretty dirty. Something about being out in the wild makes you care very little about silly things like showering. A good swim is usually considered plenty. But yeah, after about day 3 you start to get pretty funkalicious. If you're by yourself, eh, and even if you're with other people, heck, they stink too. I don't usually want to clean up so much to be proper, it's just to freshen up. Get the grease and dirt off your skin, unfunk them feet, the bits and pieces, pits, and the face - not in that order. I've tried countless wipes and meh. I guess they were better than nothing but immediately after finishing, I really felt no different. The wipes were small, not wet enough, and often OVER scented. Just a waste. So I tried yet another brand, SofiesSecret. Sofie!! Where have you been all my life???

Went on a week long camping trip to ME this fall. My hopes were eh as usual but the first night, after a long day of travel, really want to scrub my face down. WOW! What a towel! It feels actually similar to a thin wash cloth. Very damp with solution and this fresh, natural smell. It even suds up a bit. It was such a pleasure and so refreshing I was cleaning everything I could get to while dressed. So, so refreshing. Used these throughout the trip and they really helped me stay non-funky. I actually smelled nice the whole time and they did not dry me out. Never funked my main pair of long underwear - wore them every day. And quite possibly the best part, it made my facial skin look fantastic. This is not something I really care about when doing activity but even wind burned and cold nipped, I almost looked like I had makeup on. A very nice bonus.

The man even got in on the fun and he couldn't get over them either. He liked the subtle smell, moisture, ample man size, and he didn't feel dirty at all to the point he didn't shower right away when we got home. Honest to goodness, he did smell just fine.

These things are now a staple in my gear and no matter why it is you need them, I can't imagine there's a better product to keep you on the right side of funk. Don't normally post pictures of myself but that's my face on day four of sun/wind/cold #nofilter. No products other than using this wipe.

title: Excellent product, does the job. Gives me reassurance and freedom. Could be improved.
text:
Purchased this for use in the home with my mother who is at risk of falling. I use the bed alarm and it functions well. If you are in a similar situation this product will allow you to go to sleep or go about your day confident that your loved one will not get up without you knowing.

I place the sensor pad on the bed beneath her shoulders so I know when she's sitting up. This gives me plenty of time to get to her before she tries to get up on her own. I place it underneath the bed sheet and bed pad used for toileting. Check the position of the pad each time you make the bed to make sure it hasn't slipped. It is very effective and has not failed me as long as the sensor pad is positioned correctly. I am running through the batteries, so will purchase the AC adaptor for use at night.

If I were to improve this product:
1) Make more volume levels. The lowest is still loud enough to travel through walls. It is important, for the person's dignity, for them not to feel so monitored. To keep from bolting out of bed at night I have put a piece of duct tape over the speaker, and sometimes put it under the covers with me.
2) Make the alarm unit lighter and smaller so it can be worn or easily carried in a pocket.
3) Make a variety of alert sounds that don't sound like alarms. Even the chime sounds alarmy.
4) Make it rechargeable.
5) Make the resetting of the alarm unit more obvious.

Note: I do not use the chair pad for a variety of reasons. For the person's dignity, the pad should be camouflaged. That is difficult when she's sitting on a couch. She moves around from couches to chairs several times during the day and its not practical to try to position the sensor on every one or to run around putting it down before she sits (re: dignity). I keep the chair pad in case we get to the point where she is in a wheelchair during the day. Right now she's using a walker.

Note: I purchased this on my husband's amazon account therefore this review will not show up as a verified purchase, but this is the unit I purchased here on Amazon.

title: Keeps My Body in Balance
text:
Ever since I had a hysterectomy well over a year ago, I began taking pre- and probiotics as directed by my OB to help stave off imbalance and to help maintain good bacteria throughout my system. I've tried several brands and Formula Trim has a great probiotic here! I struggled to find blends that didn't trigger a yeast infection, leave me bloated and uncomfortable, or make me feel "off," and I don't want something that I have to refrigerate. This blend checks all of the boxes I look for in a probiotic OTHER than the need for refrigeration. I was really disappointed to discover that, once opened, this needs to be kept in a fridge. Unfortunately, I have to travel a lot for work and it's not worth it to me to have to figure out how to keep a probiotic refrigerated.

The capsules are tasteless and easy to swallow, and I've had no stomach issues or bloat, even when taken on an empty tummy. Because of the price, I began to taper off how often I took these and I was able to get away with taking one every other day and I still felt well-balanced. I don't believe a price can be put on good health, so this would easily scoop up all 5 stars from me if I could easily pack it with me when away from home.

title: A Good Product No One Wants To Need
text:
So I'm old enough now that I have to trim my nose hairs. I've typically used scissors, but that's become a bit of a pain. So I decided to bite the bullet and get a nose hair trimmer. I have to say, this thing works great. The base attachment trims quickly and easily, with no risk of stabbing your brain.

The eyebrow trimmer also works great. I get a few rogue eyebrow hairs that make me look like Thufir Hawat's stunt double from David Lynch's Dune. The trimmer comes with two length settings. I used the longer one and it trimmed quickly and easily.

There is also a shaver attachment. This worked fine, but is a bit small for regular use. It was handy to trim missed hairs, and would work well if you only wanted to travel with one device.

Changing out the trimmer heads is very easy, and just takes a couple of seconds.

My only complaint that would drop this to 4.5 stars if that was an option, would be the lack of a wall charger. The device has a USB-C port, which is nice, but only comes with a usb-c to usb-a cable. No plug in charger. As the bathroom is one of the few rooms I don't have usb charging ports, this is a minor annoyance.

However, overall, this is a great device and I'm as happy as I can be for a device that I really don't want to have to use. :)

I went through a pretty rough patch in my life. I lost 2 dogs, 1 cat, and my best friend/roommate to cancer all within 2 years.

My doctor placed me on Welbutrin but that stuff made me completely insane! 1 day I was angry, 1 day I was completely miserable, 1 day I was unbearably tired. I also had a horrible headache when I was taking it. I felt like was a mindless zombie on Welbutrin. I decided to stop taking the Welbutrin before it settled into my system.

I figured I would try and go the more natural route after reading all the side effects of the other anti-depressant medications they have available. I first tried [[ASIN:B00014DT1W Kira St Johns Wort Tablets - 45 Tablets]]. These seemed to help, but it was very mild and not consistent in keeping my mood up.

Then...there was Nature Made Sam-E. I tried some of the store brand Sam-E's to try and keep costs down, however, none of the other brands even came close to working as good as Nature's Made. And if you shop around you can usually find a buy one get one free at Walgreens, Giant, CVS, or even Amazon!

This stuff helped me through the roughest time of my life. I've been using Sam-e well over 2 years now and if I even missed one dose I would immediately notice a huge change in my mood. I have been taking 1 400mg pill a day since I started. Once in a while I would take took 2 or 3 in a day.

I just started taking 1 pill every other day to give my body a break because I do not like to be dependent on any type of medication. But for those super hard times, this stuff really helped to get me through.

I highly recommend trying Sam-E. Especially before trying any prescription anti-depressants. It is a natural approach to overcoming depression, has low to no side effects at all (I never experienced any), and even if it does not help with improving your mental health, at least it is supporting your joints. ;)

Hope this helps!

title: Perfect size for an anaphylaxis kit
text:
I'm using this bag not as a general first aid kit bag, but specifically an anaphylaxis response kit. Not only can I easily fit my epi-pen set in there, I can fit a 500mL bag of fluids and a gravity tubing line together in one of the side pockets for fast access. I can fit my port-o-cath access supplies in the other side pocket, including a sterile kit and an extra envelope of sterile gloves. All the medications that would go into such a kit (the epi's, epinephrine ampules and needles/syringes; IV benadryl, oral medications) all fit neatly and with quick access in the fabric tray that comes inside. Under that tray I can fit a full 1000mL bag of saline and additional gravity tubing, and I have enough room to keep a copy of my Rx and administration instructions front and center as soon as the bag gets unzipped. And it's not much bigger than a mini-backpack. I was thoroughly impressed for the money, and will be buying another one of these for a travel first aid and medications kits.

Given the review, you've all probably gathered that I'm a tad medically complex; so having this bag available in different colors yet still readily identifiable as medical equipment will definitely make my travel and hospital bag organization much simpler. I wind up having to bring a ton of my own meds to the hospital with me since they're so specific, and this will be a much classier thing to hand to the poor charge nurse than the hot mess system of ziplocks and prayers that is currently in use.

title: Cured my garlic sensitivity
text:
I've been sensitive to garlic for as long as I can remember: I feel hungover the day after eating it.

My Dad, and infectious disease doctor, hypothesized that I had desulfovibrio bacteria in my gut, which produce neurotoxins when given a supply of sulfur (garlic is high in sulfur. He suggested that I try this product.

After taking it daily for 2 weeks, I carefully ate a meal with a little garlic, and survived without symptoms. I gradually ate more and more garlic at dinners over the next couple of months, and have never had a reaction. I'm cured!

I don't know if I will need to take this every day for the rest of my life, or if I have permanently changed my microbiome. I should experiment by stop taking it and see if my cure is permanent, but I am reluctant because its not that expensive and I don't like the symptoms.

Thanks Suntory!

title: My shoes are saved, finally a spray that works!
text:
I actually thought to myself I will be buying this for the foreseeable future of my life no doubt haha. Finally a shoe spray that works. I wear sneakers for work and am on my feet 10 hours a day. part of the reason i have so many shoes is because after a month or so of daily wear they would be rendered out of commission because nothing would remove the foot odor. I would need to get another pair !!! Even if I would use other products or alternate use, as soon as I put it on it was the same issue !! I don’t feel my feet are excessively sweaty or smelly but its just the nature of having your foot wrapped up for hours without a breath ! This spray has really saved me from thinking about shoe odor and allows me to not go through shoes like water !!! I use it almost daily after I get home. I spray the inside making sure to spray from toe to heel. It definitely gets damp so I make sure I do this and allow to dry over night. The first bottle I got the spray nozzle didn’t work and wouldn’t pump - one email to customer service and they sent me another one no questions asked!!! They let me keep the defective bottle and I was able to refill the new one with the broken bottles liquid! Great customer service and I’m now a repeat customer. The bottle definitely lasts me about 2 months with almost daily usage. Sometimes over the weekend I will really saturate the shoe knowing I won’t wear it for a day or two, not sure if that’s overkill but my shoes have smelt amazing so I’m not changing anything lol the smell isn’t perfumey and after it drys it really isn’t very noticeable. I prefer not to mask the smell with strong scents and this makes that possible!

I think it’s important to note that if you have a pair of shoes that are too far gone there is only so much this spray can do. once the bacteria that causes foot odor is deep in the fibers it is difficult to remove entirely and will smell again when introduced to any moisture. I found that using this consistently on newer shoes or before it gets to that point is key to keeping the bacteria at bay.

title: Pretty good
text:
I gave these a go at a few death metal concerts so far. First off, I really appreciate the durable case with keyring these came in. Once you're in the middle of a crowd at one of these shows, things can get misplaced, but I was able to anchor this case down to the rest of my keychain.

Comfort - I had no problem leaving these in for extended periods. Of course you can tell they're there, but I'd like to see a plug that you can't. These are quite a bit more comfortable than your basic foam plug though.

Sound quality - I don't really buy into the notion that these are much better than regular ear plugs. I couldn't tell much of a difference, nor if any such difference was merely placebo.

Ease of use - Much easier to put in than the foam ones you have to crush down to get into your ear.

Value - Overall, especially considering the pretty decent price of these things plus the fact that they come with a good case and are of a durable material, I'd say these are a pretty smart investment. Maybe my ears are already too far gone from years of protectionless headbanging, but I couldn't hear too much of a difference over the cheap throwaway plugs. But I imagine I'll get enough use out of these to offset the cost eventually.

title: No Bluetooth. Good Massage SL Track 2D Chair. Bad Customer Service
text:
This could have been a 5 Star rating but let me start with why it is not:
1) No Bluetooth: Even though the title and description say it has, the chair I received is a different model than what is advertised. It does NOT have any Bluetooth speakers in the chair (see photos). I contacted the seller and their response is to return the chair. After spending 3-4 hours trying to unbox the thing off the crate and big boxes and picking the heavy chair from outside the house (the shipping company brings it on a wooden crate and will not bring it inside the house), I am not going to take it apart and box it up again.

2) The assembly instructions are not very clear. But after some thought you can figure things out. Both the side arm rest panels have a plastic button/hole where the fixed shaft from the chair is supposed to fix into. The one on the left-side arm rest on my chair keeps popping out from the plastic button/hole (see photos). Again, I contacted the seller for this and asked if they can just ship the plastic part but they refused and only option is to return the chair or get a measly discount for this and the above issue with false advertisement.

Other Cons before I get into the Positive stuff:
- Shipping on big crates and leaving stuff outside the house was not a good experience.
- Assembly instructions are very difficult to understand and maybe colored pictures would have helped.
- Pre-set massage functions are limited and there is no easy manual massage setting. Instead of a full program, I sometimes just want some part of the body to be massaged and I have still not figured out how to do that (See photos of remote and menu which I couldn't find when I was trying to buy this)

Now for the good part:
- Very solid chair (except for the left-side thing popping out).
- Looks/appears to be good quality (even though it is not leather)
- SL track is so much better than fixed. The whole family is fighting to sit on the chair for their turn!
- This is 2D massage not 3D if anyone wanted to know. I asked a question but never got an answer on this.
- The airbags do a fairly good job. Especially the legs.
- They provided extra cushion for back and hips which you can take off if you want a more deep tissue massage. If you leave it on, it hurts less.

So again, if the first 2 issues were resolved, I would have given this chair a 5-STAR rating because this is a very good massage chair otherwise.

title: Strong smell but works pretty well
text:
I have often worried about the chemicals in my cleaning supplies, especially since my younger daughter became mobile and licks literally everything in my house. I clean most things with vinegar but sometimes you need an actual cleaner to get the job done.
Then this organic cleaner arrived I just happened to have some day old burned BBQ sauce on my glass stovetop. I sprayed some on there and walked away for about a minute. When I came back the sauce was able to be wiped off relatively easily.
The cleaner itself is a milky white color, and I can't pinpoint exactly what the smell is but it is definitely strong. I used it in my bathroom and had to turn on the vent fan to get some of the smell to dissipate.
The sprayer gives you 3 different settings; stream, spray and off. The spray is perfect for the counter or stovetop that just needs to be wiped down and the spray is for the burned on BBQ sauce on your stovetop.
I wouldn't say it's the best cleaner out there, and I definitely would recommend using this on your mirrors. What I would say is that it cleaned my counters and stovetop well, along with my bathroom sink and toilet. I would recommend you give it a shot if you're looking for an organic cleaner to use in ventilated areas because the smell can definitely get overwhelming. I received a sample of this product.

I added this to my water bottle and sometimes add a few drops of a sugarless flavor to layer ontop, but I don't mind the taste directly, it is kinda like a mild salty mineral taste. One of the first things I noticed is I definitely had more energy and could stand longer without my POTS symptoms flaring.  I have lost a lot of muscle tone from my disease, and I am starting to do mild cardio and light weight lifting workouts again, and there was a huge difference between the days I remembered to take this before, during, and after my workout than the days without it. I felt I recovered faster and kept the energy to workout longer, plus my muscles felt less sore. I struggle with staying hydrated and I'm prescribed IVs at home, but with this supplement, I felt like I didn't need my IVs as often to stay hydrated. I'm excited to share this with other friends in my circle, I understand why it would benefit fit athletes, but it helped me just as much manage my chronic fatigue, nausea, dehydration, and overall maintaining a better sense of energy. I'm hooked for life!

title: Very well made, helps with pain, and my skin already looks amazing!
text:
This device is totally amazing! I’ve been using this for about a week and I can already see a difference in my skin’s appearance. My chronic perioral dermititis and rosacea-acne already look much more clear with less inflammation, so I’ve already started reducing use of my medications. I’ve also used it several times on my arthritic knees, lower back, neck and shoulder, and it seems to help with pain and inflammation. You can use any of the colors separately, or you have the option to use the red (plus the invisible infared light that comes on while the red is on), the yellow and blue lights ALL at the same time, or in any combination, which saves a lot of time vs. using each color independently. The Velcro strap works well to hold the device in a curved shape, and the device quickly becomes flat again when the Velcro is loosened or removed. And when using it for my face, I prefer to lie back with my head slightly elevated, with the mask in front of my face and neck (with the Velcro strap behind my head), as opposed to lying down flat with the device over my head. (I also like using this while seated in a recliner).

The device itself is made of a thick sheet of silky soft, smooth silicone, with the LED panel of lights protected by a clear sheet of acetate, which prevents you from inadvertently touching the lights. The acetate can be easily cleaned with an alcohol free cleaner as needed (I use Seventh Generation disinfecting spray and soft cloth). The included Velcro strap is long enough to wrap around most people’s’ waists if desired, or it can be doubled over itself to create a smaller curved shape if desired. The goggles that are included are soft and work well to protect your eyes from the bright lights during use.

And for what it’s worth, I’m a licensed massage therapist (though too disabled now to help others), so I’ve had the pleasure of using many different professional quality spa products... and this device has the build quality of a professional device, in my opinion. Because this is so well made, and is capable of helping with skin conditions as well as pain relief, I definitely think this is well worth the price! This is MUCH more effective, versatile and more comfortable than the premium LED mask I previously tried! I purchased this at the full retail price from Amazon, and the opinions in this review are completely my own. I find reviews to be very helpful to me when shopping online, so I hope that this has helped you, as well!

title: Works great and helps reduce pressure on my nose
text:
I’ve had a love/hate relationship with my plastic frame eyeglasses for a couple years. I love how the look, and most importantly appreciate how my eyeglasses help me see better, but with no adjustable nose pieces I’ve been frustrated with pain and pressure on the sides of my nose. I’ve suffered from constant irritation issues from pressure (and as I now realize, the friction) of my eyeglasses resting on my nose, so I’ve tried to address this with various types of nose pads, to no avail. I really never considered that my painful issues could be related to slippage until these little gizmos solved both issues!
I’ve used them for over a month now (same pair, still going strong) and have had zero issues with red marks on my nose since then. These hold my glasses snugly where they are supposed to be, which is great when I’m in the kitchen or looking down. And holding them where they’re supposed to fit prevents excess pressure on my nose. I feel like a genius, even though this was a very lucky break. And best of all, these don’t detract from the appearance of my eyeglasses. I can take them off when I need to wash my glasses with soapy water, and slip them back on when needed. I have a feeling one pack would last the lifetime of a pair of eyeglasses frames, assuming you don’t take them off and lose any.

title: Perfect fix for slipping glasses, and much more comfortable than silicone pads!
text:
For a couple years I’ve been dealing with constant slipping and painful nose “dents” because of my plastic eyeglass frames. My eye doctor is unable to make any further adjustments for fit, so they added some adhesive silicone nose pads. These helped with the slipping, but the dents in my skin became worse. I’ve tried 5 different brands of adhesive silicone nose pads (different sizes and thicknesses, butterfly vs. D-shape like these), but I’ve been unable to make my glasses comfortable for the past 2 years. So that’s why I gave these a shot, and so far so good!

My plastic frame sunglasses have a similar type of foam pads and I love them, so I’m not sure why I didn’t think to try foam pads sooner! These feel softer and more “squishy,” than the silicone pads I’ve tried, yet they also have a slimmer profile, which means they aren’t nearly as noticeable. The overall size is also perfect for my frames (Cinzia Designs, CIN-5076). The thinner profile seems to do what I need without adding any bulk, and because they are perfectly sized to the nose rest of the frames, they seem to be distributing the weight of my glasses better than the thicker/slightly smaller silicone pads. The edges of the silicone pads would actually dig into my skin, which is really uncomfortable, but these are slim enough that I’m not experiencing that issue. The foam pads are gripping better than the silicone this far, so I think this is the way to go. I’ll update my review if these don’t seem to hold up well, but so far I’m very happy!

title: Effective but at a premium price.
text:
I purchased this supplement at a local Vitamin outlet because I've noticed a significant decline in my memory and clarity of focus due to the medications I'm required to take. I started taking two per day (the dosage listed) for two days and saw no changes. After two days, I read the fine print on the bottom of the bottle stating that their test subjects were taking four per day, two dosages of two, so I began taking two in the morning and two in the afternoon.

I was surprised to find no jolt of energy or giddy-up, as would be evidenced in a supplement containing stimulants such as caffeine, guarana, etc....so they mean when they say Non-Stimulant. It has ingredients of a true nootropic, but the exact ratios of all ingredients are unknown, you only get them lumped into groups at one group dose.

After a week I noticed a marked improvement; I was able to think more clearly, I was less tired, my memory sharply improved and I did feel better & more confident. However at four tablets per day, to maintain that dosage, I would have to purchase three bottles per month, which I find exceptionally expensive. So at the moment, I'm trying other supplements on the market because I believe there's got to be a similarly effective option without the premium tag.

So bottom line: The supplement is great but I required the maximum dosage to get the most benefits, and averaging $25 for 40 tablets, that equates to the tune of $75 per month ($2.50/day) in a single supplement. But it IS effective. That's why I give it four stars.

title: Won't make those unwanted pounds magically disappear, but its stylish and easy to use
text:
Great scales, streamlined, stylish, and easy to use. Although made of glass, it is sturdy enough for every day use as long as you don't use it as a trampoline. So no jumping and jiggling it to try to get the thing to forget about that chocolate eclair and the two brownies you binged on! And definitely drop kickicking it when you discover you have gained weight over the holidays.

I compared it to my weight on my doctors scales. My old scales were off by 3 lbs (they were 3 lbs lighter, so I have mixed feelings about tossing it out). This scale was dead on! Guess I will have to lose those pesky 3 lbs. At least it has a bright, easy to read display so that my bleary old eyes can read it as I stumble into the bathroom each morning. Some days, I'm not sure that is such a good thing...Remember, if your self-image is inextricably tied up with the numbers on the scale, you need to weigh yourself first thing in the morning, at the same time each day, making sure to give that special someone a thrill by weighing yourself in the buff. And make sure to do this before you eat or drink. Even then, expect some fluctuations due to water weight. This is especially true for women due to hormonal variations, but if you happen to have grazed your way through a bowl of nachos, gobbled down a bag of salty chips, indulged in a pizza, or hit the local salt lick, expect to weigh more the next day regardless of your sex.

Note: I had chucked my old scales out weeks earlier, so when I first looked at my weight on this thing, my heart leaped for joy. Then, I realized the scale was in kilograms. It took multiple tries on my part to convert it to pounds, so hang in there. It will come around. Of course, you may not be all that happy when it does. I rather liked only weighing 45% of my normal weight.

title: LOVE IT!
text: I've been on a skin care rampage the past year searching for products that actually DO something and this is one of my very favorites.  Most of the creams and lotions are totally disappointing (Olay and Loreal have done nothing for me, despite their glowing reviews).  I have very dry, fair skin with some annoying dark spots and large (not gigantic) pores on my nose.  I've only been using it for a couple weeks and I can definitely see a difference.  It decreases pore size.  I apply this after I wash my face with a mild cleanser.  I follow with Hyaluronic acid with a drop of water mixed in, then Neutrogena tone correcting moisturizer with a couple drops of Argon oil mixed in.  My pores have been dramatically minimized.  The dark spots are noticeably faded and my skin is much smoother.  I know this is playing an important part because the improvements were obviously accelerated with its addition.  I've also been using it on my neck and chest where I have some sun damage and I can see a difference there as well.  It's important that your daytime lotion contains a sunscreen with this product.  I did have some initial stinging, but it didn't persist long and didn't result in any visible irritation. I will absolutely reorder this.  The customer service is excellent and they included a couple of generously sized samples with it.  If you have any sort of sun damage or pore issues this is a must-have for your skin care regimen.  I always want to choke when I say this, but I am in my mid-forties. This makes the challenge of finding good products both daunting and exhausting.  I'm so happy to have discovered this.  Now if only I could find an effective eye cream...

title: Received an OPEN BOX! Great product, don’t buy from this distributor.
text:
Let me preface this review by saying I LOVE ScandiShakes! The product itself is phenomenal and you can’t go wrong if needing high calorie nutrition. The taste can be a tad chalky to some, but I don’t mind the flavor. It isn’t very thick and goes down easily - especially when mixed into a milkshake! Play around with various liquids and find your favorite to mix it into. ScandiShakes are a simple and efficient way to get calories in without a consuming large quantities. Great for failure to thrive, cancer, cystic fibrosis, transplant patients, and so much more!

Where it went WRONG...
This 1-star review is for the package I received from this distributor. It was a box that was obviously opened by another customer, sealed with scotch tape and returned. Then shipped out to the next customer without so much as changing the tape to something more than scotch tape! I’m appalled by this and will be returning and purchasing from another distributor. This is for a cancer patient and cannot take any risks. The ScandiShakes themselves don’t expire for awhile so they’re likely is perfectly fine, however I didn’t order an opened box or returned item. I expected to receive a brand-new, sealed box.

Very disappointed in this and hope they do not continue selling opened boxes to customers expecting brand new. Not only is it a cheap move, it isn’t safe and carries risks.

I was excited to purchase from this distributor because the value for price seemed great, but some things are too good to be true. I’ll be paying a few extra dollars to purchase elsewhere in the hopes I don’t receive an opened box.

title: HIGH QUALITY Formulation! Pills in Capsules for Better Absorption! Improved My Joint Pain In Only 4 Weeks! Slightly Expensive.
text:
I have not tried a Glucosamine Supplement before so I was anxious to give the Viva Labs Glucosamine Chondroitin combination a try. I dove into the research and discovered that this particular supplement is designed to help relieve your joint pain, improve skin health, and remove toxins as well as help repair cartilage. Diving into a bunch of clinical studies I found many that showed improve of subjects, and also many that showed it was no better than a placebo. With the scientific studies being divided I figured the best thing to do was to give it a good try.

I compared this to a lot of other products you'd find at Wal-Mart and other online and it seems this product may be slightly less potent per pill than other offerings, but if you calculate the price vs dose ratio it isn't actually much more expensive. I also feel that the capsules allow for better absorption than those solid pills.

I gave this particular supplement a minimum of 30 days to ensure it was given plenty of time. I have back joint issues, knee issues, hip issues, wrist and shoulder issues, etc. So I knew if it worked I would at least know from one of these improving.

A lot of places suggested to take a "higher starting dose" for the first couple of weeks to help build up the body's levels of the supplement. So I took a daily double dose for those two weeks, and then a normal recommended dose the remaining 2 weeks. The pills themselves were fine and I had no issues, they were slightly big but nothing too difficult to swallow.

I honestly did not notice significant improvement until well into the third week. I was getting out of bed and going about my day without even noticing any pain, when previously I acknowledged the pain constantly as it was hard to ignore. By the end of the fourth week I feel that there was a 75% reduction in joint paint throughout my entire body. I look forward to trying it longer to seeing if there is additional improvement.

DISCLAIMER: I was given a sample unit by the company. I did not promise them a review but seeing as I used it, and I love to review things, I was more than happy to provide a fair review to help other users make an informed purchase.

title: Best But Not Good
text:
I take several pills that have to be split, and two of them are difficult. With extra effort, this device gives better results than any I have been able to find on the market recently.
It is NOT, however, without its' own idiosyncrasies. I thought it would have snug slots for all standard size pills, thus assuring centered shatterproof cuts. If there is a slot that precisely fits a pill, it is almost impossible to get the pill to 'lie down' in it and if you do, it shatters. Instead, I place the pills into one of the combo round/oval slots and 'shake' the pill into position and then bring the cutter down while holding the device slanted up in front to keep the pill 'fallen back into the slot.'
Please understand, the pills I take, even my doctor has said are difficult to cut with the further comment that if I cannot split them satisfactorly, he will come up with another solution. This device can do it and perhaps on a relative scale, I should have given it 5-stars.

title: I Think Billionaire Is A Bit Of A Stretch...
text:
Eh..eh...ehmmm, may I start by saying...
These suck.

Hear me out! And come with me and you'll see a world of puuuurely objective opinions.

I will start by saying that I have never tried hemp wraps before; I have only ever used tobacco leaf wraps. What I will say to start is this is quite similar to tobacco wraps and I completely understand why there is another option on the market. But even with this, I feel like this particular falls flat in what makes wraps so sought after.

1. There's no gosh darn flavor!
I clearly didn't heed the warnings in the comments about these being bland. And bland doesn't even cut it because these are criminally minimalistic in everyday possible. And some of the smells I can't even begin to understand how they arrived at that scent for that "flavor". In example, OJK is usually a kush-esque smelling wrap or a completely plain wrap (in my world of wraps). It smells like off brand fruit snacks someone's eating in the other room with the door cracked and tastes like rolling papers. Yes, there is a significant difference between rolling papers and blunt wraps. Come for me, I don't care, It's the truth. Also, every single one, as you can see in the photo, has been opened to find one with flavor. The answer is none, but the grape and blueberry ones do actually smell like they should. Don't taste like anything...but do smell like stuff. Which, I guess, is something. But I literally don't know what some of these flavors should be, js.

2. Do I look like Spiderman? Am I able to secrete a sticky substance from areas that don't make sense, so I can keep my shotty, little blunts together? No. No, cuz I'm Dr. Batman and I don't even have blunt glue on tap on my utility belt. Crazy right? These have little to no stickiness, which is important in blunt wrapping. Just saying, I ain't a miracle worker and I though I do wrap decent blunts...I need help, okay? Batman needs help keeping their blunts together cuz it's either not enough or one lick too much with these.
I am a flawed person asking you to see me, not judge me.

Pluses tho...
1. Doesn't rip easy
2. Doesn't taste super chemically
3. Is a little harsh, but not as harsh as some other wraps I've tried
4. Decently priced

Wrap it up cuz this has been waaay too long? OK, so these are not great and also not good. These are BASIC asf. If you like basic, you are valid in your own right, but I can't understand your life choices. All that aside, I think these would work for people who like a little hint of something, but mostly want to smoke to get the job done. These will get the job done and I think that's the most accurate and sensible thing I can say without digging too deep into myself to find the "right" words. Am I being too harsh? That's relative. You don't read Batman for nice. You read Dr. Batman for real. Mwah.

Baker Vaper or similar, and simply order your juice at 50/50 ratio, double the nicotine you like and extra flavor. The key here is order from somewhere you can get extra flavor like MBV. Then simply mix the juice 50/50 with this VG and voila, you have 75/25 ratio at the nicotine level you want and the extra flavor makes up for dilution. If you have time to let your fresh custom juice steep for a while you only need one extra shot of flavor, but if you are worried about enough flavor, order 2 extra shots. title: Even if it's a placebo, it works!
text: How many of us imbibe some herb, pill or potion that we believe will make us healthier? This is partly out of superstition, but cider vinegar has amassed enough rave reviews that there must be something to it, right? Anyway, this stuff is as unpleasant on the tongue as Listerine, and that's why I down a healthful ounce per day. The price on Amazon is comparable to roadside stands in North Carolina that sell Yoder's as 'home product', and so I order it shipped, five bottles at a time. I am relieved to think that it is a daily swig of Yoder's that has held arthritis, reflux, diverticulosis, seborrhea and a dozen other afflictions at bay in my aging (73 years) body.

title: Immune System Booster
text: A savvy naturopath friend from Boulder swears that this extract is a powerful cancer-fighter. Stock up on it now before others start to believe it and the price increases 20-fold.

title: Does It Actually?
text: Let's face it, you either believe that Yoder's is good for whatever ails you or not. I find the evidence persuasive that a little apple cider vinegar each day (this brand also contains many other ostensibly healthful natural ingredients) helps promote good health. My ex, who turned me onto the stuff, swears that it has done wonders for her nails. Apple cider vinegar, like baking powder, has a hundred proven uses, so it's hardly a stretch to believe that ingesting it will do "something good" for the body. Whether or not the slight alkalinity it introduces into your system helps fight off cancer will probably never be known, but like many such remedies, it can do no harm and probably (like kimchee) does some good.

My feet changed after having kids. I used to have regular feet and never really noticed anyone else's feet, either. But after my first kid, my feet changed. They became some scaly, dry, chicken/lizard skin feet that would crack and peel. Gross, I know. That was my life. I finally got my first pedicure about seven years ago and the lady who did my feet broke a sweat trying to remove the calluses. My sister told me that when you comment on the dryness of your feet and how bad they are, the lady always says, "Oh, no. I've seen worse than this!" Then you feel better and move on. So I said to the lady working on my feet, "I'll bet you've never seen worse than this." All she said was, "Oh, well, you know." And that was it. I had the worst calluses she'd ever seen. On my feet. I tried really hard from then on to keep them pretty but I can honestly tell you there's nothing out there short of a belt sander that would suffice. Lotions work but they leave a residue that attracts every dirt particle within a mile to your feet, and creates a very slippery surface if you're going to shower at all within a week of applying. Since I shower every day, I had some issues with that. I did manage to find a pumice stone I might use if I bathed and could soak my feet. It took quite a while to get results even then. I also had a small oval disk that I would use to try and manage my feet but it took so long to get where I needed to be that my hands would literally cramp up! I know, gross!

Enter this beautiful callus remover. I didn't know it existed until recently when I came across it on Amazon. I read every single review and decided to put it on my list. My sweet husband bought me presents from my wish list and voila! Callus remover for Christmas! I used it that very night. I honestly didn't know what to expect but I was BLOWN AWAY at the results: I have regular feet again! By simply turning this on, my feet were getting softer by the second as I ran it over my heels. It looked like it snowed. Gross, I KNOW! But that's what you WANT to see because that's all the dead, dry skin that pedicure ladies work so hard to get off your feet! I used this for a few minutes and learned pretty quickly that, even for someone like me who has heels that resemble a Saharan riverbed, you can't keep the callus remover in one place for more than a few seconds at a time. I thought I had lost the ability to feel through my heels but if you do keep this thing in one place for very long, it starts to feel hot and burning. I thought it was friction at first, because it is. But it's also because it's so efficient at removing that dead skin that it will remove even good skin you didn't know you had, hiding under however many layers of chicken/lizard skin. So learn from me and don't do that. I never inured myself, mind you, but I definitely felt the difference. This little machine powered through everything I had thrown at it and never even blinked. You don't have to press down hard for it to work, you let the sandpaper do the work for you. Keep that in mind when you use this. That being said, it's still a little powerhouse and my husband, my children, my sheets, and little tiny pedicure ladies all thank it profusely.

title: Adds variety to our daily workbook time
text:
Currently we are working on writing. It takes a lot of practice as most parents know and I feel like a variety of tools help to keep the child interested. We do have many workbooks and try to incorporate crafts as much as we can.

This workbook is different in that it has the special pens/ink that go with it. I often struggle with the fact that we are writing in our workbooks and feel like sometimes I should make copies. But then that’s extra pages to keep track of. There have also been times where we could have used extra practice on certain lessons. Once regular workbooks are used they can’t be used by other children in the family either. I liked the idea of the disappearing ink as well because unlike dry erase, it doesn’t need to be erased.

This is a neat set and it has added some variety to our workbooks we do daily.

title: Plenty of sound options
text:
The white noise sound machine is controlled by the top plastic gray circular piece. There is an included quick start guide with the set that shows all of the buttons and what they do. The symbols are very universal and quickly recognizable. However, it’s certainly always handy to have the resource. It’s also small enough that it could be placed underneath the sound machine to always have on hand.

The white noise machine comes with a cord but it does not come with a wall adapter. So it is important to have one of those or some sort of other outlet.

The touch type buttons on the top of the sound machine are immediately responsive. This has not always been my experience with touch buttons so that’s very important to me.

There are six nature sounds, four lullabies and six white noises to choose from. There is one lullaby in particular I really like that doesn’t get irritating like some others do, but that’s just personal preference. There is a nice variety and it has a very pure sound.

The volume is controlled by the touch buttons and can get quite loud especially for a sound machine. I think it’s very helpful that the speaker is directly on top of the sound machine. It really helps project the sound.

There is a timer option. The timer options are 15, 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes. The button can also be held to turn the timer completely off. I personally don’t use the timer.

The outer portion of the sound machine is a cloudy white color. Everywhere that’s the cloudy white color can potentially light up to one of the night light colors. There is a large variety for different settings and different preferences. The night light can also be turned off and not used at all.

Overall, this is a simple and efficient sound machine to use.

title: Tightly sewn and soft
text:
This sleep mask has the markings just like the dalmatian pup. The ears are 3-D and fold over the face mask but are secured with loops of thread. The inside of the ears are both pink while one is black on the outside and the other is white. Everything on the mask is either embroidered on or a different colored fabric which makes it that much more durable than sticker types or appliqués. The eyes and nose have been embroidered on. They are tightly stitched and a vivid black color. The inside and the outside of the face are as soft white fabric. The strap for the eye mask is black and has good stretch.

This is a really sweet sleep mask and could fit a younger kid or an adult. I personally wear it with no problem for fit. My kids recognized the character right away as it has been very well done and looks just like the puppy. Definitely a fun but practical sleep mask. I also machine wash on gentle.

title: Slight typo on the box but doesn’t affect the product
text:
So I opened the box with the bath bombs and kept reading the outside of the box trying to figure out what was wrong with the words. I think my brain was auto correcting it. So the mistake is a letter off but I can assure you it doesn’t affect the bath bombs. Plus my littles can’t read it anyway.

The bath bombs are a very large size. They are beautifully variegated colors and smell great. Each bath bomb is wrapped in plastic and then in tissue paper. The bath bombs say they are scented with essential oils but the essential oils are not labeled individually on the bath bombs. So that’s a bit of a mystery.

The large size of the bath bombs provide color, fizz and scent to the tub. They have not irritated my children’s skin at all. They enjoy holding them and playing with them as they break down to add color to the tub water.

After their baths are done , I drain the water and rinse them with clean warm water before towel drying. This system works and keeps their skin protected and not irritated. Also I have not experienced any staining of my tub.

title: Thick bags

title: A bit dicey...
text:
.
New to the supplements industry is forskolin extract, said to help increase energy and metabolism to burn fat.

This Nature is Best brand offers a daily 250 mg serving (2 capsules) of standardized 20% forskolin extract. The two capsules are taken one each, 30 minutes before a meal. The 60 capsule bottle lasts 30 days.

Like so many manufacturers of supplements, Nature is Best makes what I would call some inflated claims. For example:

*This brand offers "the best and purest 100% Forskolin available in the market." Maybe, maybe not.
*The product description calls this supplement a "premium formula," but there is no formula here, just an herbal supplement.
*The product description refers to "Nature's Best 125mg 20% standardized Forskolin." First, a serving actually is 250mg (divided into two doses). Second, the name of the manufacturer is not Nature's Best, but "Nature is Best." Nature's Best is a mega-wholesaler of whole foods that likely wouldn't appreciate this confusing description.
*While they're usually just humorous, product descriptions written by persons for whom English is not a native language (or for whom high school English class was an occasion for napping) can cause confusion. Like this one: "APPROVED BY THE EXPERTS---This amazing dietary supplement is made in the USA in top Utah laboratory and it is approved by FDA." The writer apparently intended to say that the facility in which the supplement is manufactured, not the supplement itself, is FDA approved. This is an important distinction. The FDA neither reviews nor approves supplements. I would like to think this particular product description is a syntactical error, rather than a flat-out attempt to deceive.

Regarding that last concern,I erred in ordering this brand because it doesn't meet a hard-and-fast rule I have for every supplement I ingest--production in a GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice)-certified facility. While this brand might be produced in an "FDA certified" facility, it says nothing about a GMP certification. Perhaps worse is that it makes no mention of third-party testing, which has become a gold standard for supplements in the U.S.

Having said all that, I will say that this product does help me with cravings and appetite control. Notice that I said it "helps me," not that it does it "for me." It's a tool in my arsenal against a lifelong tendency to overeat. For that I'm giving it three stars. But I won't be reordering it because of the dicey product description and apparent lack of GMP certification.

I recommend shopping around.

title: A different view of these sponges....
text:
.
Are these the greatest sponges ever? Depends upon what you're looking for.

Reviewers seem divided by one primary issue -- the texture of these sponges. I think they're missing the point. Texture isn't right or wrong; the issue is what kind of texture your face needs. This sponge, as stated on the Amazon product description, is "gentle," a description that automatically neutralizes complaints that the sponges don't "scrub" or exfoliate enough. These are not "scrubbing" sponges.

Having said all that, I can say that I really like these sponges. I don't need or want harsh exfoliation, but just a good face-washing -- something better than my bare fingers, but less trouble than face towels that require frequent washing. The shape of this sponge is just right for the face. The narrow end is for eyes and nose, the larger end is for chin, cheeks and forehead. The sponge fits these areas very nicely, and it's easier to control than larger sponges or washrags.

Another complaint of some reviewers is that they don't know "what's in the sponges." Again, the Amazon description gives that information. "Our sponges contain only TWO INGREDIENTS, ground root of the konnyaku (konjac) plant, and bamboo charcoal. No chemicals, no parabens, and no toxins." The konnyaku plant is edible and made in a variety of ways, including use as a dietary fiber and weight loss ingredient. As a sponge, it's particularly good for sensitive skin, or for people like me who just don't need or want a rough exfoliant.

The bottom line here is that these sponges are neither designed nor marketed as strong exfoliating sponges, so if that's what you want, these are not for you. If, on the other hand, you want sponges that will scrub/buff your face and leave it ready for your serum or moisturizer, these are terrific. They make cleanser go further, they 'buff' my face without scraping off the skin, and my serum goes absorbs better and more quickly after using the sponges. I clean the sponge after each use by squeezing it flat between my palms several times until all the soap is squeezed out, then hang it from a hook to dry. I use it morning and night.

So, why am I giving them four stars instead of five? One reason: price. Five dollars each seems a bit steep. It's made from a plentiful Asian plant, and while everyone deserves to make a living from their products, it seems the price could be a bit lower on these. Other than that, I recommend these sponges fully.

title: Maybe not for crowns?
text:
Nice to try, won't buy this brand again, but would be interested in trying another.

In the morning I feel a little build up behind the back of my bottom teeth (where my tongue touches) and on the cheek side of my molars (which are porcelain crowns). I've been wondering if perhaps when I finish brushing I should mix the used paste with hot water then gargle with it to better reach all areas of my mouth? Maybe that would help with the bacteria growth from my tongue? Maybe I'll try an organic mouthwash and see if that helps.

The taste is gross, but after several days I don't notice it anymore.
Also, spitting out the brownish residue was a touch off putting at first because I couldn't tell if my gums were bleeding or not.

I have noticed that my gums aren't as sensitive as usual, don't bleed as much when I floss, and seem less cold sensitive.
My teeth don't seem any whiter, but they are shiny after brushing (as expected).
I have noticed that my mouth isn't sore from brushing anymore, and I don't find skin strings in my mouth in the morning.

Buuuuut, I'm not so sure this toothpaste works for crowns. I notice my real teeth feel very clean (and stay clean) but my crowns always feel dirty on the chewing surfaces. Perhaps the porcelain has been scratched from the normal toothpaste and that's that I'm feeling?

I also don't like how the coconut oil coats my toothbrush and bristles and makes it harder to clean and sterilize.

EDITED: I forgot to mention two things:

First, I'm not sure how, or if, this has helped to freshen my breath, but I haven't noticed a bad breath or a fresh breath smell either.

Second, because of the coconut oil the container leaves a ring on my counter and drips oil down the sides. .
