text:
I really wanted to like this helmet. Unfortunately, it's poor tubing makes the contraption largely useless.

The two tubes from each can holder join and form a single tube which flows to the mouth. Unfortunately, the tubes were overly compressed and bent early in their design and, as a result, any liquid pulled through the tubes is unbalanced (between the two sides) and full of air bubbles. Essentially you will be drinking 10% from one side, 40% from the other and 50% air from the poor connections. You'll have a belly full of air before you get a mouth full of soda (or your choice of canned beverage).

While I greatly desired it, I do not recommend this product. I hope there is a better alternative.

title: Smells Good But Not a Real Bomb
text:
The best part about this product is the presentation: It comes as a set of six individually wrapped tablets on a very nice box. One caveat is the box reads "Showen Steamers" and not Shower Steamers, which I take is the name of the Product as this apparent misspell also appears on their product pictures. Minor detail but worth mentioning

The instructions tells you to don't put them under a direct stream of water but at the same time they have the name bomb on the product and show a lady on a bathtub. This is confusing as these tablets are clearly not bombs but just a way to make your shower smell good and have some nice smelling vapor while you shower. Using it as a bath bomb will be a failure and not the intention of the product, but I can see some people will use it this way, with the expected poor results

Smell is good but very faint, and it will depend on how sensitive you're are to perfumes. If you get allergies or are easily affected by any fragrant -like me- you will like these steamers. In the other hand, if you're looking for a strong perfume and long lasting fragrance, these are not for you

title: Professional iconic ironing brush----BEST MOMMY BRUSH EVER!!!
text:
I am always on the go as a mom, and I typically throw my hair up into a quick bun. My husband is over the bun. I always have to look for a way to get my hair done in a fast, efficient way. This lovely ionic ironing brush does the job. This brush is a little bit larger than my normal brush. I would say it's roughly about 9 inches. I like that this brush has an LED indicator with temperature gauge. Looking at the temperature you can set it so you don't burn your hair. The brush heats up fairly quickly. I like that the brush detangles your hair. This brush also gets very close to your roots and helps flat iron it better than if you had a flat iron up against your roots. When pulling through my hair towards the end, the tips of my hair did become slightly frizzy. The easiest way to handle any type of phrase throughout your hair from this iron brush is to add a little bit of Moroccan Oil and the job is done. Overall this is an excellent brush for on-the-go people. Every mom should have one.

I have taken ashwagandha for over 7 years now and I tried many different brands. This one was on an extreme discount so I deviated from the brand I normally buy to take advantage of saving money. I became skeptical the product and looked inside of the container that I keep it in and found a hair, which I'm not sure if it's animal or not. I was so horrified that I did not think to take a picture and threw it in the trash. I ordered the ashwagandha that I normally order so that I could compare, and I've taken a picture so that you can see - on the left is this product (which you can see little brown spots - I'm not sure what that is), and on the right you can see the quality product that I normally buy, which is pure and clean. Honestly, I don't know what is in this product, what it's cut with or what the brown spots are but Im sending all the packages I bought back to Amazon. The moral of the story is if the discount is too deep there's probably something wrong with the product.

As a side note, I went to the company's website address that is on the package and it said "domain name does not exist". Very concerning.

Molly's Suds cleaned well. And that's it. I purchased the liquid because I do a couple loads of cold water washes a week and the liquid supposed to dissolve easier.

I thought about using the powder version of Molly's Suds until my husband convinced me to make our own. It wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. And I'm glad I did. I can place the powder into the soap dispenser even on a cold water wash and it dissolves without a problem.

title: got rid of a very loud squeak in my daughter's room.
text:
The product worked just as it promised. There were 2 spots in my 2yr old daughter's room that squeaked. One was next to her bed which was so loud it would wake her from her sleep if we walked over to that side. Needless to say, we avoided that side of the bed. Not any more though! I used 5 screws in total. The first 2 were wasted... and I blame that to the joist finding bit. Although following the directions told me there was a joist underneath, the squeaks were still there. I just switched to using the hammer to "hear" where the joist was and found them easily. 3 screws did the trick and the squeak was gone!

The other squeak I mentioned earlier was nearby the door to her room. It was very small but I still wanted to get some use out of this thing and so I used the hammer to find the joist and used 2 screws to get rid of the squeak. EASY!

And even though I know where they were, I couldn't tell they were there by seeing or feeling. The carpet seamlessly covered the screw and the snap off part was undetectable with my fingers.

Excellent product!

title: More Effective Than the "Non-Lex" Formula, But Still "Not There"
text:
I thought after using this for a week after finishing the regular Braini formula that I was on to something really great. I really thought this would be a better solution for me.

Compared to the regular formula, this is three capsules instead of two capsules per serving. If you look quickly you may not notice this major difference and how it contributes to an obviously higher amount of each ingredient in the formula (925 mg vs 700 mg)

Further, this adds Omega-3 DHA and Zinc to the formula. I am not sure which of these factors led to it working better for me, but I would probably be safe to assume it was the overall serving size versus what I was seeing with the original formula.

All said, this had a decent impact on my focus the first couple of weeks of use. After a month, however, I wasn't able to notice anything compared to if I missed a day. I tried this by using it five days a week and taking two off. Sure, there are always traces of supplements that remain for "off days", but I got to a point where I didn't feel too much different. That has been magnified in the time since I emptied the bottle. I really want to think that these ingredients, unique that they are, could be more beneficial than they are.

Is it worth a shot? Absolutely. Their brain test and money back guarantee is pretty interesting. If you are so inclined, I think it's worth trying this out. Otherwise, there are many other proven ingredients that you could either take individually or combine into your own stack for goals trying to be reached with BrainiLex.

title: Good, Not Great Supplement for Brain Focus
text:
There is a lot to be said for this supplement. I thought it did a pretty decent job within the first two weeks but then leveled off for the rest of the 30 day period. I found that I could measure performance being marginally better when using this versus when I took a few days off after. It was on the third day after that I knew that something about this supplement did in fact work for me.

That said, I find that there are other options that provide better value and better results. In fact, their other product (which is a little stronger in three capsule form) is significantly stronger than this one. However, I still find other options are available with other ingredients that work as well for me at a lower cost.

My suggestion would be to try this product first, take the 30 day challenge (I did not take it) and if it works great for you, awesome! If it works pretty well and you're fine continuing something, try the Braini LEX formula they also have.

title: Love the Serum, But the Toner Leaves a Little Too Much Moisture/Grease
text:
This is a nice overall skincare set with the serum being the better half of it for many reasons.

I'll start with the scent. I really, really like the scent of the serum. It's a lemon type of smell that works well for me. It absorbs pretty well and is drawn in for the most part by the accompanying toner.

The toner isn't my favorite. It doesn't absorb very well on my skin and I find that my face is shiny about 2-3 hours after applying. I thought at first maybe the serum was the contributing factor, but found that when I used just the toner there was no difference. However, with just using the serum, I did not have the same issue.

All said though, there are some great ingredients in both of these products. I think that other than the greasy feeling, I like what it did for my skin tone and consistency. I would recommend it with reservation.

title: Good Ingredients that Strangely Had Zero Effect on Me
text:
I have gone through the entire bottle of this supplement and can report that nothing changed for me. I didn't feel increased energy and my focus was no different. In fact, during this time (and there were some other factors I am sure) I felt LESS focused.

I am not sure what it could be other than the fact that some of the ingredients can be obtained from a number of different sources. There is a lot of diversity in the "types" and quality of these ingredients. That's not to say that all of these ingredients are of poor quality. It's more likely that it wasn't the "type" that worked well for me. Unfortunately I can't recommend the product since it didn't work.

title: Good Quality Black Seed Extract
text:
I am a huge black seed oil (Nigella Sativa) fan and have used it for YEARS. I don't use it for skin care, although it definitely helps in that regard too. For me, it's all about building my immune system up as well as I can. This is one of the core ingredients in doing so.

The quality of this seems to be good. I do like the fact that they were able to use an extract, which can result in a better "use" of this supplement. Sure, drinking the liquid straight out of a bottle does have advantages, but you really negate that when you're able to extract the right "stuff" that matters to the goals you have.

I would recommend this brand and product based on the fact that it seems to have worked as well for me as my other favorites. With that said, it must be pretty good. :)

title: A Very Yummy Chocolate Collagen Treat That Takes the Cake...or the Fudge! 🍫
text:
There are so many collagen powders available to put in the coffee. I measure my success by a couple of areas: flavor and how well it settles into my coffee. Many of the collagen powders I have tried clump at the bottom and don't stir in effectively. Then some that do blend in well don't have the best flavor. Yes, I have had some vanilla and other flavors that I really like, but this one takes the cake...or is it the fudge?

This collagen has a really good chocolate flavor. It doesn't dissolve perfectly, but it doesn't clump in the bottom of my coffee as so many other collagens have in the past. I get a little bit of the powder in my last sip, but it's acceptable given the great flavor. I think that the addition of protein (whey and milk) is great and at 20g per serving, you're getting quite a boost there. So that is a definite bonus for me.

Overall, this is one of my favorite collagens to date. I find that I like a lot of them I have tried more recently, so I will keep this review updated if anything changes.

title: Bland Flavor With Minimal Impact on Workout
text:
Some of us prefer a little less flavor to our pre-workouts. I definitely would be up for less aftertaste and more impact at the expense of too much flavor. This is a product that after one scoop in ten ounces of water tasted more like water than it did any type of berry.

There are a ton of ingredients in here that SHOULD have engaged me much more than it did after 15 minutes of use for a period of five workout days. Each day I felt the same. I felt a slight buzz followed by a pretty difficult workout compared to when I use other supplements for my pre-workout. My workouts were around 20% less effective using this than with other supplements.

To make sure that I wasn't having my own placebo effect because of the lack of flavor, I tried this again after going back to another supplement and also doing a workout with no pre-workout. Further, I tried two servings to see if it made a difference. The flavor was of course more pronounced. However, the effectiveness after the 15 minute "slightly better" buzz was still less than other supplements. I am not sure if I am just not responding to the ingredients or if I needed more than one or two servings to get results.

title: Good Taste with Great Ingredients for Intra or Post Workout Energy
text:
This is one of the better initial tasting post-workouts I have tried. Yes, there is that BCAA aftertaste that happens with nearly every supplement. However, in this one it is not as pronounced. I otherwise really enjoy the flavor of this After Party.

Without this it is more like a hangover, so it's a great play on words with the product name. This does keep things going and has kept me from crashing or otherwise being sore. Unlike many other post-workouts, this one has caffeine in it as well. That is a nice thing to have to keep things flowing for another half hour or so after finishing a workout.

I would definitely recommend this based on the ingredients alone, and would further recommend it on the fact that it works. I'll give a five star recommendation to anyone who can figure out the after taste plus give me the ingredients and impact of a great intra or post workout supplement.

title: Inconsistent Sizes, Inconsistent Flavor = No Way of Getting the Correct Serving Size
text: These gummies were very disappointing to us. They appeared to be broken apart, the taste was inconsistent across the board, and I just simply don't trust them to be effective. Sadly we ended up discarding the bottle because of what we saw as potentially poor quality control. Perhaps they had melted in transit? I have no idea, but I can't recommend this.

title: Works for a SINGLE Use - But Changing the Attachments is Nearly Impossible
text:
We came to terms very quickly that we were going to use ONE attachment on this device. That attachment is the head shaver. No, I didn't use it on my head, but I did get good use of it as a body trimmer. The blades dull out really quickly and there is no cleaning solution included with this (unless I was just missing it from my box). When it is fully charged, it works VERY well and has a nice close shave without any issue. A few uses in though showed a bit of dullness that didn't hurt the skin, but instead "skipped" hair that should have otherwise shaved off.

This could be a great set if there was more quality control and a much, much easier way to change the attachments. We tried the nose/ear hair trimmer one during our initial use and found that it worked great, but we ended up breaking the attachment when trying to remove it.

There are better products on the market for all of these needs, and I'd recommend you check those out first.

title: Five Star Ingredients, One Star Flavor
text:
Sometimes products meet right in the middle with their quality and usability. I have used "sweet" preworkouts in the past, but most of them use terrible ingredients as artificial sweeteners. I am personally a fan of stevia and think that it may have been an ingredient that was missing with this. That said, I can't be sure because I have NO idea what this is SUPPOSED to taste like.

Let's start with monk fruit, which is an ideal sweetener. However in this case there either is not enough or what is enough is countered by some of the taste of the nootropics and other preworkout ingredients. Would the addition of stevia helped this? Would those who are for whatever reason opposed to stevia had been more open to this had there been a better taste because of it?

I am not sure, but I do wish that there was a better flavor for this as the ingredients ARE good and they DO help once you choke it down....but I am not willing to choke something like this down when there are numerous alternatives on the market.

title: Significantly Helps with Digestion and Overall Belly Well-Being
text:
There are a number of probiotic supplements on the market. Many of them make the case that they are better than the next one based on having billions and billions of strains and other mumbo jumbo. Reminds me of a famous burger joint. :)

Anyhow, this is one of the best probiotic supplements I have used for digestion help. I have never gone so long without any type of discomfort in my belly prior to using this. Sure, there are always going to be things we eat that cause some discomfort, but overall this has been wonderful. At a cost of what appears to be less than 50 cents per day, this is a valuable addition to one's daily nutritional intake. I look forward to continued use and to seeing great results.

title: Good Ingredients, Decent Flavor. Better Than An "In the Air" Brand
text:
I have tried two different elderberry based gummies in the past few months. This one from High Level is, well, a higher level gummy. There is significantly less added sugars and less not-so-good additives in this formulation.

The flavor is not the best but the gummies are indeed edible. They have a sort of "dry" feel to them versus any other gummy you may be familiar with. However, if you are not super sensitive to the feel of your gummies, you'll be just fine.

I can't speak to the effectiveness of these other than to say that I have come close to catching a bug this winter only to have it quickly leave my system. I do take other supplements as well, so I can't conclude that this elderberry supplement was the one factor. All said, it could very well have contributed to my well-being.

Give it a try for sure I say.

title: Great, Subtle Energizer
text:
I have tried two products by this brand - the other being a supplement that time releases energy ingredients around the time you should be waking up. I loved the idea there, but wasn't sure if I could totally correlate the effect - but I think it worked.

I know that the Stay Up booster works - and works very well. It has given me a nice, subtle sustained energy that lasts several hours. My problem with most energy supplements is that they don't work at all or they work too quickly and crash and burn soon thereafter. This is a very nice median. I find it even more effective when I take two capsules instead of one. I can't recommend this since the directions imply differently.

Great supplement for sure with a variety of great ingredients to help get through the day.

title: Super Great Case for my T:Slim X2
text:
For the last few years I would put my T:Slim pump (X2 and prior) into my pocket. When the Dexcom integration became available, the pocketing of the pump would result in a communication error. I needed something to fix this. I tried putting my phone in the opposite pocket. I tried as much as I could to have my Dexcom sensor on the same side as my T:Slim. I wish I had realized earlier that all I needed was a belt loop style case.

Now I can carry my pump on my belt loop without any signal loss. It's easy to take off of the loop if I am not able to bolus or perform other functions. While you can adjust the holster to align your pump vertically or horizontally, there i still SOME challenge to entering data as the pump is either sideways or for me upside down. I put up with this slight inconvenience for the fact that my CGM data from the G6 is being transmitted 100% of the time now versus consistent disconnects in the past.

The case seems to be very sturdy. You can change your infusion set without taking the pump out of the case. Just an overall great solution to so many challenges.

I experience almost no ear fatigue from usage so far. Hopefully that remains true.

Solid purchase.

title: Nice
text:
There is a lot that makes this deodorant the best thing I have ever stumbled upon and I'll start with the fact that It's not "thick" in consistency whatsoever and yet it does a way better job than any deodorant I've ever used. In fact, rubbing it on, it does not even feel like you are putting product on your skin. It's like rubbing yourself against a nice smelling bar of something that leaves its scent on your skin, so the residue it leaves on your armpits is super light and not visible to the naked eye unless a tiny bit of it gathers up in the folds of your armpit, which will happen with anything. It's that unnoticeable feeling-wise, which is just amazing since I am used to seeing and feeling the deodorant from a regular bar. I used to use Lady Speedstick before deciding to switch to an aluminum free option.

I actually only tried one other aluminum free deodorant before this one and it did not bode well for me. That was the lavender scent from Love Beauty and Planet, which has a much stronger perfume scent to it than anything. That other one was working out "meh" for a few days. I always had to keep reapplying it though because I would smell heavily of BO within only a few hours. So every three or four hours I was applying it and still the faint scent of body odor would waft through and intermingle with strong artificial lavender.

I'm glad to say that is not the case at all with this brand. I think I found my go to from now on, as long as the success of it keeps up. I've been putting it on only once a day in the morning and then again at night and I have not smelled like BO even ONCE since using this deodorant. It is that effective and it's almost magical just how effective it is for not having aluminum. It does use bamboo and zinc, so it seems that is a winning combo.

I will also add that the previous aluminum free brand I tried did not give me a rash at first but after about a week, it started irritating my skin, which led to a rash that persisted for four days even after I stopped using it or any product for that matter. That's when I found this brand and ordered it and awaited its arrival. This one has not irritated my skin in the slightest and it feels light, like there's nothing on my armpits really. My aluminum deodorant would clog my armpit follicles and cause ingrown hairs. This brand appears to be very good for not doing that either, so far at least.

The smell is light and airy and not artificial smelling at all. It smells like Fruit Loops, or like how real lavender smells. Can't really smell much of the vanilla but that is okay. I DO hope they make other scents besides just the pine, the lavender that this one is, and non scented in the future. Something with citrus or sweet pea would be absolutely fantastic.

However, I will say that I do think that the price is a few dollars too high. If this bar were around $8 to $10 instead, it would be a lot better in my opinion. Especially since the creator of this brand does not have to invest in more expensive packaging other than paper. I wonder why the cost is so much higher, if that's the case? The amount for the cost is pretty disappointing, in my opinion. I know the ingredients for the amount you get are not worth that much. It is my only real gripe with this brand, but it is a biggie for those who want a healthy and eco conscious deodorant that actually works but are not rich by any means. It's one of the main reasons a lot of people don't want to make the switch - because a lot of aluminum free deodorants are WAY too overpriced, so they just end up sticking to their $4 bars because they simply can't afford it.

I don't think body healthy and eco conscious products should be exclusive to only those who can afford luxury items. Seems counter-productive to me if the goal is really to get everyone on board to help their bodies and the environment. That's really the only reason I give this four stars instead of five. I've been using it almost 2 weeks now and it hasn't let me down since, so I will likely be a return customer as long as the price goes no higher.

title: Not for Me
text:
This is an attractive little gadget. It is shiny and ergonomically shaped to fit in your hand nicely. The blue is very bright and shiny. The "business" side is a little sticky, which I guess is how the hair removal takes place.

There was a label directly over most of the brief instructions on the little box, but I was able to find them elsewhere. I followed them. I chose my forearm because it said to use a part of the body that did not have sensitive skin, and because I have never shaved there the hairs were easy to see. I also chose a small area on my leg in the back that I somehow always manage to miss when shaving, so I knew I'd have that 2-3 week window that they instruct you leave open between uses of this stone. I made sure my skin was clean and dry and totally free from lotions, etc.

Then I moved the Hair Eraser in a circular motion, using some pressure but not being too aggressive. I have to say that maybe I'm missing something, but there is no way I'm devoting the time it would take to do my legs and actually remove the hair. You will see from the photos I'll upload that, while some hair was removed, it was not a whole lot. The spot on my leg was better, so maybe it works better on shorter hair, but it is still time consuming. It has a pumice effect, and there was some flaking. I stopped when it started to feel like I might damage the skin. The skin on my arm and that one area of my leg experienced a mild burning sensation afterwards. I did use a moisturizer afterwards, and you definitely need it. My skin was flaky.

Frankly, I prefer shaving. It is quick. Sure you may nick yourself, but it doesn't happen that often. The stone is already a little scratched from just this one use. I don't see it lasting more than a few months.

title: Don't say 1800 Billion
text:
Been taking these pills for 20 days with no issues. Seems like good insurance to take probiotics, recommended by several articles/podcast guests that I trust. No weird tastes, no weird reactions, no weird side-effects. Pretty sure it's helping, all systems seem heathy, running like clockwork.

But what is weird, is the 1800 billion claim in the Amazon title. What? A little math shows that's the total number of CFUs in the bottle. What? (I did the math, seemed quicker than counting them!) You have to take 3 pills a day to get 60 billion CFUs. Knocked half a star off for that. And then, looking closer at the label, while I didn't see anything bad, Made in USA etc all good, there could be more. More certification, more transparency, more details, more variety. So knocked another half point off.

Four stars. Hope this review helps you.

title: Much better than a multivitamin pill
text:
Latest research suggests that daily multivitamin pills are a waste of money, and do no measurable good for otherwise healthy Americans that don't need special supplements for medical reasons. Oh. Dang. What I do now is take these powered mixes as a simple insurance policy, giving me a wider mix of supplements at one go from what has to be a healthier non-chemical source than old multivitamins. Has prebiotics and probiotics, antioxidants and fiber.

The taste is mostly sweet green apple, with no weird aftertastes or gross burps. The fine powder mixes quickly and easily. Seen no adverse reactions. Really like that it's vegan and certified organic made from US plants, not cooked up in some Chinese garage. Does it work? Well, I'm pretty sure it doesn't do everything they claim, but it is good ingredients and is my tasty easy insurance policy, replacing old multivitamins. Hope this helps.

title: Great source of protein
text:
I'm not a vegan, and not a vegetarian either as I eat fish. So I don't need to use vegan protein powder. But it's cool and healthy to get protein from pure plant sources, to mix things up, and I like that this is made from certified organic brown rice & peas. They are the two ingredients listed first. With no "proprietary blends" or other mystery meat nonsense in the list. Very fine powder, super easy to mix. Taste was more subtle than many chocolate protein powders, little weak, but it was just fine for me.

It's low fat, low sugar, low chemical additive, no-milk product, mostly organic protein powder. It does have stevia, however. No huge impossible claims on the tub. FDA registered plant, not Ripped Bob's Backyard Secret Recipe or shipped in from China. I liked it. Hope you find this review helpful.

title: Pure moringa
text:
We have a moringa tree in our garden. Could conceivably make this at home, but would be way too much work. Really like that this is ground super fine, certified organic, pure clean simple.

My South American wife has heard all claims it will regrow limbs, restore sight, etc etc, and clearly we have no proof of any of that. But if you want to add this to your supplement mix this is probably the best way to do it. Now, on it's own, it is gritty and tastes, well, like ground up leaves. Not my cup of tea, at all. But if you're adding it to existing smoothie mixes, or muffins, or whatnot, then it works much better. Hope you find this review helpful.

title: Feel good life insurance.
text: Feels like a great choice. Trust Amazon to supply what they say, and the testing results published look super. The pills are larger than the well-known one-a-day silver product, but it's truely just one a day. They smell yeasty, not really yummy but not revolting. And plant-sourced rather than industrial chemical factory output has to be better for my body and my planet. Only two things missing from the list was organic and non-GMO sourcing. Still, very happy with these and now set-up in my subscribe and save settings.

title: Love this in teas

title: Best sleep mask
text: This is the best sleep mask I have used. It is soft and comfortable to your face–and conforms nicely to your nose and forehead. It has two straps that are extremely adjustable. I can't imagine anyone with a head or hairdo so large as not to be accommodated by this mask. The mask is large enough so that it blocks the light out completely around your eye sockets. The two strap setup ensures that the straps do not constrict, or irritate your ears. Also, the length adjustments are on the side not behind your head so you can position the claps where you need them for maximum comfort. The adjustments are quite small too, not large buckles that would be difficult to sleep in. The silk is all black without any silly designs or logos.

It isn't as sweet and has just a hint of a bitter aftertaste. But it is better than most powders I have tasted so I rate it high. Obviously, the powdered form is not going to be as good as fresh. In a smoothie, this will be excellent.

title: Convenient
text:
This is different. But different can be quite good. In this package, you get 30 individual "vials" of liquid magnesium supplement. While it does have flavor, there is very little fluid so you probably won't taste it all that much (it doesn't taste bad but if you don't like the flavor, don't worry, it's probably not even enough to make you pucker).

This is convenient because you can always pop off a few vials and take them with you. They're not reusable so you can dispose of them when you're done. Not a bad thing to have around.

title: Inexpensive and useful
text: Turmeric is an excellent natural anti-inflammatory. I've never spoken to a healthcare professional who didn't recommend it. In this case, you get 30, 1200 mg servings for under 10 bucks (at the time of this writing). You just can't go wrong with that. Turmeric is an important part of a healthy supplement regimen.

title: Good but not high potency
text:
My wife and son have already blown through this completely. They loved the taste. If you're looking for flavor, you'll definitely find quality here. Ingredient wise...well...I've seen better quality. It's refined sugar and even has some vegetable oil. That's not so great. But hey, it's got natural flavor.

Let's get to the Omega 3 content. There's very little. This is absolutely not a replacement for a standard Omega 3 supplement. You'd have to take the whole bottle to get a comparable amount of EPA and/or DHA from a high quality supplement. It's basically candy (good tasting) with a little Omega 3.

title: Kava is Great
text:
Kava is awesome. It's pretty much the only natural sleep aid that actually helps me. Drugs are not an option. I won't dope myself up.

Liquid Kava is the way to go. Capsules are nice, but this is much better. It goes down easy and works quicker in this form. If you've tried other, natural supplements that haven't worked for you, try this. I've been pleasantly surprised at how effective Kava is.

title: Good
text: While this supplement may seem pricey, it's fast absorbing. What's the point in having high doses if your body just purges it, unused? With a good amount of Zinc and Vitamin C, you can get the immunity and energy boost you need, especially at a time where that counts.

title: Awesome
text: This is definitely a more robust immunity supplement than most of the others. Often, you find Elderberry, Vitamin C, and Zinc. This one E, B6, and other herbs in addition to the normal. Best of all, the only inactive ingredient is the capsule. That is absolutely awesome.

title: Good dosage, Good Deal
text:
For about 18 bucks (at the time of this writing), you get a 2 month supply of the critical vitamins D3 and K2. There's even a little calcium in this. Both D3 and K2 are critical for the absorption of calcium and D3 is a critical part of the immune system. With summer nearing an end, a lot of people will not have the needed sun exposure to produce the Vitamin D they need (many don't have it even in the summer).

You're getting needed vitamins at a decent price. What's there not to like!?

title: Interesting
text:
This is an interesting collagen supplement. Most of the time, they're either chocolate flavored or completely unflavored. I've had a couple of berry flavored. This is the first time I've seen an apple flavored collagen supplement. Neat idea.

A single serving has a whopping 10 grams of collagen. For the price, this is a really good deal. I've seen similar sizes and serving number collagen supplements that are twice the price of this one (or more, for that matter). To top it off, you get moringa in this as well. If you're supplementing moringa, you're getting an even better deal (one less supplement you have to buy).

I typically put collagen in my coffee (with steamed almond milk and butter). Apple flavor doesn't really mix with coffee so this one will just be going in the almond milk plain. The nice thing is that my coffee frother mixes cold beverages nicely as well.

title: Great
text:
I like to keep ear plugs on hand for students at the range. Even with headsets, some settings are so loud that they need something more. Also, at times, an outdoor range may be conducive to just using ear plugs so people might prefer them over lugging around a headset. For whatever the reason, I typically have students asking me if I have ear plugs.

This set has two plastic containers with 5 pairs each. These are nice and thick - thicker than some of the other ones. That makes them extra good for range use. My people are going to be thrilled with them!

title: Doesn't have additional vitamins
text:
For those that are looking for a pure elderberry supplement, here it is . . . at least, according to the label. There's good reason to have a pure elderberry capsule without additional added vitamins. If you're using other supplements, you don't want to oversupplement (especially zinc, which is a common in elderberry supplements).

Here's my only issue. The listing claims the presence of Vitamins C, B6, and A. The label, however, does not indicate anything other than concentrated elderberry extract. Which one is correct? We don't know. The reality is, I'll use it anyway because I've been taking elderberry for quite awhile now. Things just need to be consistent.

title: Strong
text: [[VIDEOID:2f6e63e34a3cfd297532df1110de71fd]] My son says this tastes like swedish fish. It has better quality ingredients than a lot of gummies out there. It's also a heavy dose of B12. If you're looking for a B12 supplement, this is a great one.

title: Awesome
text: This product requires no extensive explanation. I live in southern Florida. When you get out of an air conditioned car in the hot weather, it's near instant fog up on the glasses. Of course, right now, we have really nice, cool, breezy weather. So I sprayed this on my prescription sunglasses, then breathed on them as hard as I could. No fog. Perfect. This is something I've been long overdue to get.

title: Good but pricey
text: [[VIDEOID:be0666c6e3b211fdb913538e1d623c9e]] This is actually a good quality collagen supplements. It dissolves pretty nicely compared to other supplements. The individual packets are helpful for travel and convenience. The kicker is, it's pricey. For 7 packets you're paying almost $20 (at the time of this review). Good collagen supplements are indeed expensive but you can get 30 servings for $40 - $50 on average of a similar supplement . . . it's just not in individual serving packets.

title: To The Point
text: [[VIDEOID:974dda609185e0904bb6153d64cd000f]] This is an interesting one in that the label is very plain. You don't see a bunch of weird fluff to get you to think it's something special. It's biotin. That's special enough if it's what you're looking for. It's a whopping 10,000 mcg per serving (many of these supplements are between 5000 and 10000). There's also some calcium which wasn't expected, but cool.

title: Effective
text: [[VIDEOID:e05597f0f5330de15f37ef0345bfa430]] This is probably one of the best electrolyte supplement capsules I've used. Check the video. You can literally see the salts and stuff inside.

title: Tastes like soft jolly ranchers
text: [[VIDEOID:d3b8dcc1fb3c3fcbff5f70d06cd760eb]] My wife gave these a try. She said they taste like soft jolly ranchers. They even smell like jolly ranchers. If you like that flavor, you may be tempted to gobble up the whole bottle (don't do that). This is a great supplement for those who are picky about taking capsules.

title: Tastes like berry tootsie rolls
text: [[VIDEOID:9d8f63acdf512909e483642c7c585afd]] If you like tootsie rolls, you'll probably love these.  They taste pretty much the same (with added berry flavor). The only thing I'll point it is that the first two ingredients are wheat flour and corn syrup - not really that great. Of course, it's just a small chew so it's not a huge thing. But that is about as low quality sweetening as you get.

title: Yum
text: [[VIDEOID:b7fb4ad962cca5ab4443182a6996cfb]] This is probably one of the better tasting gummy supplements. It has organic tapioca syrup and raw cane sugar, so at least it uses higher quality sugars (instead of High Fructose Corn Syrup). Great for kids or adults that are sensitive to the higher dosage adult probiotics.

title: Natural
text: [[VIDEOID:b98e9eefbc4c91e3bca2fb21890263d0]] The nice thing about this supplement is that there isn't any artificial garbage. Keep in mind though, that a single capsule is 500 mg. If you're switching to this from another supplement, many of them have a serving size of 3000 mg, which means you'll need 6 of these to match it. That'll leave you with 10 servings.

title: Comes with a keychain container
text: [[VIDEOID:b1fe859bd11b981aee27aa8c05bb948]] These are standard sized, disposable, foam ear plugs. They're not any different than others. What sets this apart is the little keychain that holds two at a time. That's pretty cool. The nice thing is, they're standard size, so after you use these up, replacement ear plugs will likely fit in here too.

title: CoQ10 softgel
text: [[VIDEOID:c078fdb98072ff27f5108c63346b3beb]] You get a nice dose of CoQ10 as well as Vitamin E in these easy to swallow softgels.

title: Natural
text: There's nothing like using natural items. I'm not some loon, there's just real science behind keeping things as natural as possible, especially in this artificial world. A bamboo and activated charcoal sponge is a great addition to the collection of more natural products in the shower/bathroom. Certainly seems effective so far!

title: Good Comfort
text:
I got these for my wife (that's probably obvious). To my surprise, she had a lot of great things to say about these, as in they're probably the best ones she's ever had. Here's what she described.

It's softer than other main brands. There is a slight fragrance when you open the package, which is nice but not overwhelming. The thing she was most happy about is the wings. title: Tastes like orange slices
text: [[VIDEOID:3df08d8580247c9441c5a5ec680ad86a]] These things look and taste like the orange slices you'd get at a convenience store. They're even coated with grains of sugar. The Vitamin C count is decent. If there are children (or adults) in your life that are resilient to vitamin supplements, they'll probably love these.

title: Multi-Purpose
text:
This is an interesting protein powder as it is marketed as multi-purpose. That's pretty cool. It's a big container and there's a lot in there. While the powder does settle, as normal, there's still quite a bit.

You can use this for baking, adding to a shake (like a lot of people do), or in my place, adding it to my coffee. i've been on Keto for 2 years and I use protein powder, butter, and coconut (or MCT) oil in my coffee. No sweeteners. For a multipurpose protein powder, it actually wasn't half bad as far as dissolving. It's a little chunky, but that's normal. I steam it (almond milk) so that takes care of the chunks. I did notice an additional creamy texture. The powder itself doesn't really have any flavor; it's just bonus protein.

The next thing to try is making Keto chicken strips with almond flour and this protein powder. I never thought of using the powder like this but why not? Plus, I have a growing teenage son who is devouring his own body weight in protein every day (well, maybe not that much, but a lot).

Anyway, again, you get quite a bit in here and it's quality. The multi-purpose setup is cool. I don't do baked goods anymore so I haven't tried that use out but I'm sure other reviewers have.

title: High DHA and EPA
text:
There are a lot of Omega 3 supplements on the market, and interest in them is rising due to it's immune boosting influences (re: Covid-19). The thing to keep in mind is that they are not all created equal.

Typically, when I see an Omega 3 supplement, they iron out to be about 1 gram per gelcap. In this case, it's about 1 1/4. The concentration of DHA and EPA is higher than most that I've seen (those are the two top types of Omega 3 that people look at, with DHA being especially important for brain development in children). There doesn't appear to be any garbage in it.

Here's the thing with dosing Omega 3. The label has their serving sizes and that's all well and good. Often times, it's 2 (which is usually about 2 grams of Omega 3). I double it (and if I've just treated myself to restaurant salad dressing, which is loaded with Omega 6, I take even more). Good Omega 3 is something you can add more and get additional benefit. Sometimes, doctors even recommend it (a friend of mine takes 12 per day to help with arthritis based inflammation, it's the only thing that works for her).

title: Dissolves Nicely
text:
I've tried several collagen powder supplements. Almost all of them have the same problem: clumping...some clump worse than others. This one, however is different. This one dissolves nicely, even in almond milk (my wife and I make coffee with almond milk, collagen, butter, and coconut oil). I've only ever tried one other that does this. Seriously, put it in, mix it up a bit, and it's ready to be steamed!

Another nice thing is you get over 10 grams of protein and over 40 servings. While the price may seem to be high, I've seen numerous collagen supplements with 5 - 7 grams of protein and far fewer servings...so this isn't a bad price. The grass fed bovine sourcing helps.

The only oddball thing is that it doesn't have it's own scoop. Instead, you use a teaspoon measuring spoon and put in two heaping servings. That's a little different. It's doable though because overall this is a great supplement.

title: Nature Calls
text: I got these pads for my wife (as you probably figured). The package is small and easily portable. The reality is, it's good to keep some on hand when you're out. title: Brain Boost
text:
This MCT supplement looks kind of like Omega 3 supplements. They are gold-colored gelcaps. These in particular are a little more narrow so it's easier to swallow them.

The labeling is very interesting here. Allow me to clarify things. They're throwing out 3000 mg per serving. That's if you take 3. Let's translate this so it matches other MCT oil supplements...into grams (using mg is an advertising thing because of big numbers). Each individual gelcap is 1 gram. A serving size, according to the bottle, is 3 grams.

Here's the thing with MCT oil: effective serving sizes might vary. So again, just think of each gelcap as 1 gram. A lot of liquid MCT oil supplements are between 10 and 15 grams, to give you a hint. If you were to match that with these gelcaps, you would be taking between 10 and 15 per serving. You'd blow through the entire bottle in a couple of weeks.

What's important is to know how well you react to MCT oil. In some cases, a few grams gives people the boost they're looking for. Others need more. The value of this product really rests on the individual. I actually take them for a quick afternoon boost, but I use pure MCT oil (in liquid form) in my coffee in the morning. That's just me. In my case, this supplement does have value.

title: A Powerful Convergence is Underway Which Will Strengthen the Church
text:
"The Catholic Tide Continues to Turn" builds on author David Hartline's well received "The Tide is Turning Towards Catholicism" (see my review at [...] which was published in 2006. Hartline in "The Catholic Tide Continues to Turn" spends a great deal of time on today's post-modern culture and attacks on the Church dating back to the Reformation. In the midst of what appears to be turmoil, Hartline notes that the Church has made great strides under the leadership of Pope Benedict XV1 - and these positive developments have not been covered by the "mainstream media."

Hartline details Pope Benedict's visits to the U.S. (2008), and the U.K. (2010) which exceeded the expectations of the media and attracted massive crowds. He also highlights the World Youth Days and the lingering effects of both Blessed John Paul II's and Benedict XVI's on the youth of the world. Many have become the water and fertilizer for spring of the Church.

There are many powerful forces converging to make this a great time to be a Catholic:
* Very good lay leaders and clergy are emerging
* The Church is providing greater moral clarity in a time when moral relativism rules
* There is a boom at the parish level in bible studies and catecheses
* Catholic Conferences and programs (Magnificat, Marian Conferences, Catholic Professional and Business Clubs, the Napa Institute, etc) are growing geometrically
* EWTN is now broadcast globally while Catholic Radio has expanded into nearly every major U.S. market
Catholic Internet news services, You Tube videos (including a Vatican channel), and blogs are bountiful
* The number of excellent Catholic authors and speakers - lay and clergy - has grown exponentially
* Converts are increasing as traditional protestant faith traditions implode
* The Church is continuing to grow globally...and in the U.S.
Orthodox Liberal Arts Catholic colleges as a preferred alternative are gaining strength and students
* Screenwriters, producers, and directors are showing a presence in Hollywood and in the media
* Eucharistic Adoration is growing rapidly in parishes around the U.S.

As a producer of a Catholic speakers series, Catholics@Work, I see the good things underway in the Catholic American Church first hand, and have met many who are making the difference in the public square. Hartline's "The Catholic Tide Continues to Turn" would have been a much better book if he had focused more on the converging forces, those who are change-agents for the Church, and less on the "resistant culture," secularists, and the attacks on the Church, particularly those that are centuries old. At times, I found this book to ramble and stray off topic.

On the other hand, the book is loaded with detail and historical facts which will be useful to those who are less informed about the state of today's Church.

title: Almost 5 Stars...
text:
I bought this product as an alternative to a more expensive gelatin product I was already buying from Vital Proteins. After confirming with Amandean that their gelatin product was also derived from cows that had been raised in pastures (primarily grass-fed) and were free of undesirable things (such as added gluten, GMOs, rBGH, ractopamine, or preservatives), I decided to give it a try. I found the Amandean gelatin to be every bit as good as the more expensive brand. The usage measurements are the same and, as a bonus, you get 2.2 pounds of gelatin from Amandean versus only 2 pounds from Vital Proteins.

Amandean deserves 5 stars for taste, quality, and quantity, but I'm only giving 4 stars because the package it comes in far exceeds that which is necessary to hold the product. I don't know if this is a marketing ploy to create the illusion in the mind of the buyer that they are getting SO MUCH more, but it is unnecessary since the weight is clearly indicated on the label. So if Amandean would stop wasting natural resources by using an unnecessarily large container, I would happily revise this review and give them the 5 stars they deserve.

In the meantime I'll keep buying and watching for a reduction in the container size. It's everybody's responsibility to conserve our finite natural resources.

FYI:

I use it to make a healthy and gut-friendly beverage that is much less expensive than outrageously priced bone broth, but just as beneficial. For those that are interested, I am listing the simple recipe below.

1-2 shakes of sea salt
1-2 shakes of ground black pepper
1/4 tsp organic ground turmeric (Note: organic spices are not irradiated, which destroys their natural health benefit.)
2 level scoops of gelatin
1 cup of organic chicken broth (Note: I use and like the Pacific brand.)
4 ounces of distilled water *
1 Tbs of organic coconut oil
(* Don't use tap water. It typically has chlorine, or chloramine, and fluoride in it; all of which are toxic and wreck havoc on your gut.)

Put the ingredients in an unheated pan in the order listed, except for the coconut oil. Do not stir. Apply a low heat (e.g., simmer) to the pan and let it slowly warm to a tolerable sipping temperature. When warm, add the coconut oil and stir. Drink and enjoy. Your gut will love you for it.

07/02/19 - The review is being altered in that I have now rated the product with 5 stars because Amandean has posted a comment that it has reduced the size of its container. Well done and thank you!

title: Good quality divided storage containers
text:
I received divided storage containers that have two compartments—one side 16 ounces (large enough for 2 cups of liquid) and the other side 8 ounces (one cup of liquid). They are very similar to the reusable storage containers made by the major brands but more affordable. The lids fit tightly and have a lift-tab to help in removing the lids easily. They are dishwasher, microwave, and freezer safe—which is very convenient for advance meal prep, storage, and then you can eat right out of the same container, dirtying the minimum number of dishes. These are packaged in sets of 3 and come 18 in total (6 sets of 3 divided containers, each with a lid). The divided compartments are particularly convenient for advance meal prep—I can store a casserole on the large side and a biscuit, side dish, or dessert on the small size. I can freeze a bunch of them ahead of time, take them one at a time out of the freezer in the morning for that day’s lunch at work, let them thaw during the morning, and then heat them in the microwave at work for lunch, then toss them in the dishwasher when I get home at night. A great way to save money eating the healthy food that pack myself instead of buying lunch every day. Overall, a nice set and good value.

title: Not one size fits all. Made for a tall person probably a size large.
text:
I was excited to get these pants and I wanted to like them but they are just not working for me for a lot of reasons. The “one size fits all” is not true. I am only 5 feet tall and 120 pounds. I would normally wear a small and these are probably a large.

They are advertised as high waisted and they are VERY high waisted. The waist band is about 6 inches high. I doubled it over and they are still very high-waisted.

Not to be graphic, but I can grab a whole handful of excess fabric at the crotch. If I pull them up further to loose that excess fabric, they are even higher at the waist.

I had to roll up the pant legs about 3 inches at the ankles.

I am also not pleased about the fabric. It’s 88 percent polyester and 8 percent spandex—which should be okay normally, but these pants have no “control” feel to them at all. They don’t “hold you in” at all. They are also not smooth to the touch-they are more of a woven or knit fabric.

Last but not least, there is no way I am going to hand wash or dry clean this type of garment as the tag instructs. An evening gown yes—but yoga/work out pants—nope. If this can’t go in my washing machine, it’s not for me.

On the positive side, the inside of the pants near your skin is like a jersey feel (they are advertised as fleece lined and they do have a bit of a warm fuzzy feel to them.). This is soft and would be nice in winter. But that can also be too warm if you are active.

title: Mixes well with no appreciable taste.
text:
I have been working out pretty regularly for a couple years. Mostly this
is because it helps me keep my back pain to a minimum, but also for the
other benefits. Unfortunately, I really have not made gains in about a
year. My workout regime has gotten stale and I probably need to change
things up. I have taken protein, but even that's not been something I do
regularly. I had the opportunity to purchase this highly reviewed creatine
at a reduced rate in exchange for my honest opinion and figured I would
also buy some good protein to go along with it. For the next few months I
will be religiously taking both the protein and creatine, obviously time
will tell as to what the results will be. Since I just started taking this
product, I cannot really comment on its affects. What I can say, is that
the product was packaged very nicely. The powder itself is very fine. I
read a lot about when I should be taking this. There are currently 3
camps. Camp 1 says take it before the workout. Camp 2 says take it after
the workout. Camp 3 says take it anytime, it just needs to be present in
the body. I read a pretty lengthy article that mentioned some support that
there may be some increased benefits for taking it after the workout, but
those tests were inconclusive. Ultimately the writer of the article said
that if you really wanted to maximize results taking it after would
certainly not hurt, but taking it at any point in time as it's convenient
for you would provide you with statistically sound benefits.

I have used some creatine in the past and wasnt impressed and stopped using
it because it didnt mix well and tasted terrible. I am happy to say this
stuff is great in that regard. I mixed this in plain water, nothing else
just water to truly gauge its taste. The results? No appreciable taste at
all. The powder when dumped into the water just kinda sat there, after
stirring the water it was cloudy and really never seemed to go away after a
few minutes of sitting. I went ahead and tried it and noticed no taste
even though the water was cloudy, there was a bit of "grit" to the water,
but its barely noticeable and mixed with anything would be perfect. If I
provided any useful value to you, please click that my review was helpful

I gave it to a smaller framed co-worker to try, and he complained of the same.

Pros:
I suppose it does pull your shoulders back as it's designed to.
Easy adjustment and ease of putting on
Includes padding for extra comfort (they sort of double as a carrying case if you bunch up the harness enough)
Soft materials.

Cons:
Everything else
Very uncomfortable, even with the included pads.
Caused more pain in my shoulders than what I was willing to bear.

I realize after buying this, that I'm already pulling my shoulders back to where they need to be and this didn't do anything to help that. Maybe it'll work for someone else, but I don't need it.

I'd recommend it for anyone that needs to get their shoulders back. Contrary to things I've read on internet forums and other places, these devices will not fix "nerd neck".

title: After sight-assisted set-up, a breeze!
text:
With your phone plugged into this product, you pick up the receiver and a female voice says "Name to dial please", and the user states the name that he or she has already recorded - preferably EXACTLY as recorded or it may choose wrong entry. The device responds by stating who it's dialing, at which point you allow it to continue if correct or disconnect and start over if by chance it offers the wrong selection. This is RARE. We are so grateful for this device which of 6 voice-activated cell phones and numerous other voice-activated devices we have tried, this is the ONLY one that consistently responds to and correctly interprets my mother's voice. Further, it has worked flawlessly for several consecutive years. Note that this model only responds to names, while others in the line will respond to spoken numbers as well.

Note this: If someone does not want to use the device to make a call, after the "Name to dial, please", simply press any number key to get to a dial tone and dial as normal.

The device is voice-specific: The intended user must speak the names to be recorded, and someone must then enter the phone numbers, including the "1" and area code for long distance. For this reason I think it would be difficult for a visually impaired person to do the initial phone set up.

It is essentially a small "brick" to which you attach your own phone that holds roughly 40 voice-recorded names and manually entered phone numbers. Longer names and numbers take more memory, so if you have several long entries, you may not be able to store as many. A great device - has been reliable and worked without flaw at least 5 years for us.

Update 1/19/13: Almost immediately after writing this glowing review, we began to have difficulties with this older unit, but it served so well for so long, ordered a new one, the Vocally Freedom. After doing an "erase all" on the older unit, we have re-entered some of the names and numbers and use in on a separate phone in the house - and it is working fine. The new unit works fine, but periodically announces "Name to dial please" or "Freedom Mode" during calls in a quiet, muffled background kind of voice. Still satisfied but could do without the announcements.

As for the smell, it is simply a new product smell which goes away in a couple of days. New cars, new dolls at Christmas time, and new DVD cases have stronger odors that last longer. I use mine primarily to drown out the barking of my neighbor's 3 dogs that are tethered in their yard 24/7, and it works. text:
Why I got the product: I've been seeing products like this pop up everywhere. All the youtube peeps are talking about it. Personally, I have dark circles so I am always in need of an eye gel to help me out with that.

How to use the product: You can use it at night or in the daytime under makeup. I actually found it decreased creasing on my eyelid.

What I know about the company: This is my first time buying from this company and I haven't heard anything about them (good or bad).

Compare it to other brands or similar serving products: I don't know much about the chemical process of these eye gels but they always give me the same results. That being said, it works.

Packaging: Everything was sealed for my protection.

Color of product/design: I like the design and color, it fits well on my makeup counter.

Why I gave 5 stars: I’ve done it too. You look at Amazon and said 4 stars? Why not 5 stars? Was something wrong with the product? Why did they give it 4 stars? Well, if the product has nothing wrong with it I’m going to give it 5 stars. If it has something quirky about it, I’m going to give it 4 stars. If I had to return it because of an error in shipping or I really wasn’t happy with the product, but its an overall good product, it gets 3 stars. I rarely give 1 or 2 stars, but those are for the real stinkers. Like receiving a bag of chocolates that are melted together. That’s a 1. So 5 stars doesn’t necessarily mean “I love it” which is what Amazon says it means. It just means it’s exactly what it says it is. There’s just no way to say “I love it” to some necessary items. I may mark 5 stars on my monthly subscription to toothpaste because it cleans my teeth, but that doesn’t mean I actually love toothpaste. It didn’t make my day better—It just was what it said it was. Anyway, I felt the need to clarify why I give out mostly 5 stars. I hope this was helpful.

title: This is a superb single operator neck, back massager. it does the job, and is not bulky or noisy.
text: I will divide my comments into pros' and cons for this. As an overall rating I think this is great because it gets to spots that you cannot reach yourself. Now while it is nice to have a fill blown massage chair that cannot reach your neck, this can and of course it doesnt take up the same space.  So PRO 1. This is a single person usable device, meaning you dont need anyone else to hold it or position it. I was a little confused with the stirrups initially but as it turns out they are genius.. not only can you position the massager where you want it but you can control how hard the pressure is applied. PRO 2 it is composed of the traditional shiatsu rotating balls that we have all seen, they can go forward - backward or reverse direction and they heat up. Now the heat could be warmer, but thinking thru this if someone ever left this unattended it would not be hot enough to burn or scald so points here warm not hot - good. PRO 3 you can use this on just about any part of your body again you dont need someone to hold it to apply pressure so simple one person operation. The only CON that I can come up with is that the power cord could be a little longer -- this was simply solved by adding an extension cord.  The unit comes with the neck unit as shown in the pictures, a power supply cord that detaches and a cigarette lighter plug cord which for the life of me I dont understand. This is a superb single operator neck, back , massager that I have used. Totally portable and when not in use you can just put it in a drawer, it takes up very little space.  I love it.

title: Smells just how it should, works well on my skin.
text:
I received this tea tree oil for free to try and review; regardless this is my 100% honest opinion. I use tea tree oil for a few different things, but I do warn that this is not an essential oil that would be good for the average person to use for any kind of aromatherapy. It does have a very strong smell that is not pleasant to everyone, I know some members of my household do not like the smell at all, and it doesn't bother me because I have been using it for a couple of years now. It is an acquired taste so to speak...

That being said it does smell exactly how it should and how other products that I have purchased or reviewed in the past have smelled. The odor is strong and vibrant, it might make your eyes water if not diluted in carrier oils or products so I highly recommend that you do this until you are totally use to it or sure that you want to continue using it. It can be used to make household green cleaning recipes which I haven't used it much for yet. What I use it for is beauty recipes for acne such as a foaming face cleanser and an oil mixture moisturizer. My other most important use is for treating my scalp for dandruff and scalp itch. I make recipes of hair oil treatments or shampoos using it mixed with carrier products but when my itch or dandruff gets really bad I use it straight on my scalp. Do allergy test before trying this to make sure you don't have a reaction as this is an essential oil that should be mixed with a carrier product/oil when using because of how strong it is. This doesn't cure my condition but rather helps me keep it tolerable and I really depend on tea tree oils for this! I've used this product multiple times and it works just as I expect it should if it is a true pure natural essential oil and not mixed with anything or a synthetic fake.

title: Smells like chocolate and it works too.
text:
I use sunscreen like crazy, I have very sensitive skin to both products and the sun so I am always trying out various types to see what works well for me. I jumped on the opportunity to try this sunscreen for free* to review since I can go through it so quickly and sunscreen can be expensive. Now it's winter right now, but I live in Northern CA so most days the sun is still shining and I tested this out one day that I was out and about and knew I would be spending some time in the sun. It's not about heat, but sun exposure and I've been known to burn during winter in the snow even. Overall it worked just fine, if I was around stronger sun exposure and in and out of the water I would want to apply it more often or to use a higher SPF which this doesn't currently come in. As someone who burns easily I take my sun screen seriously so I wouldn't recommend something that won't work well for me, because it definitely would not work for others. My kids are definitely not as sensitive to the sun as I am and this will be a good one for them to use as well, they usually use the lower SPFs that I have on hand during the summer.

Now this is a kids sun screen so it might sound weird that as an adult I am trying it out, but as mentioned above I have sensitive skin so often I buy children's or babies sun screens because they don't irritate my skin as much as some of the other adult ones can. The other thing I hate about having to live with constantly using sunscreen is the greasy feel and the gross sun screen smell. I really hate both. This sun screen is made with more natural ingredients and is made not just to block the sun but to also moisturizes as well. This is a slightly brown/grey color but once blended into the skin you can no longer see the tint. It blends and soaks in quickly and doesn't leave behind a sticky or greasy feeling that name brand sun screens can. The sun can also be drying to the skin and I felt like this moisturized my skin well.

Now the main perk of the sun screen is the smell, they scent it with some cocoa giving it a chocolate scent to appeal to kids. Well I love chocolate and not smelling like sun screen so I really liked the smell. It wasn't too strong and didn't bother my allergies to scents. I would say the scent lingers on your skin for about 30 minutes after which I no longer smelled it. If your hungry or craving candy it might bother you but other wise I found it fun and it made me happy smelling it.

I did think that this product was a bit expensive when I first saw it, it was running around $19 but Amazon prices can quickly fluctuate in any direction so that might not be the current price. The would be about double what you would normally pay for a name brand product in stores, plus shipping and that's why I thought it was pricy. However when you think about those commercial products they smell funny, are greasy or sticky feeling and are full of all kinds of who knows what chemicals. This product costs more, but is made with more natural ingredients that will probably be better for your skin in the long run.

*regardless of getting this sun screen for free this is my 100% honest opinion.

text:
THIS IS THE SECOND ARIA I HAVE BOUGHT FROM AMAZON. THE FIRST ONE CAME LAST WEEK AND I COULD NOT GET IT TO SYNC. I SPENT 4 HOURS ON THE PHONE WITH FITBIT TO TRY TO FIX THE ISSUE. WE COULD NOT GET IT TO SYNC SO THEY ADVISE THAT I SEND IT BACK TO AMAZON. I DID THIS THIS. I GOT THE NEW SCALE YESTERDAY AND TRIED TO SYNC IT TODAY AND HAD THE SAME ISSUES. I COULD CUSTOMER SUPPORT AGAIN AND WAS TOLD IT MORE THAN LIKELY WOULD NOTY SYNC WITH MY MODEM. THEY SENT ME INSTRUCTIONS TO TRY BUT IT DID NOT WORK. WHY THEY DO NOT PUBLISH THIS INFO IS BEYOND ME.

Hi Colin,

We're sorry to hear that you're still experiencing trouble with your scale. We appreciate your efforts to troubleshoot.

The error you are encountering indicates that the scale has been unable to communicate with your router. The most common reason for this is the router's configuration. Based on your particular router, you may need to change the setting from N-only to mixed mode. (The following instructions were found here: http://customer.comcast.com/help-and-support/internet/about-the-wireless-gateway/)

If you have an '802.11 b' device, the gateway's Wi-Fi mode needs to be set to '802.11 b/g/n' to allow 'b' devices to connect:
1. Log in to the Admin Tool at http://10.0.0.1.
2. Go to Gateway > Connection > WiFi.
3. Click Edit.
4. For Mode, select 802.11 b/g/n.
5. Click Save Settings.

After you've made this change, we recommend the following tips before attempting setup again:
1. Keep the scale within 10 feet of your main router.
2. Clear the cache and cookies in your browser.
3. Keep the Automatic (DHCP) IP setup. Static IP configuration is not supported.

Please let us know if you still need assistance setting up your Aria.

Sincerely,

Marie M and the Fitbit Team

title: Subpar based on Expectations and cost.
text:
I want to start by saying I am a heavy guy, 6'1" 350lbs, so I bought this with the expectations/hope that it would provide comfort and relief as I sit in an office chair for several hours a day. The office chair also has a memory foam aspect to it, which if anyone has used memory foam, it a) retains heat, and b) can be quite firm during extended use. The Purple Cushion was really thick, and I liked the sleeve that came with the Cushion, those are both a plus. Initially I thought it was really comfy, however, one of the advertised qualities was it's cooling features, which was absolutely not the experience I had. If anything it was quite the opposite. One of the biggest problems I experienced was I began to develop a soreness in my tailbone if I sat for anything longer than 90 minutes. I never had this problem with my office chair. One thing I will say is that when I tried it in the kitchen as an experiment with a wooden dining room chair I experienced very little of these problems I had with my tailbone/lower back. However, the heat issue was still present.

Ultimately, I imagine if this product was half the price, I would be less disappointed than I am. I specifically targeted their "Halo" product, which I have now learned was a mistake. It is not entirely the money that is the issue, but compared to other options this one was one of the higher priced, and I chose the name brand over the other options that may or may not have had better reviews.

The phrase, "It's not terrible" comes to mind, which is not meant at all to be a compliment. I know there are plenty of others who have had a great experience with this product, and that is why I gave it 3 stars, I don't believe in going lower than that unless the product is absolutely not good at all.

title: Over-hyped, in my opinion
text:
I'm not going to lie, having at least any cushion under my bum has helped loads with the amount of sitting I do. I typically sit at a desk most of the day, anywhere between 12-16 hours (I know, it's not the greatest). You can imagine that it gets pretty tender downstairs during that time range, day after day. Yes, I need a cushion and this one works, kind of. I honestly think I would be better off with a different cushion. In my opinion, the purple cushion is extremely pricey relative to other brands on the market, squishes too easily, and moves too freely. Running me $80, I expected I'd never need to think about my backside again. Was I wrong. I got the 2 inch pad, after long debate of getting the 1 inch. I mean, I am a large dude, 6'4" and 280 pounds, but the 2 inches doesn't even cut it. I sink straight through it and feel the chair underneath me, so much so that my backside will start hurting after an hour or two. The pad slips around a lot, and not just the pad as a whole. Sliding off the chair, I could probably deal with in other ways, but this pad, because of its flex and grid like design, collapses extremely easily and can go from about a foot and a half long and 1 foot wide to a collapsed 6 inches of uncomfortable hardened goo under my tush. I'm constantly readjusting myself, changing my posture, repositioning the cushion to expand it back to full size, etc. The pad also heats up after a little while and becomes even more malleable than when it's cold, increasing the above issues twofold. Because the pad gives so easily, I find my posture being hunched over more often because my butt has no firm support around the tailbone area. That makes my lumbar have to do all the work by hunching over uncomfortably.

I decided to try this cushion because of all the advertisements I've seen on Purple products, the egg test, the satisfied customers, the "science of it", etc. I really wanted to like this cushion, what with all of Purple's claims and such, and have given this pad over 6 months of constant use. I'm sad to say I'm greatly disappointed. Purple's product just really is not that great for such steep prices. I imagine the thicker you go, the more comfort you would get, but I could barely afford the 2 inch pad, let alone the thicker ones, which seem to double and triple the price.

Like I said, I needed a cushion, this technically is one and kind of works, thus the 3 stars. My seat is more comfortable than before, but there's a whole new host of problems that you purchase willingly with your 80 bucks. Just be aware.

title: Protect yourself and others with this handy breathalyzer. Good for keeping kids honest as well.
text:
Cymas Breathalyzer, Digital Breath Alcohol Tester with LCD Screen

There is nothing better after a long day that a few of your favorite alcoholic beverages. But if you decide to have those beverages outside of your home, you run the risk of getting a DUI. Everyones body processes alcohol differently and depending on what you've eaten or done, your body may process alcohol differently each day. That is why I think that it is wonderful to have a breathalyzer with you to provide a quick reminder of your level of intoxication. With this breathalyzer and an Uber account, there is no reason a DUI should even be a concern any more.

The breathalyzer comes in a handy drawstring pouch with an instruction book. The back panel opens to reveal 5 washable mouth pieces. I definitely recommend changing mouth pieces between each reading and washing them after each has been used. I flip them up in the holder after they have been used. The breathalyzer takes 3 AAA batteries (not included). It is easy to use, just slip a mouth piece into the side, press and hold the button until it beeps, wait for the 15 second countdown, and then blow until it beeps again. It will then give you your BAC in either %BAC, %.BAC, or mg/L. Just press the button to change the reading. Caution is displayed when you are from .2 to .499% BAC and Danger is displayed and the beeping blasts when you are at .5% BAC or above. The beeping is one of the most annoying sounds in the world, but it gets its point across. It seems to be rather accurate when tested of various friends. Make sure not to eat or drink anything at least 20 minutes before testing for accurate results.

This would be great for checking your children when coming home from outside of the home.

I received this product at no cost to me in exchange for my honest, unbiased review. I am in no way affiliated with the seller, nor the product itself. All above expressed opinions are solely mine and true.
