title: Sanity Saver - So Good I Bought Two
text:
I love the white noise it brings to a room, day or night. To be fair, I DO also sleep with earplugs most of the time (I am a nut about sound) but even without plugs, my husband has still come and gone long after I am asleep, the dog barked or scratched in the night, and I never stirred. First time I tried to fall asleep with Marpac and without earplugs I thought "Too loud, I'll never fall...." Zzzzz... Street and people noise outside are drowned out.

It seems like it works in layers creating its own wall of white noise - if Marpac is the closest sound to me, it works best to disguise noise outside of that closest layer. I put Marpac between me and the source of the noise (side of the window or wall where bulk of noise comes from) for best results. I am sure you would still hear someone snorting right up next to you however. Someone described it as the constant rush of air sound you would hear in an airplane, and I'd agree. Some reviews say it's too loud - well, depends on your sensitivity and what you need! I want it to totally mask outdoor noise (I am in a single family home, residential area, so people noise around the yards, typical residential street noise, early birds, etc.) and I do not find it too loud at all. Can easily hold a normal conversation in a room with the machine on. I bought the 580 as the top twists and adjusts to allow more or less sound. The lowest sound (the smallest holes opened to allow sound) is not too much for me but I can see how some people would think its loudish. I move it around the room to suit and I can adjust to make louder, which is why I got the 580 vs. the other model.

An example of use not just for sleeping: I can hear the kids next door, one property over, playing (read: screaming and banging things really hard on the ground) to varying degrees in my own home and I was at my witts end, and I even have extra wall insulation for sound. Can NOT tolerate noise. Priced out sound proof windows. $$$$!!! Bought another Marpac to keep downstairs. Listening to the tv over the Marpac is not an issue and I don't have to have it blaring to hear over Marpac. The air-sound just fades in to the background.

Note - it will definitely help drown out and mask the higher pitched noises. I tried to listen for the screaming darlings next door playing basketball over Marpac and couldn't hear them. It can not however stop things like heavy drum beats, loud stereo thumping...sound with vibrations you can feel through your body. You need to physically stop the sound waves from traveling in those cases.

title: Stretchy enough to fit well. Stay in place without feeling tight
text:
I'm only borderline diabetic, but figure why not do all I can to guard against any bad effects? These socks looked a bit short at first, but stretch easily (9% elastane) to properly accommodate my size 10 feet. They are ankle-length, and stay up well without exerting any noticeable pressure on the ankles to do so.

Advertised as keeping feet cool, I was worried about the opposite, as my feet tend to get cold before the rest of me. So far, no problems in that regard. These mostly-cotton socks gave me enough warmth, while still feeling well ventilated.

Happily, the socks did not shrink noticeably when washed and machine-dried, another plus.

The appearance of the socks is dressy enough for work or church, but also fine with jeans or sweats.

Overall, a very fine pair of socks I look forward to wearing regularly. Recommended.

Update 6/18/19: Amazon also sent me a pair of these same socks in size Extra Large to review, as sometimes that's a better size for me.

The larger size easily accommodates my size 10 feet, with plenty of expansion room, but no unwanted fabric bunching up. (Note: my size 10 feet are within the recommended size range for both the Large and Extra Large versions of these pairs of socks.)

title: Great Item, In Theory, However, Disagreement over Whether Practical.
text:
What we received
We received a near square medium duty clear tape sealed plastic package, measuring 9” x 11" x 2" weighing in at near (10) ounces. Folded within was the footrest/bed. Inserts were included inside, that gave basic instructions.

Too small
I was really excited to receive this, from when I opened the package to when I started to open this up. However, my spouse had to do a mock trial and said in theory this appeared a great item, however, disagreed on its practicality and whether the steward/stewardess would allow this to clutter the row. Point acknowledged, but how about the tray? That’s down. So, we would have to be taking this off and on depending on the vagaries of the attendants and bumpiness of the ride. Because it did seem a little unstable.

Quality
Seems sturdy and durable enough.

Would I select this again.
I say yes, my spouse said no.

Rating
Based on the totality, I compromised and allow a weak four (4) stars while my spouse said lower.

Gifting
Would be okay for gifting, although no tags, the packaging was simple and it kind of looks like a commodity item that was bought on the cheap.

Value
In hindsight, and now having this in-hand, having this priced at near $50 is too high. A price less than half of that would be an idea to consider giving this a try.

Measures
Measures near 32” long and 18” wide. The average leg room is 31” on a plane

I hope my thoughts were informational.

title: Not your mother's...but then, they were great nail files!
text:
Revlon used to make nail files with diamond grit. They lasted forever and were absolutely the best
on the market. Every few yrs you now you have to buy another set of these. They aren't even in the same ball park as their old ones. These work. Have to go lightly on both sides, because it is hard to tell which is which--other than they're labeled--or my last set was-- "shaping" and "finishing". When new, be careful so you don't tear up your nails, and after a while, it doesn't matter which side you use, the grit's worn off. This is a case of if it's not broken, don't fix it. They fixed something that wasn't broken and now they're junk--even Revlon knows it. That's why you get 2 at a time for a few dollars. Maybe Revlon will get back some pride in their product and make them like they used to. I'd pay more than I'm paying for these two, to get just one old Revlon Diamond (grit) file. However, I suspect, no one's old enough at Revlon to know what a good nail file is and what they used to make 40 +/- yrs ago. It's a shame!

title: Just SAY NO!!
text: I ordered these end of last year, they came in November 2, 2020.  I noticed the rectangle shape was a little small however, I had ordered from two other companies and they were a little small too.  I washed them that night.  I use YL Thieves Laundry soap and have for years.  I used a netted garnet bag with other delicates.  Our washer is a Samsung top loader with no agitator bar in the barrel.  He worn one mask the next day.  He has two masks for school everyday four days a week.  He has nine masks total.  He usually only wears one mask during the 7 hours, but knows if the one he's wearing gets dirty He has a backup.  He's in Kindergarten and has nose bleeds and allergies.  He also has SPD so he can't handle certain textures.  Anywho, yesterday was mask washing day, same routine as above.  I take one out after drying and the inside layer had a hole and the material had completely disintegrated.  I pulled out the other four and three of them had the same hole, almost the same size, in almost the EXACT same location.  I asked my son about it and whether he was chewing on the material or something.  He had his totally honest, almost in tears face and said, "they just get really wet, I didn't chew on it though."  I realized what happened was every time he wore one of these masks they get moist from talking, breathing, sneezing, scratching his nose, etc. and then when he would talk or move his nose or mouth that moist material rubbed against his skin which disintegrated the material.  He breaths that into his lungs 7 hours a day, 4 days a week.

This comes with everything you would get from Nutrisystem except for the outside box and the meal planner booklet. No meal takes longer than 2 min., to prepare. I broke my ankle, so I needed something to control the spread during my convalescence that I could make easily and still be nutritious. And I didn't want to break the bank either. Very easy and healthy way to loose or maintain your weight. What are you waiting for?

title: Not my favorite selection
text: Nutrisystem works and is a good product.  Bought these because I broke my ankle and did not need to slowly expand while I park it on the couch for the next 8 weeks.  But this particular offering "Belly Buster" is not my favorite so far.  I've tried the Red Starter Kit (Good!); the Slim Balance (Good!); the Power Lean (Good minus); and this one (Belly Buster - meh to icky).  The breakfasts in this offering are good.  The White Bean & Chicken lunch is very spicy.  I'm not a fan of spicy.  Had to water it down.  The Edamame & Chicken power bowl sounded fabulous, but it was absolutely disgusting.  My husband ate it (but he will eat most things).  I just had a Power Shake instead.  Obviously flavor profiles will vary, but I would not order the Belly Buster again.  All the dinners save one are chicken and so far 2 of the 10 lunches and dinners are a hard pass.  Overall it is still a great product.  Just be sure to purchase the shakes (I prefer the Atkins Protein Plus shakes, cheaper, ready made and 30 grams of protein - 11 oz that fill you up) just in case a meal is not to your liking.  Good luck - you can do this!

title: It works.  Safe to purchase on Amazon.
text:
This is my second box. Glad I purchased from Amazon because I received the authentic product, complete with all meals and the meal planning guide at a better price than from Nutrisystem. That didn't happen when I purchased from Wally world. Between COVID and a broken ankle, I needed an affordable, healthy solution that was easy to prepare. So glad I tried this. The meals are actually pretty good! And there is plenty to eat. While you can't pick your meals, you can purchase different kits for variety, or if you are trying to focus on different aspects of your diet. I first tried the "Balanced" plan, now I'm trying the "Protein Powered" plan to address bone healing. Very easy to use, all you need is a microwave, so if you're hobbling around on crutches or a knee scooter like me right now, and can't cook, it's a breeze to still eat healthy and prepare your own meals. There are treats and protein shakes too (separate purchases, however). You can add a simple salad, or slice of bread, almonds, fruit, veggies, an egg, avocado, etc., to enhance your plan. It is all in the meal planning booklet. You are also eligible for online support if needed.

This is a great, healthy system to allow you to lose or maintain your weight in a nutritionally sound, but realistic manner. This ensures you will keep it off and restart solid eating habits, or teach yourself how to eat better going forward, or simply stay on course. And it won't break the bank. Ordering it from Amazon makes it so easy, nothing to join, no commitments to make. So glad I tried it; can't recommend it highly enough.

title: Leak bad at night but otherwise good diapers.
text:
These diapers are.... All over the place so we are going to start this with a pros , cons, and random list.

Pros
-They are super cute patterns. I absolutely love them. Especially the monster one since it is one of my son's Nick names.
-They fit great. I love the snap style. They stay very secure.
-Front size adjustable snaps.
-Have a insert sewn in already so if your kid is good with one insert there is no need to stuff.
-Inserts are pretty absorbant.

Cons
-we use these as overnight diapers and add two inserts. Yet some nights they leak really bad. Other nights they are fine. With a total of three inserts I don't think it is how much my son pees.
-The inserts provided staiabsorbent.
-I really don't know if this is a "con" but one of my diapers was not like the others. *cue song* most of the diapers were white with an insert sewn in. Then one, the feather one, had no insert and was charcoal. Dunno if someone got mixed up or what.

The main reason I rated low is due to how they hold up overnight. If you don't plan to have your baby wear them over night then they work great. I haven't really noticed any leaking during the day and the leaking at night isn't every night. So I think maybe the PUL just can't hold up to a certain amount of pee.

title: Not for heavy days, but comfortable.
text:
I wish I could give these four stars, but I can't. I am new to reusable pads. I got two sets. These and a set of big over night ones. These ones worked great...about three days into my periid. They leaked around the stitching and got blood on my panties. I was even experimenting with a cup too. My other pads worked just fine. So a warming, if you have a heavy flow the first few days I suggest getting some overnight pads and then using these ones for lighter days.

Pros though! I did feel super dry! I could not tell the pad was full. There was also no smell. I read that the nasty period smell is cause by disposable products. Apparently it is true as I experienced no nasty period smell my whole period. I also did not experience a sliding issue. If you panties and pants fit well enough you won't.

title: Overall great product
text:
We use this as a white noise machine to help our infant daughter sleep. It works pretty well, but my only complaint is that I wish it could get a little bit louder. We live in a small house, and noise from other rooms in the house is still audible (although faint) over this machine. It's a great deal for the price though, and it's not so bad that I am going to buy a different machine. I like that it runs on an on/off switch rather than a timer, as some other brands do - this way, when I turn this machine on, it is on until I turn it off - no spontaneous shut-offs that lead to her waking up.

UPDATE: 9/20/2015 - almost 2 years later, and I feel like I should update this review. We have been using this sound machine every night (and nap time) since we bought it. I originally thought it wasn't quite loud enough for our daughter's nursery, but over time I have come to realize that it is just the right volume and level to help her sleep without me having to be concerned about her hearing. There are other 'sleep noise' products that are probably just too LOUD to be using every night. With this Dohm sound machine, I don't worry about whether her hearing is being negatively impacted by the noise. It IS possible to hear loud noises outside of the room when using this machine, but the machine provides a great sound to dull most noises to a background level. It also is not so loud that it is distracting or intrusive in a way that would keep you from falling asleep.
In the 2 years we have been using this, my daughter has slept great. We even pack it with us when we travel - I am willing to give up valuable suitcase carry-on room for this machine when we fly, so that should let you know how great I think it is. My daughter even asks me to turn the machine on before she goes to bed if I forget.
I am currently ordering a 2nd of this same item since we are expecting a new baby again, and I want to use this machine in the newborn's nursery as well since it's been so helpful for promoting good sleep for our first child.
I've updated my product review to 5 stars.

title: I don't really use the top support right now - in fact I've tried it upside down and used the top support as additional bottom s
text:
The quality is higher than I expected. Honestly, after searching through tons of these belts online and so many of them look very similar to this model - I was nervous. However, it's really solidly built. I will agree with some of the previous reviewers it's definitely for a larger size woman. I'm normally a 12-14 and at 29 weeks pregnant for hip support I have it as tight as possible on the bottom support. I don't really use the top support right now - in fact I've tried it upside down and used the top support as additional bottom support which I like.

Cons: There are no instructions or diagrams for placement in regards to belly button, or something like that- also no indication of top or bottom so you have to figure it out based on curve, or try it on and realize the correct direction. Granted, I'm a smart girl and figured it out, but when I opened it I was in the throes of despair & pain and would've appreciated a simplified system. Also, the design does place extra strain on your mid back (which I would assume most do). However, if you're experiencing any mid or upper back pain then this belt will not alleviate and may add to that pain as the design puts your middle vertebrae in a stationary position which isn't exactly neutral spine.

Overall, I'm pleased that I chose this one and I throw it on a couple of times a day when the pain gets really bad - it's a nice alternative to always tightening the round ligaments or holding my hips in with my hands. Can't wait to see what support it provides as the belly gets bigger.

title: Printing on bottle shown not what I received, check less expensive seller of same item
text: Looks like the price went up since I ordered this a few days ago...if you search Amazon for Emuaid Argentum Metallicum and you will find for $47 with free prime shipping...many more reviews and answered questions and bottle shown there is what I received. Hemorrhoid treatment is one of many uses for this product.  It is an anti-inflammatory first aid ointment, not a product developed specifically for hemorrhoids. The ingredient shown in the image of the bottle for this item says Phytosphingosine which is listed towards the bottom of the list of inactive ingredients on my bottlle. The active ingredient is the Argentum Metallicum. I guess I'm nitpicking but I expect to receive the product pictured and assumed since it is listed specifically as Emuaid for Hemorrhoids that it was a treatment for that specific condition (my mistake).  If it works I'll be happy but need to try first...just wanted to alert potential buyers of cheaper option that is the identical product even though the images are different (and other seller doesn't list hemorrhoids in title) I guess it's nice that it is useful for many other conditions but had I known it wasn't an ointment specifically for Hemorrhoids I might have thought twice about spending so much money, or at least would have searched for the first aid ointment with Argentum Metallicum to get the best price and benefit of the information in the 300+ reviews for the product listed for $47 ..there are so many Emuaid products that it can be confusing and it helps to include a photo of the actual product you will receive...at first I thought they sent me the wrong thing. I'll update with new rating after I get the chance to use this (just received it last night)...hoping that it works well but with hemorrhoids I suppose every person is different. Time will tell.

title: Seems to work, but erratically
text:
I was pleased to see this device, as it really annoys me having to throw out alkaline batteries. Here is an opportunity to get some more life out of them so I don't feel quite so bad when they finally make it to the landfill.

I tried this on duracell and energizer alkaline AAs and it seems to have re-energized them, although it does seem a little inconsistent.
One thing to note is that the LCD display is not reliable. I have 4 AA batteries in the device overnight and they were marked as charged in the morning. I pulled back the spring loaded connectors in the unit and reconnected to the batteries and then all 4 were no longer marked as charged and kept charging again for another few hours. I did a quick check of all the batteries as they came out to see if they would operate a small 2 x AA flashlight. Some worked fine, others hardly at all. If I find my voltmeter I may make this a little more scientific.

So, overall I give it 3 stars at present as it seems to work in part. I won't (and didn't) expect miracles for the price.

title: I haven't had this new lamp for that long but I like it.
text: I am a retiree with an art school background. I had a lamp very similar to this Luxo for many years.  It is my hope this Luxo combo lamp will last the remainder of my life because I do like it.  However, I wanted to change the CFL bulb which came with the lamp with a 75 watt replacement (also 14 watts actual usage), LED bulb.  I put in a General Electric Reveal LED HD+ bulb.  I used to love the GE Reveal incandescent bulbs when they were still available. The GE fit into the lamp socket and worked, but it weighed twice as much as the CFL bulb, in addition to being much longer, so it stuck out past the rim of the shade.  I worried about possibly putting a strain on the lamp because of the weight of this larger LED bulb, so decided against using it.  I was able to find at a local store a general purpose GE Soft White LED bulb of the same size as the CFL (the same A19 size with 800 lumens brightness and 2700K warm light appearance; which is also a 60 watt replacement bulb, but this LED uses 10 watts of power instead of the 14 watts used by the CFL).  My eyes sometimes get irritated by fluorescent lights, which is why I was hoping to find a replacement.  The circular (22 watt circline) bulb which also came with this combo lamp is fluorescent, as it should be. It doesn't seem to bother me when I have it turned on at the same time as the new LED bulb.  With both bulbs turned on, I have a balanced light, which is how this lamp was designed.

title: Overall a great alternative to disposable/ great starting kit.
text:
I have a huge allergy to the chemicals and bleach used in conventional disposable pads, most people don't realise that they are used to make cotton whiter as natural cotton is more of an off-white to a brown color, but that is not socially accepted. I have been using reusable pads and menstrual cup since I was a teen and this stuffed was not very commercially accessible or talked about. Most women don't realise what a huge advantage it is, both monetary, health-wise and it's not that difficult to wash, contrary of what people believe, I haven't experienced any stains and leakage. This has a total of 5 layers one being PUL making it bullet prove. The only other company in the pads that does this is ''party in my pants pads'' but they are very expensive in comparison. Also, I had never used one with a bamboo charcoal layer. So I found pros and cons.

A huge pro is a minky material that against your skin is super soft, it's very breathable and absorbent so you won't fell like you're wearing a wet diaper. In comparison to other cloth pads they are very thin, I love that I can wear leggings or some tight clothing it doesn't bulk up like other cloth pads. I find the prints very girly and adorable, one of the advantages of using cloth is this. Also, I have not experienced any leak because of water prove layers. The snaps are very well done, they fell secure and are made with plastic so they won't rust over washes. They are also two so you can adjust them if you need them to be thinner. All the stitching were perfectly done. I love that it brought a mesh washing bag, I usually just throw it in the laundry with my intimate but this is nice to have. You get a pack of 5 this is a huge deal as they tend to be so expensive. They fold very small for your wet bag if you need to change them on the go.

I didn't find so many cons is more of a preference as I am not a huge fan of microfiber, YES I know they are more absorbent than cotton or other material but they tend to smell over time, there's a wildly know trick to just hang them to dry in the sun and this would work miracles also with stains. They are not as long as I prefer they would compare like a regular size diaposable pad. In the begging, the charcoal smelled like well charcoal after washing that went away, but that was another thing I had notice. I didn't find any instruction on how to take care of them. So after years of usage ill give a word of advice. Never add softener to your cloth pads as this diminishes the absorbency on them. Always wash in COLD so they won't stained, If you can try to soak them prior to washing them.

I will attach some picture in hope it will help someone who might be interested in this produc. If you have any questions or comments about this product or my review, feel free to message me and I'll be glad to help. I also posted a picture of all of my other cloth pads as people always think because I was sent a promotional item I am in the obligation to give a 5 star or I am being biased and this NOT the case. I am very passionate about the environment and I believe any knowledge that might be useful is always good to share.

I began taking this to grow my hair. It wasn't thin or short, I just wanted more hair. What I immediately noticed after just two weeks was a total rejuvenation of my hair line, so many new hairs were growing. What I noticed after two months was fullness and body I've never had. I have always had longer hair, the weight and probably the types of hair products (typical sulphate and artificial shampoos that coat your follicle with junk like Pantene and finesse) made my hair so limp and stick to my head...it was essential to wash my hair daily to get body... vicious cycle.
Anyway, my hair changed in texture, folicle thickness, strength and I didn't have the weird spiral hairs from damaged follicles anymore. I had new hair and my scalp became less oily. I've always had very nice fingernails, but noticed they were growing even faster than usual.
I will advocate that when taking this, I would only take one capsule (I encapsulated my own in the 00 size I think) a day and I took a quality B vitamin complex (garden of life b complex which is food derived, not synthetic) at a different time of day. I eat a healthy diet full of unprocessed fruits and veggies, few carbs and grains and grassfed beef, wild caught salmon etc... i noticed no adverse side effects. I also put myself on a three month on two month off cycle for the horsetail. On the off months I take biotin daily and diatomaceous earth weekly. My hair which used to be very straight and limp is fairly wavy now and curly like I used medium hotrollers at the back of my head which used to be wavy.
The hair on top of my scalp has so much body I have to straighten it to lay flat. I look like I'm wearing captain Hook's wig if I slept on my wet hair overnight, its so tall on the top of my head it's comical. My hair holds a curl better now when I use hot rollers.
I can't recommend this enough for hair growth, New hair grows, better hair grows. Make sure you have a cycle where you take a few month off to let your body replenish any lost minerals. Make sure you take your b vitamins and possibly potassium and a good overall vitamin. Eat healthy. Enjoy fabulous hair you grew.

SQUEAK SQUEAK SQUEAK...both definitely SQUEAK. However no more than two other similar items I have. These are heavy duty in comparison to other two. And they all squeak but these really do squawk in use. Of course sitting there without doing anything they are pretty quite. LOL
Anyway the important here is they are heavy duty and the non knobby one is about one and a half inch shorter which is fine with me. I'd be happy if they had same item only 2 to 2 and a half inches shorter for both items. I'd say you get a great bargain if you paid under ten dollars as I did for both today. I can see they might be retailed at upwards of 60-80 as they suggest retail priced on the sale page. But if you really are looking to buy because they might be hush quite...no they are not. I would advise seller to remove that promise because there might be a few folks who would reject these once they get them and realize they are anything but silent when used. I do wonder if there is a silicone dry spray that might help with that. The inner rod is metal and there is no give and all of this I expected. I have another model that flexes and is smaller in length and I love it but it is no where near as durable as these are. Because of their materials these are HEFTY or heavy if you need or want something much lighter I'd suggest looking at the plastic versions like some of the excercise folks sell. Giliam comes to mind but not sure that's how it's spelled. Over all I can recommend if you don't mind the squeaking and the weight and the length and want something that should hold up for quite a while or several times a day use every day year round.

title: Water Flosser for Travel or Home Use!
text:
Price is very comparable to other one-use-at-a-time-type water flossers. The thing I like most about this handheld is the ability to clean the water reservoir. I have another water flosser and is it is an all-in-one design and there really is no way to clean the water reservoir and I find that gross. This one comes right off for easy cleaning and seems a whole lot more hygienic to me.

It is a bit bulkier then the other hand held that I have, and what I mean by handheld is all in one device, no reservoir sitting on your sink. It is bigger around but I like the fact that the wand on top folds down because when I travel with my other handheld water flosser I always feared breaking off the tip during travel.

I have used this water flosser 13 times and it is just starting to act like it should be charged. It's a bit sluggish and sputters now and then so I will probably charge it after the 14th or 15th time. It has two speeds, the gentler for beginners, and the high for experienced water flosser users. You can really hurt your gums if they aren't used to this type of cleaning.

The water reservoir has a max fill line on it, but the fill line is marked too high. If you actually put that much water in it and then try to attach it to the device, water will spurt out of the top of the reservoir and maybe even shoot out of the tip. So just be cautious about that and don't say I did not warn you! This is a quick fix so I hope the manufacturer will adjust the water line max mark.

I added several pictures so you can see what the product looks like right out of the package. It came in gift box packaging which I think is pretty cool when it's something available on Amazon. If you buy it for somebody else it's like it's already gift-wrapped and you don't have to pay Amazon to do it! Score!

If you found my review helpful in your decision-making process, please let me know by clicking The Helpful button!

The stand, full put together, is not real tall. For reference, I am 5'3". The steam bar is around elbow length and the controls/water holder sit about waist high ish.

For me, I am blessed to have a reclining chair with my couch so I simply reclined it and had the steam cover me from there.
I will definitely use this frequently and I recommend if you have the space/time for some relaxing, pore opening, sinus clearing self care.

This gives them a versatility that you don’t typically have in compression socks and allows choices to wear them just to add a level of comfort for an active lifestyle. The level of compression is generally good, though for people with smaller ankles, some compression is lost. While I understand that a size listed as small/medium has to fit a broader spectrum of physical characteristics, it is a consideration that there’s extra fabric in any area because in terms of compression, efficacy is diminished.  In my case, the toe section is considerably larger than I need, and I had to make an effort to situate the placement of the heel, working out small wrinkles, in order to avoid blisters. In other words, the foot and ankle sections would seem to be well-suited for a medium size, but a little more awkward to fit as relates to a small size. title: Super delicious!
text:
I’ve been taking elderberry supplements for just over a year now. After taking another supplement on a cruise and managing to not get sick while my travel partner did made me thing there was something to elderberry, so I’ve been taking it ever since. I had the opportunity to give this one a shot, and I am definitely impressed!

This product came well-packaged in an envelope, plastic outside seal and interior safety seal intact. The product label indicates a serving size is one gummy, which has about half your DV of vitamin C and Zinc as well as elderberry. Because single servings of previous supplements I’ve used are two gummies for a serving and have closer to 100% your DV of Vitamin C and Zinc, I opt to take two of them. This yields a 30-day supply.

This gummy is delicious! The flavor is berry of some kind and it’s sweet with just a hint of tanginess. I really liked the texture compared to other gummies I’ve tried: it’s super soft and almost sticky on the inside (they don’t stick together in the container).

I can’t quite speak to the efficacy of this product because I’m observing strict COVID protocols like minimizing my trips out, social distancing, and masking up, but there is some research showing elderberry does have some antiviral properties and Zinc is known to help fight colds, so I’m satisfied. The price is a little higher than other supplements I’ve tried if you do double up on the serving like I do. That said, I do recommend this product!

title: Turmeric is a powerful anti-inflammatory supplement but read tips/cautions below
text: Turmeric is a very popular supplement right now and with good reason. It reduces inflammation and is a powerful antioxidant. (That said, it's not for everyone. It can thin the blood and be dangerous for anyone prone to bleeding, awaiting surgery, prone to gallstones, taking warfarin, etc. If in doubt, do some research or talk to your doctor before trying turmeric.) It's also important to know that black pepper makes turmeric more bio-available to the body. It's a good idea to add a small amount of black pepper to anything you make with turmeric. I like to make a turmeric tea by boiling water and adding a few teaspoons of this powder with some grated fresh ginger, fresh lemon juice and 1/8 teaspoon of black pepper. I also make golden milk by heating milk/coconut milk/almond milk and adding a few teaspoons of turmeric with 1/8 tsp black pepper and some honey or agave. There are countless recipes online or on Pinterest for turmeric tea, golden milk and other creative ways to use turmeric. This particular brand of turmeric is reasonably priced and seems to be very high quality.

I'm immunocompromised, so I didn't want to spend hours in the ER waiting to be seen, during this pandemic. Anyways, I read the reviews on this, noticed it was GMP certified and a decent price. I paid for rush shipping and noticed a difference immediately. Now, it relieved the symptoms, but since my bladder infection had a few days to grow, I couldn't cure it with these. I went to a local Walgreens pharmacy clinic and got a evaluation and test. Sure enough my bladder infection was still there, however, the "colony" was so small that it was causing no pain or symptoms and hadn't spread to my kidneys. I have to think it was these pills. Especially being on chemotherapy for lupus, you'd think those little bacteria would have had a field day with my system, but no... The "colony" was less than 50,000 according to the culture done instead of in the hundreds of thousands. Anyways, get this, take it according to the directions, follow a healthy diet, relieve yourself promptly, speak with your doctor and I bet you'll have no problems out of pesky bladder infections. After this one clears up this will be in my daily arsenal of vitamins and herbs.

title: Probably good for some, but haven't helped me
text:
I bought these SOLE insoles when I bought my new ASICS GT-2000 shoes. I typically get the green Superfeet and have been pretty pleased with them over the years. After running X amount of miles in my last pair of shoes/insoles I hit the point where my back started to hurt after a run, which usually indicates that the shoes are "dead". I was hoping to ramp up my running distances in order to run the Tough Mudder, then maybe a full marathon later in the year (I've only ever completed a half marathon to date). Since these insoles were advertised as being used by "ultra-marathoners" I thought they'd be the ideal insole. This, however did not seem to be the case.

As background I'm currently about 220-lbs. and 6' tall. I've been as heavy as 255, and as low as 200 over the last 10 years. Running was one of the primary methods of exercise that I've used to try and lose weight, and I have fairly flat AND wide feet, so good insoles were the ONLY way that I was to do this. So far I've logged about 20 miles using the SOLEs and still find that they not as supportive as the superfeet. I feel the most pain in the outer edges of both feet along the bottom (almost from pinky toe to heel) and sometimes in my arch. I'm hoping that this is simply indicating my feet have weak muscles and they will stop hurting after I've ran a bit more to strengthen them. (will update review in another month or more to see if this is true).

Overall I'd say my best insoles were custom fitted insoles from Road Runner Sports. They were $75, but lasted quite a while. Next in line, and the most affordable were the green superfeet. I'd say they are the best performance per dollar that I've used, and will probably switch back to them for most running needs. For the marathon, if I choose to do it, I'll probably go ahead and get another pair of the custom insoles.

title: Great cleaner for dog messes & bathrooms, general sanitization and wipe downs, not deep stains
text:
We have a room where we keep the dog crates for when they need to be in there to sleep on rare occasions (like if we're staying overnight elsewhere) and we're all quite aware that we're a bit noseblind to the dog scent that now pervades it. And with dogs and a family of four that includes kids, bathrooms can tend to get messy very quickly, so keeping them clean is a regular struggle. Those two spots seemed like the perfect place to test Pacific Spirit's special brand of DIY spray cleaner which, in an effort to save people money and reduce the production and use of additional plastic bottles ships its cleaning product in cardboard envelopes and has you create them in home.

It's an idea I'm fully on-board with and one we've used before with other products (not always as powders, sometimes as incredibly small, very concentrated liquid formats that you then dilute in bigger spray bottles. Again, if it reduces the ultimate environmental impact of shipping cleaning product around the world and the number of big cleaning spray bottles being made and not really recycled great. That's definitely a pro.

But, they still need to pull their weight as cleaning products.

So, that's the big question: Does Pacific Spirit work as well standard bleach, general tile cleaner x, Windex, etc?

As a general wipe down cleaner, like a Windex or bleach wipe, it seems to be fine, but where it didn't seem to be quite as strong was in the realm of stain removal, even though we erred on the side of higher potency and made it slightly higher in concentration than recommended in order to really give it the benefit of the doubt. That's fine, as we already have to buy two different products to use for those two general use-cases since even Windex or bleach wipes are particularly effective at stain removal.

So this package-saving product can still potentially replace basic glass and surface wash and sanitization sprays, just not something more specialized. That's still making an impact, even if it's not as big as one as we'd hoped.

***Overall Value***
It's absolutely cheaper than buying 6 additional bottles of a Windex or even generic bleach wipes at just $3 (at time of review) for a pack of 3 envelopes that goes on to produce multiple bottles of cleaning spray. That's a great value, and again it's much less environmentally bad than a bulk pack of bleach wipes that both has to ship those wipes in larger packaging, produces a lot of waste in each wipe, and cost more to do both. Lots of value added there.

title: Daughter's first curling iron to call her own, auto-shutoff is key
text:
Like many girls growing up, our daughter's first run in with a curling iron was her mother showing her what it could do, and letting her see how it changed her appearance in a manner of minutes. And since we keep her hair relatively short, a little bit of crimping/curling is one of the few things she can do to add a little bit of extra flair without putting in extensions. Consequently, as she's gotten older she's started using her mother's curling iron A LOT and so we figured it was time she finally got her own. This seemed as good a place as any to start.

1. Auto shut-off

One of the key things we wanted for her first curling iron, more important than how good it was at making curls, was an auto-off function. While I trust her to be responsible and not burn the house down, if I can choose a model that has a built-in failsafe/time function (60 minutes) to ensure it doesn't just stay on all-day if accidentally left plugged in, I'm going to opt for that, and I tested it before giving it to her.

2. Easy to use

It's her first curling iron, it doesn't need to have any frills, just be of a size that let's her get a moderate amount of curl in her short hair. That's it. This does that, and she's pleased with the size of the curl/shape it adds. So everyone's happy.

3. Fast

Most of this thing's use is in the morning before school, so if it works it needs to heat up fast and do the job faster. So far, we've not had any school day mornings where the curling iron was a cause for delay, so that's a mark in its favor.

Last but not least...

4. Safety

None of the pieces or latches appear to be loose, the handle is responsive, and she has plenty of clearance between the iron and skin. The kickstand works and doesn't collapse or tip over.

And there it is, the four criteria this curling iron needed to satisfy for us to be comfortable with our daughter having it as her own and it passed. I'm still going to pick it up from time to time and ensure nothing has come loose, but for now, I trust her with it and it to not harm her.

Is it a good value?

It's probably not the cheapest model for a girl's first iron, but I'd rather have one with the auto shut-off than a dollar store model without it. The peace of mind is worth it.

-Design allows you to continuously feed a small amount of 'clean' floss to the head, and remove excess off the end with a built in cutter so wastage is minimal.
-Small head easily fits into mouth and is easily maneuvered around while flossing.
-Floss track works and keeps the floss were it needs to be - I have not seen the floss slip out like I did on the "Y" style flossers.

CONS:
-The design utilizes a small blue plastic cap between the handle and the nub (see the photo) in an attempt to friction lock the floss in place and keep it from feeding slack when in use. It doesn't work, but there is a work around - see below.

Initially I found that I could can only floss one or two teeth before cap allowed enough slack to occur that I could not continue flossing. Fortunately, there is an easy work around. Ditch the blue cap and just use the nub to lock down the floss in both directions. It's a little bit of a pain to unwind it (twice), but it works and I was already doing that with my Flossmate so it was nothing new to my routine.

title: Perfect Bag For a Blow-out Kit
text:
I bought this bag for a blow-out kit to carry when shooting and bushcrafting. It is perfectly suited to that purpose. The two things you will want to get at with the absolute minimum of fumbling are a tool for quickly and safely opening clothing and shoes (in this case, my Benchmade hook/safety cutter) and a C-A-T tourniquet. I've attached these to the molly web on either side of the bag for immediate access. Inside there is room for an Israeli bandage, several 4x4 gauze pads, a HALO occlusive bandage, some steri-strips, tape, nitrile gloves, and assorted wipes. Most of the time it lives on my range bag, but easily switches to a backpack or vest for trekking.

It easily opens with a single pull, and is so well arranged that I, or anyone needing to use it on me, can see everything and get at it without fumbling around.

On the other aspects, the device is really clumsily designed and far too big. It is the size of a coffeemaker - for a water pick and a toothbrush!!! There is no need for the tank to be so big considering that they recommend that you unplug the pick from the tank when you use it to brush your teeth. And you must drain the tank when you unplug it since otherwise the water will leak everywhere! It is as if the people designing it did not even use it to see if the design made any sense.

But perhaps one of the most annoying features is the poorly written instructions which seem to be a straight internet translation from the original Chinese. If the company could not even bother hiring a professional writer to at least convert this translation into something readable in English, then I don't see how it can be trusted to put out a quality product.

All in all, I guess I am lucky that this crappy product broke in its first half hour of use and I can now return it. Given how flimsy the hose was, it could have broken off any time (and it is built in and thus not interchangeable!!!). Had it broken after the return period, I would have been screwed.

title: 2 year review follow up
text: Okay I've owed this pillow over 2 years i did a lot of research checked many different pillows and this one seemed like the best choice. I wanted to make sure i got a good quality pillow and it would last a long time. The problem began i believe just after a year i started to notice allergies I've never had before like i couldn't have dark beer or my airways started to close up. I thought well that's weird i guess i will stay away from beer which is okay since i usually don't drink much. After a few months i started to notice when i ate wheat bread my airways would start closing again or horrible bathroom experience sometimes both. At this point i'm thinking maybe i'm getting old (25) body is changing i can't have somethings. One night i wake up and i couldn't breathe! I had to sit in the shower and inhale a little water just to breathe again it was horrible. I figured just to be safe ill go to the doctor see what he thinks. I get told i have asthma, which I've never had, and i played football and basketball growing up i'm in good shape still play basketball a few time a month. I figure this doctor is probably stupid but i couldn't deny the attack i had that night so i figured what the hell i get an inhaler in case my airways close up again. I probably should have gotten one sooner but well i don't like doctor visits. So after a few more months i started to wake up with a runny noise itchy throat and wheezing sometimes. I thought okay time to do some research to figure out whats going on. I decide its gotten bad enough i need to put pillow covers on and mattress covers on my bed and fully clean the floors with special cleaners from the allergy store. I even washed my blankets and sheets in special detergent for people with allergies which is suppose to help and remove dust mites. I even took this pillow apart and washed it. This seemed to help but after a week i was back where i started if not worse. I thought okay maybe i have to do this every week. After a few weeks it didn't seem to work as well i was still waking up wheezing. I thought okay maybe i'm allergic to polyester which is what my pillow and sheet covers are made of. So i bought nice cotton everything. Which still didn't help well a little but not much. Finally i thought maybe its the pillow this all started after i got the pillow it is buckwheat and i'm allergic to wheat it seems. Then i did some research on buckwheat allergies. Turns out all my problems can be caused by this pillow. I remember reading that the pillow is suppose to be fully washed and cleaned to prevent these type of problems. Now only about 1 in 6000 people or so suffer from buckwheat allergy if they are not cleaned correctly. If they are then my understanding is it is extremely rare to have the problems I've been having. So rare that I don't believe there is an exact est. well i couldn't find one anyway. So are these pillows washed and cleaned like they should be well you decide. But anyone with allergies be careful. Oh on a side note i even developed an allergy to my cats which has now slowly diminished after about 5 months or so of not sleeping on this pillow. The Pillow was very comfortable but i will never do a buckwheat pillow again. I hope this review helps someone!

UPDATED ON 10/27/15

title: You will need a lot of this to get even a light brown color! Looks dark when in the mix, but is 10X lighter when dry.
text:
Mixed in easily, but gave a much lighter brown than ideal even using a 25:1 concrete to pigment ratio by volume.
Ordered a 3 bottles to get even a light gray on a small 800SF resurfaced concrete driveway (Quickright resurfacing concrete).

Looks dark brown in wet concrete, then gets 10X lighter color when the concrete dries. Good thing I was not seeking a uniform color. You think it looks great in the mix, then 2 days later you see what you've really got.
Also, the pigment tends to float to the surface and is easy to wash away. I minimized this effect with a plastic cover over the concrete, but still had much of the pigment wash off the cured concrete in the first week after.

Still gave it 3 stars since it would be OK if you use a lot of the pigment, but you should order a lot of this if you seek even a medium true brown. Experiment first since the surface gets much lighter after the concrete dries.
I used a brown dye a few weeks after the job to get the surface back to even medium-light brown.
Hopefully the combination of pigment in the concrete and the surface dye together will provide a longer lasting result than a dye alone.

title: Misleading Product Description - Nothing Permanent Here - Disappointing
text:
I've undergone laser hair removal from a professional salon before so I knew what I wanted from this device. The product is advertised as "Permanent Hair Removal" but after several months of using this product at the highest setting, I still have no evidence of any permanency. The hair does get thinner over time but it always grows back.

In addition, the included instructions say there are areas of the body on which this should not be used. Such as the neck. That should have been mentioned on the product description page.

The product is advertised as "Laser Hair removal" but it's simply not. No laser here. It is IPL technology (Intense Pulses of Light). The product description also implies that it is FDA certified. This is misleading. There is only only FDA certification for the general process of using high intensity light for hair removal.

Misleading product information is bad enough in my book but more importantly, the product simply doesn't work. That is, unless your goal is to regrow thinner hair. In that case, it's marvelous.

title: Game changer!
text:
Game changer even though this has been out for awhile and enjoyed by our UK brethren. Only now is it catching onto the US market without having to resort to ebay.

This is the real deal in terms of pure paint protection with water beads that rivals ceramic coating.

If you are unsure about applying a ceramic coating, or don't want to pay the high cost to a professional to get ceramic coating, this sealant just might be for you!

Of course do the usual, use a paint cleaner, or finishing polish (like M205/M210) and make sure your paint is as good as it can or acceptable to your standard. Then applying this two panels at a time with thin and light coats. What also helped is soaking and wringing the included sponge out first to soften it up. Then remove the first panel, apply to the next corresponding panel, remove the previous one that was waiting. Keep going until your done.

Technically there is no "cure time" but a general rule for sealants is to let it cure at least 12-24 hours for best bonding.

Sit back and enjoy super long lasting protection!

text:
These are reasonably priced gaming headphones but the saying "you get what you pay for" definitely applies here.

Visually these are nice looking headphones but as soon as you pick them up you can feel the build quality or lack thereof. They are extremely lightweight, which is good thing in some cases however the plastic they are made of seems hollow. If you have hard floors in your gaming area like I do, treat these with extreme care because they don't seem like they can take any sort of drop.

Sound quality is what you would expect from headphones this price, they aren't terrible, but naturally cannot compete with well known brands in this department. The good thing about them is they do a fair job in eliminating outside sounds which I do enjoy.

The microphone is controlled by a mute/unmute switch attached to the wire and swivels up and down as needed. However speaking of the microphone, after just one week of use, the microphone is no longer working. I tried many troubleshooting steps to get it to work but its completely dead. title: Which is not good if you have no idea what you're doing
text:
This is definitely not a high-quality set. However, it does give you an idea on how to set up and use a gun and use the practice skin. This comes with everything you need to learn how to start tattooing, including two guns, needles, bottle for sanitizing soap (soap not included), practice skin, power box, rubber bands, ink and more.

This comes with no instructions on how to work these guns, so you have to Google how to set this up and how to work it. Which is not good if you have no idea what you're doing. I almost want to take this kit down to my local tattoo shop and ask them how to set this up just in case I've been doing it wrong, because honestly, I have zero clue. I figured out the general idea, but that was about it.

Out of the two guns, one arrived broken and will not turn on when hooked up. The other one stops working randomly, and I did double check and make sure that the cables were inserted fully. The guns themselves feel pretty cheaply made but look kinda cool. I do like the "hardy" look they have going on.

I haven't used this on actual skin yet, as I'm definitely not an expert, and really never touched a tattoo gun until now...but the ink didn't have great results on the practice skin, so I don't think I would even attempt it on real skin, even with practice

Overall, I think this would be an okay starter kit if you're just wanting to learn how to set up a tattoo gun, and maybe tattoo the practice skins, or some fruit...but you'll definitely want an upgrade if you want to tattoo skin. Also, keep your fingers crossed that the guns arrive in working condition.

It does have a pretty strong fragrance, but I think there is more to the product than just scent, I think it does contain enzymes and they work. I would like this product to be larger in size, however, as 17 ounces isn't very much for any household that has a puppy or a senior dog.

title: Pleasant Tasting,  Worked Wonderfully For All Over Relaxation
text:
I heard of the relaxing effects of Kava from a friend, and was curious to try it for myself on nights before bed when mind and body are still buzzing from a long day.
The directions on the bottle state to take two squeezes of the bulb or 1/4 of a Teaspoon. I was pleasantly surprised with the taste. I was picking up hints of berries, which leaves me to question what the full ingredients are for sweetener. It does list vegetable glycerin which may be responsible for the pleasant taste. As far as consistency, it's slightly thicker than water.
It took about 30 minutes for the effects of this medicinal tree root concoction to do its magic. I soon felt a total relaxed feeling. I practice holistic and healthy living and can see this being a wonderful addition, along with my CBD and essential oils, to my natural first aid kit. There is no doubt this Kava works, however I think it's important to mention that after doing some more indepth research on Kava and the effects on the body, I discovered it's not the greatest for the liver. That being said, neither is alcohol and I already gave that up! Lol. I will use this only when needed and I would advise the same for anyone looking for a little added help to chill out. Used in moderation, I'm comfortable with it. 
I posted some photos to give you a closer look and hope that they, along with my experience, helps you out a bit with your choice.  Thank you!

It's a drop of soda, and it may be my imagination. :-)  I am pleased as punch to be moving towards a one-time-use plastic-free home and these are helping along the way.  I have not found a 'permanent' straw I'm comfortable with, but more so, I'm using these for cans of soda or fizzy water, to be used once and then recycled/composted. title: Decent kit for $20
text:
I purchased this first aid kit, because I want to be more prep aired for what life throws at me. I know from personal experience that the worst happens when you least expect it. I was recently traveling on the interstate and witnessed two semi-trucks collide. It was late and I was the only one there. One of the drivers was pretty cut up and I didn't have anything in my car but Kleenex to give him to wrap his hands with.

To me, this wasn't acceptable. That's one of the reasons I purchased this. I think every car needs a first aid kit and I now have one for both of my cars, as well as one in the house. This one is great. It has all the basics. It's much better than Kleenex...aka nothing.

If you don't have a first aid kit in your car this would make a great addition. I'd also recommend a flashlight, blanket, and some bottled water.

I would definitely recommend this product to my friends. You can't buy all of this stuff separately for this price.

This kid isn't my favorite out of the three I purchased. It's a very useful kit and has a few unique items that the others don't such as a whistle (one of the others had this), a compass, and a glow stick. This kit has a few items that I feel are not as necessary such as a few wooden tongue depressing sticks and several q-tips. The other kits I purchased had more band-aids and those are what you're likely to use the most of, as well as a bigger variety of band-aid sizes.

I would still recommend this kit. It would make a good car kit and it's only twenty dollars.

**UPDATE** I tried to give this a shot. It didn't make it a month. Ordered on the 28th of March, Received on the 30th of March. As of today, April 25th, it's trash. Nice concept. Bad Execution. I like the overall size of the mask, but, the light leak around the nose is so much that it almost renders the mask unusable. I sleep with a mask nightly and I go through them rather quickly, so I'm often looking for masks that will work as needed (blocking all light) and will last more than a hand full of months. I barely made it through one night with this mask. The instructions say to "adjust the nose" right, there isn't anyway to adjust the nose section, at all. The edges aren't even pretending to be sealed, you can clearly see the foam center all the way around the outside edge of the mask. Sadly this one is going to end up in the bin and I'm out the $8.

title: BEST Supplement/Pill Organizer I've Ever Used
text:
The best I've found. I use mine for supplements. Each day can be easily removed from the box separately so carrying just a couple of days for a weekend trip is a breeze. (For me, loading a week's worth of pills is easiest if I take the compartments out of the box and pop them all open. title: Really wanted to love this scale
text:
The basic idea of a WiFi scale is great - you step on, it records the information, and you're done. You can do it every morning when you're groggy and you don't have to try to write it down or remember. Having the log on the website over time keeps you honest. I have good strong WiFi signal throughout my house and that part works fine for me.

The problem is that the Aria isn't actually a very good scale. If I step on, get a weight, then rotate the scale 90 degrees (on a flat surface) it might give me a weight a pound or two off. Then if I rotate it back it will produce some third number out of the air. It's not very consistent.

This is the company's first effort at making a scale and frankly it shows. And I think they were so enthralled with the technology of the scale that they forgot the fundamentals - if a scale can't weigh things consistently it's not useful. I really wish I'd spent a little more and bought the withings scale which by all accounts actually works. My recommendation is to either do that or weight for the next generation Aria because this one isn't there yet.

title: Good but has some quirks
text:
I like this alarm but it definitely has some issues. Here's what I like: the light can be adjusted so that you wake up to really really bright light or something much dimmer or anywhere in-between. You can also wake up to the radio which is an added plus. My old wake up clock would start getting light 30 minutes before the alarm; this one is 15 minutes and I think it's perfect. Here's what I dislike: the snooze is way too easy to set off (though that can be fixed by just making sure the snooze sensor is angled away from any potential movement) and when it does snooze, the next alarm doesn't turn the light back on. The backlight is way too bright so at night you have to turn the backlight off. This could be a plus because if you wake up in the middle of the night you have no idea what time it is so that has actually helped me fall back asleep easier. It's annoying to have to turn it back on in the morning. I am going to try and find some type of film to put over it. I have a wicker nightstand and if I move the alarm, the reset button on the bottom of the alarm gets hit so have to reset everything. The buttons aren't easy to press, hence I sometimes accidentally move the clock and set off the reset button.

I had the Hammlecher progressive clock before this and will say that now that I've figured out the kinks with this one, I definitely like this over the Hammlecher.

title: disappointed.
text:
I give it 5 stars for warmth - I have Raynaud's and I am constantly searching for better ways to heat my toes. Heated socks were good, but they had hot spots (that hurt) and had no durability. Last year I tried heated insoles, which work great in my extra thick slippers but the heat was focused on the instep, leaving my toes to still get cold unless I used the hottest setting. So far these heated slippers are better as they seem to heat my whole foot - my toes are pretty happy again.

I give it 4 stars for wear-ability. The fit is good (ordered the small and I have small feet, men 8.5), but when walking around I feel a slight tendency for my foot to roll off the side of the sole. This feels a little dangerous.

I give it 4 stars for operation. Three things I'd like changed: 1) the buttons are way too bright during operation. When sitting in my lounger watching TV, the lights on my feet are a distraction. 2) Once turned on, it is way too easy to accidentally change the power level when your foot brushes up against anything. I think the button should be harder to press, or that you should have to hold the button down longer for it to change levels (by the way, they say to hold it for 3 seconds to turn on or off, but it's really about 1 second). 3) The color code of the power levels is weird. I have other heated devices that have 3 levels and ALL of them go Red to Green to Blue (red is highest, blue is lowest), but these slippers have Blue as medium and Green as low - that's just weird.

I give it 4 stars for affordability. $80 seems a bit high.

Something strange, but charging these batteries the very first time broke my usb adapter (rated for 2 outlets at 2.1a each). I didn't notice when it broke, but when I checked on the batteries a few hours later, the adapter was dead. It's hard not to blame these batteries, considering all of the use this adapter has had in the last few years.

I just ordered 2 pairs of extra batteries (which are not a bad price at $27) so that I can have heat all day/evening.

Update (Jan 17) - the accidental button pressing is getting very annoying. I suppose if you sit perfectly still (never cross your feet, or place them sideways on the floor or against objects) then this isn't a problem, but if you move your feet around at all, you are going to be changing the heat level constantly. Now I'm looking at my feet about every 10 minutes just to make sure I've not bumped the button again.

Update (Jan 20) - Durability - sucks. I've only had these for 5 days and already they are barely working. The first 2 days these heated my whole foot. Now, even on the highest setting, I can only feel a little heat in the very tip of the slipper. My feet are cold again. Very disappointed.

title: Packaging issue, but supposedly a great product.
text:
Ok so I ordered this oil because about a year ago I read that it's supposed to be good to shrink fibroids. When I read more about the oil, I saw all the proposed benefits, so I decided to purchase it. Honestly, I can't say I noticed any difference when I bought it a year ago from the company itself, but then again I didn't use it for the extended period of time that I read one lady suggested so I decided to give it another go.

I do recall reading that Hemp oil is supposed to be kept in a cold env't. When the company itself shipped the product to me, it arrived in an ice pack that was cold. However, when a third party seller of Amazon shipped the product to me, it was not in a temp controlled package and it was left outside on my front step. That day happened to be a bit warm and I came home late to a package that was sitting on the front step. I wouldn't have cared had it been the dead of winter, but unfortunately it wasn't the dead of winter. So FYI, the heat denatures (breaks down) the product and pretty much renders it useless.

title: It is okay but I am glad I bought it
text:
I am rating this only 3 stars due to the fact the straps DO come up high and criss cross in the front - even wearing a t-shirt, the crossing straps show. SO it is not exactly something I like to wear out in public. I have before and got weird looks and an "Oh - are you wearing a pregnancy harness?" Unlike the picture shown, if you have even slight excess body fat (as most pregnant women do), the fat will squish out above the thick belt part - and out through the "triangle holes" you see on the waist of the model in the picture. I wore mine OVER a tank-top yesterday just around the house. It looked a bit better. But I'm not about to go out in public with this belt on the OUTSIDE of my clothes.
As for the support it offers, it is great! I am a small person who tends to grow big babies so I need that extra lift. It definitly helps take the pressure off my hips. I will wear this belt (around the house) as long as I'm able during this pregnancy for sure! So if you are a woman who can stay-at-home, this belt is great. If you are a woman who is constantly on the road, I would suggest a more descrete belt.
Happy shopping!

title: Interesting and useful device
text: I got this because not only did I want a room air freshener, but I am very interested in cold plasma technology which I believe is going to revolutionize medicine, environmental clean-up, sanitation among other things. Who knows, maybe it even gets rid of ghosts! It is small but sturdy and well-made, was well-packaged in a strong little box,  and seems to work. I have a stuffy room in my house and after putting it in there for around 15 minutes, the air is noticeably cleaner. I still haven't quite figured out the best way to charge and then use it, it does take a couple hours to charge, then runs 3 to 4 hours before it needs charging again. I don't think it's designed to run continuously though, instead it clears air in a room or car fairly quickly. It could be useful to bring somewhere with you where the air might be bad, or there is a fear of germs in the air. Anyway it's an interesting device, it takes a while to really figure out how to use it and discover if it may have additional applications which I suspect it does. It does come with directions in English, though I wish it was a little more indepth.

title: Quick pick-me-up
text: A very nice set of shower steamers, lots of different fragrances to choose from. It's a very pretty box and ideal for gifting too. One steamer lasted me 3 showers. A lot depends on where you place the disc, the temperature of the water and definitely, how long your showers last. I placed them in a small soap dish with holes on the bottom, in a corner of the shower, away from direct stream from the showerhead. The fragrances are light but certainly discernible. I have allergies, so strongly perfumed products typically become more of an irritant. But these are pleasing. They do bleed color (as expected) while you shower but they also wash out by the time you're done showering. A nice pick me up first thing in the morning to wake up and feel refreshed. Alternatively, you could also use these as air fresheners in a restroom, if you peel away a bit of the plastic layer. Or even as scent boosters for clothes (especially if you store clothes away seasonally). However, maybe remove the plastic seal, wrap in wax paper so the color doesn't deposit on clothes, make some holes in the wax paper for the fragrance to waft. It's a fun product.

title: Heats up fast and works great
text: I desperately needed a new curling iron. Mine was super old. After searching online I decided to give this one a shot. I hate to spend time doing anything to my hair, so being able to style quickly is a must. This iron heats up very fast. I use it on the hottest setting (400 degrees) so that the curls set tight and fast. It only takes about a minute for it to reach this degree. The display is easy to use. Hold the power button on a few seconds use the up and down arrows to select your temperature. The numbers will blink until the temperature is reached. I was able to curl my whole head of hair in just a few minutes. When I was finished it was easy to store the iron, as you can secure the wrapped cord with an attached velcro strap. My curls were so much nicer, tighter and held a lot longer than when I did the same style using my old curling iron. I am very pleased with my purchase.

text:
Not sure why my first review was removed. It was strange. Still waiting to hear back from Amazon about it.

This unit is full of compromises. But mainly, it was too weak so it was an instant return for me.

Pros:
1. It's small and portable

Cons:
1. It's too weak. Strength of the water is equivalent to about 1-2 in the standard Waterpik water flosser - it's simply too weak to really clean anything. It's almost as if swishing water in your mouth will be more effective.
2. Even though description says it's 220ml, I filled the water reservoir to the max line and measured. It's about 145ml. The water lasts about 7 seconds in high setting, so you will be constantly refilling it.
3. It has only one button. You have to press it and hold it to change modes - so if you want to change strength or whatever you have to first turn it on (water starts shooting out) while you are trying to change the mode. There should have been a separate mode button.
4. Unit looks well built but the LED lights look cheap.

Doctor after doctor just kept putting me on stronger and stronger medications. Also I'd wake up every hour at night to pee. In my mid 30s I was thinking, these are just signs of aging.

After some research, I came across Dr. Dean and her Magnesium miracle. So I started buying magnesium supplements from my local pharmacy. I was thinking Magnesium is Magnesium, so why shell out $30 for a magic potion? Man, was I wrong! My symptoms did not go away. My blood pressure had elevated to 265/138 even with 4 medications and the doctor wanted to rush me to the ER.

I ordered a bottle of Remag out of desperation. Literally, within 2 days, my leg cramps were gone! Gone! My unusual and noticably hard heart beat normalized. I thought hmm, that's strange. And no more waking up every hour to pee. At my job as a Data Analyst, I find that I am more relaxed and focused when I'm writing code or working on large complex datasets.

Thanks you so much for this product. It is worth its weight in gold to me.

Update 1: I got lab results yesterday (03/24/2021). My hypercalcemia is gone! I will update again as I get more lab results over the next few months.

title: A great fit for the Fitbit ecosystem
text:
My wife and I have been using the Fitbit Aria scale with our pair of Fitbit Flex fitness trackers. Fitbit does and excellent job of tying these devices together, and I really applaud them for making setup as seamless as possible. I use this scale every day. Weight and body fat measurements are stored in the cloud, and you can access them from the Fitbit mobile app or any Internet connected device, complete with fitness goals and a graph chart of your progress.

One minor drawback I have with the device is the screen resolution. There's only enough room on the screen to display your initials on the device when you step on, it would be nice if it was able to display your full name or any additional information. And like most cloud-connected devices, there is a premium price which can be a deal breaker for some. But if you're sold on what Fitbit has to offer, or have any of their other biometric trackers, this scale is a must have.

title: Ideal for my purposes
text: I purchased this to help a bit as I recover from a foot issue that includes a broken bone. It's been wonderful -- it has reduced pain a great deal because I can off-load a bit of weight onto it, just enough to relieve pain. And it has helped normalize my gait since I've had to favor this foot for weeks now. I wish I had had it sooner. It has exactly the features you see and they all work on mine. The light works fine and I use it if I need to get up at night and trundle off to the bathroom without disturbing my husband by turning on more lights. It's pretty bright and I could see it would be great at night walking through a parking lot, for example. It snaps together in a flash -- and as per the directions, you should make sure each part is snapped in place. But it is perfectly reliable if you check on that. The height adjustment is easy. One of the best features to me is how it pivots. Very helpful. It's true that the "foot" is small but that's what I wanted so I wasn't tripping over it -- that means that it's less stable standing alone than a big four footed cane. But on a hard surface, it stays put. On a soft surface like a carpet, I just lean it against something or lay it down even. No big deal. And it does have a wrist strap if you need it. It's light and folds easily and has a case. I would always travel with it now -- just in case.  For the price, it's really great. People use canes differently and it's fairly personal -- but for my particular purposes, this one is exactly right.

title: The best mask, so far.
text:
I've purchased so many masks the past 18 months. This is the only mask that actually keeps my glasses from fogging up!

I was hesitant to pay this much for a single mask, but my friend had purchased and recommended Halo to me. This mask didn't disappoint! I could have saved so much wasted $$ if I had known about this brand months ago.

I cannot drive or read without glasses. I wear glasses all day at work, inside and outside. I also wear them to workout and to Zumba. Surprisingly, my Halo mask prevents fogging 95% of the time (the exception is when it's really cold outside and I'm breathing hard from exercising, then my glasses do fog up).

The only thing I don't like is that after wearing my mask everyday for approx a month, I noticed that the material around the chin area has stretched out and also the ear bands. Hoping that when I wash the mask that everything will shrink back into place (?)

If your a bigger person looking for a large mask, this is a great choice!

I would definitely purchase again.

title: Integrating this with your Fitbit turns monitoring your health into part of your lifestyle.
text:
This is an awesome addition to your fitbit. A lot of people have reported that the body fat % feature does not work because there is too much variation depending on how hydrated you are at the time of weighing. I use this to my advantage because it gives me a great idea of how much water I'm holding when I suddenly regain 2lbs due to a salt heavy meal the day before. I really like this product and would recommend it to anyone who is interested in purchasing it.

I weigh myself every morning wearing the same general sleep clothes and my fitbit and it updates my fitbit dashboard with my progress toward the weight goals I set. It has a graph that starts the day you set the goal to the day you achieve the goal and shows you your progress on a daily basis. It's a great tool.

Also some people complained about getting it to connect with their wifi. Even though I broadcast my wifi, I used the option to manually type my SSID and password instead of selecting it from a list. (Mine never showed a list.) Its important to remember your WIFI network name or ESSID needs to be a single word with only letters and numbers. Once I did these two steps, the scale connected and has been flawless ever since.

text:
UPDATED REVIEW: 3 stars to 5 star.

Customer service is great. I received a new brush that isn't shedding and works like a charm! I'm glad I made this purchase and that Latherwhip stands behind their product(s)!

After all the positive reviews, I really wanted to like this shaving brush, but it's falling apart like the cheaper Van Der Hagen brushes. I'm a bit disappointed, as I know how to properly take care of them.

(-): It's shedding left and right, even after 15-20 uses. I purposely held off on the review to see if it stopped; it still hasn't. My shaving cup is full of badger hair after each use. It also seems that the glue in the handle is starting to come out as well.
