title: Licorice is very useful plant. It contains many anti-depressant compounds and is ...
text:
Licorice is very useful plant. It contains many anti-depressant compounds and is an excellent alternative to St. John's Wort. As a herbal medicine it has an impressive list of well documented uses and is probably one of the most over-looked of all herbal wonders. Licorice is useful for many ailments including asthma, athlete's foot, baldness, body odor, bursitis, canker sores, chronic fatigue, depression, colds and flu, coughs, dandruff, emphysema, gingivitis and tooth decay, gout, heartburn, HIV, viral infections, fungal infections, ulcers, liver problems, Lyme disease, menopause, psoriasis, shingles, sore throat, tendinitis, tuberculosis, ulcers, yeast infections, prostate enlargement and arthritis.
Hundreds of potentially healing substances have been identified in licorice as well, including compounds called flavonoids and various plant estrogens (phytoestrogens). The herb's key therapeutic compound, glycyrrhizin (which is 50 times sweeter than sugar) exerts numerous beneficial effects on the body, making licorice a valuable herb for treating a host of ailments. It seems to prevent the breakdown of adrenal hormones such as cortisol (the body's primary stress-fighting adrenal hormone), making these hormones more available to the body.

title: Great little machine for this price point.
text:
I didn't really want to pay this much for my first foot spa, but this was the least expensive model I could find that heated water rather than just maintaining already warmed water (or just claiming to and not even doing that much). However, this FB-600 model lives up to its claims. It does heat up water for you within a few minutes, and provides as close to a salon type pedicure experience as you can give yourself (or someone else) at home.

I got this to save money on those pricey salon visits to get my nails done. I've only used it for pedicures as it was designed for, but honestly I think it's versatile enough to be used for your manicures, too. Beats buying a second gadget for the same purpose if your goal is similar to what mine is - to save yourself $30-40 every 1-4 weeks to get someone else to care for your hands and feet. It makes for a very relaxing evening or weekend afternoon in my recliner with my favorite tv show and a glass of wine. Even though I'm the one doing all the work.

For the other features, now that I've attested to the effectiveness of the one everyone wants to know about - THE HEATING - here's how I think they rate.

Bubbling - 3/5
Moderate noise that is muffled once your feet are in the tub. Be careful with any lathering products you might be tempted to put in the tub for your soak because this setting will make MAJOR bubbles like the kind on a cartoon when someone tips over a whole box of bubble bath. Only put in one or two drops at the most.

Vibrating - 2/5
Very noisy to the point that if you're using this while watching tv or talking to someone on the phone you will have to adjust volume to do both. I think this is supposed to give a massaging effect, but honestly I didn't feel anything when I used the vibration function except annoyed. Does not cause as much lather as the bubble setting does.

Heating - 4/5
Like I already mentioned, this feature is VERY GOOD for this price. It heats the water to a nice temp and keep it that way for as long as it's plugged in so you can have a 15 minute soak or take an hour to do a full pedicure and be slow about it. Two minor adjustments that would make this PERFECT that are probably available on higher end units for a lot more $$$. 1) A thermostat to actually set the temperature you want your water/ It just happens to get it right for me, but everyone may not be as pleased as I am with the auto setting. 2) It does not allow you to use ONLY heat, so in order to have heat you must turn on either bubbles or vibration as well. This is a minor inconvenience to me as I'm finishing a pedicure and really don't need the bubbles anymore but would like to still have the tub warm for the foot I'm not working on. Minor, but still an inconvenience, no less.

Attachments - 3/5
These are moderately useful, especially if you don't keep your own pedicure tools around or are just starting out. There are two pumice stones with different grits, a brush, and a roller for massage. They are all mounted to the machine and can be detached for use (yes, even the one in the middle). It's a nice little bonus. Personally, I like the little storage hatch up at the top of the machine with the three attachments not currently in use (whichever is not in the middle) and think this is a great place for me to store my other tools - cuticle nippers & scissors, nail clippers, files, cuticle oil, etc.

title: My Stop-Smoking Hero and My Helpful Crutch Down the Road
text:
I would give these 10 stars if I could. They are the reason i was able to quit smoking in November 2002, and they are the reason I never backslid, because I could have one of these instead of a regular nicotine cigarette.

They are not as tasty as my menthol Virginia Slims, or my Misty menthols, or even the generic menthols I was smoking at the end because cigarettes had gone up so high, but they approximate smoking well enough, and taste enough like menthols, that I was not only able to quit with no nicotine withdrawal (because I switched to these a month before I quit), but also I always had my pack of Honeyrose around after I quit in case I felt the urge for a smoke. That urge dissipated over time. I haven't smoked one of these in a couple of years, but I still have a pack in my freezer just in case.

I didn't follow the Honeyrose advice specifically. I just stopped the nicotine cold turkey and switched to these. The habit was really more compelling to me than the nicotine addiction, so the act of smoking overcame whatever withdrawal symptoms I had. Then I quit smoking the herbals. I did it out of town, out of the country even, while staying with a friend in Montreal, not around smokers, and it went OK. I'd say, "I want a cigarette," he'd say, "You're missing the point," and that would be that.

I smoked these on and off for years after I quit, sometimes just one or two, sometimes a bunch if I was drinking. I always enjoyed smoking (which makes it really hard to quit in standard ways -- nicotine delivery systems really aren't helpful for me, as I miss *smoking*), so it was nice to have the option to have an occasional cigarette.

I still walk by smoking people and breathe in their smoke and enjoy it. I remember that during my transition time I ran out of herbals and bought a few packs of regular menthol cigarettes while I waited for my Honeyrose cartons to arrive. The nicotine does make a difference, and you really realize it more when you haven't been getting any.

Btw, these cigarettes smell a bit like pot. I've gotten a few weird looks. I was once outside a Greyhound bus smoking and someone asked, "Do you realize ...? " and I said, Yep, I know, they smell like pot." :) I was at a music street festival in Montreal at some point after I quit, and I commented to my friend, "Hey, people are smoking herbal cigarettes." ;)

They may not be just as good as the original menthol cigarettes I smoked, but they always felt good to smoke. And I think it's fine that they don't taste like smoking, since it's better not to smoke anything at all.

(And they still taste way better than non-menthol cigarettes! :D)

title: Handy!
text:
I quite like this shaver.

What I like about it is the fast charging and how easy it is to clean. I'm the type of person who has to shave every day during the week, I always have. I work in an office and, to be honest, I quite like to shave in the morning.
So normally I use a Gillette manual razor because you can't beat it, and I was always going to compare the quality of the shave with this and the Gillette. It doesn't really compare, not well at least. This electric shaver gets fairly close and does fairly well. But there's no comparison here. Also, I've noticed you may have dryness on your skin after using this. I have, some of the time it feels a bit itchy.

But you have to think about the benefits of this, too. It's much cheaper than using razors all the time. It's also more portable because you don't need to use shaving foam. Also it's quicker. Ive come to use this on the weekends when I can't really be bothered with shaving, and I really like if for that purpose because it's a quick sweep over your face and it's good enough.

Think about it this way, it's $30 and it is good enough. You can't really expect top of the line quality shave but for the price you are honestly getting real value for money and convenience. I think that's what you are buying it for.

title: You have to think about this
text:
These face masks are extra comfortable. They fit nicely around the nose and sweep down to close snugly right under the jaw line. They poke out a bit infront allowing for this nice pocket of air that makes these super comfortable and very easy to breathe in when you are up and moving around. It's an excellent design, mostly. If you are like me, wearing the disposable masks most of the time then you know all about the itchy fibers inside the mask, the burning of the strings behind your ears. So comfort is a bit of a thing for me.
That leads us to the downside. There isn't any sort of wire along the top for your nose. What happens here is you have a space where the air you are breathing basically swishes upward. Now if you are conscious of safety as your main concern this is a big fail for a face mask. It should be fitting close to your face around the edges of the mask, otherwise the vapors are escaping and it defeats the purpose of wearing a mask in the first place.
That's not to say I think this is entirely a fail. These might be fine for the most part but if you are in a close space with a group of people this is probably not the best mask to be wearing to be considerate of other people's safety.

I believe I will be able to use them because I have my own office and I'm not really close to a lot of people. Regardless of that I keep the mask on at all times just to keep other people safe. So I will likely wear these as I think they will do enough under those circumstances.

title: Too expensive
text:
I love Soylent Powder. I have a box of 14 days of food sitting in my kitchen right now. That's in the pouches though, the tub is just not a good deal.

For strangers to this world, Soylent Powder tastes to me like milk that's been blended with some fiber and a hint of banana, making a slightly gritty and thin shake. It's really pretty tasty, and takes well to any flavorings you want to add. Definitely something you can eat for multiple days without getting tired of it. And yes, I've lived on Soylent for some time (although I'm a tall guy requiring over 2,000kCal, so I eat "normal" food in addition to Soylent).

What you get- 2.4 days worth of food. The Tub has 24 "servings" at 200 calories each, meaning the average adult needs 10 scoops per day. Soylent was invented as a total food replacement so you are supposed to live on Soylent for all your meals. With only 2.4 days in the tub, I'm just puzzled. Are you only expecting to live 2.4 more days? They should have rounded it to a whole day, even if they want people to mix it into their normal shakes.

What you don't get- If you order the pouched version of this product through Soylent's website, they include a free pitcher with your first order which allows you to prep a whole day of Soylent in one go. You don't get that with the tub, just a scoop like any tub of protein powder.

What you pay for- Soylent Tub costs almost twice as much as the pouches, which doesn't make any sense. In a bulk package like this, it should cost less. What happened?

Overall- It's the same contents as the pouch, for twice the price, and in an odd increment that doesn't divide evenly. This doesn't appeal to Soylent's fan base. I also don't expect it to take off with the nutrition crowd, because it contains more fat and sugar than most people would like to have in their daily protein shake. When I'm doing shakes, I prefer to have a protein shake in the morning so that it will balance out against the fats and carbs I eat during the day. This might make sense for people who just want to test the waters of meal replacement shakes, as one Tub is less commitment than the beginner subscription to Soylent Powder in pouches (which is 7 days of food, instead of the Tub's 2.4). But that's the only audience I can recommend it for, and then I'd encourage them to switch immediately to the more cost-efficient pouches.

title: A few things I dislike but an overall decent bike
text:
The scooter was very simple to assemble and adjust to my height. I was pleasantly surprised to open the box & find a blue scooter. I say surprised because I ordered black but had literally just complained to someone there were no good colors to choose from so black was the default. I like the dark blue I received much better. The scooter maneuvers very easily. The dual hand brakes are fantastic bc sometimes I have to carry something in 1 hand & steer/brake with the other. I also HIGHLY recommend getting a scooter with a basket. The basket on this has been so helpful.

There are a few things I dislike. The knee pad is shaped well but the padding is pretty hard and the fabric covering is hard too. After 1 day of using the scooter, my shin felt bruised and sore. You can buy knee pads, but I found putting a soft folded towel on the seat under my leg seemed to fix the problem. The paint on the scooter chips off easily. When I slid the basket onto the 2 prongs that hold it, it immediately scraped a bunch of the paint off the prongs. My other big gripe is transporting it. This scooter is too tall to fit easily in my car's backseat. The handlebars fold forward so you can turn the scooter upside on its seat but you have to take the basket off to do that. I was able to rearrange my trunk to fit the scooter so I found a solution, but it would've been better to have the handlebars hinge the other way.

Other people have mentioned the scooter hitting bumps or cracks in sidewalk, spots where the floor changes from carpet to wood, or in my case large acorns, which cause the scooter to pop up or bounce & lean causing people to lose balance or fall down. I have had this experience but that doesn't happen with just this scooter. That's going to happen with any knee scooter unless you get one designed to go "off-road". It does have a few flaws, but if you aren't needing it for a long period of time, it's a pretty good knee scooter.

Update: Now that I've used the scooter for 1 month, I have discovered things I never would've thought of. The vibrations from rolling over sidewalk cracks & dips & dividers, etc caused 2 of the bolts holding the knee pad in place to wiggle out. I had to go buy 2 new screws from Home Depot. I suggest checking your screws for looseness regularly. I've also found the metal basket vibrates against the metal prongs holding it and squeaks incessantly like nails on a chalkboard if the basket is empty. I suggest wrapping the prongs in electrical tape, duct tape, fabric tape, etc or something to keep the metal from touching. I'm sure these issues are not limited to only this scooter. So be prepared to make modifications to any scooter you purchase.

text:

It provides a good heating surface larger than many other heating pads. It is premium priced undoubtedly due to the extraordinary health benefit claims and the addition of jade ceramic pieces which the seller claims have health benefits beyond normal heating pads.

The science behind the seller's health benefit claims appears uncertain at best especially when FIR is employed in combination with jade ceramic chips embedded in heat producing fabric using heated wires. Most scientific studies using FIR and ceramics use jade and tourmaline in powdered and tiny particle form embedded in fabrics emitting FIR using body heat. In my opinion, this device should not be mistaken for or inferred to provide the same therapeutic effects as these scientifically researched devices.

While the health claims made regarding this product seem a bit over the top in my opinion it is an excellent general purpose heating pad if you're willing to pay a premium.

title: DON'T FOLLOW DIRECTIONS - Secrets from a 3rd try with Loubs
text: Alright, so I'm typically too lazy to write reviews, but these go on my Loubs so I feel the need to let you know. Plus I've now put these on 3 different pairs... 3rd time's the charm, right?! First don't trace and then cut. That doesn't work. The tracing doesn't come out right because the Loubs are so slick on the bottom and it's hard to get a perfect cut - you end up cutting too short and leaving parts of your shoe vulnerable. Instead, unstick the whole 3M sheet and lay it down on a clean surface (sticky side up). Be careful about the toe placement (place at the top of the protective sticker) and stick the sticker on the bottom before cutting. When you do this, you have some flexibility of readjusting, but when you press firmly, it's permanent and hard to remove and replace. It's easiest to ensure the bubbles are out in the middle then smooth over the rest of the shoe. If you remove and replace, the plastic 3M does stretch out. Smooth over the bottom of the shoe and THEN cut (very carefully) along the edges. I used a pair of cross-stitch scissors - they're smaller bladed and more precise then regular fabric or kitchen-drawer scissors. When you cut, sometimes it's easier to cut the larger chunks off first then the edges. Just do what you think and feel rights. This was the easiest and most successful way to install these protective soles on my 3rd pair of Loubs. My other 2, I actually traced and left chunks out and now regret doing it that way. So please, do what you're most comfy with, but don't trace and then cut too short.

text: I bought this exact pack at Costco, so needles to say that I had EOS balm for months! I was excited about the hype and using a new lip balm. All of the sudden months later, I started to see the sides of my mouth where both lips connect crack. That area started to look very dull and very dry. It was horrible. Well months went by, same problem persisted, but now my lips went drier and drier every day. To the point that I had to reapply the balm 24-7 or else my lips would crack and bleed. I thought initially that it was a new mouth wash I started to use. I stopped using the mouth wash and the dryness persisted. I could not imagine that the lip balm I was using was the cause until the day that my lips reached its worse conditions (see picture) and I complained to my husband and he mentioned he saw on the news a lawsuit against these suckers. I immediately stopped using them and bought back the regular lip balm I was using before. It's been a month since I stopped using this product and my lips have gradually improved but I still need to use lip balm every day but not to the point that I need it 24-7, thank goodness. I hope my lips would fully recover but buyers, please beware. If you see the first sign of dryness while using these, toss them away!

title: This oil is NOT an oil at all  👎🏼
text:
I’ve taken borage oil supplements for years. I’ve used various brands, and although Jarrow is probably my favorite, in reality I’m not sure there’s any difference between them all. They’re simply soft gelatin capsules filled with the golden oil.
When it came time to reorder this month I noticed a brand, new to me: Starfire. The price was better and it offered more capsules so I wouldn’t have to reorder so soon. Seemed like a no brainer. You know that saying “ If it’s too good to be true ...”?
The capsules arrived and even before I opened them I noticed a difference. The bottle was lighter and the capsules moved freely (you know soft borage capsules often stick together .) The real shock came when I opened the bottle: hard gelatin capsules, similar to the old cold relief capsules, filled not with oil ... but with a strange gray powder.
Who knows what’s in these things, but I’m NOT taking them. It’s back to a reputable brand for me. I suggest you do the same.

title: If you have a Kindle, this is for you.
text:
I bought my fiancee a Kindle for Christmas last year, and she really loves that.
However, she finally mentioned to me how nice it would be to have a reading light to allow her to read in bed or otherwise in low light.
I went about scouring the Net for reviews that indicated which of the scores of reading lights out there worked best for the Kindle.
It didn't take very long to see multiple well written and glowing reviews for this interesting Verilux light that uses a cold cathode tube for illumination.
This is different technology from conventional incandescent, LED, or even fluorescent lights, even though the nature of the lighting element on this Verilux is most similar (at least in terms of appearance) to fluorescents.
However, there IS a difference, that being that this uses a highly efficient low energy version of the same basic technology as that used in conventional televisions.
The result is a tiny tube about the thickness of a pencil lead extending the full 3" across the reflector head that evenly distributes a pleasingly white light for its full length.
The light level is bright, but not so bright that it becomes unpleasant, and has two brightness selections.
It has a very good integral clip that permits it to clip to the top of the Kindle, allowing the illumination to wash the full length of the screen, all the way down to the bottom.
I also like that its slide switch has the "Off" position at one end and both of the brightness selections at the other, instead of (poor design if you see it) having the "Off" between the brightness selections.
Having handled this light, I find myself puzzled at those who mention questioning its durability.
I find it durable without being heavy, and I don't intend to use this to drive nails anytime soon.
Another nice thing about this light is that it uses two ordinary AAA batteries, making it easy to find a fresh set to keep the light going if you run out of power.
A very good idea that Verilux had when they designed this was to allow it to uses rechargeable Ni-MH batteries, charged with the included USB cable.
You can even run the light with no batteries at all, using the USB alone for power, making for a handy way to read while sitting at your computer.
I can make one suggestion to anyone who wants to use this with rechargeable Ni-MH batteries, which is to strongly recommend batteries labeled "Pre-Charged," as those batteries hold a charge while not being used considerably longer than those not so labeled.
The pre-charged variety hold a charge for a couple of months, quite unlike the others, which self-discharge (run down while not in use) at a rate of approximately 10% per day.
My fiancee is quite happy with this outstanding reading light, and I will recommend it to anyone else I know in need of a reading light, be it a Kindle user or an old school cardboard and paper reader.

title: Spark tastes AWFUL!
text:
Many of my colleagues swear by Spark. I have resisted trying it for a few years now, only because I don't love the idea of caffeine/chemical drink mixes. I finally gave in and gave these samples a try. I have been through 4 flavors and they keep getting worse and worse. Admittedly, I'm mixing them in probably 20 oz of water, and not the 8oz recommended. I can't imagine what a concentrated taste would be! Apple, grape, and watermelon are all undrinkable. Pink lemonade was tolerable. Fruit punch, mandarin orange, and mango strawberry are still in the lineup to try. The immediate smell when opening a package is a mix of 1980's chewable vitamins, dogfood, and burnt hair. Really--I'm not trying to be dramatic. The taste is whatever the flavor is, but you can still smell that awful smell. The energy from it is unremarkable, and I probably prefer a redbull for the effects I'm looking for (at least those taste like sweet tarts). I'm still making my way through the rest of the flavors, but as it stands now, I will be leaving this taste test failure behind.

title: Weak zip seal, but EXCELLENT product inside!!
text: I love this product. I was a little skeptical about purchasing because there were only 3 reviews and I thought they were probably paid or got the product for free, but nope... just like a couple of the reviews mentioned, this somehow tastes clean...good and clean. The chocolate flavor to me has sort of a chocolate malted flavor, which I love. The ingredient list is simple. I'm overweight and using this as a meal replacement once a day. The only negatives (and they aren't really that bad) are 1) the sodium content is a bit high for me because I have hypertension and I'm trying to drastically cut down my sodium intake (@ 450 mg this means that I really have to cut down the sodium in the other foods that I eat). 2) the ziplock bag was broken when I opened the package (the package was still completely sealed, but when opened the one side of the zip was stuck into the other side which made it impossible to reseal). Luckily, I had a 2 lb container for another company containing the most horrible, gritty, plant-based protein ever. So I just dumped the other into the trash (Let's face it, it was going there anyway after sitting on my shelf unused for a year) and filled it with this awesome protein powder, then I cut off the nutrition label and brand label and taped it to the container. Voila! That problem was easily solved. I'll just save this container for future orders too, and I'll definitely order this again. The price is right, it tastes fantastic, and it's not loaded with a bunch of crap you don't want in it! I do hope that the makers come up with a low sodium version that tastes just as great in the future, but I'm willing to cut sodium in other foods because this shake is great-tasting and super convenient. I almost forgot to mention that yes, this powder blends SMOOTH. I haven't used a shaker cup, so I'm not sure how well it does with that, but I use one of those portable mini blenders that use the sports bottle right on the blender (I think I paid $18 for it here on Amazon), and it works perfect. I use a cup of nonsweet almond milk with a little water, blend that, then I add a few ice cubes and blend that just to make it colder. It really is fantastic. I've tried a lot of protein powders as well as shakes that already come as a shake, and this has them all beat. It's a creamy shake (there is no gritty texture), and it's so good. I'm happy with it and feel like it was money well spent on a quality product. Thank you JW!

title: Smooth head buzzer with good battery life.
text:
W(AidallsWellup) Head Shaver, AW Men’s 5-in-1 Electric Head Shavers for Bald Men, Head Shavers for Men, Anti-Pinch, Ergonomic Design...-

This is a pretty good shaver. About a year ago I gave up the battle with balding and just started shaving my head. Since then I have been on the hunt for the easiest way to do this regularly on my own. This type of buzzer has been the best solution. This particular one I would say is pretty much in the middle in the range of best to worst head shavers I have used so far. I have tried 5 different ones for context.

Pros-
I like the 6 shaving heads. It covers a good surface area.

The battery stays charged for a good bit. I am able to shave my head two days in a row before I need to charge it.

It also charges up quickly.

It doesn't pull and this is actually something that I have noticed in general with these types of buzzers. If I use this same type on my face it typically will cause irritation but on my head, this doesn't.

Its water resistance is pretty good. I will detach the buzzer head and run it through the sink halfway through shaving and I can immediately pop it back on to finish without drying it.

Cons-
It's hard to clean the little buzzers. I can get most of the hair out but it takes a bit of effort.

It's not the most durable buzzer, some of the plastic covers have popped off. This is common with all the buzzers like this that I have used though.

I really don't find a ton of use with the attachments. They don't work all that well.

Overall I am a fan. I would definitely get another one of these if/when this one does need to be replaced. If I get a few months out of one of these buzzers then I feel they are worthwhile. So far this one seems like it will easily hold up that long at least. The price point on this is reasonable too.

title: Scorch Torch Caspian Single Jet Flame Lighter Exploded After Refilling, A Warning to Buyers: Beware!)
text:
I have tried any number of these torch type lighters. Some I've had should probably have been called flamethrowers rather than lighters, but this one is noteworthy, but unfortunately not for the right reasons.

Cigar enthusiasts as well as others will probably enjoy this model, but buyers should be aware of the obvious dangers as well as be aware of other dangers. From my experiences with many other torch lighter models, I can tell you that this one will stand out.

I have this item, and let me tell you, it is apparently not very well-constructed. The picture doesn't really do it justice. It is a refillable butane lighter with an adjustable single-jet flame. It fits nicely in your hand, has an easy to use push-button igniter, and it has an aptly curved torch flame emitter with a convenient, attached emitter cap. If the plastic cap were instead made of metal, it would more readily extinguish the flame.

The problem I had with this lighter has to do with regular use, simce this requires its butane supply to be refilled. Refillling it can lead to injury or property damage, considering what happened to mine after its very first refill. After refilling with canned butane, you and your property could be damaged when it explodes without warning. That's exactly what mine did after I refilled my Scorch Torch Caspian. I was driving home and all of the sudden, something hit my windshield. At first, I thought someone fired a gun, but it turned out to be the sound of my exploding Scorch Torch Caspian lighter. It exploded soon after I refilled it, and the lighter was not allowed to become hot as if it had been left in a hot car. It had been inside, and never exposed to extreme heat. But, it exploded anyway, and the entire bottom piece of the butane tank came flying off, hitting my car's windshield so hard I thought a bullet had hit my car. I had to pull over to check to see if my windshield was broken in the impact. Thankfully, it wasn't, but it could very easily have been, or worse yet, I could've been injured by it, my eye could've been injured, I could've had a wreck since I was driving along when it happened, or worse yet, I could've veered into another vehicle in the chaos.

It feels very comfy in-hand in terms of its size and its weight. It is also stylish and aesthetically pleasing. The smooth polished look of silvery gun metal functions in contrast with black parts, and it makes for a little aesthetic contrast, while repetitive gun metal accents lend to the item's visual appeal. It is striking, so much so that others are impressed whenever they first see it. That is, until I have to explain how something like what happened to me may happen to them.

Others who talk me into "a light" say things like, "Wow," "this is what you call a lighter," or simply that they "like this lighter." It's when I ask for it back, right after they used it, that they will usually ask, "Where can I get one?" For these reasons alone, this Scorch Torch Caspian Single Jet Flame Butane Torch lighter makes a dangerous, buta aesthetically pleasing gift to get or to give. (BUT DONT GIVE OR GET ONE, SINCE YOU DON'T want to cause your loved ones to experience dangers, risks of personal injuries, or any disasters while owning it.)

title: Fantastic for female comfort under breast area--very gentle, no rash!
text:
My review is not tagged as a "Verified Purchase" only because a friend bought the product for me; I assure you however I've been using it for several days and I genuinely love it--especially for maintaining dryness and comfort in the under-breast area, even after exercise. This is important to me because it seems like my skin is becoming more sensitive everyday and hyper-prone to rash--and sweat is a MAJOR culprit.

I wouldn't have thought to turn to Gold Bond for this problem; I guess I always associated it with men and--to be honest--feet, haha. I actually tried a cream specifically designed for women first; it didn't work AND gave me a hellish rash. Talcum powder is out these days due to health issues, and so I was out of ideas. Then along came Gold Bond (non-talc) powder spray. Good stuff. Recommended--and not just for guys and their feet! 😁

title: Fits a large-ish arm, is comfy, protects the elbow
text:
No one would ever accuse me of having skinny arms--they're quite plump past the elbow--and this thing stretches to fit my chubby upper arm just fine. It's not binding, it stays in place, and best of all, it cushions my sore elbow really well. Time will tell, as I've only been wearing it about half a day, but so far, I'd give it an A+. If there are any changes, I'll update.

UPDATE 5/5: As of today, I have been wearing my (what is it, Bird & Cronin?) mesh elbow sleeve/protector for a little over a week, and I really like it. To help you decide whether or not this is the right thing for your elbow issue, I've measured my arm in two places so you can compare with your own arm size; personally, I find reviews that provide this kind of info very helpful. So: just below the elbow, the circumference of my arm is 10-3/4". Just above the elbow, it's 11-3/4". The sleeve fits me comfortably with *plenty* of room to spare; the mesh is very stretchy. Seriously, it could stretch two more inches, maybe even 2-1/2".

Something you may want to be aware of is that it does tend to slide down during the night while you're sleeping, but a strip of medical tape on either end easily prevents this. And if, unlike me, you don't squirm around in your sleep very much, it shouldn't be an issue at all.

Conclusion: If you have contact dermatitis, a persistent rash, or any kind of minor cut or abrasion on your elbow and you're on the fence about this item, I recommend that you try it. My allergic rash (to a synthetic fabric in which I had encased a decorative bed pillow) had become increasingly irritated every day I left it uncovered, even though I had removed the offending allergen. The rash is now virtually gone, and I owe that healing to this garment as much to the hydrocortisone cream I used to treat it. We all lean on our elbows probably more than we realize--until we injure them in some way. After this experience, I'm convinced elbows don't heal especially well without some sort cushy covering; without that, you just keep reinjuring it. Of course, you could make a thing like this at home--I'm all for Do-It-Yourself, if you can make improvements without spending too much money or time. In this case, however, a homemade sleeve would probably not be much better functionally--and when you think of all the different bandaging products you'd have to buy to make it work, definitely not cheaper.

title: Great idea but screws need constant tightening to remain solid
text:
I bought this for my blind, elderly father to help him out of his favorite chair, a recent pin-stroke has left him with weakness on his left side & raising himself is now a challenge.
Assembly is easy despite the provided illustrations; when first assembled the unit feels fairly solid given the lightweight materials and is a big help to dad in raising himself out of his chair. The handles adjust so I'm sure it would function well for people of various heights. Dad is 5'6" & 112 lbs and it works well for him; a larger, heavier person might find the unit a bit flimsy especially after some use which is wherein the only issue I have with the unit arises. I have to check the assembly screws & re-tighten them every few days or the unit becomes quite wobbly. If not I fear the unit would eventually come apart & dump dad as he tries to raise himself. With that warning I recommend the unit; if the person using it is elderly or blind & unable to regularly tighten the assembly screws they may well be in for a nasty fall. Since dad lives with my wife & I and I can regularly tighten the unit it works for our purposes; were he living alone I would seek another solution.
For the price it is a decent, functional solution --just please be mindful of its' limitations before you buy.

title: Great brush for showering!
text:
UPDATE: After only a few weeks of using this, the plastic piece that holds the bristles started to crack (I did not drop or damage it in any way). Soon, those bristles began falling out at an alarming rate because the some of the plastic actually began to break off. Then, the cracking moved further down and more bristles fell out. Currently, about 1/4-1/3 of my bristles are gone and the cracking has widened the plastic base enough that it's now overhanging the edge of the brush and it's a bit painful when it slides against you skin as it's almost sharp. Otherwise, for now, it still functions but it's going in the trash once it gets beyond the point of using. I don't recommend this product.

I currently have a long handled brush that I'm looking to replace as it's a bit awkward in my standard size tub shower and the wood is splitting down the middle and the bristles are falling out. That said, I had some reservations about getting this wooden product. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find that the handle on this brush seems to have a coating on it to make it more water-resistant than the brush I currently have. Like other reviewers mentioned, the bristles are a bit stiff at first but it was easy to solve by using less pressure; otherwise, I love the exfoliation, it's much better than a loofah or washcloth. This brush also works well with both bar soap and body wash. Overall, I'm very pleased with this purchase and I'll use it until it too needs replaced.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest opinion. I make my recommendations as though a good friend or family member was to read my review. I rely on Amazon reviews to purchase products as well so I always give my honest opinion! Please let me know if you do not find my review helpful and I will strive to answer your questions.

title: Helpful!
text:
This was a panic purchase for a last-minute camping tripping to the mountains of Georgia with a predicted low of 26.

I don't own gloves. That is my cold weather preparedness.

They seem pretty flimsy. The sole is thin, there's a thin wire coming out of it, connected to a plastic battery box. It is not fancy or high-end.

It is, however, helpful. My feet were not toasted, but they DEFINITELY took the edge off of the cold. They stopped working after maybe...8 hours? And I could tell. The batteries still worked, the light lit up on the box, but when I plugged the insole in, the light went off. They better have just shut off to regulate themselves! But even if they end up being a one-use, for the price it was worth it.

If you're looking for something to be warm to the touch, like the disposable hand warmer things, this isn't it. If you're looking for something to help keep the cold at bay, this works great.

title: Sized too small - not sure about the mid back support - and I'm a chiropractor
text:
I'm a chiropractor and my wife has an arthritic spine with poor posture because of it. At her work she has to do some occasional lifting. I looked around and there are braces where you can spend hundreds - but if you can find something that works for less then why not give it a go? So this one looked like it might work - maybe. I ordered one based on her waist - according to the instructions on Amazon. She's about 30-inch waist (not hips). When it arrived she put it on - it fit - sort of. It's sized smaller than it states on the Amazon site. But I did notice her standing with better posture. She tried it for two days and decided she didn't like it.

This brace comes with 2 coated-metal (I don't know what they're made from - either thin steel or aluminum) flat bars - you can see that in the Amazon photo (the lighter color black areas) which provide some mid back (thoracic) support. The two arm straps wrap around the shoulders, across the back, to the opposite waist. The instructions say to wrap it inside the back support but that doesn't work very well. Therefore wrap it around the outside of the brace. The lower brace is for lumbar support. Everything attached by velcro.

I would wear it for a day or two or three to see how (or if) it works for you. And remember to squat when lifting - like a baseball catcher - and use your powerful legs instead of your weak back. Because you're wearing a brace doesn't give you the excuse that you can do things carelessly and get away with it.

So I sent this one back and ordered similar but in a size medium.

title: PURPLE: I don't know about the safety of any eggs, but my back-side thinks it's okay.
text:
To be blunt, it is not what I expected and it isn't exactly what I wanted. First, it is heavy: yes, I bought the biggest one that is double the height, but it was still heavier than I expected. The upside to this is that it doesn't move around much on the seat. Second, the shape is very specific and the cover is made to fit that: I had the cover on backwards at first and it was less comfortable. The upside is that with it corrected, it's fairly comfortable.

THE MAIN REASON I BOUGHT IT: to deal with a hot butt. I have used many other types of seats and the only one that comes close to the heat dissipation of this Purple seat is a sobakawa pillow. But even this will get swampy if you never move. I find that I still have to adjust about every 20 minutes, but here is where it succeeds: I stand up and stretch and then sit back down (20 seconds or less) and it has completely lost all the heat! Most everything else would still be hot, but the Purple seat does the trick every time!

Summary: Is this the most comfortable seat ever? No. But it is better than most other things out there and with someone like me for whom heat in the seat is an issue, it works wonders and I would recommend the (high) price.

title: For PORTABLE washers only!
text:
[[VIDEOID:fb8c9964eab86140f5960a86837c418f]] When I ordered, I was skeptical because there was a HUGE dichotomy in the reviews on whether this works or not. Since it was cheap, I rolled the dice because I've been on the search for anything that can reduce the ungodly amount of white cat hairs on my black clothes. After having just tried one, I can safely conclude that they DO work! Not necessarily a whole lot of hairs, but tons of lint has been caught for sure. All of the customer complaints must be from people who didn't read the product description, which is usually the case when a product has a dramatic split between 5 star and 1 star reviews.

If you have a front-loading high efficiency washer, this is a waste of money for you. I don't know how you would expect something with a floating foam flower on top to work while being jumbled in a load of barely wet clothes, but apparently some people have. If you buy it anyway and are dissatisfied with the results, you were warned.

If you have a full size top-loading washer, it probably won't do much for you, either. The agitation mechanics in a full size washer are different than those in your average portable washer. I attached a video showing how the lint trap works in my portable washer so you can see the difference. If your full size washer agitates like my portable one, this might work for you. The key to making it work seems to be that it gets submerged during waves of agitation and then bobs back up to the surface, hence the foam flower. Otherwise, take a pass on this and try another product.

title: It's been 5 months and I am losing my patience
text:
5/30/2022 - I am done with this. It has been in use at least once a week since December 28. There is no thinning no slowed growth. By now there should be some results, the hair is still back to above skin stubble within 24 hours of shaving. After 6 months that means this doesn't work AT ALL. Zero stars.

5/15/2022 - I have been using this once a week for almost 5 months now. By now, I should start seeing slower hair growth and thinner hair. That's not happening. I am sometimes zapping twice a week at level 4. Level 5 hurts and I'm not ready for it. It's not showing any results. I will update this again in 2 months. I do expect slower results but right now we're looking at NO results.

This laser hair remover was definitely worth trying because covers a range of skin tones up to medium dark and most hair colors. It’s an important factor as many of the at home units will only treat lighter skin tones.

What you need to know:

I am rating it for:

Hair: medium, medium-coarse, coarse

Skin: Medium brown

Areas: Chin, jawline, upper lip, neck and legs

Now let’s manage expectations: This is an at-home product, it will not work at the same speed as professional machines for that price. If professional sessions would work permanently in 6 months, I expect this to take double that time or a little more. This little machine is costing less than a single professional treatment so I don’t expect it to work like my dermatologist’s monster unit.

It is super easy to use. I barely read the instructions (not recommended).

The auto-zap setting is very convenient. I prefer it to having to press the button for each inch of treatment.

I have spent thousands on laser removal at a dermatologist that specialized in people of color skin tones. It worked meaning that the hair fell off and took longer to regrow BUT after 6 months of treatments, I stopped and not only did all the hair grow back, but some of it also grew stronger and I got more in areas that had very little before. Now it is very likely hormonal, and I could understand new hair growth but not in the areas previously treated over months.

Week one, Level 1–daily treatment (not recommended). I noticed some bald spots on my legs after use (probably from some of the hair being burned off. I am doing it daily because I know that the mild zapping cannot and will not kill the hair root if left to a normal 4-week schedule. My skin can handle it. Do not take this as advice.

I am now at week three and Level 3 – level 2 was easy and pain-free for me. I can feel the zapping more at Level 3, I would not consider that pain. My facial hair is still growing at its normal rate and looking the same. I am not expecting visible results for another 3 to 5 weeks. I am now zapping every 3 days.

I will update this review when I have more to offer in terms of results or lack thereof. For me, because I have so much facial hair, this is an expense I could justify whether or not it works in the long term. It’s one of those things I had to try, because if it works, I will save thousands (that I don’t have anyway).

title: Get your neck posture back in shape
text:
This is my second neck "traction device" the other is a different with a heating pad and acupressure points for the back.

I will warn you that this pillow at first is not for the faint of heart. It goes right to work and can be painful for someone with severe "straight neck"

I had already started my therapy with softer angle so this was easy for me on the first try but still I could feel my vertebrae loosening and my shoulders falling back into the floor mat. I timed 5 minutes and I was fine but it would probably needs to be shorter for people who haven't used these kinds of devices.

Pictured is how I used this. Knees elevated on a wedge to keep my back flat on the floor and using a yoga mat for comfort. I could feel a different from the first use, better posture, less neck pressure but this is a process. I am planning on using it at least 3 times a week for 5 minutes at a time and gradually increase to 10 minutes over time.

I don't recommend using the item on a bed. It sinks into the mattress from the weight and could be detrimental to the rest of the spine.

title: They WORK! But bring two, they dry out quick.
text:
I'm happy with this product. IT WORKS! Just used it for the first time yesterday on a hike in a Hawaii rainforest (aka, mosquito heaven). Here's the results:

1. I received two mosquito bites, both through my clothes, which were areas I didn't apply Ben's.
2. Overall it felt like the bugs were just leaving me alone, weren't flying around me, etc.
3. I required TWO wipes to get my arms, legs and neck coated well enough to suit me. First wipe was all dried up after my arms & neck.
4. This product DOES have an odor when you apply it, but it seemed to go away once dry. Also, after the stuff dried, I felt like there wasn't any greasiness or stickiness to my skin, like happens with OFF!.
5. I will start carrying hand wipes though, because I wasn't comfortable having this stuff on my hands. I was worried I might touch my eyes or nose and create irritation.
6. I have sensitive skin and was concerned about skin irritation. Right after applying, my skin looked blotchy, red & white. But during the hike, my skin was fine, the blotchiness went away, I did shower when I got home after my hike, and I can confidently say I had no skin irritation.

Minus one star for requiring two wipes, but even double the cost is a small price to pay to avoid mosquito bites!

title: One of the better protein options for the money
text:
This protein from EAS can be significantly less expensive per pound than what you'd pay for some of the premium stuff at GNC (if you catch a good sale at Amazon or if you have a membership to Costco/Sams). Some of the reviews focus on the fact that 23g of Protein in 2 scoops is a little skimpy. While this may be true, I'm not sure you'd want/need much more than 23g in one serving and if they used any less than 2 scoops for that same amount of protein you'd definitely sacrifice some of the taste. I've found that this EAS Protein tastes better than most other protein powders out there. The chocolate blends very well with skim milk and I usually throw a banana into the blender as well and it comes out great everytime. I strongly suggest using a blender as shaking by hand or stirring with a spoon will leave large sticky clumps in the glass and eventually in your mouth.

You may be able to find better products out there, but the price is reasonable and the taste is definitely above average.

title: Where the past meets the present
text: After practicing yoga and meditation regularly for a few years, I have developed an intuitive sense of when I am deeply calmed. When I reach this state of calmness, I can feel my whole body throb with my heart rate, I can then "clock" my inhalations and exhalations to my heart beat. I also see distinct visual patterns with my eyes closed. But I never knew if these sensations were indicative of a good practice of meditation or if I was just imagining the whole thing. The Healing Rhythms method works very well for me. It was a pleasure to see heart rate variation and Galvanic skin potential applied to the ancient practice of meditation in a visually pleasing manner.  I can achieve all the visual targets using techniques I have honed through my intuitive practice. The instructions that precede the biofeedback exercises are quite nice themselves but it sometimes feels a bit inadequate. Yet if you stick with it you can usually divine what you need to do (or what to let go) to reach the final state. I find myself closing my eyes during the practice and seem to get to the goal without much feedback.

title: Great Size, Great Price
text:
This is a very nice standard essential oil diffuser. I own four diffusers currently, one USB portable one for my car, one USB one at my desk, and one other big one for use in my bedroom. Additionally, I have purchased and returned two others previously, a small bottle shaped one that stopped working after one use and another car one that did not fit with my car's configuration. I mention this because I want you to know what I find makes a good diffuser, and why this is a very nice one.

A good diffuser has longevity. My bedroom diffuser has been run nightly for almost a year without a hitch; meanwhile, the attractive bottle-shaped one I purchase for use in my workout room at my office lasted exactly one day. I have used Aiho's diffuser in a couple different rooms in my house over the last few months without any difficulty.

A good diffuser has decent aroma dispersal. My little desk diffuser is only powerful enough release enough mist to surround me the and the length of my desk but none of the surrounding offices, which is fine for this particular application. My bedroom diffuser could be a bit more powerful to intensify the strength of the aroma by my bedside on the opposite end of my bedroom (and we have an average sized bedroom). This diffuser is strong enough for a bedroom, but not as strong for use in an open-air living room like mine with two huge entryways. It would be perfect for enclosed rooms or smaller spaces like an average sized kitchen or dining room, but probably too strong for small bathrooms and not strong enough for a big basement. With a quality oil and a full tank, 15 drops or so will provide a potent enough scent to awaken your mind and memories.

A good diffuser has a large reservoir for overnight use. 500ml is one of the biggest sizes you can buy for a diffuser, and it will most certainly last you all night long. This is one of the most important features for me because I don't want it beeping that it's empty in the middle of the night, and I like to wake up to the scents in the morning because it starts my day off the right way.

A good diffuser is quiet. The Aiho diffuser is never louder than a soft whisper, but if it's very quiet in the room, say at night time, you will probably hear a sound like running water, which is the bubbling in the reservoir. I happen to like that sound because to me it's very feng shui, but if you think that would bother you, you may want an alternative style of diffuser like the kind with the wicks which do not make that sound.

Other features: the Aiho diffuser is very similar to almost all of the other diffusers I've owned. It has a lighting feature to emit a soft colorful glow. I only use that in my child's room as a nightlight or if I'm setting the mood. Otherwise it has basic on/off buttons and high/low buttons. I can't imagine any other features you really might need, but this has all the basic necessities.

All in all, this is a very good diffuser for the price. I am happy with it and hope it continues to last as long as my other one in my bedroom.

title: The great thing is that you can grab the hair and ...
text: You press a button to set the temperature (instructions included).  Wait about 10 seconds.  While waiting, put on the heat-proof glove (included) on your non-dominant hand.  Divide your hair in half along your part and clip (clips included).  Then divide the half you will start with in half top to bottom and clip the top half.  Simply brush through your hair at a slow pace.  I count to 5 to make it through one section of hair and repeat as needed.  My hair is naturally wavy, not curly, so you may need to make multiple passes.  The great thing is that you can grab the hair and hold with the gloved hand immediately and not burn your fingers.  Also, the black tips aren't hot so you don't hit your ear tips or your scalp.  Only the blue part gets hot.  Repeat through the remaining 3 sections of hair.  It takes me about 10 minutes to get hair as straight as with an iron but without the damage and burns to my hands/face/ears.  I immediately bought another one for a family member after using this one.

title: Comfortable, padded waist bag
text:
Are waist bags cool again yet???...
Well, I like them, anyway - particularly for biking.

I bought this one in yellow. I have to admit it caught my eye specifically because the style, especially considering all 3 available colours, is very Star Trek. Even the logo vaguely adds to it. Am I crazy?! Yes, but I knew I had to get this one. The size and padded straps had something to do with my purchase too, but... you know.

It's large for a waist bag, a little small for a utility bag. It packs a whole lot of stuff in it's various pockets. I can use it for the bike tools and supplies I tend to carry with me if I'm out for a while on my bike, or any of my other daily items.

- The largest pocket is in the back. I fit two boxed bike tubes in it, or alternatively a full package of baby wipes, plus my Kindle and a little bag of Red Vines.
- The pocket in front of that has two internal compartments (one is zippered), plus a little key holder clip. It can hold many small items (for me: phone, oximeter, pill case, chapstick, trial size lotion, few pens, charger).
And the pocket in front of that is a diagonal small zipper pouch that can hold something small and skinny (just notes and receipts for me).
There are also two small side mesh pouches; they're not large enough to hold a water bottle but they're about inhaler sized.

The back of the pouch is very padded. It'll prevent any sweat from reaching the contents.
There's also a wide channel between two padding layers so you can stick your belt (or anything you need to carry?) through it.
The shoulder strap is removable but the waist strap is not (though it could be stuffed into the side mesh pockets if you need to).

THINGS I LOVE: The padding that extends out to the sides makes it super comfy. It can carry quite a bit of stuff, the zippers don't snag, the shoulder strap is removable, and most importantly: it's heavy duty and high quality.

THINGS I DON'T LOVE: The bottom isn't padded like the back, there are not small pen/coin/etc holders inside any of the larger pockets.

I bought this discounted in return for my review and opinions after use.

title: Compact monthly organizer
text:
The things that I like about this unit is that it is compact and organized and gives you an entire month. Each wedge (day) has 4 compartments for morning, noon, evening and bed if needed. Each wedge has a light colored number on one end for those days that haven't been completed and a dark colored number when you are finished. This allows you to easily see where you are at in your daily rotation without having to remember what day it is. It has a slot in the front to put your current days wedge until you have taken all of your pills for the day.

It came with a cylindrical pill splitter and pill crusher. The pill splitter did not work well with the pills that I have to split in half. It crushed them instead. At first I thought it was just the type of pill, but my wife gave me a spare splitter she had and it worked flawlessly. Since it is brand new, I can only suppose that the blade in the splitter isn't sharp enough or the blade itself is too thick.

Two minor flaws with the wedges. The covers open extremely too easy. Even when just handling them to place or remove them the covers will pop open. Not convenient when you have to carry the wedge with you to work in order to take your mid-day pills. Also, when filling the wedges for the month, the wedges tip over with all the covers flipped open, making it difficult to drop the pills into its appropriate compartment.

Overall this unit gives me everything I wanted while remaining compact and organized. The pros far outweigh the minor flaws.

title: Durable Lunch Bag
text:
This is a very nice unisex reusable lunch bag. The light gray color makes it perfect for men and women and gives it more of a sophisticated look.
What I like about this bag is that it's large yet compact. It has a decent amount of space inside for you to fit containers of food, beverages, utensils and more for what you need to bring to lunch. Also, the inside material of the bag makes it easy to clean up any spills that may happen with a napkin. I use this bag for work and I can fit all my food inside without my bag taking up too much space in the office refrigerator. This bag has two smaller pockets; one in the front and one in the back. It also comes with a detachable strap to carry this bag around your shoulder if you don't want to carry it by the handle.
What I don't like about this bag is the zipper to the main bag. The zipper is double-sided, so there's one on each end of the bag to close. This makes the side where the zippers end have a weird shape I'n not a fan of. If you pack a lot of items in this bag, this can make zipping the bag close difficult.
Overall, this is a good bag that I like to use almost daily. I would recommend buying.

title: Prepare for slobber...
text:
Here's my advice after trial & error with this whitening kit:

MOST IMPORTANT- make sure the mouth trays are SOFT enough.. they need a full 15 seconds in the water, any less & you will not be able to suck out the water/air enough. They need to be TIGHTLY molded to your teeth in order to stay in while whitening. I messed up my first tray, but it was the extra one ( was nice of them to supply ). I was able to mold the other 2 with no problems.

Secondly, if you're going to use the blue light, you're going to slobber.. stay close to a sink where you can spit periodically.

What I like about this kit:
1. My teeth looked whiter after only two treatments.

2. I can put the gel exactly where I want it. I have a couple molars that are way too sensitive for the gel, so I skip those & put it directly on my other teeth, then put the trays in. Voila.

3. I have extremely sensitive teeth.. they always hurt like heck after crest whitening strips. I don't know what the difference is here, but this gel does not make my teeth hurt. Big bonus for me.

A little health history: I have problems with low blood pressure and after having my son 18 yrs ago I noticed a problem with my heart. I did some research instead and came across Horse chestnut and hawthorn. I took a bottle of Hawthorn over the course of a month, then ran out and stopped taking it. (busy working Mom not taking care of myself first) The effects lasted for months, so I thought it cured the problem. No such luck. I went to find the same Hawthorn, only could find a complex (Hawthorn/Horse chestnut/ and buthchers broom). I usually only take one a day, unless I feel like I am going to have a heart attack/pass out. Over the years the cost has really come down do to competition. My first bottle was $28 18 years ago. If you wear a monitor, take it and dumbfound the stubborn doctors that are skeptical of herbal remedies.

I switched my diet to more alkaline based whole foods (lots of green veggies), started taking Bragg ACV 2X per day, and started taking some Miracle II Neutralizer daily too (started with the recommended 7 drops, now I'm around 25 drops or so).  I also bathe with the miracle II soap and use a black charcoal soap too.  I put the neutralizer directly on the hives when they are flared up and it seems to help calm them down.  I don't know if the neutralizer is the sole reason for my now almost cured hives, but I won't give it up.  I've just ordered a bottle of the gel because it will stay on better than the water.  This is good stuff and I will continue using it.  It's great for many other things too.

title: Cute And Does the Job
text:
This is a small hot water bottle made of silicone.
I was particularly looking for a hot compress for finger tip injury. While other small rubber bottles were ok sizes, I picked this blue raindeer bottle because of the two reasons. One, it is silicone. Two, it stands.

I know I would use a bottle cover for the rubber bottles when in use, but due to my skin problems, I'd rather not use rubber products around. So the silicone was my preferred choice. Then comes the shape aspect of the product. This bottle is not a uniform recutangular pillow. It got a slight tapering and gets narrower towards the top. And it can stand vertically, if you so wish. That was a HUGE plus for me. I can change the angle of warm surface that touches the injured area by changing where on the bottle I decide to grab. The bottle stays warm about an hour, so I can either place my hand flat on the bottle and try to warm the entire palm or, grab it and hold vertically, so there is less strain on my wrist and have a better contact with the actual scar tissue I am trying to warm up.

Yes, for holding it upright, this bottle is a great shape and size.
And it's cute to look at. The price isn't necessarily on the economic side, but if your need is more than just a tiny warm compress, this item is a good choice.

I took a star off because of the plastic screw cap on the bottom extending further than the surrounding "leg" portion even when closed, the bottle doesn't stand firm. It wobbles and leans, so not a perfect stand. And because the twisting cap has such a shallow indentation for finger tips to grab the knob, people with big fingers might have a hard time opening and closing it. My fingers aren't that big, but when I first try to unscrew it to wash, I couldn't open it. Had to get a piece of paper towel folded over it and used a pair of my trust worthy pliers to gently unscrew it.

title: Don't Believe the Hype
text:
Although I am going through a return problem with the seller I am going to try and keep this review as product oriented as possible.

First of all HumanWare boasts about their super crisp braille display that users rave about. To be honest here I didn't notice much difference between this and the Smart Beetle 14 cell braille display by HIMS. The price between the two is significant though, the Smart Beetle (which I've also reviewed) is around $1300 USD however the 14 cell display does make it a more cumbersome job to read much of anything.

When I got my HumanWare Brailliant BI 32 I was excited, like a kid at Christmas time for sure. The unit came in some pretty sturdy packaging and it came with a bunch of goodies. The carrying case that it comes with is a let down in my book, it's just a neoprene thing with a zipper at the side of it, honestly I felt more like I was going to drop it putting the Brailliant into or taking it out of the carrying case. For something I'm spending nearly $3000 on you should either not mention the free carrying case or get a better one like with the other braille displays.

The box also comes with a USB cable and it's one of the high end shielded ones, which as the manufacturer reccommends you should only use that one. You can also just go down to any store that sells USB cables and get another shielded one for not much money. It's not like there's a magical stone inside that thick part of the cable or anything. It also had a pretty huge and awkward DC power converter/charger thing. I didn't verify this but I assume it's got a power condition inside of it so in the event of a power surge the charging unit itself will burn out instead of the braille display. I hope that's the case anywahs.

As for the Brailliant BI 32 itself I did not get a chance to test it with my iPhone since the bluetooth didn't work, but I did get to play with a few different screen readers and PC's. It's performance was really quite responsive and the button layout was really very easy to figure out. The one thing HumanWare figured out was their thumb keys, those things do rock pretty hard core in my humble opinion! The perkins style braille keyboard was pretty standard issue honestly, but it had a nice and fluid motion. Some braille keyboards are so stiff and noisy and clanky you just give up on typing because it sounds like a crappy techno song or something LoL.

For me personally I feel like HumanWare has spent more money making up marketing material for these than they have in R&D for them. If I'm going to pay almost $3000 for an electronic device it better be fully functional and it better knock my socks off. This is just a braille display, it only has 32 cells and it takes an act of congress to switch between USB and bluetooth - or so it seemed that way, I never could connect via bluetooth. I ended up finding another braille display for about the same amount that has an SD slot for braille books, 40 cells and a switch that moves between USB and bluetooth - and the bluetooth works too!

title: Best combo i've ever used -- for best performance;
text:
Best combo i've ever used -- for best performance; 1-place wax in sun or hot water then wash and clean car [may clay], ***-important -- use pre-wax cleaner on light cars ONLY!! Works better than other cleaner or cleaner wax. Do small area at a time or will be hard to remove
2- wax- shake well and apply a very thin coat to one section at a time [one bottle has lasted me through 3-cars and 2-SUV's]. I apply to trim & windows also.
3- As it starts to haze wipe off with soft terry cloth or towels, and Buff with clean towels, terry cloth, or buffer.
Major points of emphasis --- warm and shake wax b/f use -- apply very thin coat -- leaves a deep shine to body, trim and wheels. Make sure you buff the windows extra well or will leave a film noticed as sun comes in. I recommend applying a second coat no sooner than 1-hr after the first , gives it time to bond well. May use this or Collinite Marque D'Elegance Carnauba Paste Wax #915. r. Just don't use the #915 on trim or windows. The results you will find amazing!!! How long it lasts will depend on your habits of washing, climate and soaps you use, but it usually lasts much longer than anything you will find in auto or big box stores.
I'm retired and do waxing and detailing part time as a hobby. So i've used a lot of products.

title: This disc completed my "Your Hit Parade" CD collection -- marvelously!
text:
As a life-long music collector, I found that there were precious few across-the-board labels I could recommend.
Very high on that list, the now ancient Time-Life compilations released on CD.

I own quite a number of complete collections from them, most of it music I'd heard on the radio growing up in the 1950s & '60s and later began amassing on disc (45s, LPs), tape (8-track cartridges, open reels, cassettes) and finally on optical discs.

While the bulk of my collection was music for the 2nd half of the 20th century, I'd heard a great deal of music from the first half -- via family fondness for music of THEIR lives -- as played on piano, phonograph records and even sung to me while still a toddler.
Thus adding Time-Life's "Your Hit Parade" was both a journey of new discovery and of partial reminiscence.

It took a number of years to complete the set and how altogether fitting that "#1 Hits Of The '40s" was the final disc I needed -- and found, here on AMAZON -- with such ever memorable tunes as
"Don't Sit Under the Apple Tree"
"Besame Mucho"
"Chattanooga Choo Choo"
"Sentimental Journey"
"Riders in the Sky"
"Mairzy Doats"

Those are only a few of the 36 songs on this 2-disc set, all of it transferred with the impeccable quality expected of the Time-Life producers who began releasing the "Your Hit Parade" series in 1988.

Wistfully, I wonder how much appreciated it might have been had the many now-deceased relatives been given the opportunity to hear these delightful selections in such a great format?
That is, not on the worn, cracked, skip-prone, 78rpm relics THEY collected and which still survive them.

title: VERY nice knee sleeves from a great company
text:
The package you get comes with a PAIR of sleeves, that is to say you get one for each leg (At a GREAT price!)
The material and make is thick and sturdy and the improved stitching looks, feels and responds well.
The support and heat I feel in the joint from the correct size is VERY good.

I was looking for knee sleeves to train heavy and hard in for prevention, re-injury avoidance, and support.

They felt great while training. I rolled them down to my calves during other movements and rolled them over my knees for squat cleans.
I forgot about them for the last round and realized they were still on my knees for all movements!
I loved the feel. I am usually rushing to get my knee lifting wraps off!

I will wash them often, but in the shower when I shower (with COLD water) so they will last a long time (and don't build up a stink!)

I have been training/natural bodybuilding/lifting/competing for 40+ years. Add in military service and other hard service and I have quite a few bangs on me, but I address them pre, during, and post workout as well as on off days, and I rarely notice any of them. I started ramping up my training again a year ago and am now training more and more intensely (as everyone should throughout their life.) I see that there will be some monster dead-lifts, squats and other lifts on the horizon, so knee sleeves were a must. I shopped around and liked what I was reading on Rip Toned knee sleeves.

I have thick calves where the measure is taken 6" below the center of the patella (17"+) and I thought I would like a tight sleeve (because I am use to wrapping my knees with thick power lifting wraps) so I ordered one size down.
Recommended size XXL. Ordered XL.

At the same time I happened to order a second pair for my lifting partner whose calves are 14"
Recommended and ordered size: L.

It turns out that the L was a size too large for my partner who has tiny joints and the XL was still a size too large for me (I have small joints too!)
I contacted Rip Toned to exchange the XL for a Med and they were VERY fast to respond.

If you have thick limbs and small joints, and you want a tight sleeve, you might consider a size or two smaller.
If you get it wrong, the company was very supportive and helpful in helping to get to the right final size.
For reference: 6" above the patella my legs are 22"+ and 6" below they are 17"+. My knee @center patella measures 15.5"

I took the L sleeves I bought for my partner and wore those last night for some squat-cleans.
The sleeves went on snug (YESSS!) and heated up the joint right away. At the bottom of the squat (well below parallel), and throughout, I felt solid support from the sleeve (VERY nice.) At the same time they did not impinge my movement at all.

The medium fit my partner nicely. At first, the comment from my partner was that they were tight at the top, but after the first squat, the comment was that they felt good and fit snug while providing nice support.

Since I am built sturdy and thick and handle gross weights, I expect to really give these a serious test over time.
I will update the review with my observations.

As others have noted, right out of the zip-lock pouch they come in, they are outgassing. So, open em up outside and hang em out to breath!
Those are likely VOCs you would be breathing. I could not smell anything day 2 unless I hold it to my nose.

In addition to the sleeves, you could get an RT Beanie if they are still offering them (I did not use the code, so did not get one.)
Now that I love this company, I wish I had :-)

They sent a knee sleeve e-guide with general info as well as basic info on care, very important because I want them to last!
Plus they offer you a ton of complimentary video and ebook content that covers many, many goals in training, diet and lifestyle areas!

The videos are good and informative about proper training form and about quite a few errors in training that I see often.

As I have been a high level trainer, am now working on my PhD in Physiology with a BS in exercise science and bioscience, and 3 decades training others, I could have written most of those e-books, but a cursory look at them was sufficient for me to say that they would be valuable to beginners and intermediate level trainees.

title: Simple and effective
text:
Have been using these for a few months now and finally feel ready to review.

First, the vendor is good, shipping was quick, packaging nice, instructions helpful, it is good there are two different strengths in the package.

I have had 4 big babies the regular way, and been doing Kegels pretty religiously since the 3rd (sporadically before that) The main reason I bought the Gyneflex is that I notice if there is anything in my bladder I can't jump around in exercise without, well, if you've had babies you know. Have been assured by trainer and gynecologist that this is normal for those who have had larger babies or many babies. I am fit and thin and since exercise has helped everywhere else I was hoping that upgrading the Kegels by adding resistance would help with this problem. Purchased the Regular strength since I had many births but had been doing Kegels all along.

Whew! Resistance does help but not with the original issue. I did get much stronger below, and moved from the light to dark pink, and see continued improvement. The device really makes it more clear which actions are working (pulling UP squeezes it closed better than pulling IN, for instance) The Regular set was the correct one to start with. The sex benefits may be overstated in the pamphlet but are real, when you are more fit down there everything feels better. But the exercise problem did not improve, still have to be very careful when jumping. I think maybe if you have this issue BECAUSE you are unfit below this may work, but using it to go from "normally fit" to "super fit" did not make a change in this.

I do not like the idea of using lube every day so took the advice of a previous reviewer and use jojoba oil, which works fine.

Exercise Notes - if you do the exercise reclining, as in the instructions, you may be closing the device by leaning into the bed, not using your muscles. At first I did this and thought "wow this is easy!" but then figured out it was being closed partly by the force of the body laying on the bed and not by the muscles. Switched to using it standing in the shower, which gives a better idea of the correct use of muscles and also less chance of being walked in on by a child and makes it easy to wash it off right away. I recommend strongly that you use it in different positions, not just reclined in the bed. I was a little freaked out that all the movement was front-to-back so do turn it sideways approximately 1/4 of the time. Also I think that it's better to do some medium tempo squeezing, some long holds, and some flutters instead of just pacing it evenly as per the instructions.

In short, highly recommended, device is great, but pay attention as you use it and figure out how it works best for YOU, don't just follow the instructions. And don't expect it to fix everything, but be glad for the results you get.

I don't know how effective this product is in helping hard smokers quit because I feel as though they would be more propelled to go back to the old stuff, even have a new appreciation for the bad stuff!
