title: 0 stars for durability  -5 stars for sustainability
text:
My mother purchased the Verilux Natural Spectrum Floor Lamp a couple of years ago and about 6 months ago it stopped working.

My husband tried the following:

1) Replacing the $25.00 bulb (these bulbs are difficult to find - fortunately we live in a larger urban area and have a specialty lighting store) - Didn't fix it

2) Purchasing a new "transformer"/plug for $50-$75 from Verilux - Didn't fix it.

3) Went to a lamp repair shop and were told that they couldn't fix it and that it probably couldn't be fixed without sending it back to the factory.

4) Called Verilux support and was told that it was probably the bulb fixture mechanism and that they not longer make that part for the lamp so she would just have to buy a entirely new lamp.

The bulb store did take the bulb back and Verilux took back the plug, but we now have a pristine unfix-able $200 coat-rack that has sat in our garage until we decide relegate it to some landfill or try to recycle.

Oh yes, we are now on their mailing list.

Happily, we can recycle paper.

P.S. It is no small irony that this lamp that died so soon after purchasing has the name HERITAGE and a nice ANTIQUED Brushed Brass finish.

title: BRIGHT, hard to see
text:
I'm on the hunt for an LED anti-aging mask and so far have tried the Dennis Gross instagram famous mask, an amazon brand APHRONA mask, and now have tried this CurrentBody mask which comes highly well reviewed.

My quick take: Way too bright in the eyes and pulls on the face, not for me

The breakdown:

Wearability: Meh. It comes with ear straps but realistically the mask is so wide that hooking the ear loops on your ears does nothing. I have a larger head than most and still my head was too small.

Thankfully they include a vecro black strap that hooks into additional loops so you can tighten the mask around your head.

This does mean however you're pulling the mask against your face, so your features are smooshed ever so slightly.

Also the mask is light, but you can still feel the gentle tug of gravity on the mask, ever so slightly dragging on your skin, causing your features to sag. No thanks, trying to defy gravity here.

Convenience: Decent. The mask is attached by cord to a remote that also serves as its battery source. It's light, long enough to fit in a jacket pocket and doesn't drag on the mask. You could theoretically walk around doing stuff while masking it up.

Visibility: So here's my biggest issue with this mask and how I instantly knew I'd be returning it. Those lights are BRIGHT and RED and RIGHT into your eyes. It doesn't matter how much you try to smoosh your eyes against the eyeholes, those LEDs are shining straight into your eyeballs. Everywhere you look is going to be brightly tinged with red like you're hulking out, and did I mention it's BRIGHT?

Let's not even talk about how near infrared light may or may not cause cataracts to form faster - in general how functional am I going to be, squinting through a haze of red? How can I do anything?

Not worth it for me, esp with such a hefty price tag.

title: I am SO happy with this product!
text:
I am SO happy with this product!

I like to wear socks with treads around the house; because of a stroke many years ago I have drop foot and slippers fall off my right foot. But tread socks are always way too small, even the ones that claim to be the right size for my feet. I wear size 12W shoes, am tall, and have some edema in my feet and ankles. Until now, every single pair of socks I've bought both with and without treads have been too small and it's a struggle to put them on.

Well, after reading a lot of reviews of various socks on Amazon.com, I found that I am not alone. An overwhelming number of reviewers complain that men's socks sizes always run far smaller than advertised. So with that in mind, and for only about a dollar a pair, I decided to try these Single-Side Tread Socks XXX-LARGE. They were delivered today. I tried on a pair (which I am wearing as I write this) and I can't tell you how nice it is to put on a pair of tread socks that ACTUALLY FIT MY FEET AND ANKLES! They are perfect! They were easy to put on and they're snug enough to wear securely without being too tight.

I'm going to make sure I wash them in cold water so that they don't shrink. And if the tread wears excessively (as some other reviewers have averred), for only $3.24 for three pair I'll buy more. To me they're worth five times that price. Last night we had our first cold New England night of the season, near 40 degrees and it's cool in the house. These socks are snuggly warm, and with my weak right foot I feel confident in walking in them without slipping.

At the same time I ordered these, I also ordered 3 pair of black and 3 pair of white socks in sizes that on the surface would be ridiculously large -- they say they fit feet that wear size 16 to 20 shoes -- and all those socks fit my size 12W feet perfectly also. Lesson learned! I have no idea how the all the various manufacturers can be so wrong about their sizing on so many different brands of men's socks... but I can say with confidence and now from experience: If you wear a size 12 shoe and/or have any type of swelling in your feet or ankles, you'll probably be delighted as I was to find these tread-bottom socks that actually fit comfortably and securely and are wearable.

title: Don't buy the hype.
text:
I'm not reviewing the product, just the ad - which is misleading and full of errors and outright untruths.
The alkalizing action of this product is probably fine, but they go too far in advertising it as "ionizing". Ionizing can not be done with some minerals in a metal container dropped into a glass of water - ionization involves positively- and negatively-charged particles, which require energy, usually electricity.
"Micro-clusters", while also a valid scientific concept, are also not achieved by packaging some minerals into a metal tube.
There are alkaline sticks out there for about $4 - don't pay an extra $10 for the hype.

title: Let It Grow, Let it Grow!
text:
So I don't have a beard but our eldest son DOES! And it used to be a straggly mess (who knew there was more to bears than just let it grow!)
Finding the best beard brush to meet your hairy needs is a matter of finding the right brush that will penetrate your beard without scratching the skin under it and absorbent enough not to lose all the oil before it hits said hairs. Loving the soft horsehair (though when you think too long on it - horsehair.) with a round wooden handle, nice in the palm but could be a bit bigger. This brush is designed to spread beard oils evenly throughout your beard supplying nutrients to your entire beard. I know he was dipping it into a lovely shea butter and rosemary concoction and said it had a nice 'drag' to it.

To apply the oil, simply douse out a few drops in the center of the brush and work it into your beardy drawing it circularly throughout. Simple enough, right?

The brush is equally easy to clean - just wash it with a mild soap and water and air dry. No reason though unless the oily build up is too much or you are changing product.

Before the purchase (which we got a nice discount on to leave an honest and forthright review of this product!) we'd read that it "fits well in the hand and helps to remove knots and smooth the beard. They also say that it distributes oil evenly throughout the beard."

Some people mention that this beard brush works better for shorter beards than for long dense beards, this is likely true - but our sons beard is just past his lower neck now - quite long.. but it is also very coarse and he wonders if this brush will hold up for the long haul.

If you have a thicker coarser beard, it is better to have a brush with firm bristles so it penetrates deep enough to spread oils or balms completely throughout your beard. All in all, I think an excellent purchase -and the travel tin is handy to keep the oil off your bathroom counter tops!

Serious thoughts about a return ... though I just paid $150 to get in in my house. Will update when/if legs get attached. How doesa clip in photo come off, to allow the leg module to hang, without ruining clips. Expensive products, which don't come with instructions, should be avoided like a plague!

UPDATE: Here is an Amazon customer who was able to explain an assembly step Not in the sorry excuse for a manual, or anywhere else on the web.
maurice talley answered:
"The manual isn't clear at all in this area. There are two posts, one on each side, that the leg bracket slides on to. Before you can attach it you must remove the locking clip from each post which is not stated in the manual. Once the clip is taken off of each post everything makes since. Just lift it up and place the post on each side through the hole in the leg attachment and then slide the clip over the post to lock the leg attachment into place. The key, identify the posts and remove those clips which require a squeezing motion to unlock them. I hope this helps." Thank you so very much Maurice Talley!

title: The top rolls, but otherwise a great product with potential!
text:
I received an offer to review this product and I chose to accept because I do experience knee pain. This said it would ease the joint pain and prevent injuries.
I purchased the XL, which the seller indicates measures 16-17.7 inches.
The compression sleeve arrived packaged in a plastic zip bag. The zip bag is printed with care instructions. For washing you need to use a neutral detergent and hand wash in water that is less than 30 degrees Celsius. You are not supposed to tumble dry or dry clean this product. You also cannot use bleach or iron this product. It is made of 35% rubber, 55% nylon, and 10% spandex.
The product smells a bit like a craft glue when it first comes out of the package. It is not too terribly strong, but for some it might seem a little off-putting. The sleeve itself is black with a red logo on the front. There is a size tag inside the sleeve, but not the care instructions. I recommend keeping the zip pouch.
The material is really durable and yet it is very light weight. Not as thick as some of the neoprene sleeves you find. I actually really like the feel of the material. It’s soft and yet very strong.
Putting the product on, it appears that it is sized a bit smaller than I would have thought. The top part is actually about 14-inches around. You can stretch it out further, but when you put it on it will roll down very quickly if you move. It says that it is elastic (which it is) but there is nothing preventing it from rolling down. It DOES slip.
Without any movement, I managed to get it to stay in place and I can say that it was incredibly comfortable to wear when it was in place. I could see wearing this all day (if it weren’t for the moving) and not even realizing it was there. It was not super sticky or hot like some of the neoprene sleeves can be.
In a nutshell, I really do like this product except for the rolling down. It has a LOT of potential if they can fix that one issue.
The product is made in China. They do have a 100% satisfaction guarantee. If you are not happy with your purchase, you can return it for a refund.
I purchased this product at a reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. The thoughts and feelings expressed here are my own and are not influenced by the price I paid for this product.

title: Concise and yet goes beyond pressure point therapy into much more!
text:
Several years ago I read a newspaper article about pressure points in the body that could help relieve headaches. I figured it didn't cost anything to self-administer and I found it quite helpful, but I'd not really looked into for other pains. Not that I'm pushing 50 and getting more pains more frequently (specifically sciatica) I decided to take a look at what Dr. Pinkus had to say and ordered this set of booklets.

You get two spiral-bound booklets with the main one being 75 pages long and covering a lot of ground. The second booklet (which slips vertically) is 34 pages and contains maps of pressure points on the body for specific issues. The smaller booklet has nothing in it that isn't in the larger book, but serves as a nice and more portable reference for when you actually are ready to get to work.

The larger book runs 75 pages and the first 40 pages cover what pressure point therapy is, how to find these points on your body, how to apply pressure for healing, what not to do, and then he also has an informative section concerning diet and nutrition and the need for magnesium and Vitamin D. The last 35 pages of the main booklet contain larger versions of the body charts found in the smaller booklet.

Yeah, it's a nice booklet, but does it work, too? I'd been given some stretches to do from my doctor's office for my sciatica and of course they never mentioned supplementing it with acupressure. I have done that, with the help of my wife though you can apply pressure in almost all areas by yourself, and it certain has helped my sciatic nerve issues, so this has been absolutely worth it for me. A great system for helping to manage body pains. Great stuff.

I just ordered from NOW, and I'm gonna replace some powder with whole food.

Technically, it's not really "Paleo" anyway. Paleo isn't just one part of a food that our Paleolithic ancestors NEVER ate on it's own, and it's certainly not an adultered version of that single part. And egg whites are worse than chicken breast (the last thing our ansestors did was eat the least fatty, least nutrient rich, part of an animal, and throw the rest away, let alone completely alter its structure). Our bodies will take what it can get, but it can tell when we stray from the foods we evolved on (e.g. you can replace the yolk with whatever Paleo fat you want, but it's unlikely you'll get the same satiation that the full yolk-egg white combo provides--You for sure will not get the complete amino acid profile or Omega 3's pastured eggs would provide).

The stick allows me to stay on those points as long as I want, as hard or soft as I feel necessary. There were no enclosed instructions with my Stick, but I started using it and figured it out right away. It rolls smoothly and is long enough for me to reach my upper back without straining. It feels sturdy and I do not fearl that I will somehow snap it in half.

title: A blessing...sorta
text:
Running a pet "sanctuary"... I've got many critters that need pills. This is so easy to use and eliminates so much stress.

The "soft" tip makes it a "lead pipe cinch" to get the pills, way back in the throat so they can't be spit out.... and I don't worry about hurting my guys since the soft tip eliminates that concern.

Even if you're real familiar with giving meds to pets.... this will make the job much easier for both you and you pet...

And no.... I don't own stock in the company....

PS.... I did need to put a small "slit", on both sides of the "soft tip". It was a bit small to grip many of the pills.

The small slits allow all pills to be given and the tip, even with the slits, still held the pills firmly in place. All that's needed is two, maybe 1/4 inch slits on either side of the soft tip.

UPDATE.... I still stand by my original review. BUT.... in view of the soft tip, the "push rod" will sometimes slip to the SIDE of the pill and won't push it out.

Especially if the pill is tiny. Also, depending on the type, a larger pill will sometimes NOT stay in the soft "holder" as it will be pushed out by the tip as it tries to keep it's shape and exerts pressure on the inserted item.

Still use the heck out of it and really like it. Just be aware of these little "issues" and you'll be fine. Critters allow me to insert it way back in the mouth as the soft tip doesn't even phase them. And I know I'm not causing any undue stress with a rigid pill popper.

I also didn't get instructions on what sort of placement or correct tension to use, If I did I didn't see them. I have other pain as well the top of my arm is also often hurt during several hours of play. The old people said to just get stronger their is no band for that. h. One charge has always lasted me a full day,
i. I like the magnet in the earbud and the charging station since they help with the charging and keep the ear buds in place and they don’t rattle around when in the charging station.
Some things I am not happy with or need improvement: a. Size can be reduced, b. Needs more info/pictures on how they should look when in your ear(position), c. They probably come with the middle of the three size plastic ear dome covers which felt ok at first but later tried the larger ones and they worked best (have never fallen out of my ears), d. It was not made clear for me in the beginning that the red ring(circle) around a bud was for the right ear and the blue ring was for the one that was left (pun intended), e. This kit is a very good value for the money.

title: Not sure it's really doing anything
text:
I got this for my bedroom to help with allergies. I have laminate floors that collect dust and pet fur easily. I know it gets dusty in here despite cleaning, because I'm always stuffed up when I'm in here for a long period with the door closed. I had high hopes that this would help clean the air and make it easier for me to breathe, but I'm not sure it's really doing anything.

This is a very small, portable unit, which is what I wanted. I've run it daily for 12 hours for over two weeks now and have not noticed any difference. Even after cleaning when you stir up more dust initially, this never goes above the first setting (low) on auto. I'm not sure that the sensor is reading correctly because surely the reading would change instead of always being 12, which is considered "good"?

The essential oil pad does absolutely nothing. There doesn't seem to be a way for it to dissipate throughout the air since it's a solid top. I thought it sounded like a nice feature, but I think it's more of a gimmick.

I've checked the included filter and it looks like it did the day I put it in. That's good in the sense that it won't need to be replaced all the time. But if it's still clean, it makes me think it's not really filtering anything either.

I wish I could recommend this, but I can't find any evidence that it actually works.

title: Mother-Daughter Approved!
text:
My daughter has cystic acne and I’m battling hair loss so after researching the benefits of high frequency we both agreed that this device is conducive to our needs.

Studies have proven that high frequency has shown remarkable results for the issues we’re dealing with so we both added this device to our beauty regimen & we’re glad we did!

This Eternal Clear High Frequency Therapy Wand treats both the skin as well as the scalp. It comes with four different wands that easily attach and detach just by placing it in and pulling it out. It’s easy to hold and the turn dial button simply adjusts the frequency. It’s recommended that you use it up to 3-4 sessions per week.

We’ve only been using it for two weeks now so we haven’t notice a significant difference. However, my daughter’s skin does look visibly clearer. Her dark spots are definitely less noticeable & her skin has a healthy glow which can also be contributed to a combination of her facial serums as well.

I’m currently using the comb and haven’t seen a reduction of hair loss or thickness as of yet. The glass comb feels tingly but soothing to my scalp and It glides easily throughout my hair. Neither of us has experienced any pain, discomfort or irritation.

As we’re both in the early stages of usage, we’ll continue to use this device in hopes of achieving optimal results. As for now, we’re both enjoying the ease of using this EternalClear Therapy High Frequency Kit!

title: Didn’t work as expected
text:
This Phorra electric razor came well packaged in a box with the instruction manual, a small cleaning brush, an usb charging cable, razor cover and a storage bag.

I was excited to get this razor as it can be used wet or dry. I also have sensitive skin so I was ecstatic that it was equipped with aloe strips as well. The ergonomic handle made it easy to hold and use. It also arrived fully charged so I was able to test it out right out of the box.

Unfortunately, I was so disappointed that it didn’t effectively remove all the fine hairs from my legs or armpits while showering. I just had visible patches of hair & stubbles remaining even after going over those areas numerous times.

However, I had better results while my skin was dry. The razor did painlessly remove the finely sparse hairs from my arms though. But again, it did leave some hair stubbles as it’s unable to get a close shave with this electric razor.

Having said that, it just didn’t work as expected so I can’t recommend this razor.

title: A Budget-Friendly Option for Wound Care Needs
text:
I'm currently in the middle of addressing some modest wounds on one of my legs and was excited to get the chance to try out this JJ Care Premium Gauze Roll 30-pack.

These arrived nicely packaged. Each roll is individually wrapped and is 4" wide by 4.5 yard long. The promised roll of free medical tape was also included, though it's a mere .5" wide and certainly wouldn't be a factor in my decision-making regarding this product.

These gauze rolls are noted as being longer and thicker than many rolls. They also are noted as featuring breathable gauze. They are noted as 100% polyester and free of latex. I appreciate that JJ Care mentioned the latex free feature as I do have a latex allergy.

The first time I used a gauze roll I actually applied it myself. As a paraplegic with somewhat limited fine motor skills, this can be difficult. I found these gauze rolls to be flexible and I was pleasantly surprised with how easily I could wrap my own wound. I was a little disappointed with the overall thickness of the gauze as I could easily poke a hole through the gauze and had to be ultra-careful to not do so. This ended up also being true when a friend of mine helped me wrap the wound as she also was pretty easily able to poke a hole through the gauze simply by trying to apply it.

Overall, however, I was pretty easily able to adapt to the thickness issue and I don't necessarily think that's wildly different from other gauze products including name brands. I actually expected much worse considering the price point here and was pleasantly surprised by the product's performance.

The gauze adhered to my skin without sticking to my wound. It also was able to wrap around my bandage and firmly hold my bandage in place. I'm not quite willing to call this a 5-star gauze roll set, though I'm quite impressed by it and it easily performs better than I expected. There's no question I'd purchase it again.

I really like that these are individually wrapped, latex free, and 4" in width. It ideally meets my needs and definitely has me looking at and exploring other JJ Care products. These are much more durable than I expected and they are definitely a quality, affordable addition to my wound care needs. I've purchased these twice and I've been happy both times.

title: Great product!  Love the other 2 Charlie's products, too!
text:
I liked the Charlie's laundry powder so well that I decided to try their other two products, too--the all-purpose cleaner and the laundry liquid. I started using Charlie's laundry powder after reading many favorable reviews about it, first in my old top loader and then in my new HE front loader. The laundry liquid is just as good. All three products are excellent and actually do what they claim to do! I would recommend all three to anyone. They are non-toxic, coconut-based detergents that are biodegradeable and made by a small family-owned company here in the US. They have no additives and do not leave any residues in clothes or in the washer. Buildup of residues can be the cause of odor problems in HE front loaders.

I have used about half of the bottle of laundry liquid for entire loads, and have also used it a few times as a stain pre-treater. It works very well, and so far I can't tell any difference in results between it and the Charlie's laundry powder, which I have used for several months. Both of these laundry detergents will pull old suds and other residues from your clothes first, so it takes several washes of each item before you get a true picture of what they can do. They both dissolve easily, rinse well, and leave clothes soft and very clean once all the old residues are gone. Fabric softeners are not recommended or needed, but stain treatments and bleach are OK to use with them if desired. I usually use only the Charlie's with excellent results. I don't ever intend to go back to my old detergents! Charlie's leaves no scent and the clothes just smell very clean. It's amazing how much softer towels and jeans are after several washes with this detergent, although they took more washes to get rid of the old suds than lighter items did. Charlie's is recommended for cloth diapers, baby clothes, and for sensitive skin. As is also true of regular detergents, it is not a disinfectant. It works great in regular machines as well as in HE washers.

I could use the laundry liquid from now on and be happy, but I like the Charlie's laundry powder even better, only because it is so compact, easier and less messy to measure, and cheaper to use. One bag of the powder will do 80 loads, but the 16.9 oz. bottle of liquid will only do about 16 loads for approximately the same cost. I'm rating it 5 stars because it works so well and has so many desirable qualities. Use one tablespoon scoop of the powder, or two tablespoons (1 fl. oz.) of the liquid for most loads. An advantage of the liquid is that it can double as a stain pre-treater. It is also offered in a medium-sized container, a gallon which does 128 loads. The powder only comes in an 80-load size cloth bag or recyclable jar, and a huge 5-gallon bucket size which does over a thousand loads. Both are excellent products, really just personal preference for a powder or a liquid. The Charlie's all-purpose cleaner is also a good pre-treater as well as for general cleaning.

You can find the ingredients for all three products and more technical info than you probably need on the [...] site. There is also detailed info for using it in hard water, on cloth diapers, for allergies, etc. Their customer service is great, and if you email a question or comment you'll get a quick response. I am hooked on these products.

title: Is there an ideal lidocaine patch out there?
text: I have pain and muscular dysfunction due to a shoulder injury that has affected my neck, in which I have a pinched nerve, and radiates down in between my scapula. Being that is a very dynamic area of movement, most lidocaine patches do not stick sufficiently to substantially relieve pain. It doesn't matter what I do, many that I've tried don't stay on or work. As far as these thin, flexible patches go, I've tried these patches and a similar product called Re-Lieved. The Re-Lieved patches work best, but the adhesive irritates my skin. I wear them during the day and have to use prescription steroid cream overnight. I always wash the area I'm applying the patch to and dry the area very well before applying the patch. These patches stick very well, maybe too well, because I have a irritated spot on my neck from wearing one today and even getting in the shower did not make them easier to remove. It was like ripping a giant band-aid off and a ton of adhesive remained stuck to my skin. I feel that I got some benefit out of the patch today, but not much more above lidocaine cream which needs to be reapplied. They do not work as well as Re-Lieved, but I did not have a reaction to the adhesive even though it was stuck to my skin. The patches are thin, light, stretchy, easy to apply, and comfortable. However, I don't think these work any better than the plain Salonpas menthol-type patches. Those smell terrible, but they stick and work. These might work for you if you don't have to worry about getting the adhesive off the middle of your back.

title: My way of taking dried Nopal.
text:
My best friend introduced me to this product and I have only been using it for a very short time. I am trying various ways to take it and find that mixing in any liquid is the hardest way for me. The best way I find to take Nopal powder is to mix a little in with a spoonful of black beans, veggies, sweet potatoes, anything soft, warm and salty. Then follow with a glass of water as dried nopal can swell up quickly. This could be why many people experience a dry, gaggy feeling when they take it without anything to help it down. Most places recommend 8oz of water. Makes sense. Outside of this Nopal is amazing and I have already noticed a slight decrease in my blood sugar....which is the main reason I am trying it. I tried tablets, but did not notice any changes. This is different and may take some experimenting to get it easier to take. Not sure it will get more palatable, but I find the soft salty warm veggies work best so far. If this is something anyone wants to try...do some research; contact local natural food stores for info; and by all means please discuss with your physician anything that is taken to replace allopathic medicines. I advocate natural anytime it will work, but that does not mean it works for everyone.
After the rambling, I am glad my friend introduced me to this powder. It smells funny and tastes funny, but it's working and that's the important part for me. Great brand. Great price. Will comment again once more time has passed.

text:
I decided to buy these ear plugs because of the variety of designs. That way I could have more than one option to fulfill my needs. When I tried the orange and blue ones, it made no difference at all. I could hear the same as having nothing blocking my ears. The green one fitted better into my ear, but the percentage of noise canceling that I perceived was about 10% effective. While using the green ones, I asked someone to speak to me in a normal tone of voice, and I was able to understand every word, just a little bit muffled. Someone outside my room was playing a game on her cell phone and, even with the ear plugs on, I could hear the sound effects of the game.
It includes 3 pairs of moldable plugs. I haven’t tried them yet, but after reading the instructions, I learned that they can only be used up to three times, because the material is sticky and can result in an ear infection if you use them more than that.
In short, I paid 11 dollars for two pairs of ear plugs that don’t work at all, a third pair that is effective 10% or less, and 3 moldable that I can only use 3 times each. I expected something that allowed me to sleep while isolating my ears from surrounding regular noise. This didn’t work.

title: Easy to use
text:
I'll admit I have a high tolerance for pain so I might not be the best judge on pain levels but I thought it was more like a pinching sensation everywgere except places with longer hair like my upper arm. My face barely hurt except when I'd hit a stray hair that was longer. It felt like I was plucking many hairs at once.

If you're used to pluckingbor waxing you can handle this. If you find those to be painful you might struggle with this.

It is a slow process but the results are worth it. The areas I've worked on are 100% smooth and the more you remove hair at the root the finer the hair grows back. Over time the hair will stop growing back. This is the true power of an epilator.

If I had to nitpick the product my only two complaints are its a slow process but thats true of all epilators. My other complaint is it comes with accesories but no storage bag. That would have been a nice touch. But it doesn't negate from the quality of the device.

I give it 5 stars. Its compact enough to take anywhere as a razor for your purse. The epilator works exactly as described and it comes with covers for both heads. An led light to make it easier to see where you're shaving. And a brush to clean the heads plus a charging cord.

I think this is a great value especially if you are looking for a way to remove your hair at the root without the mess of sugar or wax.

title: Works great for autoimmune disease!
text:
I've been using this as part of a treatment regimen for a cat with a life-threatening autoimmune disease. It's crucial to use immunomodulating supplements, as opposed to immune stimulants, when treating autoimmune conditions and reishi (fruiting body) is king in the world of immune modulating supplements. I wanted a pure, organic formula, and so far this is the only one I've found that fits the criteria. I can't understand why more medicinal mushroom formulas aren't organic. If you're taking it for immunity because you're sick, the last thing you want is to bombard your body with pesticides.

The only side-effect kitty has experienced (that I'm aware of) is an upset stomach if the dosage is too high. Cats can take 10-25 mg./1 lb. of body weight daily. I started him at the max dose (not the best idea, I know) and have had to decrease it to the minimum, which still appears to be effective. He definitely has more color and energy on the reishi. When I've stopped it for a few days due to tummy issues I've seen a decline in color and overall well-being.

He usually eats it mixed with his regular food, so the bitterness doesn't appear to bother him. He is a bit of an odd duck in that regard; I think cats generally aren't fond of bitter foods. If you wanted to try it on your own cat, you could probably disguise the flavor in something stinky like mackerel.

I'm planning to add cordyceps, another immunomodulator, to the regimen before long.

title: Buyer Beware
text: I could not feel more robbed then how I feel about this purchase. Obviously, if you need a portable shower you are probably dealing with some very difficult thing in your life. In my case, a family member recently paralyzed. The instructions for this expensive but cheaply made shower are hidden in the box with the shower hose.  We did not find these until calling to try to get it returned. Our first shower was a disaster with all four shower walls falling to the ground (my fault since we didn't have the instructions telling us to screw the PVC together). We got a good laugh out of that. The shower rings are C rings which very easily fall off of the narrow PVC pipe that forms the stall. The shower curtain came with a tear in it. The pump does not pump the water out of the base when the water is not deep enough to cover the entire hose.  Therefore, you are left with a fair amount of water in the base at the end of the process. The seller was rude and not open to allowing a return. Accused me of having "buyer's remorse." Actually, I just wanted a shower worth $729 that worked as described. The manufacturer called me and spent a lot of time trying to convince me of the incredible quality of this shower. I could probably make this myself for $200. He also told me that I could purchase closed shower rings at the Dollar Store and that the torn shower curtain was HOTEL QUALITY.  The pilot holes in the PVC so that the shower walls can be screwed together were nearly non-existent and I drilled 1/2 of them myself.  One of the corner connections broke when I was screwing the walls together but I guess that is what duct tape is for. A reputable seller or manufacturer would have taken the shower back.

He also came back with an annoying habit of wanting to go outside and use the planter boxes as his own earthy litter box. While I was quite alright with it, the boss was highly agitated at him kicking over the bricks that make up the planter and digging out the soil. I figure hey there has to be a product that will deter him from doing these shenanigans. I bought the Nature’s Mace product praying it would keep Gus(the cat) from tearing things up, and my wife (the boss) from flipping her $h1t every time it happened. So after getting the bottle(thank you amazon for fast as heck shipping) and shaking the heck out of the solution inside I went out to spray down the box. This box is aprox 3’ by 2’, and as I said made up of rough bricks. The first couple of spays had me thinking it was just a cinnamon solution, however a far worse smell was coming. Have you ever been around a realy REALLY old person, the kind with bad dentures and really bad halitosis? Ok now give that person a couple of sticks of Big Red gum and let them chew for a few, then have them exhale on you. That smell is the smell of this product. As the odor drove me from that corner of the garden I thought ‘Holy $h1t, this has to work!’ Sadly, I was very wrong. That very day Gus climbed right back into the box and wreaked havoc on the planter. Then promptly came in the house with feet that smelled like he had tromped through a crap covered cinnamon patch. In the end I ended up putting a thick layer of lava rocks over the planter soil to keep him out.

title: TERRIBLE!
text:
I have very long,, pretty thick blonde hair. It's down to my waist. For years my hair has always been so fine and wouldn't hold a curl for anything. I'm in my 50's now and have had cancer, my hair fell out and it is so thick and coarse, and the curls are ridiculous. Not that I am complaining!! But once in a while I'd like straight hair. I have flat irons, curling irons...and saw this and decided to give it a try.
When I got it my straightening brush, I was a bit surprised. It's much larger then a normal hair brush and a bit heavier then I thought it would be.
I washed my hair the night before and it was all brushed out, no kinks or tangles anywhere. I plugged in and turned on the brush, and waited a few minutes for it to heat up. Then I sectioned my hair to make it easier for me to do.
I started to use the brush, but it got stuck in my hair about 3 inches from the top. It wasn't stuck from having knots or anything, the red rubber "balls" that sit atop the brush bristles - one broke off and got stuck in my hair. Once I got the brush and ball out of my hair....I thought that would be it. I tried to put the brush through my hair one more time, and this time a huge chunk of my hair came out on the brush.
I then turned the brush off and put it back in the ox once it cooled.
That is my experience with this product. I don't think I've done anything wrong - I used it just as it says to use it. First try a red ball "protector" breaks off, and the 2nd try it took out a huge chunk of my hair. AND...my hair was FULL of static!! From just one pull of the brush through my hair.
Broke on the first try. Pulled out my hair. Gave me a bad case of static on one side of my head.
I can't return it because I've used it and it broke <and I will say I did nothing so strenuous as to make that rubber ball break off -no yanking to get the brush out of my hair!!>. But I did just waste a good chunk of my money on a product that- in my opinion - needs a LOT OF WORK.
Maybe this is better suited for short hair.
I would not purchase another one,nor would I recommend it to any of my family or friends.

title: AWESOME BUBBLES!!!
text:
I have read most of the reviews on this product and almost didn't order it. Being the person I am, I wanted to give it a try. The price is right, and it was what I was looking for. And although I do give reviews some heed, I can form my own opinion. I am SUPER HAPPY I didn't listen to the negative reviews because this Bubble Spa is AMAZING!

FIrst let me say I have a jacuzzi bathtub, but the motor blew out over a year ago. I broke my neck and back while in the Army, and have endured 44 surgeries, and I have severe Fibromyalgia and Rheumatoid Arthritis. I have a Morphine Pain Pump transplanted in my body to help with the pain. I used to take 20 minute baths every day to also help with my pain, but when the jacuzzi broke I stopped.
I wasn't looking for a new jacuzzi because we will be remodeling our bathroom in the near future and the tub will be replaced with a different jacuzzi tub. So I just wanted something with bubbles or to help the water move to help my muscles, for the time being.
Here are my finding!
THE SMELL. There was NONE! I opened my box and it had 3 wrapped parts - the mat, the motor and the hose. All shipped in separate plastic bags. None of it smelled like plastic or rubber - there really was no odor. Once I took the mat out and opened it fully - there was a slight odor, but it went away. I'm pretty sure anything made out of rubber/vinyl/plastic will always have an odor, but the odor dissipates within a few minutes. It cetainly isn't a deal breaker for me.
MAT SIZE. I have an oval jacuzzi garden tub and the bottom of the tub measures about 4.5 feet. The mat is about 5 feet. There are 6 jets in my tub, about midway up the tub wall. The walls go straight up, there's no taper. I am able to stick the suction cups either on the sides of my tub, even with the jets, or lay it on the bottom and stick it that way. Laying it flat - there is about a foot that goes up towards the top of the tub, however it's still under water.
THE MOTOR. It comes with what looks like a very small "canister vacuum" motor with a handle. It is not heavy, even I can lift it, and with my neck and back - 10 pounds is a struggle for me. When all is set and we turned it on, there is noise. after years of my LOUD jacuzzi jet noise - this thing purrs like a kitten. But remember this is a motor and will make some noise - it's just not so loud that I couldn't use it and disrupt everyone n the house. Still not a deal breaker.
HEAT IN THE TUB. I've read reviews that say the water did not get heated. I didn't read anywhere in the description where it said this would heat the water, so it must be me! I can say this.... When my jacuzzi did work, the movement in the water kept the water warmer for longer, but it never "heated" my water. I've always added super hot water to my bath and if needed, my husband would always bring a bucket of hot water from our other bathroom. You are only supposed to stay in a hot tub for 20 minutes at a time, otherwise your muscles start to "break down". My Pain Specialist doctor and my Rheumatologist told me to take baths every day to help my pain but never longer then 20 minutes. If you put hot water in your bath to start, your water should remain hot enough for 20 minutes. There is warm water coming from the hose, but air is air and it will cool off any water. I had no problems with my bath water retaining it's heat.
BUBBLE BATH, OILS, SALTS in the water. It says not to add any of these products, and I even read one review where she did add bubbles and it made too many. In my jacuzzi - if I added bubble bath - I disappeared! I did add Epsom Salt to my bath water and it was fine. I added oil - and it still worked fine. I then added bubble bath, and knowing just how many bubbles generate from my jacuzzi - I added little drops at a time. I do have a large tub, about a 50 gallon tub, I added more, and then more. I never got an amount of bubbles to make me stop. I stopped adding because I didn't want my skin to freak out! My point is I had no issues using any of the products I mentioned. And it didn't clog/ruin the mat.
THE BUBBLES!!! Since reading quite a few reviews saying this is "Crap", "Don't waste your money", etc., I was skeptical. Once in the tub, my husband had to turn it on for me as we sat the motor on the floor and I couldn't reach it. For this time I put the mat on the bottom of the tub. He first turned it on the lowest setting, it took a minute <maybe> for the air to fill the mat and the bubbles to start coming out. Then he put it on the medium setting, with more bubbles, and then the highest speed, with even more bubbles . I was actually quite surprised by not only the amount of bubbles, but the strength of them! It was WONDERFUL!!! It is almost as amazing as my jacuzzi!! I actually took a video of it working but I don't think I can upload it on here with my review. For the life of me, I can't understand how anyone would not like this! I mean, really, if you want a jacuzzi - GO BUY A JACUZZI!!! This is NOT a jacuzzi nor is it mean to act like one - it is a BUBBLE SPA! There IS a difference between "jacuzzi" and "bubble spa". Jacuzzis use Jets, Bubble Spas use Bubbles!! This product provides GREAT BUBBLES!!!
I can say - that if you "Sit" in the bathtub - you WILL block the flow of air therefore you will not get the full effect of this bubble spa! I lay down in my tub, with my legs partially drawn up and my head resting on the pillow on the end. Yes my butt does touch the mat, but not in any way close to the way it does while I am "sitting". There is a difference! Lay back in your tub, pull your legs up a bit, and you should get plenty of bubbles! The bubbles flowed up my entire body, feeling great at my neck. Of course, where my butt touched the mat - not so much bubble as the rest, but the bubble were still there. While I sat in my tub, getting everything, ready, ie; lighting candles, getting my drink where I could easily reach it, getting my oil, salts and bubble bath - my big butt blocked off the air and I only got bubbles on my legs from the knees down, and towards my back a little bit of bubbles. Once I layed back - the bubbles flowed properly. The bubbles felt so freaking good I almost fell asleep, and that does not happen to me!!!! Mymuscles haven't felt this good in a year!
I can say with all honesty - I am overweight. Since I broke my neck the 2nd time, it has been much harder to do anything like I used to, therefore I have gained weight. I am 5'8 and weigh 198 pounds, so I am not little by any means. The mat is not a hard foam but once the air flows through it it does "blow up" to be firmer. If you sit your booty on the "pads", you will not disrupt the flow of air as bad as if you "sit" on the mat, meaning the pad and the rest of the mat. It's kind of hard to explain!
Taking this apart was super easy. Turn the motor off. Drain your tub. Take the hose off the mat and don't let water get in the hose or you'll have to hang it to drain the water and dry. Take the mat out, by the suction cups or you risk ripping the mat, let it drain as much as possible in the tub - then either stick it to your shower wall or hang it over the shower door. We have tile in our bathroom so any excess water drips were easly wiped up. Put a towel underneath to protect carpet if you have it. Once it is dry you can fold it and put it away until the next time you use it. Very easy!
All in all - I am impressed and VERY happy I bought this. I would buy another one to use it in conjunction with this one and stick them to the side walls of my tub, if I wanted to get more bubbles, but it is definitely not necessary>. Definitely worth the price - and I would absolutely pay full price for it!!
I hope my review helps someone. Not everyone has the same super high expectations as the next <and yes I do believe you have un-attainable expectation if you think this sucks>! Give it a try and if you're not happy - you can always return or replace.

My original review is here :
This is one of my favorite purchases of the last couple of years. honestly. I am always traveling and it's hard to pack a standard or portable waterpic. I thought at best, this would be a good substitute while I am on the road but once I tried it--I immediatly offered my old waterpic to my husband. This thing is KILLER! the consumer video shown was really helpful, but for me a little misleading. This thing looked Giant--but in real life, I can wrap my hand around it easily and turn it on with my thumb, not finger, but you can do it however you want. The daily set up consists of flipping your "pic" of choice up, pulling the water tube down (it's rigid) and turn it on. High speed is GREAT. If you have a problem with the water not drawing either the water tube is up against the bottom--a slight design flaw, but you can control how far you pull it down, just millimeters off the bottom is fine, or you have a REALLY tight seal between the cup and the unit--just loosen it up to let some air out, and you get all the power. If it leaks, I think that's operator error, you need to get that "pic" on good and tight, but you only need to do it once. Once it's in, you just flip it up to use and flip it down when done. The cup is so handy, attaches to the bottom and holds your water via twist while in use, and when you're done, flip the pic down and the cup goes on top. viola! EASY to travel with and it actually looks great on the bathroom counter. Beautiful packaging is just a bonus. It comes with a USB cord, but not a charger, but you probably have a charger somewhere. I use it twice daily, have charged it twice and have owned it two weeks. It has not died, I just figured that a week was a good time to charge it, I can't say enough good things about this product. Flippin awesome!

title: Done searching for organic hairspray!
text: I have a completely organic regimen for getting ready in the morning (shampoo, conditioner, makeup, moisturizer, hair pomade, etc), and recently realized the ridiculous irony of finishing all that off by spraying my head (and bathroom) with stinky, chemical-laden conventional hairspray. I just couldn't find anything else that worked. I tried every type of organic and natural hairspray available at Whole Foods as well as through my organic buying club, and most of it just went on like water. In contrast, I'm delighted with this hairspray! It smells fresh, it isn't damaging my lungs or spraying carcinogens into the air, and perhaps most importantly to anyone reading this review, it really holds my style well. I have a mid-length cut that I curl into wavy ringlets, so I really need it to stay put or it just looks straggly by mid-morning. The cost is well worth it to me to avoid breathing in fumes as my head off-gasses all day from conventional "salon" sprays, and I'm easily making it through humid Midwestern summer days without my hair losing its shape or hold. It's nice that my search is over.

title: Not the same Uncle Bill's Sliver Gripper I've used for years.
text: A manufacturing step has seemingly been eliminated in the two I received. I only noticed it moments ago when I tried these new ones to extract a tiny cactus thorn from my fingertip, after watering my houseplants.  I had bought them for a birthday gift, keeping the keychain one for myself in a toolbox. It seemed to hurt more than my older Uncle Bills tweezers that were in another location. So I compared them. This new one appears identical to the older model at first glance, but there is a difference that can be seen with the unaided eye.  Each of the "arrow" points is the same metal thickness all the way down the angled tip to the points. Crude. Formerly, the "arrows" edges were filed or ground to be narrower, more knife-like, so that the tips were smaller and would go into a small skin hole more easily. These newer ones are not horrible but inferior IMO. I am returning them to Amazon. In my professional case I have a “Diane Pointed Tweezer #9184” available many places, which is far superior to even my old Uncle B tweezer for slivers and thorns. But it is twice the length with a much sharper and narrower tip; hence is not a pocket item.

title: Too Expensive. An Excellent Product. But Not Good Value Because of the Cost
text:
Here's the deal. I am a huge fan of the Soylent concept.

And one of the ways I maintain my weight and keep my weight down is by applying the philosophy of calories in calories out. And so, I have a protein meal replacement for breakfast that clocks in around 240 calories and has 39 grams of protein, 3 grams of fiber, 17 grams of carbohydrate and 3 grams of fat.

Now, let's say that one wanted to maintain a weight with a consumption of about 2,400 calories per day. As Soylent points out, although one could, one shouldn't get all of one's daily requirements from just consuming Soylent.

But if each serving of Soylent (24 servings per this cannister) is 200 calories and one were to use this product for two meals as a meal replacement, one could blow through a 24 servings container in no time at all, thus making it an expensive source for your daily protein.

So how do I really review this product?

Is it excellent? Yes.
Is it neutral tasting and not unpleasant and able to be flavored with cocoa, etc. ? Yes
If I could get it for a lower price would I use it regularly? Yes

So the only comment I have is that it is a very very expensive way to do a meal replacement. If the 2.3 lb container is set up for 24 servings of 200 calories each that means that, for a daily 2,400 calorie diet, the container would be for two days. Hence, consider it only as, say, a replacement for your breakfast meal.

title: Best Face Mask Available
text:
[UPDATED REVIEW]

We discovered a couple of shortfalls with two of the eight masks we purchased across two separate orders through Amazon.

At first we purchased four individual black adjustable masks, finding them to be light, comfortable to wear and featuring a very practical keeper strap.

After one wear and wash, however, thread on the keeper strap on one of the black masks was found to be fraying, the material bundling, and it looked like it was about to fall apart.

The white adjustables just arrived in the last day or so, and upon opening the package today we found one of the four to be missing a loop through which the keeper strap is to pass. It looks like it's just a little tab of material, and it doesn't serve any purpose. The mask is useless without it.

I reached out to the Seller to request replacements for each of these two defective items. While the response time could be better, Buttonsmith stepped it up, sending to us replacements for the masks that were not up to standard.

Things happen. A great measure is how a company or individual responds when said things happen. I'm more than pleased to share with you my experience that Buttonsmith did right by us.

I am a survivor of COVID-19, battling the disease for 36 days. There were times during the first couple of weeks in particular I thought I was going home. As a Post-COVID19 Long-hauler, I'm still battling symptoms.

It's not political. It's not about control. Do our part. Show you care. Mask up. Buy this mask. Buy plenty of these masks. And wear 'em. (We've since purchased another set of four white adjustables.)

title: iSelector 500 ml Diffusor has quality product and provides value
text:
This is my third diffuser. I was less than happy with my first two diffuser purchases. This is the first diffuser I have purchased where I believe the product provides the value I was looking for. I gave it 5 stars although it is not faultless.

PROS: Lights do not turn on immediately as with my other 2 diffusers. I do not want night lights to turn on as soon as I power up the diffuser since I primarily do not want night lights on. It is easy to turn on lights and select your color or all colors but it is a separate button (LEFT button). I find it very nice having a separate light button. The iSelector 500 ml diffuser provides a large reservoir to hold water for diffusing. Although I can't verify that the amount is actually 500 ml. However, the iSelector has lasted slightly over 24 hours at low volume when I put it almost at maximum volume. I was pleased! I can see it spraying (it is near a room light) and can usually tell the difference between low fan and high fan speeds. It makes my bedroom smell nice. It has separate button (larger CENTRAL button) for on and off and timing intervals or continuous on for diffusion which I like. Each time interval selection (i.e., 1-hr, etc.) lights up which to make it easy to choose. I almost always choose continuous interval timing but there are shorter options.

CONS To me the cons are not deal breakers but they may be a deal breaker to you so please read. The last button (RIGHT button) allows you to adjust the spray to high or low, which is a nice choice at times. However, this button is somewhat problematic as button makes spray low volume - high volume – spray off (3 choices) but there is no indication on your selection. This can be confusing especially if your diffuser is in a dark spot. It's obvious when spray is off but sometimes hard to tell difference between high and low spray volume. Some reviewers complained they had trouble telling this difference. Another issue is how the manufacturer describe the product – glass diffuser. This is not really true. The inside of the machine is all plastic although it states it is free of BPA. While it has a pretty glass cover, it goes over a plastic bottom and a plastic enclosing lid. Plastic surrounds the therapeutic oils and water. If you are looking for an all glass diffuser look further. This iSelector 500 ml diffuser is not for you. However for me iSelector is the best diffuser I have found. I am finally satisfied with this product’s quality and will now stop looking for the perfect diffuser.

title: Product Seems Soild, Great Customer Service Experience
text:
The product arrived nicely packaged in a white Aruba's Apothecary Glass box. The box has separate compartments for the more fragile items, and a larger one for the smaller/loose items. Glass seemed snug enough, and my order arrived free of damage.

One odd thing that I noticed about the water bottle heads is that, when shaken, there is an audible rattle that can be heard. Honestly, I have no idea what to think of it, and am not sure how concerned I should be about it, but so far the bottles have worked great for me anyway. The bottles have both a spray and a stream setting, which not all bottles have. I only plan to use the spray function, though, but appreciate the extra feature. The spray is being used mostly to mist some house plants, and has been excellent for that so far.

The box also came with 2 screw-on tops that could be used to turn the spray bottles into more of a storage bottle (I could see converting one with essential-oils mixed in at some point). The caps came inside of a separate compartment on the inside/edge of the box, so I definitely appreciate the care taken in packaging all of the items!

The box comes with a nice instructions/inventory/thank-you letter too, which is where my customer service experience came into play. The list mentioned several items, including: 2 bottles, 2 lids, sticker labels, and a bonus roller bottle. I then noticed that the last 2 items were missing from my box: the marker for use with the labels and the funnel.

I promptly reported this omission to their customer service, per the letter, and received a response the next morning. The customer service rep was great, and assured me that the missing items would be shipped to me promptly. Sure enough, one week later I received the 2 missing items. This was excellent customer service, and makes me feel confident about keeping the product given their response to the issue I had.

So far, everything else has been working excellently! The bottles themselves look great, and the glass definitely feels like a step up from plastic bottles I've owned in the past!

title: One of the better protein shakes
text:
I'm having bariatric surgery, so I've had to try a lot of protein powders/shakes and I will say this one is among the best.

I mixed a whole scoop in my Blender Bottle (which is a must have in my opinion) with 8oz of plain cool water. It mixed well and easily. It did foam some, but if you let it sit for a minute it's fine. I followed another review and didn't add ice until after I mixed and it worked well.
It's a bit tart and has a definite strawberry and kiwi flavor. It's not thicker like a lot of protein drinks, so it goes down easily. The only real negative to me is the protein taste. It's less than most other shakes/drinks, but it's still there. I will say that it's much better chilled. I took a couple of sips before I added the ice and the protein taste was much more prominent.

I recommend this to anyone who is tired of the boring chocolate and vanilla. It's a refreshing alternative!

text:

If you're looking for odor elimination, this isn't a good choice.

This pillow was a disappointment to me, but it may work out okay for my husband, who is larger and has broader shoulders than I. I tried it for two nights and both times ended up swapping it out in the middle of the night, unable to sleep comfortable on it.

To be honest, I already have one of these pillows and have used it (and loved it) for years and bought this one for a second location. My original was a hand-me-down and had no tags on it, so I cannot be certain it was exactly the same manufacturer, but it looks the same (and I've not found others on the market) and the length and width are exactly the same.

Why this one falls short:

1. While the length and width are what I expected, the height is much greater; the original being a little less than 4" and the new one being more like 6". The additional height on this one bends my neck out of the proper resting position.

2. Both the bolster (tube) and the pillow are stuffed so full of filling that they are very hard. In my original, the bolster is firm and the pillow is soft. In this one the bolster and pillow are both very firm. I really do not detect the difference in firmness between bolster and pillow that is described in the listing.

3. It does not fit in a pillow case, not even a king-sized case. My original easily fits a king-sized case. This one can be crammed into one, but doing so completely defeats the purpose of the bolster/pillow design. I have temporarily pinned a towel around it and will make a custom pillow case to fit if it turns out my husband likes it.

I thought about washing it to see if that would soften it up, but it has no laundering instructions. I looked to see if there are special cases for it and found none. I also looked around to see if the pillow comes in different sizes but found no alternatives. I wish they made a smaller one.

In fairness to the company, I did not complain or try to return it, or test their "satisfaction guaranteed" promise. I did not pay much for it and it so far it is working okay for my husband. There are no quality problems, it is just that the design is poorly executed for a smaller person.

title: Ok but I found a different option for me
text:
The concept is great but for me they are too visually and physically distracting. When you put them on, it is apparent they make a difference and they are soft behind the ears. But, for me, it is just one extra step that I don't like; you have to size each one around the ear; in other words, you can't just slip your glasses on. The same process when you take them off. And for me, after I take my glasses off and put them on the desk, I have to look at them with the forms on them, and I have the subliminal image that I have to go through the process again.

So, I have stopped using them and have gone to a new solution. I went to the local hardware store bought various sizes of very thin rubber washers in black. Not the big thick ones, but thinnest I could find in various ring sizes (.15-.75 cent each) because I was not sure of what would work. I then twisted the washers like rubber bands (which I suppose you can use) around the tip of my frames, experimenting one side to the other until I got a fit that worked comfortably behind each ear and voila-no extra step and no distracting visuals. When I put my glasses on, they sit just great, occasionally I have to make adjustment when putting them on, but it is a matter of a slight pushing the rubber back or forward.

title: Comparable To Ensure With Slight Differences
text:
I drink Ensure very regularly because I have chronic pain and some days it is just too difficult to eat, so I drink to get my nutrients. I wanted to try this as an alternative and there are both positives and negatives compared to Ensure.

Pros:
* It is significantly more watery. Ensure is very thick and very hard to swallow. This is essentially like milk, which makes it go down easy
* It tastes less sweet. Ensure is very sweet compared to this.

Cons:
* Ensure tastes better, though the flavors are very similar. Perhaps because this is more watery and has less sugar, it dilutes the taste which makes it taste slightly worse than Ensure.

I'm pretty sure no one likes drinking these nutrient drinks. I try to gulp them down in one go. So for me, this is easier than ensure just due to the thickness. But if you sip on it, then maybe Ensure may be up your ally if you prefer a sweeter, tasier alternative.

title: awkward layout of buttons for the way I use hair dryers
text:
[[VIDEOID:3c7f3f1d5fde35bb98555c8703900a2c]] This is a beautifully designed hair dryer. The layout of the buttons are a little different from your usual hair dryers. For speed and heat, you can adjust it on the back of the "head" portion. For on/off and a shot of cool air, it will be where the handle is. The way I dry my hair is I go back and forth with both the heat and speed depending on how dry my hair is getting, so if I'm using the dryer I would have to briefly stop, bring it down to my eye level view, press the buttons, and continue. Although this does a great job of drying my hair, it just isn't as smooth for me in that sense. My fingers can't reach those buttons when I'm holding on to the handle.

I also found the sound to be quite loud. I'm not saying it is any louder than other hair dyers but probably about the same. It says 60 decibel and I don't know what my other hair dryers are on the noise level but it doesn't feel like it is any less loud.

I really like the magnetic nozzles that just snap onto the head. You can also turn it around if you want the wind to go a certain direction on your hair. I like the variety of nozzles they provided, which you usually don't get with other cheaper hair dryers.

What makes this hair dyer special is the negative ions/lava nutrients but I didn't notice much, if any, difference on my hair. I have long hair, quite dry and sometimes frizzy from damage of hair dyes, so I don't think any special technology will do much to fit it. If you have good condition hair, perhaps you'll get a more noticeable difference. Mine is too tangled up on a daily basis to notice.

Make sure to remove all the sticker that was protecting the machine prior to use. There was one I forgot to take off, which seemed to be blocking the air so the machine was making an extra loud muffled noise. Make sure to check the entire machine to ensure you removed the packaging, which can be dangerous especially when the machine/wind starts getting hot.

Overall this is a beautiful hair dryer with a cool, modern design. I do like it but it isn't the hands down favorite one for me. If you don't mind about the layout of the buttons perhaps this will be an excellent choice for you.

title: Very “clean” product but my face needs more scrubbing
text:
This cocoa face scrub has a very short list of ingredients, which shows how “clean” this stuff is. I didn’t see it posted on this Amazon page so I had to do some extra research and this is what I found.

Ingredients: Glycerin, Theobroma Cacao (Cocoa) Extract*, Tocopherol *Organic Ingredient

Short and sweet!

While I do love the ingredients, I found it to have a little too paste like consistency and not enough grit. I prefer a rougher scrub with more “stuff”, like ground up nuts or something that will at least scrub the built up gunk from my face. There were some but it wasn’t much. I kept squeezing more paste onto my hands so I could get more grit, and probably ended up using more than I needed, which is a little wasteful. I don’t dislike the results though as my face felt clean, soft, and moisturized afterwards. It smells like cocoa, a light scent, not at all overwhelming.

title: melt in your mouth strips, no peeling off afterwards
text:
These are different from the whitening strips I used to get (the popular brand in drugstores and everywhere) because you just stick these on and let it melt in your mouth. There is no peeling anything off after the 15 minutes, which seems to be a better concept than the ones where you have to peel off afterwards. The strips are thin and tiny, should most likely fit the row of teeth. There is no folding or tucking required, no bulky feeling. Once you stick these on, your mouth will feel a dry and the inside of the mouth will be stuck to the strips. I didn't want to move my mouth too much as the strips are working so that made my mouth feel even drier. I'm only on day 2 of these strips and although the instructions say to use twice a day, I am only doing it once a day because I'm worried about teeth sensitivity. After the 15 minutes was up I did rinse my mouth with tap water, and the water did make my teeth feel a little sensitive. It felt fine afterwards. I think these strips are great and I can't wait to see the results at the end of 4 weeks. If used twice a day, the instructions say you'll see it whiten to 7 shades in two weeks. There are 56 strips per box. The expiration date is printed on every foil packet (all 56 packets).

My only improvement feedback for this product is they could have packaged two strips in each foil packet instead of one, just to cut down on the waste. I have to say Moon's outer box and the individual strip packaging already seem to use much less material than the big name brands but it'll be even better if they put two strips per package, as most people are going to whiten their top and bottom teeth together anyway.

At first I did not like this shaving brush. All my life had used imitation or boar bristle shaving brushes, and along comes this limp thing that honestly felt like a miniature mop. I was not impressed, at first.

Then I dug into the history and types of shaving brushes, and oddly the badger bristles are considered a premium brush. To me it looked like something a woman would use to put make-up on.

So I gave Professor Fuzzworthy's shaving brush a few more days. After its initial use it seemed to stiffen up a bit more, but not a lot. And have found that lathering up with William's shaving soap takes a bit more effort, yet my face feels worlds better using this brush in comparison to a boar bristle. One can pamper their face with this.

Final verdict, it is a fabulous shaving brush. This Huon Pine seems stout enough and fits well into my large hands quite well.

Lagarostrobos franklinii is a species of conifer native to the wet southwestern corner of Tasmania, Australia. The timber has a very high oil content, methyl eugenol to be precise, which renders it impervious to insects, waterproof, and imbues it with its characteristic sappy perfume.
Huon pine timber is highly sought after by crafts people. It's easy to turn and carve due to its elastic qualities, and rarely splits. It has a unique aroma, and some of the trees in Tasmania's wilderness are up to 1000 years old.

One can see why so much emphasis is placed on the wood of this outstanding shaving brush. I shall cherish this Professor Fuzzworthy's Luxury Huon Pine Premium Shaving Brush for the rest of my years.

But it DOES make me better able to cope with stress without it impacting my physical health, and it also improves my mood by default a bit so it's easier to fend off depression and overworrying.

I get serotonin syndrome easily from antidepressants and get my serotonin supply burned all up, so that's why I take 5HTP instead (with my psychiatrist's approval). Instead of trying to limit the reuptake (e.g.) recycling of the body's serotonin to trick it into making more, 5HTP supports the actual production of serotonin. Because of this, it should NEVER be combined with prescription antidepressants - the combination is almost guaranteed to create serotonin syndrome. However, for someone whose brain still doesn't increase serotonin production with an antidepressant limiting its reuptake, 5HTP can be a literal lifesaving alternative. Chances are high in these cases that your brain needs help with MAKING serotonin in the first place; not just with regulating it.

title: Treatment in the privacy of your own home
text:
The Babonir IPL Hair Removal device is sleek and solid and easy to use. I have been using it for a few weeks and believe that I am starting to see a difference in my treated hair follicles, with the hair growing back finer and less quickly (I will edit my review in the future if I find that it is actually not effective and I am just imagining it - I have had the device a while now, so wanted to share my initial thoughts rather than waiting for the whole recommended regimen which will take quite some time because you have to wait for repeat phases of follicular growth cycles). The various sized heads allow for better control over where you are directing the light pulses, making it easy to treat smaller and larger areas, although larger areas such as the legs require some patience and time to fully treat. Luckily the lamp lasts for a very high number of flashes. I have fair skin and darker body hair even though I am a ginger on my head, so I am the ideal candidate; some darker skin tones are contraindicated for safety and comfort and those with red body hair will find it ineffective, per the manufacturer information.

I do feel a mild sting and will smell a burnt hair smell, particularly if I hit an area where I did not shave down the hair before use, but I do do not find it to burn or really hurt. Sometimes after use I will feel a residual warmth for a few hours in the treatment areas, less than a very minor sunburn, but I am using the device on the very highest level. It is not painful, I can just feel a minor irritation. Only a few times have I experienced any redness and it was very mild and did not require any treatment to make it subside. I find that the device can be a little finicky when using the manual mode, because I like to move fast so I am probably not aligning it as carefully as it would like (not a bad thing for safety really) so I turn it to auto and it will pulse as soon as I have it moved to the next spot (tip: pick it up slightly and place it down at the next spot so it knows you have moved it and it will pulse faster).

I have found this to be a well crafted device, which is much more convenient, comfortable and cost effective than treatments by a professional. Because it is an at-home treatment and they want it to be safe, you have to have reasonable expectations as to how quickly it will work. So far, so good!

title: Very, very Mini but very functional.
text: I bought these as part of my "gear up for potential hurricanes and be prepared for all disasters" Then the box arrived and I looked at it and thought, "hmm I wonder what this box is" because I couldn't figure out what could be in a box that small.  As it turns out, THREE, yes THREE lanterns.  So they turned out to be a little bit smaller than I had expected.  Now this is entirely my fault as the dimensions are listed in the product description.  It does say mini, I just didn't expect them to be quite SO mini.  As for functionality, they work just fine.  The light is very bright and no complaints about battery life.  I was without power for 24 hours and the battery lasted the entire time (so I can't say how long the whole battery life is because the battery did not run out while I had them.) They're light (I mean this is the light-weight sense this time as opposed to the light vs. dark sense.) easy to carry around since they're small and really since they are small they are easy to store.  The only negative with them being small is the way the light is dispersed, with a bigger lantern you'd have more vertical area that would be dispersing light in 360 degrees whereas with this lantern it's a very narrow band that because it's so small.

The key is the small silver particles being suspended in the liquid, for proper absorption in your body, when taken.

The same thing will happen to Colloidal Silver if it freezes. It will turn clear and will appear a little cloudy at the bottom. When that happens.... the bottle is Ruined! This MediSIVER may be less costly, but it has never happened to the 10 or so bottles of MesoSilver 20 ppm Colloidal Silver, 500 mL, which I have taken. I have chronic Candida and Colloidal Silver seems to be the best treatment for it. I have become resistant to many of the other products and treatments for Candida.

There are other good quality Colloidal Silver products out there, just be careful and do not buy it if the bottle is tinted as it is most likely and impostor (Silver Ions). Also, do not attempt to make it at home with an Ion Generator. That is also Silver Ions, and is not nearly as effective.

title: Best Earplugs I've Found
text:
I was not, and will not, be compensated for this review! These earplugs are the best I've found. I use them while I'm sleeping because the people upstairs are loud and the floors offer very little noise reduction. I have also used them while shooting at the range. In both cases, they work much better than a similar 3M earplug. These ones are much softer and keep their shape longer, while offering similar or slightly better noise reduction. The foam expanding ones are stupid and take forever to expand to fit your ear canal. These you just slide in, and they have a piece that extends out of your ear to make them easy to pull out. The part sticking out of my ear does not affect or annoy me when sleeping on my side.

For any reviewers complaining that these don't completely eliminate noise... you do not understand the purpose of earplugs. They are decibel rated and reduce noise by that level of decibel. Most earplugs are rated between 20-32dbs. These earplugs are rated at 32dbs, which means sounds will sound about 10-15 times quieter than without them (each 6-10dbs sound twice as loud to your brain... it's different when measured by equipment but numerous studies show the human brain perceives every 6-10dbs as twice as loud, look it up). The only way to get true noise cancellation is via very expensive electronic noise cancellation headphones.

Also, for anyone with slightly larger ear canals, these work fine! Mine are larger than most and I've bought some similarly shaped earplugs that wouldn't even touch my ear canal if held right in the center of my ear. They aren't gigantic, but if you have to use the large set of pads that come with earbuds, these will fit you just fine. They are also tapered, so they can fit smaller ears as well... my daughter can use them without any problem and she has to use the small pads that come with earbuds.
