title: My Procedure to Avoid Getting Occasional Stings
text:
1) Fill case to line with disinfectant.
2) Let carrier soak in solution to wet carrier and get reaction started while doing next steps...
3) Take out both contacts and put them in one palm. Bare with me.
4) Rinse both contacts with disinfectant. This ensures that the eye-side of the lens is well-coated with disinfectant.
5) Place contacts in carrying case and squirt some more disinfectant on them for a few seconds. This is actually in their instructions.
6) Let soak for at least 6 hours.
7) Remove holder. As a final safety check, put your finger nail in the remaining solution. If the tissue around your nail turns white, then soak the lenses in normal saline (e.g., B&L Bio True) for 15 minutes. This should be rare. Otherwise, rinse lenses in holder for 5 seconds with normal saline.
8) Remove a lens, rinse eye side of lens in palm with more saline, and place in eye. Repeat for other lens.

This is not fool-proof, but does seem to help.

They weigh almost nothing and have no frames, so no dark rims to your field of vision. Perfectly clear lenses (once you realize you need to take the little static-sticky plastic protectors off, derp) and hold on well enough to lean all the way forward or upside down.

title: Yes. IT DOES WORK - Just be sure you understand it
text:
I own this product and have done my own tests. Yes, your car does get hotter if it's parked in the sun. You have a lot of window surface area, so you have a lot of solar heat. Not to mention, the frame of your car absorbs heat as does the dark dashboard. What do you expect a little solar fan to do?

In my tests, I placed a thermometer/hygrometer in my car in a shaded area (the thermometer -- not the car) at about mid-level. I did this test over several days to compare the results and to account for cloud cover, etc. On a typical hot, southern summer day, my car was getting to over 138 degrees. I do not know how much higher than 138 it gets because my thermometer starts flashing 138 when it gets over 138 and doesn't climb any higher. (Side note: When I had this same thermometer in my car in the summer in Arizona, the outside temperature was 112 degrees. This same thermometer not only flashed at 138, but the liquid crystals in the display turned the screen completely black until the thermometer cooled down some! -- That's HOT!)

Again, I had the same results for several summer days. I then used one of these solar fans on the side where the afternoon sun was shining. At the same time of day where my car would have been 138+ inside, I read 108. I did this for a few days to compare the results. Some days it was about 110 inside, one day 105.

My conclusion is that the fan is working. Lowering my inside temperatures down by 30+ degrees allows the A/C to cool my car's cabin down faster.

I have been using this product for a few years now. I use two. One on each side of the car to catch the pre-afternoon sun (eastern sun) and the afternoon sun (western sun for when I'm leaving work.)

Something that is also effective is using a windshield sun guard. You know the one, where you unfold it and it has a shiny surface that you put behind your rear view mirror and on your dashboard.

Ideally, it would be nice to have a thin film solar panel on the roof of my car that can power the car's internal blower without draining the battery. This would solve the problem of having to remember to put this little fan in the window along with the rubber 'weather stripping.'

I recommend this if you can't park in the shade. Be warned too that if it stars raining heavily, even with the rubber strip in your window, you can get some water in your car.

title: Works best on hard floors--not enough oomph for carpet.
text:
Let me start by saying--skip the smart phone app. Mine crashed every 30 seconds (or less). This comes with a remote and that should be all you need.

I've never gotten one of these autonomous vacuum cleaners because I've always been a bit skeptical about how well they would actually clean the room. The Hoover Quest 700 is my first one and I think my suspicions have been confirmed. Oh, sure--it picks up dirt and crumbs and things, but it just doesn't do nearly as good of a job as our upright, manual vacuum (also a Hoover, in case you wanted to know). The upright will fill up its canister on carpets that don't even look all that dirty in 10 minutes of vacuuming. This Quest 700 scuttled around the floor for about that long and got some stuff, but compared to the upright, it was laughably little. I also watched as it did its thing and noticed that it sometimes missed debris. There was some paper (the shreds that are left after tearing a page out of a spiral notebook) on the floor that it passed over a few times before it finally got it all up. Note that I even picked up with it missed and put it directly in its path and it still only got it about 75% of the time. The upright would have gotten it in 1 swoop, no sweat.

That's carpet. It seemed to do pretty well on hard floors where it didn't have to work against all the carpet fibers. I think that's where it got most of the stuff I emptied from its waste bin. Oh, yeah--getting to and emptying its waste bin was more difficult that I would have expected.

Yup--for carpets, I'd call this a toy. It's something to keep the kids busy and happy while also picking up a few spare crumbs here and there. When you really want to get the carpet clean, though, you will need some bigger guns. As noted above, I've never tried a Roomba or other similar device, but I suspect I'd feel the same about it as well. If your goal is to pick up cat hair from a wood floor, however, I'm sure this would do the trick quite nicely.

On the plus side, it is very quiet (aside from all the beeping that came as a result of connecting and disconnecting from my phone). The "Spot clean" function seemed to do the best job of really getting a particular area clean. Just watching it do its thing naturally, I couldn't help but notice that it passed over the same few spots several times before ever getting other spots the first time.

title: Great gloves as long as you aren't using them for heavy-duty tasks; great for aquarium use
text:
These are great gloves. I recommend them to others as long as you're using the right gloves for the right task.

These are not heavy-duty gloves. They look fairly flimsy, and they are. If you're doing a lot of pulling or heavy lifting, you're going to rip these. For lunchroom use and other light tasks, these would be great. The material on these reminds me of really thin, office-style trash bags (not the stretchy kind but the plain, clear plastic kind).

I use mine in a reef tank aquarium on top of smaller neoprene gloves. It keeps my arms dry when I'm reaching down into the tank, and I have the neoprene gloves too in case I accidentally grab something sharp. They work well for that task. I've used a dozen or so and have not had any leaks. However, I wouldn't try to move live rocks in my tank with these—they'd probably rip for that. But, the benefit of not having heavier-duty gloves is that you don't lose much precision or feeling because these gloves aren't really thick, so I can still tell which part of the coral (stone base or soft polyp, etc.) I'm picking up.

For lighter tasks, these are great glove that I recommend to others.

title: The food tastes, smells and looks foul...
text:
I signed up for Nutrisystem's program over a year ago on a whim... They had a 40% off with 3-months automatic delivery deal. The worst mistake I've ever made. I was 127 lbs, hoping to lose 10 pounds or so and I thought this will save me time (no cooking required) and will help me achieve that goal in 3 months. A year later the food is still collecting dust in my pantry. :( Quite frankly Nutrisystem achieved what I thought was impossible: they produced a variety of dishes that are equally offensive to all your senses at once: your sense of smell, sight and your taste.

I have to say that their breakfast items and snacks are okay... Nothing tastes particularly good, but they are edible... Some of the muffins, scones, etc were very dry so I had to soak them in milk. Yes, that added calories to my "meals", but at least I could swallow the food. I ate all 3 months' worth of breakfasts and snacks without much of an issue. My deal also included their shakes, which were okay, but nothing great, so I still have some of those.

The real issue was with the lunch and dinner items. Aside from the portions, which were laughably small (and this is coming from someone who is not obese, just needed to lose a few pounds... I just can't imagine anyone 200 pounds or above not passing out from a "lunch" that consists of a tiny can of soup (120 calories and literally 6 spoonfuls...), there is also the issue of taste. NutriSystem lunches were either salty or tasteless. There was hardly any other taste. But generally the lunch items were still less offensive than the dinner "dishes."

I have to admit I was only able to try 6 of their dinner dishes, and I could not finish any of them. Let me share one experience that might stay with me for the rest of my life. On day 3 of my diet I had already substituted 2 meals with other food because I simply couldn't eat what the "chefs" at NutriSystem had planned for me... After a long day at work I got home and unpacked my dinner for the day: Chicken and Dumplings. How bad could it be, right? Well... Brace yourself. I cracked open the vacuum seal to let the meal breathe in the microwave when a strong smell hit my nose. It was absolutely rancid. I was afraid to look at it. I warmed my "chicken and duplings" for a minute and then took the mystery package out of the microwave. As I opened the lid fully, I saw a brown stew with runny liquid on top of it. The smell intensified. I was scared to taste it at this point but my hunger got the best of me... Big mistake! I will not elaborate on the combination of sensations that hit me when I bit into the hard dumplings, sprinkled with overcooked chicken shreds floating in a light brown liquid of unidentifiable origin... Suffice it to say that I had to flush it down the toilet and somehow it looked better and more fitting in the toilet bowl than on my dinner plate. It was among the top 3 worst things I've ever tasted in my life...

It is hard to imagine that anyone could stick to this diet, though if one had the willpower to empty their fridge, their pantry and all other food storage areas and kept nothing but NutriSystem at home, I am sure he or she would lose weight. But starvation is not a good idea and one would need to starve because eating this putrid junk is probably not an option. Don't get me wrong, I understand that diet food is not necessarily gourmet food, but I have eaten pretty much every dish available from Lean Cuisine and 90% of them tasted good! So my expectation for NutriSystem was similar... And I was extremely disappointed. I've never in my life had food that tasted as revolting.

Please skip their food, your stomach (and your eyes and nose) will thank you for it... If you are looking for diet food that actually tastes good, I recommend buying a bunch of things from the store in advance and creating your own diet plan with food that actually tastes good. Special K cereal for breakfast, Lean Cuisine for lunch and dinner, and a piece of fruit or some trail mix as a snack will contain about the same amount of calories that most prepackaged meals do but the taste will be many times better. The price will also be similar. Good luck.

title: Comparison
text:
TrueNutrition has two versions of their EAAs and I've tried both. One costs about 40% more and is "instantized". This means it should mix better and possibly be digested more quickly. I'm not sure on the digestion part but the mixing seems only slightly better than this non-instantized version. I use a very small battery powered blender with a wish to mix approx 10g with 6oz of lemonade. If you can, I'd advise making your own lemonade using stevia but regular lemonade with sugar should be fine.
Take this on an empty stomach. Do NOT mix it with fats or proteins, carbs or OK but I'd keep them simple. If you mix this with fats or proteins you will screw up the absorption and it probably is going to waste. Make sure to give about 30 min after taking this before consuming any proteins or fats.
If you want some good info on EAAs Google Ben Greenfield Fitness Amino Acids. There's a good podcast there with a Doctor/Ironman who explains all you need to know.
I will continue buying these EAAs from TrueNutrition. I'm going to order my 3rd package now but will probably order and regular and instantized together to get a better comparison.

title: Q&A about this product
text:
Question and Answer time!
Q: Does this have all of the essential amino acids and in the proper ratio?
A: This has EIGHT essential amino acids (arguably the most important for muscle retention) and according to TrueNutrition's website it is the "perfect ratio".

Q: It says 10g per serving, do I need to buy a gram scale to use this properly?
A: Nope! It comes with a scoop (may take some digging to find it) BUT the scoop should not be measured to the top. There is a small but very visible ring a few mm below the top that you should aim to a fill for. If you fill to the top you will be close to 13.5g (I did buy a scale when I purchased this and have now verified the weight)

Q: Does it really taste that bad and how do I hide the taste?
A: It really does taste... not good. The best way to hide the taste is with quality not overly-sweetened lemonade preferably without artificial sweeteners or HFCS. Do NOT take this with any drink containing fats or protein (see next question for details).

Q: When is the best time to take this?
A: This part is very important. You should take this no sooner than 4 hours after a meal with protein or fats. You should also not eat any fats or proteins for up to 30 minutes after consuming these EAAs. Doing this ensures proper absorption by the digestive system. I take mine in the morning before working out, again right before lunch, and again before dinner.

Q: Have you noticed any differences while taking this?
A: I've only been taking for a week or so and I immediately noticed I had significantly more energy and was able to push more during my workout. I've also noticed my hunger being decreased quite a bit. Before taking these, if I didn't eat something within about a 4 hour period I would start to get shakey and jittery like I had low blood sugar (I've been tested and not in the hypoglycemic range). Since taking these EAAs I haven't had that happen once.

If you are not used to this type of machine, I would definitely say work up to the strongest modes. Personally, I like to star on the first mode at the lowest setting. After a few minutes I switch it to the next mode on the lowest setting, then after a few more – the next mode. Then I circle back to the first mode but put it on level 2 – and then I do the same for the next two modes. Circling back once again, I do each for a few minutes at the highest intensity. When I remove my hands – the dots are present in my skin – but my hands feel great. Working up is the way to go. I really do like using this machine.

title: Works but not designed for ease of use
text:
The first thing that sets this apart from other similar devices is that it comes with a “cover”. It says it is for sweat and stuff. OK – I guess. It is sort of a pain to put on and looks weird as it attaches to the front of the device with velcro but wraps the entire inside. I prefer t sue it without the cover as any type of movement at all – even maybe breathing – you can hear the velcro on the cover make noise. It is so weird. No cover – it is silent. I guess it would have been better if it were black but the directions say it was designed to transmit the light through. I just skip it.

The power bank plug comes disassembled which is a little odd. At first I thought it was one f those plugs that rotated in the socket so that is why. But nope – it doesn’t rotate. I think the only reason it comes in two pieces is so it fits in the box – and that is weird. It does fit – but weird. There is no direction about putting it together – but it is not rocket science. But no mention in the directions.

The belt itself seems to work fine in regards to red light therapy – it is just not the easiest to operate and use for a few reasons. First, the power button is in the middle of the buttons – and I am dumbfounded at that. All the buttons are close together and look the same. And actually, they are not buttons at all. It is hard to see what you are pressing and hard to see what setting it is on. All of the lights for the buttons are also colored the same – except for the time which is blue. You can barely read the words on the “buttons” as the print is teeny. Lastly – unless you are going to use this thing like on your abdomen or your upper front, though – the button placement is not great. Maybe if you are a teeny tiny petite person and you wrap it around your waist – the buttons may fall at the front if you are treating your back. For me – they are at my side when treating my back. It is weird that they are at my side and I can not see what the heck I am doing. You can’t really feel your way either. I, instead turn the thing on on my abdomen and then have to swing it around to my back. Plus, since the buttons are not really buttons and are easy to change inadvertently – you can mistakenly turn it off or change the setting easily while using.

This thing would have been MUCH better with a remote attached to the cord like most others – or even an actual remote. It does come with a detachable battery pouch and a USB cord so I guess you could hook it up to a battery pack and use it that way which is good. I just plug it in for the wall as I am not going to walk around with it personally and I use it when I’m relaxing - like sitting on the couch. It fits me just fine and will fit bigger people – although it is not that big.

So, it’s fine – it is just odd to use. I have used others that were much easier to use.

title: Pretty versatile where you can use it
text:
This pad is smaller than maybe some other ones but the size makes it much more versatile in where you can use it on your body. It is neat that it has a detachable pouch for a battery if you want to go that route. You can plug directly into the wall but you have to use a USB plug slot. Or you can attach the battery pack and attach the little cord (there is a little baby USB cord too) to a power bank and then you have a portable belt. It also comes with two belts too – a wide belt and a thinner one. So, this thing will fit almost anyone – and almost anywhere. Use one belt – or use both for a lot of length. It is completely flexible as well.

There are two buttons. On is power on/off. The other changes the setting. The button on the belt changes color with each setting – Blue, White, Green, and Red. To me, the settings mean this blue is heat only, white is a red light, green is a lighter red light, and red is a very bright red light (I never look at the light – but peeked at the glow emitted on my body). Now according to the actual instructions, it says the red color is red light, the blue color is near infrared, the white color is red light & near infrared, and the green color is red light & near infrared & 73 hz pulse. If there is a frequency, I am unable to hear or feel it
So, it must be working deep inside.

Either way it feels pretty good – all settings feel warm on the body and some I feel more than others – almost like an odd feeling – maybe a tingling or the ever so slightest stinging – but not really. So, I guess it depends on how sensitive you are to the red light for how you will feel. It does seem to help me overall with my pain. I guess that means the light is working but other than that I don’t really have a sensitivity that I know of anyway.

title: So far, so good - on inflamed skin and issues with tendon
text:
I am not yet sure of the claims and the effectiveness but I have been told about infrared-light therapy in the past – especially for pain. I have issues with my ankles and tendons and have torn my achilles tendon in the past. I still have pain most of the time so thought I would give this a try. I never heard of the red-light therapy for skin issues but am still fighting an allergic reaction on my hands to something I used in home repairs more than a month ago – so wanted to try it there as well.

The instructions say to use the light one to three inches from the surface of your skin as otherwise you may burn your skin. I do not think the head of this things where the light is emitted gets that hot. It gets warm. So, I did not get any burns even when I put it directly against skin. Although I did not hold it in one particular place but rather moved it around slightly. The body of the flashlight gets hot though – well not hot per se, but more very warm – much warmer than the head at least – I should say that is where I felt all the heat.

For my ankle – it didn’t make it feel any worse and after using it at night I felt no pain in my ankle. My pain is not constant, though anyway. I tried it on my left hand as well – where the prickly skin is from my allergic reaction. Upon waking the next day, my left hand looked better – less red – than my right hand. But to be honest, my right hand is my dominate hand – so it might have been worse off to start with. Suffice it to say, I am going to continue to use this device on my ankle tendons and on one hand to truly see if I get relief – and long-term relief at that. So far, so good.

title: Works pretty OK - heavy and could be angled better
text:
This bath brush seems plenty long enough to reach different parts of your back. But it is heavy at the head – like quite a bit. It is fine if you are doing a straight over head/shoulders reach back as the weight will help you reach your back. But in trying to come from the sides or the lower back upwards for all the parts of the back totally – your wrist will REALLLY feel the weight – especially coming in from the sides. So certain angles are uncomfortable. Plus - the angle of the handle and/or the head - does not allow it to fully rest on your back - only maybe half the brush makes contact... The silicone ones are the worst at making contact due to the angle - the two brushes work better there.

You get 5 different brush heads. The three silicone ones attach to their own plastic disks which then attach to the machine. The heads sort of lay on top of the disk and do not really attach that securely. They seem to stay on fine while using but when trying to place the head the silicone cover comes off VERY easy where you still need to remove the plastic disk. As for the actual bristled ones - one is super soft – like a make-up brush – and the other is super firm – feel like I am cleaning my car a bit. The firm one I can not imagine using all over or for very long as I am pretty sure it is taking skin off (hopefully only dead skin) very easily – even on my legs it felt a bit uncomfortable. The soft one seems super soft and doesn’t really scrub at all – just kind of lathers you up – almost like being tickled by feathers. I do wish that there was another one or two brushes that feel between the super soft and super firm – as that would be nicer.

It is also tricky getting the entire head off of the handle – it doesn’t twist or unscrew – but rather “pops” off. It felt like I was going to break it with the force I had to use – but it did come out. Once in the hand, though – it is not very easy to hold easily – it is large and there is only a small lip that helps you keep a grip. Not the best thing to use without the handle. Also – it is very heavy. I think I will leave it attached to the handle always.

I take turmeric every day as it helps with pain management as well as inflammation. These days if there is anyone that does not think they have any inflammation at all – take turmeric for a while and you will notice the difference. With ashwagandha, I notice that I am calmer – like things upset me less and I am easier to let things go and not dwell on them. Ashwagandha also lowers the rate of my heart by anywhere from 4 to 8 – which is good. I do not have a high pulse but the slight yet consistent lowering puts me more into athletic territory.

If you have any mental illness avoid ashwagandha as there have been extreme side effects with certain meds. Also avoid if you have MS or lupus or a thyroid condition. Again, ashwagandha reacts with a lot of meds or can exacerbate certain conditions. Remember – just because something is “natural” does not mean it is for everyone.

title: What Space Saving Engineering! - Really love this mop set!
text:
I love products that are super functional yet engineered really well too - especially when it comes to the space saving aspect of something you want to stow away in a closet or cabinet. This definitely fits the bill across the board.

First it comes in a small box - just large enough for the bucket. But the mop is also inside the bucket. Genius!
Now when I unpacked it I was like will this mop be sturdy enough as it comes in pieces you screw together. But YES - it totally is - and I was surprised! It was sturdy and stable and yet maneuvered very, very well as it swivels beautifully. In fact, even though my older mop is smaller - this one was much better for getting behind the toilet - again because it swivels and moves so well. It did a great job. The parts of the handle never came apart - until I took them apart (which was also easy). It is also much longer than my old mop which, for me as a tall woman, makes life sooooo much easier! In fact at the end of mopping my bathroom I was able to stand outside the door and finish up and was actually able to stretch and reach almost the entire bathroom from the doorway - I was impressed. It was very easy to use. I was even able to really scrub with it and it was still very sturdy.

The best part is the bucket. It is super tiny yet super functional. It is also much better than using my bathroom sink - as now I can properly dispose of dirty water right down the toilet. Plus it does not take that much water to fill that part of the bucket - again the engineering is super helpful and thoughtful and conserving. The mop definitely got up the dirt and I was able to rinse it well and then run it through the dry side a few times where it really did get rid of most of the water - you could see it literally pour off the mop with the little attached squeegee. Then I just left it standing against a wall and by that night it was completely dry! (Unlike my old mop which took like days to completely dry!)

Lastly - when you are done with it - you just unscrew the handle and put it all right back in the tiny bucket. Super easy to put on a shelf, in a closet, or in a cupboard. REALLY space saving! My pic shows the size next to a bottle of champagne - really small! I am impressed with he size, engineering, durability, and ease of use. Great product! Totally recommend!

title: Very useful item at a good price
text:
This works well and is very inexpensive for its features. I like that it has a rating of up to 10,000 lux, as that is the recommended brightness for winter depression. Also, you can control the color temperature (color hue, or how much yellow/blue appears). I don't see that it was a CRI (color rendering index) rating, and some other more expensive bulbs make a point that theirs has this; however, I have not seen CRI ratings being required for winter depression in any medical literature, so I'm ok with it.

For color temperature, I prefer as white as possible, as that seems to give me the lift I need in the morning. The directions suggest less white if used in the late afternoon or evening - I have not tried this, but it makes sense that you'd want as white as possible in the AM and less so in the PM, as that would imitate the sunlight throughout the day. It also has an optional timer so it will turn off automatically after a period of time, if desired. All the settings are controlled either by multiple presses (timer) or press/hold (color temperature and brightness), which is easy, though not so intuitive. This is explained clearly in the directions, and is easy, once it is known. I like that it is LED-based, as this uses less energy and creates less heat.

Overall, this is a nice, well-priced item that is going to be useful this fall/winter, as the season gets darker, and the sun starts coming up later and going down earlier.

These are great for carrying an entree or sandwich to work, or for any kind of pre-portioning. I use them for almost any food that doesn't fit in my smaller deli containers. These are robust and seem like they'll last a long time. They're compatible with similar-looking generic containers from other stores (with the plus sign). This is a huge labor saver for me since I have several generations of similar sets that all fit together.

Also these aren't leakproof, but hardly anything is, and if it's leakproof then it's expensive or breakable or I left it in my car all weekend so now it's dangerous to open. Anyway, instead of trying to find the perfect leakproof container that won't ruin my lunch bag or the stuff in my backpack, I got a small all-plastic lunch cooler and some pint Mason jars (for when I have soup). If the sandwich containers leak a little in my cooler, it's not a big deal.

title: Affordable option with some serious drawbacks
text:
This tripod/selfie stick is really useful but pretty quirky when you try to use it, especially if you need to take it out often, or you're using it with the back-facing camera instead of in selfie mode.

The wireless feature of the remote works via Bluetooth. The remote on the tripod triggers the camera shutter by sending a signal to change the volume of your phone. That means to use the remote, you have to have a camera app that lets you take a picture by pressing the volume button on your phone. If your default camera doesn't do that you should be able to download a compatible camera app in the Play/app store. Btw, if you don't have your camera app open when you press the button on the remote, it will just bump your ringtone volume up.

The tripod is a telescoping metal tube with a phone clamp on one end and a convertible handle/tripod base on the other. There's a tiny remote that slides into the top of the tripod base, so you can either leave the remote in the handle and use your thumb to take photos while you hold the selfie stick, or you can remove the remote and take pictures without touching the tripod or phone. (And don't forget that you can trigger the shutter on many camera apps by saying "cheese," "smile," etc.)

The remote runs on a coin battery, CR1632. The box says it's replaceable.

It was crazy easy to pair the remote with my phone. I turned on the remote by holding the button down for a bit, turned on Bluetooth on my phone, scanned for devices and tapped "SelfieCom" when it came up. Done! (To turn off the remote you hold the button down until it stops blinking.)

The hardest part of setup is actually getting the phone into the clamp and adjusting it. It's hard to line it up so you can access all the buttons and not cover any cameras or anything. I wanted to use the back camera for pictures for a review, but I accidentally closed the clamp on the power button, couldn't get it off again for many seconds, and rebooted my phone. Review deleted :( My fault but man, really? It's like a snapping turtle.

You can put the phone into the clamp face up or face down, but if you want to angle the back camera down toward the ground (like if you want to take a back-camera photo showing an item from above), you have to put the phone in the clamp backwards so that the clamp covers part of the the screen. You can't tip the phone both forward and backward. It only tips forward because it's designed for selfies. (Like you can adjust it up and down to get pics of any part of your body, but you can't flip it over to get pics view of someone in front of you.) It's hard to explain. But if you're looking at this as a cheap phone tripod for your back camera, it's not ideal. It's for selfies as it says.

The tripod head can't be twisted on the telescoping pole, so if you've placed the phone on the tripod unevenly to keep the clamp from pushing buttons or covering your viewfinder, the unbalanced phone will make the tripod tip over, and you can't twist the clamp on the pole so that the phone overhangs one of the legs and the weight will be balanced. Some phones will hang out over the spot between two legs where there's nothing to hold them up. That means you have to hold the phone up, so there's little benefit in having a tripod.

It is nice that the clamp is really narrow so when you put the phone in backwards, the clamp only covers a very small amount of the screen. (But it would be better if you could flip the phone cameras to point downward on both sides.) I used a different phone stand with a wide clamp and it prevented me from using my fingerprint scanner. This one works fine with my fingerprint scanner. (And btw it seems like a good stand for a phone that's repurposed as a security camera, because you wouldn't have to keep taking it out of the clamp like you do with wider clamps.)

It is fussy to get the phone in the clamp as I mentioned, and you have to put the phone in the clamp different ways to get different camera angles and avoid pressing buttons, so it's really a hassle if you put the phone in wrong or need to get a different angle or something, and you have to take the phone out and put it back in. The clamp is spring-loaded and there's no good handle to grab on to open it up or ease it onto the phone. It just snaps on. Plus it seems delicate so it's stressful pulling on it, thinking you might break it.

I don't think it will last that long, especially the moving parts, and I'm concerned about trying to replace the battery.

I wish this were fully adjustable and had a little grip/handle to hold to open and close the clamp. But if you need an affordable tripod that doesn't have to be too durable or adjustable, this could be an option. It was really helpful for taking pictures once I got it set up.

The colors are vibrant and pleasing, but I think red would have made a better sock trio than orange, but they *are* the colors of the daleks in charge so I understand why these colors were chosen over other possible combinations. The design is clear and I can't see any errors in the execution. The socks are not super thin as I had anticipated, but they are also not super thick; a middle weight knit that works well almost year round. I will be gifting a set of these to a friend for the holidays and I can't wait for us to be able to wear our socks while chasing our kids around the house or poking them with our toes and saying "exterminate" over and over. I am very happy with these socks and would recommend them to anyone looking for a great smaller gift for the Whovian in their life. I received these socks at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review and I think they totally rock!

title: Many Uses for Zinc Oxide.
text:
I love this zinc oxide powder! You can look up recipes using zinc oxide powder and find many uses with instructions, including sun screen, diaper rash cream, lip balm, deodorant, and probably much more. In addition to the "recopies" you can also add this in to lotion you already have. It is such a fine powder that it mixes in extremely well. I do suggest wearing a paint or medical mask since it can get into the air if you're breathing over it as you get the powder out of the bag.
A great attribute of this particular zinc oxide powder is the sturdy resealable bag it comes in. You would have to try really hard to puncture the bag. Because it's tough, you could throw it in a suitcase without worrying about it getting everywhere. Once we get to our vacation destination, we'll mix up several containers of sunscreen. You can actually mix this in a bowl and seal it or put it into plastic bottles.
Since Tommy and our youngest son do a lot of surfing everyday, a heavy mix of zinc oxide lotion to coat onto their nose and under eyes is a must. The lotion sits at the top of the skin to protect those points on their faces that often get sunburned. It does not soak in. Keep in mind that this also means they have white face paint but so do a ton of other surfers so that's normal in our surroundings.
This is the first time I've done DIY sunscreen and If i had know this years ago I would have saved a fortune. We all know what the prices are like, I try to get it when it's on sale but it still does sting the wallet a bit. I received a free bag of zinc oxide powder and in return agreed to try it out and leave my honest opinion in this review. It's definitely a very handy item to have around! Do a search to find suggestions on how to make an assortment of zinc oxide items.

title: Suitable for Henna Body Art
text: Better than expected for henna body art. These bottles are rather stiff and difficult at first, but after spending about an hour working with them they softened up and were much easier to handle. I definitely recommend taking some time to test drive the bottles the day before you intend to use them for body art. The two largest gauge tips worked best for me, but the powder I used to make my paste still had a tiny bit of stringy plant particles in it. Better results might be had from using an extremely fine ground powder however, I would not recommend using a super dry paste or something with coffee/tea in it as these tips are too narrow. I used a Rajasthani powder with a ratio of 1/2c powder to 1/2c lemon juice to 1.5 tsp tea tree oil to 1.5 tsp granulated sugar. Produced a reasonably smooth paste that piped well with these bottles. The bottles hold more than enough to do several hands/feet for festival work. No need to keep refilling. Will definitely use again for henna body art.

title: Confusing control buttons
text:
Update 7/11: dryer is now dead after less than 10 time of use. Terrible.

I never thought I would review a hair dryer using a term called “user interface” or UI, but the UI of this hair dryer is simply too confusing and make it very hard to use. First of all, I don’t know who needs to control the temperature in one degree resolution. To crank up or lower temperature, you need to hold the + or - button and wait it to go from say 90F down to 60F. Why can not just have three preset temperature and the user can switch between them in one single click? It is a hair dryer not a computer and majority of the people just don’t need such feature. Also, I can never understand why when switching from hot air to cold air mode and switch back to hot air mode, it can not remember the temperature I used previously in hot air mode. It always starts with 50F which is simply to low and I have to spend another 10 second to crank it up to 90F. It is just too difficult to use.

The third highlight for me is that these cutting boards are dishwasher safe - I mean, really, what busy wife/mom wants to stand and have to hand wash something - I know I sure don't. Finally, these boards are reversible - they are identical on the front and back with the exception of the liquid catching groove - the back side of the board is smooth - perfect for cutting breads, sausages, or other dry foods.

Five stars all around and a definite recommend!!

title: Efficient and intimidating hair removal system at the same time
text:
The cordless feature of this epilator makes the task much more practical, especially using it where there is plenty of sunlight. The product comes with a little light, but is not bright enough to make a difference, the idea is good, but not to the point of relying on it for the job. It comes with dual speed, I prefer the slower one and it is just right for me. It's likely that younger users would prefer the faster one. Here is an interesting detail that I don't know how to explain the reason behind, but using the epilator in the bikini area, I noticed more irritation than other ones I have used in the past, however after 2 days, all is gone. The shaver works well for the thin hair and the noise level is low, I will be using less of the shaver attachment that the epilator head. The little brush included, is useful for the blades more than the epilator because in the last one tweezers are needed to pull out any hair stuck in between the coils. Changing the shaver with the epilator's heads is very easy, but the speed controller is on the hard side and it takes both hands to do it.
The rechargeable epilator and shaver combined are definitely an efficient way to get rid of unwanted body hair in your own personal accessory.

title: Simple and functional design
text: My husband and I decided to choose our own gifts this year for Christmas.  Our tub was recently refinished and we can no longer use epsom salts in it or they could damage the new finish, so I wanted a foot bath I could use epsom salts in. title: Rinse well to see the different blue and red plaque.  Always stains tongue though.
text:
I tried these with my kids. First off, I think the flavor is pretty good, unlike most reviewers here. My kids thought it was really gross but to me it tasted like Smarties candies. This is pretty ironic because I don't like candies, whereas my kids love them.

Secondly, the way I used them was to chew them then swish them around and in between my teeth, spit out, and rinse really well about 10x. After that I could see different blue older plaque between my teeth in the areas of recessed gums more towards the back, and some red plaque on my front teeth near the biting surface as well as on the top edge of my bottom incisors. These are definitely spots that I would miss easily. I had to floss to get rid of the plaque that was in between the gum pockets.

One of my kids had blue plaque only -- but she is pretty bad at brushing and definitely misses those areas all the time (near the gumline esp the top incisors). The other kid had a different staining pattern with blue and red areas. So if you are getting only one color on all your teeth, just keep rinsing out the excess dye until you can see a difference.

We all had to brush our tongue a lot but could not get the last 10% of the stain out. In the morning it seemed to have vanished, which means that we probably swallowed a bunch of red dye, not the best scenario.

Anyway, it does work and is a useful learning tool to shock the kids into brushing better, so I am happy with it.

title: Don't waste your money on this test...
text:
After ordering a test for myself, my husband and my daughter, I decided to do a little more research on hair testing for allergies (wish I would have done this before I ordered-- stupid me!), and have basically come to the conclusion that hair testing is one of the LEAST accurate ways to test for allergies. If you ask me, it's not worth your time. And, here is why:

1. I initially ordered the test for myself because I had a rash on my hand for about a year that wouldn't go away. Shortly before ordering the test, I stopped eating all nuts, and it cleared up within a week! I wanted to get an allergy test done anyway so that I knew for sure it was nuts (I didn't want to avoid them for the rest of my life it that wasn't even the problem). When I got the results back, nuts were NOT listed as an intolerance for me (YAY!) so I starting eating them again.... and guess what, the rash came back.

2. My husband already knows he has a shellfish allergy (his hands swell up big time), but that didn't show up on his test. Hmmmm....

3. I find it kind of odd that "bread, baguette" was on the list for me. So just bread?? Baguettes, specifically? What about crackers or pasta? Did they mean gluten? I'm confused. This seems really vague to me. In fact, all of the results were vague and disappointing.

4. Cats were listed as an intolerance for my daughter, but she sleeps with our cats every night and has no known allergies or symptoms to anything. I simply ordered the test for her out of curiosity.

5. The list of foods that came back on all of our test results as intolerances have never been a problem for us. But the foods that DO seem to be problematic for us, DID NOT show up on our results.

To be fair, I don't think any allergy test is 100% accurate. The only way to know for sure if your body is reacting to something is through trial and error. In my experience, you have to eliminate one thing from your diet at a time that you suspect may be a problem for several weeks, and then see if you experience any improvement.

title: I am very wary about this company
text:
I bought this bone broth as a change of pace for a more popular brand and decided to give it a try without doing the necessary research involved in supplements which I usually do. After receiving the pouch, I was taken aback at the taste, it basically tastes like ground up bone dust as the best analogy I could make. I decided to do as much research about the company as possible and only found a website that tells very little about the product or the company or the sourcing of this product and more importantly, exactly where this company is located and where the animals are and how they are cared for. They claim the bone broth is from Organic Grass-fed pasture raised, No hormones, No antibiotics, Non-GMO, which is all good but they do not back anything up and MOST IMPORTANTLY, there are NO third party quality assurances about what is going on.

After finding no quality assurances about this company anywhere on the internet I threw the bulk of this away in the garbage. I will not subject my body to an unknown. I am amazed that these products have been allowed onto Amazon for sale with so little information to back up the quality and sourcing of this bone broth and am shocked to not find them anywhere else for sale. I am now back to my original bone broth with collagen mix and will stay with that since I know for sure of its quality.

UPDDATE: Feb, 2018 - This company is now called Sun Cow Grass. Why? That's three corporate names in less than a year.

title: Unique among face rollers I've tried (and feels *great* on my face and neck)
text:
I'll be honest: I have no clue whether this is doing anything magical for my skin or neck, but I know that I love using it! I've had several of these face rollers, and while they've been ok for applying serums or night cream, they've always just been another step. This one I grab and roll along my face randomly during the day (I clean it often, so I'm not rubbing grime into my pores).
It's way different than the other face rollers/massagers I've had. The first thing I noticed when I took it out of the box was how *heavy* it is - this thing is solid! The second thing was how short and strongly curved it is, compared to other rollers. These may sound like drawbacks, but actually mean it fits perfectly into your hand and doesn't feel like it's going to slip out of your grasp if you don't hold it just right. Seriously, this is the first face roller that seems like it was designed by someone who actually uses face rollers. :D
The big rolling wheels are the perfect distance apart to roll along my jawline, my cheekbones, and my neck muscles, and, again, the solidity means I can roll it along my tight neck without worrying I'll break one of the balls off. I keep meaning to put it in the fridge, but because it's thick metal, every time I pick it up, it's already nice and cool, and stays that way for a while of use, so I haven't bothered.
If you like rollers, this one is aces. If you don't, the massaging action along the neck and jaw may be enough to convert you. :P

title: 6 units stopped working quickly, no matter how careful
text:
How is it that there's even one good review? Sure, it works well when you first get it, but it takes very little for it to stop working, no matter whether you empty the sprayer after every usage, soak in warm water or alcohol (as the company recommends).

We were using the sprayers with a very dilute solution of betadine, and I'd say we got about 50 squirts out of each unit before they stopped squirting. First it squirts full blast, then less and less until barely anything, then you are pushing the plunger down with no resistance whatsoever (pressure gets lost). This happened for the 2 units we purchased, then AGAIN with the 2 replacements (at which point we emptied the sprayers after every usage, in hopes of extending the life), and also with the extra 2 pivoting sprayers that were sent to us as a consolation. One of the sprayers lost the tiny plastic piece in the tip, which could be very dangerous if lost in the nose. We tried cleaning in alcohol as suggested, and also warm water. Nothing resolved the issues.

Customer support was wonderful the first time around, but when I reached out to them a second time after the replacements were also non-functioning, I got no reply.

It's a lot of money to spend on something that caused so much time to try to repair, and ultimately doesn't work at all. I'm very disappointed.

title: OFF-LABEL USE is very promising
text:
I am not using this for weight loss per se, although I wouldn't mind losing some weight [update: I have lost 6 pounds without trying in the last 2.5 months]. I am using it, rather, for improvement of overall health, a long bought with insomnia, and severely under-functioning adrenals. I originally learned about the off-label use of this device from Dr. Mark Sircus, found some great in-depth information on the site "normal breathing dot com" (click on the "learn here" tab), and finally got some super practical knowledge from author/trainer Patrick McKeown.

There is a great deal of medical science around breathing, and why it's actually beneficial to slightly increase the amount of CO2 in the body SO THAT more OXYGEN can be released into the body's tissues (including the brain and organs). The aim of Buteyko (an MD) is that patients will reduce their breathing down to a shallow normal level, to maximize the amount of oxygen in the body's tissues at all times. This method has been widely recognized as being extremely effective for treating asthma, and it makes sense that it can help other ailments as well, due to the increase in body oxygenation. I have been researching this now for several months, and being skeptically minded, I can say that there is a lot of sound science to back up the claims.

After 10 days of use of this Breathslim device, I had the quite miraculous result of eliminating heavy heart pounding that occurs for me during sleep for FOUR nights in a row. I still remain skeptical of what lies ahead, but this is a REALLY impressive result so far, since nothing else that I've tried has had this kind of effect (and I've tried a LOT of natural therapies). UPDATE: it has now been 2.5 months with no heart pounding.

I would also like to respond to the many misleading reviews that are posted here on Amazon, which almost caused me not to buy this product. First of all, while this item is all plastic, and it is simple in construction, and probably costs very little to manufacture, I do not see this as an adequate "debunking" of the product as several others have stated. It is most certainly NOT just a sippy cup, and you can NOT reproduce the results of this device by breathing through pursed lips. There IS some truth in what these reviewers are saying, but it's not the whole picture.

As I see it, this device uses a water barrier and a mostly enclosed container to (1) give some controlled resistance to breathing for both inhalations and exhalations, and (2) cause the breather to inhale a measured portion of the previously exhaled air (to increase the CO2 in the inhaled air). You can't breathe too hard through this device or else the water spills out the top.

I was able to create a similar device which was effective, using a thinner-than usual drinking straw taped deep inside a mostly-closed plastic bag. It took a bit for me to find a straw that was the right diameter--a cocktail straw was too small and I wasn't able to keep up the breathing for more than a couple breaths. A normal drinking straw was too easy to breathe through and did not give any resistance. I eventually found a straw that was in between, which, for me, was the perfect amount of resistance to make it difficult but not impossible. I have read about others who used a regular straw and pinched it, but this is not very scientifically controlled.

Having done this experiment, I do think that this device is superior in design. I can feel a different kind of resistance (less rigid, yet still controlled) and I like that the quantity of CO2 is more controlled. The rigid resistance of the straw can be difficult on some days when I'm a little more breathless, and a little too easy on days when my breathing is easier. And I think too much oxygen comes into the top of my plastic bag; if I close it up too much then it collapses while I'm breathing.

It's very interesting that while using this devise my nose starts to get a little runny. I also frequently get warm hands, or a sudden urge to have a bowel movement (sorry! TMI).

My criticisms of this particular device, although I'm not giving them much weight because this is a relatively low-cost device (I paid $25), are (1) the seams on the plastic are a little rough on the mouth piece, and (2) the hose a slight chemical odor which bothers me a little (but I am extremely, extremely sensitive to these things). UPDATE: I bought a longer silicone hose to replace the plastic hose. It is much heavier than the plastic one, but I like that I can set the unit in my lap without having to hold it during sessions.

The doctor who wrote the normalbreathing dot com site sells a book telling how to construct your own DIY device like this, made from plastic bottles and hosing. Of course he is charging a whopping $37 for his plans, so it is cheaper to buy this unit here than to make your own, but I share this just so that readers can understand that the concept here is quite simple. The idea is to slow down your breathing and inhale some extra CO2 with every breath.

What this device does not necessarily do, but is a very important technique according to Patrick McKeown, is to RELAX your body while slowing your breathing. I found instead, for the first couple months, that I was using "determination" to breathe slower, but this is counter-productive. I get much better results with active relaxation, now that I know about it.

A person could maybe learn Buteyko Breathing from reading online or books, at no or little cost, but I myself did not have much luck until seeing it demonstrated on video by Patrick McKeown. It sounds like a simple exercise, but it is not easy to accomplish. Having tried all these different things, I am partial to this device, since it makes it so easy and gives me something active to do. My next phase, though, is to learn how to do the real Buteyko breathing so that I don't have to carry this device around with me anymore.

I purchased the large adult adjustable mask in black. I did not get the XL and although I’m pretty big, I am ordering more in the same size. There is no adjustable nose piece, metal or otherwise.

Should you make sure to get a medically approved mask? That’s debatable. I figure I see lots of people walking around with thin bandanas on, this offers similar protection. I did not buy any filters. It’s important to wash these things every day or so and they get funky. My only complaint is the limited color choices as black is fine but having a few different colors would help as far as assisting a rotation schedule.

Adjustable is nice but the big draw, for me, is the neck strap. It’s extremely convenient and I’m surprised this is not the standard. At least after 3 weeks, I can say the quality is very good. Not the greatest with glasses but okay. What I do is put it on fairly tight, and then use both hands to adjust- imitate a gun with your fingers, then pointer on the temples, and use both thumbs to loosen the bottom. Whether you spend all day in the car, the computer or elsewhere sitting down for long periods, the Royal Purple Seat Cushion is a must have item to tend that tender tushy.

In the middle of a 9,273 mile road trip, my butt was getting more, and more tender. And, the periods of having to stop, and walk out the kinks was getting more frequent (most I could do was 75 miles, before having to get out for a few minutes).

Well, as I was walking up, down and around a Travel Center somewhere in Eastern Ohio, I saw a metal chair with "Try Me" and the RPSC was on it. So, I sat down on it, and what remaining discomfort I had, disappeared almost immediately.

So, since I only had about a 60 miles to go to my hotel for the night, I didn't bother using it. But, the next morning, I was able to drive 143.7 miles without stopping. In my 45+ years of driving, I NEVER was able to drive more than 100 miles before having to get out and stretch.

However, there is one little gripe that I have, and those with wide hips will have a problem, is that it could be wider (22-24 inches) to support the entire rear end.

Well worth the $79.99 + tx price tag.

title: Important Clarification About This Product - Please Read Before You Order!
text:
This is important information you should read before you purchase. This is a bit long, but please take the time to read it all. This will explain why some reviewers think they didn't receive the complete product.

I discovered this Fatigued to Fantastic powder on Enzymatic Therapy's website when I was looking for something else. Enzymatic Therapy is the maker of this product and I know and trust their brand. All of their product lines are shown on their website. This product looked great and I decided I would buy it. It was a canister containing powder and they make two flavors - Berry and Citrus.

However, I always check Amazon to see if they carry products and compare the prices. I found several sellers offering this product here on Amazon, and I was delighted to find that the prices on Amazon are HALF the retail price. I ordered the Citrus flavor on another page from a seller who had both flavors. Please understand that I thought I was ordering the canister of powder which is shown on the manufacturer's website. I even sprung for one day delivery so I'd get it faster.

After I ordered, I received the confirmation email that said I had ordered this "Kit" that contained the powder AND the supplement capsules. I came back to the sales page, enlarged the photo and saw that it was indeed a kit with both products.

I cancelled my order. I was confused. I only wanted the powder.

So I called Enzymatic Therapy and asked them to clarify if this "Kit" was their legitimate product, since it does not appear on their website. Here is what they told me...

They haven't made the "Kit" in the photo and description above for several years. At that time they made a major change. Instead of offering the bottle of vitamins with the powder as the Kit, THEY ADDED THOSE SAME VITAMINS TO THE POWDER ITSELF, so all of the ingredients are now in the one product - the canister containing the powder.

The Kits that are shown on this page and the other sellers' pages NO LONGER EXIST anywhere - no retailer or distributor has them. They have been gone for years.

So the rep told me that all of the pages - like this one - are showing and describing the old product that doesn't exist and that the sellers just haven't updated their pages over the years. At first I found that hard to believe because in all that time, customers would have surely complained if they didn't receive what's shown.

But she was positive that if I placed the order again, I would receive the newer canister (which is what I wanted.) I receive my order the next day (yesterday) and she was right.

So, in summary...

1. The reviewers who said they didn't receive the bottle of vitamin caps with the order as they expected were right.

2. The product "Kit" that's shown and described above is not what you will receive. You'll only receive the powder.

3. BUT you will receive full value of the product because those extra B vitamins are now in the actual powder itself.

Actually, you will receive MORE than full value because Amazon's price is half the retail price plus free shipping.

Oh...one more thing. I read reviews on several pages and I'm glad I didn't order the Berry. I do not like my powders sweet. I ordered the Citrus flavor and it's perfect - definitely not sweet - it's just right. I just added it to spring water and it tasted very good.

I hope this all helps...

UPDATE A FEW DAY AFTER TRYING THE PRODUCT:

I had very high hopes for this product. Good brand, good taste, good reviews. I'm always looking for the most healthful ways to increase energy. I've been a health nut for decades and have always taken lots of vitamins and supplements and nutritional products (greens, etc) and stay current on the latest research.

However, the first couple of days I took the Fatigued to Fantatic powder, I felt abnormally sleepy. Way too relaxed. I skipped a day and bounced back to normal. Took it again and the same thing happened. Instead of giving me energy, it brought my energy way down. I don't know what ingredient caused this. Since I'm used to taking a lot of supplements, I thought maybe it's one of the amino acids. I'm also thinking that perhaps this product is designed more to benefit someone with a condition (CFS,Fibromyalgia, etc). But for those who do not have a condition, perhaps it's overload in some way. I don't know.

I'm returning it and now back to my regular supplements.

I advise you to try it yourself and see how your body reacts. All of the positive reviews can't be wrong.

title: Very clever solution to a potentially messy problem
text: I've just had the interior of my entire house repainted from builder's blah to a different color in every room - 7 different colors.  The painters left me with cans for touch ups, but therein lies the problem. You know what it is - open up a gallon can, have to stir it up, find a brush, and drip, drip, drip. I knew I would need to do an occasional touch up and felt there had to be a better way.  After searching on Amazon, I found these tubes, and thought "wow, what a great idea!"  I didn't love the price but felt the convenience would make it worth it. I did end up going to the manufacturer's website and ordered from there directly. Do check for specials they offer-I was able to get a larger tube added to the set for the same price and shipping was very fast. Once the tubes arrived, I set about to fill them.  The process was very easy and straightforward. I have only had once chance to try them out, as the paint is so new.  There was a small chip on an outside corner in my bedroom.  It was so convenient to not have to open the paint can, pour some in a disposable container, get out a brush just to fix this one small but obvious spot, and then have to deal with all the leftover paint and dirty brush. I cannot address the durability of the foam pad on the top as of yet.  While the manufacture suggests that the paint pumps be disposed of, they say they can be washed to be reused. It isn't easy to clean them and get our all of the paint in them, but I figured I'd try. I would suggest that you try to match the pump with the paint color you first used them with, to prevent any color change in the refill. Think of these as paint marking pens.  I think they will come in very handy. I only wish I had thought of them myself!

text: I would have given this product 0 stars if I could have. I cannot believe the absolutely horrible " chemical" smell that this product left on my washed and dried clothes!  I am not typically sensitive to smells but this was SOOO obvious that I ended up re-washing and drying everything with my previous Tide.  Now understand:  I have an "old school" washer that allows me to set my own water temp, water amount, "heavy/permanent press/gentle" style, extra rinse, etc.  So it's not as if I have an HE washer that washes a load of clothes in 6 inches of water.  Pretty much everything that is washed goes through a full tub of water and two rinses (yes, I know we have a water shortage in CA but I like CLEAN clothes.  Don't judge me). I noticed the overwhelmingly car exhaust-type smell (it's the only way I can describe it) when I got the damp clothes out from the washer but I hoped that the smell would dissipate once dry.  I don't use dryer sheets: I use wool dryer balls or, occasionally, line drying outside.  When I removed the clothes from the dryer, the smell was still present and was so bad I couldn't subject my family to it.  So I ended up re-washing and drying all the previous laundry loads.  I gave the detergent to the friend that had convinced me to buy/use it (I may have to re-evaluate my friendship.  Kidding).  She hasn't used it yet so I'll be interested in her results.  She, too, has a washer that is non-HE and she uses two rinses.  So I am very interested in what her results will be. I would NOT recommend this product, ever! And am disgusted at the money that I paid for this.  And am now even more concerned regarding the other Norwex products that I purchased on her recommendation (kitchen cloth, face/body cloth, general cleaning products).  If they, too, don't measure up they are going back, even if I didn't purchase with Prime and I don't get free returns.  Truly, this laundry detergent was a HUGE disappointment.

title: Back for more!
text:
I bought two packs of these about a year ago. They've been used 2x a day since purchase and are still like new.

I now have two teenagers using them too, so I need more to make it more than a few days!

A few suggestions for anyone purchasing:

Since they're made from two layers of fabric, the two layers can slip during use. I simply fold them in half, OR wrap them around a finger to create just a bit of tension to prevent slippage.

In order to get these clean and keep them more sanitary, I have a small container with a tight fitting lid that I pour straight isopropyl (rubbing) alcohol in, and drop these in to soak after use. When I'm almost out of fresh ones, I hold the laundry bag inside the washer and just pour the wipes into the bag and zip shut. I use Tide+ powdered detergent which seems (in my experience) to work better to break down stains and gets them very clean versus liquid detergents. I wash them at the same time as our facial washcloths and towels.

Once out of the dryer, I simply stack them up, and drop them into a cylindrical glass vase I picked up at the dollar store. It's wide enough to easily grab them out, but keeps them neatly stacked and I can easily see when we're running low.

I REALLY love using these in comparison to the disposable cotton rounds and so do my teens. They don't cost me any extra to launder since I add them to a load I was already doing. Plus I can't imagine how many packs of disposables we'd be going through if we weren't using these!

title: No support for head/misleading shipping & return info
text:
I was so excited to receive this Cooling Pillow after reading about it. However, it only took a few minutes to realize that there is literally NO SUPPORT for your neck and head with this pillow. Your head will sink right to the bed level. If you're a side sleeper, the same thing will happen and the end of the pillow will fluff up covering your face. I fought much of the night to use this item before I gave up with a raging neck and headache from lack of support. This company really needs to indicate the level of firmness of the pillows they're selling. The cooling concept is good but the rest of the story is not so good.
OK - it's then obvious I need to return this item so I start the process only to find out they charge $20.00 more on Amazon versus their website sales for the same exact pillow but offer Free Shipping on Amazon. That might be OK if you're happy with the item and want to keep it. But now it's time to return it. I have to pay return shipping when I feel they didn't adequately describe the pillow i.e. no reference to firmness and support, so return shipping should be on their shoulders. So I pay the return shipping and when I receive the refund, they've deducted $13.58 for their cost to ship it to me in the first place. BUT IT WAS FREE SHIPPING!!!! No where in the item description did it say if I returned it they'd deduct the free shipping! That's like saying "I'm giving you an imaginary $20 bill but if you decide to return it I want a REAL $20 bill!"
I'm just totally not happy with the company policies on this item. (Or perhaps I'm just being like my user name - a seahag.) It's such a simple fix, too. Add a level of firmness to the description. Be honest and up front in the return policy on the Amazon website description that shipping will be deducted if returned. Yup, you write it in the paper that accompanies the merchandise but not on Amazon where it can be seen BEFORE we push the Purchase button. It's too late once we receive the merchandise and then read the paper enclosed. Very MISLEADING!
Buyer Beware.

title: Poor LH test performance
text:
Unless this is the odd one out, these LH tests are a total bust. For those who aren't familiar with how ovulation tests work, the test line must be as dark as or darker than the control line. With a control line this light, you're going to miss your surge. An LH control line should be as dark as the HCG test control, and it's nowhere close despite waiting the entirety of the result window time. It's like most of the dye just bypassed the control.

The HCG test, on the other hand, is solid. There are no indents or shadows on it and the result is quick. I'd recommend these tests any day, but the LH not so much.

For reference, the LH test ran a minute or so longer than the HCG.

title: A decent bath addition to help relax and sooth.
text:
At the time of review the bath fizz was $15.99 which can be a good value or expensive depending on how you use it. There are no instructions and it's totally up to you to add as much or as little as you want. The fizzing and scent will depend on the concentration of how much was added.

So there are a couple benefits to this. You end up controlling how much you put into the bath so if a bath bomb is too much and your skin is sensitive or you are sensitive to strong scents you can tone down to where you can enjoy it and start with a little and add more rather than having too much in a single use and just empty the tub to start over.

We found the scent to be pleasant and overall mild with a couple cap fulls that provided scent, fizz and a pleasant feel to our skin after a soak. One thing I would note is if there is confusion on if this is a bubble bath. It is not. It's more like the dying of an alka-seltzer tablet so a gentle fizz. I'm sure if you add more and get more fizz the bubbles would build up, but the bubbles are mostly in the water, not on the surface like a bubble bath.

title: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
text:
This doesn't seem to be a quick fix for a plugged drain now. This is for slow but functioning drains and is an alternative to harsh chemicals which can damage pipes over time with repeated usage. So it is a preventative treatment for me to start removing a potential build up before it becomes a serious issue.

I've used 2 doses on my slow drain in my tub/shower and it seems to work rather well. I no longer have a small puddle at the drain as I shower and washing out my cat's litter box in the tub and dumping out the water drains much faster than before.

I would not try this on a plugged up drain or a sink/tub that is backed up with water already in it. I don't know if the enzyme works diluted and usually at that point it's probably going to be better to get it snaked at remove the physical clog.

title: It's labeled at 3% concentration.
text:
It is what it says it is. A 3% concentration of hydrogen peroxide with and orange scent. Remind me of the orange glo or whatever brand it was of orange oil cleaner that was big in the early 90's when I was a kid. It seems to perform like the low concentration you would mix for glass surfaces of the orange cleaner as well.

I saw a review that claimed there wasn't a labeling for concentration on the bottle. It is listed in the center of the label that it is 3%. Which is the same as the drugstore brown bottle disinfectant hydrogen peroxide you buy over the counter. The orange scent smells like orange peel oil that all orange cleaners have which smells like oranges but not at the same time.

Overall it's a pretty decent cleaner and disinfectant, but the price is rather high for what you are getting. You can get hydrogen peroxide in higher concentrations an mix a gallon of 3% for much less than half the price and if you are one who needs scents you can buy and mix in your own organic oils and make a similar product. But this saves time and guess work if you don't mix your own concentrations often and with hydrogen peroxide getting your math wrong can be hazardous so this product does have its place and value in that respect.

title: This is really great lower calories soft drink and tastes good too.
text:
I just noticed this and some other brands of carbonated beverages at Whole Foods in the last weeks. I stopped drinking Coke and other carbonated drinks because of the high fructose corn syrup and the dense concentration of empty calories as spoken about by . This brands has smaller servings, and less calories.

1 Coke has 140 calories per 12 ounce serving meaning almost 12 calories per ounce.
12 Ounces Coke 140 Calories
12 Ounces Q Kola 105 Calories

1 Q Kola has 70 calories per 8 ounce serving or almost 9 calories per ounce.
8 Ounces Q Kola 70 Calories
8 Ounces Coke 93 Calories

An 8 ounce serving of Coke has 24 more calories than an 8 ounces serving of Q Kola.
A 12 ounce serving of Coke has 36 more calories than an 8 ounces serving of Q Kola.

3500 calories in a pound of fat, so that is about 1167 ounces more of Q Kola you would have to drink to

To gain a pound of fat you would need to drink 25 cans of Coke or 33 equivalent cans of Q Kola,
that is you can drink more Q Kola for the same caloric "price".

I'm just saying that Q Kola tastes pretty good, complex, spicy, sweet and refreshing ... like Coke
with about 75% of the calories.

Plus you will drink less because the bottle aren't 12 ounces, they are 8 ounces, though you can
get 6 ounces cans of Coke now and they are cheaper than Q Kola.

I will stick with some of these new drinks like Q Kola put my money into more reasonable and
healthy alternatives.

That said I am trying to cut down on all soft drinks, and even juice, except real fresh juiced fruits
and vegetables. I find these smaller less calorie dense drinks a help in that effort, and I also do
not like to contribute money to Coca-Cola that has been going on for decades knowing they a
are contributing to the sickness and obesity of Americans.

title: Thank Goodness for this Machine!
text:
Finally I can fall to sleep. I read 100+ reviews about this machine (and there were hundreds more to read) to make sure this was the last Sound Machine I would ever need. It really works. I, too, didn't see the need for 2-speed machine and cost was an issue. When I first turned it on I thought, "Oh dear, this noise will never put me to sleep!". That was my first and last thought until I awoke several hours later.
I have really bad Tinnitus, which gets worse as the day turns into night. By the time I'm ready to go to sleep, the ringing in my ear sounds like a bunch of kids screaming & yelling. When I awoke, I noticed that the 'ringing' had subsided to a very low level.
My husband balked at the 'noise' for about 10 seconds..., then all I heard was his slow, rhythmic breathing.
I decided to purchase 2 machines so that we could use one for our dog as she shakes and trembles from all the illegal fireworks that go off in our town during the whole summer tourist season. Our dog has her own little room set up with a cozy bed, her "Thunder Shirt" and the Sound Machine. She can't hear the fireworks with this machine so she's no longer in extreme distress! I prefer using the sound machine over giving her tranquilizers every time.

title: An essential for people who use patch-type meds
text:
This is half, at least, of the solution to the problem I had keeping my pain-reliever patch attached.
Part of my problem is that I'm hairy, and part of the problem is that I perspire. I have to shave an appropriate area on my upper arm to apply my medication patch, but I've still had them fall off, sometimes in an embarrassing situation.

These are a relatively inexpensive way to keep my patch attached. They cause NO skin reaction, and as long as I place them correctly on shaved areas, they adhere fairly well, and they DON'T cause any discomfort on removal. They are MUCH more effective than the adhesive tapes I've tried.

Used in conjunction with a compression bandage I made by cutting an athletic sock at the ankle, and sliding the cuff up on my arm, they are 100% effective in keeping my patch in place for the full week, even in summer.

title: The standard bearer for rechargeable NiMH AA's.
text:
The eneloop AA's have been around awhile and have weathered the storm of competitors with huge mAH ratings in comparison by simply demolishing them in one category; longevity of charge. I've had rechargeable AA batteries for use at work and home for years now and the most frustrating thing is loading up a pair out of a drawer and they are dead or near dead. Sanyo has that solved and in doing so has made me phase out all of my other brands in favor of the eneloops. These are the new Rev A version that supposedly have a longer lifespan due to being able to handle more charging cycles but I haven't managed to wear out the old version yet! I use quality chargers like LaCrosse and Maha's that charge each cell individually. I also have enough batteries now that I can afford the time necessary to slow-charge them instead of the 1-hr quick charge cycles that are infamous for reducing lifespan.

I really can't emphasize enough the importance of knowing when you turn a device on that the battery inside still has juice in it! Same goes for having batteries stored up for a rainy day. Having a storm sneak up and knock the power out but having ample battery life on tap from batteries charged over a year ago is good peace of mind.
