title: I wanted to love this
text:
I love the FitBit Ultra and wanted to have an easier and more elegant way to track my weight. I also wanted to be able to track body fat percentage, something my cheap scale couldn't do.
I read about difficulties in setting up the scale, and I thought that would not apply to me, because I am very technically savvy. Well, it took me forever and many errors to set it up. The scale keeps shutting off while in setup mode. There is an app to use to set it up, but DO NOT USE IT. The only way to get it set up is to do it manually by connecting to the Aria's own ad hoc network.
I was thrilled when I got it set up (finally) and started using it. I tested it against my old scale, and first found it weighs about 2 pounds heavier than that scale. I tried weighing multiple times, and each time I got widely variable results, several pounds different from each other within seconds. My other scale always weighs the same. My body fat averaged over 10 percentage points higher than what it "should" be according to my recent previous measurements. I am morbidly obese according to the Aria by fat percentage, while my weight is within "normal" range by my cheap scale. I cannot trust what this scale tells me in weight or body fat.
I tried to get help. No, I am not on carpet, I am on hardwood. No, there is not something on the scale affecting the conduction of the signal. No, I am not moving the scale around so it has to recalibrate. I have no idea what to do, aside of sending it back to Amazon. I have given it almost 2 weeks to prove itself and it hasn't.
It is a pretty thing. It has a very elegant presence, but its beauty is only skin deep.

title: Love my Colema Board
text:
I know it must seem weird to say you love a colema board, but I really do love this thing. I have had slow digestion/transit since I was a child and have regularly seen a colon therapist for years, up until about a month ago when she relocated to another state. Rather than starting all over with a new person, I did my research and bought this product for myself.

I have done 'open colonics' before and the principal is very similar.

This is very effective in relieving gas and moving waste through. I am told that because you are lying flat, you will not strain or inflame any hemorrhoids using a colema board. Furthermore, your muscles still have to work, so this will not become addictive.

There are a few things to know about this...
1. the biggest danger in using a colema board is damaging yourself with improper insertion. I put a piece of tape (duct) on the speculum at about 2.3-3 inches to make sure it never goes in further than that. I use castor oil to lube it too.

2. I keep a roll of paper towels, rubber gloves, a gallon bottle of water and bleach spray for clean ups afterwards.

3. I think the tank is far too heavy to lift when full, so I use the same gallon bottle to fill the tank one gallon at a time.

I am really happy with this purchase.

It is heavy and bulky, but I don't see any way around it. To me for the relief I feel, it is worth it.

And for the record, I don't sell this product and don't have anything to do with this company. I am just a happy customer.

I was actually quite surprised that this worked as well as it did. My hair is wavy, (texture 2B) but not in a pretty way, it mostly looks tangled and messy and is resistant to styling. I control my frizz by using co-wash method and always air dry my hair.

My initial impressions were - this brush glides through my hair very well, doesn't pull or burn or make weird crimps like a regular iron does. I was able to get all the way to my scalp without burning, which was really nice. My hair doesn't look as flat as it usually does with my regular straightener. I think this was much faster than my regular iron too. I just brushed my hair and it was smooth. It was a comfortable experience for me.
My secondary impressions - I woke up to fairly straight hair with no frizz. I heated the brush up and ran it through my problem waves (namely the exact center back of my head). I was done in minutes and ready to go.

I couldn't figure out how to switch from Celsius to Fahrenheit, but this has a wide variety of temperatures for all textures of hair. I also wish the storage bag was heat resistant so it could be put away before it was cooled down. The design of the "bristles" could be better so it gripped the hair a bit better and straightening could be accomplished with just one pass. I can also see that the control buttons are not in an ideal spot and might be accidentally turned off or turned up.

My final verdict - the amazon price is good for this brush. The quality is excellent and it's easy to use. It's not perfect, but does the job I needed it to do.
Photos - I stopped midway and took pictures with half my hair done -- the straightened side is a good 2-3 inches longer than the wavy side and yet it still has some body and lift, which I love.

UPDATE EDIT... I've used this straightener every day since I got it and I've changed my mind about the buttons on the handle. It's almost impossible to accidentally shut it off or change the heat setting. It's great for daily touch ups and much faster than my regular straightener and has become part of my morning routine. I'm upping my stars to 5

title: PediSoft Callus Remover Review
text:
Having callus on the bottom of your feet can be a bit annoying at times and can cause some discomfort. I go through shoes pretty fast, mostly due to my daily workouts, so I do have callus on my feet. It is even worse during the summertime when I mowing the yard.

Last week, I was sent the PediSoft Callus Remover to review. Yes, it may seem a little odd that a male is wanting to review a product that is pink. Though pink isn't my favorite color, I just ignored that little fact and reviewed the product for what it is - a callus remover.

The Pedicure Callus Remover is a wet/dry hand-held device, similar to an electric razor, with a removable roller. It also comes with an extra roller, a brush, a charging cord and a plastic clear cap. It is recommended to charge it 10 to 12 hours before using it for the first time.

I have never owned a callus remover before, so I didn't know what to expect. It turns out that this device has quite a bit of power to it as the roller turns 40 times a second! I originally thought that the there would be a slight pain when the roller is scraping the callus away, but I'm glad to report that it didn't hurt at all. The remover does a great job of shaving down the dead skin! Washing it is real simple - just rinse the roller out and your done. Overall, I'm impressed by the Pedicure Callus Remover and I recommend it to others.

*Disclaimer - I received a complimentary sample in exchange for my honest review. All opinions are my own.

Before I started writing the review, I decided to read other comments. I noticed a few other people saying they had to wait a few days, so I decided I'd give it ONE week.

The very next day after I got out of the shower, the disgusting, calloused, thick, nasty skin on the bottom of my feet were bubbling. Not long after bits of skin were just sloughing off. I'm a picker, so of course I decided to help the process along. DO NOT DO THIS. JUST LET IT HAPPEN BY ITSELF>>> Someone else gave this warning, and I didn't listen. You'll start with the little thin layer that's come off, but it'll be attached to thicker areas that aren't ready yet, and trust me, you'll regret it, ouch!

Anyway, it's been 7 days now and my feet aren't exactly "baby feet", but they've never been so smooth and even. Well, not for at least a decade anyway. The soles of my feet were pretty bad to start, so I intend on doing another treatment and may just do this several times a year for maintenance.

title: Great Solution, but Beware of the Case!
text:
Great product if you wear monthly contacts. I'm still new to contacts (I've had them for about a year and a half) and this solution saved me! I wear Biofinity Toric contact lenses that are disposable monthly. My eyes generate an insane amount of protein buildup in just two weeks so my optometrist recommended this solution brand. The solution does the job to keep my contacts clean, but it is VERY painful if you get it in your eyes. The first time I did I thought I was going to go blind it was so intensely painful.

This solution works wonders, but you have to be careful with the case. This twin pack only comes with one case, which will not outlast the two bottles.

If you've been using the same case for too long and start to notice your solution isn't neutralizing after 6 hours, you need to replace your case. These cases have a small disc at the bottom (can't think of what they're made out of...zinc maybe?) that neutralizes the peroxide solution over the course of six hours. If the disc at the bottom is worn out, your solution will not neutralize and you'll be left with burning eyes. It took me a few days of research and unexplained burning eye pain to figure this out - but if you're careful with the cases you shouldn't have any problems. And be sure to rinse with the Clear Care rinse afterwards, or with a regular solution (I recommend Biotrue).

title: Far more comfortable than the purple "Quiet Please" version I wore for years- a good product for sleeping with a Snorer!
text:
I live with a snorer. A snorer whose sleep study came back with "some snoring observed"...who sounds like he's "yelling" when he snores-!
I have used the purple Flents "Quiet Please" for a long time (years) but recently ran across these when I was making my usual Amazon purchase. The purple version do feel a bit tight in my ears after a few days, and sometimes I need a break. So I ordered these and have been so, so satisfied!

They are suggested for sleep because they are shorter than the purple "Quiet Please" version. Therefore, if you ever sleep on your side, there is no pressure. I didn't think the purple kind were causing pressure, until I tried these!

Second, these ear plugs are much more giving than then purple version. They are softer and I can wear them every night for many nights in a row. I haven't had a "break" yet and I've been wearing them for weeks. Some people have commented here and there about size differences. I have only come across one (out of about 50!) that felt a little harder. I tried it anyway, and found that it felt the same as the others in my ear, so maybe it was closer to the outside of the container on a cold night? Who knows. But I haven't had consistency issues that others have mentioned.

Third, these are rated slightly below the purple "Quiet Please" version in sound protection. As I mentioned, my husband snores loudly, so I was concerned. No problems! These seem to work just as well, and i don't notice any difference. I haven't tried them in other settings, but they keep his snores at bay...even when I can feel the base rattling around in my chest, these work. Of course, I can hear if something happens, like my dogs suddenly bark from the edge of the bed, so I'm not worried about fire alarms, etc.

Overall, these Super Sleep Comfort Foam Ear Plugs (Flents, in green/teal) are amazing and I plan to order them next time...which is coming up soon!

title: Must weigh the pros with the cons
text:
First, let me start by saying I was out of shape and overweight before the pregnancy (180lb, now at 205lb at 30 weeks) and short (5'2"), so it was inevitable that I would have a lot of discomfort in the last trimester of my pregnancy. I bought this on recommendation of my doctor for some severe pelvic instability issues that was causing pain with walking and stairs. With that being said, I think that you should consider what you're buying this for and what you're hoping to accomplish before you judge the cons of this product.

CONS:
It makes me look even fatter - because of all the bulges it creates under my clothing. This is due to my being out of shape and overweight though, as no amount of support could be given if it were loose enough NOT to create bulges.

Its not east to put on, and requires a bit of adjustment after moving around a lot.

Its bright white! Easy to see under dark clothing.

The straps that cross in the front are visible at the neck line of all but turtle neck tops - and I have not found a way to pin them out of the way without it pulling on the item and my under clothing in a worse way (the cross of the straps is at the center of my chest).

PROS:
The pressure is relieved. Not 100%, but relieved enough to make the inconveniences worth it. I don't believe this is for someone who is experiencing manageable pain. This is for someone who is at their wits end and realizes they have months to go and they are willing to look a bit unflattering for some pain relief.

title: Like a snuggie for your face
text:
I have several varieties of masks, but this one is by far my favorite. It's the most comfortable and it doesn't make me sweat as badly as other masks do. It's so soft that I even forget I'm wearing it.

The neck strap is a must since my mask is off and on frequently, plus it makes the ear loops adjustable for a good fit. There is no metal bar over the nose, but I don't miss it because this fabric molds nicely to the face.

Some reviewers have complained that the fabric is too thin. I don't find that to be the case, but I live in a semi-rural area and I'm able to consistently maintain a 6 foot distance from others. If that ever changes, I will add a liner to the filter pocket.

I did notice that if I have a stuffy nose and need to breathe through my mouth, this mask gets sucked in because it's so flexible. A liner would probably fix that for folks with chronic allergies or sinus problems. I just switched to a heavier mask that morning and it was NBD.

I highly recommend this mask for those who are struggling with mask compliance due to sensory processing issues, sensitive skin, claustrophobia, or heat-sensitivity. It is important to me to wear a mask and keep others safe from anything I might be carrying unaware, and now I can do that without making myself miserable!

title: Nutritious & tastes good
text:
My normal go-to smoothie powder is Vega Smoothie Infusion, but I have this on occasion for a change of pace.

I like that it's plant-based (I'm a vegan) and I can't really taste it in my fruit/veggie smoothies. I haven't ever tried it with just almond milk or whatever, so I can't say how it'd be plain with liquid. But with some kale or collards and water or almond milk (or hazelnut milk -- yum!) and a banana, plus usually I add Spirutein cappuccino flavor and a dash of cinnamon and maybe a soaked date, it's super yum. Also I often add a dash of peppermint extract. Toss some ice and maybe some frozen wheatgrass juice in the Vitamix and I swear, it's like mint ice cream.

I don't like things too sweet, so most protein powders (including all of the other Spiruteins except maybe vanilla) are way too sickly sweet for me. I like that Vega isn't.

I did try another Vega product, Whole Food Health Optimizer, and I didn't like the taste. So I stick to these two. With the Smoothie Infusion powder, I also use Amazing Grass and sometimes TJs fruit-based powder and some frozen fruit.

I also only use one scoop of the Vega powders per smoothie.

I did buy a shaker cup to use with powders, so maybe sometime I will try this powder with just almond milk. If I do, I'll report back. For now, I'm happy with this powder and order it regularly.

title: Could be better but charges my 10,000 mAh D cell perfectly.
text:
This review is for the Black Battery Charger, what seems to be the 2nd generation of charger from EBL. I also have the earlier version since I have many D cells that I need charged. This charger has a problem the earlier version had.....regarding 9volt batteries......When the 9v rechargeable is plugged in a red light comes on indicating charging but there is no overcharge protection or light going out when 9v charge is complete. Like the first gen charger you have to calculate how many hours to leave the 9v in the charger!!!! Are you kidding me??? So to recharge my 9v NMH and Li I bought the EBL 9v 2 bay charger which has the light go out when charge is complete. It cost about 9 bucks but is worth it to me since I'm not going to try and calculate how long my battery needs to be charged with poor math skills.

So, for charging D, C, AA, AAA, this unit is pretty good. If your batteries are low when you go to charge them, push the select button, that will auto discharge them and then charge them. New batteries should be charged and discharged 3x for maximum efficiency but that is up to you. I will say that I find EBL batteries to be very good with high capacities and have zero fault with them. The charger needs some work.....such as auto shut off for 9v....and firmer metal sliding contact tabs. If you have D cell these fit tight in the holders......so I suggest pulling the metal slider with one hand and then inserting the battery with the other hand....otherwise, if you just push the battery in with one hand, the thin metal slider can bend really easy.

I don't care if something is made in China......as long as the item is made well, and functions properly for a fair price. I have no complaints even if it only costs 60cents to make. I will be a repeat customer for good products.

Update 6/11/17 - I've been getting good reliable charges so I bumped this up to 4 stars. I should also mention I made the mistake of buying a D cell charger at Harbor Freight some time back and discovered it would not charge batteries over 3000 mAh. My D batteries are high capacity 10,000 mAh and that is why I bought this EBL charger. I should have bought this one first. Live and learn.

title: A healing skin remedy
text:
I used this product as one of the main ingredients for a herbal homemade cream to combat psoriasis. For more than three weeks my sister had been suffering from a unusually persistent itchy psoriasis outbreak that had spread from her neck to her arms. All the herbal remedies that we normally made during her milder skin problems were not responding well enough, so as a last resort we followed a recipe that used a combination of Irish moss, a golden seal infusion, and an equal amount of vegetable glycerin.

Literally after only three applications in a eight hour period we saw the redness on her skin and the red hot itchy bumps on her arms virtually disappear leaving behind only minor traces. Apart from that their was an immediate sense of relief from the uncomfortable itching that ended after only the first application. Even though we had used many different external and internal herbal formulas that normally worked, this time the itchy red bumps had managed to form a red uncomfortable sheet on the entire surface of her lower arms. This wonderful mixture completely took care of all these problems in a matter of days, leaving her skin smooth without a single scar. Even the usual dry psoriasis patches that worsened during these episodes responded beautifully to the mixture, and quickly softened until they too finally disappeared in one weeks time.

It was an unreal experiences given how much a person can suffer from skin conditions like psoriasis. I know that petroleum jelly is often used as a base for many homemade topical herbal remedies, but the results I personally witnessed using the Irish moss instead is far better if not seem more healing for the skin in the long run, since petroleum jelly can some times encourage excessive dryness if repeatedly used. However, the sticky jelly solution that is created after the moss is heated in water makes a wonderful binding agent that gently nourishes the skin and naturally promotes the body to heal itself. Their are other formulas to experiment with depending on the severity of the problem, either way using the Irish moss as a binder would enhance the healing process.

title: Typically, I love Method products...
text: I found this as a new product at my local store.  The Method products that we use continuously in our home:  dish soap, granite polish, and all purpose cleaner. Love the fact that the bottles are made from recycled plastic, all of the ingredients are listed on the product, use non-toxic ingredients, and it is biodegradable, just to name a few.  I know my current floor cleaner cannot boast those same accomplishments.  As a matter of fact, there are no ingredients listed on the bottle of my favorite brand floor cleaner, which probably isn't really great.  However, the Method floor cleaner left a slimy, slippery residue on my tile floors.  I was afraid that I had not diluted it properly, so I then went over the floors a second time with just water, and still the same slimy, slippery residue persisted.  It was so bad, that my 6 year old told me the floors felt gross.  What 6 year old notices how the floor feels?  I have been walking around in slippers the past two days, so that I didn't have to go barefoot.  Today, I finally had time to clean the floors for a third time with my typical floor cleaner, and no more residue.  At this point I cannot say whether or not I recommend this product.  Would I try the product again? Maybe, if I have enough spare time to clean my floors twice, so that I don't have the same problem.  I will update my review if that ever happens.

title: MUCH QUIETER THAN TRADITIONAL CLIPPERS, FITS LITTLE HEADS WELL!
text:
We got this for our 4 year old son. He doesn't have any sensory issues, so I can't speak to that. We got it because, since he was old enough to talk, he told us he wanted his hair as short as possible. Nothing 'spikey'. For about a year we cut his hair with my husband's adult sized clippers. While those worked OK, I always had to go over his head again with scissors and cut all of the stray hairs that were missed on his tiny head. While this does still miss some hairs (nothing is perfect), it does a much better job of fitting his child-sized head and only leaves a few stragglers behind.

So far I've used the 2 shortest settings and they both look comparable to the length you'd get in a barber shop.

It's much quieter than the other clippers we have, though it still does make a low buzzing noise. It's quiet enough that we can have the TV on normal volume and still hear it while cutting his hair.

It has an easy to use on/off switch.

I've never tested its waterproof ability.

The package comes with several different lengths of guards, a charger, an apron, and it's supposed to come with a cleaning brush (though ours wasn't in the package). The charger is a USB, not a standard plug. I'm sure everyone has access to a USB charging port in 2017, but it's worth noting it's not a traditional US outlet plug.

For the price this is great. I'm sure if I spent a ton of money I'd never have to use scissors to clean up missed hairs, but this is totally worth it for our needs!

-The consistency is *very* oily. It goes on shiny, and it stays shiny. By mid-day, maybe my powder has worn off, I'm shiny again, which I do not like. My previous sunscreen (Alba Luminosity) didn't do this at all.Thankfully it is winter, because in the summer, I think this would just feel sweaty and probably drip off my face! I worried that the oily thickness would result in more acne, but it really has not, so don't let that worry you.

Between the oiliness and the color, it makes me feel like I'm wearing much heavier makeup than I prefer.

It does go on nicely if you can take the oil and don't mind a little color. I'm kind of on the fence about it and will probably finish the bottle, but I will probably continue my search.

text:
I was offered a full size sample of this eye cream in exchange for an honest review of the product.

This was the first time I had used an eye cream. I normally use a nationally recognized brand moisturizing lotion that's for use all over my face, and just apply that around my eyes also.

Let me start by saying this item comes very nicely packaged! It's not at all what I expected, with Argan in the name, I expected it to smell like Argan oil, which it doesn't, and I expected it to be greasy, and it wasn't! It goes on smoothly and absorbs nicely into the skin. I have to admit I was quite skeptical that I would see a difference in any area around my eyes. I have puffy bags under my eyes, and they've been there since I was a teenager. My grandmother had them, my mother has them, I just assumed I would always have them. But when I applied this cream every morning they were noticeably less puffy! I don't have wrinkles around my eye area, but I will continue to use this cream, rather than my national brand moisturizer on my eye area. I am MORE than satisfied with the results it gave me with the puffiness.

You do NOT need a lot of this cream either. A little definitely goes a long way, and jar will probably last most people almost a year. I'm extremely satisfied with the sample, and will probably purchase this item when I run out!

title: Excellent. It came quickly (just a few days) and ...
text:
I ordered this Bath Bomb Gift Set and received it free or at a discounted price for a detailed review.

PACKAGING: Excellent. It came quickly (just a few days) and was in a box which was the correct size for this product. The "cupcakes" were individually wrapped in a plastic sleeve, tied at the top with a round card which stated the "flavor" of the cupcake. The three cupcakes were then put into a thick plastic box and surrounded by pink raffia. This box was wrapped with bubble wrap and inserted into the cardboard box.

FIRST IMPRESSION OF PRODUCT: Honestly, the first impression was the smell. It was pretty overwhelming. Very "perfumey" smelling. After I looked at it, I had to close the box because I was afraid the smell would give me a headache. It was in the box for about two-three weeks, and when I opened it back up to use it, the smell was still pretty strong. Each cupcake was intended to have a different scent, but I couldn't detect a big difference, except the lavender smelled a little different.

THE LOOK: Awesome! These are adorable, and look like you could eat them! They look even better than the picture. Very colorful and detailed.

USING THE PRODUCT: I dropped the Strawberry one into the bath and had fun watching it fizzle. It turned the water a light pinkish color, and it dissolved about 99%. There was a little residual pink and white on the top of the water. The pink left a little bit of a ring in the bathtub, but it easily rinsed off with my shower head sprayer.
The smell was less overwhelming once the cupcake dissolved in the water. It seemed to leave a gentle scent on my skin--not necessarily the strawberry scent, just a gentle perfume.
The "icing" dissolved about 45% right away. To be honest, I forgot it was supposed to be exfoliating. I did pick up the small chunks and squeeze them, and I can see that it could work as an exfoliate. I would suggest not letting it dissolve with the fizzy part to get the most use out of it.
The star and polka dot "sprinkles" did not really dissolve, but acted like wet soap when I squeezed them.

OVERALL: I was concerned that, because of the strong perfume smell, this product might irritate my body. It did NOT. It did not make soap suds or anything like that, either. The product was really well made and would be perfect for a gift for someone. If I had not been overwhelmed by the smell, I would have given this product five stars.

text: Meh. I wanted this to work because my outer lashes grow upward on one eye in a way that makes it tough to make my falsies look symmetrical. So I bought this product in hopes I could curl my left lashes upward and push my right lashes downward to make them even. text:

title: Keeps my eyes from getting dry
text:
I use these eye drops twice a day, and they keep my eyes from feeling dry. If I forget a dose, my eyes tell me about it! I have seen some comments about leaking bottles. Here's my advice: Ignore the instructions that come in the box. Instead, remove the cap and then remove the plastic ring. THROW THE RING AWAY. The plastic ring is a spacer to keep the cap from accidently piercing the bottle. Next, replace the cap and tighten it down. The cap will pierce the tip of the bottle and allows it to dispense the eye drops when you remove the cap again. When you replace the cap and tighten it down, the bottle will not leak even with the pressure changes of flying in an airplane.

If you leave the plastic ring on, trust me, the bottle will always leak.

title: Incredibly Easy and Stress Free -  Even a 100% Disabled Veteran Can Do It!
text:
For years I have struggled to try to clean my service dog's teeth with a small round soft bristle toothbrush. Always difficult and exhausting to try to get him to let me into his small toy poodle mouth-especially the back. Often the brush made his gums bleed. Poor fellow has lost many teeth over the last couple years to bacterial problems common in his breed. My hesitancy to brush him due to the stress it induced in both of us didn't help. I have 45 of my own health issues due to Agent Orange exposure. For me the need for easy care and a life as stress free as possible is paramount.

I just discovered these PenVinoo cloth finger brushes and am so happy I gave them a try. Just a thumb and index finger and I am covering both sides of the mouth at the same time. Additionally, they are even easier to wrap behind the teeth which I could not do with a brush. So far I have not experienced any gum bleeding which certainly makes momma more likely to want to brush again tomorrow too.

These cloud soft cots seem to be way less traumatic for my pup. He isn't showing any signs of discomfort or fighting to get me out of his mouth anymore. I am not planning on rewashing the cots. I know that may be a cost saver but they fit perfect now and I would think they would shrink a bit in a wash and dry situation. Plus I'd rather not have dog toothpaste in my washing machine.

I've just ordered another 200 finger brushes as my Vet wants me to brush daily whenever possible.

Whether these would fit a larger man comfortably I cannot say. I am a female with hands that fit size medium disposable gloves. They fit just about perfect. They may stretch to the smaller spectrum of size large.

Buy one package and see if you, too, can reduce some stress out of both you and your pups life with the easiest brushing concept I have ever encountered.

text:
Great little light!

This Fenix PD22ue has a simple user-interface. Just turn it on by clicking the rear switch, then press the side-switch to cycle between low, medium, high & turbo. Strobe is also accessible by holding the side-switch in any of the regular lighting modes.

It's pretty bright for a single cell CR123/16340 light and the XP-L LED has a very nice, almost "neutral" tint to it. I certainly wouldn't call it "cool white".

It's very small, has a strong pocket clip, and will almost disappear into your pocket or bugout bag for easy everyday carry use.

The only reason I gave this light 4 stars is because of the slightly protruding tail switch...which pretty much renders it useless for tail-standing. IF YOU ARE VERY PATIENT you can make it tail-stand, but it needs to be on a completely flat surface and even then, it stands like the leaning tower of Pisa!

text:
[[VIDEOID:20f53798200ca7c997f1d2fa7d3ce6d4]] I am comparing this massager with Shiatsu Neck & Back Massager Pillow by LiBa. They are about the same size. They both come with home AC charger and car charger. Both are them are sold for the same price.

Pro:
- Xtreme massager comes with a carrying case.
- It also comes with 2 belts, one shorter, and one longer for different part of body, I guess the shorter one can be for your arm, neck or your legs, The longer one can be for holding the unit on your waist.
- I can carry the unit with the belt on my waist and use it in the kitchen when I am doing dishes or something like that. I don't have to be sit down and doing nothing.

Cons:
- The massage heads are smaller than the Shiatsu massager and the spacer between the head are also smaller. In another word, it gives me a closer rub on the neck, feel like 2 thumbs giving the massage. However, it is not as good as the Shiatsu massager for back massage as you can only feel the 2 thumbs because the massage heads are too close to each other. The Shiatsu massager gives a better massage coverage as the massage heads spread out so you don't have to keep moving the machine left and right for uncovered sored tissue.
- The Shiatsu massager automatically changes direction each minute to put pressure on all of your sore muscles. This unit does not have that function. You can change massage direction from the on/off switch (clockwise / counter clockwise). However, I enjoy the automatically switch over much better.
- The Shiatsu massager has a 15 mins auto shutoff timer. This unit does not have auto shutoff timer.
- The Shiatsu massager has 3 year warranty when this unit provides a 90 days limited warranty.
- This unit is slightly heavier than the Shiatsu massager, I don't know exactly by how much, maybe just 1/4 lb.

Overall, I would recommend Shiatsu massager for my personal preference. I would give this one 3.5 star. I purchased this product at a reduced price to complete and post a factual review without compensation. If you find this review helpful, please click yes for helpful. Thank you.

title: Good-bye bayou mosquitos and bats.  Hello Skin-so-Soft.
text:
I'm such a mosquito magnet that, when my husband and I walk our two Yorkies in the Houston evening in a neighborhood. No matter how hot it is, I wear long sleeves and long pants on these lovely, relaxing walks because we're 1 block from a small lake (bayou-fed mosquito heaven), and tthe BATS that live in the old-growth oaks swoop down at me and the halo of mosquitoes that circle my head, my legs, my feet. That's right, swooping bats. Mosquito halos. West Nile Virus, here we come.

I like to sit out in our backyard for a while in the daytime on a bench beneath our weeping willow. I get my Vitamin D, my dogs get some exercise running around trying to make all the dogs in the neighborhood crazy by starting a chain letter of barking. But my backyard is also near that bayou and, although there are no bats in the daytime, there are mosquitoes 10 out of 12 months each year. The really deadly tiny ones think it's a game to bite me THROUGH MY CLOTHES. West Nile Virus, here we come. I won't use sprays because aerosol mist chokes me, and non-aerosol sprays have to be smoothed on by hand. Thus one quick wipe at an itchy eye and I'm blinded from the pain.

My dear departed sister sold Avon, so I was familiar with the company line but always believed that DEET was my only solution. I tried other, more "natural" products (candles, wristbands, salves with herbs that supposedly stink to mosquitos). They stink to me, too. I usually use Sawyer's lotion and then wash the palm sides of my hands. It works great if I'm going out for several hours, but I prefer not to over-expose to DEET if possible.

So this year, I thought I'd listen to my sis and give Avon a try for outings lasting less than two hours. All of my outings between late March and early January last less that two hours. Big surprise. SKIN-SO-SOFT WORKS AND IT SMELLS GOOD. No zooming bats whirring by my ears (although the mosquitoes still halo my smallest Yorkie, but her hair is thicker than a black bear's).

So, if you hate to slather in chemicals and don't plan on being out all day or all night, give this a try. You'll be very pleasantly surprised and smell pretty good, too.

title: Beautiful Piece of Equipment, But...
text:
I have to say, this really is a beautiful, well made, well thought out piece of equipment. However, it did not come with instructions on how to work the non-traditional locking levers. It took a bit to figure those out, but we finally did (**instructions will be at the end of this review). And, *it should come with stipulations on user physical size limitations. In addition, it DID NOT come with and sanitary disposable covers, though it lists those as a selling feature. I purchased this for a friend who had detached retina surgery. Unfortunately, this device will not work for someone who is on the shorter side with a pudgy middle section. She is about 5'3" and maybe 250 pounds. She was not able to bend at the middle section enough to be able to lay her head in the post surgery required head position. It just would not work. We did set it up under the mattress as a trial, so she would be able to lay flat on her abdomen with her face in the cushion to sleep. That worked well. It was easy to set-up. We also finally grabbed an adjustable height table, so that she could lower it enough to be able to bend over at her mid-section (without the provided chest cushion as her weight prevented use of that), to be able to place her head bent over and flat in the face cushion. But, that required that she had to sit on the very edge of a chair, not back and comfortable. A position she could never maintain for 5 minutes, much less, 7 to 14 days as was required post surgery.

title: Flax seed oil has countless benefits
text:
I have been taking flax seed oil supplements for years now. Since I began taking it, my energy has improved, it helps with my constipation and just makes me feel better overall. This Number One Nutrition flax seed oil supplement is very high quality -it's organic, the gels are easy to swallow and have no aftertaste or side effects. Flax seed oil has countless benefits. I researched and highlighted some of these great benefits below:

Flaxseed Oil also known as Linseed oil, has a rich source of healing compounds and has been cultivated for more than 7000 years. First cultivated in Europe, the plant's brown seeds were regularly used to prepare balms for inflamed skin and healing slurries for constipation. Rich in essential fatty acids, or EFAs, flaxseed oil is used to prevent and treat heart disease and to relieve a variety of inflammatory disorders and hormone-related problems, including infertility.

A source of fiber for linen fabric since ancient times, the slender flax plant also boasts a long history as a healing herb. Today, flaxseeds are best known for the therapeutic oil that is derived by pressing them. Flaxseed oil has earned a solid reputation for treating a range of ailments ranging from heart disease to lupus.

The essential fatty acids (Omega oils) in flaxseed oil are one of its key healing components. EFAs are particularly valuable because the body needs them to function properly, but can't manufacture them on its own. Essential fatty acids work throughout the body to protect cell membranes, keeping them efficient at admitting healthy substances while barring damaging ones.

One of the EFAs in flaxseed oil, alpha-linolenic acid, is known as an omega-3 fatty acid. Like the omega-3s found in fish, it appears to reduce the risk of heart disease and numerous other ailments.

Flaxseed oil is an excellent source of omega-3s: Just 1 teaspoon contains about 2.5 grams, equivalent to more than twice the amount most people get through their diets. Flaxseeds also contain omega-6 fatty acids in the form of linoleic acid; omega-6s are the same healthy fats found in vegetable oils.

Flaxseed oil only contains these alpha-linolenic acid (Omega 3 oils), and not the fiber or lignan components that the whole plant contains. Therefore, flaxseed oil provides the Omega 3 benefits, such as lipid-lowering properties, but not the laxative or anti-cancer properties.

Whole flaxseeds (not the extracted oil) are a rich source of lignans (phytoestrogens), substances that appear to positively affect hormone-related problems. Lignans may also be useful in preventing certain cancers and combating specific bacteria, fungi, and viruses, including those that cause cold sores and shingles.

Potential health benefits of Flaxseed Oil:

Lowering cholesterol, protecting against heart disease and controling high blood pressure

Several studies indicate that flaxseed oil, as well as ground flaxseed, can lower cholesterol, thereby significantly reducing the risk of heart disease. Taking it may also protect against angina (chest pain) and high blood pressure. In addition, a five-year study done recently at Boston's Simmons College found that flaxseed oil may be useful in preventing a second heart attack. It may also help prevent elevated blood pressure by inhibiting inflammatory reactions that cause artery-hardening plaque and poor circulation.

Countering inflammation associated with gout, lupus and fibrocystic breasts

Omega-3 fatty acids appear to limit the inflammatory reaction associated with these conditions. In cases of lupus, flaxseed oil not only reduces inflammation in the joints, skin and kidneys, but also lowers cholesterol levels that may be elevated by the disease. Taking flaxseed oil for gout may lessen the often sudden and severe joint pain or swelling that is a symptom of this condition. In addition, the ability of omega-3 fatty acids to boost the absorption of iodine (a mineral often found in low levels in women suffering from fibrocystic breasts) makes flaxseed oil potentially valuable for treating this often painful condition.

Controling constipation, hemorrhoids, diverticular disorders and gallstones

As they are high in dietary fiber, ground flaxseeds can help ease the passage of stools and thus relieve constipation, hemorrhoids and diverticular disease. In those with diverticular disease, flaxseeds may also keep intestinal pouches free of waste and thus keep potential infection at bay. Taken for inflammatory bowel disease, it can help to calm inflammation and repair any intestinal tract damage. In addition, the oil may prevent painful gallstones from developing and even dissolve existing stones.

Treating acne, eczema, psoriasis, sunburn and rosacea

The essential fatty acids in flaxseed oil are largely responsible for its skin-healing powers. Red, itchy patches of eczema, psoriasis and rosacea often respond to the EFA's anti-inflammatory actions and overall skin-soothing properties. Sunburned skin may heal faster when treated with the oil as well. In cases of acne, the EFAs encourage thinning of the oily sebum that clogs pores.

Promoting healthy hair and nails

The abundant omega-3 fatty acids in flaxseed oil have been shown to contribute to healthy hair growth (in fact, low levels of these acids may cause dry and lackluster locks). Hair problems exacerbated by psoriasis or eczema of the scalp may respond to the skin-revitalizing and anti-inflammatory actions of flaxseed oil as well. Similarly, the oil's EFAs work to nourish dry or brittle nails, stopping them from cracking or splitting.

Minimising nerve damage that causes numbness and tingling as well as other disorders

The EFAs in flaxseed oil assist in the transmission of nerve impulses, making the oil potentially valuable in treating conditions of numbness and tingling. The oil's nerve-nourishing actions may also help in the treatment of Parkinson's disease, a degenerative disorder of the nervous system, and protect against the nerve damage associated with diabetes and multiple sclerosis.

Reducing cancer risk and guard against the effects of ageing

The lignans in flaxseed appear to play a role in protecting against breast, colon, prostate, and perhaps skin cancer. Although further studies are needed, research undertaken at the University of Toronto indicates that women with breast cancer, regardless of the degree of cancer invasiveness, may benefit from treatment with flaxseed. Interestingly, the lignans may protect against various effects of ageing as well.

Treating menopausal symptoms, menstrual cramps, female infertility and endometriosis

Because the hormone-balancing lignans and plant estrogens (phytoestrogens) in flaxseed help stabilise a woman's estrogen-progesterone ratio, they can have beneficial effects on the menstrual cycle, and relieve the hot flashes of perimenopause and menopause. Flaxseed may also improve uterine function and thus treat fertility problems. In addition, the essential fatty acids in flaxseed have been shown to block production of prostaglandins, hormone like substances that, when released in excess amounts during menstruation, can cause the heavy bleeding associated with endometriosis.

Fighting prostate problems, male infertility and impotence

The EFAs in flaxseed oil may help to prevent swelling and inflammation of the prostate, the small gland located below the bladder in males that tends to enlarge with age. Symptoms of such enlargement, such as urgency to urinate, may lessen as a result. The EFAs also play a role in keeping sperm healthy, which may be of value in treating male infertility, and they can improve blood flow to the penis, a boon for those suffering from impotence.

Great, high quality flax seed oil supplement!

title: Big Technical Caveat
text:
Got this for my wife as a gift, as she is a pretty active Fitbit user, so the scale seemed like an obvious extension to that. It worked great until I made some changes to the wireless network. While it is fairly obviously stated on the box, this scale is ONLY Wireless B/G. It is not Wireless N. It is also a very nuanced Wireless B/G. If you set your AP to "just G" it won't work. If you set your AP to just 20 or just 40, it also won't work. Of course, all this took several days of fooling around to discover. I finally had to buy a [[ASIN:B007ZT23ZE ASUS (EA-N66) Dual Band N900 Ultra-Fast Wireless 3-In-1 (AP, Repeater, Ethernet Adapter) Adapter With High-Power Up To 50% more coverage]] to create a stand alone B/G network JUST for the scale.

The moral of the story is, if you don't mind having your network in B/G vs. N you aren't going to notice, but if you have anything more elaborate, you are likely going to run into issues with this scale. When its working and connected to Wifi, the Aria is an excellent product, but be aware of the limitations you are buying.

title: Wasteful & Weak
text:
I was just looking for some basic, full-sized paper towels, disposable kitchen roll to deal with everyday messes without having the obnoxious "Select-a-size" (or similar) extra perforations. What I found here was wholly disappointing.

First of all, and this is on me, these paper towels are a good deal smaller than the big squares you might remember. The listing does call out their size, but if you want full size, don't eyeball it and say "that looks good enough". It's not.

Second, and more critically, the quality of the paper towels is extremely poor. They are thin, flimsy and can't clean up much without using quite a few of them. Want to blot grease? Line a plate for fried food? Wipe down a counter? Expect to have to double or triple the sheets in order to actually get the job done, and for the "line a plate" task it's even worse because they won't fold and size nicely, one being too small and two to a layer too large. I've received disposable paper napkins from take-out places that would do as good a job or better with most of these tasks. In fact, these paper towels resemble those little napkins more than they do traditional kitchen roll, specifically the extremely thin, somewhat soft ones that tear easily at the least provocation, rather than the stiffer sorts that could actually be handy for anything other than fingers.

It seems as though the makers prioritized softness. Poorly. These things have the worst traits of paper towels and the worst traits of tissue paper, and I certainly won't be buying this flimsy uselessness ever again. If you, like me, just want decent quality, full (not "selectable") size paper towel roll, keep looking elsewhere, because this is awkward sizing and terrible quality instead.

title: Soluble Fiber Redux
text:
WHY SOLUBLE FIBER?

For all of you old enough to recall, oat bran was the craze back in the late '80s. The claim was that soluble fiber intake reduces bad blood cholesterol, and oat bran contains such fiber.

WHY?

For me, the answer as to why soluble fiber reduced cholesterol, was provided by the TV-lecture version of Covert Bailey's book "Fit or Fat" which was all over PBS in the mid '90s.

There he explained that bile was essentially soap which the body created to make fatty foods disolve in water. As the digestion process finished using the bile, it would retrieve and recycle it. However, adding soluble fiber to the mix would bind with the bile, and cause the body to dump it instead of reuse it. Therefore, the body would then have to make new bile to replace that which was just discarded. Bile and cholesterol are produced by the same biological building blocks, and when given the choice between making one or the other, the body puts the priority on making bile.

THIS PRODUCT:

This product is a very fine white powder. It disolves quite well in warm water, and quite poorly in cold water. Each scooper full is 3.3 grams. I take 2 scoops in a small amount of warm water each morning, typically around 8:30am. Its effect is consistent and distinct. By 4pm comes significant intestinal gas, soon followed by the natural outcome which would otherwise invariably wait until early the next morning. The downside to this is that I'm often not at home at 4pm. The upside is that my sleep is no longer interrupted by Mother Nature loudly calling at 5:30am, which is highly frustrating. This is a major upside.

As for my LDL and triglycerides levels, I will have to wait until my next blood panel is performed to see if this product has helped in that regard.

Of the half dozen different TENS units I've recently been checking out
this one is the most common sense, user friendly - in several ways.

This is a TENS + EMS Unit. The first 16 modes are TENS > the last 8 EMS.
The size (5" T - 2 1/2" W) allows for a larger, easier to view screen (3 1/4" T - 1 3/4" W)
which allows for the 6 main mode icons also much larger.

EACH button is for ONE CHOICE (not multiple commands)
>>> There's no joy button to have to figure out how it works. (Thank You!)
> The power button and separate screen lock button are on the side. (like a cell ph)
> One (center) button chooses back and forth between channel A & B
> One button 'M' is the mode = and continually pressing it moves you one mode number
at a time = through all 24 modes of the six main mode icons. Then starts over.
> One button "T" - each press is 10 min (up to 90 min)
> One button '+" for more intensity = 20 levels
> One button "-" for less intensity = 20 levels
>>> I found this getting intense at level 6, don't think I could go very much more.

And to boot - this is a richer / classier design which is handsome on all sides
including the back which is all black with the company name.

Includes - 4 channel unit
Six sets of electrodes
Four snap leads - each include Velcro band
Charging cable (no wall plug)
Storage bag = kinda tight fit for all pieces.
Instructions.

PS = these electrodes & leads fit and work with two other TENS units I have.
I'd give this unit more than five star if I could.

title: Fully mature birds with no active new feather growth do best. I have found that birds who have a ...
text: I have run a couple dozen birds through this thing now.  As others have noted, the scald is very important.  So is the age of the chicken and stage of molt.  Fully mature birds with no active new feather growth do best.  I have found that birds who have a lot of new sheaths growing in are harder to get plucked, sometimes impossible.  Then only hand plucking can get them cleaned.  But for fully mature birds who are not in molt, it does quite well.  In my experience, more than two chickens at a time is too heavy.  The one turkey I tried to pluck didn't go so well.  It seems the bird was too heavy to keep the drum spinning freely, even though it was a wild turkey and didn't seem that large to me. Overall, I'm glad I bought this and it does save a lot of effort during harvesting of multiple birds.

title: Accurate and useful gadget
text:
This thing works as described. I was pretty skeptical at first, but after checking the readings against UV index websites, it seemed to be accurate. One thing to note is that the settings for cumulative exposure are very sensitive - I'm pretty pale and burn easily, but I ended up setting it to 6 or 7 because lower levels it would alert me that I'd met my total exposure within a few minutes on a sunny day. It definitely takes some time to figure out what your level of tolerance is and to set it accordingly. Overall, I'm very happy to have it and it's simple to use.

For those reviewers who say it doesn't work because they tested it through glass - UV waves do not penetrate glass, so you're going to get a UV index of 1 inside a car. This shows that it's working properly, not a flaw.

title: Rotates both clockwise and counterclockwise at the same time!
text:
I have been looking for a "counter-rotating" face brush and researching for a brush that actually rotates both clockwise and counterclockwise at the same time is not that easy to find since you really have to look at the description and the definition of counter-rotation is different for those products which is frustrating.

This product just that that--the brush and other heads rotate both clockwise and counterclockwise at the same time which is sooo amazing! This is comparable to another expensive product (Ageloc) that does that same function but that other product does not have actual brushes as an alternative head attachment.

This face brush comes with 3 head attachments which lets you choose how much depth you want the brush to clean your face. I love that it has a timer for 1 minute so you know if you're over-doing the face cleaning. It has 2 settings, normal speed and faster speed which is good as well to give you choices. I also like that it is not battery operated, and the charge lasts for days!

I really want exfoliation so I use this with an SA Cleanser and it just does the job. I also use it for 3 minutes for face and neck so if you don't want too much exfoliation, just do 1 minute and use the soft of the head for sensitive skin. In the first few days of using it, I can feel my skin exfoliating, of course, if you don't want to exfoliate too much, don't overdo it! And the longer I use it, the softer I felt my skin is. I think that cleaning it with this product opens up the pores and makes it easier for your skin products to get absorbed.

Overall, I am so happy that I was able to find this product which a lot of research and reading other products. I hope they add more brush heads that we can buy. The good thing is that, we can buy just replacement heads for this product which is great!

title: Awesome beginners set!
text:
I am in love with this entire set! As a beginner this set was inviting, and was easy to use without being too much. It came with quite a few things, making this set a good deal for the price.

The cuffs and collar are lined with fur, so they are comfortable to wear. They are thick and feel very durable. They have a short length of chain so there’s a small amount of mobility for the person wearing them. The cuffs can be removed by the person wearing them, if wanted or needed, which is awesome for beginners. The leash for the collar seems a bit flimsy, I don’t know how well it would hold up if pulled with force.

The whip is a bit stingy as the tassels are slim and light. It takes a good amount of force to produce any sensation from this as it is very lightweight. Maybe if the tassels were tied together it would give it more force. The ball gag is breathable, but not very comfortable. It seems durable enough to hold up for a while. It had a factory smell so I soaked mine in strong brewed, cold tea for a couple days and it went away. The blindfold is thin and lined with fur, it’s decently comfortable, but I’m unsure of how long it will hold up.

I cannot comment on how well the rope held up as I am a beginner and not yet confident enough for rope play, however, it is thick and feels as though it would hold up well.

Overall this is a great beginners set, both for the price and amount of items given. I am very happy with this set and highly recommend it.

**I received this product for a deep discount for testing and reviewing purposes. This review is of my own, honest and unbiased opinion after testing this product.

title: Fantastic, I love this thing!!!
text:
I misplaced my old non-collapsable shoe horn while I was deer hunting. And I'm glad I did!
I love this shoe horn. I was surprised by the number of one-star reviews though. All of them seemed
to be baffled by the spring. The spring is an important part of this shoe horn. With a handle
this long you'd be falling over with how far you'd have to lean back to get the horn in place
and reach down and back to use the horn. I find it a dream to use. I'm 6'2" and for some reason,
I always have trouble with the back of left shoe collapsing. I've used a shorter shoe horn for
quite some time (about 14 inches long). But this one has that one beat hands down. Even
with my height. I don't have to bend or lean at all. The spring at the end of the shoe horn
helps a lot because even though the horn itself is at an angle to start. The handle can flex
at the spring. And I don't have to lean or bend. It's great! I don't understand why so many people
report problems because of the spring. I'm guessing they're shoving it too far under their foot.
You can't put it under your foot up to your toes. But you can get your shoe on with ease.
And it's far easier to travel with. It's collapsed length makes it easy to pack in very nearly any bag
you might carry. And it's strong. My old fixed length plastic was always a hassle. And I was always
worried I was going to break it while on the road while trying to get it to fit in a bag.
I've tried to abuse this thing. And it can take it. The handle is more than strong enough.

title: Works as advertised but maybe not as great if you have facial hair, needs a replacement filter version.
text:
I just started using the Smoke Buddy a couple of days ago, but so far I'm really pleased. Hubby and I are both smokers, so I've been trying to find a way to reduce smoke smell and dust in our home. This definitely will help. When you exhale smoke into it, nothing comes out the other end, the filter captures everything. I can see where having to repurchase them frequently might be a pain, but it's so effective that I think I will keep buying them. Not sure what I'll do with the large collection of key chains over time, lol :).

Pros: Eliminates all exhaled smoke entirely. That's a HUGE pro. It works exactly as described.

Cons so far: 1) You have to exhale the smoke pretty hard to get it to go through the filter, something to get used to but not a huge issue. 2) Hubby has a goatee and mustache. He reports that for him he can't get a good seal around his mouth due to this, so quite a bit of smoke "leaks" out around the edges, and as a result he probably will not use one often if at all. 3) Frequent replacement for heavy smokers expected. I would LOVE to see a version of this that allows the user to replace filter cartridges rather than having to replace the entire thing.

title: Best option on the market for zero waste deoderant
text:
I really like the smell and sustainable packaging. Going zero waste is a huge goal of mine, and this was a step in the right direction.
I don't know if I'll be reordering this one though. It's a weird balance between not wanting to get my fingers all weird and covered in the deoderant and it feeling super hard against my skin. Like it's hard to spread, it doesn't go on well at all. Feels dry. But if it were softer, it would probably be too messy.
Also, I know that no natural deodorants work as antiperspirants but I really wish they could figure it out. I don't just want to *not stink*. I also like to be dry, because having damp pits is the pits.
It's also a little hard to store. My solution has been putting it back in the box in between uses, but that's cumbersome.
I don't know what the solution is- a reusable wood holder to keep your fingers clean? A storage container other than the carton?
I think this is 100% the best option on the market for zero waste deoderant, but I'll say it's not perfect yet.

title: It's A Sleep Mask
text:
I have extreme dry eye (Blepharitis) and because we sleep with a fan my eye doctor has suggested I sleep with a sleep mask that completely covers my eyes. I have multiple cotton sleep masks (all the same one) that I really like because I can wash them in the washing machine after every wear. This is important with eye problems because keeping the face and eyes clean is crucial.

In the past I have looked at some other very expensive ($100) silk sleep masks that look exactly like my cotton masks, but have decided against them because I am happy with the system I have. This silk mask costs $59, so I decided to try it.

First, it is exactly like my cotton masks. It has velcro in the back and the front is wider with a lip that goes over the nose. A very standard sleep mask. I have found that, like my cotton masks, it does not block all the light coming from the nose area, but I also have found this really does not matter. I usually wear this at night when it is very dark anyhow and when I wear it to nap during the day we have room darkening curtains, so it is really dark in our bedroom. The mask is just to protect my eyes.

This silk mask does go through the washing machine fine. I hung it on the line to dry and as promised it came out okay.

Here is the thing, I don't think this is real silk. It might be a silk blend, but silk feels smooth and mulberry silk, when it is squashed in the hand it will wrinkle, a lot, and it will make a very distinct crunching noise. There is a reason why the other silk sleep masks I have looked at cost over $100. Silk is expensive.

I looked up Tara Sartoria and they have a pretty good story going with their notes and their videos, but they have stores on Etsy, Amazon, Facebook, Instagram and wholesale sale offers directly on their website. This is not a small operation.

You can save your money and buy an identical and softer cotton mask.

title: For Me - Instant Relief That Lasts Hours
text:
I have degenerative arthritis in my neck and spine and my husband has a number of still point inducers and traction devices that I have tried over the years and none of them have really worked. I use a heating pad and do physical therapy exercises four or five times a day. My neck flexibility depends on the weather and how good I am about doing my exercises. As my PT says "you get out of it what you put into it". I know, I know.

When I first saw ChiroLux Curv my immediate thought was that it was just another traction/still point device. I thought that I would try it and it would work just okay. They all work just okay. ChiroLux Curv is different. ChiroLux Curv is really different.

First ChiroLux Curv is firm. Most of the still point devices I have used (especially the ones my husband prefers) are foam or softer moldable rubber. They have quite a bit of give. The ChiroLux Curv is hard(er). It has very little give. When I put my full weight on it I can feel it and it is not entirely comfortable. It feels like I am doing the exercises my PT has me do, but I am doing them at level 25 instead of level 5.

Second, ChiroLux Curv is adjustable. There are levels that can be removed so if there is too much traction or pressure, simply take out a level (the levels just pop on and off) and the ChiroLux Curv is instantly shorter making the traction less powerful.

Last, there is no smell. I was really expecting there to be some sort of smell (you know the one, right?), but there is absolutely zero odor.

The directions are simple: place the block under your neck with the curve going toward your feet. Adjust the ChiroLux Curv so the bump is in the middle of your neck and relax your head. I find relief almost instantly and it lasts for hours.

title: Works Excellently - Super Expensive
text:
Let's face it, hot flashes are not fun. I started peri-menopause last year and the hot flashes started to ramp up a few months ago. Getting old is an interesting journey.

I have used a lot of different icepacks and they work, but none of them really seem to help solve the problem. This pack feels different. I wear it over a t-shirt and usually under a thin sweatshirt or fleece. Typically I wear it in the evening before I go to bed because I find that if I cool my temperature off at night I sleep better.

I have found that if I keep this pack in the freezer I can use it for a little over an over and it does stay really cold. It is not overwhelmingly cold, but it is comfortingly cold. The claim that it pulls heat away from your body is really true. There is no other way to describe it. It is the strangest feeling to suddenly feel like your body temperature is dropping. It is pleasant.

The one drawback is the cost. At $139, I am not sure what makes this that much better than two very large gel ice packs other than the shape. Unless I had unlimited amounts of money I am not sure I would spend that much.

I live in Michigan where the temperature is starting to get colder, but I know that next summer I will be using the heck out of this pack.

title: Good Design For Dry Eye Sleepers
text:
My eyes are extremely dry and I struggle at night. I use a very thick eye lotion -sounds weird, but it helps- and eye masks help to keep me from rubbing my eyes at night. I have found some eye masks are better than others.

The masks I really like are the super soft masks that cover most of the top of my face. I have also found the masks that irritate my eyes the most are the super soft masks that cover most of the top of my face. They work really well, but for some reason, they aggravate my eyes a lot.

This mask, first of all, blocks all the light. When I put it on it is completely dark. It is easy to adjust and it is comfortable. It is all black with no design, so it is a simple and appropriate grown up sleep mask.

I hand washed it before I used it and hung it on the line to dry before I first used it and it dried within a couple hours. Simple. I wash my masks once or twice a week because my eyes are very sensitive.

This mask is firm, but comfortable. It did not cut into my face and after a little adjustment was easy to sleep with. I did wake up with sleep mask face, but I always wake up with sleep mask face. This mask, I noticed, gives my eyes some breathing room, which is so nice because I put my drops in and then stick my mask on and having a mask pressing against wet eyes is never pleasant.

I like this mask and for the price is one I could easily have a few of to rotate around while I wash them to protect my eyes while I sleep.

title: Recent Cubital Tunnel transposition surgery?  Forget it!
text:
I was diagnosed with severe Cubital Tunnel Syndrome after my ring finger and little finger turned numb all of the sudden and couldn't control them while typing on the computer keyboard. It unknowingly and very slowly progressed over years. I had to have the radial nerve, aka funny bone, moved from within the cubital tunnel in the elbow to relieve nerve pressure. I purchase this splint for the primary purpose of using it to keep my arm stable so my surgery wound (about 4.5 inches long) would heal faster.

This thing is cumbersome! Sure, the plastic is stiff to keep your arm at the proper angle. However, when the straps are tightened, the elbow moves within the splint. The wound would become irritated rubbing against material. The worst part is that one of the straps would be right over the stitches irritating them. I knew right away this wasn't going to work. Bottom line, it may help if you have a mild / moderate case to help delay surgery. My doctor, an orthopedic specialist in hand and upper arms extremities said splints are "delay devices" because Cubital Tunnel syndrome will NEVER improve...it guaranteed to get worse over time. And take it from me, don't wait to have it examined! If you think that keeping your arm in a certain position will improve your ailment...it won't! As a patient, I don't recommend it as an effective after-surgery splint at all.

Update: I purchased two of the Corflex Elbow Bursitis Pads after I returned the splint. I purchase these from the same seller "The Therapy Connection" since they were nice enough to accept a return. These pads are excellent for cushioning the elbow, provide adjustable compression with adjustable velcro elbow straps. It spreads completely open to put on without pulling over the forearm. It has an open area on the inside of the elbow which doesn't crunch-up the material when purposely flexing for exercise. I found it to be excellent at providing enough tension at night, keeping the elbow straight while sleeping (because the last thing I need is to irritate and reopen the wound by having my arm in all kinds of contortions. I highly recommend this product instead of the bulky splint. You'll need to order 2, they only come one per package.

title: Delta Elevated White Toilet Seat DF574W by Liberty Hardware Mfg. Corp.
text:
I purchased the Delta Elevated Toilet Seat at a local discount home decor store that sounds like Moss. I purchased the item for $14.99 plus 7% tax.

The product was cumbersome to install, and you will need tools (Phillips screw driver, 1/4" straight blade screwdriver, & pliers) to install it properly.

This item is best installed by someone who is familiar with the make up of bathroom fixtures. This was a super buy.

I wanted an elevated seat for the bathroom bowl because I started to have significant mobility issue with my knees and back. I am also 5'11 and most seats are simply too low for my frame.

The product raises the seat to a very comfortable level of 4" and ADA height. It has locking hardware that must be installed.

It also has sturdy support handles that hold weight pressure of around 200 lbs. without sliding. The front opening provides easy access, and there is ample space between the two handles.

I actually feel as though I am not bending at all. The product comes with a 10 year warantee. I was unable to decipher the installation directions for the locking hardware.

However, I positioned the seat over the existing toilet seat and it fits rather well and it stays safely in place.

I understand that this is not the mfg suggested recommendation for installation, but I am comfortable with this use.

However, I do not recommend this for someone who has a sever handicap or serious balance issues--please follow the mfg recommendations.

I give this product 5/5 for appearance, 5/5 for function, 5/5 for durability, and 4/5 for installation difficulty.

The product is also light weight and easy to maneuver.

title: More than I Bargained For
text:
I'd been using the Fitbit One with great success for 6 months, dropping over 25 pounds...and one day, our Health-o-Meter digital scale just stopped working. Since I was already using a Fitbit One and am familiar with the Fitbit online dashboard, the Aria has been a no-brainer replacement for my old scale.

The Hardware
In some ways, the glass top makes the Aria seem fragile, as does its slim height. However, this thing is heavy, and feels fairly solid on the inside. The Aria is also pretty bulky, larger than any other scale I've owned.

The Software
Setting up the Fitbit Aria is incredibly simple. The instructions are in the box, and in my case the wireless setup went exactly as the instructions indicated, without a hitch. Not all Amazon reviewers have been this lucky, so be aware that depending on your network you may encounter some issues.

Once connected, the Fitbit Aria will sync your weight and body fat to 'the cloud': a Fitbit dashboard utility that is free. You can read this information in a browser and also install supporting software on your PC, Mac, or mobile phone. You can do all sorts of things with the information, such as start logging your food and exercise and make the Aria part of your weight control plan, but in my case it just gets lumped in with the Fitbit One data I was already using. Other people in the house can use the scale as much as they like without having an account, or you can have the Fitbit send them a setup e-mail that will start tracking their weight: up to 8 different people can have this feature.

The Readings
So let's talk for a moment about the accuracy. Since my old scale was broken, it's hard to be 100% sure they would match up, but it seems to be reading about the same weight as my old digital scale. I've seen no reason to doubt the weight readings.

The body fat though is a different story. I've learned how to use a pair of calipers to do the 'pinch test' of body fat percentage, a process that requires some time and a partner: pinch several places, jot down the numbers, run them through an online calculator. The Aria skips all this hassle and uses electrostatic technology to 'read' your body fat in a few seconds. I've noticed it can be about a percentage off from my pinch measurements, and it is affected by other factors. If I've had a lot of water to drink but it's because I just did a ton of cardio and sweated a lot off, I might see the body fat reading go up...which can't be right if I haven't eaten since the last measurement and I've just been drinking water. If I'm wet from the shower, that also tends to change the reading. My conclusion is it's best to step on the Fitbit dry and naked at the beginning of the day. If you want to take readings more often, expect the numbers of both body fat and weight to move around. Long term, you'll see if you're on an upward or downward trend, and I've even had days where I lose a pound but gain a percent.

For You
It's important to remember that your goals are long-term and not worry about every day. Step on the scale at the same time every day, but think about the numbers in weeks or even months. The Body Fat is a nice measurement to keep you thinking about how much fat you take in and how much you burn, but don't rely on the Aria to be super-precise: be happy with the fact that it's still pretty good.

Conclusion:
The Fitbit Aria is a bit pricey for digital scales, but if you're looking for a way to lump in a lot of information, the online aspect is a big extra that the Fitbit brings to the table. If you're already used to Fitbit devices, you'll find this integrates into the dashboard really well.

title: Blends Romance, Faith and Eerie Spiritual Conflict
text:
Journey by the Sackcloth Moon introduced me to a new world, the world of Native American culture and spirituality. Young Christian Cherokee/Seminole Dina Youngblood, Pastor Aaron Burning Rain and Marty Osceola are a romantic triangle caught in a web of deceit and deep spiritual conflict. The verse that kept coming to me over and over again was Ephesians 6:11-12 "Put on the full armor of God so that you can take your stand against the devil's schemes. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms." This battle is portrayed in a way I have personally not read or experienced. K. B. Shaller knows the culture and the struggles of being a follower of "The Jesus Way" in Native American culture. Her book is filled with very real characters, some very manipulative and troubling,others rich and uplifting. Mama Hat is one of my favorites. Her warning to Dina, "Don't dance too close to the fire," hit home in my spirit.
The Christian characters in this book are very real and imperfect, sometimes making choices that lead to more difficulties, like the people I know and love, like the person I am, imperfect, fallen, forgiven and seeking to grow.

Journey by the Sackcloth Moon is an intriguing, sometimes troubling, and ultimately rewarding novel. You will not be disappointed.

The foam earplugs blocked too much sound (the Sena music as well as emergency vehicle sirens). So I picked these up and they are perfect!

They let in just enough sound to where I can hear my music perfectly, but still manage to muffle the exhaust and wind noise. I can also hear emergency vehicle sirens much better. I also noticed that I can hear higher frequency notes of my engine that I never noticed before. The included case is nice and well-built. I love that they do not stick out of your ears far, which makes them easy to wear under a helmet.

My only gripes are that sometimes when they get sweat on them, they refuse to stay in my ears and I have to dry them off to get them to stay properly. Also, because the stems are short, when removing them from my ears, sometimes I pull the little "filter" piece out instead of the actual earplug. This is only a minor inconvenience and I just have to "dig deeper" on the plug when I pull them out.
