title: This ozone generator won't kill any mold.
text:
This ozone unit won't kill any mold.
It will just give you a sore throat.

Technical data on testing:
The Berry Breeze (originally the Ozonator $50) generates ozone through a high voltage corona discharge. I measured the voltage at just over 4000 volts.
It puts out a peak 0.8 ppm ozone in the first 48 to 52 minutes; solid green LED.
It then goes into stand by for 195 minutes; blinking green LED.
Then it runs for 8 minutes. Thereafter in 203 minutes it generates ozone for 8 minutes or 8/203 (4% of the time).
This is why the 50 hour batteries can last for months.
The 1/2 life of ozone at 0 degrees C (32 F) is only 300 seconds.
The total time to decay back to stable O2 oxygen is 15 minutes.
In a standard 21 cubic refrigerator (.61 cubic meters) that 8 minute run time generates only 0.4 ppm, for a few minutes. This is not enough ozone concentration to kill anything.

Therefore the statement: "Because Berry Breeze slowly release O3 into your refirgerator, food decompostition comes to a grinding hault - preventing them from molding and rotting. "
Is FALSE. Did you notice the 3 typos?

To kill bacteria you need .25 to 2.29 ppm for 20 minutes.
To kill viruses you need .2 to 4.1 ppm for 30 minutes.
To kill mold you need 3.0 to 5.0 ppm for 60 minutes.
To kill fungi you need .02 to .26 ppm for 1.67 minutes.

So I put the unit into the crisper drawer: this works much better. The peak ozone was 2.5 ppm and decayed to 0 in 4 minutes, enough to kill fungi, but nothing else.

Then I put the unit into a 5 gallon bucket (21 liter) and sealed the lid. This produced 19.7 ppm. The decay time was 100 minutes, because it was airtight.
The only way to kill everything is to put the unit in a small airtight container, like the Rubbermaid Commercial Products, Plastic Space Saving Square Food Storage Container for Kitchen/Sous Vide/Food Prep, 12 Quart, Clear

Ozone density is 2.14 kg/m^3 or 2.14 g/l or .00214 mg/l = 1 ppm.
The unit generated a total .885 mg of ozone in the 48 minute runtime, which calculates to 1.138 mg/hour.
This is 4.5% of the published 25 mg/hour for the "Ozonator" identical unit.

I also tested the dissolved ozone in water in the refrigerator using 0 to .5 ppm test strips: after the full 52 minute runtime, in the refrigerator crisper drawer, it measured 0 ppm in an open glass of water.

I noticed that during all testing I had an irritating sore throat that lasted for hours.
All testing done in a sealed refrigerator or sealed bucket. It only takes a brief inhalation when snapping the cover on to start the ozone to cause a sore throat.

Ozone senor used: ME2-O3 (0-100) 21K19D-0136

title: Included Instructions are good for a laugh, but not much else!
text:
I bought this for my daughter so I won't comment on how well it works, or doesn't... she hasn't tried it yet. But the included instructions read like an old Hollywood comical stereotype of a Chinese tourist trying to speak English for the first time. They consist of a fold-out with 7 numbered pages, yet the "contents" lists all 7 sections as appearing on "Page 1".

The first question my wife asked was whether you use it on dry hair or wet... the instructions don't say. Kind of a key point, I would think! Some samples from the instructions with my comments in ():
"More Generally, hair hanging in the temperature 210-190 degrees..."
"Please use the power button to bower (sic) on hold for 3 seconds to boot..." (you boot a computer, not a hair styler)
"Fast Hair Straightener use a different direction, for personal use, with the personal habits."
"The hair care products need to be cleaned because residues"

Now here is my favorite (no personal injury suits in China, I guess):
"we recommend that you begin to choose the highest amount (temperature), then according to the hair to reduce the temperature level. (of course in the US, we would always say start at the lowest temperature and adjust upward, to avoid getting sued for burns and hair damage.)

Finally, if you want to sell a product in the US, you might want to consider that we do not use Celsius... except in labs. At the least offer a way to toggle the setting.

Bottom line, while I'm not speaking directly to the quality of the product, if the engineering comes anywhere close to the quality of the instructions, it will probably be a waste of money.

title: Exquisitely made, and very beautiful!
text:
Shopping for an urn can be difficult, especially when you're not really sure where to turn to. However, and with unexpected gratitude, I found this urn on Amazon (of all places), and once again discovering they really do carry just about anything you could ever think of.

My beautiful bride and best friend had just passed away after a long illness. Cremation was both of our wishes in early conversations, but I really had no idea that I would be having to prepare for this event in such a short time -- we had only been married for 8 1/2 years. Yet, I knew that I wanted to find something that would be suitable, beautiful, and representative of the kind of person she was. When I said "I do," I was also blessed with 3 wonderful step-kids that are the greatest gift she could have ever given to me. So, when I saw the 3 birds, I knew right away that it would be something she would have loved because they would have represented the kids.

The urn is solid and beautifully done. The silver metal is nicely polished, and the turquoise inlays are quite nice. However, the color of the turquoise is not 'quite' as dark as is in the product photo. Still, it is beautiful, and I love it. The unit is weighty and solid. The cap fits solidly and firmly without issue. Her cremains fit well with much room to spare.

After looking through the catalog provided by the funeral home of their urns, The prices were a staggering $300 to a couple of thousand (depending). I felt no need to pay that kind of money, and my wife would have been appalled as well. So, for a little over $100, the urn is exactly what we both would have wanted. I have absolutely no regret, and the kids think it is simply beautiful -- and that counts most of all.

I've blended it with greek yogurts, milk, cabbage juice (my personal favorite), tea and on a lark I've mixed it with club soda as well. In each instance it blends completely, sometimes just taking a little bit longer depending on the clarity of the carrier. At no point was I able to ever pick up on a taste by adding it, it is utterly neutral. Which led me to my favorite way to enjoy this powder, in my daily two servings of bulletproof coffee.

title: Superb and Long Lasting
text:
My mix of shaving soaps and creams includes Taylor of Old Bond Street Mr. Taylor's Shaving Cream, Pre de Provence, Omega, Razorock XXX, and Razorock Classic. Prep Original Shaving Cream, though, is now my favorite shaving cream. Actually, Prep falls somewhere between a cream and a soap. When I first held the tub,I could hear and feel the soap moving around in the plastic tub. I was concerned the product would be overly dry. Happily, that was not the case. I prefer to lather the cream in a separate bowl and Prep is soft enough for me to dig out a few small chunks with my finger. And I do mean small chunks. A little goes a long way.

Once in the bowl, my pre-soaked badger brush quickly produces a very rich lather. It probably takes 45 to 60 seconds to make enough lather for 3 or 4 passes. I work the brush until I have a lather the consistency of beaten egg whites. Once I soap up my beard I can feel and smell the menthol, cloves, and eucalyptus. The sensation is fairly mild and quite nice.

My only knock against Prep is the ingredient list. Yes, it includes good, natural ingredients. But Prep also contains a few sketchy compounds like sodium laureth sulfate. Of course, the SLS contributes to Prep's great lather.

Bottom line: Prep is a great cream/soap; just wish it had better ingredients.

text:
I read many of the reviews for this clock, but I bought it anyway. I should have considered them carefully, but mostly I am okay with it. I like the fact that the projection is blue, rather than red, and that the colon (:) between the hours and minutes does not flash. The most annoying clock is one that constantly demands your attention, especially if you are sick in bed and not trying to focus on the time. The time saying "hey, look at me!" like the faerie in Zelda games is not helpful. Second, the projection is so bright, it has this unwanted halo around it. My old projector clock used red, but only the numbers (and ever flashing colon) were visible. This has blue numbers amid a blue cloud surrounded by a blue halo, and there's no way to turn the brightness down. Third, the front of the clock is very bright and there's no obvious way to dim it ,but I read in the Q&A section on Amazon here that it CAN be turned off, so I will be looking into that.

As for the sounds, I like them, so long as they're called Rain. The others are okay, but I love Rain. I realize it's a short loop, and I've heard better, but it works for me. You can get phone apps that do it, but I don't want to run my phone's speakers all night.

All in all, I like my new clock, but its quality does not quite measure up to its price.

title: Comfort & Joy for the decaf crowd!
text:
Being a long-term fan of RoT, I was heartbroken when I had to cut down on my caffine intake. My previous favorite Comfort & Joy was a wonderful mix of black tea & various spices, but had caffine.

Then I tried Hot Apple Cider. It's delicious, especially with sugar as opposed to honey. (Honey overwhelms the more delicate flavors of this specific tea.) HAC strongly reminds me of Comfort & Joy, but without the caffine & one or two spices. While some may dislike the lack of caffine & the longer steeping time, many will enjoy the ease in making this tea. No worries about water temperature or forgetting to take the teabag out. I've made this with several different water temperatures & I almost always forget to take the teabag out. Since this tea is almost completely herbal, there's nothing in it that grows bitter if left in too long.

I love this tea & recommend that if anyone is interested in it to buy it now. Unfortunately this well-loved tea is also one of the harder to find flavors as it sells out rather quickly & only comes around once a year!

INGREDIENTS:

Apple pieces, cinnamon, orange peel, rose hips, berry leaves, natural apple flavor, ginger root, cloves, natural lemon flavor, citric acid, cardamom seeds (and of course the tea bags are round & unbleached, making it a great fit for most mugs)

title: Careful with highest setting. Use in shower. Need finger strength to attach water lines
text:
It's light in your hands as most of water is in the cup you provide. You can use it in the shower. It made a mess of my sink, face and mirror on smaller, stronger tip the first time I used it. So my husband is using it in the shower. Don't turn it on with stronger tip unless it is in your mouth or you are in the shower.
The smaller tip was a bit too strong for me (first time using a water flosser) and second one a bit weak so I'd like one in between the two. My husband likes the stronger one. It takes some finger strength to add and remove the water lines so heads up for those with arthritis or weak hands.
If you hold it upside down under pressure of water (smaller, stronger tip) the tip can fall off.
Charges with USB cable. Nice for travel, power outages.
It came pre-charged but directions say not use until you charge it for 6-8 hours or light turns green. The light was green in under 30 minutes.
Long term? How and where do you buy more toothbrush heads. I'm not using toothbrush as I love my small, round oral b. Maybe generic sonic will fit.
I've got a tiny house so wanted to try a small handheld unit. It takes some adjustment to using the external water cup. A hard carrying case for heads and cables would be nice. It comes with a small grey bag which does not fit the charger but seller reached out and let me know the charger should last for 6 to 8 days so for any trip I'm taking the charger can stay at home. I appreciated seller reaching out when I wasn't immediately happy with concern and additional directions for using it. Based on seller reaching out to make sure I was satisfied I'm am updating this review.

These are a great product! I have rough heels, and they stay rough no matter what I do to them. I'm most comfortable walking around barefoot, so my heels have been abused. I do moisturizer, but it doesn't really tend to help. Using these heel socks gave me noticeably softer heels, though, and I loved that about them.

You moisturize your feet with your favorite cream, them sort of pull these heel socks carefully over the heels while they're still moist. They're socks on the outside, but the inside is a sort of rubberized coating on the fabric so the sock doesn't soak up the cream. This does enable the heel to stay moist and soften better than in the air, but the rubberized fabric does grip skin as you pull it up, so you sort of have to manipulate the sock into the right place. Once they're on, they're okay to walk in, as you still have your toes, but they feel funny. They're definitely more for when you've got your feet up.

title: Green Bags work well as expected to prevent ripening; why you can't expect them to kill molds and funguses.
text: They do what they say they do.  They have a finite lifetime as the absorbant material in the plastic is used up.  I should like to comment on the negative reviews that state that these bags are terrible because they do not stop mold.  These comments are based on a misapprehension of the action and purpose of the bags.  The green bags have a Zeolite clay embedded in the plastic.  The plastic, Polyethylene, is in fact, relatively porous to atmospheric and other gases.  The simple gas, ethylene, (C2H4) is a plant hormone and is given off by fruits and vegetables and this accelerates their ripening process.  The absorption of the ethylene by the clay, slows this ripening process down greatly, and thus improves the storage life of the produce significantly.  The Zeolite is NOT an antifungal, so will not kill mold.  [You and mold are both in the same Family of living things, called Eukariots, vs the bacteria (Prokariots).  Agents that kill mold can kill you, so the idea of produce bags with an antifungal is really a bad idea.  To reduce mold growth, make sure that all produce and their storage containers are very dry.  Keep refrigerator doors open as little as possible.  And never, never, never, try to salvage bread, fruits, or vegetables that are already showing any signs of mold.  Funguses release BILLIONS of spores from a single spot on a slice of bread.  Deposit moldy produce or bread containers UNOPENED into the trash bin.

title: Not great compared to other robot vaccums
text:
My husband has called me a robot vacuum hoarder. Including this Hoover, I own 4 (all different brands) this being said I have a pretty high bar when it comes to robot vacuums.

PROs of Hoover
1. Quiet. It is a lot quieter than my other 3 robot vacuums
2. Low profile. Gets under a lot of the furniture easily.
3. Easy to set up and use.

CONs
1. Not very powerful. Compared to my other robot vacuum this one does not pick up nearly as much debris from the carpets.

So if a battery died, or you had a loose connection or bad switch or whatever, you could have a totally misplaced sense of security.  The 'horn' is a whistle that is hard to hear by folks with a high frequency hearing loss--sure does not sound like 90 dB volume.  The foam case to cover the electronics box does not reveal the important things on the box, so it was apparently designed for a different box.  The mattress switches or pressure pads apparently expect you to replace them every 180 days or less.

title: Fun colors!
text:
A couple of years ago, I ended up having some swelling in my leg due to an infection from a bug bite. I was told to get compression socks as a follow-up to help the swelling if and when it ever happened again, which it likely would, especially with my job, but never really got around to it. I decided to check these out because they looked so fun. I have huge feet and large calves, particularly when this one swells, so I went for the L/XL ones.

Pros: I love the fun colors. They’re bright and make it seem like you are just wearing fun socks. So no one else has to know that you’re wearing compression socks.

Conveniently, when they arrived, I had a day where my leg decided to swell up for the first time in a while. So it was the perfect time to try them. I only left them on for up to an hour, but I did notice that swelling went down by the next day and hasn’t really gone back up. So it will be good to have these on hand and to keep trying them.

Cons: They did seem a bit small on my calves for being able to accommodate size XL. Then again, I know I have larger calves, so they would probably fit very well on other people. I also may have felt a bit sensitive to wearing them because I did try them in summer, when I don’t normally wear socks. I also have a sensory issue with things touching my feet.

I had difficulty getting them on, not so much because they were tight - I just put them on like I would nylons - but because there were a lot of threads on the inside of the sock getting in the way. I did have to cut a couple, because my toes were getting stuck otherwise.

Overall thoughts: I will likely use these again, especially when I am noticing a flare-up of the issue with my leg. It will be fun to try to coordinate them with my clothing!

I bought this because my sister-in-law overseas used it for six months and had great results. She warned me about the side effects, which were spot on! For example:

1. Take the pill (or root, if you bought that version) right after your heaviest meal.
2. Drink as much water as you can during the day. I did over a liter daily.
3. After the meal/pill, stay close to your favorite bathroom...

My personal side effects, which may vary by person:

1. Even with all the water, I got DAILY headaches.
2. I was grumpy most of the time, but that could have been a result of the bathroom runs and headaches.
3. I could not work out because my body ached all over. Although working out isn't necessarily required, it certainly expedites weight loss.
4. I didn't have stomach cramps.
5. Bathroom breaks were not out of the ordinary...

So, I stopped taking the pills because of the side effects, but I will begin again this week to see if I have similar feels. If I can tolerate the headaches, I'll continue because I believe the pills work.

I'll do a follow-up review next month.

title: Affordable multipurpose oil
text:
Lemon essential oil is a great multipurpose oil. I use it for a lot of things including diffusing, in making my own home made deodorant, in oil inhalers, and for much more. Using oil for many purposes can cause you to go through a lot of oil and it can get very expensive. I love that this oil is both high quality and affordable. I have owned several different brands of oils from all price points and I honestly don't see much difference in them other than packaging and price. The Radha oil is comparable to the very expensive multi level marketing brands that sell you a 0.5 ounce bottle for $20+. You are not paying all that money for advertising with oils that are not sold through marketing schemes. The main thing those products can boast is that they claim they are safe to ingest which does not matter to me as that is something that I would never do with any oil of any brand. The MLM brands will claim you can not be sure of purity of other oils. I am as sure of this oil as I am any beauty product, medical product, or even food product that is out there. How pure is your shampoo or body lotion? That is the types of things I use this oil for so I do not get worried by such comments.
I think this oil is great, affordable, and reliable. I own many Radha oils and I will continue to buy and use them. I was offered to purchase this particular oil discounted for sample evaluation with no obligations to return a favorable review.

title: Smoother, Softer & Looks Longer!
text:
This is a BIG 4 ounce container of beard balm. The canister it comes in is nearly the exact same size as a can of chew if that helps. I've picked up a couple of different beard balms for my husband and it's nice to know he won't go through this one as quickly. It should last him months, easily!

I love that it is unscented as well. There is no lingering odor at all. My husband couldn't stand the last one I got him as it smelled like vapor rub under his mouth and nose all day. That is not an issue with this UrbanXY brand.

To apply I just rub my index and middle finger around on the top of the open canister until I get a bit of melted balm built up on my fingers and then massage it into his beard. In manly fashion, on the other hand, my husband digs a finger into the canister and gobs some out and then rubs it into his beard. Both get the job done.

This balm takes his unruly beard and tames it, smoothing the hairs out and keeping them neatly together instead of sticking out all over the place. It also makes his goatee appear longer than it looks without the balm. I'll include pics so you can see for yourself. It also makes it easier to comb though his beard and makes it softer to the touch. Since you leave it in, this effect lasts all day until the next time his beard is shampooed. We're really not seeing long lasting benefit just yet, but the instant improvement is pretty amazing and it's become a part of his daily morning routine.

I received this beard balm free in exchange for an honest and unbiased review. All opinions are my own and were uninfluenced by price. I would happily pay full price for this item and feel completely comfortable recommending it based on our use.

title: Can be made very tight.  Hard to get on and off. Straps are MUCH too SHORT for putting on
text:
Not comfy at all, but it does work at opening up your shoulders if your shoulders curve in, you can pull them way back. It doesn't offer any support if you curve over your mid back and not just your shoulders.

The neoprene pads are a good idea as they keep the straps from cutting off your underarm circulation.

**The hardest thing is putting it on.** The straps are way too short for putting it on, so you end up contorting to get it on if you don't have help. Getting it off is easier, if you unstrap it completely. You will want to pre fasten it at the loosest setting and then try to slide it up your arms, but that only works if you're as flexible as I am, and even i had difficulties (and I can touch the middle of my back between my shoulder blades with both hands, something many people cannot do)

I will use it when I want strong shoulder pulling back, but it won't stop me slouching. I will only mostly wear this when it's too hot to wear the full back one - HailiCare Posture Corrector for Men and Women <- that one is the best of the 4 i purchased by a long, long shot.

Also a problem: the back rides up on the back of your neck, unlike the picture shown, where it sits lower. I imagine I could tug it down, if I wanted to contort myself even more, but it is hard to maneuver. The rubbing on the back on one's neck is not comfortable.

One plus: hides easily under clothing. Not bulky. Is well made.

If you are small and have narrow shoulders, this may be the right thing for you. If you're an ex swimmer with well developed shoulders (me) I would skip it. I'm 5'6", female, relatively well developed upper body.

Bottom line? more or less worth what I paid for it (8 bucks), but even at that price, the short straps make this not my favorite purchase.

title: HUGE earbuds. They do block out outside noise though.
text:
I'm using this as part of a "ghetto" in-ear monitor system (see the setup on Instructables). Other reviewers have had various quality issues, and I am in the same scenario. One speaker simply doesn't work. I'm perfectly fine with only hearing the monitor feed in one ear on stage, but I would be pretty mad if I was using these to listen to music.

Other thing you should know: the earpieces are HUGE. I have a pair of the largest Etymotic earplugs in existence, and these are actually much larger! The foam pieces are the largest earplugs I've ever seen in my life, and they don't stay "shrunk" when you roll them between your fingers (though I haven't had any problem getting them in, despite the size).

I need these for a gig, but after that, I plan to exchange these for another pair. If they are any better, I'll update my review.

UPDATE: Got the new pair, and yes, this time both earbuds actually work. They're still ridiculously huge. At band practice, I can't hear anyone speaking unless they speak into a microphone, or I take one of the earbuds out between songs (not recommended if you practice with a bunch of "noodlers").

Considering returning these and spending the extra cash on the Etymotic earbuds, since I'm very happy with their other products.

title: Not a bad product for a quick head shave, but not as close of shave as I would like.
text:
I like the product for a quick head shave, but the product does not shave as close as I would like. If you are coming from using a normal razor blade like a headblade you will find this shaver to be OK. It shaves and helps you do a quick shave, but not a close one. If you run your hand over your head you will still feel stubble. Even if I compare it to my Panasonic Arc 5 it does not shave as close.

The good points for this shaver is it is quick and feels great in your hand for shaving. It is also a good shaver for general use and has attachments to do things like eyebrows, nose hair and beard trimming (all attachments sold separately). I cannot do that with my Arc 5 or headblade. Great for a day if you need to shave and run or to touch up areas at night.

Bottom line is that I recommend this shaver for those that don't mind some hair left over when feeling your head. If you look in the mirror your head will be bald just not as soft as I am used to. Believe me, I tried shaving cream and tilting this shaver in every direction, but it just cannot get as close as I would like. That does not mean I will get rid of it as there is room in my toolbox for this. I will use it on days I need a quick shave and for trimming up my face in general, but it will not be my everyday shaver. I know it is unfair to compare it to a blade, but even without the blade comparison it still does not get as close as I like. Don't even bother to use it for more then 5 minutes as in 5 minutes you will get as close of a shave as this can give. When I first received this I tried shaving longer to see if it would eventually get the spots I wanted smoother, but you can rub all day and the shave is still the same. Do not bother to keep shaving as it will just be a waste of time. I am knocking a couple of star off for it's lack of closeness. This shaver is more for the lazy shaver then one who wants quality, but is is good for general use. Hope this helps.

Updated 1/29/2016.
I am updating my review just to note the heads are made cheaply. They tend to get worn out and get real loud during shaving. The head for this product needs a redesign to last longer and give a closer shave. I hope this happens one day.

title: Best solution I've found so far
text:
Some history first is needed, I have a herniated disc on lower back, hurts into my tailbone

Sore lower back, sore behind, I even sit on a leather recliner, still didn't help

A year ago bought an oval donut to try, put an ice pact inside the middle, relieved the pain, was ok

Except the ice packs did damage to my skin on my seating area, red, itchy, miserable.

Quit using ice packs, but oval donut by itself was too uncomfortable, causing me to look at other solutions

I come across the purple seat, I decided on the large size, fits perfectly on my leather recliner

First 3 days, my behind was already so sore, back as well. It came in 2 days, ty amazon

I didn't enjoy sitting on this seat because of the honeycombed style, never sat on anything like this, but after sitting the first day, I noticed little pain in my back area, and lessened pain in my bottom area, so decoded to give it a week to see

Plan was if I didn't like it I'd send it back, and try another seat, or use it along with another seat to alternate days using different products to find one that works and I enjoy sitting on it

After 3 days it seemed to loosen up, or I got used to it, or both, but my butt improved everyday, and my back pain lessened a lot. It does not get hot like a regular seat. But not cool either, I missed having some coolness so I did this.

I put a towel on my chair, a large flat ice pack on the towel, and the purple seat on top off all of it.

In about 10 minutes I feel some coolness, not enough to damage area like my other seating system, but feels so much better for me.

I cant say if it's for everybody, but works fantastic to me, and seems well made, so I expect it to last, the ice packs I used are made with heavy material, blue strong covers, cost 11 bucks at a famous retailer. And I'm now set, and much happier,

As with any new material you sit on, I'd say give it 3 days, my behind was so sore I thought I could never be happy sitting on gel honeycombs, but everyday I improved and got used to sitting on this, I still don't love sitting on honeycombs but it the best relieve for my soreness I've ever had.

Now I can't imagine life without it, saved me from buying a new chair, wife and I are saving money for updating our home, or I'd try a few more seating with cooling gel and memory foam, just to see if there's a better option out there, and one day I will, but till then the royal purple helps greatly and is my saving grace, hope this helps.

Remember other reviewers claim to send it back you pay shipping and restocking fee, so there's a price to pay to try it, so if you do at least give it 3 to 5 days because if I sent it back after the first day, idk where I'd be right now, I was so miserable.

Glad I gave it a chance, love it, but it's not perfect, ty and gl

Update, had this nearly a month now, used to it, have no problems sitting on a gel honeycomb now, still put an ice pack underneath the cushion, I will not be looking any further for a solution, I found it.

Be careful of one thing is I have found I reclind my recliner all the way back to take a nap woke up an hour and a half later and my butt was sore as heck so sit upright using this on a full recline when I'm taking a nap I have to remove the cushion.

You can lay back some now but my leather recliner goes back a long way and I think it spread my butt cheeks and made everything hurt so I can recline about halfway and I'm OK with the cushion, full recline I remove the cushion and I put it back when I sit upright again, I hope I explained well thank you and good luck

title: Good for emergency food as vegan, could be great if Splenda was removed
text:
I've known about Soylent for years and I love the idea of it. I'm vegan and have food allergies and it's always nice to have options in the case that I'm in. This ends up giving you more calories than the average random energy bar and since it's powder maybe a bit easier to carry around too.

The idea behind Soylent is that technically you could eat this for every meal and still have all your nutritional needs met. Kind of like pet food for humans, and the name is a play of course on Soylent Green (although there's soy in it, there are no lentils!)

This is vegan and gluten free. It's not however organic and my number one issue with it is that it uses Splenda (sucralose) as a sweetener. I heard that Soylent can't be sold in some countries due to this and Splenda is being tied to more health issues such as messing with your gut biome and such. I wouldn't be comfortable using this full time and I think a lot of people have a negative connotation with the term "Splenda" but don't realize sucralose is the same thing.

I tested this in a real world scenario, no fancy mixing cup, just a cup with water, to see how it blended and if it was chalky. The chocolate flavor was nice, and as for the taste beyond that it had a bit of a mild oatmeal type taste, so overall good and palatable. I was really surprised by how well it blended in with the water. It's not perfect but it wasn't like huge chunks that refused to blend along with some chalky mouthtaste which I've had with other drink powders. Some powders are basically only doable if you literally have a blender or coffee frother, or if you heat them up. I found this to be totally drinkable and could see myself bringing this on flights and stuff to get some variety from meal bars.

title: Unsure of dosing and effect as someone who responds to shilajit
text:
I've tried this company's mineral drops and electrolyte pills. In the past I've had some success with shilajit, which also has humic and fulvic acid in it.

I know the liquid forms of this can be good for gut health so I decided to give this a try. It tastes just like water. I respond very strongly to shilajit and not so much to this one. I feel like it's potentially underdosed.

It was unclear to me at first that the dosage was 3x per day. At that rate this size really doesn't last that long. I also failed to notice a warning not to refrigerate, and I did, and it's unclear to me what effect this could have had. I used it after a colonoscopy and some mild food poisoning and it's hard for me to tell what effect this had, if any.

I would have liked more information on the source of the fulvic/humic acid as well, and they could have easily added a measuring device in the cap, and didn't, which makes it cumbersome.

Although I like this company's other products I'm unclear on whether this one was any good. if I wanted to try liquid fulvic/humic acid again I'd probably go for another brand or just stick with shilajit.

title: Not what I was expecting - lots of ingredients other than the 3 listed
text:
I wanted to try this blend because the main oils that were listed are scents that I like and Spearmint has been tested to show effects on focus.

However I was unclear that this blend has a ton of other stuff in it than the main ingredients, I'm going to list them below:

Bergamot, Black Pepper, Caraway, Cinnamon Leaf, Clary Sage, Coffee, Eucalyptus, Frankincense Carterii, Ginger, Grapefruit, Holy Basil (Tulsi), Juniper Berry, Litsea, Melissa (Lemon Balm), Nutmeg, Organic Jojoba Oil, Peppermint & Sugandha Kokila

Especially the inclusion of coffee is kind of concerning for me, if it could have caffeine I wish they would mention it. I also really dislake citrus sent and although it is very muted I can smell the bergamont/grapefruit.

The smell is minty but I think due to the inclusions of a bunch of other stuff it does smell a bit more artificial. I can tell it's not artificial though because otherwise I'd be getting a migraine. However I just don't understand why it's needed to throw in that many additional ingredients. Just stick to the 3 listed and jojoba oil. As others have said the scent dissipates pretty quickly. I do feel that I feel a little more awake with this but I think that you can get a similar effect by putting peppermint oil in a diffuser.

I would say just do a higher percentage of the main oils to make it last longer and cut all these extra random oils that don't add to the scent.

title: Buy a larger size to wrap yourself up in - makes a huge difference for chronic pain!
text:
I previously had a similar sheet to this but as it's not a fitted sheet it didn't really work to use as a sheet as such. This time around I decided to get a much larger sheet and use it as a top sheet that I could basically wrap around my body under the blanket before I go to sleep. This means that even more of your body is making contact with the fabric. I wasn't sure if it would make a difference but since I'm a big fan of grounding pads I wanted to give it a try. Right now I have a grounded pillow case but I just couldn't get a long term grounded sheet or pad solution working for the rest of my bed because it would be kicked off or crumpled up.

I can say for those of you who do respond to grounding pads for pain/inflammation that it makes a HUGE difference to wrap yourself up in it. It's harder for me to notice now that I've been using it consistently but when I first got it I kind of felt drugged! Back when I had tried the smaller sheet that was bunching up my husband didn't know what this was supposed to do and spent many days passed out in our bed trying to attribute the calming effect to something else! So grounding is very real. There are tons of studies on it and if you suffer from chronic pain give it a try right away. Especially if you've had relief with pillows, pads, the difference between that and a full sheet or in my case wrapping myself up is pretty big!

Another cool thing about this is that it's 10% silver threads which should in theory give an antibiotic effect so your sheets are fresher longer. The sheet is even softer than my super expensive silver thread (but non grounding) sheet set I got and is not thin or flimsy. I have autism and I'm really picky about sheets and this one is totally fine.

title: Surprisingly comprehensive vegan maintenece iron supplement - not just iron!
text:
I was super surprised at how comprehensive and science based this little iron supplement is. It's not just iron, but it's a full comprehensive supplement to protect against all forms of anemia and increase iron absorption. The supplement doesn't cheap out at all. You have the methylated forms of B-12 and folate, as well as vitamin C and spirulina for absorption. The iron form is a vegan chelated form that shouldn't give stomach issues or constipate and in my case I haven't noticed this at all. I also love this "daily" dose for maintenance and that you can take more as needed, for example during your period. This is all vegan in a veggie cap. All together this is a great way to boost your iron for maintenance and it should in theory boost it much more than just a plain iron pill.

The only downside to this is that it has magnesium sterate (but it could have way more fillers, so that's good) and that the bottle/price/amount are off. Strangely their "power iron" has the same ingredients but also comes in 60/90 pill bottles and the amount of iron in their "power iron" 3x that in these pills despite the cost being just a bit more. I feel like if that's the case why not add 90 pills? Because as someone else stated if you can take up to 3 a day, that's only a 10 day supply for 18 vs a real 30 day supply of the power iron at just over 20. And this doesn't come in the 60/90 form despite the dosage being flexible and the bottle being huge for the amount, which doesn't make sense.

Other than this I do think it's an excellent and unique vegan iron maintenance supplement!

title: Vegan caps, no filler, traditional Ayurvedic brain supplements, but may or may not fit your needs
text:
This is a supplement which has a number of traditional Ayurvedic herbs that help cognition. The most well known and researched of these is Bhrami/Bacopa. Ashwagandha helps anxiety and tumeric helps general inflammation. It also has Licorice and some other less common herbs.

I am a bit torn about this review as I do like that the company responded to me when I asked about their heavy metal testing, especially for the bacopa in this blend. For these types of herbs heavy metal contamination is an issue. They got back to me quickly and gave me a COA on the bacopa, which I appreciated, but it wasn't like COAs I was used to, and very basic with no testing for heavy metals. So I appreciated that they got back to me and that they knew what I was talking about and had something but it was odd that the COA didn't show that. We also can't know how much bacopa is in here so even if it did show that amount it may be meaningless which is a pet peeve of mine for supplement manufacturers and "proprietary blends".

I don't want to be hypercritical of this supplement because I kind of think for a certain person it might be great if you know what you're getting into. I tend to trust Ayurvedic medicine in general over Chinese herbal medicine but they both suffer from some of the same issues - that they can be contaminated with heavy metals, and that you are consuming this huge bunch of herbs and getting all these different constituents in different amounts. There is a lot of research done into this and you can see some cases on both sides - whole food plant extracts that are used medicinally often don't just have one constituent that's helpful if it's being used traditionally and have value as is, but if you want to target a certain system (at the loss of some of these full spectrum plant benefits we may not understand fully yet) you may stick to one herb that's a standardized extract and see how you fare there. In the end that's what I decided to do and I bought a bacopa extract. But there is value to trying mixes like this.

I don't think it would harm anything to try this for a while and see how it works, that's what I did and I didn't really have any ill effects. But after I heard back from the company, and the fact that it has licorice in it (which can cause issues if taken long term, and Chinese herbal mixtures have this problem as well), made me not want to take it every day and go for the standardized bacopa extract instead.

I think this is a great way to try a traditional Ayurvedic supplement if you have any focus or cognitive issues, but then as a stepping off point to see what your needs are long term. I'm not sure if this supplement is OK to be taken long term. I do appreciate that the pills are certified organic, gluten free, vegan, with no fillers, and bringing traditional medicine to people is important. I think that COA or not it's hard to find a decent quality version of some of these herbs so it's as good of a place to start as any with Ayurvedic medicine and may well be better quality than something that a Ayurvedic doctor may give you.

title: Carefully crafted antioxidant red blend
text:
I have a bunch of "Greens" blends but wanted to round things out and try a "reds" blend. I've tried probiotics by this company before and they are unique in that they don't just resell some random blend but actually research and make unique, science based supplements. Given my experience with their probiotic and what I knew about the company from then I was excited to try this.

This blend basically has 4 components: a phytonutrient/antioxidant blend with a variety of red berries and beets, some medicinal mushrooms, some gluten free grains, and a small bit of probiotics. In addition this is sweetened with monkfruit, my favorite sweetener. You can tell they really put care into these ingredients because for example they do mention they used fruiting bodies, and they could have used stevia or even some junk coconut sugar and they did not.

I have tried this a few different times and it is just a neutral pleasant beet type flavor maybe with a bit of a berry undertone. I wouldn't recommend this just on its own but I don't think many of these powders really are meant to be just thrown in some water and washed down. If you are thinking of it being particularly "berry-y" it's more of a beet type powder. In any case I haven't had any problem with things I've mixed it in with as long as a beet and sweet taste is OK in that food.

The reason I took off a star is because it is pricey and I'm not sure if I'd get it again due to this but I do think it's justified in this case as they used premium ingredients such as fruiting body mushrooms, went of their way to get GF grains, sweetened with monkfruit instead of stevia, and so on.

title: Fresh smelling and Japan sourced chorella, company cares about veganism and sustainability

The smell and color of these tablets is good compared to others. I also contacted the company to determine the source of the chorella. I am taking off a star because the marketing was using some kind of annoying tactics - for example, " it also can contain protein, vitamin b12, iron, vitamin C, vegan omegas, fibre and small amounts of magnesium, zinc, copper, potassium, calcium, folic acid and other B vitamins.* " Note "can contain"... classic "weasel wording"... title: Highly effective endurance supplement
text:
So the flavor is not the best, it reminds me of a dull pedialyte, but it's effectiveness is unreal. I started looking into electrolyte supplements after studying a bit of sports nutrition recently and am a strong advocate for electrolytes over caffeine now. It refreshes your muscles by replacing electrolytes lost through sweat and their purpose it to assist with the contraction of muscles. They help to prevent injury by keeping muscles hydrated and prolonging the onset of potential muscle cramps; actually I have yet to experience a muscle cramp while using this supplement.
Over the past few months/bottles of using this product I'd say the most effective means is to put one serving in a powered zero sugar sports drink for a more rounded electrolyte diversity and for the added B vitamins to assist with metabolism under stress (also it tastes a lot better). When you feel like you're running on empty and want to see how far you can go, slam the whole thing and you'll feel the difference; it's not like a caffeine high, it's different, it's like your muscles say "who's up for round two." For me personally I'll drink about 1/3 of the powerade mix every 30mins and continuously drink water in between (it does suppress your desire to drink water so you do need to be more mindful of this). It is more of an endurance product and by that I mean I generally only use it when I know my routine will exceed 1 hour (usually1-2 hours cardio followed by an additional hour of weightlifting). Outside of general workouts, it's great for hiking as well because one serving in a 2L hydropack lasts me 3 hours comfortably at moderate pace on an intermediate-advsnced trail. Also it's a great hangover preventer and/or hangover relief (random find). Again the flavor isn't the best but highly effective and I have already strongly recommended this product to family and friends.

title: Good product, great combination of ingredients
text:
A close friend has been taking black seed oil for some time now and recommended it for help with digestion and because it seemed to help with some itchy, rashy skin issues he'd had. He also rarely gets colds anymore, and he used to all the time, so although anecdotal, maybe this is helping with immune response as claimed. This is a good product, reasonably priced and with all the right ingredients, so I decided to give it a try.

I probably haven't been taking it long enough to see major results (only a week or so), but I can tell you that the large caps are easy to swallow because they are softgels which slide down easy and don't scratch your throat despite the size. I haven't noticed any odd flavor, which people complain about when taking this supplement in oil form rather than capsule form, and taking it with a meal, as recommended, is easier than trying to time it between meals as required with some medications or supplements.

I have had no stomach upset or any other negative side effects and am encouraged by my experience so far. I plan to stay on these long-term and see how it goes. If anything notable pops up, I'll return and edit this review.

title: Thick and cushiony
text:
These pads are thicker foam than most others I've seen. This is good for providing padding, but if your shoe is already somewhat snug there may not be room to use these. For my purpose, which was not so much padding as providing fit, they worked fine. I had a pair of leather sandals - slides, really - that were just a little too loose due to wear and the leather stretching slightly, so they kept slipping off and trying to trip me.

I got these to try to downsize those straps slightly, for more secure fit, and it worked fine. The adhesive has been holding them in place inside the straps very well for several days now (not true of the ones I'd bought at the store and tried.) The sizes and shapes provided were not ideal for my use, but they were easy to cut and shape with scissors into pieces that would work for me.

If they continue to remain stuck where I put them they will be a godsend - I liked the slides, but they were about to go in the trash before I took a header and hurt myself. These pads gave them a second chance.

title: What a neat product - where have you been all my life?
text:
This is a very useful and pleasant-smelling spray for keeping shoes fresh and odor-free. I've bought the sprays before, Dr. Scholl's and others, and they work fine for what they are supposed to do, but they all share one trait, and that's the powdery/perfumey nature of the spray. They are all similar to what bowling alleys use on their rental shoes to make them more "hygienic" but they don't truly leave the shoe fresh, just masked by the spray scent.

This spray is unique in that it's a wet spray that starts out with a fresh, almost spicey/peppery scent when you spray it, but that fades to barely noticeable fairly quickly, and by the time the shoe is dry (a few hours or the next day) it has very little spray scent - and ZERO foot or "old shoe" odor. This is the first spray I've used that really leaves the shoe pleasantly odor-free - and that's a solid win, in my opinion.

title: Adds Comfort and Convenience to Mask Wearing
text:
These mask-hook-extender things were basically an impulse selection, but on days where I need to wear an N-95 or med-pro mask for 8 hours, they have turned out to be essential equipment!

While there are a few things I'm not fond of, the positive attributes list is much more extensive.
POSITIVES:
1. Inexpensive solution that actually works.
2. Packaged in multiples that allow putting one in your car, backpack, pocket, etc.
3. Soft, flexible, comfortable material.
4. Plenty of attachment points for custom adjustability.
5. Can be worn above, below, or behind the ears without loss of function or comfort.

NEGATIVES:
1. Requires a fair amount of manual dexterity to fasten in place. (Don't try this with gloves on!)
2. The free ends flop about like a bassett hound's ears in a stiff wind.
3. You have to be willing to sacrifice a cool appearance for dorky-looking comfort.
4. They work less-effectively with cloth masks, especially if the loops are non-elastic.

title: Our house is fresh and smells like baked cookies
text: We adopted an older cat with some digestive issues so the litter box was initially shocking. Once we moved him onto better quality and more age appropriate food, the litter box became less of an issue. Upon receiving him, he is an intact older male with all the scent of musk that comes with unfixed older male cats. We bought this to remove any traces of him and litter smell in the house. We are extremely impressed with how well this works. We bought him an automated litter pan as a convenience and he took to it immediately. If you have not tried "Just the Crystals" silica litter, consider this an endorsement. The side effect of having this unit plugged in, and perhaps we are both crazy for noticing this, but since pulling this unit in, the house has this very light smell of baked brown sugar oatmeal. I am not sure if the smell of dying bacteria and DNA/RNA being deconstructed is supposed to smell this pleasant, but it adds a very light and pleasant fragrance to the house. The unit is plugged in directly behind his litter pan and runs 24/7. You could walk through that room of the house and, immediately assume we are baking cookies, but also never detect there is a litter pan in the house. On our vets recommendation, he underwent surgery and the musk smell abated. Now the house just smells fresh all the time. If only this company would com out with something that gathers up the loose hair, destroys it while making it smell like clean linen.

title: Simple, quiet and elegant
text:
This is my first foray into the world of essential oils. I have been watching as friends and family members continue to rave about lotions, potions, and other gizmos. Well ... now I'm hooked! I tried the LORIS diffuser with 100% pure frankincense after receiving the product at a discount in exchange for this honest review. As a newbie, I was a bit intimidated, but sure didn't need to be. The concept and packaging are both elegant and simple. The instructions definitely could use an editor, but I was able to follow them.

I ran the diffuser overnight after slightly overfilling it (the unit is designed to hold 120ml max but the cup that comes with it measures up to 150ml and I didn't compare the markings on both before using it). While using 30sec pulse mode, I still had about 70ml of solution left more than 8 hours later. The machine is quiet; I was able to adapt quickly to the watery whispers and they didn't disturb me from about a foot away on my nightstand.

I love playing with all the different light modes while I'm awake, but turned that part off for sleeping. The mist still functioned with no problem. My only complaint in that regard is the green/red power light still glows pretty brightly, and I'm sensitive to light so it was disruptive for me. I turned the front of the unit away toward the wall, which helped enough for me but still reflected.

Cleanup is no more messy than I would expect other diffusers to be. I get some condensation drops when removing the cover if I've just turned the machine off, but absolutely no stray droplets or moisture problems while operating (even my paperback was safe right next to the unit). The instructions say to use citric acid every 2-3 days to keep it clean; I don't look forward to having to think about that so often.

Overall, I plan to continue using this diffuser in my bedroom and am now looking to build my collection of oils.

title: Disappointed
text:
I bought this scale to go with my Fitbit app. I was so excited when it finally arrived because I use my Fitbit everyday and looked forward to the convenience of the compatible scale. However, after almost 2 hours, and following the set-up instructions to a "T," I still couldn't connect to my WiFi. I contacted FItbit, who are always extremely friendly, but couldn't solve my issue. They escalated my case, and I was contacted via email by an "expert." They gave me the following instructions to troubleshoot (See below in quotes). Quite frankly, it's not worth my time to contact my internet service provider (which is always a minimum of 2 hours for anything) to confirm the first requirements. Secondly, even if I was comfortable separately the 2.4 and 5GHz into unique channels, if it still didn't work, check out the questions they ask. Based on the password questions, it sounds like the next step would be to change my WiFi password. Why should I have to go through all of this? This product should just work. I shouldn't need to be an IT Expert to get this to work. Take this product off the market until you improve it. I'm returning the product and going with another brand. Save yourself time and trouble, pay less for a better product. (This is the first bad review I've written but that's how strongly I feel that this is a waste of money).

"We want to let you know that in order the Aria can connect to your WiFi the network must have these requirements:
- Wireless 802.11b (Note: most routers are capable of 802.11b, but not necessarily configured this way). Also Note that if your router is a dual-band router, you should separate the 2.4 and 5 GHz into unique channels, and connect specifically to the 2.4GHz, which allows for 802.11b. If you're not sure about this advise you'll need to contact your local internet service provider.
- WEP/WPA/WPA2 personal security
- Automatic (DHCP) IP setup (static IP configuration not supported)

After making sure it has the requirements above, try to set up your Aria again. You can do this by proceeding through either of the setup methods detailed at: http://fitbit.link/nncet, in which you'll find all requirements needed besides the listed above. You can also watch the video at https://www.youtube.com/embed/.

If you encounter difficulty during this process, we recommend clearing your browser's cache and cookies, turning your router off for 30 seconds, turning your router back on, and attempting setup again. If you're still unable to connect your Aria, please provide us with the following information so that we can assist you further:

1. At what point in the scale setup process do you run into trouble? Please let us know of any error messages you've encountered on the scale or your computer/mobile device.
2. How far is the scale from your router?
3. Do you use any wireless extenders on your network or more than one router?
4. Does your WiFi password exceed 31 characters or spaces?
5. Do your WiFi password and your WiFi's name include any non-alphanumeric characters (such as ! or &)?
6. Were you able to confirm that your router is configured in 802.11b protocol?
7. What is the make and model of your router? Is your router a dual-band router?
8. Do you use any firewalls or MAC filtering?
9. Additionally, kindly provide a photo of your Fitbit Aria's model and serial number located in the battery compartment."

title: Quality, well built shoulder strap
text:
This brace is very well built, I had a little trouble putting it on by myself so I got my wife to help me and that worked. I think I initially strapped the part that goes around your arm a little too high because there was too much space to move. I adjusted it to be lower on my arm and it gave me much better support.

Once I got it on I had my wife help me tighten it up and it felt really good the movement was compressed going forward and back and it felt snug against my body. I would have liked for it to be a little tighter raising my arm laterally.

I know it isn't designed for this but I also stuck an icepack in the adjustable strap/pocket that goes on top, so it kind of doubled as an ice pack holder lol.

If you don't have someone to help you put it on it will take some coordination to get the arm strap done and the back tightening strap should be adjusted before you put it on, the front adjusting connection is perfect.

The other good thing about having a strap like this is that it reminds me that my shoulder is hurt and I don't go doing something too fast with it and make it worse. I have forgotten my shoulder was in pain and moved quickly to do something and it wasn't fun.

My shoulder doesn't hurt all the time, thankfully, but I'll wear it when it flares up.

title: NOT sexy - best for last mos. of pregnancy
text:
This is my 3rd pregnancy in 4 years and a good friend of mine rec this after carrying twins for 38 weeks who were 7 lbs each! Said it was a life saver. I was doubtful it would help but I've had lots of hip pain throughout this 3rd pregnancy and I've never worn a maternity support belt before - didn't feel I needed it and I work as an Esthetician so was on my feet working on clients til month 9 for preg 1 & 2. Out of desperation I started wearing this cradle in month 8 and it has helped. When I was smaller I didn't feel it was as helpful but maybe that's b/c I ordered a size Med and s/h gotten size Small.
Key points:
1. Yes it's ugly and the front straps will show under clothes unless you tuck them out of the way under your nursing bra hooks(good tip). If you are in pain you won't care.
2. You could prob order a size down like others rec - I didn't thinking at pre preg size 8/10 (155 lbs), I usually gain at least 30+ lbs during pregnancy and would need the extra length. Right now at 32 weeks I wear it on the middle hooks (there are 3 sets). Where I wish there was more adjustment is the flexy material under your breasts - I guess in this respect bigger size is ok. After a long day it feels tight here and you can't let it out.
3. Wish it had more sets of hooks around waist so you can adjust to shorter length during early months but suppose you could sew on your own. Also wish it wasn't white.
4. I wear this over my bra and not over a tank top and don't think it scratches all that much. Granted during the summer in LA heat, I opted not to wear this b/c I was smaller and not in as much pain and it was too hot to wear with clothes. I also like this instead of the more traditional support belts b/c it's not made of neoprene or similar material which I found bulky and really hot under my clothes. When you're preggo you're already hot.
5. I bought the prenatal mini cradle to try and that was stupid - just a big strip of elastic which you could make. Here w/ the prenatal cradle it's the whole contraption which makes more sense for the $$.

I'd give it 5 stars if it had the above adjustments. I'd have been more inclined to wear in 2nd trimester if so and maybe that could've been a good preventive for aches and pains.

title: So far so good.
text:
I have had this exercise pedal machine for a little over two weeks now. I use it for a hour and a half each day (two 45min sessions). And so far I am really enjoying it.

Within the first week one of my pedals was making a thumping noise/feeling on each cycle (it was definitely the pedal and not the internals of the machine) and was quite annoying, but this was due to improper positioning. Since then I have got it in the perfect position and it no longer does this.

Overall the operation is quite smooth, but on occasion you can feel a bit of 'grittiness' on the cycling, but nothing that severely impacts the performance of the machine. It is most definitely quite too, and this a HUGE plus for me. It makes virtually no noise whatsoever. The construction of this machine is top notch, the main internals of the machine are rock solid and don't move/vibrate at all.

As far as a good exercise is concerned, it does very well for it's small package. Granted it doesn't have the strength of a full-sized pedal machine, but for its size it goes above and beyond what I expected. It has just enough resistance to get a great sweat worked up and burns calories quite well. And I am not even sure if I have mine turned up all the way (it's at least pretty close to full). If I keep it between 15-17 MPH for 45 mins, according to the machine I burn between 420-460 calories. Obviously this calorie count isn't 100% accurate and is probably a low-ball estimation, but even if it wasn't that is a decent amount of calories for 45mins IMO. For my weight and age I estimate the calorie count from the machine plus 20%. For my two 45min sessions on this machine, I estimate I burn over 1,000 calories a day on it. And just so we are clear I am a 24 year old male and have very strong legs. And this machine has the perfect resistance level for me. Not too easy, and not too hard.

As far as ease of use is concerned, it doesn't get any better than this. It is small, portable, quite and can be used with practically any chair. I currently use my computer chair and it works out magnificently. I do the machine while watching some Netflix instant watch TV shows (which are 44 minuet long shows). And the time just FLY'S by when you do it this way. In a way it's almost fun. The on-board meter that comes with the machine does its job pretty well. It has the most simplest features, but these features to me are crucial. Calorie count, time, speed, and distance. The machine cycles through these every few seconds. And for me has worked out very well. It has a auto-stop feature that stops the clock if you stop cycling (and starts back up when you start cycling again), which is nice to have. It is also easily reset by holding down the main red button for a few seconds. The only complaint I would have about the meter is sometimes it's hard to read, It would be nice to have a back-light of some kind or perhaps colored LED letters/numbers (like a digital clock).

Now finding the right position for the machine in relation to your chair/legs can be quite tricky. I suggest you mark the floor with the spots you are comfortable with (I use tape to mark the end points). That way when you use it again you will have it in the same exact spot as before. And trust me, this makes a bigger difference than you might imagine. As this is one of the biggest drawbacks of the portable machine like this, is the inconstancy with placement. Cause the full sized machines are always fixed. So if you mark the floor and keep it in the same spot each time, this will make it much better. The other part about this machine is that it does move, especially when you start to speed up. I have tried a few different things to keep it from moving, putting weights on the end, but this didn't help much and it slowly creeps forward as you use it. I now have a bar that hits the end of the machine legs and is placed against a non-moving platform. So far this is working great for me. But make sure you do something like this, because if the machine slowly moves forward, it can get quite annoying and changes the dynamics of the exercise more than you might think.

Another thing to note about this machine is that the outer plastic casing does warm up (not hot, just warm). I am not sure why it would warm up, cause if it was 100% magnetic based, there shouldn't be any touching/rubbing parts on the inside. But perhaps the heat comes from some kind of magnetic energy field that gets generated when using this. But either way the warmth isn't a problem at all, just thought I would mention it.

Overall it is working out great for me. I am not sure how long it will last, but so far with almost 25 hours of constant use, it is holding up nicely.

P.S. Oh and I use this machine with my bear feet. Never tried using it with shoes yet.

UPDATE: Well, it's been just about 3 months now since I received this product. I am proud to say I have been using it for at least 45 minuets a day since I got the machine... I have not missed ONE day of exercise since I got it, no kidding. Mixed with a calorie reduced diet and 45 minuet pedal exercise each day, I am steadily losing weight, feeling better and looking thinner.

There is only a few things I want to point out. First isn't so much about the machine, but about technique. After using this machine daily, you really start to work your way up in speed. I can now hold steady at 24-25 MPH for 45 mins straight. This ends up burning roughly 670 calories according to the bike. And believe me, even after all this time of me using the machine, I still get one heck of a burn. I have never sweat so much in my life (seriously). This may sound gross, but after I am done with my 45 mins on the machine, my t-shirt is literally dripping with sweat. My entire shirt from head to waste is absolutely soaked (especially my backside). And I have to make sure I have a heavy duty sweat rag to wipe my face and neck every minuet or so. So yeah, the machine does work just as well as a stand-alone machine IMO.

Secondly is the downsides I have found so far. For the most part, the machine still works flawlessly. It is still very smooth and the resistance stays the same day in and day out. However, it does make a lot of creaking and cracking noises when I use it. At one point it was making a very loud horrible screeching sound every time I rotation around. So I took the outer-shell off as best I could (without unscrewing the pedals) and once I put it back together the sound went away. But is still creaks, cracks and pops with every turn, and can get very annoying if you let it get to you (it's the sound of the outer-shell plastic moving against itself). If tedious popping and creaking sounds annoy you (they do for me, I also hate constant barking dogs), one thing you can do is put on a movie or TV show and crank the volume up while you use the machine. Another solution would be to completely remove the outer plastic shell around the machine. I would do this, but my pedals seems to be permanently stuck in place now, so I cannot remove them and therefore cannot remove the shell. But aside from looking a bit odd (neat inner workings though) this should get rid of the creaking noises. And far as I can tell from when I unscrewed the shell, it does nothing except add cosmetic features to the machine and make creaking noises.

But the overall operation of the machine is still is in good working condition. Aside from the annoying popping/cracking noises that make it anything but quiet, it works great and provides a excellent exercise.

UPDATE 2/19/2011: Well, this is just a minor update to comment on the bikes long-term use. As mentioned previously in my last update, I had commented that the machine makes constant creaking and cracking noises as you use it, and can drive somebody absolutely insane if your a person who gets overly irritated at random noises that are completely out of your control. Well, after repeatedly performing some make-shift surgury to the bike to finally pin-point the problem, I have completely eliminated the creaking noises by lining the entire inside of the machines shell (where the plastic meets itself) with thick tape and screwed it down nice and tight. The creaking noises are now completely GONE!

However while I always manage to fix something, another problem rolls right around the corner. So after fixing the plastic creaking FINALLY, now I am having trouble with my pedals. Aside from the horrible squeaking as I rotated the pedals (they just needed some oil) they are now getting more and more loose(side to side and up/down looseness). So this in turn often creates a strange 'lumpy' feeling on each rotation when I am using it, and can often make thumping noises too. The good thing is that this bike seems to have the same pedal threading and size as a regular bicycle pedal (and every other exercise bike pedal as well) so I think I can easily replace the pedals with different ones for less than $15. And once I do that, it should be smooth sailing!

Overall though, the internals are still working absolutely perfectly with no flaws that I can see yet, even after 45 mins a day for just about 4 months now (I still haven't missed one day yet). I am simply amazed at the quality of the construction for the moving internal parts. The pedals may suck, and the case may need fixing to avoid creaking and is cheap plastic... but the insides are built like a tank!

UPDATE 5/26/11 - Well, still not ONE day has passed where I did not exercise at least 45 minuets on this pedal exerciser. Since my last update there hasn't been any major problems that have arose. There have been some minor technical problems with the pedals, but after completely dissembling my pedals and re-oiling them, it has been fairly smooth sailing. Sure the pedals still click and 'thump' under certain circumstances, but they are holding up quite well.

Recently I tried switching the stock pedals with some non-stock pedals I got from here on Amazon, but the new pedals I got were worse then the stock ones. Only a few minuets into my exercise and my new pedals started thumping horribly, which was unbelievably annoying. I have since replaced the new pedals with the stock ones after a full disassembly and re-oiling.

In case anybody is wondering, the stock pedals for this machine are 9/16", and they have no bearings whatsoever.

title: Absolutely blown away!!!!
text: So I have a 5 month old kitten who had surgery on one of his paws and had to use the Yesterdays News for the litter (which apparently he didn’t like at first) if anyone has used that litter they know it doesn’t absorb scent AT ALL. Well, he decided to use my dirt laundry basket and hid this poopoo and till laundry day came around I didn’t notice that the clothes all the way to the bottom of the basket were wet (and where his poo was very well hidden). By this time the odor had set in and wasn’t strong but it was there. I never had a cat not use a litter box so I just threw everything in the wash and the smell didn’t go away, I washed it again and still the kitty urine was not just there but stronger. Did some research and came across this product and thought “worth a shot”. I had a heavy load (jeans, towels, sheets and other items) so I used 1/3rd of a cup and tepid water with a pre-soak (just to be safe). Not only did the urine smell completely come out, any set in stain on some old shirts that went in were gone!! A white shirt that is roughly 10 years old that I could really only use for bed or working outside had a few set in stains. I took each piece out of the washer and smelled every part of the item and came across this shirt and it looked brand new!!! So it didn’t just get out the kitty odor but set in stains on a white shirt even bleach and oxi-clean couldn’t get out. I’m beyond impressed with this laundry additive and will definitely keep it in stock at the house even just for white wash. Did a small test and diluted it a bit and used it as spot cleaner on carpets bc I have a 5 yr old cat who has tummy issues here and there and poor little man gets sick around the house. I’ve used resolve as well as an oxi-clean & hot water mix and had to scrub and scrub. Used this on the carpet and it was gone without a trace and used it on an old stain (didn’t notice it was still there bc it was in the corner of dining room) and it got it up and no odor from the kitty 🤮. Can’t get over how amazing it is!!!!! Highly recommend to EVERYONE!! Pet owner or not.

title: feels firm but is soft enough to sit on an egg & not crack. supports m 225lb weight & no tailbone pain after long sitting period
text:
ok in short summary: feels firm but is soft enough to sit on an egg and not crack the egg surprisingly. 1.25" thick, supports my 225lb weight, after long sitting perioids in car and office playing games and doing i.t. work, i haven't had tailbone or coccyx strain/pain. and its not heat producing. hav sat in chairs or cushions that trap and generate heat after while.

so more in depth thoughts and blabber:

i love this cushion more than other cushions. most are foam. but its not hot it breathes. I tried sitting on an egg even tho this is 1.25" not the 2inch and the egg didn't crack. i did it slowly carefully but leaned back and raised my arms and legs to make sure my weight was on my buttocks and this thing is soft enough to conform to the pressure of an egg without cracking it. I'm 5' 6" / 7" and a bit hefty at 225lbs. so i'm not a light weight. granted the egg was in my butt crack which has a ... well crack or space to give, but i tried same thing with egg on a normal couch recliner chair with egg in a sandwhich baggy and that egg cracked and exploded.
I slept on this as well just to see. i like firmer and fuller pillows , i'm a side sleeper , and threw this on top of a very thin pillow. its actually firm probably too firm for most people's heads my head didn't sink. this is very supportive of a lot of weight.
I sat on this in my car and my office chair and i can tell i'm physically sitting higher like my knees almost hit bottom of my steering wheel in car and i definitely sit a lil higher. so this cushions and raises your body a good inch or so. but soft enough to site on an egg carefully without having issue.
I would say its safe to assume if you're lighter in weight the 1" or thinner might support your body. i'm 225lbs and this 1 & quarter" thick supports my sitting weight fine.
My office chair and sometimes in my car i get that Tailbone/Coccyx strain and pain. so this cushion , for me, is for providing long term sitting cushion and comfort and relive pressure and pain for me. i do I.T. work and sometimes work on my computer remotely all day, shop all day, and play games ... all in one day so this last week this thing has had a lot of use for one week.
I did stretch this thing out and grabbing the ends and pulling apart, this thing stretches good. the material is like a firm jelly material. doesn't feel like typical anything really. but i've enjoyed it.
i think this thing doesn't feel as soft as it is but it supports nicely and cushiony enough but feels a lil firm but so far haven't had that pain in my coccyx so i'm happy so far so good and its not hot. i live in houston its like 85-95 but feels like 95-105 with 200% humidity so i didn't want a cushion you feel as being hot and didn't want something that goes flat but can support me since i'm a bit over weight actually and i sit a lot. but no pain in the butt after long sitting period is a double!

title: It's not that my first one was a lemon -- they're all lemons.
text:
I'm on my second Echo PB-500T after a no-questions-asked exchange at the local big box where it was purchased. This blower is a P.O.S. It worked well for the first roughly 10 times. Then, just like the first one, it started to require more and more pulls to get it started. 10, 20, 50. Today, after about 150 yanks, starting and then dying after 5 seconds or not starting at all, re-reading the manual, following the instructions (cleaned the air filter, cleaned the spark arrestor, cleaned the fuel filter, adjusted the choke repeatedly, etc.), I am giving up on Echo as a brand.

We owned a small Echo blower for about 20 years and it eventually and sadly died. The present machine is not nearly of the same quality. I live on 7 acres and have a very long driveway that must be kept clean because it is steep with a great many large trees. Cars will slide if I'm not diligent. I must own a good blower because sweeping and raking are not an option. As with most products, buying excellent quality is less expensive in the long run, less frustrating, and more productive and leaf blowers are no exception. Unfortunately, Echo has apparently followed the same path of so many others: build an excellent reputation, then squeeze as much money out of the company as possible by cheapening one's products. They lost a good customer.
