I take one serving (3 pills) per day, with a full glass of water. They're easy to swallow. I also add a Vitamin C supplement when taking these, since collagen reportedly works better in conjunction with that.

I've noticed my face looks a bit plumper (good) and my skin is less dry. Haven't noticed a pain reduction (I'm frequently sore from exercising), but I never expected collagen to help with pain. For me, collagen is for improving one's appearance and this brand does that.

title: Best supplement I've ever taken
text:
I"d never heard of rhodiola until this summer. One of the health & fitness bloggers I follow, recommended it for decreased pain and increased energy.

Well, he certainly knew what he was talking about! This rhodiola rose organic extract powder is the best supplement I've taken -- and I've taken plenty, especially following two back surgeries and a persistent TMJ issue. Fish oil, magnesium, turmeric, vitamins, etc. -- all good for what they are, but nothing seems to compare with this rhodiola.

My morning ritual now is to take 1/6 of a teaspoon of this powder and mix it into my morning hot coffee. It takes some persistent mixing to get it to dissolve, and to tell the truth some of it never actually does dissolve, but I drink the whole cup down.

About 30 minutes after drinking it, the rhodiola does its thing.

What happens? First, I get more energy. Yes, I just had the coffee, but this is a different kind of energy than what I get from caffeine. Peaceful & productive energy, not too much, just right.

Second, I get some focus. I'm as ADD-addled as the next person (maybe more so), and have a lot I want to accomplish. The increased focus (for work, for working out, for playing the piano) is more than welcome.

Finally, I feel a LOT better. The TMJ (mostly jaw & neck clicking) settles way, way down. No back pain. No headache.

Someone wrote recently that you can build up a tolerance to rhodiola, and it stops being effective. I've been using this for three months and that hasn't begun to happen. I pray that it doesn't, because I really plan to keep using this. Maybe forever.

title: Great for minor touch ups
text:
When moving or just during day to day life, it's all but inevitable your furniture will end up scratched. This 21 piece set is a good value, considering that one scratch repair marker will have cost me $5 at my local home improvement store.

Here you get not only the markers, but wax "crayons" that can also be used for scratch touch-ups. I recently helped my son move from one apartment to another and a Craftsnman-era table got horribly scratched by a wayward something in the back of the moving van. With this set, we were able to carefully touch up the scratches so that it looks almost as if nothing happened to it. Since then, I have used it on wooden horse carving that I inherited and it looks almost brand new.

Be careful with the colors that you choose, start lighter and work up. Use your finger or a soft cloth to blend areas that you treat in order to smooth out lines of demarcation. If you go too dark, it can be a glaring mistake, so easy does it. The markers and crayons do tend to last and stand up to light dusting. Over time you may have to touch up. This is a great thing to have on hand when a complete refinish of a piece of furniture isn't possible.

If you are at HIGH RISK ,  DON'T USE THIS TEST.  Please instead see your family doctor for a referral.  However,  for the millions of others out there who aren't at moderate or high risk for colon cancer.  I'd say at least think about trying it.  Consider this. Most men especially those who are considered at AVERAGE risk for colon cancer age 45 or over never even get tested at all. Wake up, stumble on scale, walk away. No buttons, no thought and your data shows up on the website. They also have an API and ways to pull down your data. 8/2014 update:
It's very picky about the wifi. It's occasionally lost it and had to go through the painful setup again. But, i'm not sure i would lower to 3 stars... because it still works great and I still love having the automated data. I think i've replaced the batteries (4 AA) once in the last year.

title: Good quality/potency, good packaging
text:
This reshii has an intense earthy flavor. In fact the flavor may be a little intense for some people at first.

They've done a decent job with high-quality re-sealable packaging, but longevity is still going to be a factor here. Herbs expire more quickly in powder form. They start breaking down more rapidly when they're ground up so pay attention to the expiration date. If you want reshii that lasts longer you should leave it in mushroom form and grind it yourself as needed. As it is it's super-convenient to have it pre-ground, so IMO it's worth the convenience, but you'll have to decide for yourself - it's probably going to come down to how much and how often you're using it.

Serving size is defined in "scoops" but it doesn't come with a scoop so there's no obvious way to tell what the correct volume for a serving is. I started with a tablespoon, and the flavor was quite intense and the effects on my mental clarity were very apparent. I worked my down to a teaspoon which I think would be more palatable for the average person. The effects of the smaller portion were not as intense, but they seemed to last longer. I would personally recommend a teaspoon three times a day - but you should follow the advice of your own herbalist (and if you don't have one, get one! lol).

Overall this seems like a good value for the price, it's a good quality product and while the powder doesn't last as long as the mushroom itself, they provide an expiration date and good quality re-sealable packaging.

title: Built like a friggin' tank!
text:
I just ordered 3 of these, 2 arrived. The paging did not survive the shipping. The factory boxes these came in were totally destroyed. That's because the seller did not bother to pack any foam, paper, or air-pillows in the shipping box to stop the two items slimming about inside the shipping box. That's also because these clamps are very heavy, and built like a tank. The fact they survived shipping says a lot about their construction.

My only gripe as to the seller's photos of the product is that the product should have been shown in use with the type of lighting it was meant to hang. These guys are actually meant to hang industrial filmmaking lighting gear which is much bigger and heavier than the entry/pro filmmaking video lighting I'm currently using. So, I've had to look for another clamp that has the standard stud for video / photo lighting.

I'm keeping all of these clamps, because now I have them, I can hang some heavier lighting in the future as needed.

These clamps have what initially looks like a common studio lighting stud, but it's not. It's a really big stud with a threaded bold inserted with a hefty washer. This aint your average DJ light clamp. I think if I end up with a couple of those heavy mover heads, I'll hang them with these guys.

I think the seller needs to be aware that by not packing correctly, this could have cause the shipping box to be damaged, and then the products could have slammed into and damaged other packages during shipping. These are very heavy, and even though they will survive just about anything, they still need to be packed so they don't slam about in the shipping box.

title: Nice organic frankincense, poor dropper
text:
I love frankincense essential oil, it smells so fresh and resin/woodsy. I know it is not for everyone but we like it at my house. So I decided to try US organic, because it is organic and finding certified organic oils is actually a challenge to do.
This one comes with a European dropper, unlike others I have used, this one the drops come out quite fast so you best watch to make sure you don't get too much, but maybe I just got a looser dropper. Others I have used do not come out this fast, it more or less dumps it.
The scent is authentic for a Boswellia Serrata, there are many varieties of frankincense so you want to make sure you get the kind you want for therapeutic purposes. It smells slightly different from another brand I have but not much.
On a spot test where you drop some on a paper and see how fast it dissipates, this one was gone in less than 5 min, this is supposed to be a sign of quality. I was impressed as the last few oils I've purchased, have not dissipated at all and have left an oil mark.
All in all, I would say this is a real deal and you'd be getting a good deal for what you are paying for. If you are looking and considering the big bottle kinds but want real stuff, choose this one over a bigger bottle. It is going to be authentic.

title: I LOVE This Thing!
text:
My friends consider me their skincare guru, and it's true I have dozens of skincare products from drugstore to high-end and the cleaning devices to match. Everything from three Clarisonic models to the Conair Skin Pod (which I also love for travel).

I'm relatively new to the vibrating silicone scrubber type brushes (the Conair is one), and I was skeptical, but I'm sold. No nasty bristles to trap makeup or which will wear out in a few months. The silicone scrubbers clean amazingly well, and this one is no exception. The thing is, you have to be aware of what you've got on your face and HOW to remove it.

You're not removing heavy foundation or sunscreen with this and a mild face wash or micellar water followed by a wash with this, nor should you be relying on that method. You're not using the brute force method employed by a traditional scrub brush with bristles.

These type brushes work best with the double-cleanse method. Either a makeup remover that will dissolve your makeup and foundation followed by a face wash used with this, or the oil cleansing method, where you take the day off by emulsifying what's on your face with a cleansing oil and water then a face wash with this.

Seem like more work? Well it's kinder to your skin, ACTUALLY removes the gunk, and outlook keep brushes like this clean forever. I have oily, acne-prone skin, and my pores can get nasty, but using this double cleanse method and this brush has them clean and empty! If you're dry, employ the oil cleanse method.

Using this with a very emollient face wash is going to gunk up the brush like it would gunk up a washcloth. Don't even think of using Noxzema. That stuff is best used in the trash bin.

This maneuvered well around my nose, and I do not have a cute little flat nose, so I've got some serious corners to get into. I "rinse" my face using disposable face sponges, which is faster than just using hands and also helps drop the bubbles off.

The "blue" is thankfully really more of a purple violet. Lovely color. Three vibrating speeds plus an extra pulsing function that I don't really use. Love the heating function. I use it on the nose and chin to dissolve sebum plugs and on my jaw to relax my TMJ. After I've cleaned, I use the cold function on my nose and cheeks to close the pores. I've never seen another cleaning gadget that has all these functions at any price point, and the price is right!

title: I use this to help make my horse's fly spray!
text:
If you ride horses you probably have flies and buy fly spray. It's expensive and filled with chemicals.

I looked around for a homemade homeopathic spray and found this one.

I use this rosemary essential oil as one of the ingredients in my horse's fly spray. It works great, but note that it is not long-lasting. I also put fly boots on my horse which helps to significantly reduce stomping.

Here's the recipe:
• large spray bottle
• Two Cups *each* of water and apple cider vinegar
• Two T olive oil
• squirt of dish soap
• any three essential oils (but not citrus), 8 to 10 drops each
Mix well and spray. Be sure to shake before each use. Keeps well at the stable.

Commercial fly sprays can cost between low $20s to low $30s. I figure this homeopathic spray costs less than $1.50 per bottle.

title: Necessity for the unhappy cubicle monkey.
text:
No...it's not pretty. AND it's not a 10,000 lux lamp designed specifically for SAD (I also have one of those) but for what it is...it's perfect.

I work in an office with no windows. I've been working in an office with no windows for the last nine years. Every winter...work becomes nearly unbearable. The dry, overheated office air. No sunlight. Getting up in the dark...leaving from work in the dark. For anyone who suffers from SAD...it's like slowly descending into hell over the course of three months.

I use a 10,000 lux light in the morning with my coffee. It helps with the worst symptoms...and allows me to get to sleep at night. But it really doesn't give me the perk in the day like getting natural light does.

The Verilux light is just what it claims to be...supplemental sunlight. I start work at 8:30 in the morning...and keep it on the "high" setting until lunchtime. (When weather permitting, I try my best to spend at least a few minutes outside.) Then I turn it on the "low" setting for the rest of the afternoon.

The effect that it has had on my productivity is dramatic. My eyes stay open at my desk. I can concentrate. I am no longer contemplating grabbing my belongings and making a mad dash for my car in the middle of the day. (And unemployment.) I keep the light behind...and about 45 degrees to the right of my computer screen...so the light is almost in my peripheral vision...and have had no problems with eye strain. To the contrary...I find that I have a greater ability to focus...and need to take fewer breaks.

The only cons are that the light is a little flimsy. If you have a dedicated desk and can just set it up and leave it...then it's totally worth it. If you need something portable...one of the smaller LED lights will hold up better. And it's NOT a SAD light. But it IS a great supplement to the outdoors for those of us tied to a desk all day.

title: An okay product ruined by lack of or bad instructions
text:
I wanted to like these. I really did. But in good conscience I can't recommend them because the instructions, when you can actually find them, are unclear at best and dangerous at worst.

First, when you get the package, you get two separate bags each with a disassembled bottle in them ... and that's it. No "hey, you'll need to buy this kind of salt to use this." No "only use distilled or sterilized water." No instructions on how to assemble them, let alone use them.

I suppose I could overlook this if the parts went together in a really obvious way (and depending on you, they might - they did for me) and that the bottle works like you would expect it to, but it doesn't. Instead it uses a unique click-button to start and stop water flow, but the only place you would learn that is going to the fourth picture deep on the updated product page on Amazon, and even then it's full of grammar and formatting errors and graphics that were hastily thrown together - you can even see they yanked the image of the pen from somewhere else and "painted" over the original text.

The page also advertises that it's able to be boiled, but can't actually touch the pot it's boiling in. What's more, it's advertised as being heat-resistant up to 100 degrees Celsius ... which is the boiling point of water. So according to this it can be boiled, but can't handle the temperature of boiling. Another reviewer tried to get around this by microwaving the product but the plastic apparently deformed and now leaks. As others have stated, if you get this product, your best bet is to boil the water separately, let it cool, then mix in your salt and add it to the bottle.

This could have been a decent product. But the lack of instructions - and flat-out contradictory information on the product page - make this almost dangerous unless you really know what you're doing.

title: A great alternative to the name brand
text:
I have (and love) an Oral B electric toothbrush. It's the kind that spins the head, it's older, it only gets a day out of a charge, and someday it will die. This toothbrush came up in my Vines queue, and I thought I'd try it as a possible replacement - with my old brush (purchases in 2011), it's just a matter of time. In the meantime, I thought I could use this as a travel toothbrush as I travel extensively for business.

First, though, the issue of the vibrating toothbrush (this kind) versus the spinny kind (my old brush); They both seem fine, but it seems like the spinny one is more rigorous. It just happened that I was at the dentist last week for a cleaning and checkup, so I asked. First of all, my dentist and hygienist both said the fact that I am brushing extensively is obvious, so an attaboy there. Second, my dentist explained that the studies he has read say there is no difference whatsoever between the two types, so pick the one you like. Finally, he said the biggest benefit is the timer that lets you know when 30 seconds are up so you brush each quadrant of your mouth for 30 seconds, and your total mouth for 2 minutes. In fact, he said, if you used a regular toothbrush for two minutes it would likely be as good as either of these types. The problem is that the average person (according to my dentist) when told to brush for 2 minutes without a timer brushes for 37 seconds. Enlightening!

So I tried this brush, and it's great. The default settings work just fine for me, but you can dial back the intensity. Remember, I'm used to an electric toothbrush, but you may need to acclimate. It holds a charge for as long as I've tried it (4 days), but I'm not sure that's an issue; the charging base is tiny so you can take it with you if you travel or use it as a holder when home. I like that the unit shuts off after 2 minutes; if you want to brush longer, have at it; just hit the on button again.

Another thing I was concerned with was the replacement heads; my initial thought was that I would have preferred the option of buying heads locally, so I went to my local drug store and bought a couple of different heads to see if they would fit. While they looked similar, none fit, so unless you find one I didn't you have to buy them on Amazon. That being said, a 2-pack of store-brand replacement heads cost $16, while a "HIEIE Electric Toothbrush Replacement Brush Heads Refill, 4 Count" only costs $10.99. This negated my objection; if you're concerned these may not be available someday, stock up, they're cheap!

I also like the carrying case, although it would have been nice if the brush heads snapped in a little tighter (they rattle around) and if there was a place to store the little charger base "puck". And, if you want a good laugh, take a look at the owner's manual - it's full of typos and bad translations. Things like "Battery can not be replaced by self, can only be replaced by authorized by our Maintenance Center or Manufactory professional person. Nonprofessionals are prohibited to remove the product". Do yourself a favor and read the manual. It's short, and it's a hoot!

In summary, it appears to be well made, works well, is dentist approved (my dentist, at least), is inexpensive, comes with a nifty case, and replacement heads are reasonable (I just ordered some). I recommend this and could see buying another one to have a home one and travel one. Highly recommended.

title: Has improved my foot comfort
text:
I've been working over 11 years as a pharmacy technician at a large retail chain pharmacy and I stand 8+ hours a day. I usually find myself standing on one leg and switching that out a few times during the day as a way to relieve 1 foot at a time.

I opted to do a review on this item and so far I'm glad to have tried them. The directions do say to only wear for a few hours a day when you first start them. Perhaps that could be beneficial but I really didn't have time to swap insoles out. I didn't need to trim them to fit my size 11 New Balance 409 series shoes, they just fit right in after removing my old insoles.

So, I just started wearing them all day right off the bat. The first 2 days were a little uncomfortable. I've worn shoes designed for all day standing that were far worse. The insole does have my heel higher than I'm used to. This did make my calves feel a bit of tension, but not in an uncomfortable way. My arch is also supported in a way that I haven't been used to.

I still have found myself shifting my feet and sometimes lifting one up but nowhere near like I used to. I've been wearing them almost 2 weeks so far. When I'm able to walk out on the floor to show a product to a patient, my feet are super comfortable feeling with them. In the evening I don't notice my Achilles tendons feeling stiff after I'm able to sit down.

I know I'm heavier in weight than I should be and that probably compounds my problem as well. We also have anti fatigue mats, which I hate, and rubbery floor tiles. I don't know if that changes how these feel overall vs an actual hard floor. There are just so many factors that go into finding a shoe or orthotic product that will be comfortable to you.

These might be worth a try for you.

title: This basket is a lifesaver. Fits the small Vive Knee Scooter
text:
I have been in a boot for 2 months. I have two Vive knee scooters, one for the car and one for the house.
This basket fits perfectly onto the two little prongs on the front of the Vive where the back pack usefully goes. The basket does come with a bracket if you want to attach it some where else on the frame. I have considered rotating it to the inside of the neck (using the bracket) because when you roll up to the counter the basket hits about 4 inches before the wheels. I have to over extend a bit to reach the sink.

I keep my scooter parked next to me at all times and everything goes in the basket for transport to and from the kitchen, bathroom or where ever. Even taking water from the pantry to the fridge, is much easier when you can just load up the basket. I can fold my clothes at the dryer, stack them on top of the basket and balance them with one hand to wheel them into the bedroom. Life is so much easier with this basket.

I can drive if I have to so if I miss something on my delivery list, I do run to the store occasionally. It is most awkward stuffing things into the backpack (that came with the scooter) when you're rolling through the store and I originally ordered the basket specifically for that reason. I was pleasantly surprised at how helpful it is around the house.

I bent the two prongs on the car scooter getting it on the first time I used it so the basket is not very stable but still works fine just. I'm hesitant to adjust the prongs because I only have one basket and need to swap it between the two. It's more a concern for the prongs giving out than the basket. Yesterday I put a case of pure protein (protein drink) in the basket. That weighs at least 10 pounds. I tried standing it up but the basket was not very stable (because of the bent prong) so I laid it across the top and it rode securely through Sam's and out to the car. I did have to stabilize the drinks going across those bumps at the door and ruts in the asphalt but the weight did not stress the basket at all. The basket was well worth the minimal cost.

title: BUYER BEWARE
text:
I have been using NiteWhite for more years than I can recall, and have always been extremely impressed and happy. But this time, with this product, I was anything but. When I opened the package, I was shocked to find these skinny syringes that held far less than half the amount of product I'd been used to for all these years. And with no reduction in price.

After reading through a number of other descriptions and reviews of this same product, I discovered that the full-size syringes I was accustomed to are 2.4 ml, and those products that offer this size specifically say so. If the description doesn't tell you what size the syringe is, you can and should assume it's the really small size. This product is the really small size.

And don't fall for the repackaging of this product that they're now calling ZOOM. Actually, don't fall for the packaging they show you of any of them, because that's not what you'll necessarily get, as many reviewers have noted, and now they "mention" this might occur in the description, too.

What they don't tell you, is that some of this product is counterfeit and doesn't work at all. That's why you see some reviews from really unhappy customers - it's not them, they received a counterfeit product. The company that fulfilled the ZOOM I got was SmileMedic, and I wouldn't trust them ever again, and neither should you.

When I called Amazon about it, they couldn't have been nicer about it and refunded my money immediately. I offered to send the rest of it back so they could have it tested to prove that it's counterfeit, because Amazon doesn't need to get the reputation for selling counterfeit products. Until they get this straightened out with SmileMedic, I suggest you save yourself the grief and don't buy anything from that company, and if the stuff you get from anyone else is counterfeit too, let Amazon know.

title: I'd urge you to consider other robots.
text:
If I could give this a rating below 1 start I would. This is the WORST vacuum cleaning robot I've ever used. I've been using vacuum cleaning robots since the iRobot Discovery and have used about 9 different iRobot models as well the Samsung robot I currently use. This robot could not find it's way out of a corner, literally. In my entrance foyer with literally one piece of furniture (a small table) it continuously got caught on a 5/8" quarter round which was a joke. It could not go onto or off of a small area rug (very thin) without getting caught. Worse yet when it gets caught, it doesn't beep for help or alert the cell phone app. It just sits there and burns through the battery running the motors on the wheels non-stop.

If that wasn't bad enough the app design is poor. When you go to discover the robot it will show a name like "Hoover 6" and the red circle keeps spinning (so I think it is still discovering or connection). Nowhere does it say to select the name to continue, but that is indeed what you have to do. I do like that the app shows remaining battery life. You can watch the battery drain while it sits in a corner and cannot figure out what to do.

Couldn't make it over small transitions on a wood floor that my Samsung and iRobot vacuum cleaning robots maneuver every day of the week.

Vacuum cleaning area is NOT the full width of the robot. The width is less than a dollar bill (6") which is way smaller than ANY of the iRobots and smaller than the Saumsung.

I'd urge you to consider other robots. This literally isn't worth the shipping cost. If you get free shipping, it isn't worth the cost of your electricity to charge it. I can recommend any of the Roombas (700 and 800 series are power houses) and my current favorite which is the Samsung PowerBot.

title: Not for self admin!
text:
One of the first things I do with a tourniquet is try and put it on myself, and this one is not easy to manipulate with one hand. I do have a fair bit of medical training and I have slapped on CAT / SWAT T types on limbs countless times with one hand, but the one thing I need in a tourniquet is the ability to strap it on myself tightly. There is an intrinsic design issue with these in that the hook and loop backing on the strap adds to the friction of the strap coming through the buckle, thus making the initial "pull tightening" of this tourniquet very difficult with one hand. You have about eight seconds to put this thing on in the worst-case scenario, it takes me about twenty seconds to put it on my arm. That does not sound bad unless you have seen an arterial bleed, you then realize that extra twelves seconds is about the time it takes to go unconscious from a femoral bleed.

With that said this tourniquet is very strong, and it definitely compresses hard enough to stop blood flow. There might be some trauma around the buckle which is cinched up against the victim- a not so ideal situation but tolerable for emergencies. The windlass holds up under standard temperatures, but I have yet to test it in colder temps where cheaper tourniquets usually fail / snap. After living in minus 30-degree Fahrenheit weather for years being involved with outdoor casualty care, windlasses snap like twigs in cold weather. DO YOUR OWN TESTING.

The value of these tourniquets comes with a price. You do get a serviceable tourniquet but not for self-administration rather, it is good to use on another person if needed. Other than that, these are robust enough that they can be used as emergency standby units or mass casualty events where multiple providers are tending to multiple injuries. For first responders especially those of a martial nature, I am hesitant to say these are appropriate. If you want a great latitude of use, then half of the utility of this tourniquet is lost if you cannot put this on yourself.

title: Not for holding a handheld with the water on
text:
The Portable Shower Arm Safe-er-Grip sticks just fine to my tiled shower, and provides an out-of-the way place to put the handheld when it's not in use. HOWEVER, it is NOT functional if your intent is to put the handheld in the Safe-er-Grip and use it as a fixed showerhead with the water on. The reason for this is that the maximum declination angle is barely 5 degrees. So the water stream will be almost horizontal.
Although there is a ball joint connecting the piece that holds the showerhead to the suction cup, it has no stiffness at all. Basically, it will always be at the maximum allowed angle if it is holding anything of any weight. This was relevant to me since I have a corner shower and thought I could get around the angle limitation by mounting it on the side wall rather than the back wall. Unfortunately, while the up/down range is almost non-existent, the ball joint does spin completely side-to-side. What this means is that as soon as you rotate the showerhead a bit to the side, the top heavy nature of the showerhead causes it to topple over.
Looking at the picture for this item it shows a a handheld shower with a fairly extreme curvature. It may be that if you have one that curves at a 40 degree angle, you would get around the limitation of the Safe-er-Grip. If you want to test it, put the base of your showerhead against the wall, tilt is out the tiniest bit, and then turn on the water. If it's at an angle that you want to take a shower at, this might be the product for you. Otherwise, the only use for this item is as an out-of-the-way place to put your showerhead when it is not in use (be sure you take it out before you turn on the water).
In defense of the Safe-er-Grip, I will say that I did not see the problem other reviews have raised with it not sticking to the shower wall. It sticks great to my tile shower wall (assuming I don't try to span the grout between tiles). In fact I had to work to get it to release its grip even after opening the clamp when I was moving it around. Obviously YMMV with the surface you are trying to stick it to, but it should stick great to a clean, smooth surface.

title: Cheap plastic
text:
This one looks a whole lot better in pictures than it does in reality. That shiny metallic look is just silvery-looking plastic. And that includes the parts where strength is essential. The piece that attaches the shower head to the threaded pipe arrived broken--the plastic was cracked making it easy to see just how flimsy it is.
There was a time when American Standard built solid, durable products. In 2007 Bain Capital bought the American Standard name for kitchen and bath products. I guess applying that name to this sort of shoddy merchandise is the result.

title: works great
text:
I ordered this for my husband who has inflammation in his upper arm and thigh following a fall. His doctor recommended treating with a heating pad three times a day. Our traditional heating pad worked okay for the thigh but wouldn't stay in place on his upper arm without holding it the whole time. We saw a few online that were more fitted for the shoulder and were in the $40 price range because they were electric. That was another problem too, since the cord always got in the way and kept him stationary near an outlet.
What we liked about this was that it was NOT electric but has a gel pad that can be heated in the microwave for heat OR cooled in the fridge or freezer if that was needed. It offered two treatment methods in one and was less than half the price of the electric ones. The Velcro strips that old it in place give the rectangular pad more options for use on different parts of the body and for different sized people. The only criticism is that the Velcro strip for wrapping around the body (as pictured) might be too short for a comfortable fit around a large person. My husband is 5'6" and 160 pounds, and if the strip were any shorter, it would probably be too tight on him. He has only used this for heat so far, but the gel pack holds the heat for the full 15 minutes that he is to use each time, so he is pleased with this. I think it is a great alternative to electric heating pads.

title: Same as any other BCAA
text:
This review is for the Gen One Nutrition- Intramino BCAA Amino Acids Powder (Watermelon). In my house we typically use the BCAA supplements as a post-workout recovery drink. This particular powder says that it is an energy drink, or more specifically an "intra-workout" formulation. As such, and given the name "Intramino BCAA", it appears that is the core target for this drink. Per the manufacturer, this drink is intended for use DURING your workout, as "the period in-between the start and end of your workout is the most critical time frame for results."

Honestly, it depends on how you use BCAA's. Some folks recommend consuming pre-workout, some during, and some after. As noted, I've always preferred to consume it immediately post-workout or even before bed to aid in healing and recovery and reduce soreness. In the case of this supplement, I thought perhaps it contained caffeine or something, given the 'energy drink' label. Oddly, I found no evidence of that on the packaging. Nor does it contain sodium chloride (table salt), sodium citrate, or monopotassium phosphate -- all key ingredients of popular hydration/electrolyte drinks. Aside from the amino acids and vitamins, it only contains sucralose (e.g., Splenda).

So give that, I really see no added benefit for use DURING your workout vs. any other time. To me, this appears to be in the marketing. And given that this is intended for consumption DURING your workout, I would say "no thanks". It just doesn't mix that well, and the taste is NOT "Amazing". It mixes well enough, if your goal is to mix it, shake it, and chug it down. But if Gen One thinks I'm going to sip on this throughout my workout, they need to go back to the drawing board.

Giving this 3-stars for "it's okay."

title: Not a bad supplement, but taste is... strange?
text:
I'm big on BCAAs, but not so much as intra-workout or pre-workout supplments, as much as POST-workout.

For those who promote use during workouts, the belief is that they reduce fatigue during exercise by limiting the entry of tryptophan (the stuff in your Thanksgiving turkey) into your brain. Your body uses tryptophan to make serotonin, which may contribute to fatigue (that's why you feel so sleepy after that big dinner).

Honestly, there isn't that much research on the pre-workout or intra-workout effects of BCAAs. HOWEVER, they can help reduce muscle damage and soreness. It is generally accepted that BCAAs may relieve soreness, strain, and inflammation caused by exercise. BCAAs can also stimulate the synthesis of protein in your muscles, which promotes muscle-building. They also suppress the breakdown of muscle protein (and thus, muscle loss). Finally, it is understood that intense exercise can result in reduced immunity, which may be due to a decrease in the amino acid glutamine. Glutamine is a fuel for immune cells. Since BCAAs can be converted into glutamine in muscle, they can help promote the immune system.

From my personal research, I have found that the consumption of BCAAs anywhere from 30 minutes to 3-4 hours POST workout can really have a discernible impact on recovery. And THAT is why and when we use them in my house. I drink them after a hard swim. My kids drink them after super-tough track, football, or swimming practices or tough workouts in the gym.

So from the perspective of BCAAs, this product seems to have it together. BUT, the "Blue Hawaiian" flavor is.... strange and kind of disgusting. I thought it would be like the drink (rum, blue Curacao, pineapple juice, cream of coconut). The only thing I can really taste is the coconut, which pretty much tastes like chugging suntan oil after a tough workout. This really needed more citrus flavoring, as well, to balance the taste. The kids definitely do not like this one, and will only use it as a mix-in for smoothies, where the coconut flavor actually adds something. Mix it with a banana, some OJ, some pineapple juice or slices, and some ice, and it's tolerable.

title: Excellent hearing protection
text:
These DownBeats ear-plugs solved a major problem for me. Aside from needing to use ear-plugs regularly as it is, since I am in loud live music situations often (as a musician, and a concert photographer), I also recently suffered from Hyperacusis (due to Bell's Palsy) that causes extreme sensitivity to certain sound frequencies and volume, and makes any loud noise unbearable. These ear plugs were fantastic. I would compare these to the Eymotic ear plugs as well, although there are subtle differences. These seemed to fit a bit more snugly in my ears, thus keeping the disturbing frequencies out, while maintaining a proper hearing situation without muffling.

The only "complaint" that I would have is that these are considerably smaller than the Etymotics, and can feel "lost" (stuck) in your ears. This caused an obvious immediate panic the first time I used them, until I quickly figured out how to remove them easily (by twisting them to loosen the tight seal in the ear). But in comparison, while both are great companies, these seem to block out the frequencies a bit better. A definite must-have for anyone around loud music or any other noise, and an a necessity for any musicians. Hearing is important, and we too often take it for granted. Protect your ears. Use these.

title: Quality you can feel...
text:
This is my third Cielo pill holder. Like the other two, it does not disappoint. Beautifully machined, a joy to hold and admire.

It differs from the other two in a few respects. The first is size. This one is substantially larger. More so than it appears in the picture. I weighed all three and they weigh 64gms, 33gms, and 22gms respectively. Not the sort of thing you want to put on the ignition key of an older GM car (a poor attempt at humor).

Also different is the text on the bottom is machined rather than printed. Beautifully done. And lastly, where the smaller ones really shouldn't be closed completely, this one can be closed completely so the O-rings are not visible. Although you don't have to to seal the containers securely.

As a matter of personal preference, I found a larger split ring made from flat stock to put on this holder. The ring that comes with it is perfectly adequate, but I think the quality of the larger ring better matches the quality of the holder. I can't remember where I got it but similar [[ASIN:B008LT3L7Q rings]] can be purchased on Amazon.

Included with this holder was a nice suede(like) pouch. But I doubt it will spend much time hiding this beautiful holder from view.

Just like you don't have to buy a diamond if a Cubic Zirconia will do. Or a Patek Philippe watch when a Timex keeps perfect time. You don't need a Cielo pill holder when you can buy a cheaper alternative. But if you're reaching for that Nitroglycerin you have stowed in it, you can't help but realize you only live once. And unlike that diamond or watch, it's a small price to pay to get the best.

Pictures of my 3 pill holders (with AA battery for comparison of size), machined bottom, alternative split ring, and provided storage/gift bag.

The biofeedback unit attaches to 3 fingers, and measures skin conductivity and heartbeat.

Since I already had the biofeedback hardware, the software only cost $80. I don't know if I'd pay almost $300 for the package, but the software put my already purchased hardware to good use.

I am pleased with this purchase.

title: Strong, absorbent, good for non-optical surfaces.
text:
These 12" cleanroom wipes serve nicely for spill control and general cleanup tasks. The polyester/cellulose composition provides excellent absorbency for cleaning solutions or solvents, and the wipes maintain good strength whether wet or dry. As with most cleanroom wipes, these are double-bagged at the factory to reduce contamination, but the bags are not as sturdy as those found on other brands I've used.

The wipes' non-woven construction allows for moderate stretch on one axis and almost none in the perpendicular direction. The wipes generally produce very minimal lint in use, but their fibers can be loosened on rough surfaces, so you'll want to stick with woven products for the most demanding situations.

Where these wipes come up a little short is their performance on optical surfaces. The wipes seem to contain a moderate level of water-soluble residue, which can result in slight haze or streaks being deposited on some surfaces (anti-reflective glass, for example). I have worked with other brands of non-woven poly/cell wipers that exhibited much better purity in this regard.

Overall, I'd give these wipes a four-star rating. Their strength and absorbency are ideal for containing spills and for general cleaning, but they're not sufficiently residue-free for wiping optical surfaces.

title: Odd packaging -- is this supposed to be oily?
text:
I was so excited to receive this package today, just as I was getting ready to do my twice daily foot soak. My toe had gotten really badly infected (long story) and is on a very slow road to recovery. As part of my treatment, I have been soaking in in sea salt or himalayan salt water twice daily. While my physician guessed by looking at photos (due to the pandemic) that it was a bacterial infection and prescribed antibiotics, as it is healing, I have been concerned about fungus getting underneath the separating nail. (TMI, I know!)

When I opened the Amazon package, I immediately noticed that the package inside was all oily -- even though it wasn't opened. When I opened the package, I could see that it was oily clumps of salt. The package does say that it is a "soak" rather than a "salt," and it definitely includes essential oils, so maybe this is how it is supposed to be. (I had thought it would be granular.) If this is how it's supposed to be, then the packaging is really poor. It is a recloseable bag -- but the bag is coated in oil. This product really should be in a large jar instead.

Considering that I was unsure of this product, I decided to try it out on my "good foot." The product dissolves easily in water, and it did feel nice on my foot -- there was no irritation. It left my foot feeling very smooth. The smell while soaking is very strong to me (but I am sensitive to scents). It does smell like tea tree and lemongrass to me. If someone is trying to correct foot odor, this would very effective.

I have tried to give my balanced opinion about this product. I do think, for sure, that if this is the correct consistency of the product, then it should be contained in a jar, rather than a package.

title: Remarkably effective...but really, $12 for ONE scouring pad?
text:
I didn't realize I was ordering one scouring pad, not three as the photo implies (even if the intent is to show design variations). A similar product here is a bit less pricey for what is clearly stated as three European scouring pads (so, less than a third the price because you actually get three). The one I received has cute chicken drawings printed on both sides, blue (on a mustard yellow background) on one side, with the colors reversed on the other side. One edge has part of a red stripe.

While touted as non-scratch, the pad feels extremely scratchy (I don't use it on non-stick cookware). It easily removed stubborn crud from glass baking dishes that's refused to budge for years. So, five stars for function less two for price point/value. As for durability, TBD, but the pad is generously thick, which is a good sign.

Update (Feb 2020): While the pad has held up great, looks the same, and still works well, over the year it has become non-resistant to bacteria buildup and the consequent odor. Each time before and after using it, I wash it vigorously with antibacterial dish soap. After use, I apply Purell to it and let it air dry, but all to no avail...the bad odor always returns. I suspect the fibers are so dense that they trap food particles, which attract bacteria. I don't want bleach anywhere near my kitchen, but I'm going to give the pad a vinegar soak and then run it through the wash in a garment bag. With any luck, that'll do the trick. If not, I'm slaying the chicken design and feeding it to the trash wolves.

title: It Does NOT Work for me
text:
When I opened the box containing the Verilux Original Floor Lamp I knew I had my perfect light computer workstation light. The height and availability of a flexible light head were just perfect. The color of the fixture fit well. The light itself has two levels of brightness and each is controlled by a toggle switch in a perfect location under the head. A flexible next permits ease of setup and ease of changing just the head's position. The base is heavy enough to keep the unbalanced head from tilting over during most operations and I have yet to find a position that would cause it to fall over.

Then constructing the lamp from 3 pieces plus 2 1/4 inch screws (critical to construction) turned into a semi-nightmare. The internal cord was so stiff it took major tinkering. It is just a bit too long and it needs to be near perfect to make for the ideal connection between the base and the extension rod going to the head. After I finally connnected the base to the extension with one of the screws I found that the screw was just too small to hold the assembly above the base. I held the extension in place, connected the head with the other screw and found a similar but not quite as bad connection. Finally, I plugged the cord into the outlet and the light at either level is nice and handy. I took a "gather my wits" break and returned a few moments later to move the light to its permanent place. I forgot about the screw and just lifted the light by the extension and the bottom fell off. Oops and it never worked as it was intended to work.

I refused to be outdone by a lamp and make my very own Rube Goldberg light at my work station in the garage by plugging the cord into an outlet and attaching the base's cord to the head without the extension. I placed the head above the area that I use for close and tedious work such as fixing watches, clocks or computer parts and am happy with the results. Even though the original setup is faulty the final product is at least useful. Maybe I should have considered a higher score but it was too much work for such an outcome.

title: I can tell a difference...
text:
I've had this for a couple of weeks now. After reading the research on the Internet about therapy light, I learned that it varies from person to person how much light is needed, length of time needed in front of it, as well as what time of day it should be used. I read to use it within the first 30 minutes of waking up and/or throughout the day.

The first day, I used it as I was applying make up and doing my hair (which occurred within the first 30 min of waking up). I placed it on my vanity. Thinking that I would benefit from continued use of it throughout the day, I unplugged it, and took it to work with me and placed it on my desk. I felt more alert on the drive to work that morning.

I left it at the office for the next week (so I didn't have it at home in the mornings), and used it the afternoons. I felt no effect using it in the afternoons. Remembering my first day of use and how my energy level had improved when I used it within 30 minutes of waking up, I decided to take it back home and try that again.

title: Is It the Real Brand Stuff? Only Your Chef Knows For Sure
text:
When I ordered the containers, I failed to see that I would be receiving 6 packs of 3 containers for a total of 18 - 32 oz plastic food containers - it really helps to read what you are ordering - face palm! When the box arrived, it was big enough to hold a medium suitcase. My first inclination of them was that they appeared to look like the real ones. But opening a set of 3, I instantly felt the thickness of the containers & they were definitely not as thick or stiff strong as the named brands. However, the containers are well made.

I had planned to organize one of my refrigerator fruits & vegetables bin as my first test spot, but first a really good clean job. Cooking & meal cheeses in one, batteries in another - if you don’t know, don’t ask! - snack meats & bulk cheeses in another two - four total for one bin. I was duly impressed. Three containers with everything sorted, and just some bacon & a celery laying loose. They are a good space savers for anything in the frig or freezer.

After using the tubs for holding food, how good are they for reuse after a wash? Excellent - hand wash was was a breeze - sponge with a dab of dishwashing liquid & you are done.

I have seen & purchased similar containers @ the $1 store, but these are far superior. They are not a direct substitute for the name brand products. But @ the price, the versatility, size, & reuse ease, these tubs are a clear keeper. Your chef might know the truth, but he is not telling anyone. 5 Stars All The Way.

EDIT: I forgot to add that I would like to see the containers come in different sizes. That would make the container packages more flexible on what you can store/size of the product. After I saw my posted review, I saw that they do come in different styles & sizes. It also appears to me that the construction of the containers might be different depending on the style of containers that are purchased.

For clarity - the reviews here are NOT for the same style, shape & quality that is in each lot. I got the 64 oz. 3 pack of 6 bundles - 18 containers total in the lot.

title: Not Bad, but not Great Either.
text:
I purchased this because I'm a huge fan of star/constellation projectors and thought this would be a cheaper alternative to a high-tech, expensive ceiling projector. The only color that I'm impressed with is the green, as two of the color settings are screwed up (it shows three different colors at once on the pink and blue settings, which I first thought was supposed to be like that but then realized that something is either broken or damaged inside of the device) and the red setting can't even be seen well. I would definitely recommend placing this on a high surface, as lower surfaces like a nightstand or most dressers won't project the images correctly, leaving huge, stretched out stars and moons on the ceiling.

The sleep sounds are horrifying. There are only a few different sounds to choose from and each sound is incredibly muffled with static and it is just obvious that the sound box inside is of terrible quality. It also seems like the sound clips are only about 5-10 seconds long before they are repeated and it grows incredibly annoying after a while. After the first five minutes of trying the sounds out, I shut them off because I couldn't fall asleep. So, fundamentally, this does exactly what it's NOT supposed to do.

I'm rating this 3/5 stars because, if placed in a good position relative to the ceiling and on the green (or blue, if your blue setting actually works) setting, this could be cool. My nephew thought it was amazing and couldn't wait to get to bed so that he could see the stars above him before falling asleep. I believe that Conair has a great idea going; the product just lacks quality.

I don't know if it's all in my head, but then again pain itself is all in our heads since that's where our pain signals are interpreted - so what difference does it make as long as it works? I have a neurological disorder that causes neurons to misfire and create pain where there is no injury, along with pinched nerves in my spine which are real. For me, this little patch actually works - creating a noticeable decrease in the pain.

My guess was that the varying reviews mean that it works on certain types of pain for certain people, so I decided to give it a shot. (I also chose to completely ignore any scathing review that said "I haven't tried it but I'm certain it doesn't work.) I'm glad I did - I'm very happy with this purchase. My only complaint is that I wish there was a more flexible version that I could use on my neck. One of my pinched nerves is at the base of my cervical spine, and I can't get the patch to stick that high up. Other than that - well, I just ordered the refill package of adhesives.

title: Seems accurate.. Fixed the problem with rechargeable batteries so you can use them now. Decent quality
text:
I have this one, and an older version of this one.. A few differences that I have noticed between them..

The stats that they give are more "real time" on this one. The older version, it would give a reading, and only update about every couple of seconds. With this one, it changes almost instantly with the pulse reading. The readings I got were pretty much identical from this one to the older version. So I would say that it is pretty accurate. I have compared them both, at the same time, one on each hand. I have also had a couple of people try them out too.. Same results.. So far, everything is excellent..

One improvement that I noticed on this one is the spring.. The older version, I could not always get it to connect to a rechargeable battery, on the positive end on the one battery, because the spring hole was so big that it was against the battery where the insulation was.. On this one, I found it with rechargeable batteries, it connected with both batteries, the first time, every time. I took them out and put them back in multiple times to try this out. This is good because you can use rechargeable batteries now with no problems.

This comes with the meter, a rubber sleeve for over it (just like the older versions had), a decently made small case to put it in, a strap that you can attach to the small case to carry it easily, 2 cheap AAA batteries, and a manual.

So far, I have only had it for a day, and have only done limited testing.. But, considering my old one is the same brand, but just a but older, and I have never had a problem with that one.. I will take for granted that this will one last too. I will update in the future if I find any problems that are worth noting.

title: I’m ordering another can immediately—I never want to be caught without this!
text: I don’t know what kind of chemical magic this is, and I probably don’t want to know, but it works! I bought this to get rid of two mystery rings that appeared on my very expensive sofa after the Christmas holidays. The cleaning code on the sofa fabric is SW. I first tested the back of one of the seat cushions to make sure there was no discoloration. I sprayed this on the stains, let it dry per the instructions, and then used a toothbrush to rub the powder out (the spray becomes a powder instantly), after it had time to dry. I ordered an upholstery brush, but the bristles were too stiff for the fabric so I used a new soft bristled toothbrush. I wanted to make sure all of the powder was out, so I vacuumed to really make sure it was gone. I only planned on using this to get those stains out, but ended up cleaning the entire sofa. It looks like a brand new sofa! I Then remembered that a chair with cleaning code S had a water stain that I had forgotten about because I turned the chair cushion over. With nothing to lose, I gave that stain a spray and followed the same procedure, and it too was gone! I really wish I had taken before and after pictures. I was just about to cave and call a professional cleaning service and I’m really glad I found this product—it likely saved me hundreds of dollars. I’m ordering another can right now—I never want to be without this in case of a stain!

title: Nice Shaver, Concerned about Long-Term Blade Availability
text:
This is a nice shaver. It has a nice, long handle and a wrist strap so it's easy to reach every part of my back. The blades are super nice - two six-blade cartridges mounted together give you decent coverage. Prior to this, I was using a shaver with single-blade safety razor blades. That thing would occasionally put a big slice in my skin. With these six blade cartridges, though, you won't cut yourself because the pressure is spread out across all the blades so much better. It really does give a great shave and you don't have to be so careful like with single-blade back razors because this one won't nick you unless you are really heavy handed.

I will say, though, that I am concerned about long-term replacement blade availability. Will this manufacturer still make and sell these blades in a few years? These blades appear to be proprietary. I was hoping there would be a way to manually swap out the blades with other cartridges, but it doesn't appear that the head can be taken apart without snapping some plastic and destroying it. I've attached some photos of the backside of the shaver heads ... I should note that the metal screw does nothing other than hold down a small metal weight.

I like this shaver a lot, and I'm going to use it as long as I can find replacement blades. But I'm not going to throw out my old shaver that uses safety razor blades because I'll always be able to find those.

title: Product you may receive may not be the same as pictured.
text: I ordered these syringes based on the photograph.  I did not receive the same syringe as photographed and I am extremely disappointed in the syringes I did receive.  I use these multiple times a day to medicate our cats washing them between uses.  If you look closely at the Amazon photo, you will see the ONLY type of plunger that will withstand more than one use.  It has an o-ring on it and not the type of tip that is a separate piece that can come off.  The syringes I received were different and are totally worthless for using multiple times.  The tip of the plunger comes off inside the syringe if you are lucky enough to be able to force it down the syringe in the first place.  This makes it useless to me.  I have attached photos.  First photo is of the new syringe with the two-piece plunger that came with the syringe.  It is not the same as the one in the photo on Amazon.  Second photo is of the new syringe with an old o-ring type plunger that I kept and I am able to use with some limited success.  This seems to be the plunger that is pictured on Amazon.  Some of the new syringes are a bit larger than my old ones making the plunger a little too loose which in turn makes it harder to draw up liquid into the syringe.  The third photo is of the new syringe with the plunger that came with it inserted into the syringe.  I have pushed it in as far as it will go, which you can see is not very far making this set worthless.  The fourth photo is of the new syringe using my old plunger and as you can see, I am able to insert the plunger into the new syringe.  I ordered new syringes because after many, many uses and many, many washings, the numbers on the outside of the syringe come off.  This makes it difficult to get the right dosage.  If the pictured plunger for this syringe is no longer available then the photo should be updated to reflect the actual product sent.

title: SAVED MY SKIN! Updated review. 18 months of use now. No more acne
text:
Updated review 8.30.2013. I have been using this product for about 18 months. Still very happy with the product after using it a year. I have multiple repeat purchases of the product and it is still working well to keep my skin smooth and clearer than it would otherwise be without using this product.

I am 37 years old and I have been fighting a pitched battle with my acne prone skin since my earliest teens. Acne is a complex problem with a lot of causes.
I have used this product for about nine months. My skin absolutely looks amazing now. It GLOWS. I can actually leave the house WITHOUT MAKEUP and not feel ashamed anymore.
By glow, I mean it looks darn near flawless. I am getting compliments on my skin for the first time in my life.

I have sensitive skin. A word of caution:
Prep Skin Refresher CAN and DOES sting until your skin becomes accustomed to it. Work through it because the results are WORTH EVERY MINUTE of slight (or not so slight) discomfort.
The first time I used it I thought I couldn't handle it. I washed it off with water after about five minutes. I was mad at first but my skin was so smooth! The glow on my skin was unmistakeable and my makeup went on so smoothly I was astounded.

I decided to try again the next day. I repeated the process. wipe on, let sit for five minutes, rinse off. I had to do this for a few weeks until my sensitivity subsided.
I can now put on the product and it does not sting at all.

I use this product on my entire face, neck, chest, and upper arms. I follow with a good clean moisturizer.
In the summer, I use it on my legs to make them smoother. It does sting after you shave or exfoliate so plan accordingly.
I shave or exfoliate at least 10 to 12 hours BEFORE or AFTER using this product.

My other secret weapon is a Glycolic acid pumpkin mask. i use these two products together for smooth glowing skin.

title: 2 Distinct Colors... NOT 3
text:
I primarily bought these because they’re pictured as being 3 distinct colors... Grey, Light Grey/White and Charcoal. They’re intended to be used by 3 distinct individuals who share a bathroom but don’t like to swap micro-flora and loose epidermal cells in the shower. To my dismay, they aren’t what they appear to be in the photos. In person, it appears that they’re 2 distinct colors.... Light Grey and Charcoal.

As far as the “charcoal-infused” claim is concerned, that sounds great and all, but I don’t see any evidence of such. Sounds like a clever marketing ploy. And what are we going to do about it? Is someone going to hold them accountable for not actually infusing these with any considerable quantity of charcoal? Or course not.

$10 is ah-ight for 3 bath loofahs. Although, if these are just standard size, mass produced junk made with the cheapest possible materials, we could certainly do better than $3.33 per unit.

Oh yeah, the unnecessary description written in French on the front of package... Trying to convince us that this somehow makes it higher quality and therefore worth the extra cost; yet conveniently keeps the heading in English. It’s like this product expects us to be stupid.

If I sound grouchy I guess it’s because I’m sick of buying junk, not knowing where it came from, what’s in it, how it’s going to actually perform and paying way more than it’s worth. Now I have to make a trip to the store to get a 3rd colored loofah that otherwise appears identical in quality as to avoid the perception of favoritism to any of its 3 potential users. Thanks for wasting my time, whoever made these.

title: Very Impressive Filter Cleaner
text:
I used this filter blaster for the first time today on the cartridge filters of my robotic pool cleaner. It was a last attempt before spending around $130 for a set of new filters.
All I can say is “WOW!!”
I followed the instructions on the bottle to a ‘T.’
First I hosed off all loose debris, made sure the cartridges are soaked well with water, then sprayed them with the blaster, and let them sit for 5 minutes. After that, I hosed them off thoroughly (important, because if you don’t you could end up having foam issues with your pool), and right in front of my eyes the cartridges turned from blackish gray to a shade of off-white. They don’t look like new, because they simply aren’t, but they look nice and clean again, and have given me the opportunity to wait on buying a set of new ones.
The company recommends to let filter cartridges air dry if you have the option, because it gives the filter material an opportunity to “fluff,” which increases filter efficiency.
I am very satisfied with this product. From now on this will be my go-to filter cleaner.
Just try it out, and you will find that this filter blaster is worth every penny you paid for it.
Just look at the before and after pictures I posted. That alone should convince you of the amazing quality of this product. Way to go Applied Biochemists!!

title: Great For The Long Hose Shower Head
text:
I have several disability problems that keep me from standing in the shower for any length of time. I have a bath stool with a rotating seat that makes it easy for me to get in and out of the shower. For years I have had a shower head with a long hose that enables me to rinse off and wash my hair easily. The shower head would just hang down because I could not reach the bracket that the shower head is supposed to sit in for regular use. My husband who used to position it for me passed away a year and a half ago and I have downsized to a smaller place so I was just leaving the shower head down until........I maintain what I can do by just keeping things neat and have cleaners come it to clean the house for me, since I physically could not handle it. The cleaners have cleaned for months with no problem until a few weeks ago. I went in to take a shower and realized that one of the cleaning people had placed the shower head up in the top bracket that I cannot reach and I have a grabber, but I couldn't get the shower head unsnapped from the bracket. It was almost funny because all the previous cleaning days no one had done that. Luckily my daughter lives down the street and was able to stop over the next day to bring it down. I ordered this after seeing it on Amazon. I serves its purpose well and so far the suction has stayed firm. Now I place the shower head in the clamp and it should send a message to whoever is cleaning the bathroom, that is where the shower head should be.

I recommend this for anyone who uses the long hose shower head if for any other reason , then to hold the shower head while soaping up or shampooing. Also bath seats are becoming more common and it is better to have the shower head at a proper height. If there is any change with this review I will come in and put an update on it.

title: LOVE THE COLOR!  No Touch System Helps Prevent The Spread of Germs BUT ONLY BUY HANDWASH SYSTEM REFILLS
text:
I ordered this limited edition kids color hand wash system because my bathroom has bright colors with butterflies on the walls and a ruffled shower curtains with colors of yellow green to aqua in the colors. So the color fits in well. It works right out of the packaging although I hate the clamshell hard plastic packaging that is so difficult to open. Just remember to peel the sticker off the soap refill before you try to snap it into place. Also there is a piece of red plastic over the tips of the batteries, so you need to open the battery door and remove this before you turn the unit on. After you turn the unit ON before you try to use it. The on/off switch is located in the back and this system actually has the words ON/OFF unlike the kitchen one that has two symbols and I had to figure which one was the ON indicator by process of elimination.

Be very careful when buying a refill for the system. The pure corporate greed plays into this because the "Handwash System Refills" and the "Kitchen System Refills" look almost identical and both are 8.5 ounces BUT they will not work in the opposite system. I originally ordered a combo pack with 2 Kitchen Systems and decided to use one in the kitchen and one in the bathroom. This was because the Kitchen System's selling points are that it is also for hand washing and is antibacterial. I sent my sister a picture of the refill bottle and she bought me a set of 3 from BJ's at way cheaper than any I found on Amazon. I decided to make sure they worked because the 2 refills did look almost identical there was a slight difference in the curve on the top of the container. I found that the Hand System Refill DID NOT WORK on the Kitchen System. I don't know if the holes at the contact point are different or what but I ended up going back on Amazon and found this more colorful hand wash system rather than the plain white ones. I tried one of the my three hand wash refills my sister had gotten me and it worked great! It is so much better, especially in the bathroom to put the soap in your hands without having to press a soap dispenser or a bar of soap (does anyone use bars of soap anymore???). It certainly helps prevent the spread of germs by not having to touch the soap dispenser first. I do not know if they come in any other colors, but I didn't see any here on Amazon during my search. The shipping was super fast and I received it in a delivery today, which is a Sunday.

Snapping on that cosmetic cap deal that was included in the box, I applied cream to my face & neck, cranked up the vibration & warm red light and moved the headoc in small circular motions across my face, adjacent to my ear, under my chin, on my neck, behind my ear. It was extraordinarily relaxing, gliding effortlessly with the cream across my skin. It felt like a soothing upscale salon facial. I didn't want to stop. After a few minutes I put it down & OMG, no-more-pain! I think I'll actually get some sleep tonight! :) Thank you development team! Thank you crowd funding team! Thank you for a non-surgical, drug free treatment for the unbearable TMJ pain.

title: Nice tissues, boxes a little small, but a great value
text:
Well, they're tissues. I don't think there's anyone reading reviews on Amazon that doesn't know what a tissue is.

Thing is, a product like this is highly personal. What feels good on my nose doesn't feel good to someone else, so reviews like this can be hard to write.

My wife said that they don't feel like they have lotion on them, she said they're fine as tissues, but the "with lotion" part didn't seem like such a big deal to us. I checked it out, and it doesn't seem any different than regular one. Not like I expected them to be like baby wipes level of wet, but I didn't really notice it, either.

Still, they're a decent value for tissues given what they generally cost these days. There are also just 52 tissues in a box, so it'll go quickly if you plow through them when sick like I do.

Bottom line, it's a good value for tissues, I think.

title: Works IF you use it correctly and only need it for mild dizziness / nausea
text: Ever since my kids (I love them, I do), I can not stand motion.  Sometimes I even feel nauseous looking at my phone in the car; ugh!  I needed something to help with my pending trip to Universal Studios / Disney in FL.  I had read many a person had trouble with the simulators and I can't even swing on a swing set without being a bit dizzy.  So, I took a chance on this bracelet and I'm SO happy I did.  First, you have to follow directions - find the pressure point (as instructed in the product details).  Second, buy the bracelet that is not "adjustable" and adjust it yourself.  This may require help from another person to hold the stretchy ends of the bracelet.  I pulled out about 4 beads (I have teeny tiny wrists) and then retied the string.  This was a perfect "tightness" when I needed and I used it to pressure & roll between the tendons when I needed stability.  When I pre-emptively did this exercise, I had no motion sickness at all.  Lifesaver over the course of the 10 days.  I even had another member of my party feel sick after one of the rides and use it to positive results.  Don't expect a miracle folks, if you feel truly and deeply nauseous, you need to take a break; this bracelet might help you recover faster / better though!  If used correctly, this is a (fashionable) and helpful tool for motion sickness.

title: Awesome Sleep Aid and Mood Booster
text:
Source Naturals L-Tryptophan has performed miracles for me. It's an amino acid that helps build the brain's feel-good chemical, serotonin. I've used it for about 2 years after reading [[ASIN:0142003646 The Mood Cure: The 4-Step Program to Take Charge of Your Emotions--Today]] for its nutritional advice, upon the recommendation of this book: [[ASIN:0553380788 Protein Power: The High-Protein/Low-Carbohydrate Way to Lose Weight, Feel Fit, and Boost Your Health--in Just Weeks!]].

I was shocked by the difference it made for me in the quality and quantity of my sleep. I'd spent the last year or two waking up, wide awake, at 3:30 in the morning & was unable to go back to sleep. I take 1500 mg of Tryptophan (3 500 mg capsules) and 400 mg of chelated magnesium before bed and now enjoy deep and restful sleep. [I've recently added in another supplement, melatonin; you can read more about that at the end of this review].

I find that I am more resilient, resistant to stress, & easygoing since taking tryptophan.

I experienced its incredible mood-boosting effect earlier this year after enduring a ruptured appendix. I suffered several complications & had to be put on super strong antibiotics that depleted all my B Vitamins and sent me into a quick but INTENSE bout of post-surgical depression (much like what heart bypass surgery patients experience, according to my surgeon). I spoke with my physician to get his approval, then took just 500 mg of tryptophan that afternoon and then 1500 at bedtime, as usual, and bounced back to my usual cheerful self within JUST 2 DAYS.

Just a suggestion--be sure you're taking it on an EMPTY stomach (about 1-1/2 hours after eating anything).

This is an amino acid & any trace of protein in your stomach will compete with the tryptophan. Don't take with milk; take with water (some experts suggest a couple of sips of apple juice--but I use H2o).

If 3 capsules at bedtime (or an hour before) on an empty stomach won't do the trick after a few days, then it's possible you aren't low on serotonin. If you awake groggy, you're taking too much.

Here's something else that works: 400 mg of CHELATED magnesium (not just magnesium oxide, make sure it is chelated magnesium); the best I know of is this one: [[ASIN:B00014D2DW Chelated Magnesium 200mg - 180 - Tablet]]. Works wonders for sleep and health; most Americans' magnesium levels are chronically low, which can lead to heart issues and other preventable diseases. Get this book to learn more: [[ASIN:1583331565 The Magnesium Factor]].

Hope this helps someone out there; I wish I'd known about tryptophan 10 years ago!

P.S. For hardcore insomniacs for which tryptophan won't do the trick (give it time & remember to take on an empty stomach), try some melatonin; read my review of this product for more detailed info: [[ASIN:B001G7R49Q Source Naturals Melatonin Complex Sublingual Peppermint, 100 tablets (Pack of 2)]]

****UPDATE P.S. Also, please remember that supplements work slowly, over time. Metabolisms vary. Educate yourself; I highly recommend you start with [[ASIN:0142003646 The Mood Cure: The 4-Step Program to Take Charge of Your Emotions--Today]] to quickly "zero in" on your own personalized needs. Good Health (and good sleep) to All!

title: Decent product, very expensive juice equivalent
text:
The product is fine, easy to use, that's 5 stars. But the cost in juice equivalency is astronomical, 1 star. So I averaged.

The suggested dose of 1.5tsp (half a tablespoon) is nowhere near raw juice, which I researched after getting this product. Most tests using beet juice to improve athletic performance have the subjects drinking 250ml or 500ml/day (1 pint, or 1 quart.) Looking at a straight juice product labe on Amazonl, 8 fl oz has 100 calories. To get 100 calories from this dried product, you will have to use about 6.7 tablespoons in 8 ounces of water. The label indicates a pound bag has 45 tablespoons, so that's about 6.7 8 ounce cups, or about 1.7 quarts.

That's $15.29 cents per quart of juice equivalent. Using the lesser 250ml/1 pint quantity, that's almost $4/day for juice.

I've been incorporating beets in my diet for awhile, but man, are they a pain to prepare! And the red finds itself all over the kitchen. A little over half pound of beets has that same 100 calorie comparison. Since beets here in the USA cost a little under a dollar a pound to maybe a buck and a half, all depending, you can get your quart of beet juice with all the solids for $3-4. If you get beets with the tops, yummy cooked greens or chop and put in a salad.

Maybe Sprouts or Hole Paycheck has juice at a more reasonable price that what I can find here.

title: Should be Registered with the EPA as Methane Producers
text:
WARNING: Don't eat one of these if you intend being around other human beings (or small pets (or open flames)) starting 2 hours after ingestion and for an additional 3 hours after that. The gas production is flabbergasting. I mean it. Fog horns come to mind. Non-stop.

Now that that's out of the way, these "Fiber One Oats & Chocolate Chewy Bars" are very tasty and satisfying. They're moist and chewy, not dry and hard. The chocolate flavor is very good and predominates (as it should since chocolate chips are the 2nd listed ingredient). Outside of the whole grain oats, there's very little of that cardboard feel sometimes found in other health bars. Eating one is basically like eating a good chocolate chip type of cookie. Of course, these aren't really health bars (and Fiber One knows it since they're officially called "Chewy Bars") since the only thing "healthy" about them is the fiber from the chicory root and the whole grain oats. But given their low calorie count, low Weight Watcher point count, high fiber content, good taste, and overall satisfying feeling, I can live with that. The level of gas production also makes them self-limiting when it comes to eating more <g>. So, I'm happy to rate these at a Very Good 4 stars out of 5.

And, just for completeness, according to the Fiber One web site the ingredients are:

Chicory Root Extract, Semisweet Chocolate Chips, Whole Grain Oats, High Maltose Corn Syrup, Rice Flour, Barley Flakes, Sugar, Canola Oil, Glycerin, Maltodextrin, Honey, Tricalcium Phosphate, Palm Kernel Oil, Soy Lecithin, Salt, Nonfat Milk, Fructose, Malt Extract, Cocoa Processed with Alkali, Baking Soda, Caramel Color, Natural Flavor. Mixed Tocopherols Added to Retain Freshness.

From a Weight Watcher's point of view, each bar has 140 calories, 4 grams of fat, and 9 grams of fiber. Plugging that into their old formula gives 2 points per bar.

Ooh. You'll have to excuse me now. I ate one of these a bit earlier and now I have to go....
