title: Review and comparrison of this model to the Own Harmony
text:
I just received my Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER - Callus Remover today and used it. Before I go any further, I need to mention that before getting this model, I had the Own Harmony unit. I loved the Own Harmony that I had.

It was easy to use, and easy to clean. The only reason that I sent it back and got this one is because the Own Harmony is no Electric, is spite of their claims. The Own Harmony is actually a rechargeable battery. Im guessing that they think they can get away with saying it is Electric because you use Electricity to recharge the batteries.

Because the Own Harmony runs on batteries, it is not very powerful. I found that the rollers stopped rolling a lot when I was using it. I also found each time I charged it, it because less and less powerful. So I returned it for a refund and got this one.

Ok, now on to the review of the Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER - Callus Remover. If you did not try the Own Harmony 1st, you might not know or miss these features that I am going to be talking about. But since I did try the Own Harmony before I had this one, there are certain things that I did not like on this one.

Pros

I love, love, love that the Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER - Callus Remover is actually Electric. This makes it pretty powerful. I have pretty tought calluses, so I need a powerful unit and this one seems to deliver.

The power cord is pretty long, so for me, I can plug it in and still sit in my shower to use. If you dont have a plug in close to your bath or shower, you might have to use an extension cord. I think there will be some that will fall into this category, so I deducted 1 star because their cord is not longer. So I listed the cord as both a pro and con since it will depend on how far away your outlet is.

Con
Power cord is not long enough. Some people will probably wind up having to use an extension cord.

Hard to clean
If you have not used another unit like the Own Harmony, you might not know what you are missing. But, since I did use the Own Harmony 1st, I have to note this as a Con on this unit The Own Harmony is a breeze to clean. The roller has no protective cover, so it more exposed that one this unit. On this unit, the protective cover clogs up with skin that is being removed. This unit also has areas on it that skin gets into that are hard to get out of even with water or the brush they provide. The Own Harmony wins on clean up hands down!!

Rollers
Maybe it was because I was used to the rollers on the Own Harmony, but I liked them much better than on this model. They do not seem as rough and look to be not as durable, but the durability I wont be able to attest to for a while since I just got it. Also the way you remove the rollers is not near as easy as the Own Harmony.

Protective Shied
According to the manual, this protective shied is what goes over the roller and I guess is supposed to protect you. But for me, this protecting cover for the roller just gets in the way. Let me explain. With the Own Harmony, almost the entire roller is exposed, so I can use the device on any area of my foot with no problem. With the Emjoi Micro-Pedi, there is certain areas of my foot that are curved, like around the arches, that are very hard to use the device on because of this protective cover. So again, the Own harmony wins hands down.

So in summary, for the Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER I love love love that it is a true electric. But in every other category, the Own harmony is the winner. If only the Own harmony was electric instead of battery powered, it would be my hands down choice.

title: Prolonging your work outs and provide you with much needed sleep
text:
L-Ornithine can alleviate your symptoms like always feeling tired, not getting a good sleep, and just wishing you could exercise without easily getting tired
Everybody deserves to feel refreshed and energetic. This supplement can make that difference to those weary muscles. Prolonging your work outs and provide you with much needed sleep.

The sciency stuff: Your kidneys convert ornithine into arginine, an amino acid that benefits your body in several ways. Arginine is a precursor for a compound called nitric oxide, which helps dilate your blood vessels when you require extra blood to your tissues. Arginine also helps your muscle cells produce creatine, a compound they need to contract. Research suggests that consuming extra ornithine can help promote physical strength and endurance by increasing the L-Ornithine concentrations in the blood, promoting longer exercise period minus the fatigue that is caused by excessive ammonia concentrations in the skeletal muscles.

Besides this obvious benefit, the supplement L-Ornithine by Pure Science is gluten free and vegetarian. Also safe and potent for two years from manufacture date, it is a controlled amount of a single ingredient. Compared to "proprietary" blends you will know what and how much you are taking in.
I understand the help with exercising but I am kind of at a loss for how this helps with sleep. Exercise helps your body sleep and exercise without fatigue is great...But less ammonia and you get better sleep?
I still have insomnia. But that is really about not being able to shut my brain off and looping thought.
This didn't make a lot of difference for me. Not less fatigue either. Maybe it WILL help you.
I was given a discount on this to try the product and review. I am not expected nor have I delivered opinions that are not my own.

title: Bad brush, goofy use, expensive
text:
This product is really bad. The main problem is that the "brush up" hardly brushes at all. There is no difference here from just rubbing your teeth with anything. Your teeth do not feel clean after (see below for what does feel clean), and you still have the feeling like you haven't brushed your teeth. The second problem is that these really only fit small fingers. I have a larger hand and the brush up would only fit on my pinky finger. You also cannot get far enough back in your mouth because you're sticking your finger back there. Finally, the product is very expensive for what it does. A minor point is that you look pretty silly sticking your finger around your mouth, and if you try to reach far back, you'll get saliva on your finger/hand too.

The only reason this is a 2-star instead of a 1-star is because it does have some breath freshener... in fact, this is the only real effect of this product. You could get the same result by taking a napkin, pouring some mouthwash on it, and rubbing it on your teeth. You feel like you have some breath freshener, but you do not get a brush (which is supposedly the point of a brush-up).

This product is a gimmick, my wife and I went through one pack of these. Just stick with some mouthwash and you'll get more for your money and feel better. You need a real toothbrush to get a brush still.

title: Awesome small air purifier!
text:
I purchased one of these as I moved accross country in the middle of the pandemic as one of several disinfecting solutions, lights, gadgets,
gadgets and gear for myself "anti virus arsenal collection"
I knew I would be staying at random hotels that may or may not be deep cleaning and following CDC guidelines.

Have been sleeping with one of these plugged right next to me since August. I can breathe highly fresh disinfected air. You really can feel the difference!

I also purchased one of the large Guardian air purifier round tanks to place at my new apartment. People have commented on the freshness and air quality in the apartment even though I have smoked inside the apartment, which I never did before, but I moved to a cold state.

Neither of the air purifiers make much noise, and the tank has a silent mode, which makes it even quieter.

I just bought a new pair of these. I noticed there's a new version which is a 7 inch rectangular plug in. In looking at reviews and customer pictures, I decided to stick with this model, because it does not block the second outlet, like the new version seems to do, plus the plug rotates, so it can fit better, if needed.

The blue light makes a great soothing nightlight, and I don't like nighlights, so this is a compliment! First time I don't mind having a nightlight, specially right next to me. :)

I bought these two extra ones to replace the one I had been using since August, as I noticed, it was getting dusty vents. Cleaned the first one and plugged it in the kitchen, and will probably put the new third one in the bathroom, close to the living room windows or any other area inside the apartment, that may not have the best ventilation and air circulation..
This model is for small places. Hmmm...should check if there's an outlet in the walk-in closet.

By the way, I used the first one for 6 consecutive months 24/7, and other than a little cleaning of the vents with a microfiber dry towel, it is still going. I noticed many questions about how long does the light last, before needing replacement. Manufacturer says 6 - 8 months depending on usage. I can vouch that claim.

The replacement bulbs are available at Amazon at a very reasonable price. I have not purchased one yet. Ì figured I wait to see how all three of them perform over the next several months.

Bottom line, excellent air quality, performance and design! Great value for a fair price.

title: I found another use for this device....
text:
What convinced me that squatting is the way to go was seeing the toilets in India. They are ceramic and have a flushing system, just like ours, but that's where the similarity ends. They have purpose-made places for your feet astride an opening over which you squat. The first time I used one of these it just felt right. If you've ever back-packed deep into the woods you'll know what I'm talking about!
Some reviewers said they had difficulty with their clothing. I can't imagine what the problem could be. You sit on the toilet as you normally would with your garments at your lower legs, then you slide the Squatty Potty forward a few inches and one by one lift your feet up on to it. Couldn't be simpler. Please do not attempt to stand on the unit before sitting down - this could cause it topple over causing injury. Read the instructions!
While enjoying my new-found toilet experience I noticed my toenails needed clipping. Lo and behold - I was in the perfect position! After cleaning up I got right back on again with clippers in hand and went to work. Voila! Beats standing on one leg with the other up on the counter!
I ordered two of the bamboo units and one arrived with a cross bracket that was 1/8" too long. Being handy I quickly rectified the situation by sawing off the excess. I filled out their customer contact form on their website to explain what happened and received a prompt and apologetic reply from Wendy Saipale and a note that they would be sending me an Ecco Squatty Potty and a bottle of Turdle-Loo for my troubles. Now that's good customer service!

title: Poor Quality Poor Seller
text:
Changing my original review below from 5 stars to 1 star based on my most recent experience.

This was a huge hassle and disappointing experience. I do not recommend this product or this seller. The seller was neither helpful nor honest with the return and refund process.

I bought 2 of these in January and they are great. Same seller, and same product advertised. Well, the wood on the 2 new ones is unfinished. This wood causes splinters when picking up or sitting on it. Also has a strong wood smell. The prior ones did not have any smell and the wood is a smooth, soft texture with a shiny coat over it.

I contacted the seller for a return, explaining the issue. They stated they could offer $50 as compensation of the $112 I originally paid. They said I did not need to return the items. When I said no, I would return to Amazon for a full refund, they made an offer of $90, still below what was paid. I stated that was not acceptable. They also said Amazon would refund me the tax. I contacted Amazon who said Amazon said that is not their policy to refund taxes. Amazon advised I should open an A-Z claim. Once this was done then the seller emails me right away to say they can offer a full refund but I have to close my A-Z claim first. I searched online and this is not uncommon for some third party sellers. One thread said they were asked to close an A-Z claim, and they said that they were born at night, but not last night.

This seller pressured me on multiple emails to cancel my A-Z claim promising a full refund. I did cancel the claim not wanting to be hassled any further. They emailed me and I was refunded the full amount.

I sent the items back as I will not use them and I do not want the seller to come back and say I never returned it to them.

I have dealt with third party sellers before where they refund or replace right away, with no low offers.

Of course this seller did not want an A-Z claim on their record as it hurts their seller reputation. However, below is from their email:

If we refund you first, Amazon will directly end the case and deduct points. So we need you to close this A-Z claim first.
Please rest assured that we are an honest seller. We will refund you the full amount immediately after you close the claim, otherwise you can complain to us directly to Amazon.
So could you please close the A-Z claim first?

That was the third email asking to close the A-Z claim.

Not honest seller if offering $50 of $112 paid for defective items. This was time consuming and a headache.

Not happy. Be aware. Be warned.

Never buying from this seller again. Think twice before you do.

I purchased at a mattress firm shortly after starting my job one year ago and I felt it was time to review it. After my shift I drop it down a 15 foot ladder onto a tile floor with a smack, throw it on my truck seat, and drive home. It stays in my truck. On 16 hour cross country road trips near the southwest that includes ample offroading. triple digit temperatures, below freezing in camp chairs or on a cooler around a campfire. This thing is every bit as amazing as the day I bought it and I honestly cannot see myself going the rest of my life without this stupid thing. I mean, its just a butt pad, right? title: Great product, with one annoying flaw, but still worth the money!
text:
I recently used this lifting device and the battery ran out while it was lifting. I was trusting the battery meter to tell me whether it was holding a charge. All 4 lights lit up every time I pressed the button, so I thought it was fully charged. Then, I had to use it, It filled the bottom cushion fully, the second one to almost, then the battery ran out. It managed to eeek out enough lift to be useful, but I had to do the rest of the lifting. The battery display should give me an idea if the battery is low. Also, the charger should be powerful enough to either fast-charge the unit, or power the system while running, so that, in a pinch, the user can plug it in and get full performance.

Overall this product is great, it works well, and I tested it on myself before having to use it. It is worth the money, but it is probably best to leave it plugged in, so you are not fooled by the battery level meter that isn't accurate.

title: I really like this stuff!
text:
I found this company on Amazon and actually ended up ordering from their website instead (they'll mix the flavors for you) but wanted to leave a review to address some of the things I saw people saying on here.

1) Some people were complaining that the beef protein "foams up" a bit when blending and that "true" beef protein would NEVER do that. I'm not a food scientist who knows the answer to these things, but I have tried other organic, 100% no filler beef protein shakes in the past and they did froth a bit just like this one does. So...I'm going to say a bit of frothing is normal lol. I don't think froth means that all these companies are liars who put sawdust filler in the product :D

2) Some people were complaining that they HAD to mix the flavoring in my hand (which is apparently waaay more physical activity than they're used to). So here's my thoughts:

a) Go order off their website and they'll mix it for you! Problem solved.... :D
b) If you want to pay a lot more money, there are plenty of other preflavored options out there for you, which brings me to my next point of:
c) The company saves money by not having to create an infinite amount of flavor/protein combos and store them alllllllllll which in turn saves YOU (yes, you, the consumer) money in the form of a less expensive but good quality product. If you were wanting to throw away all your dollars on an expensive protein drink, you probably wouldn't have hit the "sort by price" button that got you to this product, am I right?? :D
d) Maybe it's just me, but I'm not sure why some people are complaining that you get the option to CHOOSE your own custom protein base and additives and flavors. Like..........wouldn't you be excited to be able to customize what you want rather than being stock with a stock item? I really liked the ability to customize my drink, personally.
e) Some people were complaining that they didn't "like" a certain flavor (and to them I say: go pick another flavor then and don't dump the whole container in before trying it! It's super cheap and you can pick lots of flavors so why wouldn't you?) and were complaining that ALL the company's flavors weren't available on Amazon (and for those folks, I can say: um, go to their website directly and pick whatever you want??).

Honestly I'm very happy with what I got. I went directly to their website and picked out my protein base and my additives and my flavors. Some people complained that the flavors were too light (and some people complained that the flavors were too strong, thereby reminding us that you can't please everyone and your opinion is definitely an opinion and not fact) so I chose to go "heavy" on one of my flavors BECAUSE I could then just add more water to the drink if I needed to tone it down. (OOO another point! Your drink flavor too strong? ADD water! Your drink flavor too weak? Add LESS water? Magic...... You're not forced to use a specific fl oz ratio; you can customize what works best for you lol).

I even ended up getting a second container with a premade recipe that I thought looked good and I ended up liking that one too!

All in all, this is a really affordable, good quality product that allows for a lot of customization (particularly on their website).

title: JUNK!!  Do not buy.  If you already own, NEVER move it...
text:
In the 13th month of ownership, the warranty and original battery simultaneously expired. Of course, the product and App didn't initially state that it had a low battery. On the contrary, it just started miscalculating weight - falsely overstating my weight at a progressive rate of 3 lbs a week. After a few weeks and total anxiety about gaining 15 lbs yet all my clothes still fitting fine, I decided to replace the battery. At that point, it couldn't reconnect to my wifi. After repeated removal of the battery and resetting the scale and my wifi password, it finally reconnected to the wifi. However, at that point, when I attempted to use the scale, the screen would indicate "THINKING... ERR." I called Fitbit customer service for help. They told me that since the problems started after the 12 month warranty expired, they would not cover any repair under warranty. They further told me that because I moved the scale around too much (most likely from flipping the product over to access the battery and reset button), I disrupted the sensor calibration. The internal parts that operate this sensor calibration are non-serviceable, so the device is now a paperweight... This is a known issue by Fitbit. Just do a web search on Aria Thinking ERR and you will see a multitude of unhappy product owners. The Fitbit customer service person even had the nerve to suggest that I upgrade to the Aria II scale since I had a problem with this one. Of course, they offered zero compensation to cover this upgrade cost... Don't buy this garbage product! Don't trust Fitbit. They don't stand behind their products, they put junk into the marketplace, they know it's junk, and they don't take ownership of the problems they create for clients. I would rate this as the worst customer service experience I've had in consumer products for as long as I can remember.

UPDATE - June 2019. I decided that after 18 months, I was going to try again to get this scale to work. Put in new batteries and connected it to the network / fitbit, with the hope that it would load a firmware update and fix itself... wishful thinking. I reached out to fitbit to see if there was a firmware update or some other resolution. Surely, if they had thousands of complaints on their fitbit community forum, they must have realized that they needed to take some accountability for this product. Again, I got the same nonsense response. Since the problems happened after 1 year warranty expired, there is nothing they can do. I asked for a suggestion on a quality scale and they said the Aria 2 was greatly improved over the original - the issues with the 1st generation were resolved in the manufacture of the 2nd. So... I asked if they clearly knew there were defects in the original, why didn't they reach out to customers during their warranty periods to ask if they would test for the defect (many reviews showing the same fail said it happened after the first battery change). This question seemed to freeze the customer service person I contacted. They had no answer on why a company claiming to be focused on customer service and care would do such an unscrupulous act. At this point, she said there was nothing she could do, so she transferred me to a supervisor. The supervisor hear this same question and said... "let me review the entire case file and repair claim and see if we can reach a final resolution." The conclusion of this call was unfortunate. This time, they offered to sell me a replacement Aria 2 scale with "free shipping" and/or a 3 month trial membership of Fitbit Coach... What a joke. They sold me a lousy product that they knew was defective at the time I bought it (I purchased it Dec 2016 after the Aria 2 was already on the market), they chose not to notify me during the 12-month warranty period of the potential product failure if batteries are replaced, then, after I got the product failure in month 13, they said, "too bad, you reported this problem to us after your warranty has expired, there is nothing we can do." I ask you... is this a company you would want to do business with?

I've been having issues with ingrown hairs on my legs for the past 6 months or so after I switched my hair removal method. I would say as much as 60% of my hair regrowth was ingrown, and my normal exfoliation routine wasn't helping much.  Well, this little stone is wonderful so far.  I actually use it all over my body (although I've never used it on my feet as many other reviewers).  You don't want to use much, if any, real pressure when using directly on soft skin.  Just move it across your skin and let the exfoliation begin.  I even use it on my sensitive bikini area.  This little stone is an unsuspecting, yet wonderful product that I will continue using for a long time.  Seems to be holding up well.  A few small stone bits do flake off every now and then, but nothing big.

title: Blade not sharpened.
text:
I have an older one similar looking. It worked well more than 5 years. I ordered another one. Trying to split tablets, it was very hard to press down. After cracking 2 into pieces, I returned for an exchange. The 2nd one arrived. Appeared to have a blade. Broke another tab into 3 pieces. The blade looking piece was very dull. Unable to cut my finger on that “blade”. Returned to amazon and ordered a different brand. It arrived yesterday. Quickly split 50 pills evenly without problems.

It’s actually a shame. The plastic part is very sturdy, feels nice in your hands, you can see through the plastic to see if your pill moves. But my butter knives are sharper.

Update: my old one, looks and feels like the 2 I recently tried from this vendor. Inexpensive but very sturdy, these allow you to see if the pill shifts as you lower the lid. A common issue with tiny and/or cushion shaped pills. Hoping this was just a poor batch as pill splitters are a cooking need and you can easily spend the cost of a meal for 4 in some. A comment I forgot and may have missed from someone else.

IMPORTANT. If your pills have a hard coating- sometimes called enteric coating- or not scored for easy splitting, ask your pharmacist before splitting. That EC can prevent some serious stomach upset and vomiting. Some pills, when split, might not have their ingredients evenly divided. Not a big issue if you’re trying to cut back on your pain meds. But could be an issue if the meds are for heart rhythm or blood pressure or something more serious. Just ask. Also, many meds can be ordered scored which is safer.

Hope the vendor gets the blade issue fixed quickly.

title: A quality product that I use as an adjunct therapy for my arthritic hip
text: I have an arthritic hip which was causing me a lot of pain during the past summer. It was bad enough to keep me from falling asleep or, if I did, it would wake me in the middle of the night. About 8 weeks ago I had gotten a cortisone shot in my hip (which helped quite a bit with the pain) but I also decided to purchased HerbTonics Turmeric C3 complex with ginger with the hope that it would serve as an effective natural anti-inflammatory that I could take on a daily basis. I've been taking it for 2 months now and between the shot and the Turmeric I am completely pain free. I'm even able to run and play with my friend's little poodle, Archie. Now... I cannot claim that my pain-free existence is completely due to taking this Turmeric supplement but I can say that I believe in a multi-pronged approach to pain relief which is how and why I chose to buy this supplement just before I received my Cortisone shot. A third thing I did was to resume wearing my orthotics once again which I should've been doing all along since I have feet flatter than the midwestern plains. With this three pronged approach I feel I can go on living a pain free life for hopefully some time to come. In fact, I feel so good that I even cancelled my hip surgery (which even my surgeon was pleased about). Multiple curative approaches to solve my pain issue has worked well for me.

title: HOW TO OPEN SAFELY
text: I was a little freaked out after I ordered 2 sets from their website, and came here and read about people’s issue with the glass.  DO NOT FEAR!  The tips must arrive scored a little because they break off cleanly.  USE A CLOTH!  I use a doubled dish cloth and snap off one end.  Then hold the open end over the glass and snap the other end and the liquid empties into the glass.  Someone described the same in the Q&A, but in case you didn’t read that.  The tips break off cleanly.  But USE A CLOTH!  I also shake the vial vigorously up and down before opening because some particles of the liquid settle in the tip at the bottom, so shaking dislodges them.  Otherwise, I just have to assume that the ingredients are doing what they are purported to do, support the liver which is good at detoxing if not overloaded, although in the 21st century we have to assume we are all overloaded.  We are foregoing our nightly glass of wine with dinner this week, and having a grapefruit and lemon cocktail mid-morning, salad for lunch, cruciferous  veggies at dinner.  I also bought a good quality water pitcher filter here on Amazon and now I double filter my water, Brita first, then Lifestraw glass pitcher.  It’s a shame we are surrounded by so many bad chemicals, but denial is not a plan.

title: Oriental junk
text:
In truth, this piece of junk deserves minus-ten stars. I'll begin with so-called instruction manual: I can't tell whether the Chinese version is worth anything, but the pidgin-English version is worthless. For one thing, it does not even mention the "charging stand" (which is touted in the product description), perhaps because it does not work at all. Here's just one of many examples of what I mean by pidgin-English: "Pls clean inside beard if the shaver can not work after you press the switch". Hire a native-speaker translator, for crying out loud!

Then there's the razor itself, which reminded me of that passage from the Bible that describes "plucking out the hair". Aside from that painful experience, there's also the fact that the red charging lamp is practically invisible, the adapter's charging indicator mentioned in the manual does not exist, and the on-off "switch" is scarcely visible yet overly sensitive, so that simply grasping unit can easily turn it off -- come to think of it, that may be one of its best features. In addition, the 5-bladed plucking head is much too large to shave any area except the cheeks and changing "tools" is very difficult.

Before I cram this worthless thing back into its box and request a refund, I'll just note that it does have an integrated side burn trimmer, which makes the trimmer accessory redundant.

Can I make any positive comment? Well, the box is reasonably attractive.

title: It says 350lbs, but that's for the pneumatics only, the rest of the materials will degeriorate with far less weight.
text:
Weight rating can be misleading. Its a standard generic, mid-back, height adjustable chair. The arms and anchors will not hold up to weightier persons despite the 350 rating, which is really just on the pneumatics only.

Leaning back in this chair will be what breaks it, usually in the arm's, as it relies on the arms to keep the back and seat together. If not the arms, then the nuts the screws anchor into, will break free from the particle board and then the chair is scrap.

If you're wider, and if you're above 200lbs search for a better chair, and sadly that will be in the 200 dollar range. The chair I use currently was a 2nd hand special, normally 899 new, 250 "used", but the the build, stability and life (10 years I've had it, plus who knows how long the previous owners had it) are excellent, and I was hoping a "heavy weight chair" would be enough, but its no comparison. The healthline chair is for thin people 200lbs or less, despite the BIFMA rating.

I've gone through 3 of the "350lb" chairs like this one ... I shouldn't have bought it and its too much hassle to send it back, I've got some kids that could use it when their parents come over..

title: Lingering taste
text:
These Bone Strength Health supplements suggest to take 4 per day in divided doses with food - so it is a month's supply per bottle.
The bottle has a unique tear-off tab to make it a flip top - it is a nice design and it was nice and securely sealed. There is a stamped lot# and my bottle and it has an expiration date 4 years, 7 mos in the future.
Note: it will be a little difficult for someone with hand mobility issues to initially open the safety seals.
The pills are on the large side but go down alright. Initially I did not notice much of a taste but after ~1/2 hour I did notice a building taste in my throat and also reaching up into my mouth - The taste is difficult to describe but lets say similar to other supplements but for these it came later and it persisted. If you take one capsule 4x per day as suggested, you will just need to get used to the taste as it hangs on quite a while.
My bottle contained two broken capsules and their dust was distributed throughout the bottle. It made the contents dusty and the dust is very pungent and sticks on/with you.
I am rating these as 3 star. The lingering taste and dust coating my capsules reduced my rating by a star.

text:
My husband has a serious disease which causes terrible pain in his rear end AND requires long trips into the city for treatment 5x/week. This cushion has made a big improvement in his quality of life by reducing his pain.

The Wondergel (Intelli-gel) cushions are designed on a very different concept than any other cushion we've tried, and we have tried them all- memory foam, gel, inflatables, etc. Read the production description, and understand that this cushion works and feels differently than other cushions. It took my husband a little while to get accustomed to how it works, but now he loves it. And I love that it works for him.

This cushion works so well, in fact, that I've shown it to my husband's doctors. The lead doctor on his care team is looking into recommending it for their other patients.

We also bought the Roll-and-Go Wondergel cushion, which is the low-priced end of this product line, and it also works well. For many people I'm sure it would be sufficient, but for people who have serious pain issues, go ahead and buy the top of the line. I'm glad we did.

A word to the wise: if you live in a hot climate, DO NOT leave this cushion in the car! Excessive heat will degrade the gel and cause it to lose its shape.

The only downside I've found: the shipping to SO high! We paid $22.70 for shipping, and I don't understand why. Climate controlled, maybe? Miracle Cushion cushion could do a better job of explaining the high shipping charges.

All things considered, this cushion is a superior product, and I would not hesitate to recommend it.

My wife got me the battery powered unit for Christmas, it was good, but the battery model slows down with the slightest pressure applie...BUT the electric model is awesome, it just keep chewing through any callus you may have - something common on the hells of the flip flop/sandal wearing crowd. The unit is lightweight. Has a removable A/C cord and power brick (about 2" x 1" x 1")...lightweight none the less and a fairly long cord, I'm guessing 5" so you have room to operate. The "Blue" sand paper buffer in the picture is released by a small sliding switch below the roller which allows you to put in new rolls. There are three coarseness levels - Blue = Extra Coarse, Black + Super Coarse, and Green is Xtreme Coarse...I used the Xtreme to get rid of some badly cracked and thick heels - took about 20-30 mins I'd guess (didn't time it)...and as I noted, my heels are pretty smooth. The finer grit (Extra) is goof for smaller callous and in no case do I think I wore out any of the roller buffers...they still have plenty of life even after doing both feet. Soooo, highly recommended - from a guy who has been using a pumice stone every morning for the past twenty or so years - this thing make the whole process much quicker and easier...love it.

title: Some small problems but overall not bad
text:
Basically, these pads function fairly well; but there are a couple of drawbacks. First, the edges are made of a flimsy material that has a tendency to fold back on itself. This results in not completely covering the underwear between the leg holes. No matter how careful I am, I can't prevent the edges from folding and leaving some material uncovered. Therefore, urine can stain the parts of the underwear that are thus uncovered. While almost all of the leaking urine will be absorbed by the pads, it's very annoying that because of this design flaw you will still get a little bit on the underwear.

The second fault is apparently intended to be a feature since it's obviously an intentional part of the design. There is a protective pocket that holds each pad and this pocket is glued in a couple of places to the strip of thin plastic that covers up the adhesive part of the pad. So the pocket and the pad are actually one piece. You're supposed to remove the plastic material from the pad to expose the adhesive portion so it can stick to the underwear. But due to the pocket material being glued to the plastic covering it is impossible to take out the pad without also exposing the adhesive of the pad. I guess this was to prevent you from forgetting to expose the adhesive before putting it in the underwear. I think it's an indication of how needless this "feature" is when you realize that women's panty liners do not have a similar feature that automatically removes the plastic cover from the panty liner to expose the adhesive. I guess men aren't smart enough to figure this out.

So now you must be careful to throw away the pocket while still holding the sticky pad, or else try to carefully put down the pad without having it stick to something. That is stupid. I would like to be able to throw away the pocket while not exposing the pad's adhesive until I am ready to install it. Now it's certainly not impossible to work this out, but it's an unnecessary nuisance and it just makes no sense that they went out of their way to glue the pocket to the cover piece.

In spite of these annoyances I will likely continue to get these pads since they otherwise suit my needs and will comfortably absorb almost all of any liquid that I leak.

In the past 10 years, I have wasted my money on countless other brands promising me a weekend setting, but none of them came close to this one. Even though I know I paid more for mine than what is listed on Amazon, I feel like I've gotten more than my money's worth over the years. title: You must do this if you want to mix it in hot drinks!!!
text:
I was just about to give up on this item and throw an almost full container away. I purchased this to mix into hot tea. I have no plans to cook with it to make jello or gummy snacks. I really should have purchased the collagen and that is what I will do next time.
But, I read a tip that prevented me from throwing this out.

You see, they say it mixes with hot beverages. So, I would brew my tea, throw out the teabags and while the tea was still warm, I would add 1 or 2 scoops of the gelatin powder.

It was SO HARD to get it to blend it and dissolve. I thought it was supposed to dissolve it hot liquids, what the heck is going on?? It would be one huge clump that would dissolve into smaller clumps, but it was SO STICKY! I would have to throw out some of the gelatin because I just could not get it to dissolve into the fluid. It was also very difficult to clean the spoon and mug when I was done. So, if this has happened to you, or if you don't want this to happen, then do the following. It will completely solve that problem.

In a small cup, add a small amount of cold water - I do approx. 2 oz. for 2 scoops. Sprinkle the powder on top of the cold water. Mix with a spoon. This hydrates the powder first so that it will dissolve completely in hot fluids. It should resemble a thick applesauce texture. Now, spoon it into your brewed hot tea (after you throw out the teabags). You will be able to mix it completely and easily!! That's it - easy tip to avoid a lot of frustration!! Just rinse the cup, spoon and mug with hot water when you are done. Cleanup is also much easier this way.

title: Recently Diagnosed with Diabetes...
text:
and it's been a challenge realizing and learning how to live with Diabetes, adjusting every aspect of my life and navigating the health care system. When I picked up my first insulin prescription pens, a once-a-day formulation, a box of 50 needles for the pens came with it. A day later I was prescribed a different type of insulin that I used several times throughout the day but did not come with the needle tips.

When I burned through the first 50 needles, I figured I'd just go pick up another box at the pharmacy but learned they needed to be prescribed for insurance otherwise are really expensive. The pharmacist recommended buying third party needles while we worked out the logistics for insurance.

I jumped on Amazon, did some research and landed on these because of price and reviews. They were delivered within 24 hours and fit my pens with no distinctions from the ones I had from the pharmacy. Since then, I've had two new insulin brands of pens. These needles have fit and worked with all of them.

I don't know if there is a "standard" all brands conform to, but they are compatible with the four different brands I've used. I'm very happy and am re-ordering as I write this review.

I've moved it to my bedroom because it's not worth the effort to pack up and send back but I will be looking for a better chair for my living room.

It may be worth a couple of hundred dollars, but don't expect much and I would not pay any then that.

title: Not quite as I expected
text:
First... the most disappointing aspects...

This is not a white noise machine. It has a variety of noise settings. I found some of them prevented me from relaxing. I certainly wouldn't use it to help me sleep. The first/default noise actually sounded like the unit's sound system was broken, and I perceived noises that sounded like voices. The water and storm noises were anything but calming. Some of the sound settings bother my dog. She whines when I play them. But that's okay as I don't find them relaxing. The water sounds... one sounds like water is flooding, the other sounds like the sink is dripping. The lullaby sounds might sooth a baby, or it might keep them up as they're not soothing to me.

The description says "USB Charging". That would imply to me that there is a battery that can be charged. But, not only isn't there a battery, but there isn't anywhere to add batteries. That makes this almost useless as a "travel" device. You have to connect this via the USB cable to a phone charger or computer. There is a hole next to the USB-C socket. It looks like it might be an alternative power socket, or for an external speaker. There isn't anything on the unit to describe what it's for, and there isn't anything in the "User Manual"

I used quotes around "User Manual" above. I don't expect too much documentation as the buttons and usage are pretty intuitive. However, what is being called the user manual is a 3x4 inch piece of paper. One side has a picture of the unit and some specifications. The other side has the warranty information and a very brief (one or two word) description of the buttons.

I don't actually find anything positive to say about this "White Noise Machine".

Update (2-4-2022): I thought I would give an honest attempt to use the "White Noise Machine" to aid in sleeping. Based on how I felt about the sounds while I was awake, I felt there might be one or two settings that might useful as white noise.

I was surprised. The two noise settings I thought might be useful actually weren't. White noise is supposed to be constant and consistent. Most of the noise settings of this unit have a lot of variability in both pitch and volume, making them totally useless. There was one noise setting, I would describe as crickets and frogs that did have more consistent and constant sounds. It reminds me of what my yard sounds like during the summer. As the result, I was able to fall asleep faster.

The volume settings on this White Noise Machine aren't sufficient. If you're trying to sleep in a construction zone, and you're using a white noise machine to block that level of noise, this might be sufficiently loud. I don't need it to be that loud. I only need to mask the pops and creaks that my house makes. I was not able to set the volume low enough. I had to cover it with a towel to muffle the sound as the lowest volume setting was too loud.

It's still unclear to me why this unit wouldn't come with it's own power supply. The specs call for a 5V 1.0A supply. Most of my older phone chargers are smaller, lower power. I was able to find one that provided 5V 1.0A. It's a good thing I kept that charger when I got rid of that phone.

Biz is a blend of enzymes that consume proteins and other components that make up stains. I wash kids' clothes, clothes that get stained with every kind of food, plant, dirt, and blood and other body fluids. In addition to adding Biz to every wash, I keep a two-gallon bucket filled with water and half a scoop of Biz into which I toss all the dirty white socks. After they've soaked for a few days, I toss the socks and soaking liquid into the washer (along with other whites to make a full wash), add detergent, and run the wash. I once left the socks soaking for a month, and they were fine. As with all laundry products, Biz works best in hot or warm water, but I also use it in cold washes. It dissolves well and is still the best product out there.

By the way, I have a front loading HE washer, but I gave up on HE washing products long ago. I got sick of having to rewash half or more of every load. And there were still things that came through with stains. I've used powdered Biz and powdered detergent for years now, and my washer is none the worse for it. (I put the Biz and detergent, along with 1 T of citric acid to combat hard water, in the washer before I add the clothes. I also add 1 T of citric acid to the first rinse.) And in most washes, every single thing comes out stain free.

Nobody has ever offered me free products in exchange for a review. I've written about Biz to spread the word about a great product.

title: Soylent strikes again to rob you of the pleasure of food
text:
Soylent: it's pretty gross, but at least in powder form you can do more with it. While the instructions advise just mixing with water and shaking with ice, I'd encourage you to experiment with it with other foods, mainly to hide the texture and bolster the taste.

I think I prefer this for that reason to the drink itself, which is frankly gross unless you chill it to it's almost frosted over to overpower that part of your taste buds and/or psyche that's telling you to stop consuming white chalk sludge.

Not a bad product in terms of the actual nutrition you can get while barely lifting a finger to prepare it. The only thing I don't like is the 30-day window to consume the whole container. This isn't really a product I want to use 24 times in a month. But if that's for you then this is well worth looking into. I haven't experienced any adverse effects from this iteration of the product, which is updated from the earlier powdered stuff that caused some folks some distressing bowel problems.

title: Not bad for the price
text: After surgery I required crutches to get around and used axillary crutches for the first 8 weeks before an amputee friend suggested I try forearm crutches since I had a delayed union & would need crutches for much longer. Her brand of choice was Walk Easy, but I didn't want to spend $100+. I ordered a set of like new Medline crutches for $30. I am 170 lbs & my arm would slip right out of the cuff so I utilized the hair band idea to hold the cuff tighter. Bonus was that it made walking a bit more stable. The handle has absolutely no padding and was uncomfortable in no time at all so I recommend you at least add a pool noodle to give some cushion. I made the cover for mine to save money. The legs tighten up and there was no noise whatsoever. I have been using these crutches for 4 weeks and the plastic coating on the cuffs are starting to crack & I'm hoping it doesn't peel off. If it does, I'll look into cuff covers. But for short term they are worth the $30 I paid. If I needed them longer term I probably would have gotten the other brand since the handles & cuffs are better & don't need covers. Plus, they come in a bunch of fun colors.

title: Works well enough for me
text:
After experiencing several after market disasters from trying other brands of cutters this set of cutter blades work well enough for me. They do give a close shave and float on my elderly face decently. These do have a different style frame where the cutters spin in. To be specific. The outside frame does not have the same notch pattern as the original. This may be due to Norelco supposedly upgrading their cutter design that happened several years ago. Maybe in that revision, they may have changed the notch pattern. The circular frame does seem to catch and stay stationary when inserted and the plastic keeper ring is snapped in. I was concerned it would not. These spin quietly and don’t chatter like crappy competitors. Some reviewers are not getting a nice of a shave as I am getting. That may be because I am older and less “T” flowing. Another reason is that you have to look for the notches that are 180 degrees apart and insert them correctly into the cutter head frame and insert them to where the notches will catch and stay put. Then you insert the plastic keeper ring. If you don’t do this, the cutter frame could spin with the cutters or be out of alignment not seated properly, giving a lousy shave. This would be like a cars tires out of alignment.

The bottom line is that these work fine for me, it just may take a few more swipes across my face than the originals. I have time for that at this lower price.

title: Small change, big difference!
text: Although I'm 89 years old, I signed up for total knee replacement (TKR) only because there seemed to be no other option. But I was saved by the pandemic, since elective surgery is still not allowed in my area. I have bone-on-bone osteoarthritis and was most frustrated by having to rest every 15 minutes or so while trying to work in the kitchen. I have been using only one knee pad behind my "bad" knee and now find that I no longer have to take those little rests, but -- even better -- is the fact that I now can walk (with bearable discomfort) to the supermarket two blocks away, which is making a big difference in my life. I am "sheltering in place" because of the virus, but now these little shopping trips are occasional adventures and are saving me the cost of having everything delivered. In short, this device is helping a LITTLE but also making a BIG difference in my life. I've also reconciled myself to the adversities of old age and given up the idea of TKR -- I'm just grateful to be able to go on living independently.

The Aria is a great concept, but for me, it's been an expensive scale that provides the same information as another scale that's half the price!

title: If it suits your needs, you'll like it.
text: I've had several such lights, and have recently tried several more... What interested me in this one were the covers over the springs. Springs make noise, catch in close, pinch fingers, gather dust... So, having covers over them meant it was worth a try. I happened to have a left hand mounting area on my desk where I could mount this and quickly determined it was best to "base" it at desk level. The reason being is it more or less "remembers" where you were working and when you swing it back, say, after a break, the entire thing swings back in the same "set up" as you had before - no need to fiddle a lot with it again. The 1.75 magnification seems to be about right for easy work. The work area through the glass isn't as distorted as it would be at higher powers, and, you have a wider "acceptable" depth of field to work in... Meaning you don't have to be that picky about where you place things under the glass to look at - you can get "in range" and be happy enough pretty quickly. The light adjustments will probably please you - again - "good enough." I mostly just pick a setting that's "good enough" and get to work. Nothing is perfect and if you worry about "perfect" you'll waste a lot of time. For the money, a good bargain. It would be nice if it lasted several years - most don't...  BTW, the head of this thing looks a bit like a thick Flying Saucer. I noticed is was "pretty big" but soon forgot about it. It also has nice curves and smooth corners on it. Great design, especially compared with many other finger-biting, fingernail-breaking, dust-loving, and, "falls-down-all-the-time" lights I've had in the past. For the money it's a good looking work/reading light that's easier than most to live with.

If you wonder why your makeup doesn't sit well on your face it's likely you don't have the correct canvas. Skin must be smooth, and even though it may feel so to the touch, we all have layers of dead skin that must be removed routinely because it's a process throughout life yet it's never too late to take nature in hand.
I have seen such an improvement in my skin in a short time that wearing makeup to leave the house isn't the issue it once was, and that is HUGE. A small brown spot on my face, which wasn't awful but annoying, has become very pale and I expect improvement as I continue use. I've spent a great deal of money using top of the line beauty products for several years and none have accomplished what daily use of this brush has. I'm awfully glad I gave it another try just to see if there was any justification for adding a tool for cleansing. Wish I had done so sooner!

title: Need a big mask? These fit.
text:
Long story short, if you have a big head and you're wondering if these will fit, THEY WILL!

Look: most of the so-called "XL" or "jumbo" masks out there are really just regular masks relabeled as "XL". I was beyond frustrated at buying yet another "XL" mask that felt tight over my face and pulled on my ears even though it was stretched to the max. So when these came up as recommended I decided to bite the bullet and give them a shot.

That was a month ago. When it arrived, it fit like a glove. I have a huge head and this ACTUALLY FITS COMFORTABLY! I don't mean "it fits but you have to stretch it all the way out", or "it fits but just barely", I mean "it fits, it feels fine, and I have plenty of room left over to adjust". As in, "finally, someone understands that not everyone has the same size head". Since then, I ordered two more XL for me and three regular size for my wife. One of the XLs arrived with a defect, but the seller immediately sent a replacement with zero hassle. That's important: any product can have defects, but what matters is how the seller handles it.

The neck loop means you can tighten the mask as much or as little as you like, and it comes in handy when you're out running errands and going from store to store. The filter pouch is nice to have, but the mask is much larger than your average PM2.5 filter, so adding the filter won't really do much -- still, it's there as an option if you prefer.

Care is a piece of cake. We've been washing them in the washing machine using a lingerie bag, then letting them hang to air dry. We've had zero problems.

Again, if you're frustrated with fake "XL" masks and are questioning whether these will actually fit, these are your masks!

title: Excellent product but one big problem
text:
I'm mostly happy with this vitamin D supplement that I purchased for my baby. Because he is breastfed only, the pediatrician recommended a vitamin D supplement. I had been giving him the Enfamil D-Vi-Sol liquid, which has artificial color and flavor, and requires a full mL for the daily dose. Although not an issue with my baby boy, trying to get some babies - including my daughter when she was little - to take down a whole mL of a vitamin is very messy and nearly impossible. This Liddle Ones supplement has none of the artificial stuff and only requires one drop. As promised in the product description, my baby takes this vitamin incredibly easily and doesn't even seem to notice that he is taking anything.

The value of this product is outstanding, considering that if only one drop is used per day, the bottle will last for years. One bottle of D-Vi-Sol lasts for a month if one dose is given per day.

The major drawback to this Liddle Ones vitamin D supplement is the dropper. It is not well made and makes it very difficult to control the dose. The dropper does not consistently release one drop at a time, so you don't know exactly how much your baby is getting if you drop it right into the mouth. Just two drops gives twice the recommended daily dose. You can try adding it to milk in a bottle, but if the baby doesn't finish the bottle, they might not get the full dose. Putting in on the nipple before baby feeds is an option, but I'd prefer to be able to just measure one drop into his mouth.

I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

title: Blocks out all the noise at my local public library!
text: I know that this is not the specific purpose that these ear plugs are marketed for, but they block out so much sound at the public library that it is amazing! I have two small children at home and I'm a graduate student. The only way that I can get any studying or writing done is to do it at the library. I could go to my school, but there are people I like there and I like to talk, so that doesn't generally work in my best interest. The public library in my area is far from what you would expect of the peaceful and quite library perfect for all of your studying needs. People get loud, have phone conversations, watch videos, kids yell, etc. It is so difficult to focus here, but I do not have other options available to me unless I want to spend money on food or a drink each time I need to study, which I do not. So I bought these beauties hoping that they would help me tune out the world around me. I can't hear the guy next to me trying to talk to me about what he is reading in the newspaper or the people on the other side of me trying to have what should be a private conversation in public. Interestingly enough, the one day that there was actually a peaceful sound at the library was when the local symphony did a short performance and I was able to hear that enough to know that it was worth it to pull the ear plugs out so I could fully hear them across the library. The only thing that I would say I wish was a little different is that they sometimes hurt my ears when I wear them for too long due to the size. I probably have tiny ears though. The minimal pain is worth it though! Thanks!

title: Bought to use with neti pot BUT read on
text:
When quarantine first started, I began researching what I could do to stay healthy. I occasionally use a neti pot for allergies, and I came across a blog where a user used baby shampoo, neti salt packet, and this product in a neti pot and it knocked out his recurring sinus infections for good. So I decided to try that to see if it helped with allergies. I added a capsule to warm water, added 2 neti pot salt packets (salt and baking soda), and J&J baby shampoo and did nasal irrigation on each nostril. These capsules did not completely dissolve, so there were particulates visible in the water. It slightly burned when using but the worst of it was that I smelled garlic for probably A WEEK! I guess that's good if the premise works but since I didn't have an infection, just allergies, it wasn't alleviating anything but definitely was not enjoyable. Eventually it wore off, I kept using the neti with just the baby shampoo and salt.
In the past year, there have been various studies and several more ongoing trials, to test out baby shampoo and covid. Studies show that baby shampoo knocks out 99% of the covid germ in 2 minutes of neti pot use. So I feel comfortable with using that in my neti but I won't be using the garlic pill in the neti unless I lose sense of smell. Also, I told my Allergist dr that I did the garlic neti, she had never heard of anyone doing that but that doesn't mean a lot since she isn't a natural healing type doctor so I don't think she spends time on alternative remedies.
All that being said, I have continued to take these pills when I have a cold. I don't think they can hurt taking them orally and maybe they help. They taste strongly of garlic but I haven't noticed any garlic burps after taking. The price is not cheap but if I only take them when I'm sick, that's affordable.
I think the neti garlic is only for those with serious sinus infections, unless you start with only using maybe 1/8th of a capsule and work your way up.

title: This enzyme works!
text:
I am new to DAOsin, but am very happy to find a lower-cost product that, according the label, is more potent than it's competitor, Histame. A year ago I had eczema on my face and neck, arrhythmias and flushing a few hours after eating, muscle cramps, poor sleep, and occasional trouble with itchy eyes and runny nose. While searching for the causes of my food-related arrhythmia online, I tripped on an article in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition on the subject of histamine intolerance. It explained how all these symptoms were tied together. I started taking Histame, and my rash cleared up, my arrhythmias stopped, my neck spasms are gone, and, for the first time in years I started sleeping like a baby!! I can't say how happy I am that my solution was not a histamine-free diet! That thought was sickening. At any rate, I am now taking DAOsin because it costs less and seems to be working as well or better than Histame.

Having said that, Swanson should note that they were not the first to bring diamine oxidase to the US. No big deal.

I have known my stylist for years, so she understands my struggle. Recently, she told me about heated eyelash curlers and how she thought they might be something for me to try. I figured what did I have to lose, right?

I got my eyelash curler early last week and I am just in awe. At first, I couldn't tell if I was doing it properly but then I saw my eyes. I had lashes again! They were no longer sticking straight out, they had curled and looked great. In the past, I have used the little metal torture device that grabs your lashes and sometimes your eyelid but that never worked out and sometimes I not only hurt myself but I lost some lashes along the way. This little device is amazing, it gets a little warm, you swipe and voila- Lashes!

I am in love with this product!

title: They're slimy, and I don't like the scent, but my baby's butt is clean.
text:
We've used a number of different wipes. The cheap ones (they tear). Fancy organic ones. Flushable ones. Homemade reusable cloth ones. And these. They're not bad. They're actually pretty good. They're thick (no tearing). They're larger than some wipes (more surface to use). And they're stinky. I don't like scents. These are scented. Most people probably wouldn't mind.

A couple minor gripes (besides the scent, I guess): when removing wipes, they don't cleanly come individually. The next wipe sticks to it, and I end up pulling more wipes than I need out when I'm not careful.

Also... they leave my baby feeling slimy. I guess it's the lotion they put in them. It evaporates, or something... but for a while, the kid is slick. Feels weird. I don't like that. It's probably the ethylhexylglycerin, or other hard-to-pronounce chemicals that they make me wipe on my baby when I use these. Speaking of which... anyone know if all that stuff is safe? Maybe I'll go back to my cloth wipes after all.

Some bulb brands don't fit without modification (Verilux designed the lamp to be used only with its replacement bulbs; shame on them!), but snipping off the interfering plastic tabs seems to solve that problem.

text:
I need to start by saying that this is an effective, easy to use option. It is not a full solution to removing all your back hair. This helps, but it works best when combined with other shavers.

The problem with this one is that blades like this only cut one way. They tend to miss hairs that grow in the other direction.

I find it best if I start with my Man Groomer back shaver, and then finish off with this shaver. That allows for a mostly clean shave. The Man Groomer doesn't go quite down to the skin, but it does get trim id down to the point where this one can be effective.

text:
For the first couple of weeks the Vonexx electric razor has worked well, I use the unit mostly for trimming my beard also for trimming the sides of my hair. However after four months of use the razor has many problems with the battery charging, the battery light does not work, the battery charge does not hold, the battery compartment cover keeps coming loose. Do not use oil as it attracts hair, dirt and makes the blades unusable, do not clean with water or the blades and springs rust. The Vonexx shaver is decently priced for a basic unit, comes with three attachments and a small sample bottle of oil. The blades can be unscrewed for maintenance, but if the second blade is removed it is impossible to reinstall, not a good unit, the cheap plastic also shows wear and is easily cracked with a bad charging unit and plastic battery cover that does not fit and constantly comes loose, not recommended.

title: Appears to be high quality, and definitely inexpensive
text:
This is the second manufacturer I have purchased Barley Grass Juice Powder from; TerraSoul (TS from this point forward) was the first. The issue I had with TS was the taste was significantly stronger than what I was used to (prior to that, I started drinking Barley Grass from a Japanese brand Barley Grass Powder), AND it was extremely difficult to get it to mix/dissolve in water.
After reading many reviews on ZNaturals (ZN), I decided to give this one a try; especially since it specifically mentions it dissolves "easily in water". Well, once I received it, I immediately put it in the refrigerator, which it recommends (interestingly, no other Barley Grass Juice Powder product that I saw recommends this), and finished the last of my TS.
About a week later, I tried the ZN for the first time. First impressions, it mixed better than the TS in water; not perfectly, not 100%, but better than the TS. I still don't understand this as from everything I read, one of the advantages to Juice Powder over just Barley Grass Powder, is the removal of the cellulose, which is not digestible AND is supposedly what makes the Powder clump and NOT mix in water. So, if any Barley Grass product is a Juice Powder, its cellulose has been removed, and it should be completely dis-solvable/mixable in water, right? I even asked ZN before I bought their product about this, and they responded "mix vigorously" in water and it should completely dissolve/mix. While it did not 100% mix, it was definitely better than the TS; there was a little undissolved juice powder floating on top, and the longer I let it sit, more would settle to the top (again, not a huge amount, but not 100% dissolved either).
The second thing I want to mention is the taste. As with the TS product, and apparently ANY Barley Grass Juice Powder, the taste is much, much stronger than just Barley Grass Powder (at least the Japanese brand I was drinking). It is much more like wet grass; whereas the Powder was more like a strong green tea flavor. In my opinion, the ZN was very, very slightly sweeter (natural sweet, not a sugar sweet) than the TS. I actually don't mind it, but several others I've given it to could not drink it straight, they had to add something (juice, almond milk, something...) in order to drink it. I drink it straight, just a scoop of the Juice Powder and approximately 8 ozs of water, every morning.
The only other thing I will say, since there were several reviews that mentioned this, is that on some mornings, I can detect a very, very light saltiness to it; however, it is EXTREMELY light, and I really have to smack, smack, smack my lips/mouth and really try to search for it. I did not find it "overwhelmingly salty" or that it had a "strong salt flavor" to it. I DO NOT add salt to any food (on a very low sodium diet), I don't cook with salt, and I very rarely eat extremely salty foods (guilty pleasure 1 or 2 times per year). My point is, that I am usually very sensitive to salt, to the point where I have even stopped ordering steaks at many restaurants, and have pretty much stopped eating out at all, because everything seems overly salty to me now. So for what its worth, I did not find the ZN product to be salty...at all.
Bottom line, if you can stand a very strong "grassy" flavor, and you mix it very, very vigorously (or in a blender or something like that), then this seems to be a good product at one of the lowest price/oz that I found. I will probably buy again.

title: Who knew bifocals could be so stylish?
text:
I was pleasantly surprised by these sunglasses. I wanted some bifocals to take to the beach so I could read cheap paperback novels while taking in the scenery as well. The reading portion of the lenses is a little too small to let me see an entire page at once, but I quickly adapted to slightly lifting and lowering my head as needed while reading. Another plus is being able to read my cell phone screen without having to remove my sunglasses and put on readers. I was concerned that the bifocals might look dorky, but you can barely tell they are there when looking straight on.

When I first put them on, the side pieces pressed firmly against the side of my head. At first I thought they were too tight, but I left them on and within a couple of minutes did not notice any discomfort. The snug fit keeps them seated on my face and they don't slip down my nose even with sweat and suntan lotion. After successful use at the beast, I've made them my go-to pair for daily use.

title: Useless junk
text:
As other reviewers have described, the adhesive side of these does not attach to the pad. The adhesive sticks to the pull-away cover. These have sat unused for just 10 days while I waited for a new pair of shoes to arrive. While still in the package, the backing has warped and pulled away from the leather pad, with the adhesive side staying firmly attached to the strip of plastic meant to be thrown away. There is no possibility of using these as intended. Completely useless garbage, a total waste of human energy to make, a waste of energy to transport from the other side of the planet, to travel through Amazon warehouses and finally to me only to be thrown away as useless junk.

I'm ok with trial and error to find a product that works, but I am not OK with wasting $8 on something that was never going to work. A COMPLETE RIPOFF.

title: Functional, Although its Function is Unclear
text:
I honestly don't know what I was hoping to get out of this, or even what its best purpose is. What is this supposed to treat or help with?
All I know is that when wearing this, I felt choked, slightly immobilized, and extremely uncomfortable. (It didn't help that my husband enjoyed making fun of me with it on.)
I was looking for a product that would help align my neck better than it is on its own, maybe apply just a bit of pressure to help guide me to the right posture. Instead, I got this. Granted, I got it for free with the purchase of this item: [[ASIN:B0103MGBHU Neck Brace by Vive - Cervical Collar - Adjustable Soft Support Collar Can Be Used During Sleep - Wraps Aligns & Stabilizes Vertebrae - Relieves Pain and Pressure in Spine - One-Size Fits Most (White)]] so I can't complain much.
Because I don't know what exactly it was supposed to do for me, I can't be too hard on it, but because 2 stars = "I don't like it", I had to be honest.
I ended up returning both of the Vive products I purchased, although I'd be willing to give the cervical collar another shot.
I have a lot of neck problems (degenerative disc disease) and I'm desperately searching for something that will gently help realign my neck. The pain is so bad by the end of the day that I can barely do anything. Everything aggravates the pain and I just don't know what to do. A heating pad around the back of my neck helps, but I really shouldn't be using that for as long of periods of time as I am.
I'll keep searching and going to PT, but I really hope I find something that helps soon.

title: It's An Improved "Vaseline"
text:
I found the Solimo petroleum jelly was different from brand-name Vaseline, and felt the Solimo version was superior. Solimo petroleum jelly was slightly thinner and softer, which made spreading it easier. If you lubricate an area that is sore, you will appreciate this difference!

As with any generic product, the style, form, and type of packaging mimics that of the brand-name product. Thus, no advantage nor disadvantage for Solimo there.

If you regularly use Vaseline, I strongly recommend that you give Solimo petroleum jelly a try. I think you will find it comparable if not even better, and the savings will be an added bonus!

title: Expected a Five-Star Experience, Got a Two-To-Three-Star Experience
text:
Both of these items proved to be disappointing; nothing seemed to be defective, but the set just screamed "cheap" and disposable.

The sleep mask was functional, but was not the comfortable, plush item I expected. The mask was thin and flexible, not unlike the sleeping masks that certain airlines give out to customers on overnight flights. I also found the strap affixing the mask to the face inadequate. For those of us who toss and turn at night, every new position on the pillow meant repositioning the mask as well.

Like the sleep mask, the ear plugs seemed pulled from the bargain bin. My dad used to buy inexpensive earplugs like these when he planned to do woodworking, and would throw them away after use. Such ear plugs do work, once you get them properly positioned in the ear canal. However, they frequently come loose, fall out, start itching, etc.

In short, these "upgraded" items did not seem upgraded to me; instead, they were only marginally functional.

I add it to my smoothies, to my soup and even to juice.  I use 2 Tablespoons 3 times a day and it has made such a difference.  I went from using an antacid after every meal and at bedtime to only using a bedtime dose 1-2 times per week. title: An inexpensive machine with steady noise - no clicks or noticeable loops. Just wish it was a bit louder.
text:
I got very lucky that this sound machine went on sale as a lightning deal for $36 just one day after the Brookstone sound machine I'd had for over a decade finally went kaput.

In looking through the Amazon reviews of other machines, it seemed like the highest quality ones were very expensive (for me), while the less expensive ones had reviews that complained of things that bothered me with previous machines, such as clicking noises or noticeable loops in the soundtrack.

This machine has neither problem, while still being relatively inexpensive. Note that there is only one noise setting - white noise, which is the only one I wanted; there are no crashing waves or babbling brooks. I use it every night, and it's small and lightweight enough to pack in my carry-on bag for trips.

You control the sound by twisting the top of the machine to close or expose more openings. There is not a lot of variation of the lowest and the highest volumes, which is the only drawback for me. I like the volume of my noise machines to be quite loud, and I wish that this machine was louder. It's not a problem for me at home, where I live alone in a quiet neighborhood. If you are sleeping in an environment that has just moderately loud noises, I don't think this machine is loud enough to completely block those out. (Right now, as I'm writing this review, I'm a houseguest at a relative's, and I'm sleeping in a guest room with the door closed. With the machine on max volume, I can still hear my relative walking on the slightly creaky floors in the hallway, and I can hear doors opening and closing, even though it's the middle of the night, and everyone is trying to be quiet.) So, I bring along earplugs on trips to supplement the machine, if needed.
