title: BUYER BEWARE - UNSAFE LEVELS OF HEAVY METALS
text:
***BUYER BEWARE***
Sharing this for my fellow pregnant and breastfeeding moms. Re-posted from Debora's Natural Gourmet:

(You're looking at a photo of the last of our Rainbow Light products, in the dumpster behind the store. We no longer feel safe selling them).

After more than a quarter century, Debra’s Natural Gourmet is sad to announce we will no longer carry products from the Rainbow Light company. This is matter for us both of principle, and of safety. Twice now, we’ve obtained lab documents from the company itself which show potentially unsafe variances from label claim. Furthermore, they have at least once provided a certificate of analysis that we discovered to be false. Given an opportunity to address these serious issues, Rainbow Light refuses to.

In 2012, concerns were raised about the purity of a particular raw material used by a number of manufacturers, including Rainbow Light. We take these things seriously at Debra’s. So we requested certificates of analysis (COAs) from all the companies we dealt with that used this ingredient. While the other COAs we received appeared credible, Rainbow’s immediately raised red flags: simply put, the lab results were too perfect to be true -- everything accurate to the hundredth of a milligram. That simply doesn't happen in the real world.

Upon follow-up, Rainbow admitted that "their" data did not actually come from them. Rather, it came from an third party lab, who, Rainbow Light asserted, was independent and beyond reproach. Rainbow simply transcribed it onto their own letterhead, and signed it.

We asked to review the source document, and Rainbow provided it to us (and then asked for it back!) Two things were immediately obvious. First, the so-called “independent third party” was actually the raw material supplier in question. And second, Rainbow’s transcribed COA did not match the source document. It was not even close.

After an initial round of denials, Rainbow eventually conceded that their COA was inaccurate. However, they insisted this was still okay, since the certificate of analysis was not actually a certificate of analysis: the bold font across the top that said “Certificate of Analysis” was a typo. Typo or not, this still left us holding a product that did not meet label claim – diverging in some cases by more than 700%. And it left us with serious concerns about Rainbow’s attention to detail, quality control, honesty, and ethics.

Normally, this would have been the end of our dealings. But we gave Rainbow a second chance. We did this because of their 20+ year history in our industry, their trade association memberships, and the fact that the product in question was no longer on the market. In retrospect, this was a mistake.

Fast forward to June of 2017, when Rainbow again brought a product to market using a similar raw material. Rainbow initially offered to provide a COA, but then later balked, asserting that all their lab work was now “confidential.” [Note: no other company we've encountered makes such a claim]. After some veiled threats to talk openly about our concerns, Rainbow relented, and finally sent the COA they had offered almost two months previously. Unfortunately, this COA was incomplete, unsigned, post-dated – and still showed one nutrient with potential for toxicity at 261% of label claim. Most troubling of all, despite repeated insistence that the company rigorously tests for heavy metals like mercury, arsenic, cadmium, and lead – all of which are anticipated with this type of raw material – that they test both the raw materials coming in, and the finished product going out, these test results were entirely omitted from the COA.

This, for a product marketing explicitly to pregnant women.

On our end, we can not imagine any reason not to share lab results if all they do is confirm label claim, and establish that toxic heavy metals are within legal limits. (Imagine if your kid says he got straight A's -- but won't show you the report card). No other company in our experience has taken this inexplicable a stance.

For almost a month now, Rainbow Light has refused to respond to both phone calls and e-mails asking after the missing heavy metal testing, and following up on other discrepancies. All the while, their official marketing continues to insist we can all trust them for their “transparency.” For us, this is unacceptable. There are too many companies out there to choose from, ones that not only talk the talk, but also walk the walk. Companies that don't have so much to hide.

To our customers, thank you for your continuing support. And thank you for understanding if we have ever recommended to you anything that did not meet yours (or our) standards.

title: Innovative new mask
text:
I've been wearing masks daily for years due to allergies, and most inexpensive masks have just a few basic designs. This is a new one for me! I just wish I liked it more.
A few things first: The sizing is based on your ear-to-ear measurement. I got a size large, and it's a little big on my face, but there's not much extra space on the ears, so I doubt the size medium would fit. I do feel like the fit is a bit too big which maybe makes it not seal as well. They would do better to make the ear straps longer, since they're adjustable, and base the sizes on the face.

I do like the mask! It's quite thick but fluffy, so it keeps its shape well (doesn't collapse in when you breathe) and doesn't feel heavy. It does get hotter than other masks, though, and the breathable material on the inner lining can be a bit scratchy if you have facial hair.

The filter itself? Maybe just doesn't work as well for my purposes. I'm allergic to perfumes/air fresheners, etc, so if I can still smell it with the mask on, then I can tell whether it's working or not. This mask performed pretty much on average with the standard cotton masks. I'll still wear it outside in hopes that the fancy wool filter is better at catching pollen/smoke, but it's not great for my indoor allergies.

It seemed it was turning off within seconds of setting it down so that I could part my hair and do another section. I kept having to reset and wait again for the iron to heat up. At first I thought my palm must be touching and pressing the buttons but when I made a conscious effort to avoid the buttons I was still getting the same issues.

text:
Left side of photo is clean and right side is dirty.

My travertine floors are cleaned every week but the dirt is too much with our dogs and daily traffic to be cleaned with just the average vacuum and mop.

I have an oreck orbiter which is a MUST for everyone who is OCD, owns expensive flooring, and/or owns animals who live a better lifestyle than you. Because I forgot or rather blocked it from my memory, my husband claimed he had a 10:30AM tee time. After a few homicidal thoughts and counting back from 10, I did a really quick swipe of the piece of floor I just sprayed. I then had five minutes of wait time for the cleaner to sit which I used to stare at said husband with a “who the hell invented golf because I am going to make it a sole goal to haunt this person” look. After a quick wipe up and a quick dry, I assumed I would take up the chore again when my golfing husband gets back from the 19th hole. I really did not expect anything because I felt I did a very quick, poor job on the one spot. After about 4 hours of dry time, I could not believe it. The travetine and grout look great. This will be my go to when I need the deep clean but not in the mood to use the gorilla diamond polishing pads. The diamond pads are great to use to get the shine back on travertine floors.

title: Like the Bottle Says!
text:
I did extensive research before purchasing a bunch of beauty, health and fitness products recently. I'm from Australia so wanted to purchase the authentic Tahitian tamanu oil. I read a lot of reviews on different brands not having the correct dark olive color or a pungent stench but this product is a deep green shade and seems to be of a high-quality. The smell is there but doesn't bother me.

I've tried a number of things for my perioral dermatitis - steroid creams, hydrocortisone, grape seed oil, hemp seed oil, calendula oil, coconut oil - what I've found to help is to keep the area dry. The best thing to dry-out raw flare-ups is sea salt (Himalayan or Celtic) and I spray this in a small bottle with spring water 3-4 times per day and rinse or dust-off once the salt is dry. Personally, I don't use tap water as I live in New York and the hard water is too harsh for my skin, so I've recently started using alcohol-free witch hazel, which feels gentle, cleans my face well and has also assisted in clearing my skin. I find my dermatitis dries-up fast with the sea salt spray, leaving my skin a bit dry and scaley but raw bump and itch free.

I've been appling the tamanu oil overnight for a couple of weeks. The brilliant thing is that although it's an oil, it doesn't leave any oily residue or make my dermatitus flare-ups fester like a fungal infection (unlike using steroid creams or the other oils I mentioned above - especially coconut oil, although I use this for the eczema on my body, after drying it up with the sea salt spray, and it softens my skin very quickly). Now I’m waking up with smooth matte cheeks, the redness is reduced and the dermatitis scaring is fading... I'm very pleased!

Hope this review is helpful for others with skin issues!

title: i could take it or leave it
text:
Sanwood Hair Straightener Comb Heating Brush

Okay, I have to clear things up. First off, the stock photos that are shown with these brushes are not true depictions of what will happen if you use this straightening brush alone. I just want to put that out there. You CAN achieve that look, but you'll need a straightening brush, a good flat iron, and some hair products, depending on your hair texture. Fine hair can look like this with just the straightening brush and some good products. Medium to coarse hair will require the use of a flat iron in addition to the products and straightening brush. I am a licensed cosmetologist and I have used it many times, all with the same results. The straightening brush uses heat to soften and straighten out the curl pattern. Depending on the curl pattern of the hair, there will still be a slight wave or some residual frizz, which will be eliminated with the iron. A thermal protectant and some lightweight oil will protect the hair from the heat and it will add shine.

The tips on the straightening brush get hot and they will burn you if you touch them. The power button and temperature adjustment buttons are on the side, which prove to be awkward during use. Each time I use it, I inadvertently adjust the temperature several times. I am constantly having to readjust the temperature to keep it hot enough. The temperature changes in 40 degree increments (Fahrenheit). The cord isn't swivel and is approximately 6 feet long.

Even with fine to medium hair, the brush barely gets hot enough to straighten it. It will work on coarse hair but it takes a long time, something I don't have a lot of to spare in the salon. I've found I'm better off using my brush and dryer to pull out the curl on medium/medium to coarse hair.
When using the straightening brush, it's important to section off the hair and use tension on the hair while brushing.

title: Best protein powder ever!
text:
Relief from the Chocolate / Vanilla flavors!! I love this Fuzzy Navel flavor!! I mix with flavored water or carb-free sports drink to further enhance the flavor. (I've also mixed sugar free soda in!) Heck, I've put it in a bowl and eaten it with a spoon. It's THAT good.

Delivers the right amount of protein that your body could possibly absorb at one sitting -- don't be fooled by protein powders that tout "50 grams!!" There is no way your body can absorb that much at once. Anyone who says otherwise, lacks knowledge of how protein is absorbed in the intestinal tract and you are wasting your money.

Also it may seem like a good idea to mix up a huge batch that you could sip all day. This will not work because protein degrade quickly when mixed. Better to bring a shaker cup and snack bags lf powder to mix fresh each time.

Only issue is that the protein powder tends to clump thickly and easily. (Hence: 4 stars)

Two methods for best-case mixing:

1.Use a 10 -12 ounce shaker cup -- larger size will help to really mix the protein in without clumping. Powder first, then add 8-10 ounces of water or favorite beverage Shake like crazy. Drink immediately.

2. Using a glass: Use a full scoop with a larger type glass and 8 - 10 ounces of your favorite water/ beverage. Empty part of the scoop into bottom of glass, add 1/4 of the water and start stirring (a fork is best -- or better yet, a hand-held blender stick) immediately, add more water, add more powder slowly, during the entire time to keep the powder from clumping together. Drink it immediately.

title: A Pain to Set Up But Cool Once Working
text:
I've had the Fitbit Aria Wi-Fi scale for over a year now. I bought it mainly for the automatic integration with my Fitbit app and my Lose It! app. I didn't give much thought to the accuracy of the weight or the BMI calculator.

Well, the set up was a B. I had to try several times to sync the scale to my computer until I decided to call Fitbit. Umm, it turned out that they don't want you calling them, they have an entire community of users that can help you with your problems. Good thing I was determined because otherwise that scale was going right back to Best Buy. I scoured the forums to find out how to set it up. Come to find out that the best way to set it up was through my phone!!! Since then I've been bombarded with e-mails from other purchasers with the exact same problem I had. Maybe they've fixed that.

I set it up for two users. Because I have the master account I can see the weight of anyone who steps on the scale. Of course there is no name associated with it. As for my wife, she privatized her settings so no one but her can see her weights. Once I got the syncing part working it's worked well ever since. It recognized each user (based upon the weight I'm assuming) so that after you weigh in your initials pop up on the screen.

There was a span of a few months when I didn't weigh in. That tripped up the system somehow because now every time I weigh in I have to select user. The scale directs me to select a user which means tap the scale with my foot until I see my initials. Why it would not recognize me when my weight has barely changed is beyond me.

I don't know how accurate the BMI reading is. I actually lose weight and my BMI goes up. Or, there are cases where I workout feverishly for a few months and lose fat and gain muscle yet the BMI is the same. That's why I'm looking into another BMI scale.

But as far as tracking your weight in Fitbit or Lose It!, this scale is excellent. You can see the chart to see if you are trending upward or downward. It's pretty neat and it beats writing down your weight daily. I just changed the batteries for the first time a couple of weeks ago, so the provided batteries (four AA) lasted over a year. No settings were lost in the process.

In summary: a pain to set up, may get confused on users and BMI may not be that accurate, but accurate for weight and syncs no problem once set up.

title: Very Well Done, Sensitive and Appropriate for Introducing Topic to Girls Ages 9-12
text:
Comes nicely packaged with a parent guide, a reference card for parents, a butterfly pad purse, and a butterfly bracelet. The program is for girls 9-12 and meant to be viewed with together with an adult. The run time is 1:07 but the menu allows you to break it up into segments. Dr. Crystal de Freitas presents the material to a group of mothers with their daughters in a very friendly, non threatening manner. She begins by helping the girls understand the difference between being private and secret. She moves on to the discussion of puberty and the changes the girls will begin to see in themselves. She makes sure to use clear and correct language for body parts and bodily functions.

The last large segment introduces menstruation. She explains what is happening inside the body and goes through scenarios of how to manage this in a variety of situations.
Throughout the program, she uses cartoon drawings to illustrate various points. But she demonstrates quite realistically what happens when a young girl has her period. She models how to use pads, liners and tampons and how to dispose of them. She explains and encourages responsibility not only regarding hygiene but also when discussion conception.

Bonus extra, The Birds And Bees With Ease

There are two parts in this bonus. An 18 min discussion with the mothers where Dr. de Freitas explains to the moms how she will answer three questions: Where do babies come from? How do babies get out? How do babies get in?
She gives the mothers the opportunity to tell what, if anything, they have told their girls about sex and to decide if they want her to explain this to their daughters. She lets them know that they must present the information to the girls in light of their own family values and beliefs.

The last part is "the talk" with the girls about sexual intercourse. This runs about 11 min. and is exceptionally well done. She explains the mechanics very nicely but has the girls explain the possible consequences. Disease or pregnancy. She lets them know that it is illegal for children to have sex. She gives them information but not permission and speaks of the importance of making good choices and always to talk to their mothers. This DVD is well done and would be really helpful for adults who are either uncomfortable with or do not know how to begin this conversation with their daughters.

title: Wore them for 18 months, no results
text:
Let's face it, these rings probably don't do anything. Most likely any benefits gained from these rings is a result of a placebo effect. In any case there's no way to prove it one way or the other. I've worn them for a month and haven't noticed anything but I'll give them at least a year until I dismiss them completely.

One big problem with these rings is that they are very uncomfortable to wear, the plastic is very hard and pointy. And there have been several nights where they've fallen off, or where my hands have gotten too close and the rings have stuck to each other. I'm going to make a finger sleeve soon, hopefully that helps with the comfort problem.

EDIT: I purchased these rings in October 2011 and I have stopped wearing them as of March 2013 because it is clear they don't work. I wanted to believe these rings worked as all of us do but from my experience it is as I expected, they don't do anything.

I've been balding for the past 3 years and I am considerably more bald than I was when I started wearing the rings. I've seen no increase in healing, in fact I developed a RSI injury in my wrists 9 months ago and the rings had no effect in preventing/healing it.

I still think these rings can make you feel better about yourself and even improve health through the powerful placebo effect. But any benefits from these rings are most certainly the product of your mind and attitude and not the result of any real physical effect the rings are having on your body. However if these rings help you feel better about yourself because they make you feel you are giving yourself a shot at staying young or healthy then by all means wear them. It's your attitude that can in turn cause real physical improvements. It doesn't matter that the rings themselves don't actually do anything.

title: Best out of 3!
text:
Our son tends to orally fidget. I wanted him to stop chewing on his shirt collars, he's ruined a couple shirts. His favorite color is light blue, so I got him the light blue "yummy gummy" by Munchables. He liked it, was using it in school, so I ordered him the camo 'lego brick's style one by Munchables as well. He liked that one better because of the texture, but as was common amongst the 'brick' type chew necklaces, he chewed through it within a couple weeks. I just don't think there's a way to make a durable 'lego brick' chew because I the shape and corners make it too easy to bite through - it makes it too easy for teeth to do what they're made to do! So the "yummy gummy" was more durable, but the brick had better texture. So I decided to give the biscuit a try, especially since it came in his favorite color light blue.

This has been the winner! Round and durable, and has a good texture. He's had this for about 4 months now and it's still holding up. He was using it all day long the first few weeks, now he uses it more occasionally, but if I catch him chewing on something, I can ask him to get his chewy necklace and he does!

Kids at school have liked his necklaces, enough that he's gone in with the Munchables info card for them. And his younger brother (who does not have an oral fidget) thought it was cool enough that he asked for the black one for his birthday! I've included a picture of him wearing it.

Munchables nor Amazon has not offered me any kind of incentive or compensation for my review - this is just one mom's honest review!

title: Works To A Point
text: I decided to buy this cleaner because I have tried in vain a ton of other cleaning products to help with the smell of cat urine.  We have one carpeted room in our house where my 12 year old cat likes to pee sometimes if we do not clean his litter box right away.  He is a picky little butt head.  There always seems to be lingering smell and of course the carpet is light blue so it is super hard to get the stain out.  When using this I was obviously a bit skeptical.  A downside is there is not ingredient list on the bottle which would be nice to know what kind of chemical I am spraying in my house.  There is not really a strong smell to the spray which is nice because with other cleaners if it doesn't smell like cat pee, then it smells like I'm bathing in Lysol.  First the stain color itself, it did seem to fade an older stain that was on my carpet using a good soaking of this.  Also, I made sure to rub firmly to make sure it got down to the bottom of the carpet.  The smell has been reduced on an old and new stain, and in my experience seems to do better at this than other products.  I still however notice a faint smell.  Perhaps I need to use more of this.  Also, I'm not sure it could remove the smell forever unless you really soak it into the carpet padding.  For the price you pay, it does seem to me like this works a bit better than other cleaners, however, I'm not sure it will really eliminate the odor completely without using a whole bottle, tearing up my carpet, or getting rid of my cat.  I'm not planning to do  any of those three.

text:
I have seasonal, pretty much year round allergies. Dirt, grass, cat, dog, molds, trees... you name it! Suffice to say, I sniffle a lot and sneeze for a long time if I cuddle my pets a little too close. When my allergies act up and my nose factory is running at full speed, a nice, soft tissue with lotion is what I need. Even worse is when I have a cold and have the sore nose.

These are two ply, like other reviewers stated. They don't appear any thinner than a certain store brand that I buy at a -mart type of store. The biggest differences between that store brand and these are the softness of the tissue (and not just because of the lotion, I don't think) and that I can blow my nose or sneeze hard and not wear shredded tissue on my shirt. These hold up for regular use. I appreciate that they can be purchased and delivered to your home in an econo pack, though I recommend that you be kind to your child's teacher and have some sent there for classroom use. The kids and teacher will appreciate the softness.

I do think they could upgrade the number of tissues in the box, because, yes, you will go through them quickly for a bad cold.

The device arrived quickly. It comes with a cord, shaver to remove any long hair, tinted safety glasses, and detailed instructions. The handheld part is comfortable to hold which is important since you will be holding it for a while at the beginning of use. First session went well and for successive treatments I was able to adjust the power to the normal recommended setting. Five minutes approaches actual sterilization of organisms exposed to UVC radiation, including bacteria (viruses are much easier to inactivate), versus simply "sanitizing" surfaces where some pathogens survive. title: 9290cc vs 9095cc/799cc
text:
This is an update of my review (with a lot of cut & paste) of the Braun 9095cc comparing it to Braun's previous top-of-the-line 7 Series 799cc, because these 9 Series shavers are virtually identical - with the visible exceptions of the frosty silver plastic on the exterior of the 9290cc compared to the shiny chrome of the 9095cc, and the gold colored titanium strip on the 9290cc head (92S) compared to the blue strip on the 9095cc head (90S - currently virtually unattainable). And the fact that Braun mysteriously certifies the 9290cc for use with shaving foam or gel, but does not for the 9095cc - although both are designated "wet/dry," and to all appearances are identical except for cosmetics; the cleaning stations for both are identical. There is a 9295cc version of this shaver if you prefer the shiny chrome, but pay attehtion to pricing because the 9290cc and the 9295cc are the exact same shavers with the exception of the exterior finish.

First impressions: I favor the appearance of the frosted-silver 9290cc over the shiny chrome of the 9095cc. Less garish, fewer fingerprints. Dimensions and all other exterior features (below) are identical. The 9290cc, by the way, is the upgrade to the 9095cc, not the 9090cc which is not a wet/dry shaver. It is also priced less than the 9095cc generally, which makes no practical sense since it is the newer (presumably improved) successor to this shaver; my advice is to bypass the 9095cc and get this one if you're in the market for a 9 Series Braun.

Overall length of the 9290cc is about a half-inch over the 799cc, body width is similar, although the 9290cc is more tapered toward the plug connector. The 9290cc and 799cc both weigh about the same - just under 8 ounces - but the 9290cc doesn't feel like the same quality build, maybe because of all the plastic. The head on the 799cc is substantially metal, including the part attached to the shaver. The 9290cc head is almost all plastic except for the cutters, including the shaver connector. As a comparison, both replacement heads weigh about the same (about 0.7 oz), although the 9290cc head is considerably larger than the 799cc and has an additional cutter. Durability in use may be similar, but durability of materials is not. Maybe the 799cc is over-designed, but just feels more substantial.

The attached trimmer on the 9290cc is a significant improvement over the classic Braun "flimsy flapper," frequently broken on previous series shavers. It feels solid and is firmly part of the shaver body, with a positive up and down lock. The on/off button on the 9290cc is also an improvement, larger and better positioned (the 799cc button is small, recessed, and harder to push. It also collected tiny water droplets inside its clear domed surface when used wet, which was more esthetic than functional). The travel lock works the same - hold down the on/off switch for 3 seconds and the shaver locks for storage in your luggage.

The head lock button on the 9290cc is potentially more solid compared to the notoriously rather delicate lock on the 799cc (time will tell), attached to the shaver body rather than the head, with a series of click-stops for the head for different angles. It has the odd function of locking the head when pulled down, and unlocking when pushed up - the opposite of what most Western users are accustomed to when using two-way switches. Maybe another Teutonic joke similar to the eccentric way some BMW controls work.

The head itself is a little over an inch wide, compared to about three quarters of an inch for the 799cc, and is asymmetrical - it has two different flat cutters for longer hairs between the foil cutters - a gold strip for "lift and pull" like a rotary and a silver strip for straight cutting. Braun says the head can be inserted either way and it doesn't affect cutting efficiency; this may or may not be accurate based on other reviews.

The cutting technology on the 9290cc seems similar to the Series 7 shavers, although Braun touts "40,000 cross-cutting actions," I expect they calculate 4 cutting heads x number of cutting blades x linear speed, etc., for marketing purposes, because the linear motor on the Braun actually runs at 10,000 cpm. It feels like the "Sonic" technology of earlier Brauns, which is actually pretty good. It is definitely distinct in function and sound from Panasonic's top ES-LV "9" shavers' "14,000 cpm" high speed cutters, which actually provided (for me) a slightly closer shave than the 799cc. Noise level seems about the same among all these foil shavers, which are significantly louder of course than a rotary shaver. The slightly larger head of the 9290cc does cover more ground quicker, shortening the morning shave some compared to the 799cc. Replacement heads (92S) are usually commercially available for around $70-80, compared to the still usually UN-available heads (90S) that come with the 9095cc, sometimes priced as much as the shaver. The heads are functionally the same for all Series 9 shavers and are interchangeable, and identical in appearance except for the different colored "Lift & Cut" strips. Longevity should be about a year based on Braun's literature, depending on your beard and shaving technique, but there are reports that this head wears faster than the Series 7 heads. There is no 3-speed control on this shaver like that on the 799cc (which I found useful for sensitive parts of my face); it has one speed - full on.

The cleaning station has a simple, less cluttered look, but similar in function; it uses the same cartridges as previous units, inserting from the back instead of the front. It also uses a drying fan, like the Panasonic, a plus and a minus. It does a better job drying the head than Braun's earlier induction technology, but runs for 40 minutes after cleaning is done and although quiet, isn't noiseless, whereas the induction drying for Series 7 units was completely silent, and only lasted about 15 minutes. LED indicators notify you of cleaning fluid level, and abbreviated information about cleaning status. LEDs on the shaver will identify when the shaver needs to be cleaned (I use daily), and battery level, similar to the LCD indicators on the 799cc. The front LED panel on the shaver will give you a numerical reading of time left when you get down to the last 10 minutes, otherwise the standard diminishing bars indicate battery life. The shaver is centered in the unit as opposed to the oddly canted shaver position for Series 7 units. Braun says the cleaning station and fluid actually sanitizes the head, which may or may not be important to you, unlike the water-based Panasonic or Philips cleaners. Counter space occupied and height are similar. Any of these shavers can just be rinsed in running water, so a cleaning unit is not absolutely essential, although convenient.

The shave: I've been using a Norelco 9700 as my favorite go-to shaver for a while (a rotary shave), so to write a fair review I switched to the 799cc for a couple of weeks to accurately compare foil shavers. Face-feel and beard growth are different using rotary and foil shavers, so a period of adaptation is required (usually 2 to 4 weeks). Shaving with this shaver is somewhat of an improvement over the 799cc - it does seem to provide a closer and more comfortable shave than the Series 7 shavers on their Normal setting - closer to the Panasonic - although both Series 7 and Series 9 shavers require multiple passes for me to get a reasonably smooth shave. I use shaving soap and a brush, so the wet/dry technology is a must. If you shave exclusively dry, the 9090cc is cheaper and provides the same shave.

Battery longevity is similar to the Series 7 shavers - about a week between charges on the road, for me. You can charge the shaver without the cleaning unit, with the cord, which is similar in size/shape to the Series 7 cord - with a similar LARGE plug, which is actually a transformer for multi-voltage, with coiled cord. Like all wet/dry shavers, you can't shave with the cord attached but must recharge; a few minutes will get you one shave, less than an hour to completely recharge. Comes with a quality hard plastic/foam zippered travelling case, signature Braun. The Panasonic travel case is the least protective in this group of expensive shavers, and is essentially a "faux-leather" bag with a zipper; they do provide a plastic head cover, which protects the head but nothing else. The travel case is a rather important, often overlooked item for travelers, especially considering how airline luggage is handled these days, so you don't end up wrapping your $300 shaver in a pile of socks or underwear.

Final evaluation is that the 9290cc Series 9 is worthy of its Braun lineage, somewhat better than the Series 7 line as far as shave and functionality (for me), somewhat less compared to build quality and esthetics. Replacement heads are available commercially now for less than $100 generally, which is a positive change from the 9095cc heads being essentially unavailable for more than two years, or priced more than the shaver. It's a good foil shaver for traditional wet shavers, perhaps not as close as its Panasonic rival or as comfortable as the Norelco 9000 Series (hence four stars), but a better shave than any Braun to date.

title: Genuine Quality, Great Small Gift
text:
I bought this little comb for my husband, who made it a point to say he loves it. I don't blame him - It's a gorgeous wooden comb, small enough to fit in a pocket and substantial enough I'm not afraid of it breaking any time soon. Combs are so ubiquitous you hardly think about them, but this one from Guys Realm is unusual enough it stands out. Its quality is obvious the first time you hold it in your hand. It's a well-constructed little grooming tool. The teeth are super-fine and even on both rows. The sandalwood scent is there and I like it. It's subtle, though.

The center spine is fairly thick - actually the comb itself is thicker overall than the cheap plastic stuff you get at the drug store. The pictures don't do it justice - the satin finish is beautifully polished, and the stylized etching of the logo simply adds to its luxury feel. A comb is a little thing, maybe, but this one really conveys a sense of luxury in an area where you don't usually think "luxurious". If you want a small but memorable gift for a guy, this would do the trick nicely. Tuck it into a small box or a suede drawstring bag and you're all set. It would be great as a stocking stuffer or a "just because" gift for the guys you love.

Contrary to the name, this comb works equally well on both hair and beard. It was a little bit tempting to keep it for myself.

I received this product at a reduced cost in exchange for my fair and unbiased review.

text: These are really designed for thin tire casings as found on bikes, motorcycles and utility trailers.  They will work on car tires but it takes practice to avoid damaging the plug (rendering it useless).  Given the cost, they are best set aside for true road emergencies.  Besides, the brass point is not really crimped to the plug so they are not what I would consider safe as a repair for longer term on road use.  The big downside is the need to clean the tool with solvent after each use.  The gum from the plugs gets all over it and will make the next use difficult.  Neat idea and seem to be a hit with the motorcycle crowd.  Cost point is just wrong for anything other than an emergency back up.  Buy true patch plug combo's if you want to repair a tire.  Yup, you need to at least partially dismount the tire, but its permanent and safe if done right.

title: a comment on this particular scent of Taylor..
text:
First off, Taylor shave creams are excellent. They are comparable in quality to all the other high end English shave creams, and come in a slightly smaller tub for way less money. That's preferable if you're like me and like to stock a wide variety so you can smell what you want to smell whenever you shave.

So check on Taylor being as good as the others. Don't let any reviewer sway you that DR Harris or others are sooo much better. I've found different brands make better and worse in different scents. DR Harris has the best lavender, Taylor has the best Sandalwood, Trumper owns Violet.

This St James stuff is interesting. At first I really didn't care for the scent, and that was after taking in a good whiff at a local shave shop. I came home and ordered on Amazon to save about $10, and when it got to me for whatever reason I just wasn't as fond as I'd been.

That being said, scent is a very personal kind of determination. I like it enough to use it, but it's not my every day smell.

What is EXCEPTIONAL about this product is the quality of its lather. It is far and away the best lathering cream I have ever encountered. It makes me wonder if the smell is just a byproduct of their having crammed every lathering agent into the same cream.

It is extraordinarily comfortable. If I have a special occasion and I need to be as clean shaven as possible then this is what I use. You basically can't cut yourself with this stuff on.

So if you want a super lathery cream and you haven't been happy with others then go for this. It's great with that.

I only gave it four stars because of the less than universally acceptable scent, but I'm tending towards 4.5.

title: Pretty, but...
text:
Eh...
I bought these matches because of the pretty box. Why else would I pay this much for matches? I wanted to leave the pretty boxes beside the candles I routinely light. Therefore, they could be decorative as well as functional and I wouldn't have to go into another room and fumble around in the drawers for the ugly box of matches, then return them when finished. When the matches arrived, the boxes were sort of squashed. The boxes are plastic coated, flimsy cardboard. If the cardboard was heavier...but, it is not. The matches are extra long (4 inches) and good for lighting candles that are burned down into the glass votive. I use 3 wick candles. I can always get two of the wicks lighted easily, but the match will burn hot at the neck and will do this funny bending thing. If I persevere and light the third wick with it, half the time the match head falls off into the candle. I blow out the candle, retrieve the match head and start again. I've learned to go ahead and use two matches to save trouble. If the box was nicer, I would refill with my cheap matches, but as it is I will just toss them and look for a small, decorative box to store the cheap matches. Pretty, but not worth the price.

title: I am satisfied.
text:
Subtitled "A 190 lb Man's Experience with the WonderGel Extreme: Adventures in Desk Chair Sitting. The Amazonian Story...by the Amazonian. With Dwight Schrute."

My desk chair at home is in great shape, but the seat cushion has lost its push, so I feel like I'm sitting directly on the base plate below. After a while, it is painful to sit. I had tried putting old pillows underneath, but had to constantly fluff them and/or re-position them.

The first time you sit on this WonderGel Extreme, you will feel what makes these WonderGel cushions unique. As you sit, the gel cells start to buckle underneath you, and you fit into a nice cradled pocket. I like that it is durable, cleanable, and has a nice cushion effect. I also like to support US manufacturing whenever possible, so it was a nice bonus to learn that WonderGel is made in the USA.

However, it is not quite perfect. I basically had to relearn how to sit. If you have the cushion pushed all the way to the back of the chair, and try to sit all the way back, you will find a "hard" lump of bunched gel at the back. So, I actually "aim" for the center of the cushion (the cushion still pushed all the way back), so I'm able to "float" in the pocket in the middle. I find that my back still comfortably finds the back of the chair, with no resulting lump or awkward posture resulting. In short, don't slide yourself down the back of the chair, but aim your tush to the center of the WonderGel cushion.

Having learned that approach, I am satisfied with the cushion, and no longer feel any pain from sitting in my chair.

Edit 05/01/2014

I carefully removed the carry handle for a few reasons:

1) I am not toting this around; it stays on my desk chair at home.

2) When I have the cushion positioned with the handle to the back of the chair, it contributes to the "lump" effect I mentioned above in my review.

3) When I turn the cushion around so the handle faces forward, its hard "sharp" corners create discomfort under my legs.

Now, with the handle removed, I find the overall comfort of the WonderGel cushion to be notably improved. I am much more satisfied now.

title: Very pleased with the visor and the seller/manufacturer
text:
I bought this because I find myself unwilling/unable to devote 1/2-hour of sitting in front of a light box first thing in the morning like I've done in past years. I'm happy with the visor and the light it puts out but figured I'd share some observations for anyone considering buying one.

Unless your surroundings themselves are very well lit, you'll find yourself blinded by light higher than a low/medium intensity. I find myself being much more cautious even on a setting of 3 (out of 5) until the time I actually sit down in front of the computer for a while, at which point I zap it up to 5 without issue. This ends up being about 20 minutes on 3 and about 10 minutes on 5....if I'm at the computer for longer, I'll just turn the visor on without using the timer.

I've had no problems with either blurred vision or headaches even though one of my light boxes has caused this in the past (the one that has a yellowish light for some reason....my bluish/pure white ones, also what this visor provides, haven't given me any issues.

The visor is really comfortable and the battery part, connected by a long wire, stays in place just clipped onto the neckline of my pajamas...you don't need something like a belt in order to keep the battery box happy.

I haven't had it long enough for it to need a recharge (it has supposedly "in excess of" 3 hours total use time before requiring such...depending on use of the timer and intensity of light). The recharge takes up to 12 hours. The initial charging time is 24 hours. The instructions say that the lights will start to flicker when the battery gets too low....although you can then plug in the recharger and continue to use it till your intended session is up. If you suffer from seizures you may want to keep track of how much time you get on a charge and then recharge before it starts to flicker.

This morning was my fourth morning to use it and I'm happy to say that I already notice a difference (I'd started out the season just trying to rely on having a box in place in the bathroom for the time I take to get my face clean/SPF'd and use some other lotions and potions for my morning walk and then a smaller one in place for when I'm at the computer (it's in use as my normal computer light year-round). That wasn't enough because my eyes are nowhere near close enough to either in those situations.

As of now, it's cheaper to buy here than on the manufacturer website....the price is the same but shipping here is much cheaper.

I was given an estimated delivery date that started a week after the date of purchase and extended another three weeks into the future. I figured the package was going to be forever getting to me. The seller/manufacturer shipped it out UPS on the same day as my order and it arrived the next day (we're both in Maryland). I was thrilled.

title: Prevents dry nose, sinus infection.
text:
About 3 years ago I was talking to a old man that lives in the building next to ours. We spoke of the dry heat in our buildings and the air being more dry due to low humidity/dew point in the winter. The dry air made our nose dry, bleed. This leads to sinus congestion and infection. We us a warm steam humidifier with a bit of organic salt to moisten the air, but if we crack our window open; extra protection for the nose is needed. He told me to use Vaseline. I was afraid of the toxins in the petroleum so I decided to try pure glycerin inside the nostrils. It works!

I have been using the CVS type of glycerin. I saw this more natural product on Amazon and the many positive reviews. So put it in my cart.
Will write more in the review after I try it for a week, or just leave review as it is. If I don't like it; will change the review.

Also use pure glycerin soaps, detergent... Keeps the body free of chemicals.

A comical thing about the old man; I often see him in the supermarket. In meat dept. One day he was ahead of me leaving the store. I caught up to him in the park; he was sitting on the bench and pulling out from his jacket a bunch of expensive meat he had stolen from the meat dept!

title: The Brush itself is very pretty, pink and white
text:
I have very sensitive skin and am prone to breakouts and blackheads, so I was interested to see if the ChiTronic 5 Multi-Function Facial Skin Care Electric Massager Scrubber would work for me. The Mia facial scrubber brush is way out of my price range, so I wanted to give this brush a try. The Brush itself is very pretty, pink and white, and is very light, which makes it easier to use. It came with 5 attatchments, a scrubber, a soft foam like sponge, a rough exfoliating buffer, a massager, and an incredibly buttery soft polisher.

I decided to try the scrubber first, and then follow with the polisher. I rinsed my face, and then dotted face wash on my fave. I used the scrubber brush on low and avoided my cheeks since the scrubber is pretty intense and my cheeks are very sensitive. My face felt tingly, soft, and incredibly clean after. I washed the cleanser off of my face and used the polisher on my clean wet face for one minute on low. It felt like heaven. My skin felt like I had gotten a real facial.

I gave my skin a rest for a day and then tried the buffer. I wet my face and dotted face wash on my skin. I only used the exfoliating buffer on the low setting on my nose, forehead and chin, as those are the least sensitive areas on my face. It was a bit too rough for me, even on the low setting, but I think that's only because I have such sensitive skin. My boyfriend tried it and loved the buffer the most out of all the attachments. He said it made his skin fell, "like a baby's butt." haha. I used the foam attachment after using the buffer, and I did like it, but I prefer the polisher much more.

I gave my skin another day of rest and decided to try the massager attachment next. I wet my face, dotted cleanser on it, and used the face scrubber brush first. Then with my face still damp, I used the massager on high. It felt a bit odd at first, but after I was done, my skin felt like it was extremely clean and refreshed.

I like the scrubber brush, the skin polisher, and massager attachments the best. When I use all 3 in the same session, it seriously feels like you have gotten a facial. My skin is clean, tingly, soft, and bright. I pretty much stick to those 3 attachments and use them 3-4 times a week. If I notice any dry spots, I'll bust out the exfoliating attachment, and it takes care of them right away.

The only downside to the ChiTronic 5 is that it's battery operated, so I can't take it in the shower, and I have to be careful using it around water. Other than that, its really surprised me. I was afraid that most of the attachments, especially the scrubber, were going to be too rough on my skin. It is MUCH softer than it looks in pictures, trust me. My skin is softer and more clear since I started using it a month ago. It feels like a nice treat when I use it, like I am taking time to pamper myself in just a few minutes.

In summary, definitely try this out before shelling out big bucks on the Mia, I am SO glad I did!

text:
I have tried several foot files over the years. Primarily, I have used ones with the snap in round roller. These seemed to work OK, but it took a lot to get close to what this file does and I needed to replace the rollers in the other one frequently. This cost money and it was getting to the point I wouldn't use it very often to save the file for more urgent times (sandals and vacations).

I usually get a pedicure every 4-5 weeks and I always left feeling rough/callous spots were still not great. I got a pedicure before a trip with a guy I'd been dating and he bumped my bare foot while watching a movie. He said "you're due for a pedicure." Hmmmmmm. No Bueno.

Things I love about this foot file:
- easy to use
- easy to replace pads (they have a strong sticky back)
- comes with a lot of pads
- much cheaper to buy replacement pads and don't need packages of plastic rollers to last a few times
- good grit for rougher spots

title: It helped make my teeth feel better, but over time it had stained my teeth
text:
I used it for a couple of things, boiled it then soaked my stubbed toe (damaged my joint), can't say that really helped me (don't know if I was using it wrong). But the main reason I got this was to heal my teeth. I had a few cavities that I needed to take care of, so I boiled some and swished it around my mouth. It helped make my teeth feel better, but over time it had stained my teeth. Not much at first, but I made the mistake of leaving some in my mouth overnight, and by morning, it had stained them brown. A little more every time. It was in streaks so I knew it was staining something on my tooth, not the enamel itself. I had no fear because I had positive results of getting plaque off with coconut oil in the past, so once I got home, I oil pulled and brushed, and immediately I could see a small difference. I oil pulled for an hour the night before a dentist teeth cleaning, left some in my mouth overnight, then oil pulled for another hour in the morning, and by the time the cleaning was done, they were shiny white!

Four stars because not entirely sure what to think, on one side it kind of made my teeth feel better, but I don't want to use it again and risk staining my teeth. I'm scheduled to go to the dentist to finally fix my cavities, but I'm not sure what to think. Maybe I should give it another shot and really go hard on that diet, because I didn't really stay strict to the teeth-fixing diet.

Disclaimer: I did not ingest all of the necessary ingredients to heal my teeth, and cheated a bit with bread a lot and sugar occasionally. I took blended eggshell most or every night before doing this as well. I had it, but don't remember if I always took the Blue Ice HVBO. Maybe now that I'm at home (and not vacation- was there for 2 months) and drink raw milk and a more steady diet I can make this work, who knows. I've had a history of bad teeth so even if I get the cavities filled, this might not be the end of this journey for me. I will though definitely be staying sugar free. Keep in mind that whatever raises blood sugar will pull calcium, so even some sugar substitutes like sugar alcohol will be bad for teeth.

title: A Celebration of the People and Places in the Founding Decade of the Slow Money Movement
text:
Ten years ago, in 2008, Woody published “Inquires into the Nature of Slow Money.” Right around that time I was developed an interest in local food and local economy. I met Woody for my first time in winter of 2010, where he convinced me to come to the Second Slow Money National Gathering at Shelburne Farms in Vermont that June. Coming out of that gathering, I joined the founding Steering Committee of PVGrows—a Slow-Money-inspired group in Western Massachusetts.

As a name with our year in it might suggest, “SOIL 2017” is a book about our place in the arc of civilization. It paints a picture of the evolution of the Slow Money movement over the past decade (with an interlude towards the end that even feels like a yearbook). And the book particular significance for me, as I pick up on all the references and have been there for the evolution of the movement.

The aesthetic of affection, beauty, small, and local are a common thread through the entire book. Woody begins with a boldly creative and metaphorically-relevant poetic interlude. This is followed by four sections: Whereabouts, Return, Nurture, and Hereabouts. And it concludes with photography from out in the field.

Where as “Slow Money” was poetically pragmatic and revolutionary, “SOIL” feels a little more nebulous, humble, and possibly a little less ambitious. Where’s in 2008, Woody was asking “What would the world be like if we invested 50% of our assets within 50 miles of where we live?” to talking with Jeremy Grantham at Bioneers a few years later: “Do you think we can get a million investors to invest 1% of their money in local food systems?” (Jeremy’s answer was no.) At the same time, the Slow Money movement has a lot to be proud for, and this book does a good job documenting and celebrating the people and places that have been part of it all.

title: The product is fantastic.  The seller, not so much.
text:
First, the product. It's fantastic. Forget Shout, forget every other stain remover you've ever used -- this stuff is phenomenal. My daughter is a stain magnet as well as not being toilet trained. You can imagine what I have to wash, especially since we use cloth reusable wipes. Add to that the fact that I like to dress her well, and I've got a problem - nice, durable clothes that will last if only I can keep them clean.

So far, Grandma's has gotten out dried blood, road grease on the back of a favorite pair of pink leggings, innumerable grass stains, every variety of art supply you can imagine, washable or not, ink and more. I spray it on clothes and I pour some in to use as a prewash on really stubborn loads. I couple it with Oxyclean for additional punch. It's saved a lot of clothes and a LOT of money. Plus, it smells great - a bit lemony and soapy. Can't beat that.

The one thing I will point out is, that while the seller does deliver in a very timely fashion, they also charge almost a buck more than WalMart does for the same product -- and you can get free delivery, if not so fast, if you order this amount from them. Be aware and price compare, as always on Amazon, where ripoffs abound.

title: Helps tame the wild beard.
text:
Once again, Port City does not disappoint. The Beard Oil Leave-In Conditioner is an amazing product that hydrates and tames my husband's wild beard. We are fairly new to the beard world, as he as always had a job which has required that he keep his facial hair basically gone. But since he has been out on an injury he has been able to see what growing out his beard does for him. And might I say, he wears it well. At first we just figured we cared for a beard like any other hair. Of course, we were wrong. Beards need different care. The coarse hair of a beard needs more moisture than the hair on your head and the multiple natural oils in this beard oil helps to moisturize and smooth it out. The Port City Beard Oil comes in an attractive amber colored apothecary jar and has a dropper top that ensures that you get just the right amount without wasting oil. Just a few drops will do. The oil is easy to work with. My husband puts a few drops in his hands, works it into his palms and rubs it in to his beard, through to the bottom. The scent is light, manly, not overpowering and does not overtake his cologne. The oil quickly, chills out his wild hairs and keeps his skin moisturized and staves off the flakes from dry skin under the beard. Definitely a new staple in his morning routine.

title: Lamps are great and nice to have around the house.....cords and bulb assembly SUCK!
text:
The lamps themselves are nice and I like them very much. The power cords and base rings that you have to insert to hold the bulbs, leave MUCH to be desired. The power cords are why these lamps receive 3 stars and not 5. A brief explanation as to why I am rating the cords. Without the power cords and the bulb fixture on the cord, the lamps would be useless and they would just be salt on a block of wood.
I purchased this set of lamps in May of 2014. Upon receiving the lamps, which were very well packaged, I immediately had issues with the power cords. There is an issue with the lamp cords/clip in base light. The clip in light brackets are not short enough for the lamp base to sit flat. They are ALL too tall for the bases in all lamps and the lamp sits and wobbles because of this. I sent a message via Amazon to the seller and this was my response:

"I have attached several pictures. Some with the lamps standing and some of the bottom view of how the cord end fits in the lamp. It couldn't possibly be the bulbs....they are so small and in no way being intrusive. (I mention the bulbs because they originally said they thought my bulbs might be the problem) The end of the cord with the bulb has 2 prongs on either side that you have to pinch to set the bulb into the lamp. These 2 prongs, that you pinch to insert/remove the bulb portion, are too long as you can see in several of the pictures, the lamp sitting on the prongs, not the base. The base of the lamps are not deep enough for the prongs and the prongs only go in so far so the lamps wobble on the base while standing and the metal prongs actually scratch the mess out of my tables when they are scooted a hair or moved without a complete lifting. The cord itself is not in the way at all and could go right into one of the designated cord spaces on the base if the base was sitting level. Maybe you can grab one of the sets you sell and put it together to see what I am talking about. I think the better option for a cord would be to have one that just has the plastic ring that goes on the bottom with the bulb base built into that instead of one that makes the plastic ring insert and the bulb base 2 separate parts."

After sending this response, they messaged me back and said,
"We looked at your pictures and comments and it turns out this is a common
question we have and is an easy fix. When you first get the cord and lamp
the metal connectors that hold the bulb are sticking straight down. In
order to fix this issue you simply need to put the cord in and push the
metal tabs out and toward the wood base. This will bend them up and out of
the way. Below I have attached some photos of us doing this ourselves. In
picture #3 you can see the fingers pushing the tabs down toward the wood to
bend them out of the way. If you need to further bend them you can remove
the cord and gently bend them further before replacing them in the bottom
of the lamp. We hope this helps and you continue to enjoy your salt lamps!
Thanks,"

My response to them on the altering of the lamp tabs,
"I'm glad you were able to give me a solution to the problem, however, it was not as "easy" as you might think. For those of us who do not have very strong hands, the solution is nearly impossible to accomplish without some extra brain storming and a tool of some sort. Luckily, I was able to find some tools that made the process a bit easier, but it was still tedious. I have to recommend a few options on your part, as the distributor, that you could do in order for this to stop being a problem for your consumers.

A) Include this solution to the metal prong problem in each customers box of orders in print, to ensure that they do not have this problem. Hence, giving your staff less inquiries and save them time in trying to trouble shoot in the future with others. Therefore giving you the possibility of not receiving a low rating on your products page.

B) Have this done to the metal connectors in house so that they come ready to go and your customers do not have to struggle with trying to do this themselves. **I understand that many people could probably do this, but for those who are not able to bend the metal, which is very strong and for good reason, it is not an easy solution.

C) Just distribute the lamps with a new and improved bulb assembly that does not have this problem. (My top recommendation being that this was an issue for every single one of the 6 lamps I received. I find it very hard to believe that this is not a problem for 100% of the lamps that you send out.)"

Now, this brings me to issue #2 with the lamps bulb assembly. The plastic ring that inserts into the bottom of the wooden base is too lose to stay put on every single one of my lamps and thus, when I pick up a lamp to move it, out come the entire bulb assembly and it falls to the ground. Luckily, I have learned to watch out for this problem and have not had any bulbs hit the floor and break (yet). It's just plain annoying. I've tried super glue, but over time the lamps get too warm and the hardened glue lets lose.

Problem #3 with bulb assembly, if your even still with me this far into my rant, is where the electrical cord attaches to the bulb base. The cord splits in 2 and each piece or cord is inserted into the bottom of the bulb base. Well, I could see exposed wire when I first got them, but over time, I am now seeing at least 1/4 inch of exposed wire between the cord cover and the bulb base. I'm assuming my wire is slowly coming out of the bulb base and since my new house is a bit more humid than the house that I lived in when I bought these, the lamps now sweat quite a bit and my cord, with exposed wire, now has a puddle of water that it sits in if I don't catch the sweating before the puddle gets significant. I have had to, yet again, take the bulb assembly out of each lamp and wrap each one in electrical tape so that the wire is no longer exposed.

I've come to the conclusion that the bulb assembly's just really suck and for the money paid for these lamps (I only paid $66 with shipping included), there should be WAY WAY better bulb assembly's included.
I'd love to buy more of these lamps, but I am just so completely turned off by the bulb assembly (and now the $99 price tag) that I just can't bring myself to do it. I will be looking for another set of lamps from another seller to purchase as gifts for friends and family this year and if they come with the same kind of cords and bulb assembly's, they will be going RIGHT back to the seller ASAP.

title: A really good, non-vibration, flexible and versatile, deep strong massager!
text:
No disclaimer here - I got nothing for this review. I paid for my Thinp massager, and here is my un-compromised review.

I really love it. I have deep muscle sprains along my spine on one side, and several in one shoulder. This device, in it's normal, default mode of operation works wonders on my upper neck muscles, but that's just to warm it up. After the safety timer shuts it down, I sling it over my shoulder and with a little patience I get it into just the right position to really work on those deeper injuries for another cycle or two. The heat is nice and maybe just sufficient, but a bit more would be nicer. By the third cycle its comfy-warm, but just.

For the price, the quality is quite acceptable. I went over my unit with a magnifier, saw no bad stitches! I like that the design is simple and robust, so it applies a strong massage action but is quiet and smooth. I can use it just a few feet from a coworker and they are not disturbed. It should last a long time because of its simple design. I like also that it is light weight and folds up decently for storage. The electrical connections all seem robust, and the nylon gearing sounds smooth and more than adequate for the task.

Another strength of this product is that it is VERSATILE! It takes a little patience to get into just the right position to work on certain deep muscles. I advise sitting in a big comfy sofa with plenty of pillows around. Once you get it on target it will deliver that much kneaded relief. :)

title: I really wanted to like this scale...
text:
I really wanted to like the Fitbit Aria scale. I really did. It's a gorgeous product, and the idea is so great (on paper)... I can weigh myself and wirelessly track it?! Weight tracking for lazy people?! Sign me up!

After deciding to purchase this on Amazon with the plethora of gift cards my entire family seemed to think I needed this Christmas, I was excited to rip into the packaging when it landed on my front doorstep. The packaging is gorgeous! I opened it up and the scale is gorgeous! Wow, I'm super pumped to get it working!... and this is where the problems begin.

Now keep in mind that I am a network administrator, and my fiance is a network engineer. We know technology. We know home networks. This should be SIMPLE!... SO. WRONG.

First of all, they want you to use their program to set up the scale. Now, that has my suspicions raised. Oh, but there's a little link that allows you to do the setup through the browser. YES! This should be easy. After setting up an account, I connect to the Aria's own network, provide my home network credentials, re-connect to my home network and.... no go. Hmm, okay. Check the network settings - when you have two IT professionals living under one roof, all sorts of strange things happen to your network. Ahh, there we go, 802.11b is disabled, because nothing in the past 10 years has used it and it severely degrades network performance. Enable that and try again... and still a no-go. Download the troubleshooting logs for their tech support and use my knowledge my sift through it. Oh, you wanted me to send a log with all of my home network information in clear text? NO.

Okay, let's try this again, instead of using the browser, I'll bite the bullet and use their software. Still nothing, and now I have their crappy setup software on my computer that likely is going to leave a bunch of residual crap behind.

Google search issues and find that people have had success using an iPhone. Pull out my trusty work phone (the only time I will praise them for being Apple fans is when I need to use an Apple product) and try again. OH! Something different!... oh wait, it just says WIFI ERR rather than NO SYNC....

Needless to say, after 2 hours of playing around with this scale, I am going to return it. While the idea is excellent, their execution sucks. Kind of like communism. Sounds great on paper, is awful when implemented. I am not going to re-scope my entire home network for a scale, and then slow it down to allow 802.11b. (WHAT WERE YOU THINKING, FITBIT?! 802.11b?!)

I think this probably works very well for a vanilla, wide open home network that has never been tweaked, but for anybody who actually is technologically savvy and has any ounce of knowledge on how to secure a home network past a WEP key, you need to look elsewhere - this just isn't worth the hassle.

I purchased the Skout’s Honor: Professional Strength Laundry Booster. Its a stain and odor removal additive for your laundry. I have a specific need for a laundry additive because I am sometimes dealing with animals with medical issues.. and they can't help themselves but urinate right where they are sometimes. So I have pads that I keep on the sensitive items that the cat or dog likes to lay on (IE: the sofa).

These incontinence pads are then washed but it is sometimes a chore making sure the odor is eliminated. I've tried a few solutions to combat this but Skout's Honor Laundry Booster works really well. I found that if I did notice a small odor... I could add more of the product... it helped me dial in the dosage per load. However; I am on the high side for dosage as I'm probably using 1/3 a cup per load. It's a big load. I have multiple pets. However; I doubt a single pet owner would need more than an ounce or two to add to the load. The point is, you can dial in your own dosage... whatever works. I have a high efficiency (HE) washer and add it just as I would bleach in the bleach compartment... and you still use detergent in the load as you normally would... I recommend to all pet owners...

For him, I consider any of the dime store readers I buy as disposable since I know he is going to misplace them (loose them) leave them on the bed and sit down on them (at least once a week) or leave them somewhere where our four legged son can get them to take out to the yard to bury ( I find a pair in the yard every time I mow) .

Well, I did a couple things. I stopped eating carbs alone (began a habit of eating fruits and starches only with some fat and protein) and I started taking cinnamon supplementation (real in food, capsules, then I tried this, Cinnergen).

My sugar got down to normal without losing weight (and weight control really is the best way to do it, but hey, tough, right?). Right down to the nineties, then eighties. No need for medication. yay.

I slacked off in the last year, since I started eating organic and more produce, but I do see that my sugar has come to the nineties. Before it goes back to 121 (the number that scared me into using cinnamon and food pairing to start), I ordered this again.

I love the flavor and it's so easy to take the dosage as directed. Nicer experience than just downing capsules.

If you don't use real cinnamon liberally in your daily diet (I don't, really) and want to keep your sugar in a nicer zone, give this a shot. Worked for me.

It didn't sound like the worst idea, I thought to myself, looking down at my half-eaten lunch. My lunch that day was literally a frozen microwave burrito I let thaw in my car for half my shift instead of actually heating it. My lunch was that a lot of days. So I gave it a shot. Not chalky. Two scoops me feel full. Soon enough I had a recurring shipment, a jar in my car, one stashed in the break room, a few at home. It's designed to be bland so you can do whatever additional flavors you feel like. I, being a man of efficiency, found that it mixes pretty well with coffee. Full meal and a cup of Joe in one fell swoop. As a frequent overeater, this is a fantastic remedy for any snack or meal you don't have planned. It makes you feel full! Plus, if you're bad at math like me, you can do a quick two-scoop and coffee breakfast of Soylent, a work lunch of Soylent, come home forget you only consumed 800 calories and go nuts for dinner! This stuff wins all around.

Pros:
*It does give me energy and I feel like I can mental process things faster. I like it better than coffee that gives me energy but also comes with the coffee jitters and this one doesn't.
* The color is beautiful to say the least. It looks like it has pink glitter in it or something and I keep wondering what that can be from. If you look at the video, I posted you can see the shimmer and swirl. No, it doesn't affect the inner workings of it but it does make it aesthetically pleasing.
*My favorite part- It is only 5 calories per scoop. This is great because the less calories I add the better since we know a lot of our calories are gained through liquids.
*It uses green tea extract as its caffeine source. I drink green tea sometimes and this seems to give me more energy, so I am not sure the energy boast comes only from the caffeine or if it is from everything combined. However, I like the effects without that crash that this gives me.
Cons:
*The flavor is just not good to me. I feel like a child taking medicine every time I drink it. The flavor is just so similar to a medicinal flavor that I started drinking it with a straw. Not horrible but not enjoyable or anything. (minus a star for flavor).
*Less of a con and more of an annoyance but the minerals and ingredients keep settling at the bottom if I don't drink it all right away. I have to keep stirring it every time I drink it to make sure it is evenly mixed before consuming.
Conclusion:
*I would recommend it because I did feel like it gave me more energy, but the taste is just what i couldn't take when drinking it. I understand all the things it has in it though and next to the protein powders and bars and wheat grass and everything else I have been adding this is in the same ballpark. I do like the energy from it though and the fact that it is 5 calories per scoop.

text:
Lavendar appears to be one of those catch-all, cure-all type of oils. It has so many different uses and so many different things that it is good for and helps with.

One of my favorite uses for lavender is for it's calming effects. I have a child with autism and she is prone to meltdowns. A little bit of this on the bottoms of her feet as she is getting dressed for the day has helped to keep her calm and get her through the school day.

Lavender mixed with eucalyptus and tea tree oil is also good for a variety of ear maladies. I am currently suffering from a clogged, full feeling ear. A bit of this mixed up on a cotton ball has been helpful in relieving the discomfort in my ear.

The only negative I can come up with is the size of the bottle. This is such a useful oil that you really want to have a lot of it on hand.

Overall this particular brand is clean and fresh smelling and has no gritty feeling to it like some other floral oils I have tried. I was very pleased and will use this brand again.

title: Callus remover
text:
I ordered this product for my husband to use. His feet are gross. He has calluses and dead skin. His feet crack and bleed. He works in construction, so he is on his feet all the time. I was excited to order this product to see if it really would work.

This O'vinna electric callus remover works great. Included in the box is an instruction manual, a cleaning brush, the callus remover, and 4 grinding rolls (3 extras and one already in the machine). It runs using 2 AA batteries that are not included, so make sure you have some on hand. My husband has used this product for 6 days in a row and we still haven't had to change the batteries, so it will last you a while.

This callus remover is small but mighty. It has a powerful motor that can reach up to 7500 RPM. This is incredible for how small this machine is. It is small and lightweight. Would fit very well inside a suitcase for travel use, and doesn't take up much room in your bathroom cabinet.

title: Breathable and comfortable copper sleeves! Great flexibility and improved blood flow!
text:
I have had knee problems ever since a softball injury in high school. These sleeves definitely dont offer as much support as some others I've tried tho so if you need a lot of compression you may want a smaller size or different brand, but for my needs they work well.

At the top of the sleeve there are elastic gel-like strips that hold well on your thighs. The stitching is well done and these should holds up for many uses.

I received my copper knee sleeves free or for a promotional price for testing and evaluation purposes but my review is solely based on my experience and honest opinions of this product.

title: Full service kit for all your mask wearing needs
text:
This kit has everything a person needs in order to make wearing a mask as comfortable as possible.

The kit includes 2 lanyards. Each lanyard is 28" long with a decently hefty cord lock which easily allows the lanyard to be adjustable to any length (see photo). At the end of the lanyard is a plastic clip that can be used to attach to the mask ear loops. The plastic clip is about the same size as a smaller paper clip. I could imagine the plastic clip breaking over time, but hopefully a solution for ending the pandemic happens before the clips break. I wish I had these lanyards a few weeks ago when I went to run errands with my mom. She kept misplacing her mask..too many pockets and places for a mask to hide. A mask lanyard would have been ideal for my mom.

Also included are 50 extenders that are 5 1/2" long and can be used to wrap around the back of one's head and attached to the mask ear loops. Each notch is approximately 1/8" deep (see photo). I tried to use the mask extender with a homemade mask that pretty thin elastic, but the extender didn't grip the elastic very well and I felt the mask would fall off my face. However, when I tried it with a disposable mask, the extender worked perfectly. I was even able to move the ear loops from notch to notch in order to adjust the mask without a problem. The design of the extender allows for numerous head sizes. I have a petite sized face and used the notches closest to the middle of the extender. My husband has a big melon (his words..not mine). The extender fits his head when he uses the furthest notches away from the middle.

And, there are twelve 3D brackets included with the kit. These brackets are the reason I ordered the kit. I've been wanting something that would allow more breathing room inside my mask. These soft and pliable 3D brackets help to keep the front of my mask away from my mouth so that I feel that I can breath more easily. I am home most of the time and will only use these brackets when I am out running errands and need to wear a mask, so I cannot comment on what happens when the brackets are worn for hours on end. There are hooks on each side of the bracket that allow for the bracket to be attached to the folds of an accordion style mask. I have an Olsen mask which doesn't have folds that the bracket can latch onto. I am going to sew a couple of eyes (as in a hook and eye closures..like the kind one uses on skirts) on the inside of my cloth mask so that the hooks on the side of the bracket can be used to keep the bracket secure.

This is a great product! Highly recommend.
