title: It gets the job done, although it would be nice if it lasted longer per use
text:
Both successfully Kickstarted and pitched on ABC’s hit TV series, Shark Tank, Nerdwax has gotten more than its fair share of buzz for such a simple idea. Basically, it’s like ChapStick for eyeglasses, except instead of helping to lock in moisture, Nerdwax helps keep said glasses from sliding down your nose, which is rarely a good look.

While you might ask why don’t you get eyeglasses that fit your face better, some people simply have noses that don’t properly accommodate eyeglasses, no matter how well designed. While I usually don’t have major slippage, my oldest daughter does. Even if your eyeglasses are well designed and your nose accommodating, over time, your eyeglasses, sun glasses, protective eye gear, etc., may still slip due to oil build-up, sweat, or even how your face might change subtly (e.g., swelling) throughout the day. So yeah, it’s more or less a universal problem, which is probably why Nerdwax got the kind of traction (pun intended) that it did.

Nerdwax boasts of its all natural and certified organic ingredients in its beeswax-based formula. I’m no believer in the purported benefits of organics myself, but I do care that a company takes pride in their ingredients, which this company clearly does.

Application is simple using the edge of the waxy stick to apply a little or a lot to the inside bridge of the eyeglasses, then putting said glasses on as usual. Depending upon how much you apply, your activity level, and the vagaries of your own skin, it should last about an hour to all day. In testing on my own glasses I got a little over an hour before I noticed some sliding, while my oldest daughter got a bit longer. As an extreme case, it didn’t stop all of her slippage, but it certainly did help reduce it.

While you do notice the Nerdwax substance when it’s applied to your eyeglasses, it’s not particularly annoying or distracting, and certainly does offer the benefit of not having to fuss with your glasses, or others’ glasses (much to her chagrin, I push my oldest daughter’s glasses back up her nose all of the time), quite so much. It’s clearly no miracle product, but it does work, albeit a bit too briefly versus how long I’d really like it to. Re-application, at least, is trivial, and it’s equally easy to wipe it right off if it doesn’t dissolve naturally on its own (and, in general, while it’s more or less just on the bridge of your nose, it’s actually a good moisturizer). Considering one stick of Nerdwax is estimated to last six to eight months of use, it’s definitely worth at least one purchase to see how well it works with the vagaries of your glasses, skin type, and activity level, and ultimately whether it will find a permanent home in your pocket or purse.

Thanks to Coco Joy for the review unit.

title: Hits Hard Against Teeth-All Settings Feel the Same
text: I have mixed feelings on this electronic toothbrush.  There's no wall plug with it, so I have to either use a computer to charge it (weird to have your toothbrush charging on your desk...or anywhere other than the bathroom). I've never used an electric toothbrush before this one. I followed all instructions.  The backside of the toothbrush (behind the bristles) hits/vibrates really hard against my teeth. Like when I'm brushing the top teeth, the backside of the brush taps and hits the bottom teeth, and hurts. It scares me.  Worried it could actually chip a tooth.  I have to open my mouth super big to avoid it (& I have a small mouth). Each setting feels the same to me. I can't tell the difference.  Being that it's my first electronic toothbrush,  I have nothing else to compare it to.  I really wanted one (my sister loves hers), but its almost kind of a pain to use.  I'm sure it cleans well,  I'm just afraid of how it hits hard on the backside.  I think it would've been nice if they'd placed a rubber-type coating on the back so when it hits, it's a soft surface that it hits with...no pain & no chipping. Very tempted at this point to return it. I'm giving it a few more days.

title: Great, but with some limitations: please read!
text: So here's everything you need to know to help in your purchasing decision:  1) yes, this will do skin tags and it will do sun spots and it will do actinic keratoses...BUT 2) this is not liquid nitrogen so it doesn't land on the skin as cold as liquid nitro, so this means you will likely have to do several applications. Do one application, wait a week, then do another if need be, and so on.  3) this product sprays extremely messy, even with the sprayer straw attached.  You could never 'hit' a single tiny spot because it splatters.  You will need to either a) make a template by putting a tiny hole in a piece of stiff paper/cardboard/plastic and placing it over your 'spot' before spraying or b) buy otoscope tips and use them to guide the spray.  After using both, I think a template is the best answer.  Be sure to press either of these firmly against your skin before spraying.  Overall, I recommend this product because with practice, it WILL work and will save you many $$$$ over a dermatologist treatment for non-cancerous 'barnicles'.  But if you don't know what it is (if its not tan colored and you haven't had prior education or experience with an exact looking 'barnicle' or spot) best to see a Dermatologist to be sure what you are dealing with.  Diagnosing yourself, unless in the medical field, is never a good idea.  As for me, I have age spots, also known as lentigines and also called liver spots- I hate them and get them removed often.  So I purchased this product to save me money and it will certainly do that!

title: Better than office scissors (in my house)
text:
In our house, scissors are generally abused; on a suburban farm, they get "used" for all kinds of cutting, especially the types of things that tend to trash office scissors-- plant stems, irrigation tubing, chicken feathers, plant ties, plastic of various types, shade/cover material, etc.

Most of the scissors we've had over the years, even the fancy titanium bonded ones, usually give way (simply due to the design and our use) pretty fast, and quickly become useless for even paper cutting (especially). These medic shears, however, seem to be the solution to our problem. They're MADE to cut through the range of materials we cut through, designed to NOT lose blade "grip" and to keep a good cutting edge (serrated even!).

OUr scissors usually end up floating around between the house and the yard, so they often get left outside in rain (told you we abused them!). These can generally handle that abuse much better-- with their coating and die-hard design, they end up still being able to cut-- for much longer than regular scissors. Of course, your results may vary depending on use/abuse. :)

title: The most convenient package
text:
These pedialyte juice boxes are the most convenient form on pedialyte I have found. You dont need to open up a whole 2 liter container that will go bad in a few days if you only want to drink one or two glasses. The juice boxes have just the right amount of juice and they are convenient because you dont need to carry a seperate liquid to reconstitute powder with. Its ready to drink right from the box and even comes with the straw. (Tetra Brik Pak just means the classic juice box shape you are all used to)

Kids will barely, if at all, notice the difference between this cherry flavor and a regular juice box. I tasted both cherry and the fruit punch flavor, and they are both similar. They both taste almost like apple juice. This is the best tasting flavor out of all the flavors, in my opinion, though it seems like pedialyte has done a great job with all the new flavors for these juice boxes, so I would bet that all of them taste like regular juice. The containers are just the right amount of fluid, in my opinion. They are all ready to go - no mixing or reconstituting required, and although no refrigeration is necessary, it certainly tastes better if you do.

This product says pack of 16, and you should be aware that this means 16 of the individual juice boxes total, which means 4 packages with 4 juice boxes in each package.

If you prefer to reconstitute your own, pedialyte also has the little powder packs you can mix in, although that requires you use a measured amount of liquid. These are all set to go and I highly recommend this version.

The gel is quite soothing and can be applied up to 6 times daily, if needed, according to the manufacturer. I am glad I found this Gold Gel and will happily continue to use it.

title: Not as described and an email unanswerd after a full month.
text:
I have read 100% of the Amazon reviews on this product.X001F3RDGV. Also all questions and the responses. I phoned Amazon four times and 10+ tried to phone the Nature Bell at 1-858-999-6857. Each time the recording said, the person you are trying to reach is not available, please try again later. Amazon attempted to call and the phone just rang. Amazon customer service stated they have no manner in which to contact naturebell. All I could learn was they have been a business for approximately two years. I read the information on Amazon as well as the attached label to the container. The first thing is the information is in conflict The label States a serving is one scoop which is 3 grams or a half a teaspoon. It states 85 servings. Then above their phone number it has the direction, take 2 scoops daily with meals. Is the label telling me take a scoop at one meal mean plus a second? The math with one scoop is 85 servings. With two scoops it is either 85 meals or 85 meals spread out over 42.5 days. They make statements that conflict with each other such as high in B-complex, C, E, high in proteins, and other listed ingredients. It is strange that the contents on the label have 2 g protein, 7% C, With two scoops, according to their label you will get 200% of vitamin K but is it K1 or K2. If you eat broccoli and spinach you already get a healthy amount and K1 and K2 serve different purposes. A number of customers make medical statements that are unlikely. The blood pressure reduction is an example. The neglect to include scoops as mentioned in questions is a source of both concern and confusion. If you also take vitamins there is a good chance they contain vitamin K. The recommended amount on the labeling is a total of one teaspoon per day (2 X 3 g = 1 tspn. But in the confused responses people are taking 6 times the recommended amount of powder or 1,200 % of Vitamin K + whatever they ingest from vitamins and foods. The label states certified by Organic Certifiers. Is that in CA? Amazon told me to use two teaspoons but that may be from customer responses. If it is from a purveyor that conflicts with the labeling. I am guessing since the scoop is 3 g that the missing scoop is 1/2 tspn. If we are to use 1 tspn why is the scoop half teaspoon? Is wheat grass Kosher? Why is the Kosher symbol U not used? Wheatgrass is not a fruit, meat, dairy product. How is wheat grass whole leaf? I am merely adding information on August 14. Prior to my review I attempted many times to call the two listed phone numbers but they don't answer or allow for a person to leave a message. I was able to send an email and have to think they received it more than a month ago. I base that on the email not being returned as undeliverable. I spoke to Amazon many times and they indicated they have no way of contacting NatureBell.
I went over all that I have said in my first mid-August review. More than one of the always excellent Amazon customer service people understood the math on the number of servings was half as claimed. I am surprised that Amazon as of this minute has it as Amazon choice. Based on sales volume or unclear and conflicting information?

title: Nice lamp for small spaces
text:
I like this light, I'll admit that. It provides just the right about of light over my shoulder on the couch to read my Kindle in otherwise low light. It's stylish and once put together is relatively stable, even though there are only two screws in the whole assembly. That is thanks to a wide base (which easily slips under the couch out of the way.

A few things to consider. This lamp has to be assembled. While I did it alone, I really could have used a second pair of hands. Fitting the head assembly into the shaft was challenging, but getting that top-heavy assembly into the base was extremely difficult. I got it done after putting the head on a pillow, sitting on the floor and doing the whole thing sideways. But once together, it works fine.

As for light output, I'd compare this to a table lamp. Not quite enough to illuminate an entire room, but more than enough to read, do crafts or other activity nearby. Artificial sun qualities for those that suffer from SAD - I can't speak for that as I'm no expert on that disorder, nor do I suffer from it.

All in all, a good lamp, not great, but good. If it fits your decor, you're good to go. If not, you might want to look at other offerings.

title: Good hearing protection
text:
I got these earplugs to protect my hearing when I go out to see live bands. So far I've only had the chance to test them out at home with my stereo system, but I'm going to a show later this month and another one in July, so I'll update this review then.

The package includes not just one, but TWO sets of ear plugs, a lanyard that can be attached to either set to hang them around your neck, and a small cylindrical storage case about the size of a tube of lip balm. The storage case has a ring that you can use to attach it to a key chain, or it will easily fit into a pocket or purse.

The ear plugs themselves are made from a soft silicone material that seems like it should be pretty durable. The reason they include two sets is because each pair is rated for different levels of noise attenuation. There is a blue set that filters out moderate levels of noise, and a white set for more extreme noise. Both sets are designed to reduce the level of sound without muffling or distorting it.

I tested both pairs using my home stereo system and will do further testing the next time I go to a show.. Out of consideration for my neighbors, I didn't crank the volume anywhere near as loud as it would be at a live concert, but I did have it loud enough that the ear plugs made a significant difference. Both sets of plugs noticeably reduced the volume of the music, but I was still able to make out the details of the music quite clearly.

My one criticism is that the storage case is too small to fit both sets of plugs and the lanyard at the same time. It will fit two of those three items, but not all three at once. I received a discount on this item in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. All opinions expressed herein are my own.

title: Good for Arthritis and Aching Joints
text:
This is not magic, but I find it provides reasonable temporary relief for aching joints. First wash your hands and dry them carefully, the active ingredient is a solvent that will carry whatever is on your skin surface into your body. I have arthritis and full knee and hip joint replacements. I have used this on an aching knee and on an aching hand. It rubs in fairly quickly, no need to use a large amount. I find that within a few minutes I get some relief - Not total relief, but it seems to significantly reduce the ache. It seems to last a couple of hours or so in my case. I do not use this continually, just when I have a specific joint ache that's bothering me. I would be reluctant to use it continuously because of a lack of good data on that.

I had read that DMSO has a strong garlic or onion-like scent. I can barely smell that in this case. I do not know if the manufacturer found a way to deodorize the DMSO or what. In any case, this does give me some limited relief that is well worth the cost.

Otherwise works incredibly well and eventually I'll be trained to not even need it. I've had it for about a week and already noticing a difference with out it. I received the IUFLOW bowl within 2 days of ordering (thank you amazon prime). I started using it immediately. It was easy to set up and get going however it malfunctioned. I contacted iUFlow customer service and they were amazing!!! They sent me a new one the next day!
Now for the awkward part: it has a screen on the top of the bowl so nothing falls in except urine. I can’t sit comfortably on the toilet because of this thing. Which makes it hard for me to pee “normally” like my dr requested. I wanted this so it could record my pees bc once I start, I stop and then start again. I realize this probably isn’t normal which is why I’m going to the doctor for it but the iUFlow stops recording before I finish peeing.
So it completely defeats the purpose of recording how long your pee is and how much pee you void in one session. Now the other issue is, sometimes it won’t sync with my phone. It shows it’s ready and I pee, the light is green (recording) then it flashes red and blue when you’re done, you push sync on your phone app and it didn’t record it..... so ya I can add that I went pee but I don’t have record of how much which is what my dr wants.

My honest opinion, it wasn’t worth the money. Totally disappointed. I’m going to order a regular urine toilet bucket and go that route so I can actually measure. It’s a great idea! It’s just not quite there yet.

title: Wish the vibration would stay on
text:
So, I got this for my almost two year old who is going through an early terrible two stage. The vibration soothes him. He lays on it and hangs out.

We got two actually. One blue. One purple. Both true to color.

We love these but there are cons… the vibration is generated by the user pressing on a button. The button is located in a zippered “compartment” in the pillow, easily removable. The button doesn’t have an options though. It’s just a vibrating button that only works when pressed. For us, it works great because my son only likes laying on it but he is unable to hug it and make it vibrate. I mean, he’s only 2 so, makes sense. My 4 year old does NOT like the vibration so she turns it off and just uses it as a pillow, which is great too.

Side note: the vibrating button is easy to press outside the pillow too. My son has put himself to sleep just pressing the button. It is a little intense by itself but it works for him.

I like it. If we were able to change the vibration settings, intensity, or have it stay on, it’s be that much better.

Hope this helps!

title: For homemade laundry detergent
text:
Purchased for my homemade laundry detergent because it's less expensive than 20 mule Borax.

For those concerned about the health repercussions of Borax, I did quite a bit of research and discovered that those studies mostly center around *Boric acid*. Boric acid, also known as hydrogen borate, is toxic, used as a pesticide, an insecticide, and can cause serious illness if ingested. It is a common active ingredient in many pesticide bait formulations and in some dust formulations.

Borax, is sodium tetraborate, a salt. If you look at the LD50 in mice, it has been proven less dangerous to ingest than table salt. While it is also used as an insecticide, it is the boron in the compound that kills ants.
I recommend everyone do their own research, but based on the extensive reading I've done personally, Borax (the mineral from the ground) is much safer to use when compared to the chemical laden detergents I used to use.

My detergent recipe is to pulse a bar of shredded soap in a food processor with three cups of baking soda, then I add two cups of borax and a half cup of sodium percarbonate. At a tablespoon per load, this DIY recipe is a huge money saver while giving you the security of what's on your clothes!
(I already used most of the Borax when I took the pictures)

title: Real?
text:
Pro: nice bottle, sensual fragrance, arrived early
Cons? I'm not sure if it's authentic. It doesn't smell like the dry noxious cedar smell of synthetic ouds in Montale or Swiss Arabian western oud fusion fragrances. Buuut, I can't be sure it's real. I got a mild headache even though it's a really faint scent. A dab of oil on my wrist only lasted 2 hours, and the smell stayed incredibly close to my body. In my experience, pure oud is very concentrated, so I doubt this is undiluted real oud. The smell was like leather and sangre de drago (aka, dragon's blood or fragrant palm sap). The acrid smell of the sangre de drago faded within a few min on my skin, and I was left with leather and a ghost of something sweet and mapley which was quite enjoyable but once that faded, it was pure new car smell. I don't have much experience with real oud to say if this is fake oud, or diluted real oud, but I can say that it seems unlikely to be pure since I had to put my nose directly on my wrist to smell it after an hour. In my experience with one real attar of oud, I used one drop and you could smell it a mile away for days. Perhaps age of the oud and the particular tree it came from impact the silage and longevity of this oud. Overall, it's not what I had hoped, but I'm glad I bought it with an Amazon credit and hope to try more ouds from reputable sellers to compare in the future.

text:

I have a one-gallon jug I use for drinking water all day, so I put a teaspoon of chlorella powder in the gallon. The water was a sickly green and it smelled awful, but the taste really wasn't all that horrible. I drank the whole thing and I didn't gag or give up because of the smell. It smelled like grass and dirt, not at all like seaweed.

Next, I tried it in my vegan protein powder drink. I put in lots of baby kale, blueberries, flax seed, benefiber, matcha and a really great protein powder by GoldenSource. Happy to say that the taste was completely lost, it didn't change the taste of my protein drink at all.

I did read that people who have low potassium like me have to be wary because chlorella can be high in salt. Maybe I won't take it every day, but every other day should be fine.

title: High Protein, Low Sugar, Mild Taste
text: This is one of the few (if not only?) ready-to-drink protein drinks that not only fit our macros, but does not taste awful. The item will say "High in Protein!" across the front and that's the only thing many enthusiasts care about.  Then there are those who are serious about fitness and health.  We scour food label after food label, making sure that all nutrients (macro and micro) fit our meal plans.  Well, here is one of them.  There is less than a gram of sugar for all of the protein that it has (30g), which is really great and not uncommon.  There are a lot of protein drinks like this but man, they taste awful.  This product is not a milk shake, but it's not awful either.  Funny enough, we find that it doesn't really have much flavor at all (referring to the Chocolate Marshmallow).  As soon as you drink it, the taste seems to oddly disappear, as if you never drank anything at all.  No taste is left on the tongue, which is good, because no taste is better than a bad aftertaste.  I'm happy to keep a stock of this on hand for the days when I'm so busy, I'm searching for something at night to complete my protein macro. Thumbs up!

title: DIdn't work for my sciatica
text:
I think I was able to test this cushion under the best circumstances. I am a university professor and the chair in my office is so awful on my sciatica that I can't sit down for more than two hours. This is the reason I bought the cushion but I happen to receive it in the mail right before I went on a business trip to correct national standardized high school exams -- sitting down every day for 7 days, 8 hours a day. What a great testing ground!

The first day I used the cushion, my lower back hurt so bad that I was almost in tears by 3pm (I had been sitting and working since 8am with two breaks). I stretched out to reach a pencil on the table just beyond my fingertips, and the pain jabbed me like a mad man. I tried to do a side-bend to reach my water bottle on the floor and ugh the pain was like lightning. The next day, my back didn't hurt as badly, but while I was talking to some colleagues, I mindlessly did waist-twists for 5 minutes. I wasn't sure if it was the waist-twists or the cushion, but I didn't want to chance it so I did the waist-twists every day.... except for one day when I was running late. I didn't do my "exercises" and the cushion was unforgiving. The stabbing pains were back with a vengeance.

Now I'm back at my office and using the cushion. I was able to sit for two hours and while my back still hurt, I admit that it didn't hurt as much. Normally after two hours I can barely stand up straight, but today with the cushion, it wasn't as bad. So it's "okay" but I'm going to have to invest in a very good office chair.

title: unstable - defeats the reason I ordered it
text:
I thought I read many reviews before I bought this, but now that I have a problem, I see that others have had the same problem. I bought one from Amazon. It is heavy duty. I like the finish. It took only a few seconds to snap the handle into the base. The base is welded tight and sturdy - but it's a pretty high step up. The handle has too much play in it. It wobbles back and forth - enough to make you feel like you're losing your balance. I contacted Amazon by phone. Learned that it's not returnable but that doesn't mean too bad for you. It means they don't want to pay to ship it back. The customer service rep ordered me another one at no cost and told me I could donate the wobbly one. I put it out on the street. In my neighborhood, things get picked up in less that 24 hours. This stool stayed for 4 days before someone took it. I got my second stool and it was exactly like the first one. This time I called the manufacturer to see if I was doing something wrong or missing a connector piece or something. They have been responsive but I have spent HOURS on the phone with them. They are saying that the handle doesn't pull out so it's fine. They don't seem to understand the point.
The comment from more than one person that you shouldn't use the handle to step up on the stool, only to stabilize yourself after you're already up - I'm sorry. That's not right. It's a big step. How are you supposed to get up? The whole reason I bought the version with the handle was for help getting up.
Follow up. I went in person to a local medical supply store. They did not have this bariatric version but they did have one that looks the same, model 13031SV-KD. The handle is stable and secure. That's what I'm going to get.
Don't buy this model.

title: I picked the right product to do the job right.
text:
Sometimes you just need a little something to help the healing. I had a very bruised elbow and would constantly be resting it on an arm rest or hitting it somehow, which kept it sore. After getting the Bird & Cronin Cradle my elbow has been protected and each day it hurts a little less. I didn't realize when I ordered there was 2 of the items in the package. Nice surprise! Since the description said 'sold individually' I assumed it was just one, perhaps I just got lucky.

The mesh part is stiff and tight when you first get it out of the package, but it doesn't take long after you put it on for it to adjust to your size. The cushion is a little firm and encircles your elbow on 3 sides giving you the ultimate protection. It is very easy to put on and take off and even after a week of wearing the support it still fits without slipping. Mine can be easily concealed under a bulky sweater or jacket. The picture is pretty true to how it fits on your arm. My arms are a little longer so it doesn't go down on my forearm as far. This is unisex small/large enough for both male and female.

I am looking forward to my elbow being completely healed and I no longer need to wear my Bird & Cronin Cradle but until then I think I picked the right product to do the job and the prices couldn't be more affordable.

This is NOT the solution you are looking for.

title: The best travel organizer for your buck...
text:
Since this was only around $12, I wasn't expecting much; however, I was pleasantly surprised. The front part is excellent for necklaces that tend to get tangled, and I like that it snaps for those necklaces that don't have clasps. It has two small pockets for the rest of the necklace to go in, and even if I shake it a little, they tend to stay in those pockets.
The middle part is roomy enough for several pairs of earrings, and it's a good thick material so they won't slide around. The holes are also spaced fairly far apart so you can put several dangling earrings in there and have room for studs as well.
The next flap was just a zipper pouch, and I had enough room for one pearl necklace and the matching pearl bracelet, so it's not super roomy...
The thing about the ring holder is that it was kind of hard to get my rings on it...it's wide at the top of the thick ribbon, and the snap is kind of bulky. I wear a size 6 1/2 ring, so if you wear a 6 or smaller, I doubt your rings would slide down it.
In the outer flap I could fit 3 long necklaces and a few thin bracelets. I could fit one big giant chunky bangle just inside the whole organizer since it's kind of wide.
I'd say this was a very good purchase. It held much more jewelry than a roll, and it wasn't as expensive as several others I saw. Also, it kind of looks like a makeup case when closed, so I don't think you'll have to worry about leaving it in the bathroom at a hotel...love it.

title: Nothing short of a miracle as far as I’m concerned
text:
I tell everyone about these! They are a miracle as far as I am concerned. I have had sciatica for two years. I’ve had PT, spinal steroid injections, lost weight, TENS therapy, more PT- nothing worked.

I was “better” in that I was not dragging my leg but I was in no way pain free. I was taking scheduled ibuprofen 4 times a day and Tylenol in between just to make it through work. I found these at Family Dollar of all places and thought I’d try them. I started out pretty much maxed out on them. I wore 3 the first day one on my back and two on my leg. I do tend to have a mark where a bandaid is and this is the same sort of material so I can tell where one has been for a few days. Rotate your sites.

By day 3, I was wearing 2 a day and had bought all I could find so I ordered from here. I gradually went to 1 a day and at about 3 weeks i noticed i wasn’t putting one on at all. Y’all, I don’t hurt anymore. Not even a twinge. I can sleep in any position-not just with my leg bent (sciatica people know what I mean).

I’m at the gym, I can squat, do pelvic lifts with no spasms or cramping. I keep a few at home now and one in my gym bag and in my desk at work just in case but honestly, it is just for peace of mind. If you ever had sciatica you know I’m terrified of it coming back.

Buy these you won’t regret it.

Oh! And yes you can take a shower and wear all day. They stick. Not like those from Aspercreme that are like a gel thing that roll up at the edges and stick to your clothes.

title: Works ok when plugged in.  Definitely not "rechargeable" though.
text:
These work ok. They put out a decent amount of heat, but not so much as to be uncomfortably hot, which is important since there is no way to adjust the heat setting (aside from unplugging them). Together the pair consumes ~8.5 watts of power total at 5 volts. (See the photo of the USB power meter that I uploaded.)

I also uploaded a photo from a thermal camera showing exactly where the heating element is within the insole. The heat is produced in a thin band/loop and is not as evenly distributed as the seller's photos imply. But in practice you can't really tell just how localized the heat is -- it feels more spread-out when it's worn inside a shoe.

Lastly, I don't know why the seller calls them "rechargeable", as it's a completely untrue/misleading label (although this seems to be a common claim among sellers of similar heated insoles on Amazon, no matter how untrue). They have to be plugged into a USB port to produce heat, and after they're unplugged the heat doesn't last for any significant amount of time. So if you want to use these while on-the-go and not be tethered to a wall power adapter, a simple approach is to have a USB battery power bank in your pocket and then run the wires up your pant legs to plug into the power bank. Voila.

Through the years I have used several hammocks, ranging from the little string mess camping version up through the full sized quilted monster you set up on your patio using a big metal frame.

I have to say, this is the best of them yet. It comes neatly packed in a little nylon bag with hooks and ropes coiled on top. When you pull it out, it unfurls into a HUGE nylon hammock that would easily accommodate two reasonably slim people, or one person of larger size. (It says it is rated to 440 lb, and I believe it.)

It does not come with explicit set up instructions (but does point you to a website if you need them), but in all honestly, I didn't need them, I have been using hammocks for close to thirty years, and the concept is simple, Find two tress suitable distance apart (in this case about 10 feet worked fine), wrap ropes around trees like a hitch (so they tighten with tension), attach hammock, and enjoy. Pro tip, put those end ropes up as high as you can, hammocks say and stretch out in the middle.

I thought this hammock was pretty comfortable, much better than the string versions are. It also wasn't as space consuming (and lots easier to set up) as the big metal framed versions.

Packing it up was a breeze. It easily stuffed back into the (attached) stuff sack, and the hardware fir nicely rolled up on top.

This product is very lightweight, but seems well constructed, and seems like it would be quite durable, though I probably wouldn't leave it strung up in rain and weather too long. I think it will last well if taken care of and packed up when not in use. My family is going to enjoy this.

I received one of these hammocks at a discounted price in return for an honest review.

title: This Roller is AWESOME!!!!!
text: Ok, firstly, this device arrived very fast and (as is expected with Amazon) was packaged very well with air pillows and a couple other items I had ordered. I could not wait to try this so I put it in the freezer right away!  Looking at it, it is made of a pretty sturdy plastic (would not want metal since it is to be in the freezer!). The roller is made of a water & gel blend. My first thought was that the roller seems "harder" than I expected, but then again it is supposed to be frozen so that became a moot issue. I let it freeze the first time for about 6 hours. I have some puffiness under my eyes (plus it is hot this time of year in Tulsa) so I tried it first without "needing" to after any kind of procedure. IT FEELS WONDERFUL!  I used it under my right eye first so I could compare and it really does a great job of reducing the puffiness without the mess of using another product, like gels or cucumbers etc. I was able to go straight into my nighttime routine. Today, I used a clay mask which clears pores, increases circulation and generally tingles. After removing the mask, there was some redness and some heat (all normal and expected after the mask, BTW). I went straight for my Ice Roller - maybe I just wanted another excuse to use this great tool - and I was not disappointed with the experience!  I have a derma roller on order and plan to use this after each use with that as well. I will update this review in a week or so to describe the results from that. So far, a definite FIVE STARS!  Ice Roller cools and calms the skin without adding extra "product" to my face. I can see using this also following an injury that calls for ice.

title: "Sniff it in, sniff it out, sniff it all about"...
text:
The set I received includes: PEPPERMINT, SWEET ORANGE, LEMON and ROSEMARY. So far I have tested out the sweet orange and peppermint. The set is well packed in bubble wrap and each oil comes in a sturdy cardboard tube with nice professional labeling and product information. Inside each tube there is foam padding to provide additional cushioning to limit bottles being broken. The packaging indicates 100% pure essential oil so if all is above board we should not have any harmful ingredients cooking in our air space.

Our massage therapist visited us yesterday for our various ailments and thus peppermint was on display.

THE REVIEW:

PEPPERMINT -- very pronounced and good sniff of peppermint straight out of the bottle; pours fast with 6-8 drops entering my tap water in the diffuser before I could pull back (unsure if this is the bottle design or the oil but normally 100% essential oils are thicker and come our very slow from the spout); once heated a very pleasant and pungent peppermint emanates into the air space; 10ML bottle size is pretty standard; nice professional labeling on each bottle

SWEET ORANGE -- really good smelling orange sniff out of the bottle; once lit up it has that full-on pleasing sniff of orange; nothing chemical or alcohol smelling that I detect; reminds me of my orange/pecan cannoli pie that I make for Christmas most years...nice...

I think the VALUE here is quite good since the pricing shown is barely higher than what I have paid for 4-packs at bargain retailers and the SMELL is way, way better.

If either of the remaining two scents are below par I will update this review with those. Otherwise, all is good in the neighborhood.

title: Perfection
text:
I’m trying to go 100% sustainable and natural in my bathroom. I wanted to switch to bar soap, as it is cheaper and I have been known to make my own. The problem with this is that bar soap is easily dropped, and I wanted the ability to exfoliate.

I had always used body wash and one of those shower poufs, but those things are just made of thin plastic mesh. Not exactly environmentally friendly. I figured there had to be something natural and sustainable that could replace them. That was when I stumbled across these bags.

I love the way they hold the bar of soap. Plus, they have extremely small holes, so even the smallest soap scraps are unlikely to fall out. It provides decent exfoliation and lathers better than a wash cloth. I love the string handle that allows you to hang the bags, because they give you something to grip onto as the soap gets smaller.

The only issue I had with this purchase was that the suction cups are not strong enough to hold up these soap bags. That wasn’t really a problem for me though, because I already had a much stronger suction cup hook in my shower. I just rearranged what went where. You’ll see in my picture that those exfoliating gloves are not natural or sustainable, but they are washable and I feel that throwing them out would just create more waste.

title: This is Pill-atial!
text: I was looking for a daily-dose pill container that was large enough to hold a week’s worth of pills, but small enough fit in a handbag or shaving (dopp) kit bag, and I found it with this one. I am fortunate enough to only need once daily pills, but I still have to take several a day. Other pill containers that fit the “portable” criteria were too small to hold my days-worth of medicine; anyone who takes vitamins or other supplements knows those pills can be “horse pill” huge. If you look at my pictures, I easily fit 12 large pills in one compartment and 62!! smaller pills in one.(I have coins in two of the compartments and an ink pen in one picture in hopes it helps visualize the overall container size.) The other problem I have with the small pill containers is I can’t reach into the compartment and remove the pills because, well, I have these stubby fat fingers.  So I would open the compartment lid and dump the pills into my hand, and inevitably one pill would get stuck, I’d shake the container, drop several I had been holding, and often had to chase down a dog that thought he wanted that dropped pill. The other nice thing about this container is the lids gently pop open when you depress the adjoining tab.  I was worried the lids would fly open, and send pills flying, but no-it is just a nice feature -you can just leave the container sitting on your counter or table and just push the tab to open the day’s meds. I will be honest in telling you this pill container was sent as a replacement for one I had purchased that had 2 lids that wouldn’t stay closed. I contacted the seller and they responded immediately with apologies and a note that another would be sent right out to me –and it was. The seller didn’t even suggest I needed to return the defective one, just wanted to know whether it was caused from shipping or from manufacturing. I did get this pill container at a discounted price in exchange for an honest review, but I will definitely pay full price to get more so I can fill 4wks worth of pills and get rid of the bulky prescription bottles.

title: Buyer beware if you have sensitive skin
text:
**Update: just since posting my original review I have broken out in an itchy rash while using these. I think the inability to let my skin breath has caused this. Obviously won’t be using them
anymore.

These do what they are supposed to as far as helping dry/cracked heels. With one catch...you have to KEEP them on. Think about it; of course they will help cracking/dryness as you are placing silicone on your feet, a material that does not breathe and retains moisture. So in theory, of course they will work if worn constantly. However, if you leave them off for a day or two, you’ll end up with the same dry/cracked heels as before. These do not TREAT or rid you of drying/cracking, they just prevent it from worsening.

That said, they do offer additional cushion in the heel area which is nice, especially since I have heel spurs. But the one size fits most is an issue. I have narrower feet, so these don’t fit as snug as I would like. If I sleep in them I HAVE to wear socks over them or they roll down and come off under the covers. Since I cannot stand wearing socks while I sleep, I just don’t wear them at night.

Getting shoes on over them can be....fun. I must unlace my shoes considerably to get them on without causing these things to roll down. It’s not TERRIBLY hard, but it is a bit of a pain.

I have seen medical grade ones selling for $40+ and those come in multiple sizes. I may just bite the bullet and get them at some point, as sizes would be extremely helpful. And these WILL help with dry/cracked heels but don’t expect them to cure it, or for a miracle. After all, they are $14 for five pairs. Lol.

title: Did this heal my chronic gum infection? Read it all
text:
I purchased this from Live Long Solutions when I got the refill, never thinking of coming here. I now just looked at their bottle vs here. Where it says S.O labs on the top with the doctor's Caduceus, mine just has a picture of a tooth. Mine is $69.00/bottle. (The distributor's address of mine: 37 Inerness Drive east - Ste#100 Englewood, CO USA.)
It is very tempting to buy this at 1/6 the price I pay but the reviews would be a 5 star if it were the same product. I have had chronic gum infection on the upper left side of my mouth for years. The infection literally ate the bone away despite the fact I went to the dentist complaining 4-6x/year. It never showed up on the Xray. Antibiotics, many dental appointments, chronic pain, etc. Then my sister purchased me Steel Bite Pro as a birthday gift. I never believed a silly pill (2 in am and 1 pm) would work but, By George! it DID!. My dental hygenist saw a big difference in my gums when I came in for my 1 of 4 yearly cleanings (at $140.00/pop!) I take it regularly now (and I buy it from live Long Solutions and pay the $69.00/bottle for it, gladly). At one point I did stop taking it and stopped flossing too. Within about 2-3 weeks I had an infection again. I didn't want to start up on antibiotics so I started retaking the Steel Bite Pro and they even cleared up the infection! No cleaning, no dentist. I now see the hygenist ONCE/year. I am 66 years old and have had my teeth cleaned 3-4x/year for 15-20 years. This stuff is amazing. It also has worked for everyone I know that took it. My dentist does not recommend it to his clients despite the huge difference it made with my gums. I wonder why... ;)

title: Love this scale!!! Everything I was looking for!
text: I was hesitant to buy this scale at first, because the product description (and answers to the "Questions" above) say that it does not sync to the Apple Health app or Myfitnesspal app. However, I loved the look of it and that it provided all the measurements and statistics that I was looking for. The Apple Health connection was important to me, though, so at first I bought a different scale (the Easy Home bluetooth body fat scale), but I did not like that one for several reasons. So, I returned that scale and took a chance with this Yunmai scale and could not be happier! It DOES sync with the Apple health kit and my weight uploads automatically to Myfitnesspal!! The app that goes with the scale is great too. I love that you can use this scale without the app (i.e. a guest could use your scale to get his/her weight just by stepping on the scale). This differs from the Easy Home scale; for that scale you need to use the app and have a profile created to get any measurements. Also (and I know that this applies to very few people!), I was delighted to find that I can not only weigh my cat on this scale, but could set up a profile for her on the app to keep track of her weight over time! I have to carefully monitor my cat's weight due to a medical condition, and I was disappointed to discover that the Easy Home scale would not work to weigh her. Finally, the shipping was super fast and the packaging that the scale came in was superb! Buy this scale - you will love it! :)

text:
If you've gotten to this page, you're wondering about the ShoeDini. If you're reading this review, you're considering one.

Stop considering it and BUY ONE.

I mean, I assume you already know how awesome shoehorns are - I don't need to shove/jam/force/stuff my feet down and wiggle in order for the shoe to get onto my foot without collapsed sides/back. But now, I don't bend over anymore to put on my shoes. I don't need to sit, either. I just walk to my shoes, grab the shoedini, and before I can even decide which shoes to wear, somehow there are shoes on my feet.

title: Not comfortable, chose Vital Salveo Train Tec instead
text: I was confused about which product to buy because the descriptions are very similar.  The seller said that the Train Tec S Pro has more compression and was more appropriate for athletes, whereas the Knee Tec S Pro was more appropriate for daily wear.  I bought one of each of the Joint Tec S Pro and the Train Tec S Pro, because I was unsure as to which one would suit my needs.  I wore one of each on each knee for several hours while doing kneeling, crawling, walking, sitting, and squatting.  I found that the Train Tec is more comfortable, flexes more naturally with my movements, and looks much smoother under my tights.  I do not detect any difference in the feeling of compression, tightness or stiffness between the two products.  So, I returned the Joint Tec S Pro and ordered a second Train Tec S Pro.  Both products seem to be very well made of good materials, feel soft enough on my skin, and very breathable.  I like the gel pressure pad (same on both products) to cushion my knee when kneeling on hard floor.

title: Not the Aprilaire product
text:
This picture on the Amazon website and the vendors is completely misleading. The use of the term replacement filter is the only way to tell this is not a real OEM product. Also note that Aprilaire or as they were called before Spacegard does not make theese type of box assembled filters. They have no version whatsoever. The reseller of these non replacements, since Aprilaire never made one like this, does not comment or remove the erroneous information. Also the filters have a lot of drag and do not work well. They will not last as long.

If you want the merv 13 and have a post 1985 Sapcegard or Aprilaire filter get the 213 filter upgrade kit. These use the accordion style media with the framework installed on the inner rail. Pre 1985 your best bet for non comb media is the Honeywell fc2001037. These do work for Spacegard 2200 series. The 4 inch depth is not a problem. You did not need the additional 2 inches of space for the filtration. Don't buy these at all for post and pre 1985 filter systems.

I used it to dilute nicotine of 24 down to 6, 4, then 2 by apportioning amounts;  Yes, the flavor is diluted as well, but it is an economical way to go.  My routine is to pour off 120ml of VG from the new container into the previous empty container.  This provides room to add my 120ml of flavored juice to the new container and also gives about 1/2 cup of VG to place my new, unused coils--where they prime themselves until needed. text: Have a pair of Ugg house slippers that I wear all the time. Now, if you can only make a spray safe for animals after being skunked which happened couple days ago and took me hours not only de-skunking my huge dog, but my carpets and furniture had to be dealt with too.  The formula made in a product called Skunk Out was nothing but a joke.  Am very glad I gave this product a chance, and highly recommend anyone else with stinky feet give it a shot.  Promise you won't be disappointed.

title: Useful and accurate.
text:
I compared the BACtrack Mobile Breathalyzer with the newer Ace Breathalyzer and with the caveat, despite BACtrack’s recommendation the breathalyzer should be recalibrated every year which I have never done (I haven’t used it that often), the differences in results experienced between the two were insignificant for every reading, for three test subjects.

Each employs a high qualify fuel cell sensor and in each instance, the difference in readings never exceeded 0.001%. It should be noted it is also recommended recalibration be performed annually on the ACE as well. The ACE uses 2 AAA batteries vs the other device’s USB rechargeable lithium ion battery.

While the BACtrack is more convenient to carry based on size, it also requires Bluetooth 4.0 connectivity to an iOS or Android device whereas the ACE is completely self-contained. I felt the ACE device with its’ protective yet bulky case is bit clunky to carry in one’s pocket but much less of a trial to use. Most of the additional features available via the BACtrack app – excluding the ability to estimate when BAC levels will return to 0.00% - are inconsequential to me and in my opinion, potentially intrusive. I don’t have any desire to store historical information in a cloud.

Each employs a high qualify fuel cell sensor and as noted, I didn’t find any variance in reading of blood alcohol content – as long as the guidelines for testing for each device were accurately followed. In that context, the ACE unit warms up faster and doesn’t require the user to participate in a pulmonary capacity test to get an accurate reading (a moderate strength blow of about four seconds is all that is required).

text:
This is my second time ordering root powder Its a great product but requires a bit of experience using. There are chunks of powder, just crumple them up with your fingers until fine enough to blend. Boil water, let cool to hot but not scalding and add slowly to the powder until a paste forms. It will be a sticky blob, can't separate it, that's because comfrey root is so high in mucilage which contains the wonderful allantoin and rosmaric acid that heals like no other. I apply the blob to injury (NEVER on an open wound) as a poultice (find poultice making instructions on many websites) and let sit for at least 4 to 6 hours.

I've used comfrey leaf, salves and creams for years, great for burns, insect bites, rashes. But for severe injury, such as breaks, sprains and strains, the root is the most effective healer due to the abundance of allantoin in the mucilage. The anti inflammatory rosmaric acid is the pain reliever. I only use it for a short time and never had any ill effects.

title: Nice durable case great for my parents aging hands
text:
This eyeglass case is very nice looking. It really looks like it costs double the price. The finish is very smooth, and the inside is soft and velvety. With it's larger size, it could fit pretty much any size of eyeglasses. What I liked most about this case was that it isn't difficult to open. My parents have arthritis in their hands, and their old cases would be tough to open sometimes. The hinge is stiff enough to keep the case closed, but still makes it easy to open without snapping shut on you. Also my dad has larger hands. With this case being larger, it is easier for him to grasp and open. The case also comes with a nice eyeglass pouch. It's very soft and light. It would be nice to put your sunglasses in before you put them in your purse or other bag. I used it to put my sunglasses in before I put them in a bag that I was carrying while my family and I spent the day at an amusement park. I had a lot of stuff in the bag that could easily scratch my glasses. On one ride they had no place to put my bag so I had to ride a rollercoaster with my bag....not easy nor fun. I put my sunglasses in the pouch and then in the bag. Even after being tossed around by the rollercoaster and hit by all the objects in the bag, my glasses did not have one scratch on them. So needless to say, my mom and dad got to keep the case, and I kept the pouch :)
I received this product for my honest reveiw. This is my opinion after receving and testing this product myself.

title: Buyer beware....  This thing is POWERFUL
text:
Oh my God.... the first time I put this on, plugged it in and turned it on I practically jumped out of my skin. I thought someone had pounded me on the back and I was the only one home at the time so it was more than a bit startling.

This thing is POWERFUL.... Like going a round or two with tyson or Ali. Over the years I have purchased assorted massaging devices for my back and my neck. All have a gentle massaging quality that was soothing but not necessarily deep enough to get any real kinks out. Kinks and knots wont know where to hide from this thing. My first thought when I used it was that it was too strong but I realized that I only felt that way because never had I had an electric massager give me this sort of a massage. This is what I am always hoping for when I buy one of those things but it is never what I've gotten. Until now.

This is not the massager for everyone. I have no doubt that some folks will think this is just too much. To give you some idea of how heavy it feels when you drape it around your shoulders, think of the last time you were at the dentist getting x rays... you know that lead cloak they drape on you to keep you from being harmed by the radiation? This thing feels a bit like that in terms of weight. And you need to sit yourself pretty near an outlet because this baby gets plugged in -- it is not battery operated.

So I am giving it five stars because it is the most powerful massaging beast I have ever owned. You might not want something that strong. It literally feels as though you are being pounded on by a prize fighter (okay, well maybe not a prize fighter exactly but you get my point). You need to know yourself and know what you can handle before buying. For me, it's good. I've put it on other folks who thought it was way too intense.

BOTTOM LINE: For some folks this will be the best massager they've ever spent their money on. For other folks it will be way to vigorous. Know yourself before you purchase. I received this at a sweet discount for the purpose of reviewing. I hope this review has helped you with your buying decision

You can follow up with a bit of moisturizer if needed (I Use Embryolisse in just a pea sized amount). title: Might be terrific - but just not for me
text:
I purchased 2 Adapt-A-Laps about 4 years ago, and used it maybe 3 times.

The testimonials of its value seem genuine, but I never got the point of it. A laptop, you can just put in your lap, and the monitor angle can be adjusted; that seems convenient enough.

As for books, maybe I was just spoiled from the Levo BookHolder. The Adapt-A-Lap just doesn't seem to offer much benefit, at least for me.

One of the main problems is that there are 3 protruding 'shelves' on the AAL, to accommodate a magazine, small book or larger book. But the top and middle shelf get in the way of the bottom shelf. If you place a larger book on the bottom shelf, the book doesn't lean comfortably against the main surface of the AAL. It would make more sense for the shelves to be foldable, somehow.

Before you purchase, take a look at it from different angles, read the testimonials. Perhaps you can find a good use for it. Others have.

Regarding customer service - good people. After the purchase, Adapt-A-Lap customer service kindly asked (in an email) if I could write a review of the product. I told them that I'd prefer not to review, couldn't really offer any positive feedback, but that I had no intention of trying to get a refund. They responded that it's no problem, that their customers shouldn't have to be stuck with a product they don't want, to feel free to return it for a full refund, and thanks for trying it out.

4 years later, I never attempted to return the product, and still have it. But the manufacturer's polite attitude left a positive impression.

I also did need to use a pair of sharp scissors to trim the excess bottom portion off. I trimmed 1 lens, put it on my glasses, checked the view angle, obstruction to my forward distance sight, trimmed a little more, repeating this several times until I was satisfied.

THEN I used the first lens as a template to cut the 2nd lens. Then, I checked the 2nd lens for fit, and made minor trims.

Now satisfied, I used the water to bond the trimmed lenses to my sunglasses, following the instructions.

Now, I have a pair of "new" reader sunglasses instead of constantly switching.

title: Revised x 2 - Great Product, Lenses feel like new BUT be observant
text:
Update - January 13, 2021. I had forgotten to turn off my subscription and wound up with an unwanted box of Clear Care. My traditional lense cleaner has not been doing a good job so I decided to gjve this another try.

My results this time are back to 5-Stars
1). Follow the directions on the box, wash hands, fill container to line with solution; put lenses in case, rinse lenses in case with stream of solution, put lenses in case.
2). Let soak at least 6-hours.
3). Open container, dump solution and rinse lenses with Saline solution while still in case. 4). Remove lenses from case and rinse inside with a tad more saline solution.

This last step will ensure that if the platinum on your case is losing its effectiveness or if you did not leave them the full 6-hours that you will not experience a burn.

I believe my traditional saline solution was close to expiration, but using the Clear Care in the above manner is far superior to standard overnight contact cleaners.

Update - July 5, 2020. I have decided that traditional lens cleaner works better. I wear 30 day lenses and have done several tests one month, typical BL lens overnight cleanser. At the lens change I did an entire month with Clear Care.

At the 30 day mark with standard cleaner my lenses felt good, in fact, so good that I can wear them another 10 days or 2-weeks.

With the Clear Care being used 100%, at about day 20 my lenses felt like they needed to be changed. I will use it every other day until its gone, but will not repurchase it.

I want to add that my result my not be what everyone experiences. I tend to deposit a lot of proteins on my lenses. You may not, and you proteins may be more easily broken down by clear care.

Initial product review below.

I really like this product HOWEVER you must be careful that the platinum disk is still generating the chemical reaction. Usually, one case will work for one bottle and then the case should be disposed of. I am about halfway through a bottle and noticed that my disk seemed to not be generating quite the reaction that it did early on. This morning I put my lenses in and got the horrible sting that some people have mentioned. I will continue to use this product because nothing gets my lenses this clean. I will be more observant to ensure that I get the bubbling action after I put my lenses in the case.

title: Perfect for crafters!
text:
I often make beaded jewelry, do some cross stitching, or one of several other crafty things. Sitting at a desk or on the couch working on these projects become very tiring on the eyes and at some point, I end up blinking and trying to refocus my eyes to see more clearly. Without having done a scientific study, only based on my perceived experience, this light has greatly improved my ability to see the little tiny beads, the stitching... all much more clearly for a much longer period of time.

I agree with some other reviewers that it is much shorter than anticipated or as described on the product page but after several uses, I don't mind it being down closer to my hands.

The light somehow seems "perfect" and makes everything clearer. Maybe I didn't need those extra magnifier glasses after all!

Bottom line - for crafters, a great thing to have and now, one of those things I don't think I could do without.

text:
Everything arrived in a nicely branded box, inside was the manual, 8 reusable electrode pads, 2 cables, a wall charger and a micro USB cable. First thing is to charge the unit while you read the manual. Connection is Micro USB under a door on top, and it charges fairly fast.

Once charged, you have some choices to make. Check online for proper placement locations for the pads, there are a lot of options and i am not qualified to tell you where to put them. Once down, you slot the plugs on the TENS cable to two of the pads then plug the cable into the A or B terminals at the bottom of the unit. you can do the second set as well in the same way.

Powering on the machine is quick and easy, button on the top next to the charger. This will turn on the LCD, the machine has some settings to fiddle with: 2 TENS modes, 2 PMS modes, 2 Massage modes, with 4 variant programs each. TENS is pain relief, PMS is Post Muscle Stress and supposed to help with growth, and Massage is... well, massage. You swap between the modes with the M button, the left and right arrow keys change the program, T adjusts the timer, the up and down buttons on the sides are for the power for the pads on that side. There's also a little round button in the center of the device, holding that for 3 seconds locks the keypad.

Getting wired up and program selected, this thing works pretty well, it puts out quite a bit of oomph. The different modes are a nice feature, as is the onscreen timer and battery display. The manual suggests running the battery flat before recharging it, at least twice, before having you be able to top off a charge whenever. I wish it had some sort of completion alarm, as of right now, it just powers off when the timer reaches 0. Honestly, i can't think of anything bad to say about this TENS unit., for the cost, it's a perfectly adequate for someone wanting to give it a try to see if it's right for you.

title: Good for Loose Hard to Reach Dirt on Things
text:
I had set my expectations too high with this ultrasonic cleaner and really any other small household ultrasonic cleaner. The first thing I wanted to try cleaning was the coffee stained spoon with soap and water but it seemed there was really no change. Scraping the stain off with my fingernail did way more than what the cleaner did. I realized for the price I shouldn't have expected that.

Instead these what it's good at are for things with dirt or gunk from our oily sweaty dirty body that gets built up that is hard or near impossible reach with a brush. For me that's been useful as a parts cleaner for my radio control cars mainly plastic parts using a 10 part water to 1 part of simple green.

The cleaner without the basket has a max physical capacity of 6x5x1.5" (1.5" max water line) that yep you can fit a CD/DVD mentioned on the product box and product photos in this listing.

There is a drain hole at the bottom if there's ever a chance water gets past the top gasket when being dumped out.

As another reviewer pointed out there is conflicting information about what can be cleaned with this ultrasonic cleaner and that reviewer is correct. In the included manual does warn not to clean things like glasses and dentures yet the product listing and photos here says you can. These same product photos and information is listed on their shop-beurer website too.

In the end these warnings about not cleaning certain things is to protect themselves from any liability if something gets damaged and only using soap and water if one gets injured if using chemicals not in a well ventilated area which I completely understand. So why the conflicting information?

Extra technical stuff.
It uses a ChuangXin CX-768 stuck to the bottom of the bowl to produce the 43kHz frequency. There's not much information about that part other than it's used in some other ultrasonic cleaners sold in different countries which I assumed priced similarly as this Beurer.

title: Fantastic, the only one that makes it through the night!
text:
This is the only night guard that doesn't wind up on the floor every night. It's kind of like a shock absorber, it is mainly the moldable thermoplastic around the teeth and gums which thins out when molded, and the bottom is made of a little bit harder plastic, and if you bite down it is sort of bouncy without being bulky. It fits in the front, just past the canines. I have tried other over the counter guards, and had even recently gotten one from my dentist, which was hard and awful. That was bulky and felt like it was pulling on my back teeth. I am thankful for this guard, it is the best by far. Way less bulk, no pulling or pushing on my teeth, but it fits and isn't wiggly. It is a piece of plastic in your mouth, so it might feel a little funny at first, but it is NOT uncomfortable. It isn't so big that I can't close my mouth, and my lips get dried out. I clench and grind and it has helped with both.

A little bit of advice, watch the video. It's short, and worth it. Also, prepare all of your supplies, maybe even have a helper to work the timer. Lastly, practice, run through it a couple times before you actually start. I felt a little rushed when I did it, but if it doesn't work the first time, try it again. Remember the cool water for your fingers, too! It's really worth the time, money, and effort. The one from my dentist doesn't hold a candle.

title: Nice size for me
text:
I had pretty much quit using eyelash curlers because I couldn't find one that fit my eye. I had never had this problem before I decided it was time to update all my make up tools a few years ago. I discarded my eyelash curler of some 15 years before purchasing a new one and what a mistake that turned out to be. The curler I bought to replace it (don't remember what my original brand had been) was too big for my eye socket. I would have to angle it to curl the inner lashes then angle the other way to curl the outer lashes which pretty much left the center lashes uncurled. I never thought I had an unusually small eye socket but apparently I do. I tried a couple of others from various stores but could not find one that worked for me.

The older I get the more straight my eyelashes seem to grow and I decided to try again to find a curler that would work for me. After researching the reviews I decided on this one and another brand and they both worked. This curler measures approximately 1 3/8 inch wide with the curve being approximately 3/8 inch deep. The store brands that didn't work for me measured 1 1/2 inches wide and 1/2 deep. You wouldn't think that 1/8 inch difference in size would matter but for me it did.

This curler does a nice job of curling my lashes, getting them all in at the same time. I curl close to the lid then again about half way out and this gives me a pleasing curl. This curler comes with one spare cushion strip that is attached to the curler. I thought my spare piece was missing then I noticed it was in a holder that snaps on the handle of the curler, neat way to keep it. I do wish that it had more cushion strips but hopefully they will last a while.

title: Yes! Yes! Does What It States exactly...so read the directions even moreso than the reviews.
text:
So far, so good. This Recharger does EXACTLY what it states and seems like an excellent buy for the advertised purpose with Alkaline batteries (only.) I would definitely buy it again.

Note: you DO need to give it a full 8-hours to do the job - and realize it will only recharge batteries 1 or 2 at a time; alkaline ones that actually have some degree of recharge ability left in them (not totally drained ones) - and the directions clearly state that that means probably at best 5 recharges at the most for any one battery. (Can't verify this yet but that's what the fine print states.)

What I particularly like is if a battery is really "Exhausted" with a bit of time in the gadget that read-out WILL appear. Otherwise, it will cue you when it starts recharging a battery if it can potentially do so at a 3 or 4 bar level - and maybe at a 5-bar level. Not sure tho about 5-bar as I've not yet had one of those potentially to work with with this Reharger yet.

This is also quite well made with a long-enough electrical cord to be convenient, plus the main plug has a smallish-footprint.

I'm using this right now for a portable, porch fan that runs on 8 D-Batteries and it will clearly pay for itself just in June. Our covered and super-nice front porch and view and breeze from this is perfect even in Texas Summers to use every eve or until 11am for mornings to read, catch up on the news, or simply work with my plants on the porch.

Learned of the existance of such a portable fan, btw, from a nicely dressed "homeless" woman waiting for the bus on a nearby street. Her sign said she would appreciate more "battery money" which I asked here about. Was glad to give her a few $$'s - and also glad to know that there existed, a very nice, black, trim, 2-speed, completely portable fan for such as porches, working in the yard, camping out, picnics and such. (Far itself was $20 - and costs more than that for 8 big batteries!)

title: Great fitbit wristband companion, but somewhat overpriced and not accurate
text:
I bought a fitbit charge hr last week, and I also wanted to buy the companion scale because I used to measure and keep track of my weight on a daily basis. I was also using another device to monitor and track my BMI, so the great think about this scale is that all the information you need is already measured one time, and kept in your fitbit site for you. The main problem (this moves my review from 4 to 3 stars) is that the readings are not accurate. I always weight myself in the morning after I urinated. I did it yesterday 4 times and the four times the weight and the BMI readings were different. Today, I did the same think, I weighted myself two times one right after the other, and the readings were both different. This is disappointing, especially considering the high tag prize.
The design is beautiful, setting up was a breeze, and so far everything about this is great. The one feature that goes above and beyond anything I used before is the fact that this scale measure lean vs fat, so you know exactly how many pounds of fat and how many pounds of lean your body contains. This is an essential data to analyze and reconsider what you are eating, so you can really understand the fluctuations in your weight. The reason I am not giving this 5 stars is because this is clearly over prized. The company is kind of taking advantage of the momentum they are having, and I'll go by saying that their products are just excellent. However excellent this is, though, the fair price would be something below $60-$70. it is extremely convenient, though, that by using fitbit products all your data is collected and presented in the same website, so I would highly encourage you to buy this if you have a fitbit band, and if you can afford the high price as I write this review (just below the hundred and twenty).

Updated on 4/22: rating down from 4 to 3 stars due to not accurate readings.

title: Nice, but has a fixable, yet fatal flaw
text:
It's a well priced product and is easy to install.

BUT the little blue light is a problem.
The light ONLY means that the power to the unit it on and NOT if any of the lights are burned out.
It's not easy to check the lights, since the unit is secured with four screws and duct tape.
In theory, it has a 10,000 hour (14 month) bulb and if you're changing them yearly, that's OK.
But how do you know if one died prematurely.
The light will NOT tell you.

So, I "solved" the problem by connecting the unit to a Kasa smart outlet which tells you the power consumption.
No bulbs (light still on) is 0.22 watts.
Each bulb adds 9 watts and both are about 18 watts. (See screenshot).

Also, the template says that the bulb socket is 1 1/2 inch, but if you use a circular saw, you have to take into account that the bulb socket is RECTANGULAR and you need a 2" saw.

Otherwise, it's a great value and the energy monitoring plug was only $12.
You'll save hundreds of dollars, bypassing the HVAC guy.
Good luck.
Hopefully, this was useful for you.

The first time I tried this product, it tasted really bitter and didn't do anything for me. I thought it was a fluke and that perhaps it was because I had just brushed my teeth. The lack of energy I chalked it up to me simply being extra tired.

However, I have since revisited the product again just a few days ago and I couldn't even finish it. I took two sips and it was like drinking the rind of a grapefruit. Super bitter. Yes, hibiscus is bitter, but not to the point of tasting like rind. The flavor is supposed to be berry hibiscus, but there isn't any hibiscus or berry flavor. Also, this pre-workout is supposed to be sweetened with monk fruit, but there's not a hint of sweetness anywhere. This product isn't tart, it's bitter.

Lastly, I didn't get any energy from taking this product... at all. Usually I'm sensitive to caffeine and can only get away with drinking half a scoop of a pre-workout, regardless of brand. Anything over half a scoop leaves me feeling like a jittery, anxious mess. This product however did absolutely nothing for me at all.

Based on my experience I would have given this product 1 star, however, I really like their ingredients list and how simple and natural it seems to be, bumping up my rating to 2.5 stars because I like more natural formulas and products.

text: Not at all satisfied with this product. When I first got it, I opened the bag it came in and didn’t smell a thing with the 4 pouches that are inside. I did smell them when I put my nose in the bag. My first thought was, peppermint and cinnamon are two very strong spices so why can’t I smell them? So I figured well the mice will smell them I guess. After all it is made for them. I’m building the inside of my cabin I live in and just finished a cabinet to go beside the kitchen sink cabinet. The first night I had put them out, I got chewing noises from the mouse trying to eat my newly built and installed cabinet! Apparently, I blocked his view. I did order the spray also so I grabbed that and sprayed the underside where he might have been chewing since I couldn’t see. About 15 minutes later, and mind you that spray smells so good, he started chewing again! So I grabbed the spray and doused the wood with the smell. It finally smelled like peppermint in the cabin! title: Very happy with this bag decision!
text:
I have spent the last month or so deciding on a new clinical bag. I wanted something spacious enough to fit all of the supplies I will need, but still compact. I was between purchasing this bag or the Nurse Mates Ultimate bag. I was wary because this bag did not have any picture reviews, but the video for it looked promising.

I have only just received the bag today, so this review is my first impression and is not reflective of long-term use. I also wanted to provide some more pictures that others can use for size comparison. Unfortunately, most of my chosen medical equipment is also black and may be difficult to see.

Things I like:
- The shoulder strap is comfortable and the hooks are metal.
- The sizing of the bag is awesome. It has plenty of space for items but still looks compact. The side view shows the width of the bag with the too-large organizer and the patient folder containing 2 ATI books.

- There is a large front zipper pocket, in my picture it holds an orange piece of paper that is 8.5x11" so you can visualize the width and depth.

- There is a large zipper pocket that folds down.
• Inside of it are 2 large padded pockets (I have my stethoscope in one and my foldable clipboard in the other)
• The velcro pocket organizer (when closing the bag I actually stick it on upside down as my scissors are fairly large.
• An unpadded thin pocket on the fold-down section. This also has a few loops you could put pens in.
• A small zipper pocket (I have my thermometer, pulse ox, and an extra penlight in it)
• A hook that you could attach your keys to

- On the back there is a pocket that contains the patient information folder. In my picture I have placed 2 ATI books in it so you can visualize the size of the folder.

- On the inside, there is a large main compartment, a padded laptop compartment, and a thin large compartment on the opposite side.
• To help visualize the size of the inside compartment I have included a picture with all of my ATI textbooks and a picture with a felt organizer (slightly too large for the bag). The organizer has my Omron automatic BP cuff, 2 pocket nursing diagnosis books, a pocket drug guide, and my wallet.

Things I don't like:
- Nothing really but I would love if it came with a different color interior option.
