title: My second purchase - this unit works great!
text:
This is the second of these units I've bought. I was very pleased with the first one, and they've improved it since then.

(The only issue I had with the original unit was a miniscule spring on the post that holds the roller. The spring wasn't secured to anything, and I eventually lost it when cleaning the unit after use. The manufacturer had now adjusted the design so the spring is secured to the post and can't be lost - excellent!)

My feet are callused and quickly get visible dry skin, which looks terrible. If I pumice them, I have to do it twice a week even when it's not sandal season, because the dry skin snags stockings and bed sheets. This unit is so much easier than soaking and pumicing! It's also improved the calluses with continued use over time.

I've never tried the battery version but I'm glad I got the corded one - I was worried it would be too powerful and cause bleeding, but no problem with that. Just follow the directions and until you get used to it, gently touch it to the callus for a few seconds at a time. Also, make sure your feet are dry with no recent lotion application, or the abrasive roller won't work as well.

It does generate skin dust, so I did it over a (dry) bathtub. The rollers last quite a while; I usually get at least 5-6 uses (both feet) out of one roller. I use the Extra Coarse ones, and sometimes a finer grit for my toes, as the skin there is thinner than on the heel.

You can clean it with an old toothbrush or slightly damp Q-tip, but what works even better is one of those spray cans of pressurized air, the kind used to blow dust off computer keyboards. The pressurized air can be used to clean the roller too.

This unit is a big time-saver; each session takes me about 10-15 minutes for both feet. I usually do it twice a week. I'm so glad to be done with the 30-45-minute soaking and pumicing! If you're considering one of these units, buy it - you won't be disappointed!

title: I had high hopes, but ...
text:
My friend needed a walker that could easily be put in a car, lightweight and not bulky. On screen, this one looked perfect--and indeed, it was very maneuverable. Not too hard to put together EXCEPT that the length of the seatback bar did not match the width of the walker and could not be inserted. I contacted the seller, who replied in one day that he'd get the maker right on it. That was nearly a month ago; I haven't heard a word since. Strike 1.

Then my friend tried it out. And we learned a lot about walkers. First, the wheels on this one, as on the simple frame walkers with no seat, were fixed in position, they didn't swivel. This means when you want to turn, or even slightly repoint the walker, you have to pick it up, turn it, and set it down. Very tiring, and hell on carpeting. Strike 2.

And the brakes ... there aren't any. It's designed so that when you sit on it, the posts of the back legs (the ones that are forward when you're sitting) hit the ground and keep the unit from moving. Unfortunately, when you simply lean on the walker a bit as you walk (as my friend, fresh from back surgery, had to) the posts engage the surface (floor, pavement) and voila, you're stuck! Strike 3, and you're out!

Bottom line: Well-made but poorly designed. Don't buy this.

title: Amazon has issues with its tissue products!
text:
This is NOT Puffs Plus with Lotion! The tissues are very rough - hard to use on your face and definitely LACK any kind of soothing lotion in or on them. I cancelled this from my Subscribe & Save because this 2nd delivery of 10 boxes is no better than the first. I had to go to CVS yesterday to purchase a few boxes of Puffs with Lotion, because I'm not going to return a huge box of 10 ... I will just have to slowly use them next spring-summer, when I'm not sick with a cold or exposed to lots of cold, dry air.
I have to say that I used to have the same problem with Amazon's Kleenex facial tissues, so that was why I tried this subscription for Puffs Plus instead. Sadly, they were no better than the rough Kleenex tissues. This makes me think that large companies like Amazon must negotiate with these manufacturers to have them make these substandard products that are cheaper, thus increasing their $$ margins. I agree with others who have said the same thing as I am -- you get what you pay for.
I had this exact same problem with buying Amazon's Charmin Ultra toilet tissue. I stopped buy toilet paper from Amazon, and I'm now buying it "in bulk" from Target (free delivery!). Target's Charmin feels like real Charmin Ultra toilet paper, but Amazon's definitely does not. Amazon's Charmin is rough - sometimes as rough as the Aria and some of the other 'recycled toilet tissue products are). Since I usually get $10 off each order via Target, I will start adding some Puffs Plus or soft Kleenex facial tissues to my Target order in the future. Sorry Amazon, but these tissues are no deal!

title: Feels nice on tired feet
text:
This wooden foot massager is great if you are someone who works on your feet all day. It comes with both the wooden rolling massager and the blue spiky ball as seen in the listing photos. The ball was a lot harder than I had imagined it to be. It's solid and does not flatten when you step on it. It's great if you really want to get a deep massage. When I first tried it, I thought it tickled a little bit, but as I put more pressure on the ball, that feeling went away. I would just be careful you put the ball away after you're done using it; you don't want to accidentally step on it in the middle of the night!
The wooden roller is also nice. It seems very durable; I can put a lot of pressure on my foot and it doesn't break. There are five rolling cylinders that each have knobs sticking up that push into your foot. On one of the cylinders, the knobs are larger and spaced farther apart. It doesn't slide around when you put your foot down, as there are pads underneath that make it stay put. The massager feels very nice on the bottom on my feet. I honestly wasn't too sure about it when I ordered it, because I have extremely ticklish feet, but I was pleasantly surprised. You can use the wooden massager for lighter pressure on your foot, or if you're looking for more pressure, you can always press down on it harder. The only thing that I don't really like about the wooden massager is that it's very squeaky. Every time you roll your foot back and forth, it squeaks. My cat was even spooked by the noise and comes to investigate every time i use it! So if you're looking for a quieter massager, I would suggest using the ball!

title: Innovative
text:
I’d like to start by saying I have very long, thick, curly hair. I didn’t realize just how long it was because I hadn’t straightened it in about 18 months because with 3 kids I simply don’t have that kind of time. A friend of mine mentioned getting a hair straightening brush and how much faster and easier it is so I thought I’d give one a try.

The Moxie Brush really is significantly faster than my regular flat iron, cutting styling time at least in half! I was worried that the brush would pull my hair or cause excessive static, but that wasn’t the case at all. It actually left my hair really smooth. I even noticed that since I was simply brushing my hair, I wasn’t getting burned. I have the heat resistant styling gloves, but I really don’t like to wear them because I like the feel my hair as I straighten it.

At first I kept pressing the buttons on the side while using it, but quickly I got the hang of holding the brush so that my fingers didn’t touch them. I think one thing that makes the Moxie Brush wonderful is that for people who aren’t used to using a regular flat iron, it’s a much simpler design. Aside from being great for your average user, it’s also a game changer for younger girls who haven’t used heated styling tools before, boyfriends who can’t be trusted not to burn off your ears, and people, like my mom, who just love the feeling of having their hair brushed.

I do have to deduct one star because though it took the curls out very quickly, when it came to getting the subtle kinks out it either took a lot of work or simply couldn’t straighten them and I had to go back over them with my regular flat iron. If you’re not looking for pin straight hair then this is absolutely the product for you. I think even despite having to use two tools to get the job done instead of one, this brush still saved me a ton of time and that is what I was going for anyway.

I was lucky enough to get to try out this product at a discount in exchange for my honest review. The Moxie Brush is extremely innovative with a ton of potential. It absolutely saves time, is way easier to use than a flat iron, and less likely to cause burns making it a must have tool for everyone that wants straight hair.

title: Worked great – while it worked
text:
This foot bath had some serious bubbling action going on – very relaxing and effective on those sore foot muscles after standing all day. It also maintained the warm water indefinitely – my footbaths usually last at least a half hour. But unfortunately, the product just didn’t stand the test of time.

After about eight uses, this footbath stopped bubbling altogether. Just one tiny hole producing a couple of stray bubbles was left. It still maintained warm water, the vibrating action still worked (which, in my opinion, was useless anyway), but without the bubbles, the added effectiveness over just a plain old soak in the tub was gone.

Although frustrated by spending good money on something that didn’t last, I have to admit I was avoiding using the thing anyway, because it has little knobby rollers on the bottom that are supposed to massage your feet, but are made out of such a hard plastic that they were downright painful. I had to keep shifting the position of my feet to avoid them. In addition, it emitted an especially strong, unpleasant chemical smell while it was hot and bubbling.

I previously had an earlier generation model of this HoMedics product which lasted for years and was comfortable. The bubbling action was far less effective, but I wish I had kept it. HoMedics needs to go back to the drawing board on this one. Hopefully, they will come up with a cross between the comfort and reliability of the older model and the advances of the new one – and use a less stinky plastic.

title: Tasty & convenient coffee alternative
text:
I'm somewhat new to chicory, but have been drawn to it in search of a cup of something warm to drink in the mornings to replace my previously daily cups of coffee. I'd previously purchased the Leroux brand of instant chicory a couple of times, but was drawn to Prewett's for being organic. The pricing and availability of either brand seems to change on a somewhat regular basis, but depending on when you catch it, Prewett's can sometimes be a better value...and for organic, that's pretty impressive. Another difference I noticed between the two is that Leroux recommends 3tsp for every 8oz of water, while Prewett's suggests only 1tsp per cup of water...either actually vary based upon your taste/preference. I find 2tsp is adequate for me with either brand. I do think that Leroux has a slightly more sweet flavor to it than Prewett's.

Shipping time for this product took longer than I'd anticipated since it wasn't offered with Prime...since I'd run out of my stash of Leroux, I wound up purchasing some *actual* chicory (Frontier Natural Products Organic Roasted Chicory Root Granules, 16 Ounce) (vs. instant) to tide me over (the Leroux pricing at the time was more than I'd like to spend). Maybe it's just because I started out with the instant kind to begin with, but I think I actually prefer the instant chicory over the chicory granules :T It's more convenient and I like the instant's flavor better!

I drink anywhere from 2-6 cups of this stuff every day, so I go through it relatively quickly. When I run through this current supply, I'll be back to see if Prewett's is still in stock at a reasonable price.

title: Crunchy algae
text:
I've been wanting to try spirulina but have been putting it off because I'm not a huge fan of powders -- I buy them and they sit on the shelf and I forget about them. The dried nibs caught my interest because I immediately wanted to try them on salads and other foods. They are satisfyingly crunchy and make a very nice salad topping as an alternative to bacon bits (or in addition to them). I ate a few right out of the bag. It's okay, but they're definitely better with other foods.

A teaspoon of the spirulina nibs contains an impressive amount of protein and a teaspoon is just about the right amount of spirulina nibs for a topping. title: Toxic Beauty
text:
This is a toxic product. The number two ingredient (water is the number one ingredient) is "Propylene Glycol".

Propylene Glycol (PG) is a solvent used to deliver other chemicals into the skin in topical products, it is also found in anti-freeze. Although PG is considered safe, PG can accumulate and cause lactic acidosis, central nervous system depression, coma, hypoglycemia, seizures, and hemolysis. Patients at risk for toxicity include infants, patients with renal insufficiency, patients with epilepsy, or burn patients who receive extensive dermal applications of PG. PG toxicity can occur at dosing of lorazepam as low as 4 to 6 mg per hour in adults. The clinical diagnosis of PG intoxication may be difficult since many institutions do not measure PG levels. However, the osmolar gap, anion gap, and lactate are commonly elevated in PG intoxication.

Also high on the list of ingredients are parabens. Parabens are used as preservatives (to prevent growth of bacteria and fungus).

"Parabens are a group of synthetic compounds commonly added to cosmetics and body products because they prevent the growth of fungus and bacteria. They are dangerous because, like so many ingredients in this list, they disrupt hormone functions, potentially leading to increased risk of breast cancer and reproductive toxicity. Five common types of parabens have been banned in the EU, and the FDA is under pressure to ban them in the U.S." [Amy Myers]

Following parabens is "Triethanolamine". Triethanolamine in huge doses causes liver cancer in mice. Also in huge doses it causes a decrease in betaine and choline.

The container is eight ounces at 100,000 IU of retinol per ounce for a total of 800,000 IUs of vitamin A per container. You can use these numbers to calculate your daily dose based on how rapidly you use this product. To be safe you probably should not use more per day than would result in using this up over a span of about two years. Note: there is more of all of the above mentioned toxins than there is vitamin A in this product.

I don't care for the odor of this cream.

Depending on your approach to living in a "chemical soup" you may or may not wish to apply this to your skin on a daily basis. In small doses, most people should never develop a problem. For those aiming for a long and healthy life, this might not be the product for you.

title: Vibration is Excellent; Sound Alarm is Faint
text:
When I first used the watch, the alarm was faint, hard to hear. But after I put in a new battery (YouTube has demo on how to do that), it was loud enough. So I was able just to use the hourly beeper without setting any of the 12 alarms -- this to save battery life. After a while, the vibration & alarm stopped working, though the watch read the time. I learned that when this happens, it means you need a new battery. It lasted may 1-2 months at first, with too faint alarm, then alarm quit. The battery that came with it must have been low to begin with. So with a new battery, I will now find out how long the battery lasts. The method of setting the options is a bit complicated. Fortunately, one can find a manual on line, if one loses the instructions that come with. I give 4 stars instead of 5 because of the difficulty in setting the parameters.

What is above is post script. What is below is my first impressions.

This watch does what I wanted; it reminds me every hour on the hour. This watch has both an hourly beeper (hourly chime) and also 12 set alarms. I hardly notice the sound alarm; it is too high pitched & faint for me. Maybe it would seem louder to a child, as one loses the ability to hear high frequencies with age. So for me the sound alarm is practically useless. I don't notice it usually. Fortunately, there is an alternative alarm by vibration. You can chose vibration only, sound only, or both. So I get a vibration every hour via the hourly chime (hourly vibration) setting. Then I also set 12 alarms per day; set to go off a little after the hour so that I get both alarms. On the hour I get a single vibration. 12 times a day I get multiple vibrations, which need to be turned off with the ST/STP button. I don't know how long it would keep vibrating with discrete pulses if I didn't stop it each time. If you lay the watch on a wood table, it makes the table vibrate noticeably.

I do wonder how long the battery is going to last with the vibrations on.

The instructions were difficult to follow, but eventually I figured it out.

The watch has 4 buttons, 2 on left & 2 on right edge. On the left 1) light, 2) mode.
On the right 3) ST./STP, 4) SET / RST.

The 3rd button is in case you are driving a car & run out of oil. You push the STP & out pops a can of STP, the racer's edge! [just joking]

The black leather band is nice, but thinner (~1/2 inch) than I would like as a man. The watch itself is standard diameter for a man's watch. The numbers are easy to read, but not as easy to read as with the $20 Armitron watch, which has a slightly bigger diameter and the loudest beep alarm I have found yet.

I now have bought 3 watches:
the $20 Armitron,
the Timex Ironman Sleek 50-Lap Full-size Digital Men's watch #T5K335,
and this VibraLITE12.
I sent back the Timex for a refund, which Amazon did very efficiently.
The Armitron was so cheap that I didn't bother returning it.

The Armitron is not loud enough for me either, though the loudest of the 3; sometimes I hear it; sometimes I don't notice. I am over 39; my hearing IMHO is within normal acuity limits, but probably not quite as good as when I was 18. If you are young, have excellent hearing, & want an auditory beep watch, you might do well to try the $20 Armitron first, which has an hourly chime. Unfortunately, you are not likely to find in a selling description a good description of the alarm or hourly chime (dB's of loudness, pitch/frequency, duration).

Apparently this VibraLITE's primary target user is the bed-wetter. I did not get it for that purpose!
Can you imagine being woke up every hour at night to go to the restroom!!!
Of course you don't have to set it to do the hourly chime/vibration/notifier. That is an option.
And you don't have to set any or all 12 (major) alarms.

Post Script, a couple of days later:

Suddenly the watch seemed to have completely deprogrammed itself. It showed the wrong time. I don't know how I did it, but I must have activated a different time program. Apparently the watch has 3 time programs; so if you are a jet-setter, and live one day in Peking, one day in London, & one day in Minneapolis; you can set the watch 3 times for the 3 locations; then by pushing a button or combo of buttons, you can change the watch for the new location. Or if you were an Amateur Radio operator, you could set one time program for GMT, so that you could log your log in GMT. Or if you have relatives in Japan, & want to know what time it is there before you phone them, you could set one Time program for Tokyo.

So, there was apparently nothing wrong with the watch except that one can accidentally change time programs (zones). I probably changed the time zones accidentally when I was turning off the Vibration after an alarm went off. I had not planned to use this "3 TIME ZONE" capability, so I didn't bother to learn how to use it. Maybe I pushed to Vibe off more than once & that did it.

title: Beautiful Eyelashes Without Expensive Mascara!
text:
I am the last person on Earth to ask about beauty advice. I grew up as a tomboy, and to a certain degree, I still am one. I wear makeup maybe once a year, more often if there is a wedding or other special event. So when I was asked to review the Lovely Lashes Eyelash Curler (or LLEC, for short), I figured that I would give it a try, just to do something different. So, without further ado, here is my review:

Construction

The Lovely Lashes Eyelash Curler by Izy Trends, in terms of function, is no different than other eyelash curlers on the market. They operate by inserting your finger and thumb into the handles; spread the arms apart to open the guillotine-style press that curls your eyelashes, and pinch the handles together to bring the base of the curler up to the top metal portion, closing the guillotine and pressing your eyelashes into a curl.

In terms of durability, the LLEC feels durable and is comfortable to use. It weighs in at 0.8 ounces (22 grams) and has a solid construction at the joints that appear to be able to withstand frequent use. The handles have a rubber insert along the inside of the loops so that your fingers and thumb do not press against the bare metal (which many other brands do, sometimes leaving a mark). Finally, the lower half of the press that is used to curl the lashes is lined with a rubber strip that helps the lashes to curl more gently (as opposed to eyelash curlers that have only metal, which can sometimes damage the hairs). The LLEC includes a spare strip should anything happen to the first one.

Usage

I have a disease called Sjogrën’s Syndrome, which is basically a more severe form of dry eye (as well as other mucous membranes). As a result, any type of mascara, eye liner, or eye shadow getting into my eyes is bad juju. So while I don’t wear makeup, when I do I am limited in what I can use. An eyelash curler is definitely something that I want to keep in my arsenal, so I made sure to use the LLEC every day for three weeks.

Pros:
• Works best when the eyelashes are wet; immediately after washing your face or a shower is ideal.
• I was able to curl every eyelash, even down to the corners of my eye, with no discomfort.
• The curl on both eyes was consistent and even, so I didn’t have to worry about a lopsided look.
• The LLEC cleaned up easily with no stains or other residue; I didn’t even need water at times.

Cons:
• Manipulating the LLEC to the correct angle to get to the corners takes a bit of practice. While it isn’t painful, it does require getting used to positioning the curler so that it grabs just the eyelashes without pulling on your eyelid.
• While the extra rubber pad is a nice touch, it is small and potentially VERY easy to lose.

Overall

The Lovely Lash Eyelash Curler is a solid product that is constructed well and performs exactly as promised. It is comfortable to use and includes an extra pad to extend the life of its guillotine-style curling press, and when combined with the Lifetime Warranty offered by the manufacturer, it makes the LLEC a great value. Whether you eschew mascara due to cost or because of a health issue like I have, the Lovely Lash Eyelash Curler will enable you to have eyelashes that will bring attention to your beautiful eyes without the price tag of expensive eye-related cosmetics. Just be prepared for all of the compliments!

title: Helpful combination remedy; economical in wet doses
text:
This combination remedy is good for general purposes and can help with specific ailments when you're not sure which single homeopathic remedy is most appropriate.

I use homeopathic remedies and am used to allowing the pillules (round pellets of single remedies) to dissolve under my tongue, which, depending upon the size, takes about 15 minutes. Pillules are small, smooth and round, so they don't bother me. However, I don't care for the sensation of these dry tablets under my tongue, and they take a long time to dissolve. Instead, I make a "wet" dose, which also works with pillules. Wet dosing is also an easy and gentle way to dose dogs and cats.

Here's how to prepare a wet dose: Put one tablet in a glass or bottle of water (room temp. or cold) and allow it to dissolve -- it may take up to an hour, but that doesn't matter. (I prefer not to use hot water or any hot beverage, though my homeopath will put remedies in hot beverages.) Even before it's fully dissolved the remedy's energy has entered the water, so you can start sipping it right away, which you'll want to do if you have an acute, urgent need. Sip the remedy throughout the day, particularly when you feel symptoms.

I recommend using glass bottles because you can transfer an ounce or so of the original wet dose to more bottles of water, thus keeping the remedy going for days. Dilution doesn't effect the potency of the remedy. You can also shake the bottle a few times before use, which very slightly increases the potency, a practice often recommended. If you use a glass, just stir the remedy before each sip. Store the bottles in the refrigerator to keep them longer.

Wet dosing is the most economical way to use homeopathic remedies because you can get several day's worth of doses from one tablet or a few pillules.

If you're using a single remedy in a higher potency you need to monitor your response and adjust the dose accordingly -- consult a reliable source on homeopathy for dosing!

title: It’s done wonders for me.
text:
I was bitten by a tick with a target shaped rash early July of this year (2018). Due to past history of spinal injuries, and auto immune issues, Lyme Disease set in quickly with very difficult symptoms. After one cycle of Doxycycline it was better for about a week, then it returned with vengeance. Second round of Doxycycline didn’t work and the next step with western medicine would’ve been long term and serious antibiotics in both oral and possibly intravenous forms.

I came across this formula while reading Dr. Will Rawls M.D.’s book “Unlocking Lyme” which detailed how various herbs work with both the infections and the symptoms with excellent scientific explanations. The herbs in this formula are all listed (minus stevia) but it’s missing Andrographis if you want to follow Stephen Buhner’s protocol which is also recommended in Dr. Rawls’ book. I opted to start this formula plus andrographis while I was still finishing up my second cycle of Doxycycline. My body did go through herxing. Started with 1 dose per day, eventually increased to 2, now I am on 3-5 doses per day. When I was herxing, I was sweating profusely all day long. My sheets stunk of sweat that didn’t smell like me. The sweat must’ve been pretty toxic as my sheets also started to deteriorate when I wished them a couple times later. As soon as I started taking this formula, I could feel my brain functioning more clearly. I still got winded easily, but I was not exhausted to the point of dysfunction any more. It was a gradual process to recover out of the fatigue. And my physical pain also began to subside. My flexibility actually increased and got better than before Lyme (I lost quite a bit of flexibity due to my spinal injuries). This is because of the anti-inflammatory and immune boosting qualities of these herbs. But I still had swollen joints and pain if I ate too much starch/gluten/sugar/dairy. After running a test for rheumatoid arthritis and it came back negative, I started a gluten-free, low starch, low sugar and low dairy diet 3 weeks ago. In the past 3 weeks, I lost 8 lb. I have never been able to lose weight this fast my whole life. I have gone on similar food regimen before, and I was lucky if I lost 0.8 lb per week. I can see these herbs are repairing my internal system, and my body is absorbing nutrients differently therefore eliminating the need to store fat.

I started with the 2 oz package, and it was okay when I was ramping up the dosage. I ordered the largest loose powder package to follow suit, it looks like I’ll be through with it in the next 2 weeks again. (I am dosing 3-5 days everyday). I dilute it with a small amount of hot water then mixed with a little bit of cold water, and down it like a shot. It’s not pleasant but it’s not intolerable. I also ordered the vegan capsules. For some reason I get constipated when I use the capsules, so I am sticking with the powder. But the capsules are very convenient when I need to be out of the house for a while.

I am planning on continuing this formula plus the andrographis for 6 months in the high dosage. I am not sure what I would do after. I am glad my body is healing. Hope this information is helpful.

title: A godsend for those of us who can't stop hitting snooze! Thank you, Lord!
text:
If you're like me, waking up early is the absolute worst...something akin to torture. It's so bad that it's *actually* physically painful. And while coffee is great - it IS life's splendid elixir, after all - it has its drawbacks. For example, you have to take the time to brew it, consume an entire (at least) cup, AND wait for it to work its magic. That's fine on a leisurely weekend morning, but what about when we need to get up early to take on the day? This is all a horrible recipe for oversleeping, or at the very least, having one hell of a time getting up. Can you say "unpleasant", "tired", and "not happy"?

Well, that's all a thing of the past.

Introducing Mocca shots. You just take one of these small, sweet chews and you're done. No having to gulp down a massive, steaming coffee the size of a football field to wake up. If you still want to enjoy your cappuccino or what have you later on, that's fine. But these "gummies" will jumpstart your system, and fast - the same way one would jumpstart a car with a dead battery, and the car is instantaneously running again. They're not only great for those of us who struggle with waking up, but also us troubled folk who experience the dreaded daily afternoon slump (you know what I mean: yawning, listlessness, nodding off at the desk. Keep a few of these suckers handy and you won't have to deal with unwanted afternoon drowsiness again!)

They have a texture that's kind of akin to a very chewy caramel, but with a chocolatey/coffee-ish taste. Some people don't like the flavors but I am personally finding them to be pretty darn enjoyable and yummy. When you consume one, you don't feel like you're eating a vitamin/supplement/health gummy/etc. It really just feels like you're enjoying a chocolate-and-coffee-flavored candy bite. That's a pretty sweet deal - literally.

This is a fabulous life hack. Just one of these babies has 100mg of caffeine - almost exactly the same amount as a cup of cawfee. But it works five times faster and you don't need to gulp down eight+ ounces of hot liquid. These chews are awesome and I happen to think they taste fabulous. So far, I love the "Dark Chocolate Orange" and "Dutch Cocoa" varieties. Obviously, I bought them for the energizing effects, not the flavors, but this is a nice bonus!

I was also really impressed by all of the other bells and whistles this product touts. You would expect a coffee gummy to be bad for you, junky, and low-quality - just loaded with chemicals and corn syrup and a million calories. Well, not these. They're merely 25 calories a chew (you only need one, maybe two tops) and are made with high-quality ingredients like cane sugar, organic cocoa butter, and ginkgo biloba extract. Nice, right? Additionally, these 'lil nuggets are dairy-free, vegan-friendly, gluten-free, non-GMO (awesome), all natural, and are even made in the USA!

I was also shocked (in a good way) by the nutritional value - it seemed too good to be true! Here are some of the vitamins/minerals they contain, as well as what percentage of your daily value just one cube provides. The breakdown goes like this:

Riboflavin - 70%
Niacin - 60%
Vitamin B6 - 60%
Vitamin B12 - 120% (!!!)

That's impressive. So, not only are you getting your coffee in the form of an easy-to-consume, small, low-calorie, yummy treat, but you also get a shot of some essential vitamins.

I hope they continue making these. I can't wait to put them to further work.

Stay caffeinated, my friends! And if you're looking for a faster alternative (or supplement) to your morning cup 'o Joe, give these a try.

PS Another way this helps you get out of bed? It's something to look forward to...kind of in a similar way that one might look forward to their morning cup of coffee, BUT without the work. It's instant gratification, and in many ways. You just pop open the package and enjoy a sweet treat, AND you get some energy within minutes. This is a winning product. I highly recommend!

title: Strong but effective toner.
text:
This Clear and Smooth Anti-Acne Pimples Deep Pore Cleanser claims to "lift dirt, grit, oils, and sweat from pores while depositing salicylic acid into pores to control blemishes"

It comes in a 6fl oz plastic bottle. The only downside to the packaging in my opinion is that it does not have like a squirt top to dispense the product, it's just an open screw top lid. This could make for a quick spill and the loss of a lot of product if you over pour.

Now when I ordered this, I thought it was going to be like an actual gel facial cleanser, this is not it's like a toner, which was fine because I needed a good toner too.

Does it do everything it says it does? I think so. Per the instructions, you cleanse your skin, then use a cotton swab to apply this product. It warns against using too often because excessive drying could occur. I used as directed once a day for a while now. It absolutely lifts oil and dirt, because they're is always makeup on the pads when I get done toning. It's very strong. My face has cleared up a good bit, and my pores seem smaller. It is very drying so be sure to use a good moisturizer afterward.

As long as your skin isn't very sensitive, I recommend this toner. It think it has really helped out my problem skin!

title: Insanely Delicious!!
text:
I just tried this on my fried eggs and they were phenomenal!! All I did was sprinkle some over top and cooked it right in. Not saying that this the best way to use this powder, but it WAS crazy delicious.

I decided to do that after opening the bag and sniffing it first. Broccoli can have a uniquely unpleasant odor anyway—you know what I’m talking about. In a concentrate like this, I figured it would be pretty ripe, so I was shocked when all I could smell was just a really yummy, savory broccoli soup-type aroma.

Honestly, I’m not sure who would then decide to blend this with fruit, oh my word no! That’s a personal choice, obviously but this is not going to pair well with sweet smoothie ingredients in my opinion. Gross.

Flavor-wise, it’s sooo much better than I expected! I can think of many other ways to use this. The flavor is amazing. And since I heated it up in a pan, of course my whole house smells like broccoli now. But it’s actually still a very yummy smell, not like the big green fart I was expecting.

I’m going to get more of this for sure. I think it’s a brilliant way to work tasty, clean, mega-greens into multiple recipes. The only way that was going to work for me is if it tasted good, and this is crazy delicious, so CHECK. Now, I can’t wait to try the spinach too!

It lowered my estrogen beautifully, as well as the drug. It also helped my arthritis for the first 15 months. After that, I suffered from low estrogen arthritis, which is to be expected on any estrogen lowering product I am told.
I am NOT a doctor, just a patient. I have terrible reactions to medicines. If there is a 1% chance of a side effect, it seems like I get it.
I can't say it will work for you, but it did me. I didn't have any choice but to try something else--well I could have had my ovaries removed and I didn't fancy that. I am NOT paid by this company--I wish I were!!!! As a cancer patient, I would not recommend this to other women if I didn't think that it worked. God bless you and good luck with your treatment, whatever you choose.

title: A Few Minor Issues Mar This Otherwise Decent Product
text:
UPDATE: I just had my first visit to the dentist since I started using this toothbrush and the hygienist said that there was a marked improvement since my last visit. Bottom line is that the toothbrush works and it works better than manual brushing.

Over the years I've used a number of electric tooth brushes. This is the first "sonic" brush I've used and for the most part I'm pretty satisfied with it. After using it for the better part of two weeks I can say that for the price it has worked out nicely. It feels well made and solid. The case it comes in appears to be sturdy enough to survive being tossed into a travel bag. There are enough settings to accommodate everything from gentle to more aggressive brushing and the two minute timer with stops every 30 seconds is a nice touch.

It should be noted that the product ships with two brush heads. The photo seems to indicate that there is one attached to the body of the brush with two spares. That is not the case. That's not a big issue, but it should be noted for those who shop by photo and not by description. A more serious issue is that the charging base doesn't provide a solid support for the body of the unit. While the handle drops into the base easily there is nothing to hold it there. No clip. No magnet. No friction. The end result is that there is nothing to keep a slight nudge from topping the handle out of the base. You're not going to want to leave this charging anywhere it can be bumped and sent crashing to the floor. Also, the cable that comes with the unit has to be connected to a USB port. No power supply is provided with the brush. You will either use an AC to USB converter or plug it directly into a port on a computer.

The fairly limited directions that come with the product make no mention of how to obtain replacement brushes. Since the suggested life of the brush head is three months you will need to replace the two that come with the kit within six months. Fortunately, there is an email address in the directions and when I wrote to ask about replacements I had an answer in under 24 hours. They are available on Amazon and that was a good thing to find out. It was also nice to discover that there is someone on the other end of the email address and if their general support is as good that's comforting.

All in all, if you're looking for a sonic toothbrush this one is pretty good. I'll update this review down the road if it warrants additional comment.

title: GREAT for night driving, photochromic not so great
text:
[[VIDEOID:7ce66efa321fe9e8f2af0641c7e1a5b5]] I like night driving glasses. I've been using a set of polarized night drivers for some time. They really do cut down on the glare of oncoming headlights and the super bright LED taillights that are in common use today.

For that, these are awesome! The style is a classic aviator, pretty much the granddaddy of all sunglasses. Hard to go wrong there and these are right on the standard for that style.

The build quality is excellent. They have a generously sized lens and overall frame width. My head size is ~23&3/4" (~60 cm) around, measured just above the ears & eyebrows. I wear a size extra-large hat most of the time, depending on the brand and style. I've got a pretty big noggin, a big face, and I'm generally a pretty big guy. These glasses with their large frame and spring hinges fit my head great, and should fit most people even large headed folks like myself!

For me the really interesting part was the "photochromic" aspect of the lenses. I have been wanting to try one of the budget brand photochromic pairs for some time now so I thought I'd give these a shot. Keep in mind, they generally won't darken in a vehicle anyway so that feature is probably somewhat useless on a pair of driving glasses, but still.

If you check out my attached video you'll see that these DO darken under UV light. They don't darken as much or as dramatically as a pair of prescription photochromic lenses, but they do darken. I guess that's a checkmark in their favor. Still, given that they don't darken very much and don't shade very much they would never be a go to pair of glasses for sunny days for me.

I'd describe the total shade level, even after exposure to bright sunlight, as very light.

The polarization is legit. I verified it with a polarization test card, my computer monitor, and some water splashed on the driveway outside. In all tests, there is an obvious polarization effect. There are levels of polarization though and I would describe these as only lightly polarized. Good enough for driving but I'd not like these for a day on the boat (either for total shade level or for level of polarization).

All in all these are a really nice set of NIGHT driving glasses. Other than that I just don't see any value in the photochromic effect on these glasses so I'm knocking off a star for a 4 star total rating. It would be 3 stars but they are really very nicely made glasses and excellent for night driving so I might be generous in this rating.

title: Not all features work
text:
This is a pretty good unit. I like that it has a cell presence. No matter where dad may roam, we have a chance of him being safe. The people at the service are nice, but they've got some work to do. First, there's a feature called "Find Name" you just text "Find Name" with the first name of your loved one and it texts you back a map showing where they are. HOWEVER, if it can't find the person because they're in a cell-inaccessible location like a basement of a hospital or something, it just sends you a map of the last place you located them. I would rather it just said it didn't know where he was. This is a software issue. All they'd have to do is make it more pro-active where it reported its location more often. Pretty simple actually! Also, the company should have some additional hardware like buttons we could put down low in case dad falls and doesn't have his unit on.
Dad doesn't complain about the weight, but it does bang against things regularly. This triggers the fall alarm. Fortunately, it asks him if he's okay before it sends the alarm. He can cancel it by pushing the button. It's not really loud, so there's another thing that could be improved.

Update: As I mentioned, the locate feature is wildly inconsistent. I discovered that the company is even worse. I told them to remove this charge and I didn't notice they didn't until my credit card expired. I know, that's my responsibility, but it's a small amount so I didn't notice. I went to update my account online and you can't. What kind of tech company doesn't have an online payment / account management interface? So I cancelled the account. Go with a better company!

title: "Betting" on Glucosamine/Chondroitin/MSM in advance of medical consensus, because research is slow and life is fast
text:
The honest truth: I don't know if this joint health combo is helping me or my husband to any great extent, either in the now or prophylactically. Clinical proof of a supplement's benefit from one source can be contradicted by another study, or critically disparaged due to some flaw, bias, or oversight in the research that is claimed. I don't have time to acquire the medical expertise, but have come to rely on a certain rough consensus of experts not directly connected to the supplement industry, using my hit-and-miss method of searching Web MD, online news, etc. Through this method, I've recently eliminated Omega-3 supplements from our diet (while commensurately increasing natural sources where I can, just in case), and I guess I'm a bit on the fence with Glucosamine formulas. My joints are feeling a little better these days, but I've also made a few other good choices in the area of diet or exercise - and got more supportive shoes! -- so there's no attributing that improved joint comfort to one thing or another with any real certainty. (Nor would I want to delay other positive changes in my health regimen for the purpose of "isolating" results.)

Oh, and It also bears mentioning that the studies most often cited for glucosamine indicate that the effectiveness is more pronouncedly noticeable where joint pain suffered is greater in the first place. Not that I equate short-term pain relief with long-term benefit, but as someone thankfully more creaky than actually sidelined by pain, I'm not anticipating dramatic results.

I like and trust Viva labs for the coconut and other gluten/dairy-free flours, etc. from its grocery line, so am happy to try out this product. It's an easy to swallow vegetable capsule that surrounds the Glucosamine, Chondroitin and MSM, and being particularly intrigued by the claimed benefits to cartilage, tendons and ligaments of MSM - yeah, I've had a few problems there in recent years - this is a formulation that I'm very happy to try for awhile, particularly at the price.

The capsule itself is claimed Halal but those following a Kosher diet should be advise that the Glucosamine is derived from shrimp shells. Not relevant to me specifically, but I appreciate that Viva is meticulous about spelling these things out.

Viva Labs provided me with a complimentary bottle of this product for evaluation.

The taste is a lot like sugar only lighter, a bit less sweet and because of that, more pleasant, imo. Much nicer that Stevia by itself. I've also ordered a Stevia/Erythritol blended product to try, especially for baking. You need more Erythritol than sugar if replacing in a recipe, and that would get more expensive than I like very quickly.

I think the best use of this product is sprinkling it on fruit like strawberries, oranges, etc., or maybe topping baked goods. It will add some sparkle for anytime you want to see those sugar crystals. The crystals are larger than table sugar, which makes them especially decorative.

title: This was once a great phone--now, not so much
text:
I work as a contractor with a state program to secure telephones for low-to-moderate income people with hearing loss. The average cost of a higher-volume amplified phone is around $140. Any phone that amplifies up to 40 dB is only for those with mild-to-moderate hearing loss. Most who can benefit from amplified phones need 50+dB of amplification. The FCC funds telephone assistance programs to participating states so people with hearing loss can have access to phones they can use, since the phone service is funded in part by American tax dollars. To check availability of a TAP program in your state, go to [...] and type your state name in the search box.

Having explained that, I should say Maxi-aids introduced this phone about 8 years ago, and it was a wonderful, lower cost phone in a whole range of amplifications from 30-50 dB. Our state used so many of these in the 50dB model that it was on backorder. When it came back in stock six months later, it was a much less satisfactory product. The electrical cord (necessary for any phone which amplifies above 35 dB, to support all its features) was no longer visibly polarized--one blade larger than the other. Plugging it in incorrectly, however, caused the phone to lose all its power features--no backlit keypad, no amplification, no tone control, no louder ringer. This can happen in only a few weeks.

Other unfortunate features are noted in the previous review: Plug this in near a phone which is set up with an emergency alert (you know, the amulet you press when you've 'fallen and can't get up' to alert 911 action), and you'll hear a truly ghastly sound. It's also subject to static on the line, and just manages to last out the one-year warranty. Usually. This phone has been cheapened out cut costs and increase profits. It is NOTMM worth the price.

It's important to keep your receipt when you purchase anything. If you find it does not live up to expectations, send it back. Most decent resellers have a money-back guarantee, as does Maxi-aids. ALWAYS ASSUME THE 30 DAY MONEY-BACK PERIOD STARTS THE DAY YOU PLACE THE ORDER. And always call to secure an RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) before you send anything back. Maxi-aids: is quick to ship out. I've received stuff in less than 24 hours with standard shipping. I've never received anythiing in more than 5 business days. So you have time to try the device and return it, if necessary. And if you can, go to your area Telecommunications or Telephone Assistance Program demo center to test out equipment before you buy it. Hope this helps!

It also slices pretty easily on anything that has an edge, like between the stainless finish of a microwave and the glass. Each one can be used twice in my opinion at most or until the surface on both sides are no longer white. I use it to clean the tub/shower, sinks and appliances.

Video Background: I added a video of cleaning permanent marker off a Simple Human stainless steel trash can. At the time of the video, the marker was about 1 week old. When my son first did it, I tried to clean it off immediately. First trying with a rag with soap and water but it was pointless. It would not come off. Then my husband suggested the magic eraser. It came off so easily! I was amazed. I regretted I didn't document the process because it was so unbelievable. 1 week later when taking out the trash, I notice I missed some of the permanent marker so that is when this video is taken. Even after 1 week it was still easy to remove. All that I did was wet the eraser with water. I did not use any other products.

title: Does the job...
text:
I wear earbuds often, and earplugs to sleep, so there is often a buildup of earwax inside the ear canal. While I have dry earwax that is often easier to clean than someone that has wet, gooey earwax, these larger clumps are often very difficult to remove. I have tried hydrogen peroxide, water syringes, and even a Q-Tip to try to ease these out, but they simply don't want to come out.

With this camera, I was able to remove it in about 5 minutes -- it does take some time for you to get used to how to do it, and you definitely don't want to rush it or go too quickly. The app does have a Left/Right mirror function so you can match it with your hands and the direction you are going. Depending on how large the earwax is, you may have to change the spoon tip to match the earwax so it can be removed properly. But this is certainly better than doing it with water as long as you are careful in your approach as you don't have to dry your ear canal or have bouts of dizziness after you irrigate the ear canal.

title: All coarse grinding heads - Vacuum is kind of cool!
text:
With the electric foot file device I received six (6) small grinding heads, and two (2) large grinding heads. All of them are coarse-grit. There is a USB charging cord but no adapter. Attach either 3 small grinding disks or one large (your preference), turn on the machine at one of the two (2) speed settings, and it does a fine job at smoothing down dry skin.

The vacuum is kind of cool! There is a fan behind the grinding disk mechanism that is facing inwards, into the handheld device. It pulls air through and behind the grinding disks. The dead skin that it catches goes into a fine screen mesh cup with holes that are too small for skin to pass through. Empty the cup by removing the grinding head and a plastic grind head holder. It's easy to clean because the parts are water resistant.

One star removed for there being only "coarse" grit grinders unlike the ad mentioned. All of mine are "coarse" grinders. However, the product works as advertised. Follow-up with something finer like a nail file or fine pumice stone (if needed afterwards). I only needed lotion afterwards.

The ad says the following, but I can't see or feel a difference between any of them.
> Three Different Replacement Roller Heads
> • Fine roller head: Suitable for dead skin on hands and feet, or some delicate skin care.
> • Regular roller head: Suitable for new calluses on feet and normal skin care.
> • Coarse roller head: Suitable for stubborn thick calluses on feet, corn, and dead skin.

title: Thick, Sturdy, Nose Clip, No Filter Pocket, Breathable (S: Age 4-7)
text: I got the "S: Age 4-7" sized masks. They are a really cute smaller sized mask! I measured them differently than the seller did. I measured from edge to edge without counting for the depth of the mask. Please see photos for those measurements. The masks are thick, sturdy, and not very stretchy. There is a strong nose piece that will stay-put! The straps are soft and have a bead that you can slide to adjust for your child's ear-span. There are TWO leashes that come with the four masks. They are not a break-away type of leash so you may want to look for another leash if needed. The leashes are a nice rope type with metal clasps at the ends. They are usually worn to help a mask stay on, or to keep the mask dangling in front while eating - also so the mask won't get lost or touch a contaminated surface.  The leashes have a push button length adjuster that slides up/down itself. They are cool looking masks but they do not have a filter pocket. If you have your heart set on these, maybe you could cut a slit in one end and make a hemline so you can insert one between the layers. Nice masks otherwise!

title: Things I learned about the product.....
text:
I believe this is one of the best purchases I have made! This is what I discovered about the product and using it:

(1)- One roller is included with the product. It listed as extra course, so I was a bit worried that it would be too abrasive and that I might use it in such a way that it would make my feet feel tender. It was just fine. It is not nearly as abrasive as I feared. In fact, if your feet are very bad you may even want to consider ordering a replacement roller [refill] that is even more course.
(2)- I had thought I might need the cone shaped attachments that can be purchased as a separate accessory in order to do the area around my toes. I did not need them. The roller that comes with the product gets close enough and works fine.
(3)- Since the roller was not excessively abrasive, I decided to do my hands also. It worked great! I even learned how to get close to my nails and smooth the rough skin around them.
(4)- It is good to use lotion after use. I had considered the cream that the company offers to put on the feet after removing calluses. I did not get that, but instead used the Gold Bond Ultimate lotion that I already had and it works well for me.
(5)- The only reason I did not give the product a perfect rating was the cord. I thought since the information about the product said 'corded' that it mean the cord was made permanently into the product. It is not. It uses a cord that is similar to the type that would be used to charge a device and the portion that plugs into the electrical receptacle also has the same type end that almost every rechargeable devises have [not just the standard prong like for a lamp]. When I first received the product I thought perhaps they had sent me a rechargeable callus remover, but they did not because the one I got only works with the cord in it, as the product I ordered stated. The cord itself does not bother me because I knew it would be there. What has bothered me is that it sometimes comes out of the device while I am using it. No big deal--I can plug it in again, but I am concerned that over time as the cord comes out more frequently and is plugged in more and more, that it will be difficult to keep it in. But if it does, I will figure a way to tape it onto the device somehow. (5) A very important thing I learned is that it is best to put something such as a towel under your feet when using the product. Especially in your initial uses there will be a lot of dust!
(6)- I am glad I did not get a battery operated model. Not having to replace them saves money.
(7)- Even with the cord issue I mentioned, I am still glad I got the corded product because I can store it in a drawer out of sight when I am done with it. When I am ready to use the product it is always ready for use since it never has to be charged.
(8)- The cord that comes with it is about 6 feet long. For me, that is adequate, but if not, it could always be plugged into an extension cord. (8)- The product head can be rinsed under running water [do not immerse in water].
(9)- Taking the roller out is very easy. All you do is slide a button on the side of the product and remove the roller.
(10)- A very small brush comes with the product to dust off the roller. But after using the product a week, I remove the roller and scrub it with an old toothbrush using soapy water. I then put it on a paper towel for several hours to make sure it is dry before I store the product.
(11)- I love this product and I have decided that I won't ever be without one of these devices again!

title: EXACTLY what I was looking for!
text:
I am SO glad I found this! My aging feet are starting to hurt too often, and I'm becoming more aware of shoe cushioning. However, I've been bewildered with the multitude of insoles offered on amazon... most of them have a dozen rave reviews written in poor English, and I wonder whether they are legit. I tried such a pair, but returned them... they were for flat feet, and didn't really provide much cushioning at all.

Rather than go through that again (and again), I found a link on a running site from someone who made their own from this stuff, so I decided to give it a try. Being one who likes to make things complex, I decided to use some old sorbethane I've had forever and add some inserts at my pressure points. I used the existing manufacturer EVA insole to trace the contour, but also to determine where the pressure points were... I layed some transparent drafting film over the old insole and traced around areas that showed excessive wear... the ball of the foot primarily, and surprisingly the toe. The heel was not too worn, but I went ahead and added one there. I then cut the shapes out of the film and used the holes as a template for the sorbethane inserts. I've attached a pic of the final creation.

And it works wonderfully! Better than I could have imagined! I'll report back with a long-term review after I put some miles on them, but so far it's great! Like another reviewer, I'm going to see if I can find something to glue a thin cover to everything so that the parts stay in place. I'm thinking some 3M automotive trim adhesive, since it's made for all materials (including foam and rubber) and is designed for extremes of heat and humidity:

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0002JMPRK/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o03_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1

But already this is EXACTLY what I was looking for!

title: Accurate and strangely inspiring
text:
The first stick I used showed I was already in ketosis which made me nervous, as I did not think I had been strict enough for long enough to show ketones. A couple hours later I got the same result. I then had two people who are not eating low-carb to control test them for me to make sure they do not just turn pink for everyone. The sticks passed those tests with flying colors. Or rather no color change at all, as should be the case.

A week or so later I had a few too many carbs at a banquet, and the next day the sticks showed I left ketosis briefly then gradually showed more ketones over the course of the day. I am impressed by how responsive they seem to be.

I feel great and, for whatever reason, I feel the sticks really help encourage me to stick to my low-carb lifestyle more than the fact that I feel so much better when I eat this way. The day after that banquet I returned to my pre-diet gastro issues and lethargy. You'd think that would be enough to keep me eating like this but it just isn't. That is bizarre to me, but it is true. You'd think one's own health and feeling great and lsoing about two pounds per week would be enough inspiration but, for me at least, making a little stick turn pink is just this tiny little win that keeps me on track.

What's really great is that these are inexpensive enough that I can use one several times a day without feeling frivolous.

title: You need to really Like Peppermint to Like these
text:
I have ordered and tried several different flavors of Tummydrops; they have these Sweet Lychee and a few other flavors on the Peppermint side and they have a variety of flavors on the Ginger side. I do not prefer the different flavored Tummydrops that are peppermint flavored. However, The Sweet Lychee Peppermint is the sweetest (and best tasting) peppermint flavored Tummydrop and the Lychee fruit helps to cut the strong peppermint flavor. So if you really like peppermint, then these are very palatable and I advise getting them for morning or car sickness and to help with GI Issues. There is no aftertaste, your teeth don't feel sticky and it does not effect your breath in any negative way. If you want a super strong peppermint flavor that is not so sweet, the Fresh Crushed Peppermint is the right Tummydrop for you. You can't go wrong with Tummydrops being Gluten free, Nut free, Vegan, Organic, Kosher and Non-GMO! Plus the company is so wonderful to work with. I had trouble using their coupon and they emailed me back with-in a few hours and fixed the error. This company wants to make sure you are satisfied and happy. If you don't end up liking them, let them now and they will fix it.

The only pitfall to Tummydrops is they are expensive, so waiting for a coupon or signing up for the company newsletter is the best way to go to get a deal on them. Tummydrops come 33 to a bag and they recommend taking up to 12 a day..that means if you took the max dose you are getting almost 3 days worth and the cost of them starts to add up. They are about 18 in a tin; so the tins that come in 3 packs will last 4 1/2 days if your taking the recommended up to 12 a day but the tins are more expensive than the bags by about $4.

Tummydrops also has Ginger flavored Tummydrops. The Ginger Tummydrops are much, much better in my opinion. The Ginger ones do actually help with GI Issues, help regulate your bowel movements and are delicious to suck on. All the Tummydrops have only 4 ingredients and I can feel the difference in my digestive system when I suck on them throughout the day. I highly recommend the Pineapple Ginger, Sweet Ginger Pear, Double Ginger Peach and Sweet Blackberry Ginger.

I use lens wipes on my glasses every day. Lens wipes usually come in two extremes; really moist, or really dry. Too moist and the often leave spots or streaks. Too dry and they don't clean oily smudges but rather smear it around. Where these wipe "sets" stand out is that it's basically a two stage cleaning system. It plays through any standard stereo (3-conductor) 3.5mm earphones or headset, though "in-ear" earphones are best. Avoid "Open Air" headphones since the sound coming out of them will cause feedback. Also, very high sensitivity (greater than 100db) earphones work best since the amplification is not tremendous. The user's own voice gets amplified, so you have to get used to that. They're much better than "cheapies". It does have a "tone control" that can boost either high or low frequencies. But I find the limited total frequency range of the device limits the usefulness of this feature. It has another jack on the front that allows you to directly connect the stereo RCA jacks on the back of a TV to this device with the included long cable. I received this support vest this past Saturday. It was packaged very nicely and was preceded by an email from the vendor. When I opened the package containing the vest, I was overwhelmed by the smell of rubber-like chemical smell. The smell was so strong that it lit up the entire room. I immediately removed it from the house and placed it on an hanger in the garage in an attempt to let it air out. I checked on it Sunday, Monday and Tuesday and it still had a strong smell although less than when I first received it. I tried it on and adjusted the straps as instructed. As some of the previous reviewers indicate, the strap material going under the arm is very uncomfortable (on top of a long sleeved shirt) even when you loosen the straps. This could have been avoided if the manufacturer had lengthened the vest material enough to go under your arms as it is less abrasive.
The buckle used for the strap adjustments is also an issue as it presses up against my side.

As for the magnets, I feel nothing, and wouldn't have noticed that they are there had I not read reviews concerning whether or not they are authentic. I have not tested them.

Today is Wednesday, I decided to wear the vest while working. Again the smell is still very strong and actually gave me a headache and upset my stomach after wearing it at my desk forcing me to open my office door. The shirt I wore yesterday wreaks f the rubber chemical smell. the straps are very uncomfortable no matter how much I adjust it. Overall, the vest does provide decent support, but tends to ride up when you are wearing it. The magnets have no affect whatsoever.

I will give it until Saturday to see if the smell dissipates before I return it. It appears that this was a decent design concept at the start, but a failure upon execution due to the poor materials used. I will update on Saturday to let others know whether or not after 7 days the chemical smell has dissipated. I'm unsure why it has such a smell as I have purchased many items that use neoprene and not one including several support belts had this smell when I received them. The fact that it gave me a headache and upset my stomach gives me pause as to whether or not it is safe to wear. (short of sending it over to EPA or FDA to safety evaluation)

title: A couple of tips...
text:
I opted to buy my ReMag off of the actual product website because I received a % off coupon for signing up for the emails. So even though this isn't a verified purchase through Amazon, I have indeed purchased and used this product. Here's my review of it-
I've been taking magnesium glycinate for about a year now to control heart palpitations (menopause related, Dr. says they're normal). I was out of town at a friends house and my heart started fluttering because I had forgotten my mag that morning. She gave me a 1/2 tsp of ReMag and they were gone in 20 minutes. She also gave me the book to read that Carolyn Dean wrote called 'The Magnesium Miracle' and it really opened my eyes to how deficient we really are in magnesium. I'm not gonna lie, this stuff tastes completely horrible. Do NOT try to do a shot of it, found that one out the hard way. I found that if you put a 1/2 tsp in (at least) 24oz of water, it's extremely palatable and easy to drink, plus you're getting a good chunk of your daily water intake out of the way. This product seems expensive compared to the other mags that you can buy, but you're getting a 3 months supply in the 8oz bottle which breaks it down to approximately $10 per month. You're going to pay this for a month of magnesium that isn't as bio-available, so you might as well pay it for a quality product. If you go to the ReMag website and sign up for the emails you can save 15% off the cost, plus you get emails with discount codes for future purchases. Hope this helps!

As much as I'm wearing it I'll probably wear it out faster than expected so I'm thinking about ordering a second one to have on hand, just in case. Anyway, depending on whichever brand is the best cost wise at purchase time, I have no problem switching between these and the other brand. title: These really work!
text:
I have been using these for several months (and through the hottest summer I can remember). You can actually wear shoes with no socks and these are quite good at keeping odor and wetness away.

I ordered from their website and put them in a pair of well-worn, slighty-stinky shoes. You wipe out the inside of the shoe with a wet cloth to help the rubber backing stick. After the first day, the old odor was gone from the shoes--I was delighted. I put them in all my closed new shoes now, and they keep the insides looking nice and new.

i have not tried them in sandals or clogs (because the clogs have cloth footbeds that the rubber can't stick to). I have also not tried them with socks or stockings--mainly because that would defeat the purpose of using them. But I can say that they keep bare feet dry and odor free in closed shoes with non-porous insoles.

After a while, they do sort of wad up while you are wearing them, but I have noticed that this is about the time they are ready to be changed, so that may just be that they are past effectiveness and my feet are getting sweatier.

I am so happy to see them on Amazon Prime now!

title: Works well as long as you watch for food interactions
text: This product works fine, but you need to be careful not to eat certain foods while using it. If you don't completely avoid cheese, red wine, coffee, avocados and all soft drinks (diet or regular), and refined carbs and sugars, you will have side effects. Those side effects can become serious, so do your homework. In my opinion the suggested dosage is too high. You need to start with one capsule only, in the morning. Taking it without food and lots of water is better as to avoid interactions, but if you watch what you eat, you won't feel any side effects like jitter, accelerated heart beat, chills, etc... Even throughout the day, you have to watch what you eat, because yohimbe will stay in your system for many hours. Slowly increase the dosage if you want, to test your tolerance, but I would recommend avoiding taking this any time after 1pm if you want to be able to fall asleep at night. The benefits of this product outweigh the risks **IF** and only **IF** you know how to use it, and that means watching closely what you eat, and starting with ONE capsule per day only. If you find yourself shaking too much, cold sweating and jittery, for sure you took too high of a dosage and/or you've eaten foods that interact with yohimbe. Be careful, and you'll be able to enjoy the benefits.

title: Needs two cleaning vials, only includes one, plus other cons
text:
I have been wearing soft contacts since 1975.

PROS:
Disinfects but with a lot of PITAs and potential high risks to my eyes.

CONS:
1. Since this solution is highly dangerous to put directly in the eye, the neutralizing tab at the bottom of the cleaning vial is necessary to neutralize the solution over a stated 6hr period. If this tablet doesn't work for some reason, even if you rinse your contacts after the period with saline, they will still burn your eyes (just read the dozens of 1-star reviews). The tablet's neutralizing effect wanes with each use, so that Alcon states you MUST use a FRESH VIAL with EACH NEW BOTTLE of solution. Yet Alcon saw fit to provide two bottles of solution in this two-pack, BUT ONLY ONE CLEANING VIAL. This means in order to use both bottles of solution you will have to buy another Clear Care package just to get the vial... which means the new bottle with the new package will be useless without buying yet another package... Supplying only one vial potentially puts people's eyes at serious risk, as some people will reasonably assume the single included vial must be made to use with both bottles, or they would have included a second one. No, it won't work with both bottles, and yes you should have gotten a second one.

That alone is worth one star as Alcon is supposed to be dedicated to eye care, but this decision to include only one vial to save a few pennies on each package, says all I personally need to know about Alcon's ethos. They know some people will assume the single vial will work for both bottles, while they can point to the fact that they clearly state in the directions that a new vial is needed for each new bottle. Yet, it's not included. Making the second bottle useless - or what Alcon hopes, an impetus to buy a new package to get a second vial... making the new bottle useless... and so it goes.

2. The very important directions for this product that can be so potentially dangerous to your eyes if not exactly followed, are printed on the inside of the box, rather than supplied on a leaflet, making it more difficult to get to them. Some people won't cut the box open but will just try to read the tiny writing by peering inside. The more dangerous a product can be, the EASIER it should be to read vital directions. I took the box apart and copied it, then glued/taped it back together as I wanted it to store the bottles in it. PITA.

3. I did not read the 1-star reviews before ordered it (something I always do in every other case) but because this product had so many sales and a solid 5-star rating, I didn't. While waiting for it to arrive, I came back and read those reviews. I recommend anyone considering this product read those reviews.

While some people simply didn't read the directions and thought they were buying contact solution (user error), MANY others found that the neutralizing tab simply didn't work, even after an excess of 6hrs, and ended up with chemical burns to the eye. A good portion of these people were *fans* of this product, having used it and loved it for some time, and so contacted Alcon to report a potential bad batch of neutralizing tabs. None of these people (that I read here) sounded satisfied with Alcon's response, and you can see by the dates of the 1-star reviews *that had this problem* it was sporadically reported over a period of **a few years** which indicates no apparent recall of the bad lots, or attempt to rectify the problem. Instead Alcon *appears* to have let these bad lots sell through, **if the continued reports are any indication**. That is another CON because I had no assurance that the package I would receive would neutralize the solution. I HOPED it would, but I couldn't be sure, given the reports and the *apparent* lack of action on Alcon's part. In fact I considered just throwing it away.

4. While the bottles of solution have an expiry date printed on them, according to the directions, once a bottle is opened it must be discarded after 3 months, regardless of the expiry date. Wasteful. I taped a sticky to the bottle with the date I opened it. Another PITA.

5. You have to do a lot of rinsing of the parts with the bottle of solution (rinse the case, rinse the contacts when you put them in the vial's carousel before inserting it in the vial to soak). A lot of waste. The directions do say you can use plain saline for this instead, so I bought two bottles of that as I use multipurpose solution and it stated to use plain saline. I didn't know if that was necessary but was another inconvenience.

6. During the cleaning process the solution foamed out the top of the vial (there is a tiny hole to release air from all the bubbling action). So put the vial on a folded paper towel or paper plate, or make sure it's not a surface that could be damaged. Yet another PITA. And on the second try, although I snugged down the cap it wasn't snugged ALL the way down, so 3/4 of the solution foamed out leaving the contacts above the solution - if I hadn't happened to walk thru the bathroom and check it, they would have dried out and been ruined. So when the cap feels snug, apply a little more strength and turn it more until it won't turn anymore. (i.e. apply more pressure than you usually would with plastic parts)

The package I got did indeed neutralize the solution - though I left mine to soak 12hrs – twice the stated time needed to neutralize it - and thoroughly rinsed the lenses in saline before I inserted them. I do feel it cleaned them some, but not in such a fantastic way that I'm sold. In fact I will never buy this again.

If the package came with two vials I would have given it 3 stars, as in my case, it at least neutralized the solution. But the cleaning was nothing special.

After reading more about cleaning regimens, I will be instead buying a daily cleaner and then enzymatic tablets to prolong the use of hydrophilic (soft) lenses. I never bothered in all the decades I've worn contacts, but they've gotten so expensive now, I don't mind going to a little extra work to extend their life. This is a safer way to go imho. No worries of neutralizer tablets working, or no longer working because they've been depleted and there's no way of knowing (such as the tablet changing color to notify me), until I insert them in my eyes and see if they burn or not. I can't see going that route when safer alternatives exist. My eyes are too important to risk chemical burns because a neutralizing tablet became depleted or was faulty to begin with.

All my personal opinion, FWIW.

I've got very sensitive feet, especially my right one where I've got a bunion below my big toe that came from standing on concrete floors in heels when I was teaching, dumb I know, but I looked good :) The first few times I used the Orion, it was very painful, and my feet were actually sore afterwards.  It's under my computer desk where I come in the mornings to check on Amazon, Facebook, etc., and I figured a good foot massage would get my day going. Some mornings I've dreaded sticking my feet into the thing, but I persevered, and now it's beginning to feel good. When I walk, I can tell my feet are more flexible. I actually hadn't noticed the stiffness till it began to dissipate. I do two short sessions each morning. If I could change anything, the remote would operate a bit farther away from the machine, but it's not a big deal. The remote is tiny and doesn't take up much space beside my computer.  The kneading machine seems solidly built, and I hope it lasts for a long time. I would recommend it if you're willing to work you way into a good foot massage. Sometimes it feels almost sensual and makes me wish I had a human friend who could massage feet that well. I guess a robotic friend is better than none!

title: The Best Dishwasher Pods I've Used
text: These dishwasher pods are incredible and this is coming from someone who's used to using the generic budget pods. My normal pods always did the job for the most part but they would sometimes miss a couple food spots that I also missed during my pre rinse and they didn't always feel fully clean, but with these, all of those problems have gone away. I still tend to rinse my dishes off the best I can before I put them in the dishwasher, but I did test these with a few slightly dirtier dishes to see if their "no pre rinse needed" claims hold up. Spoiler alert, they do. The dishes that were dirtier weren't as dirty as in their advertisement but there were a few with some spaghetti sauce stains and some that had grease residue. These pods made all of those dishes not only completely spotless, but they also had a fresh scent smell to them and they felt incredibly clean. My dishes and silverware looked almost brand new and were shinier than I've ever seen. Overall, these are incredible dishwasher pods that will work for everyone. I don't live in an area that typically has issues with hard water, but these pods were great with the water supply that I have. I highly recommend these as they are miles better than the budget pods I've been using for years.
