title: Works good but a little uncomfortable.
text:
It took me years to figure out why I don't sleep well. What have found, was my sinuses were the root of the problem of poor sleep. If you can breath through you nose well, you will sleep well. For the past decade, my sinuses have been giving me issues and are sensitive to pollen, dry heated air in the winter, and smoggy air. When they get blocked which makes it difficult to breathe through and in turn I get poor sleep. I have been using a NeilMed sinus flush for past few years and it is very helpful, but doesn't solve all the problems. Decongestants, steroids, and antihistamines don't seem to help me much.

The Silent Angel nasal dilator seems pretty good. They are a little uncomfortable at first but do indeed help open up your nasal passages. I have been getting better sleep which is really nice. Before, I would toss and turn while sleeping and wake up with a really dry mouth because I was breathing through it. Now, sleeping through the night and only breathing through my nose while sleeping which is excellent. I still might try a few other types to see if are some that are more comfortable. There was some small tabs that are supposed to hold them in, but I cut them off because it made them more uncomfortable. It comes in four different sizes which is good to find what best works for you.

title: Great brushes for the price - Very durable and portable
text:
I'd like to state up front that I did receive this item for review purposes from the manufacturer. I was not required nor given incentive to provide a 5-star review - The manufacturer was releasing this new product and needed critical, honest feedback for potential shoppers on Amazon. This review is written as if I have paid full retail price for the item myself.

That being said, I'm very happy with the quality of this brush set and it is fully deserving of a 5-star review! While this item is relatively inexpensive and simple, I still think it is better than the competition. I gave this set to my wife and she's very happy with it. Here are some key points that she loves:

EXCELLENT FOR TRAVEL
This product was really designed with portability and travel in mind. All of the brushes stow away into a container hardly bigger than a tampon, and are extremely easy to carry around with your makeup or travel bag. My wife even tosses it into her gym bag for in between the gym and going to work.

BUILD QUALITY
These items are built with excellent quality. The brushes are thick and durable, and the container is heavy-duty for the price. It feels like these brushes will hold up far longer than the competing products we have tried, which remind me of some 'Fisher Price' paint brushes or something that will likely snap and already flex a lot.

Overall I'm very happy with this item. My wife has already referred two of her friends to grab these for their makeup collections - She's happy with and swears by it!

text:
This stuff is awesome. It's got both sunscreen, moisturizer, and insect repellent all in one. I love having it all together. I keep a bottle in my "go bag" to be ready for any emergency. I also used it to repel mosquitoes in a lightly wooded area on Independence Day. No one got bit. I don't trust most insect repellents with my daughter's skin. When I hang out outside at night, I use Deep Woods Off. I find that product burns my skin. I would NEVER put it on my toddler. I definitely recommend this product for all moms of little kids.

title: Love this cupping set! I get a nice clean feeling without disturbing my lash extensions.
text: If you haven't done cupping before, I suggest testing these out on your thigh, or arm- or anywhere other than your face. It takes a little practice to get the movements down. You want the area to be lubricated, and start moving the cup around as soon as you have suction. I cannot use oil on my face, because I break out from it, so I use bliss lash and lid wash. Just water works too, but the bliss product makes the cups glide a lot easier. I get lash extensions, so I always have to be careful washing as to not disturb my lashes (they are expensive, so I take care of them!). That is one reason I really like this set; I can control the area I'm exfoliating and cleaning and not disturb my lashes. Once you get the hang of it.. you might get hooked! I really like how my face feels after cupping. I haven't been doing it that long, so I will probably update my review after a month, but so far I'm happy with the results. Having sensitive skin and lash extensions doesn't give me a lot of options for face treatments- so far this one is a keeper. One more "tip".. you can also use these on your lips to plump them up a little. That might not work for everyone, but my lips are the right size to use the larger cup to plump them a little.

title: A quick fix for my back pain.
text:
My employer has provided my department with some very poorly constructed office chairs. My chair was causing me pain in my lower back and one of my shoulders. I inquired about getting a different chair, but I’m facing a gauntlet of bureaucracy to get this done. I was told I could bring in my own chair, but I don’t have the funds for this at the moment., Buying the Purple cushion was the quick solution. I may still buy a chair in the future, but now I can hold off for a while.

As for the Purple cushion, for what it is and what I’m using it for is helping my pain substantially. Purple appears to have 4 different options for seat cushions. They have one with 3 different thicknesses all the way to 4 inches, much like their mattresses. Then there’s this one… the main difference I see with the “Royal Purple” are the rounded edges on the cushion. Based on this and the 2 inch thickness, I opted for the Royal. I wanted something thicker than their cheapest offering, but not so thick that it would interfere with the feel of the chair and hight of the armrests.

After trying this cushion in a few locations other than my office chair, I can say that it feels/works best on hard surfaces. Putting a cushion on top of another cushion feels….. odd….. like it’s not suppose to be there… to put it simply. You might say if feels slightly unstable in a way. But I’ll take the awkwardness over back pain. I do wish the cushion was about 2 inches wider in both length and width. This would fit me and my chair a bit better and lessen the awkward/unstable feel.

Purple needs to collaborate with one of the higher end office chair manufactures like Herman Miller, HON, Steelcase, etc and come out with a purpose built Purple office chair. Tempur-Pedicure did this once, and sadly, I can’t find this chair any more. Point being,… if they did this, we could have something that felt much more natural than a cushion on top of another cushion solution.

title: Not Even Full Daily Value for Most Ingredients
text:
Zinc and Vitamin D3 are very useful supplements for general health and a healthy immune system. These pills are easy to swallow and contain a good variety of essential vitamins and minerals beyond those two.

However, I have these concerns:

- The serving sizes doesn't contain even a full "daily value" of any ingredient except B6 and D3. But even D3 is "only" at 100% when you will find most supplements containing D3 at a much higher value. At the price of these supplements there's no reason to skimp.

- Unless I am missing it somewhere in the super small print, I cannot find where these are made. I can find the name of the importer, but not where they were made. There are enough hints on the bottle that it is China, but I can't be sure. It's troubling that this is not stated clearly. There's also a lack of the GMP seal and that's a bit troubling too given that nearly every supplement maker goes through the trouble of being able to make that claim.

Bottom line is I think there are probably better sources for these important vitamins and minerals.

title: Vitamin D is Important!
text: Vitamin D is made naturally by the body in the presence of bright sunlight, so if you don't get a lot of sun exposure then you may be vitamin D deficient (your doctor can test for this). Supplements are a great way to avoid that problem, and this supplement is easy to take and provides the upper limit for recommended supplementation in healthy people. This supplement is easy to swallow and has no significant taste. It's a pretty good value too at $10 for a 120 day supply.

title: It's Nice, but not $35 Nice
text:
First, I think this would make an excellent gift for anyone on your list who sleeps. Research shows that even small amounts of light in a room while sleeping can trick your brain into unhealthy sleep patterns and restless nights. And with every electronic gizmo in the world these days emitting some kind of light, a "dark room" can end up being not that dark (I am talking to you Alexa-with-a-display). For that reason I sleep with an eye mask to make sure that all my peepers see is... nothing.

As a gift the presentation of this silk eye mask is nice. It definitely comes through as a luxury gift in a fancy box.

But I can't imagine spending $35 on this for myself. It's no softer than the polyester eye mask it is replacing.

I did notice that my head size resulted in needing to extend the adjustable strap almost to its limit. I don't think my head is that large, really, so this may not fit a very large person.

If you have money you don't need, I think you'll find this eye mask is an excellent way to lighten some of that load.

title: Simple device sold as an expensive product.
text:
Got this device issued to me for a broken metatarsal and it seems to be working...but....it another reason why there should be caps on how much medical devices cost. I am an electronics technician and when I first saw this device I couldn’t believe the cost. The parts to construct a low powered electromagnet are not that expensive. At the most without the fancy plastic casing I could make one in my garage for under $100. Wire for the electromagnet coil, power (9v), few components to limit voltage and a timer chip to pulse the input power. Why is this thing $3k to $5k? The 30 min/day limitation is stupid. I received many many more times electromagnetic radiation in 60 secs working on high powered radars than you would if you used all 270 days of this thing.

TIP: I did find out that if the 9v battery is removed from the compartment during a session then that session is not counted. You can pull the battery out at 29 min and 30 secs and it will allow you to start the session over again.

title: Compact and effective trimmer for facial hair
text:
I use this kit to trim my facial hair - nose hair, ear hair, side burns, and eyebrows. Work great!

WHAT I LIKE:
* Compact -- small enough to travel with if you need to. Takes up minimal space on vanity.
* Rechargable -- much better than battery operated. No need to replace batteries
* Easy to swap attachments -- just a small twist to remove and install
* All attachments do what they need to - eyebrows, side burns, nose hair, ear hair
* Small brush to clean out any hair still on the blades
* Can rinse tip under stream of water without concern of damage (would not submerge it though)

WHAT I DON'T LIKE:
* As typical these days, it does not come with a charging block -- just a USB charging cable
* No travel case or storage tray/case so there is no easy way to organize the attachments on the vanity

SUMMARY:
A nice compact facial hair trimmer at a reasonable price -- currently just under $20 with free Prime shipping.

title: Convenient for travel

I use a water flossing system every night at home rather than flossing since it is easier for me and the dentist claims it is actually better for my gums. When I travel, I use floss since my water floss system is large and bulky and would never make sense to travel with. For this device, its strength is actually that you can travel with the handle and use use the tube to pull water from a cup or container. I am not a big fan of using this at home since it is rather bulky and more difficult to maneuver than my current system where I just hold the small nozzle and the pump is located with the resevoir (which is what makes it non-viable to travel with).

With this new system, I now have a viable travel option for a water flosser as well as a backup for my at-home system if it stops working.

title: Safe and effective option for unplugging heater core
text:
I have seen traditional CLR used effectively to unplug heater cores and save a bundle on a heater core replacement. Also effective on removing rust and corrosion from radiator and cooling system if you are having overheating issues on older, high mileage vehicles. This CLR PRO should be even more effective than the normal CLR and certainly a safer bet than various home-brew flush solutions that could damage your cooling system. I like the fact that it is non toxic and biodegradable, which is pretty surprising given the job that this has to do to break down calcium, lime, and rust (hence, CLR) and remove all that scale and clogging. But the description clearly states "Non Toxic Products: CLR PRO Automotive products are safer alternatives and contain no phosphates, ammonia or bleach; Non toxic and readily biodegradable" which is awesome. The small pint and a half containers are nicer than the large gallon jugs in my opinion since you don't end up with half used jugs around and these smaller containers are easier to store.

For DIYers looking for tips on how to deep flush a heater core with CLR, there are lots of videos online, but I recommend searching on youtube for "sound main auto CLR" for a great short video on a great DIY flush technique that is very effective and uses inexpensive parts rather than expensive professional equipment.

title: Small, but jam packed
text:
This is a well constructed first aid bag that is very small so it is a great option when you are tight for space. It has a belt loop strap on it so you can run your belt loop through it and also has a couple of small loops you can run a cord, hook, or caribiner through to hang it on the outside of your backpack.

In terms of contents, it is very oriented toward bandages of various types so it is really made for treating scrapes and cuts. It has scissors, tweezers, gloves, and antisceptic wipes as well. The most unusual element is a large number of safety pins. They may come in handy, but seem out of place compared to other parts of the kit. There is so much stuff in there that it is a tight fit to get it all back in the case.

I am keeping this in the trunk of my car for emergencies and can take it out with me on a spontaneous hike or climb as well. The compact size makes it a great option when you are really tight on space. Would work great on a bicycle.

title: Soft and comforable
text:
These ear plugs are soft and comfortable and easy to install. Once you get them in to where they seal, they do very well at lowing the sound level. Because they are very soft, they are pretty comfortable. I was a bit concerned about the "handle" on the blue ones that I thought my be a problem when sleeping on my side, but it was not an issue (at least for me) since the handle sits completely in my ear (kind of angled downward toward my earlobe). I like the individual cases for easy transport, storage, and reuse. I think these would work well on for travel (both on a plane as well as in a noisy hotel room). The one pair of black ear plugs work similarly well and are also very soft -- the handle on these is different, so they may work better (or worse) than the blue ones for some folks depending on their ear size and form. The one drawback with the black ones is that they don't have a plastic storage case like the blue ones.

It would be better if they came with some instructions and guidance, but I was able to figure out how to insert them and get them to seal. When dealing with your ears, it is always best to have guidance and instructions though.

Price of around $16 (currently) with free Prime delivery seems reasonable at $4 per pair.

title: like the mesh material & 3 color options
text:
This is a pretty nice set of heel cushions. I like the mesh material better than the leather material I have used in the past -- they are softer and more breathable and I think it makes them more comfortable (hopefully, they are as durable over time). The grey, black, and beige color options allow you to match your shoes so they don't stand out as much. These are generally useful if you get abrasion on the back of your heal and need extra protection/cushioning OR if your shoes/bookts are a bit large and your heal slips up every time you raise your foot.

The key with these is to place them properly and to get it "right on the first attempt". If you get them in there wrong and have to pull them off and retry, you will lose the adhesion and they will not stay on as well over time. I recommend testing out the placement without removing the backing to make sure you have them where you want them. Then remove the backing and fold in half, get the center aligned, and then push out the sides and press into place -- hopefully, you get it perfect on the first attempt.

My only concern with these is the lack of directions and lack of English description on the product. I recommend that the marketing company update the product packaging to include full English directions for the US market.

title: Convenient and effective shaving
text:
This little cordless electric shaver works well on legs and underarms. The double edge razor works best for initial shave pass and then the foil head can be used for remaining short stubble as necessary. Both heads worked smoothly with no signs of nicks, abrasion, or irritation. The heads can be exposed to water and shave cream, but we prefer to keep the body of the shaver as dry as possible (despite the claimed IPX7 waterproof rating). If used in the shower, I would dry the body off quickly when I was done.

In terms of charging, it holds the charge plenty long for a shave and charges fully in under 2 hours. It uses a USB charging cable (included) -- and I wish it came with a wall charger, but no such luck (you have to provide your own USB power source).

The storage/carry bag is a convenient way to keep the kit together.

It is not clear what the guide combs are used for -- looks like beard grooming attachments used by men. They seem kind of useless for a women's razor (perhaps to loan to her husband if he forgot his razor on a trip?). Weird.

Overall, this is a nifty women's electric shaver that is effective and convenient.

title: Nicer than other gel heel protectors we have tried
text:
These are a significant step up from some other gel heel protectors we have used in the past. My wife has a condition with her heel that can flare up from time to time and cause significant pain for weeks on end. When this happens, she really benefits from gel heel inserts to allow her to go about her business and still recover.

WHAT WE LIKE ABOUT THESE INSERTS:
* The deep cup with the gel coming up around the back of the heal for about 1/2 inch of back heel protection is really nice. Some others just provide the gel on the bottom of the heal. This one stabilizes the heal a bit with the cup and also provides some protection on the back and sides.
* A wave pattern on the inside where your heal rests provides extra grip and slip-resistance
* Around 1/4 inch of bottom silicone gel is about right to provide the protection and comfort she needs without creating excessive instability or raising the heel too much.
* The gel is sticky and stays in place in the shoe without need for adhesive (allowing you to easily move them from one pair of shoes to another)

AREA FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* We struggled a bit to pick the right size since there was not real guidance on how S, M, L matched to shoe sizes. There were dimensions on width, but that doesn't help most people. In the end, we got the M and it worked well for her size 8 feet. Would appreciate some extra guidance on the product page on sizing (referencing men and women shoe size ranges)

These are a bit more expensive than other options we have used -- but in our case, it is certainly worth it to get the extra features mentioned above. Particularly given how useful these are when my wife has a flare up.

SUMMARY:
A great set of silicone gel heel protectors for anyone suffering from heel pain.

title: Works great on face, nose, ears, and hairline
text:
This is a flexible device that works great at several occasional tasks...
* I use it to trim my beard down if I have let it go too long. It helps my foil razor shave better to pre-trim with this trimmer if I go a week or more without a shave. Then my foil razor will do the rest.
* Nose hair trimmer is quick and effective. Just move it around in your nose and any stragglers are clipped off in a few seconds.
* Ear hair trimming is also quick and effective with the same attachment. Just run it over any emerging ear hair you see and it will disappear quick and easy.
* I also use it occasionally between haircuts to trim the hair on the back of my neck and re-establish a clean hair line until my next haircut.

It is small enough to leave around on your bathroom counter so that it is available if you notice a straggling nose or ear hair that needs to be addressed.

It is very easy to swap out the attachments.

It is easy to clean with the cleaning brush or running the attachment under the water -- I don't let the main unit get wet even though it claims some level of water resistance.

Operation is super easy with just a simple on/off switch -- no complicated controls or speeds to fuss over.

Charging is easy and the charge lasts plenty long -- wish they provided a USB wall charger so I didn't have to provide my own USB power source.

title: Effective replacement insoles
text:
I use these as normal replacement insoles, not to address any particular foot issues. I found that they do conform somewhat to your foot as advertised -- it can take a couple of weeks. Overall, I like them and consider them a nice upgrade from my OEM insoles (that were getting a bit worn).

A few things to note:
* You need to allow a couple of weeks for these to conform to your foot
* I found these to be thinner than other insoles I have tried, especially in the toe area where they are quite thin. They are similar in thickness to factory OEM insoles that come in your shoes.
* They don't have the very aggressive arch support that you get with many insoles on the market, so if you are looking for extra arch support or any other "corrective" features, these may not be the best choice
* They seem a bit pricey (currently shown for ~$70) for replacement insoles. They do have the nice feature of adapting somewhat to your feet, but I am not sure I would pay that much extra for this feature.

SUMMARY:
A nice set of replacement insoles that adapt to your feet, but a bit on the pricey side -- perhaps the price will come down a bit.

title: Great for ingrown toenails
text:
This is a nice quality toenail trimmer that is well suited for trimming ingrown toenails.

WHAT IS GOOD:
* Nice wooden handle
* Nice case that is custom fit for the clippers
* Comes with blade protector to avoid damage and provide safety
* Good spring action -- opens easily
* Good quality steel
* Easy lock mechanism to lock closed for storage

WHAT IS EXTRA GOOD:
* Sharp blade makes cutting easy and precise
* The narrow blade makes it easy to get into tight places when trimming a jagged edge on an ingrown toenail. You don't want bulky trimmers when you are trying to do precision cutting in a tight area. This is the most unique and useful aspect of this particular set of clippers.

title: Helpful in the right shoes when applied properly
text:
I initially tried putting these in an older pair of athletic shoes in which the rear heel padding area had been torn up a bit and I needed some additional padding. I had a couple of problems with it. First, because of the torn material, the pad did not stick well or hold in place. I don't feel that these are great for shoes that have a material for the back of the heel area since it can't really stick well to that material. The second problem I had was that when I first put it in, I put didn't get it in perfectly straight and at the proper level. The problem is that you really only get one shot at that since you really can't move it after it sticks (or it will lose its "stickiness"). So my second lesson I learned was to to make sure you get it right where you want it on the first attempt.

I then tried them on some boots that are slightly oversized and in which my heel slides up when I walk. They work very will in this case. There was a clean and firm area in the back of the boot to which to attach. I kind of test fitted them prior to removing the backing and then after removing the backing, I folded them in half, got them in position, and then applied them carefully and pushed them on firmly. So far they are working well. I am a little concerned whether I will push them off when I insert my foot into the boot over time. I will have to wait and see on that.

SUMMARY:
They work well on the right type of shoe or boot, but make sure you get them right where you want them on the first attempt since any attempt to adjust their position will reduce their ability to stick well.

title: Easy saline nasal irrigation system!
text:
I did alot of lawn work today which got my allergies worked up a bit so I decided to try out the nasal irrigation. I had not done this before, so I wasn't sure what to expect -- kind of figured it would be a bit painful or burn as the saline went through my nose -- but it wasn't at all the case. It was very easy and painless. I emptied one of the saline packets in the bottle and filled it to the 300 ml mark with warm/hot water and tested the water temp with the term gauge/strip and it was right in the middle of the "green" (for good). I leaned my head forward a bit over the sink, put the plug in my right nostril, tilted my head down to the left (so my left nostril was below my right), and pushed the release button the bottle. I watched as water poured out of my left nostril and barely felt anything (just kind of smelled the salt water). After a few seconds when I thought the bottle was about half empty, I switched sides and watched the water pour out of my right nostril. The bottle never completely emptied -- I think that it may stop when there is not enough water pressure to keep forcing it through your nasal passage, so I ended up pouring the last ounce or two out after the treatment. I did keep my mouth open and reminded myself to breath the entire time as instructed. Easy peasy. After the treatment, my sinuses feel free and clean.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Effective and thorough irrigation of sinuses with no pain or discomfort
* Release button on bottle lets gravity release the water at the proper rate (rather than squeezing a bottle and getting to much pressure)
* Good directions
* 2 adult nozzle tips in different colors so my wife and I can each have our own tip
* 1 child nozzle tip
* 30 saline packets for 30 treatments

SUMMARY:
Looking forward to using this during allergy season to keep my nasal passage clear of pollen after spending time outside.

title: Comfortable and mold to your feet - BEWARE OF TYPO IN SIZING!!!
text:
I used these to replace the OEM insoles in my well-worn ASICS that I use for my daily walking. I ended up with the L (large size) of the "Everyday Narrow" style and they were a perfect fit for my size 12 ASICS -- amazingly no trimming was required. I overlaid these insoles over the factory insoles and there were a perfect fit so I put the scissors away (typically, some level of trimming would be required).

They provided much improved cushioning in the heal and toe as well as arch support immediately. However, on the first couple of walks, I noticed that my leg muscles were feeling some strain after a long walk. As I continued to wear them, they formed to my feet and the leg pain went away. After a couple of weeks now, I find them very comfortable and am quite happy with how they have adjusted to my feet.

BEWARE OF SIZING:
On the webpage where you pick the size, I selected "Mens size 11-12.5, Womens size 10-11.5" and they sent me a size "L". Now you will notice that the advertised size range is clearly in error since a Mens 11 is not a Womens 10 -- they should be the other way around. So the L that I was sent were actually "Mens size 10-11.5, Womens size 11-12.5". That is why I did not need to cut the insoles to fit in my size 12 ASICS. So when you are picking your size, you need to mentally swap the words "Men" and "Women" since they have a typo in the selection (unless they read this and fix it as they should). You can see this clearly by looking at the sizing chart which shows an L is Women 11-12.5, Men 10-11.5 (which is correct). I got lucky that I was able to use the smaller L size (10-11.5) vs the XL size (12-13.5) I would have ordered because my shoes are right on the boundary. MAKE SURE YOU USE THE SIZE CHART OR SWAP MEN/WOMEN SIZES WHICH ARE INCORRECTLY LISTED!!!!!

Hopefully, they quickly fix the typo in the sizing info since as it currently is, most people will order the wrong size for either men on women (unless they happen to notice that the men and women size ranges don't make sense and realize the typo).

title: Amazing for shaping and polishing natural nails
text:
These glass nail files (with very fine etching or embedded particles) are pretty amazing! They make super quick work of shaping your nails and then you can use the same file to buff and polish the tops as well and they come out very polished and shiny -- look great and you can do each nail (shape and polish) in a hot second!

They only have the file on one side and the end is also smooth for you to hold onto.

They are washable and come in a nice container for storage. Because they are so small, it is easy to take them in your pocket, purse, glove box, whatever -- they take up no space.

They seem pretty robust so I expect them to last a long time -- much longer than a traditional nail file.

The only tricky part is that you have to get used to using a file with no bend or give to it since these are a hard surface. If you are used to an emery board, you will have to learn to follow the curve more explicitly since this file will not bend or follow contours for you.

They are SO good!! All I can say is that regular paper towels are trash in comparison to these. These are SO absorbant. Yesterday I knocked an entire mug of tea off my coffee table and right onto my rug. One of these picked up 80% of my 12-16 ounce mug. I would have had to use a million regular paper towels. I'd say these have about the absorbency of shop towels, so really awesome. After the spill, I just rinsed the towel under cold water with some dish soap and it was good as new. I've been using them for all sorts of things and apparently, you can even throw them in the wash!

title: The Best Deal if You Try This Hack
text: At first I was tempted to give a lower rating because the cotton wicks are much smaller than with other inhalers I have purchased. That might explain why they are less expensive. Because they are short (and thinner) the cotton wicks slide down to the bottom, farther away from your nose, when you go to sniff from them. This results in a less concentrated aroma for the amount of oil that you put on the wick. However, after I figured out a little trick these work EVEN BETTER than the ones with the bigger wicks. What I do is add the oil directly to one tip of the wick - this end gets inserted first. At the other end, I put a bend in it so that the entire wick holds more securely inside the tube. I use a pen to push the wick as far down into the tube as possible. This results in having the oil closer to the opening of the tube and a stronger smell. I do not believe this trick would work with the thicker wicks.

title: My feet are usually nice and soft but for some reason after this past ...
text:
This product is interesting. My feet are usually nice and soft but for some reason after this past winter they were pretty rough/cracked. I needed something more than just moisturizer but really hate filing my feet so decided to try this.

The booties it came with are disposable but durable. About 5 minutes after I started my treatment my dog decided he HAD to go outside. Not wanting to clean up an accident I used packing tape (lol) to secure the top of the booties, put a pair of socks and my shoes on over them, and walked my dog around the block. It was a bit awkward but the booties held up without ripping/leaking at all.

For me the peeling started 3 days after I did the treatment. I soaked my feet it warm water like some reviews suggested not expecting much to happen but as soon as I took my feet out they were starting to peel. It took a good 4 - 5 days for them to stop peeling and look normal again so I wouldn't recommend using this if you need to show off your feet anytime a week or so after using the product.

The amount of skin that peeled I'd say was comparable to when you get a sunburn that peels. It did make my feet look/feel softer but didn't completely eliminate a couple of my deeper rough spots/calluses.

All in all I'd say the amount of improvement made this product worth the price although it didn't eliminate all my issues. I'm hoping just keeping my feet moisturized etc will help improve the few remaining rough spots I have, but I would buy this product again in the future.

title: UPDATE: They decrease my pain and help healing!
text:
UPDATE: After 3 months, I’m ordering a 2nd pair, I like them so well!
WHAT ARE BLITZU KNEE BRACES LIKE?:
Blitzu Knee Braces are seamless sleeves of (polyester?) fabric woven around thin elastic bands, the same as in elastic waistbands. The sleeves come in 4 sizes, 2 knitted designs, and 11 colors. Blitzu Knee Braces are comparatively priced and come in pairs. Blitzu Knee Braces are made in China. They do not contain neoprene.
HOW DO YOU USE BLITZU KNEE BRACES?:
I wear these on my runs and if my knee hurts when I return home, I leave the brace on for 24 hours and then wear it during the day until the pain is gone. Also, if I fall or twist my knee, I put the knee brace on for 24 hours and then wear it during the day until the pain is mostly gone. Usually, the brace stays on for about 5-7 days.
HOW DO YOUR BLITZU KNEE BRACES FIT?:
I followed the size chart on the Amazon website and mine fit perfectly. You slide them up over your knee, and mine stay in place by compression and wavy beads of silicone at the top of the sleeve.
HOW DO YOU KNOW IF BLITZU KNEE BRACES FIT?:
They should stay on your knees without sliding down while applying about the same pressure as an elastic bandage wrap. If they slip or clamp too tight, they may be the wrong size.
WHAT DO YOU LIKE ABOUT BLITZU KNEE BRACES?:
1) I have an immediate decrease in existing pain within moments of putting on the brace. Then, the pain resolves after 5-7 days with daily use.
2) Mine have been durable — they lasted months without ravels or loss of stretch.
2) Right now, the price is reasonable and they come as a pair!
WHAT DON’T YOU LIKE ABOUT BLITZU KNEE BRACES?:
When I wear them, they form wrinkles behind my knees. But when I hand wash them in warm water and dry them flat on the bathroom counter, the wrinkles are gone. Official care instructions are under the label.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
I have used compression sleeves off and on since I started having knee trouble at 13 years-of-age and I’m still running. Knee braces help. If you have clinical knee problems, see your M.D.
If my report changes, I’ll let you know by posting an UPDATE on my Amazon Profile.
You’re welcome to read my reviews, check for UPDATES, & follow my profile — just click my name.
I hope this review has been really helpful for you. Enjoy your running and walking!

title: Help for Plantar Psoriasis
text:
I have only had this 1day so I can't speak to its longevity ... but after only 1 use ... my feet feel better than they have for a year. I suffer from severe plantar psoriasis. At times my feet were so cracked and bleeding that walking was difficult. Even when not in a "flare-up" my feet were so ugly it was embarrassing. I bought this machine and the attachment with the cone-shaped thingies. Used it for 10 minutes then put some oil on my feet ... they look & feel almost normal again.
Some reviewers comment that the machine stalls-out if you press too hard. Yes. I think that's a good safety feature. You don't need to press hard. Just be patient and go slow. My feet were horrific yet it only took 10 minutes to get them looking and feeling much better. I like the blue roller. I don't think I would use a coarser one.
The cord is nice and long. I used this outside on my front porch b/c I knew it would be messy - dead skin powder flying around. Gross, I know but the long cord is helpful for that.
I only wish my doctor had told me about this thing instead of going through years of suffering and trying cremes that didn't work, cortisone shots, etc. It isn't a cure for the psoriasis (limited sugar and no bread seems to help) but I'm very happy with this little foot-saver. If you have calluses on the toes and ball of foot, the cone-shaped thingies are a good addition. All the parts were easy to use.

title: It's OK, but going to try something else.
text:
It's OK, but going to try something else. Loved the pump they supply to get the paint in the tubes. Love leaving the big cans of paint in storage and having these little tubes in a nearby drawer for a quick touch up . Like with nail polish, they come complete with a shaker ball inside, so a quick shake and you're ready to touch up. The downfall is the applicator. Its about an inch wide, round, and flat with a hole in the center through which the paint is squeezed. What it really needs a small brush. Squeezing onto a flat foam surface offers pretty poor control of how much paint comes out, and shaped the way it is, forget precision application completely. I found I was expressing paint accidentally as I was trying to position the head better. Was frustrated attempting to feather the edges for good blending with more paint being expressed than i wanted. Forget applying to uneven surfaces like trim moulding or corners. Ended up grabbing a small artist brush and dipping into the paint applicator. I kept thinking, there has got to be something similar to this that has a brush applicator instead...

Update: After searching for the answer I wanted elsewhere, the closest thing I could find was a pen applicator, of which its immediate downfall was its diminutive size (like that of an actual pen) and tiny brush. And worse, you cannot refill it, and it's pricey. Another option was a bottle that looks like an oversize nail polish container, but the brush looks thin and cheap, and I'm guessing I'd get frustrated with the results of such a brush, so I'm sticking with this brand and keeping my artists brush handy.

I had expected this to be significantly more expensive than the large container - and while it is about 40% more expensive, the difference is less than I expected. You pay for the convenience of not having to measure out the portions, and there's also the environmental cost of extra packaging.

Compared to the current price of the ready to drink bottles, this is slightly (less than 10%) more expensive - when comparing calories. Each packet (200 kCal) is similar to half a bottle (400 kCal) of drink.

Overall, convenient, especially for some situations - such as bringing onto a plane, or packing into a hiking bag. But if you're using this on a regular basis, the large container is a better value.

text:
I have no idea why anyone would put the velcro closure for the lining in the back. This might be of use to someone who is not already injured or a child, but I spent 20 minutes of up and down and all over the room trying to get just the lining closed. I ended up getting it as closed as possible, with the rough side of the velcro rubbing against my leg. The compression straps were self explanatory, but then the strap around the top, again going into a loop at the back of the ankle, was hard to get hooked, then just forced the rough Velcro against my ankle again. Because of the back closure, I think struggled to get it off so the velcro would stop tearing at my skin.

My injured ankle now hurts more than it did before I started, and I now have a raw spot on the back of my ankle.

I’ve worn many ankle braces in my life, and the design of this brace makes no sense. It’s difficult to put on because of this awkward design (it really requires two people). My ankle isn’t that big, it may be swollen a bit, but that shouldn’t have prevented a well designed brace from going on it.

title: Solid scooter. I use around obstacles- tire shop
text:
Fantastic little scooter. Sadly I have owned 2 other types of knee scooters from bad motorcycle accidents. Now this is my 3rd. And I love this little scooter.

Pros- scooter is easy to set up. Fantastic little rear shock really nice on bumps and going over air hoses obstacles, nice basket pops off/on easy. zooms straight easy and when you steer too far it really stops/slows down as the tires scrub. This is annoying but I have gone too fast on another brand and i flew off and crashed. So the slow down is like a safety feature. Nice fat grips really helps keep the scooter stable and under control. Rear tire being a single tire is great this way you dont run your leg into it....I have and hurt my foot toes and ankle a lot banging the rear tire/axle nut into it. So this one is nice. No seams knee pad reduces digging into knee. All terrain tire are nice as the cushion the ride. I've had solid tires and they are no fun at all! Good brakes also but 1 tire brake can be weird on low traction situations. Like snow and or ice. Well see what happens in bad weather.
Cons- it's a little front tippy. Balance is a tad scary if lean to far forward. Since the tires have air the whole scooter is a little spongy and jiggly. But this also saves the knee and gives a better overall comfort. Takes getting used to. The knee pad lock isnt working well and it twists and slides down. (I have adjusted it with minimal results) also the tubes that come with it are the wrong stems they should be brass and 90 degree for ease of inflation. The ones on it are really hard to inflate and the little pump included though helpful is hard to work and getting the on the stems between the wheel spokes is no fun at all. Rear brake had to completely reset pad way out of alignment with rim. Also rear rim is in no way true and if you apply brakes you get a jerky slow down. I want to try and use a front wheel to see if it's better to get rid of or at least reduce the jerky operation due to the wheel being out of round. Arrived with scratches on the frames paint. After 30 mins of adjusting and testing. I have now put 25 hours of use on the scooter in 2 days and working very well. 4 stars because of tubes and scrathed paint, jerky brakes, ect.
But overall a solid scooter!!
oh and I'm 170lbs and 6'2" works great!

title: Time to Buy in Bulk!
text:
My 22 month old son leaks during the night without fail. I’ve tried changing him multiple times during the night, sizing up, and different brands of diapers to no avail. One day while browsing Amazon I came across another brand of diaper boosters and decided to give them a try. They definitely held him over longer, but still didn’t quite do the job, so back to searching.
There are a handful of choices and after reading that the Northshore brand holds 12 extra oz of fluid, I bought a pack. Bingo! A dry night finally!! I couldn’t be more pleased with my purchase and will definitely continue to buy this brand to save on a soaking toddler first thing in the morning.
These diaper boosters have a sticky strip on the bottom to adhere to the diaper which I personally like- - no sliding while trying to close the diaper. They also are wide and long enough to cover a good portion of the diaper (size 6). Since I have a son, I place it to where just a tad of the pad is peeking out of the top of his diaper. Also another plus of the adhesive, when you go to take the full diaper off, you don’t have to worry about it slipping and sliding around like other pads and accidentally touching a pad drenched in urine.
If you have a baby/toddler, special needs individual, or have incontinence, I would definitely give these Northshore Disposable pads a try for nighttime protection!

When, many years ago, I purchased my first Norelco shave it came with a notice that it'd take a week or so for the beard to 'adjust' to the new shaver. I thought then that was likely nonsense -- just a way to stop disappointed buyers from returning the shaver when it shaved less well than the ads had promised.

But now about 10 days into the use of this Norelco type shaver I have found it to be shaving much closerr than it did at first. -Especially on the shave resistant (with all shavers) neck hairs.

Did my beard adjust? Or did the shaver need to somehow break in? Whatever the case this low priced rotatry shaver is now doing an excellent job. Five star excellent!

* * * * *

I've favored electric shavers for most of my now many years. Started with a Norelco rotary, then a Remington foil type, then back to a Norelco. But for the last 9 years I've used a Panasonic.

In truth no one was really that much better than the others. -Or that much worse. All did a pretty good job. All failed for some reason with the lower neck hairs. The rest was just convenience, handling, shape and weight.

The Panasonic was as good as any -- but it had a flaw: The cost of the blades and heads which were supposed to be replaced yearly.

I did that after year one, and then started stretching the time period between replacments because of the cost. About $60.

When the Panasoncs's head and blades just HAD to be replaced I rebelled at the cost, and bought this entire shaver for a small fraction (one fifth!) the price of just those replacement parts for the Pani.

Basically it is a return to those old Norelcos. Same basic experience. Same level of shaving efficiency.

This unit feels good in the hands. It is very quiet. It seems to hold a charge well (and charge quickly)

Its trimmer is better than average. Its snap on cover not very well designed -- not easily attached and not too secure.

And that's basically "it." Nothing great. Nothing particularly wanting. But, especially at the current sale price with a large 'coupon' discount, a truly terrific bargain.

All that remains as a question is its durability. But even if it needed replacement after a few years it is a lot cheaper (and basically just as good) as the Panasonic with its expensive to replace blades.

title: Obnoxious fan noise.  Low CFM.  By default no ozone for better or for worse.  Some light leakage.
text:
I actually got this for the intent of possibly gutting it and using it in another application, but first before doing that I've been using it in its intended manner.

First, it does use a UV light and could potentially eliminate some of the *CAUSES* of odors like certain bacteria by k killing germs in any air that cycles through it. But that UV light is, at least by default, one that only produces 254.3nm so does not produce ozone. This means it won't really directly eliminate odors by actually binding with the particles in the air that cause them but can only do so indirectly by killing things. There do seem to be some bulbs that can fit it that do produce ozone however, just these are third party and not official with the official ones not offering such an option. On one hand, it is worth remembering that ozone can be as bad for you as it is to other things, but on the other hand, a 3.5W lamp wouldn't produce very much and should dissipate very quickly unless you're pretty much right on the thing (which you shouldn't be anyway!) Since this is third party only (with most options not even shipping within the same country) I'm a little disappointed given the intended purpose of this (which is largely to clean the air -- especially of odors -- where ozone+UV would be much more effective than UV alone.)

I definitely have to make a major complaint about its fan though. I almost wonder if I got a unit with a bad fan or something because it makes a fairly awful noise. It's not even so much that it's loud as that the noise is very obnoxious. I think maybe the fan must vibrate too much or something, but I'm not really sure what exactly the cause of the noise is. The fan doesn't seem to push as much air through as it really should (especially to be truly effective in even a relatively small room) so I'm definitely not happy with this part of its design at all. Perhaps a "blower" type fan would be better for this sort of task. One thing that can definitely be said though is that it doesn't push enough air to cover even a relatively small space very well and I wouldn't expect it to be terribly effective in anything bigger than a closet. Perhaps if placed right over the sources of odors (like in the case of a litterbox for example) it might still be useful, but otherwise it probably isn't. Of course, such a dinky fan has very little static pressure and they couldn't put any sort of filter over it, so it will pick up dust fast and tear up fairly quickly if placed too near to a litterbox anyway. As obnoxious as its noise is, it might make a cat decide not to use the litterbox if it were there anyway.

I also wonder a bit about the light leakage. Near to the top it has plastic which carries some of the light intentionally and may be opaque to UV ranges so perhaps ok, but the holes at the top do not filter the light at all and nothing particularly blocks it, so the top lets the light through unfiltered. Perhaps at this level it is not enough to matter. I really can't be sure and so I may just be nit-picking here, but I do think they should have angled the output so the air could go around but the light would not given the potential for harm from the UV light.

EDIT: The more I use it the more I think it doesn't even work stock. I've been sniff-testing it and get nothing really. 253.7nm light seems to produce something in the air that has a bit of a smell. Not ozone (officially it breaks down ozone in fact) like 185nm light does, but all my real 253.7nm lamps produce a very strong and not very pleasant smell (which, if anything, is actually worse than the smell of ozone IMO.) This, however, does not seem to. I temporarily swapped in a bulb being used by a sterilizer that matched the specifications of this thing and suddenly could smell something obvious. So I think the bulb that comes with it may just simply not be very good. Most likely it requires one of those third party bulbs even to really do the job it claims to do.

The incredibly obnoxious noise the thing produces is enough reason not to like it however. The more I try to use it the more it begins to drive me crazy.

title: Ehhh. Not bad...
text:
Ok look. I'm a professional body worker. I use oil a lot. I tried this out.

Pros.
1. The unit heats up quickly
2. Another reviewer left a helpful comment, which is to keep the dial at ZERO when turning the unit on to avoid blowing a fuse. This DOES work. Thanks random commenter!
3. The oil does get good and warm or almost hot, eventually. It feels quite nice.

Cons
1. I've tried plastic and metal oil bottles. Both leak oil as it heats up, continuously. It requires a towel. It can get pretty messy. (if anyone knows a hack to get around this please share!)

2. I've left both bottles in for 30 minutes at full temperature. The oil inside only stays warm for about 15 minutes after I remove the bottle to use it. So that means if you want it hot enough to last you for an hour massage, you better have it warming waaaaay in advance. If you want consistently very warm oil, two oil warmer spots isn't going to cut it. You'd need 3 or 4 so that you can rotate every 15 minutes or so.

3. Plastic bottles WILL get very soft and mushy. They still hold form, but it's a little disconcerting and possibly unhealthy. It may likely leach microplastics into the oil, into your bloodstream and into that of your recipient/client. I switched to a metal bottle.

4. Naturally, the bottle will be notably hot if it has been warming for a long time. No way around that.

5. This will not work for most lotions, and no creams. The high heat will change the chemistry too much in anything else and it will make it runny and gross. Oil only.

The National Academy of Medicine lists the upper daily limit at 4,000 IU, though doses up to 10,000 IU have been found NOT to cause toxicity in healthy humans. For this reason, I won't be taking daily mega-doses of vitamin D. I will take these capsules once or twice a week in supplement to my daily multivitamin, which contains 100% of my daily supply of vitamin D. I like taking more, especially during the winter, as my health insurance does not approve vitamin D tests in healthy individuals my age.

title: Not Portable, A Little Finnicky
text:
At first I thought mine was broken. I had read the instructions carefully, but couldn't get anything to turn on. It says click, but there's no buttons, just a touch monitor. I would press. Press and hold. Eventually, I got it with a tap. A very brief tap. The only time you need to press and hold is to turn the nightlight off.
When you press play, a little voice says "music on" before starting, and similar when you turn it off.

There's a little ring when you plug it in to tell you it's working, and there is no on/off button because it has no battery. So you must plug it in. It is also a standard two prong outlet plug, and not a usb port which has become the popular power cable.

There's no back button on the sounds, so you have to cycle through all of them to get to the one you want, though it's broken up between two buttons, the "music" icon and the "fan" icon, so there aren't as many you have to go through as with others.

The nightlights changes into a variety of colors, first two being soft light and bright white before going to colors. This is really nice for reading in bed.

title: It's fine, but don't use the hooks
text:
This silicone bath body brush works much like the dozens of other similar products that have shown up recently. It's all one piece silicone, even the handles are silicone and there is no metal frame that I can tell. The whole thing is very flexible and can be folded and rolled up. The biggest advantage of the all-silicone material is that it doesn't really get moldy if you leave it in your shower, like a wooden back-scrubbing brush will.

One side of the brush has silicone bristles and the other side has rounded bumps. I didn't really find the bumps to be useful, but the bristles work for cleaning your back. If you are using a body wash liquid soap, it helps if you lather it up in your hands briefly before applying it to the bristles. If you apply the body wash directly to the silicone bristles, you can work it up into a lather, but it takes more effort. You cannot really work up a lather on the bumpy side. From there you just hold onto the grips and use it to scrub your back. It works and it's easy to use.

As part of the package, you receive two adhesive hooks. The hooks have a thin transparent plastic square of plastic with adhesive on the back, and a metal hook is embedded into front-side of that that plastic square. I was able to affix the plastic hook to the tile in my shower and it has remained in place for over 3 weeks now. It supports the entire weight of the silicone scrub brush. However, after just 3 weeks the tiny metal hook is rusted and corroded beyond belief. The rust bits get all over the handle of the silicone brush too. Give it another 3 weeks and I bet the metal part of the hook falls apart due to corrosion. If you buy this, don't bother using those hooks. They're useless.

In conclusion, this inexpensive silicone scrub brush makes it easy to clean your back with body wash. However, you're probably only going to use the bristle side, and you shouldn't use the included hooks. It's fine for the price. If you buy it, though, i suggest you buy a 3M shower hook that is all-plastic and won't rust.

title: Short Term Relief
text:
I purchased this because it was less expensive than Penetrex and I'd thought I'd try it out.. Unfortunately, compared to Penetrex, at least for me, I do not feel that it is worth the savings. I'm using it for Plantar Fasciitis and Osteoarthritis in my knees. Although it does provide some pain relief, the duration is limited to a couple hours, whereas Penetrex lasts for up to half a day. However, SynthaFlex does offer a little more relief, albeit very temporarily, for my Osteoarthritis than Penetrex does. It is not nearly as effective for my Plantar Fasciitis pain. Ultimately, if I have to apply it many times throughout the day, it is not cost effective in comparison.

The SynthaFlex has a slightly greasy feel to it and leaves my hands feeling that way even after I've washed them. The menthol scent is pleasant and not overpowering.

text:
I love bath bombs, but i don't love spending a lot of money on bathbombs which are, at the end of the day, a relatively brief pleasure for me. My daughter in law can spend hours in the tub. Me? 30 minutes is about my top. Hard for me to spend the equivalent of a movie theater ticket (okay matinee) at Lush for that.

These particular bombs have pros and cons. First, they transform the color of the tub quite quickly and offer a lot of color saturation. The smell is not too strong, but that works for me because I have perfume allergies. I find them oddly different from many bath bombs in that they aren't very buoyant. They sink and dissolve and at the end you have a slightly silty, highly colored bathwater just the same, but without the intermediate effervescence. Unlike some higher end products, all of the bath bombs seem to be the same in color and scent.

They *are* a good size. I'd be pegging this as base-level acceptable if not for that- but the generous dimensions make them a cut above. I've bought big-box-store bombs that were about the same price but half the size, which nudges these up in my estimation.

title: doesn't work the way they show in the commercials
text:
When I first saw this advertised on TV (in retrospect though, it seems, only because I was recording Frasier reruns in the middle of the night, because I didn't see those commercials at any other hour on any other channel I happened to watch) I thought this brush would take the market by storm, and was impatiently waiting for some reviews before I splurged. But none of that ever happened - there still isn't a single review of this on any beauty blog or YouTube, the couple of articles you can Google aren't actually reviews if you read them, their own ad on YouTube hasn't garnered any comments in three months (this is unheard of), and the TV commercials stopped airing as well because I am guessing they ran out of money. A few reviews did trickle in here on Amazon over that period, and half of those couldn't be less helpful.

I finally decided to bite the bullet and just try out the brush myself.

Well, my experience with the brush really wasn't great (I'd say my true rating is about 1.5 stars). I have 2c/3a half wavy half curly hair, and anyone with curly hair would be able to relate: you know how when you dry brush your curls out you end up with this huge frizzy mane? Well, the effect I got with the Clamp It brush wasn't much better. It did straighten, but it didn't leave the hair smooth or shiny, it was just this big head of straight (and dull) hair. Honestly even when curly my hair is much shinier. It also didn't straighten the ends of my hair for some reason, I still had a little wave going on there. And everything I am describing continued to be the case even after multiple passes.

Also, the big selling point of this brush was that it can straighten large strands of hair at a time. Well, here is the thing: with my hair, at least, if I took a wide strand, it wouldn't go THROUGH the heated comb teeth, it went over ON TOP of them, and that's with the brush fully clamped! In order to get my hair to actually go through the heaters, I'd have to take a very small strand at a time, and that kinda defeats the whole purpose - I mean, the whole reason I even wanted the Clamp It in the first place was because using any other straightening tool is such a pain.

Oh well, at least I was able to return.

title: I've read that L. Sakei is missing from the sinuses of chronic sinusitis sufferers.
text: In December of 2015 I got the flu. It was bad, and when I finally started feeling better a couple weeks later my symptoms returned and I got worse, and I'm pretty sure that I got pneumonia after the flu. I was sick for almost a month. After I got back to normal I could not get rid of the "sick smell" that you tend to get when you are sick. It can best be described as an "infected sweaty gym sock". I smelled that horrible odor for a couple of months, hoping that it would go away on it's own. In June 2016 I went to the doctor who put me on Augmentin, which did absolutely nothing except mess up my gut. The stinky smell continued for three years until I got a prescription for Keflex, which cleared up the stink within three days. While the stink was gone, I now have a "sweet smell" that I've been dealing with since Dec 2017. It is 100 times better than the stinky smell, but it's still annoying and my sense of smell and taste is about 90% diminished. I have had no other sinus issues like pain, swelling, or discharge. I've read about this strain of L. Sakei and how it is not found much in people suffering from chronic sinusitis, and hope that it can help my sinuses return to their natural flora. I've only given it three stars to start with, but will amend my review each week as I continue to use the product. I used it for the first time last night and notice that the sweet smell is somewhat diminished. I'm really hoping this stuff works.

title: Itsy Bitsy Container with an even smaller spoon, If I miss a dose, I notice it
text:
The container is only 1 1/2 inches across and 1/2 inch deep, while the spoon a whopping 1/8 inch deep, and 1/4 inch wide. Inside the container is a tiny little moisture absorbent bag that makes it seem like you are getting even less of this. But the container has 100 doses using that tiny spoon, and if you start out with half doses like me then it will last even longer. But just getting over the shear tininess of this product is a hurdle.

Okay, I'm over it, and have been taking it every morning for a couple weeks now. The flavor is terrible, mixing it in water doesn't help, I just take half a spoonful dump it in my mouth and drink some coffee, yuk. For me, the tiny dose helps me get over my AM grogginess and I really feel it helps "lift" my mood for the day. When I miss a dose on a crazy morning is when I notice it most, sort of a "what is bugging me today" feeling. On those days I get the plastic smile out of my desk and put it in my mouth. Hopefully someone finds this rather personal description helpful.

Of course I looked it up on the good ole net and read all the info about it, the research verdict is still out, but there is "mounting evidence" that it has multiple positive effects, and like almost anything you can take to much, stick to the minuscule spoon once a day. As a consumer who thinks drugs are over regulated, I would like to stick my tongue out at the doctor who wants to take this out of my hands. pfffffffff

I have used many different types of lidocaine/numbing patches for the nerve pain I have emanating from my spine. All other patches have worked somewhat. These did not work at all. Moreover, something about the stretchiness of the fabric made my skin itch.

I really wanted to like these, but they seem useless. I highly recommend trying a different brand. Who cares if they stay on if they don’t numb anything?

title: Handy, But Slightly Bulky to Carry On
text:
It took a bit of time for me to get on a plane to try this. I was pretty excited to use it to help the inevitable discomfort of being in a plane for 5-6 hours in a seat that is slightly cramped. First off, having this in my backpack takes up a fair amount of space. Would it be worth it? I soon discovered that attaching it to the seat in front of me was easier than I expected it to be. Your mileage may vary, but for the most part, I think this would work for most larger planes.

The rest does what it says, and my feet no longer touched the floor, but lay suspended in a hammock a few inches off the ground. This is comforting, but also leaves you a bit less mobile (the passenger next to me wanting to get out five times during our flight)so having to take your feet out and let someone get out takes more time of course. Did it help? Somewhat yes, so in that respect it is a success. But the cost of it being the bulk and trouble of setting up knocks off a star. It's really up to you to decide if it's worth it. I only tried it on two flights, so I will update if anything changes as far as how it holds up over time.

Build quality is alright. It seems sturdy enough to last a bit of time, but that remains to be seen. I found the effect of it more comforting on my return trip due to my feet being sore and elevated positioning helps with that. Overall, I say give it a shot.

title: Quality product to make your own reishi capsules
text: I've taken reishi for many years, in many forms. When I was younger I made my own reishi tincture, but for the past few years I've preferred capsules. My huge respect for Paul Stamets lead me to his product line, but it's pretty expensive and I realized recently that those capsules are filled mainly with mycelium. So I started investigating products that are made from the fruiting body of the reishi mushroom, and thought I would try filling my own capsules. This product is really high quality and a much richer color than what was contained in other capsules I've purchased. The package suggests adding the product to smoothies or hot drinks, but I found it to be too bitter for my taste. I bought a package of size 0 empty capsules, and a little scoopula, and set about filling the caps with the reishi powder. It is a tedious process and a lot of the product stuck to my fingers. Nonetheless, if you are quality and value minded, making your own caps out of this excellent product is a worthwhile task.

title: From what country is this sourced?
text:
I am alarmed at this increasing trend of consumer products failing to disclose country of origin. Did that stop being a law? If so, when?

I know...the bag says "USDA organic." In some countries, however, one can only imagine the corruption that would cause this label to be inappropriately given.

It also says "certified by CCOF", which is California Certified Organic Farmers.

Yet, when I search the CCOF listings for "Super Organics LLC," I find nothing. Even a Google search brings up little. Only a document that Super Organics LLC is a Florida LLC, perhaps owned by LC Natural, LCC?

The last thing I want is a "health food" that has sketchy sourcing.

title: Frustrating Technology that Cannot Handle Transition Between Carpet and Floors
text:
[[VIDEOID:8ea5dfaa166848a736fa1f56072ca2a0]] When I was told of the opportunity to review this Hoover robotic vacuum, I was very excited. I had wanted a robot helper around the house while I was at, and I had high hopes that the machine would eliminate or at least reduce the frequency with which I had to vacuum the house manually. Unfortunately this unit suffers in a number of areas: set up was not as intuitive as it should be, the Bluetooth connection worked only sporadically, and worst of all the device was completely unable to navigate over area rugs and easily became hung up on objects.

The quick start guide on the box seems deceptively simple. Simply find an open stretch of wall for the charging base, turn the unit on, and let it charge till ready. The blinking light indicates charging...until it stops blinking. Powering it on resulted in the unit backing up, beeping, and returning to the base to charge. Sometimes pressing the top power button results in a squawking beep and refusal to move. After much trial and error, the unit did start vacuuming on its own.

I had hoped the Bluetooth connection would help with the lack of feedback from the unit itself. However the Hoover app doesn't seem to work well. I selected the model, and the app searches for nearby robots....and searches...and searches... The Hoover app did not find the robot most of the time.

These little inconveniences could be overlooked if the robot worked when it got going. Unfortunately the area rugs for certain parts of my hardwood floors were insurmountable objects. Worse, the little robot would get part way onto the rug and become stuck rather that backing up or realizing it couldn't mount the rug. Manually placing the robot on the carpet, the robot will vacuum; however, it becomes easily stuck on furniture.

At this point I have to give this unit a 2-star rating: I don't like it. If I wanted someone to refuse to vacuum and squawk at me when I ask it to work, I'd try to make the kids vacuum.

text:
Forskolin is a much ballyhooed herbal supplement, that weightlifters and people looking to lose fat are starting to use. However, if you think you take a bottle of pills, and stick to a poor diet and low activity level, then wake up one day laying in a gooey puddle of 40 pounds of rendered fat that sweated thru your skin overnight, you're dreaming. The slow, natural loss of weight seems to the weight that stays off. A proper diet and sustainable exercise plan makes much more sense, than crash diets and over training. title: Cherry Lime is a better flavor : Pricey Water
text:
About the Product: Love the square shape of the bottle, the label design and the ingredients in it.

About the Taste : "Defend" Cherry Lime flavor for Toxin Defense. This one is better tasting than watermelon, still mild in flavor but drinkable. No sugar is good, sweetened by Stevia leaf extract.

My take:
1) If the company or anyone can prove the claim about the drinks with good scientific research then I would understand. Also even if you can prove the claim how many bottles do we have to drink to see a tiny bit of difference. This is very expensive Infused Water in a fancy bottle.
2) I understand that most of these kind of products have big claims and we all at one point go with our instincts, a little bit of blind faith and/or reviews but after going through what I would like to see is does it taste good? and is it economical? For these reasons, I would like to pass on this one.
3) These and the other big brands like VM, G, P etc they do work in the sense that they do hydrate our body, they have either some electrolytes and/or some sugar or a lot of sugar. Ideally, this formula will give you some energy so they work. But for certain claims, I am not very comfortable.

I rather make my infused drinks at home.

Tip: 1) Take a big Thermo Flask, put some ice in it, squeeze 1 lemon, squeeze some mint juice and put the leaves in it, shred some fresh ginger, pinch of turmeric, black pepper, cinnamon, and some honey. Shake it and drink it all day. (Keep adding, subtracting or changing the ingredients, there are no rules)
2) Before every sip, take deep breaths, 3 times. This will change you life. Peace.

title: This is a Euphoria Machine
text: This footbath was surprisingly impressive. I was concerned with the collapsing body that it would maybe be flimsy, but the unit is durable and structurally sound. The body does indeed collapse for easy storage, but the walls are thick so it stays firmly when set up. First time set up and usage was simple, just fill with water and turn the unit on. I used already warm water from the tap and the heating feature worked well. The jet and massage features were a nice touch and the remote is a nice feature so you do not have to bend down to change settings (nice for those with mobility issues). Design wise, the bath was big enough but the added features made for a strange almost divide in the footbath which was awkward for the rest of my family as their feet were larger. They mentioned it was not annoying enough to outweigh the benefits from the warming and massage features. It comes with a carrying handle but I would not recommend using it after the bath is filled, as it can become fairly heavy. All in all, I am extremely happy with the footbath and look forward to using it more

title: Expensive for what amounts to foam.

title: It’s is big and comfortable
text: I bought this from watching Alex the trucking guy on YouTube. Since I do Uber and sit down a lot I’ve been looking at truckers lifestyle because it is similar and one of the things they mention is the ultimate seat cushion. Not going to lie I was skeptical. No way a seat cushion could get rid of my but pain ache and sores and on top of that it was over 100 dollars too. I looked over the reviews and saw positive ones so I guess I’d give it a try plus as I mentioned before Alex the trucking used it so I’d thought it be good. Anyway shipping took about a week and half and came in a big cardboard box. Then when I opened it I received the ultimate seat cushion as well as the back cushion I ordered and the double seat too. I did read the reviews so they did mention that it smells or it is toxic and it can also melt too. When I took out the seat cushions from the packaging I did notice a smell or I guess you could call it fumes. Yeah it was really strong. But I didn’t care, others do if you read the reviews but all I cared about was if it worked or not. So I read the instructions and properly put the seat cushion together and even with the cover on it still emitted a strong smell. Then I put the ultimate seat cushion in my car seat and man it was huge barely fit. I am 6’0 so I already and cramped in my car. I previously owned a Toyota Camry and was cramped in it. Then I purchased a Honda HRV 2019. I was okay in it but when I put the ultimate seat cushion on it my head was hitting the ceiling so I adjusted my seat down but it still wasn’t enough but enough to drive which suited me. I’d recommend if you put this in your car maybe remove the drivers seat because that alone takes up 2-3 inches of height which would help a lot if your tall. But then I’d go to home depot and make your own driver seat from wood steel or plastic and somehow make it work. I’m actually considering this because I’m on the border we’re it’s annoying having my head hit the ceiling of my car and just taking time to get used to. The double seat cushion I purchased too wasn’t the best. Maybe for sitting down for a hour on foldable chair but for car seats I wouldn’t get it. I returned it and am going to buy the royal seat because on the chart where it describes the dimensions and the weight and so on. There was another review on here saying if the ultimate cushion is to much and the next step down is the double seat. Eh.. I don’t agree because I bought both and keep in mind I am under 200 pounds around 176 lbs. The guy mentioned that if you are about this weight then the double seat would work but I doesn’t maybe if you weigh 100 pounds or less. I’d say the next step down after the ultimate is the royal then maybe the double seat after that. I did have to wash the ultimate and the back cushion because they smelled so bad. I put it in my washer for cold water like instructed because heat is its enemy. To much heat will make the cushion melt. After the washer it still smelled so I put it in my bath tub and used my dish soap(Dawns platinum x4 cleaning power) that seems to work but still smelled so I squirted about half a bottle over the cushions making sure soap was in the squares on both sides or at least most of them. After that I let it set and came back checking up every 10 minutes and every time I would take them out of the water and re submerge about 4 times then leave and come back and do it all over again a couple more times. Then it the smell finally started to go away but smelled when you got really close but it was good enough for me. I did notice hat doing that did something to the plastic or the purple stuff like it started to peel off so just be careful when doing this. Over all the cushion is nice and comfortable recommend 5/5 I only used it for 1 day maybe I’ll keep updated on my review late on.

title: I have a kid who wears glasses pretty much 24/7
text: I have a kid who wears glasses pretty much 24/7. He wears Rec Specs for soccer, which have the strap built in, but is now old enough to want to have "cool" glasses for normal school. Since insurance pretty much covers it, he's sporting a pair of sweet Ray-Bans. They look great on him, and he is actually pretty darn careful with them (knock on wood), but I am no fool. I'm sure he does things more often than I care to think about that you probably shouldn't-- like I watched him playing football in the snow, go down (shouldn't have been wearing the Ray Bans at all, but you know... 8 year old going to run home to change glasses when hanging with friends on snow day? I think not). Anyhow, he went down, and glasses actually came off his face, but thanks to these, at least he still had them attached to him. Otherwise, we would have been carefully treading all over a neighbor's lawn for the next 48 hours (until the melt), or someone would have stepped on them because they were lost in the snow (blue/black frames, not easily seen in snow). I take off one star because they have a few loose threads right out of the package, which Mom (me) obviously cut/burned right away, but they really are pretty good. My kid sweats a lot, very active... and these don't slip off or look nasty fast (we have the blue). I also like to keep a pair of these as back up in case the Rec Specs tether/backing fails on his sports glasses. So far, no need... but there is always next week!
