title: Nite nite
text:
I’ve used lots of masks over just as many years, but very few were purchased- either gifts, found (factory sealed in thrift shops, of course) and what appeared to be a lifetime supply of JetBlue “disposables” given to me by an FA friend- there were sort of a go-to collection, when the non-adjustable elastic stretched beyond useable limits, move on to the next pair. But, when I lost them all (and everything else) in the recent CA wildfires, it was one of those things you don’t think to grab under evac orders- sleeping in a shelter tended to make me regret that immediately, they aren’t really conducive to lights out sleep. But then, I am not sure I would not prefer to keep one eye open anyway. As luck would have it, I found a weird zebra-striped unit in the box of donations for we victims, but it was cardboardy and cheap feeling, it made it two nights. I did find two tucked into the suitcase I grabbed as I hastily packed, this was a small blessing (in view of everything else, very small, but I’ll take it)

So enter the Tlinna (?) which I liked it right away, it had a baby-butt smooth surface on both sides, boasting mulberry silk on both sides; reversible is a nice touch, and I find either side equally comfortable. Two strap models are always superior, and with tiny buckles for adjustment it’s a lot easier to slide them into a comfortable length. (Continued wearing on the same side molded the thing into what seems like a tiny bra, so I now plan to flip it daily- I take enough flak for wearing one in the first place)

The buckles lie flat, and the straps come from the center stitch of the mask, so while it may not be sold as such, I am finding either side equally comfortable. Properly adjusted it is as a mask should be- barely there.
No gaudy statement of a print or pattern or faux fur, just a pleasantly opaque blackout. I have had so many MRI’s recently that the imaging place tend to comment on my eye mask du jour)

Time will tell how the elastic will wear, so I might pick up a spare or one for travel; although actually needing to purchase one tends to make me keep – a closer eye on it (sorry)

title: Solves the problem of the fragile lens cover
text:
The G15/G16 is probably the best pocket camera available, but it has a weakness. Thin leaves automatically cover the lens when the camera is off, but the leaves are easily bent. The bottom line is that the G15 is a pocket camera that really cannot be kept in a pocket. The Quick-Change Adapter works by using an adhesive ring to attach a threaded filter adapter to the front surface of the lens mount. I was suspicious that the adhesive would really hold, but so far it has been solid. The included lens cap does the job of protecting the lens assembly.

Other solutions I've seen involve gluing a piece of glass over the lens. that's unacceptable because it makes another surface to clean and make internal reflections. There are also filter adapters that affix a large tube around the lens, with means it is no longer a pocket camera.

Today we pulled this out out the closet where it has been safely stored (again for the record,new, in it's original box), plugged it in and set off to curl my daughter's hair for prom. I watched over an hour of YouTube videos.
Results were poor ... no consistency in the curls (well, waves are more like it), and could only do about a finger thickness amount of hair at a time. But, hey, I had no experience using it, so perhaps I did it wrong despite following the same technique as shown in every single video i watched.
It was also so not that you couldn't hold it except at the very ends, but a lot of people wear gloves so maybe it's normal. But it left my daughter's hair so hot that it burned to touch it and that was even with a quick swipe to "tame" the fly-aways. Wasn't sure if this was normal but it was concerning.

However, the bigger, more dangerous issue was the loud "pop" that came from it, the burning not little projectile ball of rubber that shot out of the electrical cord where it connects to the iron and the smoke that came pouring out of the hole left behind from the tiny little explosive "pop". We had used it for about 20 minutes.

This is extremely dangerous. Don't risk your or your loved ones life with this garbage.

title: Fits weird and pinches my nose.
text:
The first thing I noticed upon opening this was that it looked weird, compared to other eye massagers I've tried. That would be because it has acupressure nodes built right into the face of it, instead of covering them up the way other units do.

At first I thought that meant it might not be as noisy as other units. That part, as it turned out, is debatable; it doesn't have the same SOUND as the ones that rely on air compression but I'm still hearing the motors turning those nodes around. It wasn't loud, I'm just thinking that making these things quiet is a case of the technology not catching up with the idea.

Anyway, second thing I noticed is the fit. How well it works for you depends on your face shape, but this was one of the awkward ones for me--the massager was actually too small to leave room for a suitable position for the strap, resulting in me having to either sit the massager too high on my face to make the strap hold it in place properly or have the strap push down (and past!) my ears to make the massager sit in the right spot. Also, there must be a more significant difference between this and the kneading on other massagers than "the nodes are not covered" because I went through every mode and every one involved pinching my nose.

And the third thing I noticed... it takes a long time for it to warm up enough to feel it. I was about ready to turn this thing off by the time it actually started feeling hot enough to use as a "hot compress."

The unit did seem to help stave off the migraine before it had a chance to grow into anything truly painful, though.

title: Bulky, cannot be used while charging, modes are somewhat confusing. But feels nice to use.
text:
I have, thanks to a combination of spending a lot time on the computer and slinging boxes around at work, the occasional twinge in my wrist that may or may not be carpal tunnel (undiagnosed). The occasional PAINFUL twinge that interferes with the previously mentioned activities when it occurs.

While the fact I have one of those "on your feet all day" retail positions means I can't exactly use this at work at a moment's notice, it takes care of the problem quite nicely at home.
Well, sometimes. See, while it has a rechargeable battery, it can't be used while charging. Maybe a safety feature, maybe flawed design, I don't know, but it means that for a product that only lasts a few sessions per charge you have to remember to charge it regularly... or wait until it's charged when you might need it most. It's also quite bulky which limits where I can be while I'm using it; need to declutter besides the point, my current desk would probably work but I would never have been able to use this when I was dependent on a tiny little student desk, and it's really not comfortable enough to sit in my lap the way one of the official product photos suggests.

But when it works, it works well. Heat if you want it, something resembling the fine-pointedness of acupressure (that'd be what makes all of those temporary pressure marks in your skin when you use it), multiple pressure intensity options, multiple modes depending on where you want to focus that pressure.... And a timer indicator that works in five-minute increments, giving you somewhat an idea of how much time you have left during your current session.

My two biggest problems that I think need addressing both relate to power.
One is mentioned above and that's the inability to use it while it's charging.
The other is that it uses the much older style round plug-in on the UNIT'S side... and USB on the charging end, making it difficult to charge if you don't have any shelves conveniently near a USB port without investing in a USB extension cable (not included) and all but impossible to swap cords if and when the included one wears out, unless in both cases you're lucky enough to find a "universal" cord that has the right size connector. Frankly, if they were going to use USB they should've gone USB the entire way, charge it with as universal an option as if I were charging my cell phone.

title: Does okay to block out light OR as a heated mask but not both. Cord too short.
text:
I will say, I like the IDEA of the whole "3d molding" that went into shaping this to allow airflow to your eyes instead of making yet another compress... but I think they tried a little too hard to protect that airflow with the result that it doesn't properly fit all users.

By which I mean, I can use this as a heated mask and have it slid halfway down my nose, leaving enough of a gap at the bottom of my eyes that it will never work as a light-blocking mask, OR I can pull it up far enough to actually block the light but with the result that the (extremely hot) bottom of the mask is resting almost on top of my eyeballs. Nosepiece is simply too stiff for me to pinch it shut like I'd need to get both benefits at the same time.

Also, never thought I'd be one to complain about how short the cord is, but it turns out, when you're trying to plug it into a surge protector that is directly under your bed, pull the cord over the bed, and then plug it into a mask positioned somewhere in the middle (bearing in mind that the top of my TWIN size mattress comes to less than two feet off the floor), 4 foot really doesn't leave you a lot of room to move. Especially as I have fallen asleep while wearing this on multiple occasions (usually long after the heat turned itself off) and woken up to find it unplugged as I tend to move around a lot in my sleep. Probably good that it means less risk of tangling in my sleep but I wouldn't mind having enough slack to use it when I want to shift to laying my stomach... which would put the mask's plug-in on the opposite side of the bed from where the surge protector is located.

title: Not like the picture...at all...
text:
First and foremost, this product arrived super fast and was packaged securely in with a couple of other products I had ordered from Amazon. As far as seller and shipping goes I'd give that five stars!

Now on to the reasons I can't give the product so many stars... Bunions, or "pones" as my aunt likes to call them, apparently run in the family on my mom's side, with the females anyway. My aunt has her "pones" and my mom was starting to get them. My grandmother had them so bad that she had to have surgery and they were painful for her. Her toes had started turning to the side. I was always afraid I'd get them and sure enough, a couple of months ago I looked down and saw the dreaded POINT on the side of my foot. ARGH!!! PONE! I immediately started freaking out trying to make it go away, pushing my toes around thinking I was just seeing things... NOPE! My husband commented on it and said he could see it. :/

I stumbled across these correctors while looking for other things and decided I'd try them to see if they'd help...they're made out of silicone. They aren't supportive like they look like they would be from the pictures. I put them between my first and second toes to see how they would fit and the corrector wedged correctly between my toes but the side was floppy and not shaped to the side of my foot like it shows in the pictures. When I walk it just flops around all over the place.

So. so based on my experience, I can see where it might work as far as keeping your toes apart, but after wearing it, I could only give the product itself two stars. I don't think it's good to wear in your shoe the way it flops and twists around. Maybe if you could use some adhesive it might work better, but it's not advertised that way.

I must include that I did receive this product at a discounted price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. That being said, I will always add a completely honest review based on my own experiences with a product whether there is any type of compensation or not. I expect to read honest reviews when I am considering buying a product and I hope others do the same.

title: Great for smaller ears and the longer stem makes for easier removal
text:
I bought myself a pair of the long stem earplugs and my boyfriend the regular ones. I'm really glad I got the long stem version, as they still aren't overly noticeable and make it way easier to take out. I have tried both the Hearos High Fidelity Ear Plugs and the DownBeats, and do prefer the DownBeats because they fit my ears better. Apparently, I have small ears, or at least small ear canals--the Hearos Ear Plugs couldn't even fit fully into my ears and it was really annoying! The stems on the Hearos were also much longer, to the point where I felt like I had antennas sticking out of my ears. The DownBeats, on the other hand, fits great and does a good job with the sound.

Personally, I really like loud music and almost prefer it, and I feel like these ear plugs do almost too good a job of reducing sound. Despite this, the sounds aren't muffled and is not totally blocked. My boyfriend loves these since his hearing is super sensitive and he oftentimes finds himself with ringing ears after we go out.

I love the case as well, as it's easy to hook on to a key chain or a zipper. I have a bag that I always use when I go out to shows, and I keep the case looped on an inner zipper so I never lose them. The Hearos I had came in a snap case and I thought I lost them for the longest time until I dug them up again in a different bag, but with the DownBeats I never need to worry about that!

These are overall a very good quality pair of earplugs for a decent price.

title: Very user-friendly
text:
I flunked, as in got an "F", my high school typing class back in the 60's.
So, I have to look at the keyboard to type and I hit the keys harder than
a touch typist.

This large print board is helpful because: my tired old eyes can find the
keys right away, it's very quiet, the light doesn't glare off the keys, and the
size of the unit is actually a bit smaller than the older black one it is replacing.
I bought the one with the white keys with black lettering because I found
that to be more eye-friendly.

If I were a good typist or typed a lot, I might be concerned about the letters
on the actual keys as they are just thin decals and might wear off sooner
than the painted or embossed keyboards. But then, were I actually a good
typist, I wouldn't even need lettering on the keys, right?

There was no installation required, just plug into your computer's USB port
and start typing.

UPDATE: It's almost 5 mos later. I use this keyboard about 10-12 hrs per
day and it still works great. I still can't type worth beans and I kept
hitting the caps lock, so I just removed it! It was my fault, not the
fault of the keyboard.

My vision's fine, but I do recommend this for hunt and peck typists like
myself.

title: Great for lowering the volume a couple of notches, not for noise cancellation.
text:
Purchased these ear plugs for going to concerts and they DO protect my ear drums from exposure to extend loud conditions, but they don't CANCEL noise completely.

If you want to want to have a conversation with someone and just turn down the volume a couple of notches, these ear plugs would be good for you.

If you are on the market looking for ear plugs that will cancel out noise completely, I would suggest an alternative pair.

Pros:
- Excellent shape that will keep ear plugs in place in your ears. (This is coming from someone who avoids ear plugs headphones because they are constantly falling out of my ears)

- Good for shows because I can still hear the music and talk to the person next to me without removing the plugs from my ears.

Cons:
- The storage case that the plugs come in gets two stars.
The material of the plugs in combination with the hardshell case causes the plugs to stick to the case, preventing the case from sliding to a closed position.

I recommend using an alternative case while on the go for easy storage and removal.
(I use a keychain case that held my old ear plugs)

Overall:
I would recommend these plugs to anyone who is looking for a pair that doesn't completely cancel outside noises who also struggles with keeping ear buds in their ears, because they really do stay in place for all (adult) ear sizes. :)

Please let me know if you found my review helpful. :)

title: I'm getting the new 4g-5g unit - 2020. Reliable.
text: Let me correct previous incorrect statements (911 operator), and give review as a 6 year owner of this model unit. When you first get this unit, you need to call your local 911 system unit for a TEST of unit (after its fully charged). When you talk to the actual 911 operator for your area you need to inform them of the address this unit is to be registered to (your home address). If travel away from home, do a test in that area where your visiting to register a temporary address.  You should repeat this TEST every 90 days to insure both 911 system and this unit recognize each other. This unit does use GPS for locating you within 35 feet, unless obstructed like other GPS items gets obstructed by trees buildings and other things. You may experience this with your cell phone calls that are dropped. Many things obstruct signals, not necessarily the unit itself. Doing this TEST with your 911 local unit is like "pairing Bluetooth signals", so 911 will go to your registered residence directly, if it pings your in that 911 response area. If your not in that area another 911 system will locate you by repeat pings to your alerts button. You do not need to talk after activating this unit, standard protocol is 911will dispatch police to the button location because you could be unconsciousness due to medical emergency (heart attack seizure etc). This unit has been reliable for me and I intend to get their new 4g-5g unit coming out at end of 2020. I don't like an emergency service company deciding if I need help, I'd rather speak directly to 911 myself.  Having a unknowledgeable service company person ask a bunch of questions delaying the call to 911 dispatch could endanger me.

title: Travels well and useful long term at home
text:
I travel 30 weeks a year. The "travel" versions from the big name manufacturers (Water-Pik, Oral B) failed me in a variety of ways. I abandoned them and simply used only dental floss while traveling, while my routine at home is to floss manually and then use my water driven device.

I’ve now used it for both home and travel.

There is a simplicity to using the same micro USB cord(s) I use for virtually everything else, phone, tablet, etc., and it means less to carry, as well. Last week I was at a client site in Washington, DC and I forgot to charge the thing all week. It was still going strong on Thursday, the day I flew home, so now I know it has a battery life that exceeds four days when fully charged.

These guys really have come up with a better mousetrap.

I felt the only real design flaw is a minor one: when I remove the lid, I’d like to be able to place it *under* the water carriage so I don’t lose it. I have not lost it to date, but I just know one of these days it is going to stay behind in a hotel room.

It can also be smaller. Since I travel, I don’t need to leave enough water or mouthwash in the reservoir for more than that day. When I am home, the reservoir holds enough water or mouthwash for almost a week.

Using a micro USB charger is brilliant: Water-Pik batteries wear out in four days, *and* don't hold enough water or mouthwash. Oral B has a huge plug attachment with a converter that weighs more than the flosser itself. Using a common power source, because all of us have micro USB something or another, eliminates both problems and also makes the package lighter when I place it in my bag, Every ounce counts when you are stuffing enough business attire into a suitcase for a four day client visit.

It is really important for me, with receding gums, to take the best care I possibly can in order to avoid the inevitable dental surgery to replace the lost tissue. It sucks. I had the same surgery about ten years ago and couldn’t eat for a week after. They harvest tissue from the roof of your mouth to “refill” your gums, and the spot on the roof of my mouth where they cut out the tissue just plain hurt for a full week afterwards. So I really do floss religiously, because I would like to keep my teeth in my mouth and not have them in a jar when I am old. Well, older than I am now, I guess.

I do still feel the need to floss with dental floss instead of water in the evening. Minimum, before going to sleep.

title: Very decent wipes, dust and lint free, tear-free
text:
These are very good wipes. They are very unlike kitchen towels which are really multipurpose and can be used at so many different places in the house for cleaning purposes. The kitchen towels are obviously recyclable paper and absorb water so easily. These ones also absorb water but a bit less so, plus if too wet they will leave water or fluid on the surface being cleaned. Perhaps that true with any type of wipes but these are certainly less water absorbent as compared to kitchen towels.

They don't get torn when in use and these can even be used to clean up and mop up the floor. Obviously floor will need bigger wipes and these are not going to be good enough. (these are 9x9 inches and 300 count which is actually quite a lot and will last for a very long time)

The other good thing about these wipes is that they don't leave any lint or dust behind. Kitchen towels usually leave some lint on the glass or other surfaces that are being cleaned, especially when use for the 2nd or the 3rd time. But these are quite good to use and almost dust-free.

These wipes are re-usable too. Did notice that they pick up dirt easily and thereafter that dirt can almost get washed away with water. Once these are dried again, you can use them again.

Now on the flip side, these are made out of polyester and therefore not very environment friendly. That is probably the only drawback of these wipes. Not sure if any other recyclable material can be used to make such wipes that don't leave any lint or are tear-free.

Overall very decent product.

title: A great value exerciser
text:
This is a great little under the desk exerciser, but if I were to do it again, I would have opted for one about twice the price and quality. But overall, it's not a bad little exerciser, especially for the price. It was easy enough to assemble. The instructions were clear and it came with everything I needed to set it up.

What I like:
-Ease of use
-It calculates time, distance, pedals and calories with a reset button
-The base keeps it steady
-It's pretty easy to increase resistance with the knob
-I can burn 350-400 calories a day, casually pedaling while I work, so I could potentially lose a pound every 10-14 days without doing anything else, depending on how often I use it (at least according to the calorie counter)
-It's very quiet. My desk chair makes more noise squeaking while I pedal than the exerciser does
-I can easily use it at my desk (it helps having a desk I can raise, if needed)

What I don't like:
-The screen doesn't tell you what stats it's showing so it can be hard to know what you're looking at
-The pedaling can feel a bit disjointed
-The resistance knob has no markers, so you have no idea what resistance level you're setting it on
-The resistance level seems to drop over time, so it's hard to keep a consistent resistance level
-The straps for the pedals are screwed in, so you need a screwdriver to adjust them

Overall I like this exerciser and I'm glad I have it, but if you can afford it and want something nice to use long-term, I would recommend investing in a higher quality one. For shorter term or casual use, this is a great value and does what it's intended to do.

title: Just What I've been Looking For
text:
Saw there weren't any reviews yet and this pipe defiantly deserves a few words of praise.

For two years I've been searching pipe and tobacco shops for the "just right pipe." I wanted something unique, but not so showy that regular use would seem a novelty. After countless "generic" and "ridiculous" styles, I found this guy online and fell in love right out-of-the-pouch. The carved lines are attractive, rustic, and subtle - if it's not in your hand you don't even notice them. The grooves have a great feel, the bowl has nice depth, and the airflow and overall size provides a great smooth smoke.

The only negative is I've heard pearwood burns a bit hotter than regular briar, and I did notice the bowl felt a little warm after one fire-up, but I don't think that'd be a problem unless you're keeping lit all day.

If you're looking for a every-day pipe with a little uniqueness without looking like a novelty, you can't go wrong with this one!

title: the dark bags are getting lighter!!

I’ve been applying it and letting it dry before applying my facial lotion, primer and makeup. To be honest, I haven’t seen any difference in the puffiness of me under eyes, but I have noticed that the color is a little brighter under there. My skin seems to have taken a bit of a more even tone and the color isn’t nearly the gray-brown bruised look that it was last week. I truly wish I had taken a before and after picture.
When applying the lotion, it’s very wet, like melt in your hands kind of wet. It stays rather liquidy on the skin and does take about 12-15 minutes to dry enough to apply more lotions and stuff. I’ve been using about ½ of one pump per eye and it goes a very long way.
Attempting to help with the puffiness, I also applied to the tops of my morning eyelids, no such luck there either unfortunately. Despite the lack of puffiness fix, I’m very satisfied with the product overall. Its ability to let me use less concealer on the color of my under eye bags is a lifesaver. text: I've used this in the past on my shoulder while lifting. I'm a heavy lifter and this was recommended to me from a friend who does power lifting. It's similar to an icy hot but with much more intense heat and no icy feeling. It worked well on my shoulder and lasts for hours. The downfall to this is even after a shower it still lingers for a while. They say to try it on test spots to see how your body reacts to it. I didn't do that for my hamstrings and paid the price. I like it for my shoulder but I will never use on my hamstrings again. I put it on my hamstrings in the afternoon and it felt great. However hours and hours later I went to bed. I woke up at about 1130 because my legs felt like they were on fire. I put an ice pack on them but that didn't help. I washed them off with soap and tried going back to bed. That didn't work. So then I jumped in the shower and took a freezing cold shower and washed them again. I then grabbed another ice pack and was able to fall back asleep after midnight. I would strongly advise testing this on ALL different body parts before fully using it. And always shower before you go to bed. I would not recommend using this after the shower (if you shower at night or after working out).

title: Nice Starter Oil Blend Kit
text:
This oil blend set by Vyver is nice for a beginner oil user who wants to start out cheap before investing a lot of money in the high end oils.

They are very nicely packaged in a gift quality box and each bottle is individually sealed. This keep the oils fresh and prevents leakage during shipping. They are already pre-blended which is nice for beginners who aren't sure about mixing amounts or combinations to use.

The set includes the following:
Deep Muscle: Rosemary, Eucalyptus and Black Pepper
Stress Relief: Orange, Lemon, Peppermint, Spearmint, Geranium, Ginger and Fennel
Breathe: Lavender, Ylang Ylang, Bergamot
Health Shield: Lavender, Orange, Bergamot and Ylang Ylang
Good night: Ylang Ylang, Neroli, Sandalwood, Mandarin, Roman Chamomile
Head Ease: Orange, Lemon, Peppermint, Spearmint, Geranium, Ginger and Fennel

The scents are all quite mild, so it takes several drops to get the amount of fragrance I desire (about double what I would use with my more expensive brands). The dispensing is inconsistent, some of the bottles the oils come out almost too fast and others it seems like I'm holding it in the air forever.

Overall, this is a nice set, and would make a great gift for someone starting to experiment with oils. There are a few oil quality issues, I recommend these for diffusing and not skin application or internal uses.

*I was provided a sample of this product at no cost for testing and review. No promise was made for a positive review.

title: Great Quality Coconut Oil!!! Love it!!!
text:
I use coconut oil for so many things it's crazy. I use it as a moisturizer, in my smoothies, for lip balm, in cooking, oil pulling and I could go on and on. However, when using coconut oil properly it needs to be good quality coconut oil. There are some brands out there that are over processed and have been refined. Those brands won't even smell like coconut when you open the jar much less be able to taste it. This oil by Abundant Health Labs isn't one of those.

The product arrived professionally packaged and as soon as I opened the jar I could smell that rich luscious coconut smell I love so much. I got a little on my finger to taste, because I'll eat it by the teaspoon anyway for digestion. The taste is very good I can clearly taste the coconut and it seems to be a true extra virgin unrefined coconut oil. I love this oil and for the price the jar size is a great value. I can’t say enough about how impressed I was with the quality of this oil and I highly recommend it to those looking for a true quality coconut oil product.

title: Good but could be a lot better
text: The Homedics Body Bubbles Bath Spa is better than what was on the market before, which was essentially nothing. But it is not as good as the old Regina Euro Spa that I had for 20 years. This product could use some improvement in five areas: First it should have a GFI circuit built into the cord to prevent a user from possibly getting elecrocuted. Second the pad that sits in the tub is so soft that when you sit on it, the air is mostly cut off from half of the pad, so the spa action is not as good as it could be -- I have to keep it on at least medium speed to get any air up to the far end when I am sitting in the tub. My old Euro Spa had a more solid pad that was hinged into three sections, and it was solid enough that the air was distributed thorughout the pad. Third, the pad needs to be a little shorter: I have it in a very large jacuzzi spa (I prefer the bubble spa action to jacuzzi action) and it is too long for the length of the tub. If it is too long for that tub (big enough to hold me at over 6 feet tall) it must be too long for a normal tub too. You have to wet the suction cups before using, and make sure they are on a smooth, flat surface or they won't work. The unit is a little noisier than I'd like. When I am trying to really relax in a spa tub, the last thing I want is a whiney motor going on. But it is not as noisy as my spa tub's motor, which was terrible. Lastly the pad should have a hook built into it so you can hang it up to drain and dry when you are done. So I'd be a lot happier with this unit if these four things were addressed. That said, it works, and it is relaxing as long as I can deal with these issues. It could be a lot better and I would buy a better one if Homedics would improve it.

I am almost done with my second 1" 5 yard roll of this tape and am searching for a reasonable price and most of all, reasonable shipping fee. These are small rolls. It's a shame there is no stock here at Amazon.
This tape isn't as gentle as I'd hoped it would be, especially on the delicate eyelid area. But it is the best I've tried so far in the past five years of having to use something to keep my eyelids closed while sleeping.
I have had to try just about everything, too. For those of us with chronic dry eye, you know what it feels like to wake up in the morning if you eye dries out. Like me, you whose eyelids no longer close all the way know what a pain it is to find something that will keep them closed, avoid drying out and all the painful corneal abrasions that go along with this problem.
Taping one's eyes shut is no easy thing. Having to look at the alarm clock, for example, it is still difficult to peel this tape back, but it is much easier than the next tapes which are made to hold on bandages. Goggles are uncomfortable or can move off, the same with head bandages, which can also leave your hair mushed. Which I guess is a better alternative than corneal abrasions. I'd give five stars if the tape was a bit gentler.

title: Great tape for those that want to go strapless.
text:
Works pretty good and stays all day. I am not new to using kinesiology tape. I am new to using it for my boobs though. I usually use it for my ankle and knee to help with support. The stuff works wonders. Kinesiology tape has a stretch to it. This one is about 3" wide. My sports ones are 2" or 4" wide. The box it came in was damaged and opened. The pasties were laying in the Amazon package. They were individually wrapped so it wasn't a big deal.

It took me a little bit to figure out how to apply correctly and make sure my boobs were symmetrical. I highly recommend watching some you tube videos. I found a one that showed someone applying the tape (and not just talking about it and showing pictures)

Tips:
• don't forget to put the pasties on before the tape. Your nipples will thank you.
• round the corners of the tape to help it from accidently catching on clothes and coming up
• take 2" off the paper backing to start and take the rest of the backing off as you apply. This will help prevent it from sticking to itself. (Just pretend you are ripping the tape. The paper backing will rip and the tape won't)
• if you are having trouble getting the paper off the tape, stretch the tape a little. The paper comes right up.
• for the first 2 inches and last 2 inches don't stretch. Just apply
• for the rest I would only stretch up to 25%.
• rub the tape for 30 seconds after it is applied. This should help the adhesion stick to the skin better.

title: (5 1/2 month update) First time wearing heel protectors … failed at just over 2 miles
text:
[[VIDEOID:fceaf07df1742d003d474a09e5bd82af]] final update: almost 5 1/2 months after first application.

I must say that while I was disappointed that these heel protectors didn't 'glue on' the way I wanted to, I am more than pleased with the longevity of these protectors once they were applied. While I did have to apply some 'touch-up' glue to the protectors a couple of times over the last few months, I did find that these protectors did the main job that were designed to do; that being protecting the heels of my shoes from wearing down as quickly as they would do otherwise. What just happened here recently was that the upper front part of the shoe (where they bend around the toe-line) gave out before the heel protectors worn down to the point where the original heel of the shoe would starting impacting the ground. Without these heel protectors in place, I believe (based on the miles I put on my shoes) that the heels on the shoes would have worn down to replacement level at least one or two months ago. So, I do think these heel protectors work (though they do require some maintenance 'glueing') and am therefore giving the product a couple of extra stars.

update: 2 weeks after first review (see below) ... i completely removed the pads from the tennis/walking/running shoes and then reattached the pads to shoes using a more-than-generous amount of rubber cement (the type used to attach patches to a bike inner-tube). Since that time i've put in excess of 30 miles on the shoes/pads and have had no issues. to me, this indicates that this product --might-- be useful on non-rubber soles, leather for example, but isn't useful on rubber or rubber-like soles like the ones i have on all my tennis/walking/running shoes.

Review of: Miiooan Invisible Shoe Heel Protectors

I’ve found in my experience that the soles of my shoes, especially the heel portion of the bottom of the shoe, normally gives out far before the upper part of my shoes give out; and there have been many times I’ve had to buy a new pair of shoes even though the tops of the shoes were still in good condition.

So, I was really hopeful that by adding these heel protectors I could get some ‘extra time/extra miles’ out of my walking shoes.

What I found, however, was that the very first time I wore shoes with these heel protectors on was that the pads failed right around the 2-mile mark of my planned 6-mile walk on city streets/sidewalks.

To prepare for the first walk, I carefully followed the instructions that came with the heel pads. I used a brand-new pair of tennis shoes/sneakers/walking shoes that had never been worn before, I cleaned the bottom of the shoe (including using rubbing alcohol) and I firmly applied the heels to the bottom of each shoe and I waited 3 days before going on the walk.

After only 2-miles, however, my right foot scrapped across a bit of sidewalk that was slightly raised on one side (by a tree next to the sidewalk) and the front part of the heel pad peeled back and away from the shoe. And, since the glue was ‘hardened’ by that time, the flap of heel pad wouldn’t reattach to the shoe.

What did happen, though, was that the loose flap of heel protector continued to grow to the point where, at right around 2 ½ miles, I had to rip the protector off the shoe just to be able to continue to walk safely down the sidewalk.

And, when I got home and checked the heel protector on the other shoe, I saw that the heel protector on that shoe had also started to pull away from the shoe.

The bottom-line for me is that, in what I consider to be a real-world test of the heel protectors just walking down a city street/city sidewalk, is that one protector failed completely and the second protector was on the verge of failing.

This product, for me, doesn’t come close to getting a passing grade.

title: an average, middle-of-the-road toothpaste when compared to name-brand sensitive toothpastes
text:
Review of: Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for Sensitive Teeth

I’ve been using the Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for the last week or so and, so far at least, I’ve been pleased with the product.

I found that the taste of the toothpaste is actually pretty good, especially in comparison to other ‘fresh mint’ flavored toothpastes I’ve tried before that seem to have an off-taste or bitter after-taste them. The mint taste of the Spotlight is present but not overwhelming; which I like.

The foaming action of the toothpaste I consider to be about average; certainly, enough in my estimation to feel as if the toothpaste was getting to every corner of my mouth but not so much as to be annoying.

The active ingredients I also consider to be about average for a decent quality ‘sensitive’ toothpaste; Potassium Nitrate and Sodium Fluoride. And, after using the product a few times now, I consider the effectiveness (based on the potassium nitrate level of 5.0%) to be about the same as many other ‘sensitive’ toothpastes I’ve tried in the past.

After brushing, the Spotlight toothpaste does leave my teeth feeling clean and does leave my mouth with a nice, somewhat minty taste.

For me, while this toothpaste is noticeably better than some bargain-basement type sensitive toothpastes, it is roughly equal to many quality, name-brand or store-brand toothpastes.

The cost, however, for this 3.5 ounce tube of sensitive toothpaste is a concern for me as I consider it to be on the higher side; especially for what I rate as an average, middle-of-the-road toothpaste.

title: I don’t feel that it is likely that I will try the Sprayzee Shoe Deodorizer a second time
text:
Review of: Sprayzee 100% Natural Shoe Deodorizer & Foot Spray

I’ve tried the Sprayzee Shoe Deodorizer on 3 different pairs of tennis shoes; one pair for general walking around in, another pair for use at the gym and a third pair of shoes I wear out in the garden. And, so far, I’ve come to a couple of conclusions about the Deodorizer.

The first item, and the most obvious, was the aroma of the spray. While the spray promotes itself as some version of mint, to my sense of smell at least, the aroma was closer to being medicinal; something similar to a pine-scented all-purpose, floor cleaner. While I did not find the smell to be even vaguely pleasant another family member mentioned that the smell wasn’t too bad, almost a peppermint-type aroma.

The second thing ‘discovery item’ for me was to realize that I should always use the spray outside. I first tried using the spray in the garage and discovered that the ‘aroma’ of the spray covered the interior of the garage and lingered for at least a day. This, to me, is an indication of the power of the spray which is a plus.

The next item I noticed was that the bottle itself was somewhat difficult to use. The spray nozzle worked fine when positioned upright but didn’t work well, or at all, when positioned sideways or upside down. This meant that I found it hard to spray up inside the body of the shoe without having to manually hold and maneuver the shoe with one hand while spraying with another hand. And, of course, I found that this led to the spray getting on my hands and the ‘aroma’ getting on my hands. And, this in turn, led me to understand that the spray, with it’s unpleasant smell, was not easy to wash off my hands.

Finally, after letting the sprayed shoes sit for a day or so, outside, I determined that the spray had indeed cut down on some of the original foot-odor the shoes had a day earlier; which is what the product is intended to accomplish.

Unfortunately, I found that original odor had been replaced with a odor that was half foot-odor and half pine-scented floor cleaner. To me, that aroma was perhaps a little better than the original smell, but not by much.

I will most likely continue to use the remainder of the product but I don’t feel that it is likely that I will try the Sprayzee Shoe Deodorizer a second time.

title: a convienient 'just-in-case' kit for those unexpected stops when traveling
text:
[[VIDEOID:a87ad8307c2097351858440688a0e620]] Review of: All-in-One Personal Protection Kits |Travel Pack by The Premium Shoppe - (3 Pack)

I try my best to remember, every time I get in the car, to make sure I have a face mask, some gloves and some alcohol wipes with me. That way, if I have to make an unexpected stop, I at least have the minimum ‘equipment’ I need with me.

I could, for a lesser price, throw some separate items in the back of the car, of course, but, for me, I wanted a pre-made kit where each item (glove, mask, wipe) in the kit is individually wrapped and the aluminum-foil wrapped kit is fully sealed. Then, when I find a need to use the items, perhaps months down the line, they will still be useable.

For this review, I opened one of the 3 kits and I found that my ‘want list’ was met by this product. The glove, which to me visually looked to be at least a medium sized glove and appeared to be large enough to be comfortably worn, was individually wrapped. The mask, an adult sized paper mask with elastic loops was also individually wrapped. Included also was two foil wrapped packages with the alcohol hand wipes.

Each item, at least visually, looked like they would serve their intended purpose at least on a short-term basis; which is exactly what I wanted and needed. I may not ever need to use them but, if I do, they will be in the car ready and waiting.

title: Decent quality, one-time use latex gloves that do what I need them to do
text:
Review of: gracosy Disposable Gloves, 100 pcs White Large

I’m pleased with the results I’ve had with the Gracosy disposable gloves. These gloves aren’t anything fancy of course, but I’ve found that for general around-the-house use these gloves will get the job done; and that is exactly what I wanted.

The quality of the gloves is about what I expected for disposable gloves; not super thick but not so thin so they tear super easily. Of course, long nails or rings (etc.), anything with an edge could poke a hole in the gloves but, in my experience, the same could be said for other similar gloves.

The gloves are ‘powder free’, which I prefer, but I found that the gloves were still easy to slip on.

The gloves I tested are listed, on the box, as being a size ‘large’. I normally wear a size small in gloves so, for me, I found the gloves fit very comfortably without having to count on any stretchiness on the gloves. As I prefer gloves that are looser, this fit was fine for me.

As a quick test, for this review, I tested the stretch of the latex gloves by trying to put two hands into a single glove and I found that test worked okay as the glove stretched without tearing. After testing the stretch of the glove, I found that a medium sized hand should fit without too many issues. My test also demonstrated to me that a large size hand, even if the glove doesn’t tear, may find the fit too tight to be comfortable.

For me, the Gracosy gloves are just what I need for working around the house.

title: I’m really pleased with this powder.. I’ve used it on 3 different meals it has enhanced each dish
text:
Review of: Super Organics Red Reishi Mushroom Powder | Healthy Immunity - Organic, Vegan & Non-GMO, 4 Oz

I’m really pleased with this product … I’ve used it with three different meals and the ‘Super Organics – Red Reishi Mushroom Powder’ has enhanced the flavor of each dish.

My first use of the powder was in Turkey Sloppy Joes. As you know, using turkey in any dish and you lose some flavor as opposed to using beef. Adding the mushroom powder amped up the flavor and gave the mixture a deeper, almost beefier taste.

The next use of the powder was as a topping on baked Zucchini. But a tiny amount of olive oil on top of sliced Zucchini … sprinkle on a little mushroom powder and a little Romano cheese powder on the top and then baked … so good. Not only tasty but also healthy for you. Just remember, when using as a vegetable topping to use it sparingly, you don’t want to overwhelm the taste of the Zucchini or overwhelm the taste of the cheese.

The third use of the powder was in Lentils. Add a scope of mushroom powder to the Lentils (after they were cooked) and you can impart a ‘mushroomy’/almost beefy type flavor to the Lentils. Cook the Lentils with some carrots, celery, onions and then add the mushroom powder … scope over some cooked rice and you have a full, delicious meal that even the most strident meat-eater will like.

I haven’t tried it in tea or a smoothie yet … but I am looking at making a stew fairly soon and I know that I’ll be adding this powder to the stew. I’ll need to experiment with the amount of powder to use as a stew needs a heavier/meatier taste than the other meals I’ve made. Oh … and know that I think of it, maybe adding some of this powder to some Zucchini bread would be good. Hey, there are all kinds of options for this powder.

I can’t really comment to heavily on the ‘healthy immunity’ claims on the product page but as this product is organic, vegan, non-gmo and gluten free and doesn’t list any negative ingredients or additives then the product is probably as healthy as fresh mushrooms.

If you want a little extra flavor with your meals then this powder is something you should consider.

title: Impressive quality, functionality and comfort in a knee brace.
text:
Review of: Ancocs Adjustable Knee Braces for Women & Men with Side Stabilizers Breathable Neoprene Open Patella Relieves ACL, PCL, LCL, MCL, Meniscus Tear, Arthritis Cap Pain Knee Brace (Black1)

Upon opening the package I immediately sat down and put on the knee brace.

I have a 13 ½ “ – 14”knee width (using the ‘bent’ knee method described on the product page), so I’m on the lower side of the range; but with the 3 hook&loop fasteners there is still plenty of flexibility to allow for a perfectly tight fit.

Then, I went on a 5 ½ mile walk. I don’t run anymore; no surprise here, my knees don’t ‘take kindly’ to running; but I do enjoy walking as much as I can.

And, I must say, for the entire walk the Ancocs Adjustable knee brace was extremely comfortable. I would never go so far as to say it didn’t feel like I wasn’t wearing anything on my knee, but it was pretty close. Unlike many neoprene-based knee braces, which quickly get soaked by sweat, this knee brace stayed cool for the entire time.

The lateral coils (which is where I need the support), performed their function well and did it with surprising comfort. At no time did I feel any ‘hard mass’ trying to push up against the sides of my knee. Just the right amount of support to do what I need a knee brace to do.

The flexibility, meaning how easy is it to bend the knee when walking, was very good. The shorter, middle hook&loop strap came around enough to keep the brace tight enough but didn’t dig into the back of my knee with every step.

I think this is a product worth trying.

I’ve included some pictures to give you an idea of the overall length of the brace, the size of the individual hook&loop straps and the width of the brace. I’ve also include a picture of the lateral coil ‘stabilizers’.

title: Figured out the problem
text:
Device seemingly stopped working the second day. Then it worked on my forehead. But when. I place the device on my cheeks and jaw, my face won't twitch very much anymore. The manual says for best results use every other day. So could it be possible that my muscles are so tight right now that the twitching stopped for a few days? And maybe after about a day or two my muscles will twitch again? Idk. I also hear that you aren't supposed to use a device with this many amps but once every 24 hours or so. Maybe that's why.

Update: it turns out I was right about the device. I started out on high for the first two days so my muscles needed a break. After researching faradic pulse and muscle contraction, I learned thar poor contractions with the device is because to much lactic acid build up, over worked muscles and or not removing all of the dirt and oil from skin. After resting for two days I used the device today and it works like a charm. Guess I should've followed the manual that says use every other day. I used it for almost 40 minutes on both sides of my face so that was my problem. Couldn't get my face to twitch for two days. Also don't use with wet hands because water can get in the device through the cracks. I'm pleased with it as of now, and it's definitely better than nuface. I used nuface for two years. Problem with nuface is it just retrains your muscles to sit in the old position, which is almost like botox, but it does nothing to build muscle tone.

Second update guys. My face is amazing! The muscles in my face sit up high and there's an increase in volume. At some point I became worried that my face might start looking buff lol. But thata not the case, but I recommend only using the device every other day for two to three weeks and then using twice a week or once a week to keep the tone of your muscles just like if you worked out your body. I'm surprised I like this more than nuface! I didn't get an increase in volume with nuface, the only thing I got was my muscles sat up for a few days. With this you get the lift and the increase in muscle volume. But yeah I wouldn't over do it because you might start looking a little muscular in the face lol. Like around the jaw. And on the side of my face near the jaw i can see a noticeable increase in muscle.

title: Really good Sound Appliance
text:
I have been using various sound appliances for the last 20 years because I am a very light sleeper. My children are also light sleepers and naptime, especially, is problematic because any little sound from another room wakes my little ones up. I have had 2 digital sound appliances go haywire in the last 2 years. We leave them on all the time because we are busy and we don't want to take a chance that we might forget to turn one on in the kids rooms. They start making very loud stuttering, crazy noises which woke my children up! So, I started looking for something different, better.

I seem to have found it with this appliance. I like that it is mechanical, not digital. Who needs or uses rainforest sounds? The idea is to mask outside noises, not have your baby believe he is sleeping in the rainforest! So far this appliance has been very reliable and helpful. My only complaint would be that I would like it to be just a tiny bit louder. I adjusted it to its optimal setting and we just leave it go on a table across the room from the baby's crib and it just fills the room with a soothing, soft sound. Very womb-like!

Next time I purchase another one, I will spend $10 more for the more expensive model in hopes that it will be a little louder. We like to use a sound machine inside the baby's room as well as outside the door. I'm very happy to have found this supplement because my medium/thin naturally curly hair needs help!

Pregnancy does many things to your body and my hair has suffered. Before pregnancy, my hair was full, soft and grew quickly to the middle of my back. During pregnancy, my hair continued to grow and was lush/full; then my son was born and my hair literally fell out in clumps (hormonal imbalance) until I had to cut it all off because there were literally bald spots on my head.

title: Great starter kit or upgrade
text:
I've been using One Touch meters for almost 10 years now and never have had any problems with the meters I've used in the past. So far the readings have always been accurate compared to the ones in the doctor office and my A1c.
But... there were times in the past when I could not afford the strips - at $50 to $100 a pack of strips it wasn't possible. I had to use a different meter with strips that either were affordable or prescribed and covered by my insurance.
Now that there are generic test strips that work with the One Touch meter I am back and happily so.
I was so excited to come back to using One Touch that I bought the whole kit just so I could have a new meter - even though my older one still works well - I have 2 (one to carry with me and one at home).
These strips are very easy to use, need a decent drop of blood and I've only come across an error twice in a month - I test every morning for fastings and again at least once during the day for randoms. I'm T2 and on insulin. Testing is very important to me, especially before injecting insulin.

This meter I'd recommend to others who are also looking for something affordable and a meter that is easy to read - large printout.
The set in this kit is very nice as well - the lancing device is not one of my favorites but it does the job well (I wouldn't recommend to someone who is recently diagnosed though because the lancing device makes such a noise that is intimidating or scary and you can see the lancet move forward to jab you in the finger). The trigger on this lancing device is a little rough and it hurts sometimes for me and I have it on setting #2.... and I inject insulin every day so I'm used to needles.

Overall this is a great starter pack or even an upgrade.

title: It works!
text:
All my life I've struggled with my weight. I have a borderline thyroid issue & losing weight is an absolute battle for me.
I've gone on the carb counting, low fat eating plans & even cut out sugars, most processed foods & started an exercise regime. Still no weight loss. In fact, the more I tried to lose, the more weight I gained. The moment I would stop eating on a restricted eating plan the weight would come back double.

Well, here I am now telling everyone out there that this stuff works. I have been on diet pills, carb blockers, fat blockers... you name it. I've downed the shakes, tried the bars... Nothing worked for me like this product does.

I ordered this pack with the 2 shakers & starter pack of the powdered drink. I keep one shaker in my purse, and the other right next to the salt shaker at home. Everything I eat I sprinkle Sensa on. Be creative, sometimes you have to be. :) Stick to it, because if you don't sprinkle every time you will fall out of the habit.

Right away I noticed my appetite was shrinking. The very first weeks are hard, that I will tell you. I was hungry just an hour after eating & would again eat a little more (still sprinkling) and feel bad because I was still eating when this product said it would curb my appetite. I stuck to it. Day after day I continued to sprinkle Sensa on everything I ate & I do watch to make sure that I am not putting too much unhealthy food into my body.
The first week I lost 1 pound. Well, to some that is nothing, but to me when I have not been able to lose anything, but instead continue to gain weight one pound is great!

My advice is to stick to it. Sprinkle on everything. Watch what you eat, this won't work if you are stuffing your plate with junk food all day, sprinkling this on cake for breakfast & pizza, a burger & fries for lunch. Be sensible with what you feed your body. Get in the habit of always using this. I even ordered the chews to help out in between meals & really they are just the right amount of sweet to keep my sugar cravings down & they do work to curb appetite. The chews are super soft, easy to chew & not like taffy or anything that will stick to your mouth. The chocolate are like a tootsie roll & the berry ones are like a starburst. It also helps to drink the powdered mix in between meals, just to help fill you up & it offers a little bit of energy from the B complex vitamins in it.

Consider what diet pills have in them, and if you go on a restricted diet, you will put on all the weight back once you stop. This is so simple. Sprinkle it on what you eat, and that's it. No harsh chemicals, no side affects.

I'm learning now that it takes time to take the weight off & honestly I have 50 pounds to loose, and every time I get on that scale and see one more pound gone, instead of gained I am elated. No matter how slowly Sensa takes to help me take this weight off, I will continue to use this, because it is the only thing that has helped me lose weight.

Hopefully it will work for you too.

title: Very happy to have found this product, great job Julian Bakeries!
text:
***2017 Update***

After looking at a lot of protein powders from various different sources, eggs, meat, vegetables, milk, etc...I chose this one.

Below are the reasons:

-U.S. Based manufacturing and ingredient source, some powders are produced outside the U.S. and I have read there is metal or other contamination that can occur. Though I did not confirm this I assume U.S. based products would not have this issue or are safer than non-U.S. products.
-No filler ingredients, this is literally powder egg whites, which by default are a whole/natural protein source. Other powders have so much weird un-pronouncable "stuff" in them that you don't even know what your taking or how accurate the claims are.
-Non-GMO and no antibiotics used on chickens
-Eggs are cooked and not air dried (this prevents a avidin health issue), they are also pasteurized. This was confirmed by calling Julian Bakery's in California and an email to their nutritionist.
-No Soy, no Lactose! Large amounts of soy diets can cause hormonal issues for both men and women. Avoid soy proteins! I am also lactose intolerant so pure egg protein is great.
-Price per. protein comes to 30 g per. dollar., really good rate compared to other products out there.
-Low calories, basically you are taking in calories only for the protein not other fillers (e.g., sugars), it is about 4.32 calories per. protein
-The expiration dates are very reasonable, my two bags are about 2 year + to expiration.

-One con is that it does have a lot of salt (381 mg per serving), so if you are sensitive to it, or this is something you watch, it is something to keep in mind

One thing that stuck out is that the empty scoop weighs 9 grams and filled it is 34 grams, I am not sure why this is, maybe they are rounding the servings to a nice number. Technically each scoop has 25 grams (34 grams minus 9 grams) of powder, which i hopefully means it is 25 g of protein and additional 5 grams is just rounding since serving size is 30 grams.

***CORRECTION*** I realized that the scoop measures close to 30 grams, but its impossible to design something to pick up the exact amount of powder every single time, you will need a scale if you want exactly 30 grams every time, or just live with the fact you will scoop anywhere from 25-30 grams.

Overall good product and one of the best I found. The taste is so-so, that means it won't make you puke, but it isn't like ice-cream. It's just plain. I am in the middle of my first bag. Before protein powders became a fad and different brands/recipes went out on the market, in the 90's eggs were considered to be the best source of pure complete protein (i believe it still is). I am comfortable with putting this in my body over a long period of time on a daily basis due to its very very short ingredient list.

Please always consult a doctor before changing your diet or exercise program. I am not a doctor and nothing here is offered as health advice. Please as always verify everything once you receive the product or before you buy.

title: Good Quality Sound Machine, Just Not For Me...
text:
Very good quality sound machine with a few drawbacks. My wife and I have been using sound machines, air purifiers, and/or fans since we were both children. I have never been able to sleep well without some sort of white noise in the background. We had been using a homedics machine (sorry can't recall the model) for about 10 years - and had been reasonable satisfied. However, I had wanted to buy this machine for years and found it on sale for ~ $35 after Christmas last year (on Prime!) - I couldn't resist.

After reading all the great reviews I had very high expectations - my fault. I say this because I was disappointed with the sound machine. I anticipated the sound manipulations will really help me select an optimal background sound - it did not. First, there is no true volume control - you can adjust the volume by limiting the size of the wholes, but only within a pretty tight range; there is no way to limit the volume to a low level. Second, the sound was all in the same style, we did not find changing the sound to make any real difference on whether the sound would be pleasing. It was hit-or-miss, just like any other $20 sound machine.

We also take our sound machine when we travel; however, we had always balked at the size of the machine. The Dohm sound machine is smaller in size than the previous Homedics, however, it is much heavier - there is no way we could travel with it.

Despite the negatives (some subjective), I did not want to take away more than one star from Dohm sound machine. The assembly/build are great and the sound is consistent and I'm sure very good for users that like the tone. I'm just not one of them.

title: Ineffective, overpriced, not very solid-looking
text:
I frequently go swing dancing and sometimes the bands and/or DJs play unsafely loud. For hearing protection I've been using [[ASIN:B01IBT7R48 Flents Quiet Please Foam Earplugs Nrr 29dB - 50 Pair Hearing Protection with a Clear Plastic Travel Jar]], highly effective but I don't like poofy things sticking out a bit from my ears. I thought by spending oodles more on these I would magically get the same level of hearing protection without the unsightly foam poking out. I was quite wrong, these are only rated for 18dB (printed on the package but suspiciously not disclosed on the product description on the webpage), better than nothing but not enough in my view for hearing protection in nightclubs, and they did not fit well in my ears, so I was probably getting only about half that. So back to the poofy things for me.

At $13.95, this is probably the most overpriced thing I've bought at Amazon, I would say this product would not justify even half that cost. Further, the plugs do not give me the impression of being solidly built, and I would be concerned over time about the stem or other parts breaking off while pulling the plugs out from the ear canal, requiring a doctor's visit to dislodge remaining remnants from the ear.

title: Work great for precise mixing and reusable.
text:
I use these to measure 2 cycle oil for small 8 ounce batches that I make when doing yard work. I have both 50:1 and 40:1 trimmers.

I did the math and found 4.81 milliliters gets me the 50:1 mix with 8 ounces of gas, and 5.91 milliliters gets 40:1 with 8 ounces of gas. Allows very precise and clean mixing. I use an empty Seafoam can or similar as the screw cap seals well and to avoid having lots of unused 2 cycle mix sitting around going stale. I use a measuring cup with funnel to get 8 ounces of gas spot on from my gallon container.

50:1 requires 2.6 ounces of 2 cycle oil per 1 gallon of gas. 8 ounces is 1/16 of a gallon. Divide 2.6 by 16 to get 0.1625 ounces of 2 cycle oil. Convert ounces to milliliters and you get 4.81.

I used the same formula for 40:1, substitute 3.2 ounces, divide by 16, get 0.2 ounces, convert to milliliters and get 5.91. Ratios stay the same and my trimmers are happy.

title: Lifesavers during the first trimester
text: My wife and I are pregnant with our first child. During the first trimester, she struggled with morning sickness (honestly sickness all throughout the day) quite a bit. Especially when she would wake up. But also when she would see one of her food aversions, smell something that made her queasy, or sometimes just while sitting on the couch for no reason at all. These little lifesavers were awesome! She kept a couple in her purse, and in her pockets when she didn't have the purse and would pop one in at the first sign of nausea. They really lessened the severity of most of her episodes, if not staved them off completely on several occasions. The ginger flavor was evident, but not as strong as she was expecting and more than tolerable. She actually doesn't like ginger flavored things, but the creamy texture and natural flavoring toned it down plenty. I would highly recommend these to any woman that is considering trying them for nausea related to pregnancy just based on my wife's praises of them.

title: These are strong, comfortable to hold and come in fun colors!
text:
I'm an ER nurse and can tell you how big of a difference good quality vs bad quality scissors are. For the first year of my job I had cheap scissors. I couldn't cut splinting material, clothes off patients or anything else thicker than paper. I've owned about 5 pairs of scissors over the last 7 years as a nurse and can attest to quality.

Princess Care Scissors:
These are great scissors. Just 3 days ago I cut jeans off a trauma patient. They cut like butter through the pant legs, the belt area that has multiple layers of material required a little more pressure, but they cut through it fairly easily. My coworker who was getting the other side was only halfway up that pant leg when I got done. After she asked where I got my scissors. I have used these for fiberglass splinting material and they work like a champ with that as well. I cut through a thick stack of post its as well for a picture demonstration.

Why trauma shears?:
In case you're not familiar with trauma shears they are bent for a safer, more convenient cutting angle. There is a flat area on the tip that sits against the skin, so there's little chance of actually cutting skin if held parallel to the skin. There's also no sharp tip that could puncture the skin. They are handy for first aid kits and anyone in the medical field or anyone doing home wound care.

Sizes:
These come in two sizes. The 7.5" is what I recommend for ER and EMS, it's what I'm holding in the post it pictures and the 3rd picture. It can accommodate my thumb in the top, pointer finger in the divot stabilizing the scissors and my last 3 fingers pushing to get a strong cut. The 5.5" are great for cutting bandaging and light clothes, it's what I'm holding in the last picture. It takes longer to cut clothes off since the blade is a little shorter and the handle smaller, which in a trauma or cardiac/respiratory arrest seconds are valuable. With the smaller one my thumb fits in the top, my pointer stabilizes them and my 3rd and 4th fingers go in the bottom loop. My pinky is free. This slightly decreases the force I can use in cutting. If you're debating sizes I would go with the bigger, but that's just my bias I guess. When I pull them out of my "holster" I guess I'd call it (a hemostat on my shirt with tape around the top and scissors put in the tape hole). The larger ones just go right on my hand, the smaller it takes a few extra seconds to position with my fingers in the right spot. .

Overall, I love these trauma shears. Out of all the sets I've owned these are tied for first place for my favorite. I had a pair of black on black that I loved as well, but I left them at work one day and they disappeared. These cut just as well as those. Remember to label your scissors! They get lost/stolen very easily and in work settings a lot of people have the same/similar shears. Princess Care sent me a few sets for testing and review purposes. I never let that influence how I rate or review products. I always use products and evaluate them honestly based on their quality and function. These are just great shears that are doing a wonderful job.

title: Changed my life
text:
I have to say that the Bodybugg changed my life. After I had my daughter I was overweight for 3 years, just couldn't get the baby weight off. I worked at a gym and was exercising, but it just wasn't all coming together. The Bodybugg helped me so much! The basis of it is calories in versus calories out.

It's simple mathematics. Every pound of fat is equal to 3,500 calories. So either you have to eat that much less or work that much off. Some people can just decide to work out a little more and lose weight, but that wasn't working for me. For me the Bodybugg motivated me so much by being able to see the numbers. I decided I wanted to lose a pound a week, so I needed a 500 calorie per day deficit. If I worked out a lot and burned 3,000 calories a day I could eat a lot. If I was a couch potato and only burned 1,800 calories I was only able to eat 1,300 that day. Anyway, seeing it all in numbers and graphs helped A LOT!

The Bodybugg isn't for someone looking for an easy way to lose weight. If you aren't committed to spending a lot of time on it, it probably won't work. In order to do it and be really successful you need to know almost exactly how many calories you are eating. That means weighing your food. It's a pain to do. I was weighing my chicken, pasta, fruit, veggies, cereal... everything basically. I packed all my lunches and snacks and logged them before I left my house. If I was out and got a snack I put the calories in my phone and logged it when I got home. It's time consuming and hard, but completely worth it. For about 6 months I did this religiously and lost 40 pounds. I am still down around my goal. Sometimes I put my Bodybugg on for a couple weeks if I need a little kick in the butt. I've recommended it to a few friends and unfortunately most of them didn't have the patience ortime to do the calorie counting necessary to be successful. I try to warn everyone how difficult it is and how you have to be prepared to weigh and count everything you eat, even condiments. If done right though, I think it's the best tool on the market.

title: Always reliable and prefer the powder over the pods
text:
I have used Cascade powder for years and it always provides nice and consistently clean dishes. There is nothing that I abhor more than to happily pluck a glass that I think is clean out of the dishwasher only to find that it has a scummy white powder film on it left over from dishwasher detergent. Such an occurrence really sends my OCD into overdrive and I have to rewash the entire load to be sure that the film has entirely washed away from my dishes. Now, I can't say that this has NEVER happened with Cascade in terms of leaving a gritty film behind, but it has happened a lot less than with some other competing brands that I have tried, so I keep coming back to Cascade simply because it provides a reliably clean result.

My other advice is to stick with the Cascade powder. I made the mistake of buying the pods a few times and I would open the dishwasher after it was done cycling and never know if I would find that the entire pod disolved as it should into the water or whether I would find a mangled, half dissolved pod sadly resting at the bottom of my dishwasher, which meant less than clean dishes.

I know that there are far more important choices in life than dishwasher detergent but if you buy the Cascade you can sleep at night knowing that your dishes will be wind up coming out of the dishwasher far less gritty than they would be if you used another detergent, and dare I say, they may even be shockingly clean!

title: VERY Uncomfortable Eye Massager that Caused me Multiple Headaches!
text:
This Eye Massager comes with a heat function, Bluetooth, as well as built in speaker that plays prerecorded sounds from the unit. The eye massager gives audible voice commands letting you know what the current program is being played at the time. You can also use the Bluetooth mode to play your own music you’ve got on your cell phone or other supported device you might have.

The eye massager part that sits around your eye sockets and forehead is made out of silicone “nodes” that’s “suppose” to feel good. I didn’t find the silicone to feel comfortable at all around my eye sockets! To me the silicon is way to hard! On the outside of the eye massager you’ll find a LED Screen that’s pretty easy to operate. The screen shows your current working mode, heat, battery power, and Bluetooth or current music you’ve got set up to play.

This eye massager comes with an adjustable strap to fit it to your head. The description claims this unit is light weight, However, it’s Bulky as well as heavy once you’ve got it strapped to your head/face. The battery life seems pretty good as it hasn’t gone down much with multiple uses. The eye massager charges with a Type-C cable(included) which is pretty standard nowadays with a lot of items.

I had to adjust the head strap of this eye massager multiple times trying to find the best fit that didn’t cause pain prior to even using it. In order to try to help take some of the weight off of my face while wearing this eye massager I reclined in my chair. Doing that does help take the pressure and weight off your nose but in order to obtain any actual pressure around your eye sockets you’ve got to make the head strap tight. If the head strap isn’t tight on your head the massage “nodes” don’t even touch the area around your eye sockets! By making the strap so tight to even begin use of this eye massager, it begins with pain and discomfort before you even start using it, DEF NOT IDEAL!

Once the eye massager is on, you’ve got to use a finger to try to navigate to the small button on the unit (which you can’t see since your eyes are covered) to push to turn on the device. Once you stumble around to locate the start button and then press it, the massager will tell you what mode you’re on. The volume for that function is LOUD! I was never able to find where, or if, there’s a volume button to either mute that loud voice or at least turn it down! Then comes the “built in music” or “peaceful built in sounds”. I found none of the built in music or built in sounds peaceful at all. The sounds only play for a few seconds and then all you hear is the gears of the “nodes” turning and grinding, DEF NOT PEACEFUL!

I gave this eye massager Multiple try’s to get use to it as well as to try to enjoy using it. After using this eye massager for the first TWO TIMES within ten minutes of being finished I got Bad Headaches! For the next Four Times of use over a couple of days the headaches weren’t as bad after using it but I did still got headaches, that’s def NOT Peaceful or Comfortable at all for anyone!

There’s no way I could ever recommend this eye massager to anyone until there’s some improvements to what all I’ve mentioned in this review. I REALLY wanted this eye massager to work for me and I put myself through a LOT of Discomfort trying to get to that point, but my experience with this eye massager Never Improved at all! Also, the “nodes” left red marks around my eye sockets even when I didn’t tighten the head strap much at all!
