title: Very accurate measurements, but does require some practice.
text:
I participate in fitness competitions so knowing my body composition is crucial to structuring my diet properly and ensuring my training is effective. For the past few years I've had DXA scans or BodPod measurements every 6 months to get a good picture of how I was progressing. After doing a lot of research into using ultrasound for body composition analysis, I decided to try the BodyMetrix. It costs about the same as three DXA scans and I figured if it was even remotely accurate, it would be well worth the investment.

=== The equipment ===
The BodyMetrix device was surprisingly light but the construction is very good. It comes with a small 2 fluid ounce bottle of ultrasound gel. At the rate I was using gel, I'll probably order a large refill. There are a number of 5 liter containers for about $20 here on Amazon. The software is downloaded from their website so there's no CD provided in the box.

=== User profile ===
Creating a user profile is a very simple. Entering your name, gender, height, weight, and "Athletic Type" is easy enough. The Mac software didn't allow me to edit any of this after the profile was created, so I had to make a few profiles while I tested to see which Athletic Type gave me the most accurate measurements. Note: The Windows version allows you to manage and delete profiles.

=== Single points / body fat calculations ===
I quickly learned that getting good images and measurements with the BodyMetrix does require some practice. My first attempt said I was 15.5% body fat, but after practicing spot measurements for about an hour I was able to consistently get estimates of 8.3% which is about what my last DXA scan estimated as well. I recommend using lots of gel and be sure the devices makes good contact at a 90° angle to the skin. Many of my poor measurements were due to being slightly off 90°.

The software provides a number of formulae to estimate body composition with varying margins of error. I found the Jackson & Pollock 7-site equation gave me the best estimate. There are new equations being developed and published in scientific/medical journals that I'd like to be able to try, but maybe in a future software update.

=== Image scans ===
Taking image scans requires a lot more practice. Again, lots of gel and good 90° contact will give you great results. There are a few settings that will need some adjusting in order to get an ideal image:

Intensity: Similar to contrast in photos, it makes light areas more white and dark areas more black. This can help in defining interfaces between muscle, fat, and bone. You do lose finer details, though, such as inter-muscular fat distribution.

Maximum Thickness: This adjusts how much depth of the scan is shown in the image (10mm - 100mm). Lower thickness means you can see smaller features near the surface and higher thickness shows deeper features but compresses smaller features so they're not visible.

Scan Speed: The device creates an image as a series of single slices. Lower scan speeds makes each slice one pixel wide (good for large areas such as the entire quadricep) and higher speeds make the slices about 6 pixels wide (good for small areas such as the bicep). There's some skill required in gauging how fast to move the device relative to the scan speed in order to get a well-proportioned image.

=== Summary ===
The BodyMetrix was well worth my investment as I found it's accuracy to correlate very strongly with a recent DXA scan. The Mac software isn't as good as it could be, but it does the job. The Windows version is much better - it allows for very fast measurements and more options for data analysis. I highly recommend watching all the videos on IntelaMetrix's YouTube channel as they show exactly how to take all the measurements. Plan to spend a few hours getting a feel for how the device works and you'll be able to take reproducible measurements very easily and consistently.

Overall I'm very excited in how the BodyMetrix will help me get into peak condition for upcoming competitions as well as monitoring my progress in the off-season.

title: An unworthy successor to the original Rayovac PS3 Universal Charger
text:
This charger offered here ([[ASIN:B003D7LHKO Rayovac Platinum AA/AAA/C/D/9V Universal Battery Charger]]) is the PS20PL. It is inferior to the original [[ASIN:B003KLYVNI Rayovac PS3 Universal Smart Battery Charger]] in many ways:

- The PS20PL is a timer-based dumb charger. It blindly charges all batteries for 8.5 hours and shuts off, regardless of their capacity or status. It is up to you to remove your batteries after certain number of hours to avoid over-charging. The PS3 is a smart charger that monitors each cell during charging, and stops automatically when each cell is full.

- The PS20PL forces you to charge in pairs (either 2 or 4 cells). The old PS3 charges batteries individually, which is the only way to ensure each battery is charged to its correct capacity.

- The PS20PL can only handle NiMH and NiCd batteries. The old PS3 can handle NiMH, NiCd, and rechargeable alkaline manganese (RAM) batteries.

On the other hand, both PL20PL and PS3 suffer from the following deficiencies:

- The maximum battery capacity is limited to 3000mAh. That means they cannot fully recharge higher capacity C and D cells, such as the [[ASIN:B0041TF5KQ Tenergy Centura C Size Low Self-Discharge Rechargeable Batteries]] (4000mAh).

- The AC transformer inside is bulky, heavy, and limited to 110V supply only.

Instead of this PS20PL, you should get a smarter universal charger that can handle larger capacity batteries. For example, consider the [[ASIN:B006OSQALU Tenergy Advanced Universal Charger TN190]]. The TN190 added a REFRESH function and a LCD battery status display. It is able to work from 100-240V AC, and can handle higher-capacity batteries up to 10,000mAh.

title: Fun little gadget - limited practical values
text:
This item ([[ASIN:B003EW82ZG T-5000 Hybrid Solar Battery Charger AA NiMH USB Power]]) looks like a versatile product. It is very compact (same size as a deck of playing cards), and offers multiple functions. You can:

1. Use it as a solar-powered charger: to recharge two internal AA NiMH cells under direct sunlight
2. Use it as an USB-powered charger: to recharge internal AA cells from an USB port
3. Use is as an USB power source: to recharge cell phone or other gadgets from internal AA cells

Upon closer examinations, however, each function turns out to be poorly implemented:

1. The solar panel is quite small (4x7cm). Even under direct sunlight at noon time, with the panel perpendicular to the sun beam, the maximum charging current is just 100mA. In real life it will take about 3 sunny days to fully recharge a pair of 2100mAh cells. The case is not weather-resistant, so it should not be left in the open. But when I placed it under the windshield of my car, the charging current dropped by 50% because the glass is UV-filtered.

2. When powered from an USB port, the two internal AA cells are continuously being charged at about 125mA. The problem is there is no 'charging done' signal. The little green LED simply remains on forever, even when there are no batteries inserted. You have to unplug the USB cable after about 20 hours, to prevent over-charging of internal batteries.

3. When used as a USB power source, the 5V output it generates is limited to 300mA max., which is lower than the 500mA from a normal USB port. I have used it successfully to recharge my [[ASIN:B0024FAC16 Philips GoGear Aria MP3 Player]] and my Motorola W755 cell phone. However, if you want to use it to recharge a higher-power device (such as any smart phone or internet tablet), 300mA is just not sufficient.

In summary, the T-5000 Solar charger is still a reasonable value if you can use it as a cell-phone charger. But it is not practical as a solar charger during hiking trips, because the case is not weather-resistant. For smaller size and less weight, you could bring an extra set of [[ASIN:B00003IEME Lithium AA Battery]].

By the way, if you need a solar charger and battery pack that can provide at least 1000mA output current, consider the [[ASIN:B005ZSSBYY Opteka BP-SC4000]] instead.

title: Keep Thomas Edison's good name away from this trash!
text:
The product description of this item ("ReNu It Battery Renewer") sounds just like those trashy commercials seen on late-night TV. It makes outrageous claims that are either half-truth or flat-out lies, just to separate the viewer from his money.

For example, it says:
"Thomas Edison first invented the Principle of the ReNu-It Technology over 75 years ago. He understood that an alkaline battery could be renewed, simply by cleaning the cells"

Fact check: Modern single-use Alkaline battery was invented in 1949, but Thomas Edison died in 1931!

For another example, it says:
"Bring life back to disposable batteries up to 100 times and enhance new batteries up to 15%!"

Fact check: The claim of "up to 100 times" is only possible if you never let the disposable cell runs lower than 1.4V at its terminals. That means you can only use around 20% of the battery capacity each time, before recharging it again. An exhausted disposable cell can never be brought back to its original capacity. Furthermore, the capacity drops with each subsequent deep discharge/recharge cycle. At best, you can get maybe one dozen cycles out of it, before its capacity becomes too low to be useful. At worst, the cell may start leaking electrolyte after just a few cycles, and ruin your battery-operated appliance. You have been warned!

Just in case you still want to experiment with recharging alkaline cells, here is my suggestion: Get the [[ASIN:B000A0IL9C Rayovac Universal Battery Charger]] instead. It is a very versatile unit designed to handle multiple battery chemistries (NiCd, NiMH, and rechargeable alkaline). That way, if recharging alkaline does not work for you, at least you can still use this charger for other rechargeable battery types.

This is a very different toner than I've ever used previously. I've used toners that claimed to be non-drying, but my experience has been that they always were, even to a lesser degree than others, in the end.

This toner, however, has not once left my skin feeling dry or tight.

When you get it, the appearance is a bit off-putting. The toner separates, and you can see the clay floating. You shake it up, put a bit on your hand and apply to your face. The toner is so opaque, I really expected to see the clay residue on my skin, but I have not. It dries quickly, leaving my skin looking clear, clean, and feeling soft.

title: Stale and/or Moldy
text:
Unlike others, I received two packs of each flavor in this bundle.

Having been delighted with the plain green pea crisps purchased at a local store, and then rather pleasantly surprised by the Wasabi Ranch flavor, that I got by accident at the same store, I decided to try more flavors, and ordered this bundle.

I opened the Tomato Basil Lentil packet first. Either the packet was stale, which seems likely as I tried the others later, or truth in advertising is not this company's strong suit. I could not taste tomato, although tomato powder and extractive of tomato are both listed in the ingredients panel. I also could not taste basil, but that is less surprising, as it is not actually listed in the ingredients for the "tomato basil seasoning" --- unless, that is, it is one of the un-named "natural flavors." What I could taste was paprika and garlic and salt --- not an unpleasant taste, but certainly not "tomato basil."

So, a few days later, after finishing off that first packet, I tried the Onion Thyme flavored lentil crisps. Yech! Moldy-tasting! Awful! There were undertones of onion under the overwhelming moldy taste, but I spit it out too quickly to detect any thyme. I may get brave enough to try the second packet of these, but I may not.

Then I tried the plain Green Pea crisps, and I'm going to vote for stale. These had nowhere near the fresh green pea taste of the original, locally-purchased ones ... flat and near-tasteless ... sad ....

I don't know if it is the seller's supplying stale crisps, or Amazon's handling of them during distribution (although I have generally been quite pleased with Amazon-distributed foodstuffs), but these just don't measure up.

title: Simple and effective--you control the pressure and it soothes muscles
text: A few weeks ago, my calf muscle was feeling really tight. I did multiple stretches and held the stretches for minutes at a time. I massaged my calf with my hands, but I couldn't get the tight feeling to go away. A couple hours after trying to stretch that feeling out-- I ripped my calf muscle when I went to jump. So I looked into what I could have done to prevent that and a muscle roller stick was recommended. I bought this muscle roller stick to help specifically with my calf muscles, and it has worked like a charm. After working out, I roll my calf muscles and that releases the tight feeling. Since using this roller stick, I have not had any problems with my calves and I can always get relief from the tightness. I also like using this roller stick on my whole body. It feels nice on my thighs after working out and my back after a long day. It is a very simple product, but it works better than I thought it would. The roller stick is a great way to massage yourself and you can adjust the pressure to your liking. I am very happy with this product. It does have a slight squeak to it, but I didn't really notice it until I read other reviews for it. It doesn't bother me at all. title: It works!
text:
I have used this treatment 5 times over a 7 day period and it does work! My teeth have whitened 2-3 shades already.

Here's how I've been using the product. When I first received it, I had to mold the trays to my teeth. The trays are exactly the same as a sports mouth guard. I boiled a pot of water on the stove then dropped the first tray in for 10 seconds. I used tongs to get it out of the water, which was a mistake because the tongs cause the sides of the tray to fold over one another and mold together before I could get it in my mouth. They were so fused together that I couldn't even try to remold them. Luckily, they give you three trays, one is an extra just for this sort of mishap! I only left the next two trays in the water for 5 seconds so they wouldn't be quite so soft and was able to get a decent mold out of them. Not perfect, because I sucked them onto my teeth too hard and ended up sucking a lot of the plastic mold onto the roof of my mouth instead of the sides of teeth, but good enough!

I used the product 5 nights out of 7. I used about .5 ml of the whitening solution out of the syringe in each tray (so 1 ml total). I wore the trays for about 20 minutes each time and used the LED light for about 5-10 minutes each time. You have to hold the light in your mouth and I'm a habitual multi-tasker, so it killed me not to have the use of both my hands, that's why I didn't use it for the full 20 minutes. I imagine if I had, that I would have had even better results because the LED light acts as an accelerator for the whitening. After the 20 minutes were up, I just removed the trays from my mouth, washed them out with warm water in the sink, and rinsed my mouth out with cold water.

The trays feel very comfortable in my mouth. My teeth were not sensitive to the solution at all, however, it would cause my tongue to tingle if any dripped onto it. The only thing that bothered me a bit was that there is really no way to avoid some of the whitening solution seeping into your mouth. The directions say not to swallow any of it, so I was trying very hard not to. However, as I was salivating, it would wash to the back of my throat and I would ultimately swallow some of it. So I started just spitting onto a paper towel anytime saliva would back up in my mouth to avoid swallowing any. I'm sure if you swallow a tiny bit of it, it's no big deal, but I was trying not to.

My teeth have gotten very yellowed because I am constantly drinking coffee and tea. I have two small children, so caffeine is my lifeline. Unfortunately, it has been ruining my teeth. The Dreow whitening kit is helping me to get my nice white smile back and I am going to continue using it until my teeth are bright white again!

I would definitely recommend this product as it is easy to use and it definitely works!

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest review. These opinions are 100% my own and have not been influenced in any way. I am in no way obligated to leave a positive review.

title: Purity, Potency, Taste, Value---Carlson's IS the Finest, Hands-Down
text:
This fish oil is amazing for many reasons.

Taste: To me, it tastes and smells exactly like fresh-squeezed lemon juice. Light texture, clean, very nice right off the spoon. Best when chilled.
Purity: Has a five-star rating for purity and potency with the IFOS. (Go to IFOS.com to check the listing).
Potency: One little teaspoonful has a whopping 1,600mg of omega-3, at 800 EPA and 500 DHA, plus 300mg of other omega-3s.
Convenience: I much prefer a teaspoonful of this oil once a day than multiple softgels that might cause fish burpiness. I just take it in the morning before breakfast and it's great.
Vitamin E: Added for preserving the oil, and to counteract any loss that you might have from processing the omega-3s. Just 10IU, so not excessive.
Natural triglyceride form: Carlson's molecularly distills this oil for purity, but does not concentrate it, thus it is left in its natural form. Nordic Naturals does the same thing with their liquid omega-3 (not the Ultimate Omega version). It works.

All in all, the Finest in cost, quality, taste.

Great value: Even at full retail price, this liquid is hands-down the most omega-3 for your money.

Are the weights / body fat consistent? Nope. All of that time and frustration because I thought it would be fun to have this sync up with my fitbit app. Absolutely not worth it.

EDIT: 2.28.17
Don't buy this piece of garbage. Not only did I have the issues noted above but twice in the past year, TWICE, the scale has arbitrarily, spontaneously stopped syncing. There were no changes to the network or the scales position in the house. It just stops communicating with the network at which time we have to deal with the horrid Aria tech support. title: Great alternative to the flattening iron!
text: I am very please with the Apalus Brush Hair Straightener.  I received it promptly and it was properly packaged.  It comes with a handy, little tote bag to use for travel (which I have already used) and it is very practical.  The design of the straightener is very sleek and modern.  It straightened my hair yet still leaving a natural look to it.  The brush does get HOT so be aware when using it.  This seems to get underestimated because it is a 'brush' and not a flattening iron!  The reason I am not giving it a five-star is because my hair would get caught in the 'bristles' which are actually a type of 'rubbery' material.  The straightener is also somewhat heavy to the hand, but may be a higher quality outer-surface in order to prevent burns?  I recommend this straightener definitely. I used a heat protector on my hair and I liked it better than a flattening iron.  If you want your hair bone-straight, this is not for you!  It does get rid of the unruly hair without frying your hair.  Get it - you won't be sorry you did!

title: health bar with tons of fiber
text:
I have a gnu bar practically every day and they are by far my favorite bar. They only have 140 calories and four grams of fat (unlike a lot of bars that have so many calories and fat that they should only be eaten as a meal and not a snack). Plus, they have 12 grams of fiber! Yes, 12 grams - or half the amount of fiber you need per day. These bars can help if you find you're not eating at least five servings of fruit/veggies a day. Plus, the fiber is good for your health and very filling.

They're great for breakfast or for a snack. I tend not to have the espresso chip unless I don't have coffee in the morning, as the bar has caffeine in it.

The only reason I gave the bar a lower rating is that the cinnamon raisin and peanut butter are OK, but kind of boring in taste. The Lemon Ginger has quite a bit of flavor, but is not to my liking.

I'd recommend the chocolate brownie[[ASIN:B000W0CHQI Gnu Foods - Gnu Bar Chocolate Brownie, 16 bar]], espresso chip[[ASIN:B003A8SY98 Gnu Foods - Gnu Bar Espresso Bars, 16 bar]], and orange cranberry[[ASIN:B000VZENSE Gnu Foods - Gnu Bar Orange Cranberry, 16 bar]]. I think anyone would probably find the first two tasty. (I gave them five stars.) The orange cranberry is not for everyone. I love it because it reminds me of the orange rind candy my Grandmother used to make. If you don't like kumquats, you probably wouldn't like the orange flavor.

Note, they are recommended by Weight Watchers and Hungrygirl.

It's much cheaper to buy them on Amazon than to buy them in the store.

title: Didn't Sync Consistently, Now Not at All - Totally Fed Up
text: Bought this scale on 2/17/2017. It took several tries to get it to connect to our wifi. After that, for months, the transmissions were inconsistent. Sometimes, the sync would work right away but often, it would fail at first, and then catch up later in the same day. There were times it didn't sync properly for up to three days, but then would miraculously catch up again even on the older data.  Finally, after all those months of inconsistency, the Aria started to more consistently behave as advertised. We almost forgot about how poor it had been. Sorry to say, that didn't last. About a month ago, it stopped connecting to our wifi at all.  We tried everything we knew or could find on the web. We finally called Fitbit Aria support. "Oh," the support person said, "Comcast has changed the protocol; that's the problem." He told me to call Comcast and tell them what protocol was needed for the Aria. I called. Comcast complied with the specified protocol change, but the Aria still wouldn't connect. Again, we called Aria support and spent nearly two hours on the phone with a woman who tried hard but really didn't know what to do to solve the problem. After the call, the Aria didn't sync, but then it synced properly the next morning.  We thought it was fixed. No. That was the last time it synced. It's been three weeks and three days now of not connecting to our wifi. I see it "spins" its little heart out but with no success. We're fed up. We have ordered a competitor's scale that promises to work with our Fitbit Charge 2's. We'll see. With all the complaints about the Aria online, it appears that Fitbit is selling a scale they know will not consistently work properly. That's a bit of arrogance, isn't it?!! If the product doesn't work properly, quit trying to dupe your customers - just stop selling it.

title: figured it would be a great starter one
text:
This is a review of the ChiTronic 82344 5 in 1 Multi Function Facial Care Massager – Scrubber.

Summary – My daughter has asked for one of these and she is at an age in where she does not require an expensive model or one with a ton of thrills. When I saw this for such a cheap price, figured it would be a great starter one.

In terms of build, this does have a nice and seems sturdy in terms of the case. It operates on two AA batteries which are cheap and common. The switch changes from a low to high speed and you get a total of 5 heads for various functions.

The first head comes installed. This is the bristle (soft) and is an exfoliator. Second is a cosmetic sponge goof for cleansing. Third is a Pumice for removing and helping eliminate rough skin areas such as dry heels, elbows and knees. Fourth is a Massager which consists of four rolling balls. The fifth is a latex brush would be ideal for cheeks.

So far I have no reason to take away stars, however, if this fails to perform as it should, I will update this review.

Two notes.
One is that it does not come with a case to store your heads and wand. Second is to give you a heads up the manual is very poor. It has a ton of spelling errors, grammatical errors and has some parts which do not make much sense. Not a big deal though as this is a very lose case product and since it is essentially straight forward with no instructional guidance needed.

title: What I love about this one is how much power it packs

title: Reasonable priced rechargeable razor.
text:
6/7/2016 Addendum. Sorry it is late. Item failed to cut properly after about 2 months. It is no longer usable to me.

This was purchased as I have joined the receding hairline club and now keep my head shaved. (I prefer to forgo the taboo come over hair style.)

For a while I was using an electric razor that I have to plug in. These work, however, I found myself constantly being irritated over the cord and finding myself limited to where I can use it. When I saw this product, I knew I had to try.

This razor caught my eye for several reasons.
-It is rechargeable and you can take it where ever you need to use it.
-It came with an entire setup. You receive a docking station, power cord, rechargeable razor, three trim guards (3mm, 6mm and 9mm), oil and a brush to keep your razor-blades clean and ready for use.
-Upon using, it did a great job and allowed me the same close shape as my past Wahl clipper. It was also quieter then my past razor but certainly not silent.
-The three trimmer attachments were also very nice. Most of the attachments you get with a razor are very cheap plastic, thin and or have sharp edges. These were thick, rounded and had no sharp edges. They attached easily and detached easily.
-There is a charging light on the side which comes on to let you know the razor is charging.
-You can use the included dock or simply charge directly without the dock.
-Comes with instructions-tips in the manual for cutting short hair and trimming.

Summary – This is a great razor, however, I had to limit my review to 3 stars for the following reasons.
-Feel this should come with an integrated auto off charging feature to ensure you do not overcharge. You should not charge this more than 8 hours or it can decrease battery life.
-My charging dock did not work correctly. I had to push and hold the razor down for it to charge while in the dock. If I do not hold the razor down, the pressure of the razor sitting on the dock was not enough to make an electrical connection. Feel it would benefit from a tighter hold or a locking mechanism.

Tips and notes.
-Fully discharge and then fully recharge the clipped every 6 months to maximize the battery.
-Keep the razor-blade clean and oiled after each use for maximum life and cutting performance.

title: Just love it, great product
text:
I give probiotic to my son since he was 1 month old, however i was nursing. Just love it, great product, nice price.
Let's start with a mini biology lesson: Trillions of bacteria already live in your child's (and your own) gastrointestinal system, many of which are considered to be good because they help keep him healthy. They've been there since birth, when your baby's GI tract became colonized with good, bad, and benign bacteria (known as flora) as he passed through the birth canal and picked up some of your microbes. Because babies delivered by C-section miss out on this, they initially end up with a different collection of flora, (Scientists suspect that this difference in colonization may be behind the higher incidence of allergies and asthma in C-section babies, but more research is needed.)
Probiotic Benefits for Children:
There is evidence to suggest probiotics are safe and effective in treating persistent diarrhea in children.
Saccharomyces boulardii has therapeutic properties in the treatment of acute diarrhea in children.
Lactic acid bacteria as probiotics reduce the risk for infantile eczema.
Probiotic and prebiotic supplementation improves the symptoms of children with atopic dermatitis.
Probiotics and prebiotics significantly prevent eczema and atopic eczema in infants.
Supplementation of mothers and their babies with the probiotic Lactobacillus reuteri reduces IgE-associated eczema and may reduce respiratory allergic disease later in life.
A probiotic mixture has positive effects on symptoms of constipation in children.
Bifidobacterium infantis and Lactobacillus acidophilus reduces the incidence and severity of necrotizing enterocolitis in very low birth weight infants.
Lactobacillus reuteri and Bifidobacterium lactis supplementation of children fed formula reduces adverse events, e.g. antibiotic use, diarrhea, etc.
Long term use of probiotics and synbiotics reduce the incidence and severity of respiratory diseases during the cold season.
Probiotic bacteria reduce the duration and severity of common cold episodes.
Probiotic therapy has therapeutic value in treating Klebsiella infection in children.
Lactobacillus rhamnosus and Lactobacillus reuteri reduce the duration of diarrhea in children with mild gastroenteritis.
"Prophylactic probiotics for preterm infants reduces mortality."
Saccharomyces boulardii is an effective adjuvant in treating acute childhood diarrhea.
Lactobacillus reuteri significantly shortens the duration of watery diarrhea associated with rotavirus gastroenteritis in children between 6 and 36 months.
Probiotics demonstrate immunomodulatory effects in atopic pediatric patients by increasing the TH1 immune response which counterbalances the dominant TH2 immune response.
Saccharomyces boulardii inhibits Escherichia coli infection in children.
Probiotic strains from breast milk are superior to antibiotics in the treatment of infectious mastitis.
Human breast milk contains Lactobacillius strains which are effective in the treatment of mastitis during lactation.
Probiotics prophylaxis was as effective as antibiotic prophylaxis in children with persistent primary vesicoureteral reflux.
Lactobacillus reuteri accelerates gastric emptying and improves regurgitation in infants.
The consumption of fermented milk with Lactobacillus casei in lactating mothers has a positive effect on the mother and offspring's immunological status.
Acne may respond favorably to probiotics due to their involvement in normalizing the gut-brain-skin axis.

title: Great supplement for everyday use
text:
Great supplement for everyday use. Great supplement.
Check all the benefits:
Astaxanthin is a reddish pigment that belongs to a group of chemicals called carotenoids. It occurs naturally in certain algae and causes the pink or red color in salmon, trout, lobster, shrimp, and other seafood.
Astaxanthin is used for treating Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, “brain attack” (stroke), high cholesterol, and an eye condition called age-related macular degeneration (AMD). It is also used for preventing cancer.
Astaxanthin is applied directly to the skin for protection against sunburn.

Because of its antioxidant properties, there has been a lot of research on how astaxanthin might help to treat various cancers. One study found short- and long-term benefits for the treatment of breast cancer, including reduced growth of breast cancer cells.
The high cost of purified astaxanthin has limited its use in further studies and cancer treatments.

There has been a lot of study on how astaxanthin can affect endurance, as well as fatigue levels after exercise. Studies on mice show that it can boost the body's use of fatty acids, which helps endurance, and prevent muscle and skeletal damage.
So far, however, evidence for its effects on human exercise is still lacking. One study using human subjects found no exercise benefits from astaxanthin supplements in relation to muscle injury.

Researchers are also looking into claims that astaxanthin can benefit heart health. A 2006 study examined astaxanthin's effects on rats with hypertension (high blood pressure), and results indicated that it may help to improve elastin levels and arterial wall thickness.
Other claims include the notion that astaxanthin can prevent heart disease and help lower cholesterol, but there isn’t sufficient evidence to support these uses yet.

Astaxanthin may also have a future in the treatment of joint pain, including conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, which affects nearly one in every five Americans, and carpal tunnel syndrome. However, results so far have been mixed.

Some studies show that astaxanthin may be able to reduce inflammation and pain symptoms related to arthritis. However, a study on the relationship between astaxanthin and carpal tunnel syndrome found no evidence to support the claim.

In a 2005 study, astaxanthin showed positive results for male fertility. Over the course of three months, the double-blind study examined 30 different men who were previously suffering from infertility.

The researchers saw improvements in sperm parameters, like count and motility, and improved fertility in the group who received a strong dosage of astaxanthin. As this was a relatively small-scale study, more evidence and research is needed to support this claim.

title: UPDATE below: Adorable, but not very effective
text:
Update:
Our baby girl is sick with a cold and this little gadget has been a lifesaver. While a manual nasal aspirator still offers better suction, our little girl tolerates this WAY better than the NoseFrida and actually smiles and laughs when we use it. The highest setting can get the most stubborn snot out but does take some poking around. No worries as the snot tip (wide, rounded tip) is soft and doesn’t bother her. The music and lights keep her engaged at not swinging her head from side to side.

All great things as far as an update goes BUT… the instructions say to boil the parts to sanitize them, including the snot collection cup, but the plastic pieces did NOT survive boiling water. I’m hoping the seller can send out replacement parts. So DO NOT BOIL THE PLASTIC PARTS despite what the instructions say.

Before our son learned how to blow his nose, we used the Nose Frida exclusively to remove snot and boogies. For our new baby, I thought I’d give this cute little device a try. First off, it’s adorable! The lights and music are great for distracting little ones who aren’t too keen on having the snot sucked out of the faces. There are several songs you can cycle through to find your little one’s favorite. You can also cycle through the suction strength to find one that’s effective for you. Unfortunately, even on the highest setting, the suction was still lacking, when compared to the manual Nose Frida. This can still work well for those who aren’t fans of the manual booger sucker, and definitely a better option than the ones the hospitals used, but it does fall short for us. I’ll keep it for the times when baby isn’t cooperative with the Nose Frida as the lights and music make it much more appealing than the blue tube.

title: No More Sticky Paper Cups!
text:
Never buy muffin cups again! I am seriously impressed with these baking cups. Even though they claimed that they were safe up to 450 degrees, I still almost expected to find them melted in my oven. I guess I'm just skeptical about new things! Instead of a puddle of melted silicone though, I got the best baking experience that I've probably ever had. I used these to make corn bread muffins for our Christmas breakfast, a task that usually leaves me annoyed and frustrated as I try to peel the paper cups off of the bread without taking half the muffin with it. Not this year though! The muffins baked beautifully in the cups, then popped right out of them once they were cooled, completely intact. We're vegan, so when I bake I use an egg replacer. It's great for making yummy snacks vegan, but it also makes the food stickier and harder to remove from the baking dish, so these silicone baking cups have really changed baking for me! We don't have a dishwasher, so I can't comment on how they wash in one, but they were very easy to hand wash. I'll never have to remember to pick up muffin cups again, and these function so much better than the paper ones ever did! I'll be buying more sets for when I want to make big batches!

title: These Sponges Are Amazing!
text:
I'll be honest: when I ordered these sponges, I was incredibly skeptical. They seemed pretty pricey for something that I assumed you would get 3-4 uses from at the most. I thought they looked dumb. I was curious though, so I ordered them anyway, and I am SO glad that I did. The sponges have completely changed the way we shower! I originally planned to count the number of uses I got from each sponge, but I lost track after a couple of weeks. I should have kept a written record I guess, but it's been a month now and I'm still on my first sponge. They're so easy to use: just wet it, give it a squeeze or two, and wash. When I'm done I rinse the outside (without wringing it out) and put it on a rack in the shower where it can dry. It stays soapy and magically doesn't develop that funky old sponge smell! I also hesitated over the scents since I wasn't particularly jazzed about either scent, but I ended up going with spearmint which I thought would be the least offensive. The scent is actually nice though (and I strongly dislike spearmint); it's a barely there kind of smell, and it doesn't linger on your skin after you leave the shower. The kids love them, I love them, I'll definitely buy again! I only wish I could get some plain, no soap facial sponges to use with my existing face wash!

Pictured are my month old sponge (left) next to an unused sponge (right), and my month old sponge lathered up to show how much life is still in it.

I did receive this product at a discount so that I could review them, however this is really one of those rare things that I didn't know I needed until I tried it out. My review is my truthful opinion. I really AM this excited about a sponge!

title: Re-hydrates better than heavy liquid versions
text:
Purchased this hydration vitamin to help with our long hikes in hot weather, to replace carrying heavy liquid as replacements. The other liquid ones worked good, but we were not sure if they were strong enough or worth the weight to carry. So far this one seems more potent for the both of us & helps both of us more for than the liquid versions.

We purchased this vitamin supplement to help us make it through hikes, without getting dehydrated & to replenish essential electrolytes to keep our energy up. When this supplement arrived, we always check to see if the pills are sealed tight, and these were sealed very well...The pills come 3 to a pack & each one was sealed tight; each packet also has a pull tab to open easily, which none were ripped.

The pills are light brown with darker speckles in color and are an average medium size for most vitamin supplements. When the pills arrived we opened them and they had a light vitamin smell, which we thought was good, since it might be full of the needed nutrients & not just filler. The packet says to take 1 tablet with 8 oz of water...wait 20 minutes to take another...and no more than 12 per day.

Our family doctor recommended we start taking some type of hydration replacement (when we take long hikes) because my wife already had some problems with becoming dehydrated since we moved west. We tried these out for 3 days (one day lifting, one day running & the last day hiking) & for us it seems we only needed one pill each with 12 oz of water. Which was more than enough for both of us & kept us hydrated for hours with no thirst or dry lips. The only time we might take extra pills, is if it is very hot out or if we are taking a full day or very long hike.

Pros:
Easy to take, medium size pill
Not bitter & no bad aftertaste
Helps to revive us & keep us hydrated
& They seem to work quickly

Cons:
Has a few other ingredients, that are not needed...this is a major complaint we have with many different supplements.

Overall we love this re-hydrating vitamin supplement and would recommend these to everyone looking for help with staying hydrated during exercise or outdoor activities when you lose electrolytes faster or if you just need a boost after a night out drinking (which our friend says they work great on as well).

Thank you for you time & interest in our review; Greg, Tina & Family

title: The tank is more of a bother than help
text:
I have a few other similar items. The difference (besides one having a camera) is the size and way that the water is handled. The one with the camera has a built-in tank that holds about 150ml (about 5 oz) and it also has a camera that records and a UVA disinfector https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B09KLM695X . I loved this in the beginning, and still think it's a damn good flosser, but I don't really find much use at all for the camera. The UVA disinfector is a great idea but, in the end, the 150 ml tank is not enough and I have to re-fill it mid-flossing.

The other irrigator https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B09L1FK5XC , was a bit of a disappointment to me because you had to dip a hose into a water glass as it did not have its own internal tank. It did a great job, pretty much as good as the other, but I liked the all-in-one style of the other irrigator.

And so this unit looked good since I could use the tank or not, and the tank is large enough for a whole water flossing session without filling. Cool. Except that with the water tank attached, this is very unwieldy and not at all fun to use. So, remove the tank and now we're back to using a water glass that I can fill with as much water as I like.

This, as with the others, does a very good job of cleaning and is easy to use with long battery life. It all comes down to the water tank (and whether or not you want the other stuff such as a camera and UVA light). After trying several of these I have come to the conclusion that, although it does not look as cool, anywhere you can floss your teeth you can find a water glass (or fill the sink with water) and you won't need to worry about refilling, running out of water, or being uncomfortable to hold. This unit is good but I already threw out the water tank.

title: It's cornstarch. It's cornstarch at $160 per pound, or 50x the price of cornstarch.
text:
C'mon now. This is a cute marketing ploy, but all that this is, and unabashedly so there is no attempt at misleading you, is regular cornstarch. The only thing different between this and Argo cornstarch ( https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00T70RNQ8 ) which is available here and in every grocery store in the country, is that this costs $15 for 1.5 oz and the Argo (or any similar cornstarch off the grocery shelf) would cost $0.30 per 1.5 oz.

It's OK to make a profit, it's OK to say that your product is differentiated (it's in a plastic sprinkle bottle, not a box or jar) and it's OK to put out some exotic product as a novelty item and charge 3x,4x,5x maybe even 10x as much as it's worth, but this is 50x as much as it should cost. Imagine the outrage if Pharma Bro did that with his medicines.

And, is it as good as a regular box off of the grocery shelf, "thicken your egg drop soup", cornstarch? No, it might be worse, and here's why. As you can see in the attached pictures, it arrived slightly open, enough to let the power out and anything else into the container. This is a product that you want to be as sterile as possible. This company is obviously buying the cornstarch from somewhere else (Argo?) and re-packing it into 1.5 oz bottles. I have no idea what their sanitation control is, but I know that their QC is lacking based on the bottle I received.

Do you want to take a chance on something that will go into your body, or your body into it, that is not bacteriological pure? I don't.

My background is in hydrocolloids (fancy word for things like cornstarch) and you will find if you do some research that cornstarch is not just cornstarch. It can be modified (which this is not, it would need to be declared on the label) and if it's not modified, it can be specially ground into various sizes for various purposes. This is none of those, there's nothing special about this, it's exactly what you'd find in a box off of the grocery shelf or if you bought basic cornstarch for cooking from Amazon.

Now that you know that it's cornstarch, if you want to apply regular cornstarch to your toys, go ahead. If you're worried about sanitation and contamination (remember, the other cornstarches are food grade) take the cornstarch, and throw it (dry) in a microwave for a bit, and it'll be more sanitary than what you're paying $160 per lb for from this company.

title: A really good tool at a really good price.
text:
This spray mop is simple, easy, and comes with the instructions printed on the side of the box it was packed in. There's really no need (sorta) for paper instructions, except ...

This is not particularly difficult to assemble, but I was stumped when it came to filling the bottle. First, the was no apparent cap, you couldn’t unscrew it because of the shape of the bottle (it wraps around the handle), and I could not pull it out. As it happens, pulling it out is exactly how you remove the bottle to fill it with a cleaning solution. The carton just says "fit the bottle onto the mop" but it was already fitted onto the mop handle when we got it, it was trying to figure out how to take it off without breaking it that was our issue. Pull hard, the bottle is held in place with an "O" ring. Make sure you have additional O rings (available at any hardware store for a few pennies), eventually this one will wear out.

The cleaning pad looks as if it was obviously not made for this mop; they are too wide and too long. But I believe that it was designed this way on purpose, perhaps to prevent the plastic pad holder from scratching furniture or walls.

This comes with three mop heads and a tool that hangs on the handle. I believe that that tool is for cleaning the mop heads.

What this is, essentially, is a giant water gun. You squeeze the trigger, and you spray water, like a toy gun. When we first put on the pad, we placed it with the excess in front; it turns out that this was a bad idea since the spray does not go very far, and most of it was absorbed by the pad. So we learned to place the pad so that the excess was in the back.

We have another one of these, not made as well and it only shipped with one pad and no pad cleaning tool. My original review said it was a toy and I was going to toss it in the garbage, but we soon found ourselves using it often and we now rely on it for quick cleanups. I was going to edit my review, but that product is no longer available. This brand and model is much improved over that one, and we will use it in one of our other homes. The aluminum tubes are thicker and denser, the plastic fittings are better and the mop heads (you get three, not 1) are softer and more absorbent. The mop head swivels up, down, to the side, etc. You will have no problem getting into spots and when hanging it up, you can make it very compact by swiveling the head.

For an insanely cheap "Swiffer" type cleaner, this is really a very good product. We just put some cleaning solution in the bottle and you never need to worry about the battery being charged. Sometimes, simpler is better.

I'm rating this 5 stars because of what it is. It's certainly not a Swiffer or other more costly product, but for what this costs, it's an excellent value. Don't be a jerk and judge it out of the box (like I was with the first model), give it some time and I think you'll really enjoy having this around.

Recommended.

title: Super product for complete oral care while traveling
text:
We use water irrigators (water flossers) every day and when we travel, we miss using them as they are too bulky to carry. I recently got a travel irrigator which I loved and did not think it could be topped but, while I wouldn’t say that this tops it, I’d say it’s comparable but different.

The key feature(s) to this unit is that it combines irrigation with brushing and periodontal care (more on that later) in one very small product, the size of a standard electric toothbrush. The other product that I like is single-purpose, just irrigation. Unlike this unit, it does not have the capability to brush or be used as a periodontal pick. On the other hand, that unit is stronger and includes a built-in camera for checking your work as well as UV lighting to sterilize the tips and water reservoir. While both are great, I think that on my shorter trips I will take this, and when I am on a longer trip and have more luggage room, I’ll take the other (which means also taking my toothbrush).

This product draws the water from whatever reservoir you use so it can be an 8 oz cup or a gallon jug. How much water you use is up to you. The other unit has a relatively small reservoir and I usually need to refill it once in order to get a good cleaning. This product knows when you choose an irrigation tip or the toothbrush or periodontal tip and the options on the handle change accordingly. On the brush and the periodontal tip, your choices are High or Low and when you use the irrigator you have the choice of Normal, Soft, Pulse, and DIY.

As mentioned, the irrigator is not quite as strong as my other portable, but it is certainly strong enough.
The toothbrush has the High and Low settings, no timer as my toothbrush has, and the periodontal tip is also high and low.

A word about the periodontal tip; it works, and it works well. It will remove plaque quickly and effectively. However, I don’t necessarily recommend that you use it if you do not have a strong and steady hand; this can rip the hell out of your gums if you slip and with the vibration, that’s a very good possibility. If you are able to control it, it’s something I’ve not seen on other units and it’s great. But it can also be dangerous; use it with caution.

Although it looks short in some of the pictures, the hose that you clip onto any reservoir is long enough to allow you to move around as you floss.

This also comes with a soft carrying bag to carry the tips and hose with you.

If I had received this before or when I received the other unit (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09KLM695X - SORRY, as of 1/1/2022 this product is no longer available), I would have named them both “2021 products of the year”. Which you choose will be dictated by your priorities but they are both great products.

Recommended.

title: Blows me away
text:
YEEEEEEEHAAAAAAA!

After a few years of using a very good electric, I'm thinking I should've gotten this three years sooner. I've rented before, this is my first one. (I got this from the listed mfr., before it was listed here.)

It got here in three days, beautifully packed (injected foam surrounds the main unit), and it is a Cat 5 tornado in a backpack, at a pretty good price. (Local, $330, + $10 for oil 6-pack, + tax. This a very good buy.)

The tubes are a snug fit --- plan on using a little lube to fit the end pipes on, as recommended in the manual. Don't be shy priming, especially on the first run. Runs great, idles smoothly, and it cleans things up amazingly well. I'd say at idle it runs close to the 2/3 point of the top-rated electric handheld. (At some point I'll use Kestrel to measure things, just for the fun of it.)

I opted for the tube-mounted trigger throttle, and find it very, very easy to use. The off/idle/throttle slider lets you set your own back-off speed (from the trigger) and acts as a cruise control. Very low-fatigue. It's pretty "tight" --- no gas smell in garage storage.

If you can handle about 21 lbs. on your back, this is pretty easy going --- but don't expect to squeeze into tight spaces in shrubbery without a spotter (branches on muffler!).

According to the manual it can be used for snow-blowing, something I've never tried with a blower. Can't wait.

This is the top-rated unit in its class, according to that well-known site and magazine. I can see why.

So, how easy is this to use, really?

My right arm is in a cast. I managed to finish Spring cleaning outside by myself. A little extreme, maybe, but still ...

title: Came with no label on the bottle. Big pill; however also only need to take one to get the max dose!
text:
Fish oil is one of nature's richest resources for Omega 3 and has been used to treat ADHD, arthritis, anxiety, cognitive decline, cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, eye disorders, and immune compromises. Recently I went to a Psychopharmocology conference and the presenter discussed that Omega 3 had been shown in new research to provide protection against the depression, and in fact, may enhance many areas of brain functioning, including mood and personality. Individuals whom consume more Omega 3 have more gray matter volume in the areas of the brain important for regulating mood. How awesome is that! A supplement with efficacious research standing behind it saying that people whom take fish oil have less symptoms of depression! Fish oil has important benefits to both physical and mental health!

Unfortunately, I was not impressed with this bottle of fish oil when it arrived. It came in an unmarked bottle with NO LABEL that was readable on it. There were two small stickers on the bottle, overlapping one another; however none of the writing on the stickers was readable. I did not even know this was fish oil until I opened the bottle. As most fish oil products do, the pills had a fishy smell to them; however what matters the most is that you don't taste anything fishy or burp up the fish oil afterwards. While I didn't burp up this supplement or have any heartburn, the pill did have a slightly taste to it when I swallowed it-- not sure if it was lemon or fishy, however I did not like the taste. This would not stop me from taking the pills though. The pills were also quite big. I am able to take quite a few pills at once; however only one of these and still felt like it was a bit large to swallow. You do, however, only have to take one pill, whereas with all the other fish oil pills I bought, I had to take two. This pill is the max concentration of 2400mg, 860mg EPA, 430mg DHA. I also like the fact that the product is made in the USA.

title: Huge improvement on average walker wheels
text:
I bought these "off-road" walker wheels for a relative who is recovering from a mild stroke. He is at the point where he is supposed to be walking more and more each day. He has been cleared to do some of that walking outside in the driveway and even in the yard. It turns out that the thin 5" gray walker wheels that come on a standard walker don't work so well outside. I haven't had to use a walker before, but I gave it a shot and could feel how much the wheels bounced when they hit a little piece of gravel or a seam in the sidewalk. The grass? Disaster. The wheels sort of sunk into the damp ground and then I was stuck.

New wheels were a must.

I ended with these wheels from North American Health and Wellness. Unlike a lot of the walker wheels sold as "off-road," this pair had tread and was wider than normal wheels. Both of these factors are needed to make a significant difference in how the walker will handle rough spots in the road.

These wheels do come on standard 1" wide walker wheel attachment tubes. The axels on these wheels are higher than the regular wheels, so the setting for the tubes will lower than usual by 3 clicks. My relative usually has the wheels at a 7; for these, a 4. *** I don't think these wheels will work for a person whose walker wheel tubes are typically set at lower than a 4. *** They go on just like regular wheels. To make it easier to go through doorways, you may want to turn the wheels towards the inside of the walker.

The package also includes 2 of the biggest walker skis I have ever seen. We have not installed these yet as the physical therapist recommends staying with the caps on the back of the walker for a while. The skis are made of a thick, smooth resin and look like they will work well.

My relative has absolutely loved these wheels and finds them to be a ginormous improvement upon the old wheels. We don't think the tread makes that much difference as it is a fairly wide and shallow pattern that wouldn't get much traction. But the width of the wheels just gives him more stability, inside the house and out. Gravel on the sidewalk is not a problem anymore, and neither is grass. He also finds it easier to _stop_ on the wood floors inside the house, which I was unaware of being an issue. The material of the tires has slightly more give than the hard gray tires he had before; it must be just enough to respond to the exertion of pressure. However the tires work, he feels more stable and is happier about doing the physical therapy.

Do I recommend these wheels? Yes, if your doctor or physical therapist also recommends them. =-) I am not a doctor or a physical therapist or anyone else that knows how a change like larger tires on a walker could impact your or a loved one's physiology. Because I have not seen tires like this at any home medical supply company, what I would recommend if you want to try them is to just buy them and take them with you to your or your loved one's medical appointment. It will be easier for your medical professional to assess impact if they can see the wheels you're talking about and compare them to what you have now. And if they don't work out, you can return the unused wheels. There are other options that might work better for you or your loved one. This is just the pair that I ended up buying for my relative. =-)

title: So far, so good
text:
My heel has been killing me for almost 3 years and nothing has worked yet to alleviate it, including a nighttime boot and a few different kinds of compression socks. So I was dubious about this splint; but after just a few nights, the heel pain in my foot is almost imperceptible in the morning. (It comes back over the course of the day, but that's expected.) So yeah, it works and works well/fast. It's kind of a production to put on and take off, but it's snug and not irritating; and it's fairly easy to adjust the tightness.

There are 2 things I don't like about it when I have to walk around; however I realize the splint's not optimized for walking, so I can't complain too much. (1) The metal strip digs into the top of my foot when I pick it up to move it. Very uncomfortable. I suspect this is a problem more for people with longer feet. (2) all the various straps and velcros that go under the foot make it hard to walk/hobble on it in general.

Overall, I'm very glad I bought it. I wear it both to bed and while relaxing on the couch for more than 20 minutes. The improvement in my heel pain has been substantial, and I'm hoping that within a few weeks it will be gone altogether.

They either suck up oxygen too fast, or are not a very effective product. But, a couple weeks after transferring the packets to the dry goods jars, the seal would hold for only a couple of weeks. The lids and jars are still good (most are new), so I doubt it is from my supplies. The rims were clean, too. I even doubled up on packets. They would make a seal for a week or two, and eventually lose it.

Yes. After opening the new package, I immediately dumped them into a jar and had it seal so they wouldn't passively absorb oxygen (no time was wasted, and took seconds to move it over). The indicator was very quick to turn blue (litterally only had it in the open air for a couple seconds). I only open the container when I was ready and had help to make the transfer go fast... and still the poor results for jars with food.

title: So far, so good!
text:
I am 5'6", currently weight 155 lbs, and am 32 weeks pregnant with one baby. I have a long torso, so I don't stick out very far when I'm pregnant, but I carry REALLY low (my babies are so low that they never "drop"). Because I carry so low, I get really bad lower abdominal and lower back pain, and I find myself constantly holding up my belly to relieve some of the abdominal discomfort. My midwife recommended this style of cradle, and I'm so glad I ordered it.

Based on other reviews of them running small, I ordered a Medium and am very pleased with how it fits. I was nervous about ordering the style that isn't adjustable, especially since my torso is so long, but I'm satisfied with how the shoulder straps adjust on this style. It feels very comfortable; the back support is great.

The only reason why I dropped it one star is because the abdominal hooks to make it different sizes are spaced fairly far apart, and I wish it had more hooks spaced more closely together to get a more perfect fit. When I first received it, the smallest hooks were too tight, and the second hooks were not quite as tight as I wanted. I wore it on the second hooks. Even still, it provided significant support and relief from the pain, so I am not completely dissatisfied. There is a third set of hooks I can use for the last month when I start to really stick out.

When ordering your size, keep in mind that the Medium is rated for 150-220 lbs and I currently am 155 lbs on the second set of hooks. I fully expect to need to move to the third set of hooks by the end of this pregnancy, but I can't imagine I'll gain much more than 10 lbs, if that, by the time I give birth. If you are on the higher end of the weight limit, err on the side of caution and order up a size.

title: Buy these! They are the best! Been using since July 2015!
text:
I first bought and reviewed these about 3 years ago. (07/2015)
I am now editing my review to add more information. (06/2018)

Charcoal bamboo inserts are my favorite because the fleece-like outer layer stays bone dry against baby’s skin. Out of all the inserts I’ve bought, See Diapers are the most impressive. The length and the square edges of See Diapers inserts make them perfect for covers b/c they cover the PUL completely, so the PUL isn’t directly against baby’s skin-- unlike shorter inserts with rounded edges. In addition to being longer than others, See Diapers are darker than others and hold up better in the wash. They are also thinner and more flexible-- compared to others, which are thicker and bulkier-- without sacrificing absorbency. They can keep my 20+ lb super soakers dry overnight (12+ hours) even without doublers.

I have also ordered charcoal bamboo inserts from Naturally Nature, AngelicWare, and Bottoms Beautiful. The Bottoms Beautiful, I returned immediately without even washing b/c their product description was misleading re: the length. (They are advertised as 16.5” but are actually 13”, whereas See Diapers are advertised as 14” and are truly 14”.) The Naturally Nature, I returned because they started pilling and the seams started falling apart on more than one insert just after the first wash. The AngelicWare, I kept and have been using since 2015, but I would not buy them again, as they are shorter and bulkier than See Diapers.

In fact, I was so impressed with See Diapers the first time I ordered them that I ordered a second set (07/2016) the same day that the first set arrived. I ordered another set about two months later (09/2016) because I wanted to try them without gussets. (I prefer gussets.) I ordered a fourth set (06/2016) almost a year later because (Surprise!) I had babies 18 months apart. In my most recent order (06/2016), the inserts were softer than ever and so dark they were almost black. The quality was remarkable. I honestly wish I had an excuse to order more, but I already have a nice stash-- 12+ covers, 12+ pockets, 50+ inserts, and 8+ doublers. Plus, my youngest is turning 2 soon, so my diapering days are nearly done. At any rate...

What makes See Diapers better:

-A full 1” longer than other brands

-Thin/soft, not thick/bulky-- but still no leaks

-Seams hold up in the wash 3 years later

-Nice, square edges and darker color than others

-Priced the same as others, despite higher quality

-Not as much pilling as others

- No sewn-in tags, so they are reversible

NOTE: I use them with Bububibi/BB2 covers. [[ASIN:B01HP1GXI4 BB2 Baby One Size Printed Minky Minkee Snaps Cloth Diaper Cover for Prefolds (One Size, Monkeys)]] (No Velcro, just snaps, so I can't speak to that issue.) Two inserts in the daytime, one insert and one Thirsties hemp doubler at nighttime. [[ASIN:B002FB7FLY Thirsties Hemp Inserts 2-pack, Size Large]] I try new detergents recommended on CD blogs occasionally, but these have mostly been washed with Ecos Free & Clear over the years-- though lately I'm using a mix of Ecos, Tide, and Foca to see what I like best. If you try to only use one insert with an older/larger baby, or if you use a detergent that can cause buildup, and so on, you might experience leaks. However, after 6+ years of cloth diapering, these are the best inserts I've ever used.

I really, REALLY love that you can change the temperature in increments because my toddler now lets me blow-dry her hair! My old dryer had only hot and cold settings and the hot was too hot for her. title: Appears to be an accurate, consistent alternative to pricey OneTouch Ultra Blue strips
text:
Genultimate Test Strips appear to be a good, low cost alternative to the pricey OneTouch Ultra (Blue) test strips I'm currently using with my OneTouch Ultra 2 meter. But of course, price doesn't matter if the strips aren't accurate. To check them out, I used both my regular OTU strips and the GU strips (adjusting test strip vial code as required and marking the GU readings as Controls). Below are my admittedly small sample size findings:
256, 223 (Control)
182, 185 (Control)
158, 140 (Control)
129, 120 (Control)
142, 139 (Control)
120, 125 (Control)
175, 152 (Control)
77, 76 (Control)
178, 152 (Control
These readings were taken over the course of a couple of days, each sample pair drawn from the same location on the same finger (but not all sample pairs from the same finger - that would start to hurt!)
The OTU strips usually read a bit higher than the GU strips, with a variance of up to 17%, but mostly they were within less than 10%. As Glucose meters themselves have an accuracy of up to 20% compared to lab testing, this would appear to be 'tolerable'.
At any rate, I'm cautiously optimistic that they are accurate enough to use since I'm mostly concerned with tracking high glucose readings.

title: Happy buns, great for wheelchair users
text:
The Good: You’d think someone who sits in a wheelchair all day would be really used to it, but this isn’t the case. I finally decided to invest a good seat cushion to reduce those annoying pressure points, and this seat cushion has really done the trick. It is very durable and it’s like sitting on a dry bowl of firm jello. I love that the seat cushion has grips on the bottom that keep it from shifting around.

The Bad: I should have gotten the 1 inch version instead as this cushion doesn’t give very much and it has perched me a bit higher than I want to be in my wheelchair. I weigh about 170, so I expected to sink in the seat a bit, but it only dropped about a half an inch. I’d recommend this 2 inch version only if you are much heavier than myself.

Pros:
-Soooo comfortable
-Great washable case that doesn’t slip from under you
-Very durable

Cons:
-It was a bit too thick for me

title: Put them on some hard toe work boots for working in some sloping woods

To get the cleats into the shoe I had to break the skin with a drill bit first to give the cleat an opening to bite into. I also used shoe glue. I think these shoes get a pretty good workout when I'm stomping around the woods in all kinds of terrain including rocks down by the creek. We'll see how long they hold up. So far just a week. I'll be sure and post an update at the end of the summer.

I also stuck one on the end of a walking stick. Works pretty nice.

Edit May 27 - Not quite the end of the summer but I've spent some days in the woods with a chain saw and doing a lot of climbing on steep banks. I love these things. Nothing is loose. Probably a lot depends on the sole you put these in and for sure shoe glue has to help but I would recommend these for work shoes if you can glue them into some solid soles.

title: Great customer service, great back support!
text:
UPDATE #2: 17 day roadtrip and halfway through we had a heat wave of 100+ degree temperatures. I have fabric seats in a jeep and my options were to blast the AC and pay double for gas (6k miles is a lot of gas money already) or drive with the windows down. These saved us! The mesh support allowed the breeze to hit our backs and keep us cool. We used the air conditioning only in traffic when the wind died down. They held together well too. I didn't use them continuously but alternated on and off to give my back new positions and prevent stiffness.
I also brought them into the hotel room as support for sitting up in bed at the end of the day. They were absolutely worth the hassle of carrying them in and out with my bags.
These are definitely going to stay in my summer road trip kit. Updated to 5 stars!
UPDATE: great customer service! Cartop has a great guarantee policy for defective products and is replacing my damaged item. Hopefully it'll arrive in time. I'll update again after my road trip.
ORIGINAL REVIEW: I had lumbar surgery several years ago. It helped immensely, but I still have occasional pain. Especially if I sit too long (more than a couple minutes) in a chair without support.
These are actually great for my back. Not only in a chair, but while sitting in bed reading they provided just the right support and air flow preventing me from overheating. I felt the difference immediately. As soon as I stood up, I didn't need to stretch or move carefully for those first few steps like I always do. The ache was gone, which was such a relief.
However, one of the supports snapped its stitching when I tried to buckle it to the seat in my car. I hadn't even used it yet. Hadn't messed with the adjustable bands at all. I've used the other for all of 2 days and while it's fine so far, I'm concerned.
I purchased them for an upcoming road trip for my mother and I and I don't think they'll last those 2 weeks. I'm going to try to fix and reinforce the seams, but I suspect I'll have to buy new ones along the way.

title: Best looking functional shower chair out there
text: I bought this shower chair in preparation for an upcoming knee replacement. I'm a bit vain and didn't want a "medicinal" looking shower chair in my bathroom. I was surprised at how sturdy/stable the seat was. The legs are enameled covered metal and the top is a hard plastic with an embossed ring design that keeps you from slipping. The color is pretty much exactly as indicated in the pictures. My tub is from the 1930s and is slightly smaller than a standard tub and this fits just fine in it. My sister, who is a social worker, was fully ready to slam my choice of chair as she knows I have been known to choose form over function. However, even she approved! It has little plastic/rubber sleeves over the screws under the seat, which will keep the screws out of direct water unless the chair is tipped over and/or submerged. Therefore, I suspect the rust issues that other people reported in the past may not be an issue anymore. The feet are tight fitting rubber, so they provide stability and protect the bottom of the legs from direct exposure to water.  I had planned to use this as a decent looking side table once I have recovered from my knee surgery, so I will have this when get my other knee done down the road. But then again, I kinda like being able to sit while shaving my legs, so it might just stay in the shower!

title: DONT LIKE YOUR FEET TOUCHED?/ EXTRA WIDE FEET/ REFLEXOLOGY
text:
I bought this for my husband. He hurt the heel on his foot & his back while remodeling our new home. Nothing was really doing much to help. He HATES his feet being touched. They are super ticklish, he thinks its weird, and wants no one near them. I rarely ever see him with socks off. So me giving him a foot massage was out of the question, even though I have tried many times. I bought this without him knowing. Set it up by his chair and gave him the 'you better at least TRY IT' stink eye wife look. He did, and now loves it, and uses it twice a day. He does have extra wide feet (12 EE), but his feet still fit fine in the machine;of course they still stick out of the machine length wise, so do mine a bit. The machine, was surprisingly big & heavy. I guess I didnt expect it, because I am used to the cheap ones that dont do much for your feet. The only draw back is the remote works horribly; maybe it needs new batteries(it did come w. 'new' ones, where you pull out the plastic tab thing to activate it)? We havent tried to put new ones in yet.
There are many settings on the machine, the manual tells you what setting to use for your feel and for what corresponding body part it could also help. For example: Program #3- Focus on intestinal ,liver,stomach etc, Program #4 Focus on legs reproductive & urinary systems.....It also comes with diagrams of the foot which diff. points you can move the massager onto, such as the heel for menstruation & infertility. There is A LOT of info on reflexology points to help not only your feet but weight,detox,fatigue,blood pressure, constipation,migraines,cervical acid,menopause,dysmenorrhea,.So there a lot of info in the book, yet its laid out simply so you dont get bored reading it. Its also IMPORTANT to read the guide. There is a time limit for the massage, dont go over it, also about eating food before or after, as well as water directions. My husband dosent like to read or his feet touched. Yet there he was in the machine & really into the fun facts the pamphlet had to offer! I was so stifling my giggling in amazement! And yes it will hurt a bit at first especially if your feet are sore & in pain, but its a 'good' hurt like when you get a massage , getting the kinks worked out, if that makes sense.

title: Great looking case.
text:
I got this case because I thought the aluminum edge gave it a totally different look then a lot of other cases out there. Plus, with the construction of the back part of the case, it should protect the phone really well.

While I am happy with the look of the case and (knocks on wood) I haven’t “tested” the durability of the case yet, I am not happy with the feel of the case.

I have a tendency to hold my phone in my right hand with it resting on my pinky finger, which means that the cut outs on the bottom are right on my finger and because the case is metal, those ports dig into my finger making it really uncomfortable to hold my phone. I find myself constantly shifting my phone around in my hand trying to find a comfortable way to hold it. Granted, I have long skinny fingers so this may not be a problem for someone with beefier fingers.

Overall, I really think this is a good case; the metal gives it just enough shine to make it stand out without being garish. It fits great, is easy to remove and replace if needed, and I’ve not had any issues with my chargers or other adaptors not being able to plug in. It’s just not the best case for me.

title: It Works Pretty Well After All...
text:
First of all, this thing is made of really hard plastic so when I took it out of the package I thought, "Oh no, this was a total waste of money. How am I going to work this thing?!" It turns out that the stiffness holds your hair much better than the soft fabric kind and adds volume to your bun so it looks bigger. By the way, I have medium length hair.

For those of you who have not worked with this design, you pull your pony tail through the middle and turn the tool twice. Then you pull it through your hair almost to the end of your pony tail and roll it torwards your scalp (up, down, left or right depending on where you want the tail or french twist). When you have rolled your hair to your scalp, you pull the ends together and hook it the tool to itself and you have yourself a nice sturdy bun.

title: Good, not the best.
text:
I'm a professional cobbler and we have worked with these in the past. Why in the past, you may ask? Because the color does not match like others available at select high end cobblers.
These are thin and they are supposed to be used to extend the life of your lightly worn shoes and keep the red color on the sole and not to patch up shoes.

Keep in mind it is highly recommended to not install these soles on your shoes on your own but have a professional install them for you.

To install:
pre-work. You may want to tape off your shoes with blue painters tape before you do anthing to not ruin your uppers.
1. line up this half sole to your shoe sole and mark were you are going to place it and line up to make sure the pair are going to be identical
2. rough up and/or sand both the shoe sole (yes, you have to remove the red paint on the shoe sole) and the half sole where you are going to put on the contact cement
3. use only barge contact cement or anything stronger like renia kelbfest as the adhesive, shoe goo will not work and it will separate in just a couple wears
4. apply contact cement and let dry about 15-30min (depending on directions of the cement) until tacky then apply half soles to shoe soles
5. once half soles are applied, let dry at least 12 hours
6. trim with heavy duty scissors or x-acto knife
7. finish edge with 150 gt sandpaper, then 220 gt to make a nice edge

These are probably the easiest job we do, but someone without the right tools will have a hard time getting it right.
