title: Thorough but boring skin care device
text:
I struggled to understand what this product did, how to use it and if it was worth it. At the time I ordered, reviews were rather brief, so I thought I could review it in a more detailed way: basically the information I'd have liked to have known.

What does it do?
They claim it cleans, moisturizes, pats and pore reduces. In my experience, it is best used between cleansing and moisturizing, if you want to be super thorough about your skin care routine. I like to think of it as something that removes anything the cleanser left behind, and preps the skin for even greater moisturizing.

How does it work?
There are four modes. To paraphrase: the cleansing mode, the patting mode, the moisturizing mode and the icing mode. These are reflected as indicator lights (top to bottom in the order mentioned). Each mode takes 3 minutes each (approx) but can be manipulated by the first button if you want to get done with a mode early (pressing it will take you to the next mode). You are supposed to gently rub the device over your face with the bare, or cotton wrapped plate in contact with your skin.

What does it feel like?
You won't feel any of the first 3 modes, in terms of sensation but they make a soft brrrr sound punctuated with breaks: short pulses = cleansing mode, long pulses = moisturizing mode. The last mode makes the plate cold which reduces pores or creates a refreshing sensation.

What do you use with such things?
Firstly, you'll need thin, flat cotton discs or squares. These days they seem to be available even at local drug stores but you can order Korean or Japanese brands on this site.

For product: a watery toner, emulsion and serum that is slathered on that cotton and affixed on the plate with plastic rings (that they provide) or applied directly to your face. I am going to qualify that. For the first phase, a cleansing toner or micellar water works best, but use it after removing makeup. The second phase is the trickiest because you are supposed to use the naked plate directly on your skin and serums will absorb into your skin causing the plate to tug. Hence, instead of using it bare, I use product infused cotton for this phase as well(anything from Missha first essence to Vitamin C serum to a sample of SKII. Basically any liquid active will work.) The third phase is when you add a watery moisturizer, not a milk. I use a HA based watery moisturizer. Amazon has things like Hado Labo Goku Jyun water, Hera Aquabolic, or Skinfood lettuce watery toner. Basically if it says it adds moisture and it looks like water, it will work. Then you do the icing mode. Then you can apply the rest of your skin care routine: I just add a facial oil and call it a day.

Isn't that a lot of work?
That is the reason for the docked star. Not that it takes a long time, because they are upfront about that and it is silly to dock a star for the central premise of the product. But the process is not pleasurable. You feel nothing, so you are just sitting there rubbing this on your face for at least 12 minutes. The cleansing mode is a little gratifying because you will see all the stuff the Clarisonic left behind, but the rest of it? Not so much. These days I use only the cleansing mode, followed by two presses to the button to the moisturizing mode, and call it a day. Four minutes I can do and it has been wonderful for my skin. I don't know whether it is the technology or the prolonged contact with beneficial ingredients, but my skin glows as long as I am keeping it up.

I can say that the prescribed two scoopfuls of this berry-flavored powder mixed in water tastes pretty good. The chemical aftertaste is quite subdued compared to similar products I have tried.

title: Fail
text:
I thought these disposable gloves might be useful to wear while I ride the subway during the pandemic, but as other reviewers have noted, these size S items are small and flimsy and hence unusable.

As I look at the product page, I don't see a sizing choice. My hands are not large -- I'm a short man, standing 5'7" if I stand up straight -- but these gloves are a bear to get on.

I tried them straight out of the box (which is another story I'll get to in a minute!), and both gloves ripped at the cuff as I tried to pull them on.

I then tried applying body powder to my hands, and again the gloves ripped as I tried to get them on.

After that I tried baby oil and then Vaseline and was able to get them most of the way on without ripping them, but still I couldn't get the fingers to fit correctly.

But carrying gloves that also require oil or grease to wear is not practical for my on-the-go application.

As others have mentioned, the gloves don't come right out of the perforated window in the box the first time you use them. You have to open up the box at one of the end flaps and position the inner bag containing the gloves so you can access them properly through the window.

The long and short of it is -- if Amazon offers the different sizes of these that are supposedly available, they MIGHT work for you if a proper sizing chart is provided on the ordering page.

Until that time, you should probably give these a pass unless you have VERY small hands...

title: Good grip, heats fast
text: Ok: I'm going to review this curling iron, and I have a few comments and tips. First of all, I am impressed with the fact that the curling iron is longer than most because you can get longer hair and wrap it around the wand without that being a problem. I don't have particularly long hair, so it's not an issue for me, but it might matter to some people.  Also, take a few minutes to get to know how this thing works because it's confusing at first. The directions don't explain everything. When you plug in the curling iron, you have to press the power button to unlock it, and then you press it again to actually get the heat to set. There is a display and it automatically wants to set on a certain heating (180°c). It climbs very quickly and then stops when it gets there. What I was confused about is there's a little display that says "damaged". I didn't know if this meant the wand was damaged? Would this setting potentially damage my hair? I didn't know, and the directions don't say anything about it. I pressed the power button again to unlock it, and then pressed downwards to reduce the heat until all of a sudden it says "fragile" in the display window. So I see now I should use it on that setting since I do have fragile hair. I now understand the damaged setting should be safe for damaged hair, and after pressing the button to heighten the temp, there is a setting for "healthy" hair. I will say it heats quickly, and it grips your hair very well. I've had curling irons before where the grip wasn't so good and your hair wants to slip out. This curling iron does not do that and holds your hair in place. Even thin hair. The end tip stays cool so you can grasp it and help control your curling iron from end to end. There is also an automatic 60 minute setting in case you forget to turn off the iron. It will shut itself off. I would recommend this product, but gave 4 stars due to the poor instruction manual.

title: Great for multiple applications.
text:
Use this for creating a solution to fix up my eczema almost immediately and it works incredibly well for the job. Another thing I do is add this to my conditioners and it helps my dandruff a lot. Highly recommended.

SOLUTION INSTRUCTIONS FOR ECZEMA FOR ANYONE INTERESTED:

Melt sugar and water down in a pot, let it cool down, and mix the mineral oil and some unmelted sugar with it. Before every application you need to mix the solution (it separates after sitting for a while) and then apply it to the area that has eczema. You want to apply a thick layer and also need to make sure it sits without being rubbed off, which is easy to do. I generally apply it in the shower, but when I start getting really itchy patches on my hands I will continuously apply it until it stops itching and I forget about it.

This can be anywhere from applying it a few times in a single day to applying it a few times a day 3 days or more, depending on how bad it is and how difficult it is to keep the solution from being rubbed off (for example on my hands I have to apply it more often since I rub the solution off easier there). Also you can mix in other essential oils, with my favorite being peppermint since the cooling sensation seems to be the icing on the cake when it comes to stopping the itch. However other essential oils aren't necessary at all, the regular solution does the trick by itself.

My kids think they are great. It took them a little while to get their heads around the fact that the rice paper is edible but now they love it. title: Great concept and design, but software has a lot of problems
text:
I agree with some of the assessments of the PowerUSB device. It has a lot of promise for doing programmable power control via USB, but the software developer interface is very flaky and seems to have problems. The device driver for it appears to be a sample HID device driver, so it doesn't show up in the device list as a named device that can be recognized. Seems like most of the work went into the hardware, but it seems like very little attention was given to the software.

Also, documentation on the programmable API needs some corrections and more information than what it provides.

title: Don't buy this if you wear glasses all day long.
text: This is NOT a long-term solution to the slipping eyeglasses syndrome. I bought this product for a pair of prescription glasses I use every day and only remove at bedtime. The temples for this aged pair of glasses are too short and don't hook around my ears as they should. The EWIN ear-hooks worked fine for at least three weeks. They were comfortable and kept the eyeglass frames from slipping off my nose and falling off during exercise. Unfortunately, after a time the silicone rubberized material breaks down to the point that the ear-hooks become distorted (almost "melting" from constant use) and eventually they lose their grip on the glasses and become useless. I even tried washing them with mild soap and water, thinking that the natural oils in my skin were the culprit, but that proved to be just a temporary solution. After experiencing similar results with the other five pairs of ear-hooks, I gave up and went back to wearing my tried-and-true Croakies (an adjustable nylon lanyard with rubber "soda straw"-type hold-fasts). Although they make me look like an aged librarian and are a bit clunky to put on and take off, at least I won't be dropping my expensive eyeglasses.

title: I can honestly say it felt like my eyes just relaxed instantly
text:
So I bought these, not for me but for my fiance since she has been getting a migraine every week that usually lasts for days. . See, I am getting mine from my VA neurologist and optometrist via the send your own frame in option. I will admit, though they are not my style and I highly disagree with them being for both men and women, I did try them on. I can honestly say it felt like my eyes just relaxed instantly. Her mom tried them on for a minute, and she said that she could see better with them on than with her prescription glasses and her eyes relaxed.

So the true test came starting on Monday. She wore them all day and said except getting harassed for wearing sunglasses indoors, she liked them. Then on Tuesday.....she got a migraine. MAJOR ONE! She actually left work which she almost never does.

She said she continued to wear them (haven't gotten any of her co-workers or her boss's extensions yet to verify), and that they did help her deal with the pain she had with her migraine. She says they are comfortable and that they seem to work and a lot of people are interested in her experiences with them. So as time goes by she will continue to provide me feedback and I will try to update this.

I hope she continues to wear them, as I know I am looking forward to getting mine.

Loss of one star for the lack of claimed unisex styling. These really are not glasses most guys would be wearing, at least not for me or most guys I know.

Update: No migraine this week but due to conducting interviews and not being able to wear them. Will provide better review when she can wear hers more.

title: Best Electric Heated Lash Curler I Have Tried To Date
text:
I purchased this Orikgher Electric Eyelash Curler and another brand curler at the same time. Both curlers were comparably priced. But this Orikgher Curler performed much better than the other heated lash curler.

This Orikgher Eyelash Curler heats up very quickly and feels very lightweight and is easy to use. It is very hot and is far easier to use than the other brand curler I tried. Quality of construction and bonus massager at end of curler is great to massage under eye area with serums.

04/22/2021 Update ~ Unfortunately, I tried charging this lash curler again today, and it did not take a charge. Sadly, stopped working. Will have to return. Really a shame, as I truly liked this lash curler.

I also like the lash brush/comb tool that is included with this curler. Very useful. There were two under eye patches also included, but I haven't tried them yet. This Orikgher Electric Eyelash Curler also comes with a small cleaning brush so you can easily clean the heating element. If you allow your mascara to dry before using this curler, you will find the mascara will not stick to the ceramic heated shaft.

Heated curlers take a little practice. Different than conventional lash curlers, but with patience, you can achieve a lasting curl. Make sure you apply a very light coat of mascara first and allow it to completely dry. Using a small mirror, position the mirror below your eye while looking down. Set shaft of curler at the very base of your lashes, let it sit for a second, then slowly drag curler upwards and back at the same time. The included lash/brush tool is perfect for combing and separating your lashes as you use the curler, as the mascara wants to melt a tiny bit. When desired curl is achieved, apply another light coat or two of your mascara to finish.

title: Large Easy to Read Display
text:
I already own a super accurate bathroom scale but the display is very small and, as my vision has worsened somewhat over the years, it has become increasingly difficult to read it so I was searching for a scale with a very large display that would be easy to see. This scale fulfilled that requirement perfectly. The display is very large, it lights up, and it’s very easy for me to read even without contacts or glasses. It has a very low profile that is slim and sleek while the length and width are comparable to most standard bathroom scales. It looks and feels very well made. I really like that it has a low battery indicator. My current scale does not and the only way you know the batteries are weak is that you start to register really crazy weights, so that feature is a very welcome upgrade. It is also nice that you can change the weight units as I have friends who visit from Australia who like to weigh in Kilograms.

One of the problems I have previously run into with digital scales is that if you get off and then get immediately back on they sometimes do not register the same weight but this one does not have that problem. I have been getting off and then back on multiple times each time I weighed to test that issue and each time I step on it my subsequent weight is exactly the same as the initial one so it appears to be very reliable in that respect. My sole complaint with this scale is that there does not seem to be any way to adjust the weight if you know it to be slightly off. This scale weighs me in at 2.5 lbs. less than my other scale which I know to be accurate as it is always completely in sync with the scale at my physician’s office. title: Best brush ever!
text:
This is the brush I've used for 50 years (and my mother used before me, but she preferred the acrylic). I love the shape and materials. I'll admit that it often loses bristles within the first year or two, which is disappointing, they didn't used to do that. But it works beautifully. As the bristles are natural, if kept cleaned, it naturally cleans the hair, which they don't tend to mention. The half round is perfect for long hair, although I'm not sure it's an advantage with shorter hair, never having had that since I was a child.
The Victorian "brush your hair 100 strokes every day" is an old technique for cleaning hair without shampoo. If you wash the natural bristle brush with soap before each session, it distributes and removes oils and dust. I have personally experimented and went 6 months with no shampoo, and gorgeous hair. If you DON'T wash the brush every day, the bristles will still distribute the oil evenly, but not clean it. This is somewhat pointless in a world where we shower every day, but one can imagine in a world with no central heating and heating wash water on the stove, it would have been invaluable. I still find it great for camping!

title: My feet are looking and feeling better
text:
I don’t normally go on the internet to talk about how gross my feet are, but I know several people who have the same problem with cracking heels during this time of year and we’re all on the quest for some miracle cure. I will preface this review by saying that I have tried many oils (coconut, jojoba, argan, etc.), heavy creams, wearing socks to bed, using those cheese grater/buffer tools for pedicures, drinking more water, and even the peeling foot masks. They have all helped, but only slightly. If you are reading this review, you may understand the pain of cracking heels and the embarrassment of how it looks. To make it worse, I garden a lot, so those cracks get dirty as well, and no amount of washing or soaking seems to diminish this--it only further worsens how dry they are.

When I received this PediBunny callus remover, I did not have high hopes, but I was optimistic that it would accomplish *some* improvement. I am pleased that it comes with 3 rollers (one already attached and 2 extras). It also comes with a cleaning brush (the removed skin can gunk it up), a cover for the roller on the unit, and a charging cord. The device is RoHS compliant, which means I’m not fearful it will shock me or burn up while charging. The PediBunny has a light to indicate when it is charging, and the charge lasts plenty long enough to work on my feet.

I ordered two different brands of rechargeable callus removers within a couple days of one another. The rollers on this one feel a bit rougher, so at first I was afraid it might actually hurt. It does not. The abrasiveness works well to remove callused skin, but the motor is not quite as powerful as the other brand. At times, it momentarily drags, but then quickly regains its speed. I am careful to not overwork one area because I have done that in the past and it makes my skin quite sore the next day. So, this device works best just fine when I run it over a small area at a time, lifting every couple seconds and moving on.

I love that this callus remover is rechargeable. I tend to not get around to buying batteries very often and I don’t like to be limited by wired power devices. I see immediate results after using this product, but it will take ongoing use to get my feet baby soft, which is expected (and I continue to use oils and creams and socks). No miracle, but definitely good results!

I purchased this callus remover at a discount in exchange for my honest review. I did not receive any other compensation, and I am not obligated to write a favorable review. I have used this product myself, and all words in this review are my own.

title: Better for foreplay than for solo use
text:
My husband and I have never used a “sleeve” like the Orgasmate Katerina. My husband thought it looked fancy, and he’s pretty adventurous so we gave it a try.

The box arrived in the regular brown box. The inside box was completely wrapped in black plastic for discretion. As Amazon has to have some method for storing and locating products, I understand the need for the sticker on the black plastic. But it says EXACTLY what it is: Orgasmate Katerina Power A…” Seems like they could use a barcode and scanner for more sensitive products. It’s not really an issue in our house, but worth mentioning for anyone who has nosy roommates: Open the entire shipment in private.

The Orgasmate Katerina is larger than other products we’ve purchased. The size seems consistent with what it is intended for, but do note that you will need to be creative with storage of her. Even though the size is large, it needs to be longer. My husband says it’s kind of tease that it doesn’t accommodate his full length--so it could be a positive and a negative all in one. When he did go further than halfway in, it bogged down a lot. Certainly, the option of being able to go deeper would be preferable.

The instruction manual shows a power button with separate mode and speed buttons. This device only has one button. There are 3 settings controlled with that one button, along with on/off (hold it down to turn it off). My husband prefers the middle setting of the three.

Ergonomically, the exterior shape is easy to hold for solo use or couple use. However, it is heavy after a while.

Husband says this is a good foreplay toy, but he wouldn’t necessarily desire an entire session with it. He rates it at 4 stars as a couples toy and at 3 stars for a solo toy. 3.5 is not an option, so I’m selecting 4.

I purchased this product at a discounted price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I did not receive any other compensation, and I am not obligated to write a positive review.

title: Soft arch relies on shoe sidewall to provide best support
text:
Nearly identical to VALSOLE in the green model that look very similar in every way to these, I find the softer arch found in both brands to best fit a tighter sidewall shoe to best support my arches. These Rooruns feel a bit more cushiony then the Valsole ones I also have. Another notable difference is that the Valsole model had the perforated ball support for ventilation (possibly?) but the Rooruns have a solid ball support.

For me, these are preferred over the Valsole because I'm getting transfer from my socks stuck in the arch area of the Valsole; it's building up to the point I can feel it accumulating. I need to clean those up, if possible; I only noticed this yesterday. I haven't had these as long as the Valsole but I'm hoping the transfer doesn't happen with these. It's likely my feet, fit and my stride that cause this transfer accumulation in the Valsole but I thought it worthy of a mention. Maybe these Rooruns are the upgraded version? For the record, only a guess on my part.

title: Rigid support for plantar fasciitis
text:
The arch is higher and offers some metatarsal support. The feel is more firm than I've felt in prefer plantar fasciitis supports in the past. Maybe this is what you're looking for?

The full bed support is just what I needed to keep my wide feet from feeling the outside of my shoe in a binding hindrance sort of way. Add the firmness of the toe area in this support and I've finally found an insert that helps my 2e width shoe that I had to stretch more with a shoe stretcher to just have a little more room from that toe guard. Or maybe the opportunity found me? Anyway, I'm happy to share my findings. With foot pain, I'm always looking for something better and these didn't disappoint.

Though this is a Vine review, I purchased another pair of this insert for my use in another pair of shoes that I had stretched. The combination of firm support, full foot bed support and extra width in this support is just what I needed for these shoes I've found to be too narrow. They seem to make the stretched shoe a better fit than without these features. But here's another subjective finding with this support I've found: in my use, regular shoe strings tend to loosen and require lace tying again. I prefer elastic shoe strings with these supports. Just saying the shoe may be stretching more or my stride combined with the firmness of this support may be loosening my shoe strings when stepping off numerous steps at a time. So I use the elastic strings where the shoe uses eyelet type lacing. Otherwise, the shoes with loop guides just need retying often because elastic shoe strings tend to get tensioned in some places while loosening in other places where the uses the loop guides instead of eyelets.

Subjectively sharing my experience with this model. This OUSECAN brand maker has other unique inserts that offer other benefits. This one is firm and offers a higher arch than the others. I prefer it for shoes that for tighter on width than the others. I'm currently reviewing two other models from OUSECAN that I also like; but so far, this is the only model that I've purchased another pair of. The other supports by OUSECAN were equally good as this pair reviewed. I was unable to review them and haven't found any OUSECAN brand supports or inserts on Amazon. I do hope to purchase replacements when mine are worn; hopefully that can happen by then.

title: One or two sizes may not fit all
text:
Size 8 to 12? Arch length is a real thing; this tells the manufacturer where to place the arch support. And I didn't think the arch was so far off until I placed it on my foot and felt for the most support. What's wrong? The support has to be moved forward from heel to properly align with and support my arch. In retrospect, low arch height may make it more difficult to guage where arch should be placed; I did replicate this oddity with some other supports I have that are lower than I feel comfortable with. Both my feet can be comfortable in a medium to high arch support. My foot size is on the lower end of the sizing; no idea how the sizing accommodates those feet on the higher end near size 12?

I've tried these supports in more than one pair of active shoes; the result is the same. The right foot gets fatigued with continuous steps that may exceed 2000 at a brisk pace. I'm just not getting the support I need. My right arch is higher and foot is slightly longer. My left foot seems secure, comfortable and relaxed in this support. I really like these for their wider wrap around at the mid foot and grip offered by outermost surface but wish my right foot was as comfortable in them. They do make the foot feel secure with its design.

These supports could be a little higher in the arch. The metatarsal support was a little high for comfort, initially. But I adapted to it or it adapted to me. But the arch won't be able to better adapt my right foot. This review did not include a purchase. But for me to consider a purchase, the arch needs to be higher and the price could be less.

title: Did not work with full length foot supports
text:
I couldn't get these heel cushion pads to stay while reinserting the foot supports. The running shoes I tried these in were short on available heel area with the foot support in place. I couldn't get the pads to behind the supports (they had to angle behind them at the ends). When removing the foot supports and adhering the heel cushion pads, I couldn't get the foot support back in without breaking the seal of the heel cushions. Ruined the first pair of heel cushions I tried.

I did manage with the second pair to angle the foot support in without breaking the seal of the heel cushion. But then it seemed the padding wasn't sufficient or where I wanted it to be too get the shoe to fit more secure at the heel. I had to remove it and find another foot support that didn't make the heel feel less secure.

I tried. But not happy with the result.

title: Nightlight with a good assortment of sounds for sleep and personal time
text:
My daughter was using a more expensive sound machine. But she gave it up for this one. Initially for the night light but also for the ease of selecting other types of sounds for drawing, writing, stretching and concentration.

It recalls the volume and last sound. But will not resume if power is lost and restored. I mention this because the other sound machine I use just has a simple dial for power on and volume. I've kept a constant sound and volume by connecting it to a smart plug that resumes its present dial settings when power is restored by a sleep routine. So why mention this? I can imagine an infant finding comfort by a parent controlling an analog sound machine with a smart plug; sometimes gentle music can soothe a crying infant (like when you're confident it's not diaper or hunger causing the unrest). Can't do that with electronic controls without integrated smart home controls. This sound machine doesn't have smart home controls either. But works well for an older child that doesn't care about automation. So it's a good fit for my child.

This machining did need a standard 5V 1A power plug to get started though. We had extras of those lying around. But know you'll need one if considering this machine.

title: Odd flavor

title: Adjustability if needed
text:
I found these to run smaller than the size chart. If you have wide feet, I'd suggest sizing up and cut accordingly. Better to trim than come up short and narrow.

For support, there's adjustability if you need more arch support. I thought these were great for two of my pairs of shoes. The third pair wasn't as good as a fit. The shoe is 2e width but since these supports are thicker than my original sock liners, I found my toe in the toe box barrier.

I tried a different arch support by Walk Hero which was thinner at the toe box area. Both of these seem better than the rest I've tried and reviewed. I purchased extras of both brands. But I think the Walk Hero brand may offer more metatarsal support unless I can use one of the included discs to add more metatarsal support.

For the money, seems the most expensive isn't always the better support. Some are abrasive. Some are too soft and slippery. But this one features a top finish that's not slippery but sweat wicking and resistant to foot odor.

title: Instructions seem clear until I notice the tapered edges. Now what?
text:
So I'm familiar with my foot type now. I think so? But I've not seen this type of support at toes or metatarsals. At best, I follow the guided outlines. But I got nowhere trying to comprehend what to do with the tapered edges so I guessed. Best guess? Too awkward at edges near toes and metatarsals to put anything. So my guess is, I don't need this extra support or the shoe has some support there already. I did try using the etched guides, flipping tapered edges. Then restored to trimming to find a better fit. Nothing was comfortable so only going with the heel support wedge.

I think I got the heel right so I'll go with that. There appears to be a square support in the heel already. But looking at the rigidness of the orange square and surrounding shell around the heel, this isn't meant to be removed but standing or heel impact will collapse this cushioning level with the hardened shell. So the contoured stick-on will go on this squared orange material rather than cutout around it. I hope that makes sense. But if not, know that I tried to remove the existing square cushion but it's securely attached. It cannot be removed without destroying the heel support. It easily compresses flush with the hardened shell.

So I've settled on my fitting. Kind of narrow around the toes at widest point. Arch support isn't very high, if needed. This might be ok but I decided to just use it on an old shoe that I had discarded the original sock liner in favor of the custom fitted insert. The custom fitted insert eventually failed to provide enough heel and arch support after years of serviceability so I needed something. These were my favorite workout shoes until I lost needed support from the custom insert. May be time to just retire the old shoes but I'll give it a go at least.

title: Not for me
text:
I'm sensitive to the dimpled finish of this insole under my toes. Feels too thin and roomy as well. Doesn't feel comfortable or natural to me, particular under my big toe on each foot. I'm concerned about blistering as well.

I don't think I could recommend these for athletic shoes. I had hoped to cut to size since shoes like Under Armor have unique curves. So wider would have been ideal. And most original sock liners will also have cupped heels. These adjustability features, if included, would have helped to hold the insole in place.

If someone were looking for more room in a tight shoe, this may be ideal; if removable, replace the sock liner. Washing may help with the texture feeling but I didn't try that since these weren't what I expected them to be.

title: Loods Good, Works Great!
text:
I needed a better light by my chair to read by, and I wanted to get the current lamp off the table to free up some room, so I went shopping for a good reading floor lamp. I researched lamps, read reviews, studied various types of light, and finally decided to order this one. The research must've paid off because I really like this lamp.

I can't say how easy or hard it was to unpack or put together, since my husband did it for me while I wasn't home, but it looks great and works well. I got the nickel finish and it looks good with our decor. The height of the lamp is adjustable and the light itself swivels so I can get the whole thing positioned right where it needs to be to shine light on what I'm reading without blinding others in the room. title: Superior to other brands, and comes nicely packaged like a gift
text:
Reviewing fingernail and toenail clippers was not something I could really get into, or talk about, but these are actually the most exceptional clippers I've ever used. I'm inspired! Well, enough to say something about this product.

First, it comes in a lovely yellow tin, about the size of an Altoids box, but much less cheap. The brand name HAWATOUR, is center placed. The tin itself is a giftie, with strong hinges and a foam insert with cut indentations for each clipper to sit. And the clippers are very attractive with a nice smooth texture, but not like those cheap generic ones you see and probably have owned. Even on the base of each clipper, the brand name appears, apparent yet unobtrusive, a yellow ID blended in.

As for its integrity--I'm impressed. The file part, instead of the usual clumsy and useless band, is set like an insert, and is far more effective at filing--is, in fact, quite effective. The cutters are really sharp, and extend a bit further out than the generic ones. They cut precisely and quickly. Holding the clippers feels almost ergonomic; the weight and leverage was given though in the design, so that the clippers work effortlessly.

These would make great stocking stuffers or one of those White Elephant party gifts. You will not be disappointed!

title: It works as advertised!
text:
As a working RN, I have to wear a mask for twelve hours straight. My reading glasses fog up, my mouth is always making contact with the inside of the mask, and I continually feel like I'n breathing hot oxygen--it is always too warm inside my mask. I've been searching for relief from these issues, and as such I have bought too many masks promising plenty of solutions. But, alas, I still feel suffocated and foggy under my mask.

Until these silicone 3D Brackets came along! I had my doubts, although it also had a logic to it that promised results and a fix. And they work! I just-it it inside the mask before placing the mask on my face, and it stays in place by virtue of the mask itself covering it. No fogging up of my glasses! And I can breathe at least 80% more freely! There will never be a mask that feels massless, but this is the closest thing to that airy comfort we seek. I've given some away to friends, and they give me the same positive feedback as I expected.

The is a serious improvement over a mask flush against my face. If you seek relief from all the problems of mask wearing--and it even relieves the "claustrophobia" of mask-wearing--then try these out. I'm certain that you won't be disappointed!

title: Gentle on skin, and feels refreshing
text:
I've never owned a deep cleaning facial brush before, so I didn't know what to expect or who to compare it to. I'm also wary of beauty product adverts that promise miraculous results. My skin isn't perfect and sometimes I get blackheads on my nose, so I thought I'd give it a whirl. I tried it first at the sink, scrubbing my face with it while standing at the mirror. And, whoa! The problem with using this at the sink is that water splashes everywhere! So I had to switch to the shower. That's the only reason I'm giving it 4 instead of 5 stars, because it makes a mess if I do this at the sink, and I'd like to do this twice a day without getting in the shower both times.

However, the brush is so soft and gentle; I was surprised. It felt nice on my face and my skein felt refreshed after I finished. I'm just trying different speeds. If there are instructions on what to use the 3 speeds for, I'm in the dark, as the inserted instructions are not in English. It would have been nice to include them, but most of it is intuitive to figure out.

The HOEE also comes with a charger and a second brush. How long does a brush last, I wonder? Not having used this before, I wouldn't know, but I hope they last longer than a toothbrush. I wouldn't know where to buy (or if I could) replacement brushes. Maybe it is written here in the Asian language instructions?

There's not much that a beginner in these products can say. The circular movements feel kind to my face, but it will take time to see if there are notable results. For now, I'm pleased with my daily facial.

title: An excellent therapeutic tool
text:
For anyone working in the psychiatric community, as I do, you know the value of stress-balls, also known as fidgets. For kids, adolescents, or adults, for that matter, who have ADHD or Spectrum Disorders, stress-balls/fidgets help channel energy that would otherwise be disruptive or socially unacceptable. When I was offered a set of stress-balls from Convenient Products for evaluation/review purposes, I could hardly pass up this opportunity.

These are quality made stress-balls, and has been the case in the past, are not easily destroyed. I use them in the morning groups, in the facility where I work, and the kids and adolescents request them. I see them squeezing them appropriately and not trying to pick them apart. I truly believe that the presentation is part of the appeal. These balls come in a variety of interests--various balls used in sports, globes, and happy faces. Usually, I allow the kids to pick their preference. Data will confirm that fewer problem behaviors occur when an option for channeling energy is used. I am a firm believer in these products.

I highly recommend this product from Creative Products. My kids seem happier during morning groups, and they even request these stress balls at other times of the day in an effort to self regulate their behaviors.

title: Cute beyond winsome, perfectly rescued by stylish, quirky charm
text:
Set in 60s France, all in poster bright cartoon colours and a rather anarchic, slapstick performance style, this is a child's eye view of the world.

Nicolas (an enchanting performance by serious faced Maxime Godart) mistakenly assumes his mother is pregnant and is afraid he will be abandoned and unwanted when the new baby arrives. With his goofy collection of young friends he embarks on various plans to get rid of the baby.

Meanwhile, his parents are worried about money, trying to climb the social ladder, currying favour with Nicolas's father's boss - a hilarious dinner party scene, where you know every single gag before it happens, but delight in the infectious, witty performances.

This really is a totally feel-good film, but done with great wit and style, by all performers.

It is the quirkiness, the great look of the film, the expertise of the performances and somehow a lack of saccharine sentimentality that make this so good.

French Film, English subtitles, 91 minutes. This really is a film that can be enjoyed by both children AND adults. In patronises neither audience, nor does it indulge or overplay its feel-good nature. The length of the film is just right and stops the good jokes and set pieces from overstaying their welcome

title: A GOOD FLOSSER/TOOTHBRUSH
text:
I've used a separate power flosser and toothbrush for years, but wanted an all-in-one unit that would take up less counter space and would be portable enough for travel. This one seems to fill the bill nicely. The water pressure for the flosser is almost as strong as my Waterpic plug-in unit. The toothbrush is surprisingly good. It is very soft and does a very good job of cleaning the teeth. It does not brush as aggressively as my Oral B, yet the soft bristles combined with the high rate of vibration actually makes my teeth feel cleaner!

This is fairly easy to use. For flossing, you attach the water hose to the handle, attach the flosser tip to the handle and you're good to go. The tank holds enough water for over 2 minutes of flossing. When you are done, you empty the tank, detach the water hose and flosser tip, then attach the toothbrush tip. Both the flosser and the toothbrush have 3 speeds and 2 different time intervals. The time interval settings are interesting. Most electric dental appliances have a 2 minute timer. But this one let you choose between 1 minute and 2 1/2 minute intervals.

For travel, battery power frees you from having to deal with a cord to plug in. And the addition of a separate water hose means you do not need to take the entire unit with you - any cup or glass that holds water will do.

I should mention that this unit is sold under two different brand names on Amazon. The other brand only comes with 1 toothbrush and 1 flosser tip, but does include a small bag for travel. I had originally ordered the other brand. What I learned was that, in spite of the instructions, do not remove the water tank for filling and emptying. I did that and the water valve in the tank fell apart. This could have been a flaw in the manufacture of the unit I received, but decided to play it safe and keep the tank attached at all times. Because the unit is so light and compact, filling and emptying the tank while attached is very easy.

On a final note, I have not had this long enough to comment on its battery life. I'll update this review at a later date when I get some experience with the battery life. But overall, I believe this is a good purchase if you want the compactness of a flosser/toothbrush in one unit, and want the portability the battery power and separate water hose provides.

title: For the toastiest feet!
text:
As I sit here writing this review, I feel completely relaxed as my feet are bathed in the warmth of being surrounded by this foot warmer.

It's one of those products that you really didn't think you needed until you finally try it.

The heating blanket seems to be extremely well constructed. It's made of very soft fabric -- particularly in the foot pocket which contains fleece for extra comfort. The bottom of the blanket is lined with gripped padding to keep it in place while in use.

The included wired controller provides an ample amount of cord leeway for easy placement. There are 6 different heating levels that the blanket can be set for along with preset timers for auto shut-off.

The manufacturer claims that the Double-sided heating pad is controlled separately. As far as I can see, this is not the case. The supplied controller does not indicate separate heating functions nor does the included instructions. Is this something you should be concerned about? Well, this product is considerably more expensive than similar alternatives and if doesn't perform as described, you shouldn't be paying more for it.

Personally, my only intent of use is to insert my feet into the pocket of the blanket. I currently have the blanket turned all the way up (level 6), and it seems rather perfect without being too hot. I have found that my feet get so wonderfully warm that when I finally remove them in a 72-degree room, it suddenly feels cold.

The inside of the blanket is very roomy -- almost too much so. While it's nice to be able to have the freedom to move your feet around while inside, it just seems a bit too large for its purpose.

It seems like this should be very easy to clean. You unzip and remove the heating pad from the fabric before throwing it into the washer. The instructions claim that there are storage straps to hold everything together when not in use -- but yet another feature that is not actually included with this product.

Bottom line: This foot warmer is considerably more expensive than others I have seen on Amazon. The fact that it is "Double-Sided" may be a perk for some. I don't think this gets hot enough across the top to work as a normal heating blanket for injuries. While the manufacturer claims separate heating controls, it certainly isn't related to the included controller. The so-called storage straps mentioned in the instructions aren't to be found anywhere.

If you do opt to pay more for this, I think you are getting an exceptionally well-built blanket that should last you a long time. However, I would also consider cheaper options.

title: Don't consider these toilet tablets
text:
I have never been more let down by a product than this.

I do a lot of traveling with my girlfriend and we are very respectful of each other when it comes to bathroom odors. We always bring along a small bottle of spray specifically made for toilet use. You simply spray three squirts into the bowl before using the toilet and it does a remarkable job of covering up embarrassing odors.

I was really excited about these tablets. They look to be a more convenient solution when traveling due to the fact that they are tiny and easy to throw into luggage. I was eager not to have to deal with a spray solution anymore and simply throw a tablet into the bowl before using it.

Here's the huge problem with this product...

It's a total failure.

So, imagine this: Nature is calling and you have to use the toilet immediately. You throw one of these tablets into the bowl and then....you wait...and wait...and wait...and wait. It took a single tablet more than 15 minutes to completely dissolve. Is anyone going to hold back their movement to wait that long for the product to ready itself?

What's worse is that when the tablet finally dissolved, it left an ugly discolored stain on the bottom of the bowl and absolutely no discernable scent to cover up what comes next.

I couldn't believe how poorly this performed and I was really disappointed as I had such high hopes.

I would love to give you some sound advice: If you are looking for something to cover up toilet odors I highly recommend the small sprays made by Air Jungles and Clean-And-Fresh. You spray three times before toilet use and they are highly effective in masking odors.

This product should not be considered.

title: What you should know when investing in this foot massager
text:
[[VIDEOID:9e29f50fd04feddb524fde569839d071]] When considering spending nearly $150 for this Sharper Image product I think it's important to know the pros and cons of this purchase and whether this will make for a sound investment when it comes to your health.

My first impression when taking this out of the box is that this is a well-built heavy piece of furniture/machinery weighing in at a little over 12 lbs.

With an overall height of approx. 6.5" off the ground, it seems a bit of a "stretch" to call this an Ottoman. I am used to such pieces of furniture being much taller. My opinion is that this comes across as more of a footstool.

That being said, it looks like a nice piece of furniture, handsomely covered in fabric. When in use, a long cord protrudes from the top cushion. That cord can be removed and stored when you wish to make its functionality less noticeable to those who visit your home.

The top cushion of the Ottoman easily flips over, serving two purposes. On its flat Ottoman side, it's a simple footrest that provides heat and/or vibration. When you flip the cushion over, a more elaborate Shiatsu function allows you to slip your feet into sleeves for a customized massage.

Now that I have given you an overview of this Sharper Image product, let me dive into my impressions using the Ottoman and Shiatsu functions.

As I previously noted, this really doesn't act as an Ottoman. So, if you are relaxing in your favorite chair, this serves more like a footstool. The Ottoman functionality is not very exciting. It's basically a heated vibrating pad for your feet. A small button in the upper corner lets you choose vibration, heat, or both. I really don't see the benefit of having a constant level of vibration and a slight amount of heat being applied to my feet. If this were all that this Ottoman offered, this would be a big fail in my opinion.

But fortunately, there's more...

When I pulled a tab and flipped the cushion over to the Shiatsu side, things got more interesting. I slipped my feet into the sandal-like sleeves, turned on the power, and felt the rollers inside the unit provide an intense massage to the bottom of my feet. As this was happening, the sandal-like sleeves that cover my feet began to compress tightly and release. The combination of bottom rollers, and top compression in constant motion along with a little bit of added heat provided for a very soothing and relaxing sensation.

I must say, the Shiatsu aspect of this device is the most compelling. I think that it could probably do wonders for sore, tired feet. The motor inside is very powerful and as a result, the level of massage is very satisfying. Of course, if it's too much too quick, you can lower the intensity of the massage.

So, I have mixed feelings about this very expensive device.

It's certainly well-built. It's a handsome piece of furniture though I would not consider it an Ottoman. The flat side does nothing more than vibrate and provides a little heat (it never really gets noticeably hot). The Shiatsu side is quite good as it provides a really strong acupressure massage to the feet.

I almost feel you could spend less money and get something that's not designed to be furniture in order to get an equally good Shiatsu massage. However, if you opt for this Sharper Image massager you are getting an expensive, but solid product.

title: Very capable portable water flosser
text:
This is the second similar type of portable water flosser I have obtained, for which I am giving my girlfriend as she has watched me with envy as I use it while traveling.

These portable flossers are great. They deliver a very powerful stream of water to the teeth and gum line which easily pushes away food particles on and in between teeth. They are so powerful in fact that they rival the Waterpik units that have become a staple of bathroom hygiene for so many years.

This flosser by Miracleplus deserves the professional moniker. It is well constructed and (as I mentioned) quite powerful. It's also very simple to use: charge the flosser with the USB cable (power brick not included) and then fill the reservoir tank with water.

This kit includes 5 different snap-in nozzles, one of which is a tongue scraper. There are five different power modes to deliver water to your teeth, one of which is a nice massage burst and the other designed for softer delivery for sensitive teeth.

The inclusion of a digital readout is a nice added touch. It not only displays the currently selected power mode but also the remaining battery level.

What I love about this and similar flossers is that you get about the same amount of water power delivered to your teeth in this portable unit as you do with the larger home ones. At the same time, it's portable enough to simply throw this into your suitcase or an overnight bag.

If you have never owned a portable flosser before I think you'll be really surprised how much water power these units deliver to your teeth. It's certainly a quicker and more fun way to floss than using string between your fingers.

This looks to be a very capable, well-constructed flosser that should stand up to a rigorous amount of use both in your suitcase and in your bathroom. Don't think twice about purchasing.

title: For a fraction of the price of the Oral-B brand
text:
I love manufacturers who make these replacement brush heads.

In the past, when I first bought my Oral-B electric toothbrush, I would go to the store and shell out over 2x more the price of what these third-party replacement heads cost.

If you look through some of my past reviews I have tried many third-party replacement heads. For the most part, they are all good.

I am particularly favorable to this brand because within their two 4-packs of replacements they offer the floss-type replacement head which is my favorite to use.

I compared this replacement to the original Braun floss brush that I had on hand. They are almost exact in appearance and this brand from Yaloon fits the Braun toothbrush perfectly. Just by touch, the Braun brand floss bristles seem a little bit stiffer, however I just finished brushing my teeth with the Yaloon replacement and I can't tell the difference. The Yaloon brand gave me the same exceptional clean that I have come to expect from Braun.

What's nice about this dual four-pack is that it gives you a nice variety of brush heads. I like the floss-type heads but I have others in my family that regularly use the standard ones.

If this is your first time buying replacement heads not made by Braun, don't be nervous. Most all these off-brands are just as good as the original and this one is no exception. The great thing is, you will be paying more than half the price you normally will for replacements. I believe once you try this brand you won't want to go back to the Braun name again.

title: Exceptional travel flosser!
text:
I think I can speak for most people when I say, "I hate flossing!" I find it a hassle to measure out the string and then stand in front of the mirror, pulling the floss through each row of teeth

I did find a way of dealing with the task. I bought an electric Waterpik flosser. I must say, that flosser has entirely improved my oral cleaning habits. It's like a power wash for your teeth and it does an excellent job of loosening food stuck in-between teeth.

As I travel often, I don't have the luxury of taking such a large home flosser unit with me. My morning routine in my hotel room consists of standing in the mirror with floss in hand. When I am away from home, I absolutely miss my Waterpik.

I actually came upon this portable flosser by accident and it took me by surprise. I never knew these things existed or even COULD exist. If you have ever used a home water flosser, you know that they are very powerful and push a hard stream of water against your teeth. I never imagined that could actually be replicated in a wireless product.

In fact, when I ordered this portable water flosser, I didn't actually think it would work. However, at best, this would be an interesting experiment for me and if I was dissatisfied with the way it performed, I would ship it back to Amazon.

The flossing unit is rather large. It's bigger than holding a full tube of toothpaste in the hand. It also has a bit of weight to it. Of course, something like this would need a heavier motor and it would have to be large enough to hold a considerable amount of water.

It came out of the box partially charged so I was able to test it immediately. This flosser included a USB charging cable but you will need to supply your own USB charging brick. You can use one of the small 5 volt adapters that come with most mobile phones. I used one of my iPhone charging bricks.

The flosser also comes with 4 flossing tips designed for different types of floss applications. Honestly, I don't know much about what tip does what, but I immediately went for the standard tip as that is what I use in my Waterpik home flosser.

This brings me to a concerning point: I am not certain where I can buy replacement tips or if they are standardized across the board. For instance, I found that Waterpik tips do not fit in this flosser. I am hoping the industry has set some sort of standard for the size of these tips so that they can easily be replaced. The good news is, these tips do last a long time before having to be replaced.

When inserting one of the tips into this flosser you simply need to insert and then twist the tip to lock. The included instructions do a great job of illustrating the process. The next step is to fill the reservoir with water, secure and turn it on.

Here is the point where I became very impressed...

This is very powerful for a portable flosser. The stream of water that ejected from the tip was forceful enough that it removed slivers of food I had stuck in my teeth from dinner. I mean, I look down in the sink and there they were! I did have to refill the reservoir more than once to do a complete job, but I knew this would not handle nearly as much fluid as my home unit.

There are different modes of strength that include Normal, Soft and Pulse. I always enjoy the pulsating action as it feels good against my teeth.

Bottom line: If you are thinking of a powerful home flosser, I would first recommend a Waterpik as they are more powerful and hold more water, However, that's not taking any merits away from the Misiki flosser. It's more than half the cost, is nearly as powerful, and boasts something that the Waterpik home units can't: the ability to be portable.

I can now take a powerful flosser with me on vacation. At last, I can ditch the string and enjoy the same flossing benefits on the road that I do at home. I am really impressed with how powerful this thing is. Recommended!

UPDATE 6/27/2014 --Still works like brand new----does not flatten out after use...returns to full thickness.  /  Because of how I sit and move a lot in chair, pad does slip forward sometimes, but hey, SLIDE IT BACK ! / note..front of pad had strap to carry or move it by --- each side of cushion is slightly different, whichever you like facing up. title: Good value, hard to swallow
text:
First, I have no idea if this works on inflammation. I have chronic pain similar to fibromyalgia and, so far, the only thing that helps are painkillers and ice. I keep taking it because I like the fiber and figure the other micronutrients must be doing something good for me.

I don't know who can swallow this stuff straight or mix it into food. Makes me choke. There are pieces of fiber that have the consistency of straw and are scratchy and hard to say the least. These pieces look like the stuff I pick out of my socks after I take a walk through weeds. As for the taste--it's neutral--again, sort of like sawdust. Neither bitter nor sweet nor tangy. Definitely dry and woody.

So... I mix it with it water, strain it through a metal mesh strainer, then mix the result with anything more palatable. Here's my process: Mix one tablespoon powder to one cup lukewarm water. Wait about 15 minutes. Then strain through a metal mesh strainer and push what's left in the strainer through with a spoon, scraping the bottom of the strainer on the edge of the glass. I get about 75% of the good stuff and throw the remainder out. I either drink the resulting mixture straight (1/3 at a time, through the day), or mix it in with something else, like juice, or a protein drink.

This is an exceptional value compared to Nopalea drink, any other brand of cactus-based mixed drink currently marketed, and even the cactus powder capsules. And you know what you're getting.

title: Works wonders for me
text:
I love this little thing. I tend to go hours without drinking anything when I’m working. I just don’t realize I’m thirsty. I’ve been trying to drink more water to help alleviate some health issues in a very simple, natural way. This little guy fits perfectly around both of my water bottles. Just like the product description says, it strobes at you (it’s too fast to say blink) and once you’ve set the bottle back down, it gives you a long blink to confirm. What I especially like is the sensor/timer in the unit will take into account any drinks you take in between strobes. It is also light sensitive so it’s not waking me up in the middle of the night to get a drink.

There are a couple things that I’m not a big fan of and are the reasons I give this 4/5 stars. First, I think it’s a bit expensive for what you get. Even though it works wonderfully, it just seems what you get doesn’t warrant the price tag. It doesn’t connect to your phone or any health apps and it doesn’t track anything for overall totals. Second, I had actually had to purchase a second unit because it came unclipped to the band somewhere along the way and I lost it. I’ve superglued the second unit to the band this time around but it’s a bummer that it happened causing me to spend more money.

Overall, I really like this product and I definitely get my use out of it, however, I think’s it’s a bit pricey for what you get. I still use it daily, though!

title: A Pretty Decent waterpic....
text:
I had written a review to the company selling it already, however I spoke a little too quick... Now I have had it for a few weeks and can speak with more authority. It's a good unit, however the lid that protects the water container is of two pieces hinged together, to hold extra water pic heads . That is a neat idea, however it comes apart when you take the lid off to fill with water. I glued the hinged part together and put the pics in a drawer. then I found it sticky to get off to fill with water. (The manufacturer did an incredibly good job of making that lid fit mucho perfect... Good plastic work.
Problem with that good fit is that when you are in a hurry in the morning it is common to fumble it and even drop the lid into the water,, sooooo I glued a knob on top of the lid to pull it off and ground off the protrusion behind the hings that pressures down over the water container. Now it is perfect and doesn't stick down when trying to remove the lid before pouring in water. If the seller would encourage the manufacturer to glue a knob on top it would likely solve this problem.
Also the hand wand is made for a little girl or small woman's hand so a little awkward for an average sized man or woman. That is liveable but the wand could have been made bigger with it's switch for turning on and off.
I still like it very much, now that I've corrected those two problems with the lid.
Someone from the seller kind of mocked me when I wrote in and gave suggestions but that is ok because often those people are $2/hr people who are grumbling about having to sit at a computer and phone all day..... Hope they get a life better soon.

title: Poor Choice for Modern NiMH C and D Cells
text:
The problem here is that a good NiMH D cell is 9000-10000 mAh. Look at the spec sheet for this charger: a C/D cell is listed as 3000 mAh. So a good D cell has 3 times the capacity listed in the specs for this charger. So the specs say it can charge a 3000 mAh battery in 8 hours, but what about a 9000 mAh battery? The charger shuts off after 8 hours so leaving the battery in longer hoping for a full charge isn't the answer. Three cycles, taking them out and putting them back in every 8 hours?

A good Tenergy C cell is 5000 mAh and a good Tenergy D cell is 10000 mAh. Of course, there are other brands comparable to Tenergy; Rayovac is not one of them. For those who use just AA/AAAs or low end, cheap C and D NiMH cells this charger will be fine, but slow. For the rest of us, it'll collect dust once replaced with something decent.

For AA or AAA cells the Sony BCG-34HRMF4 is a much better charger in this price range: batteries don't have to be charged in pairs, there is an independent status indication for each battery, and it fits easily in luggage.

I'm replacing my Rayovac Platinum with a Tenergy Advanced Universal Charger TN190, which I'll review soon after it arrives.

title: Once hated, now prized.
text:
When I first heard one of these I HATED it. I was in an office out somewhere and it was already quiet in the room. All I could hear was this loud constant whoosh and it rivaled the noise in my head. I could not stand it.

But my husband started running a box fan in the bedroom at night and I was getting cold. Not to mention dust I'm allergic to would fly if it'd been a few days after vacuuming. I thought of this unit. I was already used to the fan noise at night. This thing had to improve the shiver/dust situation.

Oh, did it. It's become essential for my husband to get good sleep at night, and I've noticed when it's off that I go to sleep better and faster once I turn it on, especially now that I'm not freezing from all that blowing box fan air.

Months later I realized I was constantly agitated from high noise levels in a poorly sound-proofed home, but didn't know how to fix it. In the meantime, I'd bought a unit for my dad because trains were waking him up at night. However, it annoyed him like it had first annoyed me, so he didn't continue to use it. Then I thought of this unit and wondered if it might actually help mask the daytime noises, so Dad let me bring it home.

I regret not getting one sooner.

In a noisy environment, this thing gives me peace of mind. In my home office I can finally think when my husband is watching the yapper (TV) in the other room. And the kids and dogs amping up the noise, along with my constant companion, Tinnitus, fade away in this sweet, soothing whoosh.

My tinnitus makes me sensitive to high pitched noises, so I'm grateful I can adjust the pitch to what feels best to my ears. Perhaps that's why the first unit I heard drove me nuts--wrong pitch for me. I close most of the top and side holes for a lower pitch. Open them for a higher, louder pitch, and I start climbing the walls, but others might like it much better than what feels good to my being.

This was by far a valuable purchase for us and I recommend it to anyone needing some mental solitude in a loud environment.

title: Thought I woke up in Shoes made for a King.
text: I was considering having custom shoes made. I see Poron inserts offered by many of the custom shoe companies, there must be a reason. but it's my money and I wanted to be sure before spending several hundred, or thousand, dollars on shoes that I would regret.  I wanted to try the Poron first.  The sheet was the obvious way to go for the money spent. I was able to cut inserts for 3 pair of shoes ( 6 inserts Size 9 Mens ) and still have half of the sheet left for my wife . . if it works.  I started with my walking shoes.  I traced, cut and inserted a Poron sheet under my orthotic foodbeds; 5 miles one morning without the Poron sheets under my orthotic and the next day 5 miles with the Poron insert.  It's difficult to describe the difference pre and post Poron inserts, but after trying Poron in street shoes I can't imagine being without it.  So, the next day I tried the same 5 miles in a not high end COSTCO tennis shoe that's been in my closet for years; sans Poron the first day, with sore feet at the end of 5 miles.  During my walk I had decided to put the Tennis shoes in the garage for painting projects.  The next day I cut and inserted Poron inserts into the same not very expensive COSTCO tennis shoes under a mid-range off-the-shelf orthotic footbed.  I would have thought I paid hundreds of dollars for the COSTCO shoes.  What a difference.  The tennis shoes went back into my closet as an alternative to my high end walking shoes.  It seems that you need to match the shoe, shoe volume and orthotic to be sure it's perfect with each foot and model of shoe, but with good eyesight, a pencil, a pair of scissors and kindergarten skill set anybody can do it.  I have cut inserts for all but one pair of shoes and wouldn't think of going without the Poron. Truth be told I'm not sure I need the custom shoes.  My standard shoes, with the Poron, are damn near the comfort in the footbed that I expected with my custom made shoes.

title: Two words: NIACIN FLUSH
text:
This is an excellent product and a great all-in-one (minus creatine, but, that's inexpensive to purchase separately) with only one flaw I can find: Way. Too. Much. Niacinamide. Niacinamide is touted as the "no-flush" Niacin, but I think they have managed to put so much into one serving that even someone who is used to daily Niacin supplementation could easily get a niacin flush depending on the kind of exercise they do. I, personally, was doing push-ups when my face lit up red and felt painfully itchy/irritated. Knowing what a niacin flush feels like from prior experience, I checked the label after my workout and saw "Niacinamide: 75g (469%)" which seems unnecessary.

That said, this stuff is otherwise excellent and I'll probably keep using it anyway. I had great focus and endurance, the flavor was good (I went for "Pina Koala"), it seemed to mix fairly easily in roughly 8oz of cold water, and I have no complaints whatsoever except for what I mentioned above. Since I'm rating both the product and the experience, though, and since I'm going to spend the next several workouts with a burning itchy forehead until/unless my body acclimates to such ludicrously high dosages... that's enough to lose two stars by itself.

title: It just makes good sense.
text:
Let's say you've just come in from the garden and your hands are dirty. Would it make sense for you to use only paper towels (no water) to clean-up? And, haven't we all been told that we should wash our hands after using the bathroom? Do you do that with dry paper? No, water is used in all such instances....as it should be.

The multi-billion dollar toilet paper industry has an extreme vested financial interest in seeing to it that American consumers continue and increase their use of TP products. They spend millions annually in advertising to convince buyers of the value of their products. At one time I suspect that Mr. Wipple was better known than some rock stars. All things considered, it is downright amazing that bidets have not caught on in this country. The one "place" on our bodies that deserves real cleanliness goes unattended except for dry paper....no matter how soft it is! In this regard, Europeans seems to be ahead of us....bidets are more common there or so I've been told.

I don't recall now how I discovered bidets..its been several years ago. But to date (Dec 2011)...I have purchased and installed three of these inexpensive units in my home and in a summer house out in the country. I've given one as a gift(strange, I know). I have no trouble with cool water bidets but some might prefer that both hot and cold water be combined (that can be done but with more expensive unites and more complicated installation) This unit is simple and easy to install. You don't need to be a plumber but it's a good idea to read the instructions before you begin. It does exactly what it promises, and does it well for a very reasonable price. I've never had a problem with a leak though I suggest that after installation, you observe for a few days to insure water-tightness.

I have grown so use to having a bidet that I find I miss them when traveling away from home for more than a few days. In addition to the cleanliness factor, they also help reduce the use of TP as it is only needed to pat dry. Studies have shown that using a bidet reduces many anal problems, hemorrhoids for example. To use a pun...at the bottom of all this is just a cleaner bottom!

title: Might Come In Handy For Drivers
text:
The "Oasser Breathalyzer Breath Tester" is a multi-functional tool for checking one's blood alcohol content (BAC) that is compact enough to be carried in a purse or pocket. It is powered by a rechargeable Lithium battery and comes with a micro USB data cable for recharging. It comes with 4 reusable mouthpieces and I\it states that there is a one-year support program.

The unit can store up to 10 previous readings and has an alarm/alert system that using lights and a buzzing to warn users that they have exceeded a 0.05 BAC with the reading. Judging its accuracy is difficult without anything to compare it with, but it seems somewhat accurate so far based on the number of ounces ingested in a particular time frame. ..i.e. 2 drinks in a one hour period.

The accompanying directions leave a lot to be desired but most people can figure the process by simply experimenting a bit. One feature did bring a smile to my face-the "hammer" attachment designed to break a car window if a need to escape a wrecked or flooded vehicle. The metal "hammer" extension is nestled in the battery storage compartment so the user would have to keep it attached awkwardly to the device full time or keeping calm enough in an emergency to release the battery compartment cover, remove the hammer extension, and attach it before trying to escape. And I have serious doubts as to this lightweight plastic unit with a one inch metal attachment being able to easily break out a window. Just seems a somewhat incongruous extra for a BAC tester.

title: You will be amazed!
text:
I just got this delivered today and immediately unboxed it and tried it out. I'm a black woman and about 5 mo ago I decided to stop using chemicals in my hair (had a body wave). As you can imagine, my hair was getting very hard to comb through as the new growth really started to kick in. I had tried a flat iron (for the first time) a few days ago and it was soooo time-consuming and I did not like the results. My hair is VERY thick and I thought my arm would fall off so I did it kind of half-assed. With that experience I knew I would probably never use the thing again. Anyway, I plugged up the brush and it heated very quickly, in moments it was ready. I put it on 150C starting out. I increased to 160 since it seemed to work better on a higher setting for my hair.

Now, I have seen bad reviews on here saying how it didn't work at all or not that well. I am wondering if these people had the setting up high enough. Also, if the temperature was high enough, how were you brushing it through your hair? The key is to SLOWLY brush your hair. You also cannot use it like a regular brush, meaning you should do a section at a time and use one hand to hold the hair and give it some tension as you brush through it. That's what I did, anyway. It's no different a concept than using a hot comb (only much safer and much more unlikely you will burn your ear off lol).

So, as far as the actual product goes, it's great. It does what it says it will do, assuming you are using it properly. I honestly don't know how I have lived without this in my life for so long. My only gripe (which, I felt, wasn't reason to lose any stars) is the placement of the on/off and temperature buttons. It is a very inconvenient place and you WILL accidentally hit the buttons while you are brushing your hair. It's just not a good place to put the controls. I feel it should be further down on the handle and perhaps on the under side of it, as opposed to the side of the handle or the back. The user manual also leaves a little bit to be desired. I doubt a native English speaker wrote it. You will get the gist of what's going on though. Even though the controls are in Celsius, you can change it to Fahrenheit. Just don't ask me how this is accomplished because it is not in the manual. The change was triggered by my numerous, accidental, button presses toggling between C and F and I didn't pay attention to what was actually initiating the change. One of the previous reviewers said there is a way to lock the controls by pressing power so many times but left out how many times lol... I may update my review if I play with it to actually unlock this hidden power.

tl;dr

Buy it, learn how to use it, and you will love it!

title: Gets The Job Done FAST!
text:
First off, my hair is mid back length, partly dyed, fairly thick and *mostly* straight with a few rogue waves here and there. Unfortunately my hair is noticeably frizzy and I purchased the Kingdomcares Ionic Hair Brush for a straighter look and more importantly to get rid of the frizzy-ness from dyeing and abusing my hair for years. That being said, I cannot attest to how well it would work if you have very curly hair since I didn't buy it for that reason though I can't see from using this brush why it wouldn't work quite well. What I can say is that it does a great job at keeping my hair smoother and silkier than without it. I had one of the ceramic plate hair straighteners which I believe works better overall because you can drag it all the way to the ends. However, I find the plate straightener is much more time-consuming as well as unwieldy to use. This 'brush' is more like a wide tooth comb and has a swivel cord so it's as easy as just combing your hair out once it's dry. It's fast and it works! What takes 30 minutes with a ceramic plate straightener can be done in less than 10 minutes with this one! The only problem with it and for which I subtracted a star is because once you get towards the very ends, the hair falls through the comb teeth and it doesn't straighten well in that area. Unlike other actual brush-type units that have plastic guards so you can keep your hand over the brush to keep the ends in place while you brush through, you cannot do that with this one without risking a burn.

Overall, I'd highly recommend it. My daughter who also has straight hair but much longer and thicker than mine loves the ease of this comb over her ceramic plate one, hands down.

Dimensions: Massaging surface is about 7 inches laid flat; there are 4 rolling rows that are 3 inches wide, each has 5 rings with 8 nodules each. Each set of the 2 rolling rows can rotate approximately 180 degrees.
