title: Not sandalwood
text:
This is NOT sandalwood. [See update at bottom] I was really excited after reading the good reviews and having a ridiculously hard time finding an affordable sandalwood oil, so I ordered this. This is a blend of essential oils meant to smell like sandalwood, and it almost does — for the first second or two you sniff the bottle. Then it starts to smell like plastic flowers. If this is what some people think sandalwood smells like, they have a wonderful surprise coming when they smell a,real sandalwood or a good approximation.

The bottle says 100% essential oil, it's labeled as simply "Sandalwood", but doesn't show the botanical names of the oils that are in it. It smells like geranium and rubber tree. If there's ANY sandalwood in this, I can't smell it. I don't even smell any Amrys. Just saw another reviewer who said the same thing, and I'll second her statement that it's "perfumy". (That's being kind. Perfume sprayed on a big rig's tire after a cross-country haul is more like it.) I wish I'd had seen her review before buying!

And it's not just the scent that's concerning. I use oils primarily for aromatherapy, and when I sniff this, I get nauseated. A real sandalwood oil increases my appetite and makes me want to chase the scent. This turns my stomach and makes me want to run.

I've noticed this same basic package branded with several different names and print designs. All of them that I've tried are either horrible or questionable at best. I don't know about the citruses, but even the florals, which smell okay, induce nausea in people. I tried this one because I thought the bottle size was different. I was wrong. BEWARE: there are several companies selling oils that come in 100 ml bottles that have a sleek, salon/spa style bottle with a golden ring around the dropper top. The boxes have to be opened from the bottom because the inner box pushes the outer box in such a way that to open the top, you have to almost tear the box. I got some from a company in Malaysia. This one says it's from China. So far, every oil I've bought in these bottles/boxes either smells horrible, nauseates people, or both. I'd beware of anything in similar packaging. I suspect they are coming from the same place or at least using the same, questionable processes to make these oils. (I just confirmed this to my discrimination. I went to an eBay listing of this item, and when I look at the full description, there are oils being sold under two of the three names I've found on these bottles, so I'm gonna call them out here as a service to all consumers of essential oils. The names are all in all caps and are MAYJAM and PHATOIL. I know these are associated and highly suspect the HIQILI brand claiming to be Malaysian is another branch of the same tree. Look at the names, bottles, boxes, and prices and decide for yourself. I'm convinced. Especially after smelling then! I would advise people avoid the ones that smell wonderful,too. It's hard to make a bad smelling citrus oil, but who knows what's in these?

The good reviews tricked me into ignoring my own wisdom on this one. I hope to spare others from the same disappointment. There's someone who makes exquisite sandalwood essential oil blends that smell so close to the highest quality sandalwoods that only professional noses would know the difference, so I know it can be done. They cost 3x as much as this, but smell like oils that cost 3x more. I'm sure Amazon won't allow me to tell you specifics in this review, but I can say they don't come in these 100 ml bottles! This is my last attempt to try to save money on sandalwood. I can get 100 ml of that sumptuous, velvety, irresistible sandalwood for $47.40.

UPDATE: A few hours have passed since i put this on my arm to test, and it just keeps getting worse. I washed it off, but that disgusting floral/plastic smell just keeps getting less like sandalwood and more like soap and … well … if alcohol and baking soda won't get this off … did you see the movie where the guy cut off his own arm to get out of a ravine?

title: Exceeded Expectations - comfortable, discreet, read and follow care instructions
text:
thinkECO pads are my first experience with cloth, reusable menstrual pads. I am impressed with the product and grateful that I made this investment. The bottom line of this review: these pads are comfortable, absorbent, and discreet. Caring for them does take additional effort, but is worth it to preserve the quality of the pads. (I'll detail my care steps below.)

Prior to using thinkECO, I almost exclusively used Always brand ultra thin or infinity pads. I first purchased the thinkECO day pad three-pack to "test them out." After using them (in conjunction with my remaining disposable pads) for two cycles, I decided to invest in a "set." I was impressed with their performance and the fact that I did not notice I was wearing the pads. They are very absorbent, yet thin enough that they do not bunch-up. I purchased a set of 5 liners, 3 day pads, 5 day pad plus, 3 night pads, and 3 night pad plus. My periods are typically 5-7 days, with 2-3 days of heavy bleeding. So far this has been the right amount of pads for my need. If you use Always ultra thin pads, I would compare the the thinkECO to these sizes: Pink (slender) and Yellow (1) - day pad, Green (2) and Blue (3) - day pad plus, Orange (4) - night pad, and Purple (5) - night pad plus.

READ THE CARE INSTRUCTIONS. I read some reviews prior to purchasing that individuals were upset because the pads shrank in the dryer. The instructions plainly state this may happen. Make sure you let them AIR DRY, every time. I washed all of my pads in cold water with a fragrance-free detergent on the delicate cycle and let them air dry prior to wearing. When actually using the pads, I rinse them in cold water after wearing, then put them in a glass soaking pail with cold water and Borax. This water does get a bit stinky, so I change it out at least every-other day. When my period is done, I dump all of the pads and the dirty water in the washing machine and run a cold, delicate cycle with Borax and detergent. After washing, I stretch them (they don't need much, but pull length- and width-wise) and put them on a drying rack.

title: Decent Shower Steamers
text:
While these aren't the best shower steamers that I've tried, they also aren't the worst. For me, they fall somewhere in the middle. They differ significantly in the strength of their scents. For example, I can smell the peony decently well throughout my whole shower, but the lily had a really mild scent when I first got in the shower, and the scent was pretty much unnoticeable by the end of my shower.

Shower steamers work best when you use hot water, and with it being summer, many people don't want to take a hot shower. If you want to use these in the summer or when you want a cooler shower, I would suggest putting this in the shower, turning the hot water up as high as it will go, and then letting it steam for about two or three minutes. When you get in the shower, it will be a bit warm, but the steamer will also be working. You can then turn the temperature down significantly and enjoy the scent of the steamers. The scent won't last as well as it would if you kept the shower warm throughout your shower, but you will still be able to enjoy at least some of the benefits of the shower steamers.

For me, these shower steamers last about one and a half showers. When I have shower steamers that last for more than one shower, I generally pull them out and put them in a Ziploc bag to save for my next shower. These are a bit mushier than other shower steamers that I've been able to use for more than one shower, and they don't stay as well intact. If you can, I'd suggest just leaving the leftover bits in the corner of your shower until your next shower.

text:
I tried this vacuum for a week. It works, but just barely.

We pulled all the parts out of the box and chose a place to set it up. Our den has carpet and gets lots of use each day. With four times more than the usual 2 kids, we usually have to vacuum several times a day. It took more than 8 hours for the vacuum to charge up completely and then I had to download the Hoover app on my phone. After reading all the directions, I’m still not clear on the best way to use it. When I started it with my app and then walked upstairs, the app notified me that I was out of range. I called down to the kids and they told me that it was still moving. I don’t know if this is how it’s supposed to work or not…. It seems like quite a pain to have to stay nearby while the robot vacuum works. I mean, that’s kind of the point of the robot vacuum – you can leave it alone and it does the job for you, right?

Well, it’s a cool toy but a terrible servant. After six tries, it still leaves bits of paper on the carpet. It did manage to eat up my husband’s phone charging cord that the kids left on the hardwood floor in the hall. And speaking of the hall, the device that comes with this robot vac that is supposed to keep the vacuum out of a certain room that you don’t want vacuumed – well, that actually works. It even comes with a battery to put into it. But having to remember to replace the battery (and not knowing how long it will last or when it will run out) is a pain. title: Will only work as a parasol, I wouldn't trust it for anything else (w/pics)
text:
I like umbrellas. Even parasols when it's a day I'll be in the direct sun a lot. So when I was offered this Anti-Sun umbrella for "Rain and Wind" as stated by the product title I was in.

Let me say I've rarely had to give a product a 2 star review. I usually pick products that I'm confident will be of some quality or use. Sadly for the first time in a long time I was disappointed with a product. Upon first glance out of the package all was well. It was light weight and very compact, though the black material was a little to plastic/pleather looking for my tastes it was still ok. Has it's own sleeve and an attractive blue. I unraveled it and opened the umbrella, it didn't open properly at least the first 3-4 times I tried, I always had to "correct" it and flip the outer edges down in some way. This does NOT give me confidence that it would be any good in rough weather, or even an aggressive breeze. After I did it a few times it started to open correctly. So I started inspecting it for construction flaws, which sadly I saw right away. The post seems as if I could easily bend it with little force, along with all the ribs of the umbrella. I also saw retail type nylon tabs holding the fabric down among the skelleton of the umbrella. My particular umbrella had a hem stitching flaw along one of the scalloped edges. It was also harder than I'd like it to be to get it to fold up and the strap to engage with the velcro. There is no way I'm going to get it back into the sleeve without a lot of effort that it's just not worth expending. The umbrella is NOT a good value at over $20 at time of writing.

The ONLY reasons I would give this a two star and not a one is: The design is nice with the color on the outside, the dark black on the inside will help keep sun out. The scalloped edges are pretty and a nice touch. THIS UMBRELLA IS ONLY GOOD AS A PAROSOL (on a non-windy day) provided yours does not come with a stitching flaw as mine did. Otherwise it is in my opinion useless in any other weather.

title: A small luxury for a very good price, great his/hers gift (review with pics)
text:
I don't often wear sleepmasks but I do on occasion. My pillowcases are mulberry silk, which I've been told is good for our skin (doesn't absorb the moisturizer we just put on, doesn't crease the face as bad as other materials, etc). So when I was offered silk sleep masks I thought, well that's going to be better than the cotton one I have. I often go to sleep with the tv on in the background as white noise and though I have the backlight turned way down sometimes the light annoys me. I also like to have a little pressure sometimes on the eyes but nothing covering the rest of my face- a sleep mask fits these purposes.

I was offered a set of 2 masks, one purple (on the outside, "inside" it is black) and one all black. The set also comes with a company information card and a set of your typical orange foam earplugs (which are just a little freebie but are not really part of this review other than I'm mentioning them).

These are beautiful masks. Some have pointed out for them they are a little small. At the widest point across the mask it is 8" and the widest point along the eye covers is 4". It is perfect for me, hits me just 1/3 into my temple area, just past my cheekbones and covers 2/3 of my forehead- and I can adjust that accordingly. So if there's any question about its size, take a quick measurement with a flexible ruler or tailor's tape. I find that sometimes sleep masks are entirely too big, I'd say this is the best size I've personally come across. It entirely blocks out the light without covering the whole top of my face. The silk is sooooo smooth. I can see the approx 1" closure they used to put in the stuffing but the piping and cushion were excellently done. I don't feel any awkward bumps in the filling. What I especially love about this particular mask is NO VELCRO. So many of the masks I've had or been given have been made with that infuriating material that just does not work well in a sleep mask. This adjustable slide was easy to move and fit my face right- and the elastic has just the right amount of give and doesn't seem flimsy- so now I don't have to keep opening and closing the strap to get it to fit every time I wear it. It will also not catch my hair. These are at a very good pricepoint and feel and perform like a nice luxury item so they are a good value.

The masks did not come with washing instructions, but I'd suggest handwashing by themselves with gentle detergent and lay out flat to dry. Use a steamer and not an iron if that's necessary, but I don't forsee that being an issue. The card that the masks came with does promise quality, and a quick answer if there is any question- also says they have a "lifetime warranty". Though I have not needed to contact the company for any reason- I have yet to be disappointed with things I've purchased on Amazon that have these kinds of cards with them. I think this set would make an excellent gift for his/hers. Having used my mask for a week I have absolutely enjoyed it so far.

title: Replacement Toothbrush Heads Do Not Appear To Be Available
text:
I've been reviewing quite a few Chinese Water Flossers & Electric Toothbrushes lately.

This one is the most powerful other than my old Philips Sonic Care. 3 brushing speeds.

Toothbrush: Much more powerful than any other Asian brand I've tried. Came 3/4 chraged. Uses a standard USB cable (provided). Really only complaint:
1. The bristles could be a bit softer,

Water Flosser:

Again, the most powerful one I own. Several speed settings. This did include all 4 different syled heads, I tried out the "normal"/standard one. Worked well.

3 issues:

1. As we move into an era of USB powered devices, it is really getting frustrating that there are so many proprietary cords. I often can't find the right cord, and as they all plug into a USB charger there is no reason for this. I had an identical looking cord that didn't fit.

2. On first use, the water had a chemical flavor.

3. The charging port (the unique style, kind of like a razor but barely different sized) has a rubber cover for safety. I could not get it back on the unit after charging, so I am just leaving the charging cable plugged in. At least I won't lose the cable that way!

To sum up, if the chemical flavor goes away, this will be my go to Flosser. I would like to say similar about the tooth brush, I need to watch the impact of harder bristles carefully the first couple weeks. I also can not find replacement brush heads for sale, which if not remedied would cause a fairly short period of the toothbrush being useful.

I will increase the review to 4 stars if I can find replacement toothbrush heads & if they are affordable

title: "Not Medical"
text:
The one honest thing about these masks is the statement "not medical" on the front of the box.

Honestly, they are flimsier than surgical masks, & do not form an air seal at the top of my nose no matter how much I squeeze.

They are more attractive than surgical masks (though that won't do much good if you get Covid!), & the ear straps are more solid.

They are thinner than surgical masks, & do not have even half the layers of a true N95.

I am aware the KF94's & K95's are not supposed to be at the quality of a true KN95; but in my unofficial opinion, I'd be better off with a low protection surgical mask at a much lower price.

title: Not Quite What I Expected, But May Work Well For You
text:
My bedroom is on a noisy street & it often wakes me up. My intent was to remove the eye cover & only use the ear covers. Unfortunately, only the opposite (remove Ear pieces, leave eye cover) is possible.

Seems comfortable enough once I figured the strap out. It comes with NO instructions, & when I wrote the seller/manufacturer, they simply sent me a picture of the fastener, which I had already seen. I did finally figure out how to size it (to enlarge, move each fastener as close as possible to the ear piece).

I unfortunately had another issue which though no fault of the manufacturer, stopped me from thoroughly trying the unit: the earpieces magnified the volume of my heartbeat to where is was very nerve wracking. This may not happen for you, as I have racing heartbeat issues caused by a medication at this time.

It also comes with optional ear plugs. I really don't like earplugs, & I don't fall asleep easily.

title: Seem To Offer Excellent Protection; Cleaning Gloves Afterwards Is A Concern
text:
I used one pair to protect my hands while cleaning a disgusting toilet. It felt like they protected me.

On the down side, I couldn't come up with a method to clean the gloves afterwards that I was comfortable with; due to the extreme nature of the germs/bacteria they were exposed to; & $5 for a single use is very pricey.

I think with normal cleaning, either following the suggestion (washing in the sink with running water) or even using a washing machine would work. With what I exposed them to, running water would not be sufficient & I am not willing to contaminate my washing machine. I suspect for lighter cleaning, running water as suggested would be sufficient.

Good fit, no tearing, not difficult to put on or off.

Other than for moldy environments (like my toilet), I would recommend these. I will likely use disposable gloves for the toilet in the future.

title: It's a mechanical pumice stone essentially
text:
Sorry, no pictures of feet, just what I've found out.

What I like: It's basically a handheld drum sander w/ coarse, medium and fine heads. It's a push click square drive so I don't get the feeling it will strip out easily. There's what I presume to be a voltage cutoff circuit that stops it when it's overloaded or drained. That will stop the unit if pressed too hard, but will let you grind into good tender skin though so watch out. The run light shows which speed it's on, full lit is high, half lit is low. High gloss finish so it wipes off easy to dispose of the foot dust.

Neutral thoughts: It lists a 2000 ma battery and a 2 hour run time. I haven't bothered running it via a wall monitor to verify but is likely close. The 2 hour run time must be no load or very light duty. I get about 30 minutes before it started stopping frequently. Enough to get both feet but was close when tackling the first pass work boot buildup.

Negative: It only comes with the USB cable, no wall transformer. I double checked when I wrote this and no mention either way. I'd like to see that clarified that you have to provide that part. While by no means a deal breaker it would be nice to have it known. Seems like more and more it's just assumed you have one open and available. No mention of battery chemistry and it's non-removable which may make it slightly harder to recycle.

title: Effective at filtering construction dust
text:
This air purifier is a pretty good size. Shaped like a box fan. You open it to replace the filter. (Don't forget to take the plastic off the hepa filter like I did) I looks smooth and sleek. It has touch panel controls that allow you to have 3 different speeds and time duration. (2, 4, 8 hours)

We had a smoky smell in our house from the fire place AND lots of construction dust. I set this up in the room that had most of the dust and dirt. I noticed that it did a great job of clearing the air. If you are using it next to a fireplace I would recommend that you close the damper because the fan will pull the air from the open chimney and besides pulling in hot/cold air, the chimney smells like smoke if you use it. I closed my damper and the fan drew air from the rest of my house and filtered it effectively. We had so much dust from construction that my eyes were always itchy. I did dust and sweep every day, but this really made the difference in air quality.

I like the sound as well. It makes low level white noise. The higher the fan level, the higher the white noise. I like white noise.

title: Doesn't hurt to try it
text:
I've heard great things about liposomal technology, so I decided to give it a try. I'm no health expert, so my information is really based on the little I've read about it. Apparently, vitamin C taken in larger doses cannot be absorbed as well by the cells. When this happens, much of what's ingested can easily get flushed through our system and down the toilet (yellow pee, anyone?).

If what I'm reading is correct, liposomes wrap around the vitamin C, so that they can be absorbed by the cells much more easily. When this happens, the vitamin C better does what it's supposed to do - boost the immune system, give you better skin, and fight tiredness and fatigue. I imagine during this era of concern over Covid-19, it wouldn't hurt to find better ways to boost one's immune system.

One thing that makes me wonder about this particular product, though, is this: If liposomes are like a kind of nano technology that encapsulates the vitamin C, what exactly is meant, then, when it says that these specific capsules do not contain genetically modified organisms? I may just have "liposome technology" and "genetically modified organisms" mixed up all together, so I probably just don't know what is meant by "genetically modified," and why this particular brand, being not GMO, would be superior to its rivals on its use of liposome technology. Nevertheless, I still have this question.

So another question for this specific product is, does it work? Well, I don't know. I suppose I may not know the answer to that question until many months later, if I paid close attention to my skin, level of fatigue, and immune system. Is my urine still yellow? I take other vitamins other than this one, so I can't use this as a marker, either. What I think, though, is that if liposomes seem to be as great as they are supposed to be, it probably wouldn't hurt to use it as a means of boosting my vitamin C absorption.

Finally, a word on the labeling - white font on a yellow label makes for a *really* hard read, especially if one does not have great eyesight. I strained even with my glasses on, so I might encourage the makers to use another font color over their yellow label, in order to see the words more clearly.

title: Great hope for the future
text:
There is a great deal of information in the literature about glucosamine and chondroitin combination supplements. Both compounds are part of cartilage, which forms a cushion between bones of a joint. As you age the cushions erode and the result is skeletal pain virtually everywhere- osteoarthritis. Both glucosamine and chondroitin are part of normal cartilage. MSM is a sulphur compound which aids in to the efficacy of glucosamine and chondroitin and the three compounds work synergistically together.

That having been said, I am a good guinea pig being both very old (85) and very arthritic. I am also aware that if the mind decides a supplement is going to work-any supplement- the mind affects the cure, not the supplement. That is why in some cases, test people taking a placebo have just as good a result as the people taking the supplement. However, the Mayo Clinic researchers gave a glucosamine sulphate supplement a grade of “B” meaning that there is good scientific evidence for its ability to lessen the pain in the knee. They specify that positive results were only obtained for the knee.

Glucosamine, chondroitin and MSM are a combination that is for many effective in treating osteoarthritis, muscle damage caused by exercise, and other inflammatory joint disorders. There is plenty of anecdotal evidence for osteoarthritis relief, but until more scientific information is available, the thing to do, especially if you're elderly, is take and trust the Viva Lab's glososamine-chondroitin- MSM combo, and if you're young get on the bandwagon and start taking it, too. This supplement is guaranteed to help your achy bones.

I have only been taking this glucosamine combo for two days but will report back later on how my osteoarthritis situation fares when confronted with this supplement.. I will add a fifth star when I get frisky.

I get a lot of migraines. And I’ve spent a lot of money on different things to help with the pain. Massaging eye mask doesn’t squeeze tight enough. Microwaveable lavender eye mask smells nice but that’s about it.

Whenever the pain is really bad I always ask my husband to press on my forehead. It feels so good but, of course, he’s not really interested in squeezing my head for hours at a time.

I bought this a few months ago and threw it in a drawer. My migraines generally respond to excedrin if I take it early enough and lie down immediately. Sometimes, however, conditions aren’t just right and it doesn’t work the best. I thought it’d be good for getting through those times.

Well, today a migraine hit hard. I have an upcoming surgery so cannot take anything other than Tylenol for the next 7 days. Tylenol for a migraine is…. Like a bandaid on a broken leg. I remembered this thing, strapped it on TIGHT, and it definitely helps. Is my headache magically gone? No. But do I have some relief, yes.

Worth the $8. Might as well give it a try if you suffer from migraine or tension headaches.

Long story but my dog likes to keep me company in my workshop - I had taken the side off of my cabinet saw to clean it - I was cutting something and he jumped up in there to catch the sawdust coming out from under the blade. The blade hit him just at the border of the soft nose tissue cutting his nose and left lip leaving his nose and lip hanging by about 1/4" of nose tissue.

After a nasty divorce I am not currently working and money is very tight. It was $2,500 just to get him in the door to the emergency vet and they always seem to get the bill even higher with anesthesia, observation, medications.

-so-it killed me but we just could not afford to use the vet!

We irrigated the wound thoroughly and I managed to throw just 4 sutures to hold the nose in place and stop most of the bleeding. Put the cone of shame on him but he still went straight outside and rubbed his nose in the dirt, contaminating the wound and dislodging one of the sutures.

I put him on antibiotics (clindamycin) and was thrilled to find that I could buy this calcium alginate powder. We sprinkled it on his wound twice a day. It forms a clear jelly like substance. His nose healed within a weak to a pink scar - now after about 3 weeks all of the black pigment is back.

Since that time I have experimented around with the powder. My wife was putting the cut bases of Roman Lettuce in water - something she saw on pinterest - it grows a few small leaves then dies. Just for kicks I dipped the bottom of one of the lettuce bases in the calcium alginate powder. That lettuce base grew roots and started to grow. If it were winter - here in Florida - I could have taken it outside and planted it.

It was too hot outside to grow it and inside it bolted immediately while still in the water - but she has been doing this intermittently for years and I have never seen a single one take root.

So my experience with calcium alginate is in wound healing. Years ago we had a Mare gallop square into a barbed wire fence. There was over a 12" gash across her chest. It was my sisters Arabian I was fostering - still am 9 years later. Again no vet, not even a suture, just a big slab of swollen skin hanging down her chest. Went through rolls and rolls of Coban trying to create a bandage but rarely stayed in place. Essentially all I could do was use the calcium alginate - this was the 4x4 bandage form of it but same stuff. It took some time, but the wound healed so well you cannot even see a scar.

title: Painfully pulls on beard hairs= garbage!
text:
These blades are garbage. I rarely give bad reviews but I hope I save somebody their money and help them to avoid pain and suffering.
I had high hopes that these blades would be a good replacement but I'm disappointed. These Chineses knock-offs look like the real thing and they were a good value so I bought them. I read many reviews that said that they gave a very good shave and a few reviews that said that they did not. For me they did NOT. I don't have a really tough beard and I don't shave everyday. But these blades really must be dull since they pulled my 2 day old beard hairs like crazy. It was very painful but I kept going. And I kept having to shave over the same spot several times to get an even, smooth shave. So I ordered a bottle of pre electric shave lotion to see if that would help to soften my beard and to give me a smoother, less painful shave. NOPE! These blades are duller than the 2 year plus blades that they replaced which, despite their age, rarely yanked the hairs unless my beard was about 5 days old. I'm glad that I didn't toss the old blades, they were very dirty but I kept them just the same. So, I cleaned the old blades in alcohol and put them back in. Voila! It was like my shaver was new again.
I don't recommend these cheap knock-offs unless you like pain or shave everyday so that the hairs don't get long enough to be pulled. I do suggest that you let your old blade soak in some alcohol and use a tiny bristle brush to clean them. You might luck out like me and hopefully extend their life.

title: Best massage chair on the market!! I HIGHLY recommend it!  Stop whining about putting some parts together yourself people - geez
text: Heres the quick down and dirty. I purchased from Haverty's the top line massage chair.  It cost $2500 on sale plus delivery and warranty separately.  When they delivered the chair they brought it in, put a few things together and I was like...wow I paid a lot for delivery but oh well.  The chair itself was nice but I always felt like it was lacking.  About 9 months later, now, I still didn't feel happy with the purchase.  So I saw this chair for $799 with free delivery.  It came from a company and yes they just drop it off on your stoop in a huge box.  And you have to lug it into your house...we had to cut it out of the box and brought the pieces inside.  I'm very healthy and so is my wife and this chair weighs about 250lbs.  But for the most part it has wheels and you can wheel it around once you get it inside.  I don't see carrying it up steps though.  The thing is a pure beast of dead weight.  I see people complaining and I dunno shipping was FREE....what do you expect?  Go to a furniture store if you want it put in a room and put together, it will cost you three times this amount so stop griping. I've been there, done that and got the t-shirt.  As for putting the chair together its not rocket science but the manual sucks.  You'll figure it out though on your own.  Just don't be afraid when putting the leg piece on...its really easier than your brain thinks it is when you look at it.  Don't overthink it.  Once in the chair?  I can only give it 5 stars out of 5 stars because its every bit of what my other premium chair was lacking.  It massages your legs, your feet, your forearms, your neck, your back, and it works your butt over like a Greek!  The thing is amazing.  Its the best massage in a chair I've EVER had and I've sat on everyone of these things ever seen in a mall or Sharper Image.  If you want deep heat it doesn't have that but neither does my premium one that is supposed to blow hot air.  It was enough to make every member of my family happy even the little ones who couldn't get the full effect because they are too short.  So to all of the naysayers complaining about the delivery and having to put it together....what do you expect for free?  The company is Factory Direct Warehouse, LLC out of Georgia and I got it in less than a week.  They use a company called R&L Carriers which really does a great job - they just aren't going to bring the thing into your house and set it up for you is all.  I'm nothing but impressed.  On their website the chair is like $1000.  If you go on eBay you can get it from their store for $799 with free shipping so shop around.  But again, its low frills in that it doesn't have a zillion buttons on the remote...it still has way too many options for me to be honest...but it gives a great great massage.  The only thing is it is heavy and you are going to need space for it because it has something called Zero Gravity - which should be called - Heaven on Earth and it literally lays you down in almost a sleeping position.  And thats fine because this is the first chair....that put me to sleep.  Don't look anywhere else...this thing is the bomb and I'm not easily impressed....now if anyone is in the market for a $2500 top of the line chair, let me know....because that thing isn't going to get ANY use now that I have this!

title: I like it. Minor quibbles
text:
If I hadn't already used one of the [[ASIN:B00DL6LRNY Manatea Tea Infuser Silicone Strainer]] (by Fred and Friends), I might give these sharks a better rating. The are just not quite as good as the Manatea, in my opinion. Shark fans who drink tea should not be put off by my 4 instead of 5 stars.

And both sharks and manatees look funny (in a grim way) if you drink herbal teas with ingredients that make your tea red.

I use tea infusers like this one to hold those tea bags that don't have any strings, rather than loose leaf tea.

Pros: It is silicone, inexpensive, cute, and the tail joins the body snugly without being hard to use. Shark fans who drink tea will enjoy them. A stringless tea bag (like Republic of Tea, etc.) can be rolled loosely to fit into the shark. Doesn't stain, even with hibiscus leaves in the tea. Sharks!

Cons: They're a bit on the big side for my taste, and they don't grip the lip of the mug as effectively as the Manatea infuser does. If you drink tea from a teacup instead of a mug, it might be just about right.

Details:
The shark's head is a heavier, more rigid material than the tail, and the "mouth" that holds the edge of the mug is just slightly too tight for a standard mug so it wants to slide up and fall into the mug.

With some herbal teas, if I'm rushing off to a meeting I'll leave the tea bag in as I drink. I can still manage to sip out of a standard mug with a Manatea in it. With these sharks, that's out of the question. They just take up too much space above the mug. (Yes, I use these sharks and the Manatea at work. My co-workers already know I'm a little odd.)

That said, the tail is not so big that it displaces too much of the tea, and I think most people will take an infuser out of their cup before drinking.

title: Saves me a lot of time at a high price!
text:
Every time I come into my house I disinfect what I carry around which is a small bag and my phone. It is something that does take a little bit of time and is a little annoying and after seeing this product I thought it would save me some time.

[This product has been used from Nov 4, 2020]

This SNEGDO portable cleaner is decently sized and fits my small carry bag, phone and wallet with no issue. The power source of this bag is through a USB cable that connects on the top portion of the bag which is convenient. This portable cleaner is so easy to use and I find myself just placing my every day carry items in there and just forgetting about them until they are cleaned. There is an indicator on the side which helps to indicate when it is on. It takes 5 minutes to clean your items which is pretty fast and through the reflective material inside of the portable cleaner, the UV light is able to reach almost every single point of the items inside of this bag.

One of the things about this product is that it is pretty expensive. There are other products that serve the exact same function at a more affordable price. There is nothing special about this portable cleaner that helps to differentiate it over the competition which is something to keep in mind.

Overall this product works and helps to sterilize my personal items but the price of this product might push some of you away. If you are in the market for a UV cleaner, this might be worth a shot if money is not a concern. For this reason I give this product 4 out of 5 stars. I hope this review helps you make an educated decision.

title: Great FIR Jade Massage Table Family Loves It
text:
BENEFITS: This massage table will give your back a serious massage along with the infrared heat which can be set pretty hot. After about 4 sessions 1 per day my height increased 1/2" and put me back at the same height I was in my 20's. Now I am into my late 40's and I have always had lower back issues especially when my weight is over 230 lbs. This machine will do many great things but I will mention just two. The first is that it will help rebuild your discs by decompressing your back and heating up your discs. Infrared heat penetrates about 2" into your body which will take care of the discs. The second is that by massaging your back muscles it will straighten your back by making the muscles more elastic. You won't get this powerful massage from your massage therapist. The first massage will be painful but you get used to it after the 3rd massage. It won't replace your massage therapist either because this machine only takes care of your back. The lower rollers work your legs but are not as effective as the upper rollers. Your massage therapist will do a better job on the legs.

QUALITY: The bed feet are heavy and strong. The bed frame is made of welded steel tubing. The bed foam is stiff so it can handle heavy individuals. Everything looks and feels of good quality. The bed should handle people up to 6'-5". I am 6', but it can easily handle someone taller. The frame can take really heavy people without any problems. The 350 lb limit might come from the roller system not from the frame.

SPACE REQUIREMENT: The bed needs about 3 feet by 7 feet of space so you can use it and access it. A 4 feet wide space would be even better. You need a regular electrical outlet nearby to plug it in.

ASSEMBLY: It takes 2-3 hours to assemble it. If your back is in bad shape a second person to help you will make it easier. It comes with a users manual and assembly instructions.

SHIPPING: The massage table came in a wooden heavy pallet in 2 boxes and they called me to schedule the drop-off day. 9-5 drop-off window. You can undo the pallet wrapping and take one box at a time using a hand cart or two people. You can also pick it up and lift it if you are a strong person. I recommend help especially if your back is not in good shape. This table is a keeper so I can tune up my back every week.

SKEPTICAL? I was having a hard time dishing out more than a grand for something that I might have to return and pay to ship it back but I noticed that there are not that many used tables for sale. This means that people keep them because they work. I am keeping mine because everyone in my family of 6 is using it. The kids love it.

text:
I have turned to more environmentally friendly cleaning supplies over the past couple of years. I REALLY like this multi-purpose cleaner because of 3 main reasons:

1. versatility - you can use it to clean/deodorize ANYthing including carpet, drains, toilets, countertops and even clothing. It is important though to let it sit for a bit before wiping up (if you choose to wipe it up) to allow for the cleaning action to take place.
2. the scent is fantastic - a strong lemon scent that lingers and just smells really good (and clean)
3. You don’t have to wipe the product up (although you can if you choose). This is really great for certain tasks - especially like around the base of toilets, sinks and drains. Leaving it to dry on its own allows for the cleaner to continue working its magic (as well as providing a nice clean scent).

The product came well packaged to prevent any leaking. The gallon jug has a safety seal on it with a lock top that you press and turn to unscrew the cap. It was packaged in a heavy duty cardboard box that pretty much would have prevented any possibility of damage during the shipping process. The price is also reasonable for the quantity. I transferred some to a quart size spray bottle to use for certain tasks. Overall just a really nice, versatile product that does what it is supposed to do and leaves an incredible scent behind as well, while also being more environmentally friendly. I hope you find this info helpful!

title: Good quality, nice price

It is a fairly large bottle and is at a pretty good price at $16, given the size (at the time of this review there was also a 20% off coupon).  I typically use this in a diffuser and like it by itself (i.e. diffusing only the bergamot oil), but it also is a great EO to blend with other EO’s as well to create unique scents/fragrances (really combines well with lavender).  The oil can also be used in making DIY soaps, candles, etc. if you do those types of things.  Overall a very good product!

title: Excellent quality, great price
text: I have used MAYJAM EO’s before and have been generally impressed (their Ylang Ylang and Sandlewood are great!).  Lavender is one of my favorites though, and this one is excellent.  If you are familiar with lavendar EO’s you know that they generally fall into two main categories of scents (depending on the specific species of lavender used).  One type is slightly sweeter smelling (still strong lavender scent but the subtle sweetness takes the edge off of the scent.  The other general category of scent is a stronger, almost medicinal scent with a slight edge to it.  This falls closer to the latter.  Personally I prefer this stronger scent as I think it does a better job in a diffuser, which is how I generally use it.  It does well in other scenarios too, but sometimes the scent needs to calm a bit so that the edge is off.  I would say that while this one is closer to the stronger, almost medicinal scent, it is not the strongest I have smelled, so in that regard it is sort of the best of both worlds.  The bottle is a large, almost 4oz bottle with a screw on top.  It comes boxed with a separate screw on dropper as well so you can use either.  The box was securely packaged, as was the glass dropper inside.  The price, at under $10 for almost 4oz of high quality lavender EO, is *very* good.  Overall this is definitely a winner.  I hope this is helpful info to you!

title: Excellent scent, nice value

title: Used on stainless steel, crockpot, and enameled cast iron - see details in review
text:
I wanted to try this product for 3 very specific cleaning needs - stainless steel pans, a crockpot crock and an enameled cast iron dutch oven. All three had stains that didn’t affect the usability, but just didn’t look all that great. I had previously scrubbed with multiple things trying to get the stains out but to no avail. So, here is what happened with this product:

On the enameled cast iron dutch oven I would say that it removed 80%n of the discoloration. Perhaps I could scrub longer or put more elbow grease into it and I could have gotten it all, but I got tired (lol).

On the stainless steel skillet, it took quite a bit of elbow grease but it removed ALL stains and it looks like new.

On the crockpot crock - I had darker colored stains on a white crock and white (lime???) deposits on a black crock. I used this product on both and it was a breeze to remove the stains/deposits. Unlike with the stainless steel and the enameled cast iron I didn’t have to scrub nearly as hard to get the good results with the crocks.

So… overall I would call it a success, especially with the crocks and the stainless steel. The cleaner comes with two non-scratching scrubbing pads (sort of the size of a wash cloth) that are easy to use and easy to clean. I do wish it had worked a little better on the enameled cast iron, and I am going to give it another try but am pleased that it did at least remove about 80% of the stains. Overall, a solid 4 star product. I hope this info is helpful to you in our buying decision!

title: Great product that provides customizable comfort
text: This is a great product, and while it might seem a bit expensive, I will share with you why it is not:  I have *very* flat feet, and have two sets of custom orthotics (obtained from a podiatric specialist).  Those orthotics cost in excess of $500 each.  They work well, and last 10 years plus.  They have done well for me over the years and are what I use in most of my shoes (since they are removable).  But here is where they fall a bit short, and where these inserts step in (no pun intended):  My custom orthotics are hard/rigid material with a cushioned top.  Unfortunately, for some shoes it doesn’t work well - usually because I can’t remove the sole insert in the shoe OR there is still some sort of arch support built into the shoe.  This insert gives you the opportunity to make adjustments to the fit based on your own specific needs, as well as taking into account the limitations with the shoes they will be going in.  You get two sets of ‘pads’ that you can use to adjust the insert wherever it might be needed.  Each set contains 3 different sized pads, and the sets are differentiated by how rigid the pads are - one set is much firmer than the other.  They are pretty easily moved around so that you can experiment with them to get them just right.  The only downside is that if you are using the pads to adjust the fit/feel based on some limitation of the shoe itself (for example, if you can’t remove the existing sole insert), then they aren’t as easily moved from one set of shoes to the other.  From a size standpoint, I wear a size 10 (men’s).  According to the size chart the Medium fits sizes 8.5 to 10.  I almost decided to order a large and figured I could cut it down but opted for the medium and am glad I did.  It is true to size, and it fits my size 10 shoes perfectly with absolutely no trimming needed.  If you wear a size 8.5, 9 or 9.5 you would need to trim the medium accordingly.  But ultimately, the sizing guide the seller provides is accurate.  I am extremely pleased with the fit, the customizable nature, and the comfort.  Too early to make any judgment on longevity though.  I hope this review is helpful to you!

title: High dosage Vitamin D, with added Vitamin K to help

The product is vegan, plant-based, and contains Vitamin K which works hand-in-hand with the vitamin D to improve efficacy.  The capsules are pretty standard sized capsules with no smell, taste, or after taste.  Additionally, I have not had any gastric distress either.  If you have no problems taking typical sized capsules you should have no problem with these.  There is a 60 day supply included (1 capsule/day).  The container is a bit large for 60 so it looks kind of empty once you remove the protective cover (not sure why they have such an oversized container unless they have a standard size but offer larger quantities?).  In any case it seems to be a little wasteful as far as plastic usage goes, but it doesn’t affect the product itself.  Check with your doctor before taking Vitamin K products - especially if you have clotting issues, or are on a blood thinner of some kind.  Overall a pretty good product at a reasonable price, especially if you want to add vitamin K to your regimen in addition to the vitamin D.

title: Tea Tree Oil - A Must Have For Homes
text:
#NewYorkBiology Tea Tree Oil

I love this Tea Tree Oil though the amount is only 1 oz, and the smell is not as sweet as I am used to but that doesn't mean its not great (it smells like a strong undiluted tea tree oil). I use this tea tree oil from #NewYorkBiology for pretty much everything. When I make soap, my shampoo, detergent, face wash I put a little bit in that. As a decongestant or even as a soother in my bath. It has so many uses. This is one thing I will always have on hand in my medicine cabinet (well the side I put all my essential oils). l recommend this to anyone.

*NOTE: Not to be used with pets because it is a dangerous toxin to them, the only time you can use it on animals is if you know the right ratio to use or if you buy an animal product with tea tree oil in it. It is only safe in very minute amount.
Abrasions & Minor Cuts: Clean the area well, apply a few drops of the oil directly. If bandage is needed, allow a few drops of the oil to penetrate cotton ball, lay it face down on the wound with a bandage on top.
Acne: Add a drop to your normal cleansing routine or dab a very small amount on acne breakouts. You can also add 20 – 40 drops of the oil to your regular face wash.
Dandruff: Add 20 – 30 drops oil to any shampoo. Apply a few drops to scalp and massage after washing.
Flea & Mosquito Bites: Apply a drop of oil directly to bites.
Head Lice: Add 20 drops of oil to 2 tbsp shampoo. Massage into scalp and hair, leave on for 10 minutes. Rinse. Repeat 3 – 4 times daily, until eggs are gone.
Household Cleaning: Can be used aromatically or added to homemade cleaners to kill germs and prevent the spread of colds and flus. You can make a general tea tree cleaner by combining 2 teaspoons of tea tree oil with 2 cups of water in a spray bottle. Shake to blend and use for household cleaning tasks. This is especially good in the bathroom and in toilets.
Immune System: To stimulate the immune system, diffuse through the air on a regular basis, massage into the soles of the feet to increase your immune response.
Infected Wounds: Adding the oil to steaming water, hold the infected area over the steam. Or dilute 1 drop of tea tree with 1 cup of water and rinse the infected area 1-2 times a day, as needed.
Insect Repellant: Add 15 drops to a quart of water and use as an effective insect repellent.
Mildew and Mold Remover: Spray an all-purpose cleaner made with 2 teaspoons of tea tree oil and 2 cups of water on growing mold and mildew. Shake well before using and do not rinse.
Muscle Aches and Pains: Add 10-15 drops of oil to half cup Epsom salts, and dissolve in bath. Add 10 drops of oil to 2 tbsp of carrier oil. Massage well. Or fill your bathtub with warm water. Add a few drops of tea tree oil to the water to relax tight muscles.
Pest Control: Household ants and other pests dislike Tea Tree Oil, so a few drops put at the point of entry will deter them. Wipe cupboards out with an oil and water solution to keep ants away.
Rashes: Mix with coconut oil and massage over the affected areas.
Sciatica: Add 10 drops oil to 1 tbsp carrier oil and massage into affected areas. Repeat 2-3 times daily. Also can be applied undiluted.
Sore Throat: Add 2 drops of oil to 1 cup of warm water with pinch of sea salt, gargle 2-3 times a day. Do not swallow!
Ticks: Apply a drop or two directly to the tick and the surrounding area.
Vaginal Infection: Add several drops to the bath water. *Note: I used this for my daughters Candidiasis (A really bad type of yeast infection that causes blisters that bleed) back when she was still in diapers. Come to find out it was the stuff inside the diapers that was causing it so I had to switch to cotton then had to potty train her early due to how bad it had gotten. The doctors gave so many ointments that just didn't work. The tea tree oil with some coconut oil helped, it was like a miracle.
Wounds: Soak wounded area in water with tea tree oil, or spritz from a bottle of water with several drops of oil. Depending on the wound and your own sensitivity you may be able to apply directly.

*NOTE ABOUT CARRIER OILS: In order to effectively use essential oils – not just tea tree oil – it is often necessary to dilute the essential oil in another oil so that it can be easily spread or massaged on the affected area. These oils are called “carrier” oils. Common carrier oils include coconut oil, grape seed oil, sweet almond oil, jojoba oil, olive oil and others.

title: Fantastic for Recliner!!
text:
Okay, sorry this is so long, but I'm going to compare the Ultimate to the Purple Royal, RoHo, and Purap for a recliner and computer chairs. I hope it will save someone from having to buy a bunch of different cushions for trial and error.

I bought the above cushions for my leather Lazyboy recliner because the seat cushioning has flattened over the years, but the recliner itself is still great. The Purple Ultimate is THE ABSOLUTE BOSS in a recliner. I sometimes do embarassingly long movie marathons on my days off, and can legit sit for 12+ hours with the Ultimate cushion. I have tried both an air filled RoHo and a Purap cushion in the recliner. Neither came close to the Ultimate. The Royal would probably work in the recliner, but I haven't bothered to try it because the Ultimate is just that good. My Purap was passably comfortable for about 8 hours in the recliner, but got destroyed because it couldn't hold up to the punishment of extended couch surfing sessions. I fear the same is probably true of the RoHo. The Ultimate cushion is amazing for this purpose.

Now let's talk computer chairs. I have lumbar, tailbone, and restless leg issues when I sit too long without the proper "cushioning" or alignment, so I use a Humanscale Freedom computer chair. Now keep in mind that the Freedom chair is highly ergonomic, which might make cushions act a little differently because it forces you to sit upright and aligned over the top of your hips (it's way more comfy than it sounds). This chair has a comfortable, but "hard" seat that slopes in the front where your thighs sit. I am also talking about extended sitting with only getting up to go to the restroom (e.g., extended computer gaming session). The RoHo cushion absolutely slays all other competition in a hard seat computer chair. I have been able to work all-nighters on the RoHo without any significant discomfort. The Purap was okay in my computer chair for about 4 hours (but would probably be fantastic in a wheelchair or softer computer chair). The Purple Ultimate was okay for about 5 hours, then the restless legs kicked in...I think it's because there is no downward sloped edge where your thighs sit. My lumbar still felt great though, so I guess it depends on what symptoms you're trying to minimize. The Purple Royal is definitely the 2nd best for my computer chair, but restless leg starts to kick in at about 7 or 8 hours.

So, if you are looking to cushion a seat that doesn't have much give, go with a RoHo air filled cushion if you sit for very long periods and your chair forces you to sit upright/have decent posture. Go with the Purple Royal if you have a hard seat and sit for very long periods but do lots of stand up breaks OR sit for medium-long periods without breaks and sit with upright posture. The Royal would probably also work in a hard chair if you sit for very long periods, but with more slumped or relaxed posture (e.g., aren't sitting right over your hips). If you will be sitting in a "soft" chair, the Purple Ultimate is hands down the winner, no matter how you sit. For long periods in a vehicle, I think the same rules above would apply, but tbh, I haven't actually tried, so am just imagining based off my experiences.

I hope this helps! :)

title: Good ingredients, not so good taste
text:
Well, this was a disappointment in the flavor department. The vanilla is good, so I expected the chocolate flavor to also be good. Can’t say it is.

The ingredients and fiber content are quite nice, as are the vitamins and minerals. The shake does make a very good meal replacement and keeps you satisfied for a few hours, if you can tolerate the taste. There is just something too earthy about this particular chocolate flavor that isn’t present in the vanilla. I’ll definitely finish it because I like the nutritional profile but it will have to be doctored up to be palatable. Hopefully adding some instant coffee and half oat milk/half water will mask the flavor. Also, the price is a bit high when compared to other similar powders that tend to go on sale regularly.

title: Decent taste with a satisfying thickness
text:
I recently received this protein powder for review. Having consumed a wide variety of protein powders, both milk and plant based, I have a large pool of powders to compare this to. This Carlyle powder is quite good. It bears no resemblance in taste to products from Orgain, but does remind me in both texture, grittiness and taste to Vega's products. It also has some texture and taste similarity to the Purely Inspired line of plant based protein powders. Carlyle's powder is, however, thicker when mixed with the recommended amount of liquid.

I mixed one scoop with 6 ounces of water, and found it a bit too thick for me. When mixed with 8 ounces, it was quite a bit thinner and more to my liking. The taste is definitely plant based vanilla protein powder, and if you drink it right after mixing, it is gritty. Let it sit for a few minutes and the grittiness greatly diminishes. As for clumping, I couldn't get it smooth with just a spoon, but in a shaker bottle (without a blender ball) it mixed up perfectly clump free.

I really appreciate the high fiber content in this, and while there is a bit of an aftertaste, it isn't unpleasant. The powder is quite sweet, which may not be to everyone's liking, but mixed with a bit more liquid it diminishes. I also really like that it has a variety of plant proteins, although the main protein is from peas, adding to the grittiness. There is a nice vitamin and mineral profile in this powder which adds to its value and health benefits. If you're already high on consuming those vitamins though, you may want to look elsewhere.

I've been liking this as a breakfast drink and it tides me over until lunchtime just fine, with a satisfied feeling without bloating. Nice protein, but at it's current price, it's a bit expensive when compared with better known brands.

title: Great taste and electrolyte profile with some basic vitamins
text:
Great taste dissolved in 24 ounces of water, and it disolved easily. I love the sodium and potassium amounts in this for use when heavily sweating, as well as it having some other basic minerals and vitamin C and a nice amount of zinc.

I can definitely see using one of these while exercising in the heat. Nice product!

title: Tasty bar with a unique texture for being sweet potatoes
text:
Well, it tastes like plain roasted sweet potatoes, mashed up and shaped into a bar. Kind of what I expected, and that's a good thing. The texture though seems a bit unique. Kind of like sweet potatoes that were blended or really mashed, compressed and shaped into a bar (which is probably what happened), so it's denser than I expected. Sort of like fruit leather, but much thicker.

It's a plain, simple, tasty and healthful bar. It could benefit from a bit of salt, but you can always add that yourself. Nice to see a healthy bar that won't melt in the summer heat.

title: scale works - finally, and with no help from Fitbit
text:
10/23/13 Update: I just wanted to update this review to say that I really love this scale! After the initial setup issues, the scale has worked great ever since. I highly recommend!

I purchased this scale from another merchant (because I had a $30 coupon) and brought it home to set it up. It came with simple instructions to connect to my home wifi. I went through the steps, the software said there were 4 steps. Steps 1, 2,and 3 seemed to go without a hitch, then step 4...failure. Tried it again. Failed at step 4. There is absolutely NO phone number to call for support, only an email. So, I googled the problem. Others had success pairing the scale to their wifi via their smart phone. I tried this. Again, failure at step 4. So finally, I resorted to sending an email request for support. Their email support page said that I would get a response within 24 hours, hopefully alot less!! After 2 days, with no email response, I was ready to take the scale back, but I thought I would try one more time, this time with a laptop. For whatever reason, this time it worked, which made me happy because I really wanted the scale to work as advertised. It does upload my weigh ins without fail, and also updates Myfitnesspal automatically. Oh, and I did FINALLY get an email back from "support" which would have been absolutely no help at all, had I not already gotten the scale to work. The email came 2 days after I got the scale to work on my own. I also received an email from Fitbit asking me to rate their "support" which I did. It's too back that Fitbit can't provide decent support of their product. This scale is NOT cheap, and I bet they can afford it!

title: Good for vacuuming every day on hardwood floors but no spare parts available yet (from someone who hates housework & has pets )
text:
I have mostly hardwood floors and an open floor plan, with enough furniture and corners to prevent the floor from being really "open", and two dogs & a cat. This is my first robot vacuum, so I can't compare products, but I can compare using it to traditional vacuuming.

For my home which has 3 shedding pets and no "shoes off" rules, I need to vacuum with "Hoover" EVERY DAY to make using it practical. Why? The dust bin is pretty small and pet hair will fill it up quickly. That said, launching the robot every day while I read the paper, do the crossword puzzle and check email is much more fun than using the traditional vacuum.

So why 3* and not 5*?
- I have mostly hard floors, tile and wood, with two 4'x6' low pile rugs at entry ways. "Hoover" tries to climb up on the rugs. When it succeeds, the actual cleaning is minimal. However, the spinning brush often gets caught and causes an "I'm stuck" alert. I've decided to just roll up the rugs before launching "Hoover". Not a big deal for me, but might be a hassle for people with more carpets or rugs or anyone who wants to use the scheduled start feature.
- It does a good job with most obstacles, but not all. So after my learning what causes problems I now I spend a minute or so pulling chairs out, moving a few things that cause problems (like a cat condo tower, floor lamp, pet food & water dishes, etc) out of the way before launching Hoover. Again, not a big deal for me, but it also prevents me from using any automatic start features.
- With my open concept floor plan, I have found one invisible fence is not enough. I would really like to vacuum smaller areas, like just the kitchen, but with multiple entries, one invisible fence unit is not enough.
- I contacted customer support and while they were very responsive, I learned that spare parts are not currently available for this product (as of October 2016). I wanted to purchase extra filters, dust bin, fence unit and a sweeping attachment but because this product is so new, spare parts are not available. I will keep checking and if this changes I will update my review.

So, yes, I do like this vacuum and am happy to employ it to keep my house cleaner, though for now I can only give it an "it's okay"" rating.

title: Very cool. I like it!
text:
Edit: it is now 11 months later, and I own 2 of these bottles, and I now know for a FACT that they do produce hydrogen water, because since purchasing my first one, there is something I use that needs hydrogen water added to it in order to work (can NOT use just plain, regular water or again, it will not work), and the water that this bottle produces works perfectly. That is why I ended up buying another one (as a backup in case this one stops working at some point). Unfortunately, I have also learned that there is something very unappealing (and gross) about these. A month ago the bottle I'm currently using stopped working well, and I came to find out that there was slime mold inside the bottle. I cleaned it out really good (REALLY good). Slime mold is not dangerous, so I was not at all worried in that regard. Since then, I make sure to empty and thoroughly rinse the bottle and lid out every day.

Fast forward to last night, when the bottle started leaking all over the place whenever I turned it on to make the water, to the point that the pressure pushed almost all of the water out. When I started looking closely at it and poking around to try and fix the issue, I found that there were big, disgusting pieces of slime mold down inside where the lid screws into the bottle, in that gap there. It was CAkED with it. Once I loosened it up using a super thin, soft tool, the pieces of black and greenish slime that came out SHOCKED me. Keep in mind that I had been rinsing that thing out every single day, but until I went down in there with a tool, obviously rinsing did nothing. I cleaned it super well, and sure enough, it instantly remedied the leaking. I ended up soaking all removable parts in rubbing alcohol, and poured some into that gap and let it all sit overnight, but now I'm realizing that this bottle is going to take some maintenance in order to keep it clean. Now that I know the hiding spots, it's not that big of a deal to keep it clean (I think), so we'll see. It's just disappointing.

Original review:
I really like this spray bottle a lot. I have been looking into hydrogen water bottles lately, and while searching, this spray bottle came back in my search results. Since I'm someone who uses facial misters ALL THE TIME, I figured I would try the whole hydrogen water thing out starting with this, since it's a lot lower in price than the drinking bottles. I was very excited to get it. It is simple to use, and I love watching it in action, bubbling up and the pretty light colors, etc., especially when I first got it. It feels very refreshing going on. I use it on my face and hands and arms before applying serums and lotions (the same way I use all my other misters) but I said to myself "how do I know that this is really working/doing anything"? My answer came when I decided to spray one half of my hair with it, just to see what it would do. I have very long hair that is fine and naturally curly, so when left to air dry, it ends up a bit frizzy. Well... the side that I sprayed came back so silky I couldn't believe it. I had to run and show my family. Lol Since then I have loved it even more. Oh! And I also used it to remove a small (un-laundered) stain that I had on a piece of clothing since, I had read that hydrogen water can do that, and it came right out. Of course I can't say that it was this that did it since I didn't try plain water first, but I will do that test again in the future and I will update my review when I do. The first bottle that I received did have a hairline crack on the top near the neck, and even though it didn't affect performance, I exchanged it for another one which is perfect. I use it every day/night and continue to be happy with it. I am giving it 4 stars since I don't have anything to compare it to yet as far as hydrogen water goes.

title: Started smelling like an electrical fire - you've been warned
text:
Updated review April 2019:
Was using this dryer on LOW fan setting and HIGH heat. After about 1 minute, something in the dryer handle malfunctioned, and the fan went to HIGH on its own. I manually flipped the switch from LOW to OFF to HIGH to LOW, trying to get the LOW fan speed to return, but it didn't work. After about 30 seconds of this I started smelling an electrical fire smell - the kind where it's like a smokey burned plastic smell. I panicked - turned the dryer OFF - unplugged - and ran it out to my front porch as fast as I could. It'll stay out there all day until I calm down enough to trust it won't light my garbage bin on fire. I no longer trust buying items that require a UL electrical certification on Amazon. There's just no way of proving the dryer that almost caused a house fire isn't some counterfeit. I definitely do not want Amazon to replace this. Refund would be nice, but I'll be buying a dryer at a brick and mortar store this afternoon. Do not buy this item.

title: Lifesavers!
text:
I'm thankful and grateful for these capsules, let me tell you! If you're giving your cat methimizole, I especially recommend these - methimizole is bitter and can burn your cat's tender mouth and throat tissues if the pill gets stuck instead of going down, and this can lead to a loss of appetite and other bad things.

These capsules are worth their weight. They are clear, firm, separate easily; seem like a good quality; you can feel the pieces lock together when you push them closed with just a little pressure (and they stay closed); and I like that they're pharmaceutical grade gelatin. They're small and you can pop the pill piece(s) right inside. I freaked out a little when I first saw them - I thought they were entirely too big and how could these ever work and how could I get my cat to swallow it??. But the 2.5 piece of methimizole fit perfectly. (If you need a higher dosage you'll have to split the piece of pill again, in other words you'll have a little line-up of pill pieces inside the capsule). I use the Buster Pet Piller with Soft Tip and these #4 capsules fit perfectly inside, and, very importantly, you can draw in water behind the capsule to help it all flush down the throat. Then head up, mouth open, and it's down before you (or the cat) knows it. The first time I used it I don't know who was more surprised, me or my cat. It shot down so fast we both kinda jumped and looked around like what the heck was that. Needless to say, we're both a LOT less stressed after pill time. There's room left inside the capsule for a little something extra (I put a little Cosequin powder in the capsule along with the methimizole).

Recommended! These will make everybody's life a little easier, and they're worth the purchase.

title: I was skeptical, but it's good!
text:
I hate the old fashioned squeezy lash curlers and had given up having curled lashes. When I saw that there were curling irons for lashes I was excited but was unwilling to shell out a lot of cash for something that might not work. This curler was really inexpensive and had no reviews, but it looked exactly like one that cost 4 times as much, so I thought I'd give it a go. I'm glad I did because it really works and has most of the features that the more expensive ones have - this is a win!

Here's the rundown of what I like: It's rechargeable, so no batteries! it charges quickly and one charge lasts a couple of weeks. It has 4 heat settings. I've tried them all and even the lowest works well. It's easy to clean and has a cover to keep it protected when it's not in use. I do want to mention that the instructions advise you to put a coat of mascara on before you use the curler, and then to use another coat when you're finished curling. All of the curlers I looked at said this, but I've started just curling my lashes before putting any mascara on and it works just as well. Maybe better, because sometimes my mascara would clump when I did it the other way. It might just be me, but I like it better.

This is a great curler at a great price - definitely worth it!

title: Good brace - could be excellent with just a little change or two.
text:
I bought the Dr Welland brace after finding the Zenith version too tight (hard to get past my toes without lots of tugging). The Dr Welland version was a much better fit in my experience.

Minor gripes:
1) No instructions ; the brace is sold as being suitable for left OR right foot, simply by moving the metal support from one side to the other. Only problem - no indication (at least not that I found) of which side you should put the metal on.

2) The metal brace is not well padded - I found that it dug into my foot and caused quite a lot of pain, so I ended up simply removing it - much better (though obviously less support, so be careful about whether to do the same)

3) I am now able to walk in the brace with only minor discomfort - which is good. Sadly though, the remaining discomfort is unnecessary in my opinion ... the problem is that the straps which go from side to side under the foot, transition from a narrow tape to a wider material which then velcros in place at the side ; the transition from the narrow tape to the wider material happens too soon, in that I get a bulky section of the strap right on my arch - so when I walk that strap gets pushed up into my foot causing some discomfort (sort of like constantly walking with a stone in my shoe). If the narrow material continued for just another inch before transitioning to the bulkier material, this annoyance would not exist.

Despite the above, its a very capable brace, and still way more comfortable than the cast and then fibreglass walking boot that I've transitioned out of after breaking an ankle - so I'll take it ! :-)

title: REVISED from "Not the Best" to Horrible!
text:
Addition to my Previous Review:

DO NOT BUY THIS HAZARDOUS PRODUCT!

I purchased one in February, and it is completely inoperable. Not only has it been frustratingly low-quality, as I explained in my earlier review below, it is also dangerous. The seams in the fabric separated in many spots, and the heating elements would only come on intermittently. The last time I tried to use it, though, the power seemed to be cutting on and off. I got up to check that the cord was fully plugged in, and there was a sudden "zapping" sound, and blue sparks were flying from the cord!

Luckily, it was plugged into a power strip, so I was able to unplug the pillow without getting injured, and upon closer inspection, I could see that the wires where the cord is connected to the transformer plug had become exposed. In all honesty, I have grave doubts that this product meets safety standards and plan to submit a complaint to Amazon.

First off, this is a functional, inexpensive, and portable massager which seems fairly sturdy. That said, the manufacturer obviously took several shortcuts when they designed this product.

The heat is insufficient to loosen up tight muscles.
The included cord is flimsy and far too short to reach an outlet.
The buttons are poorly designed. When you sit / lay against the pillow, the power button can easily be pressed inadvertently. It's very annoying to have to keep getting up and turning it on.

I would not recommend this product. One with better quality would be a better choice.

title: Not the lifesaver I was hoping for but.. ok
text:
I am coming off a memory foam cushion and have a bad back due to an injury.

1. The pad itself is beefy and heavy
2. It is not as soft or forgiving as memory foam.
3. I am unsure if #2 means it will last longer or give better, long term support.
4. I cannot say its a huge pain relief or back saver. Because its not as soft, its more rigid and It took a few weeks for my body to adjust to sitting on it. That meant pain and discomfort for me.
5. Now that I have had it for a bit I will say its better.. not great.. its still hard.. but it does the job and keeps things more neutral and it stays that way.

So if you are looking for super soft, comfortable and cozy.. this isn't the pad for you.

If you are looking for something that gives some support and stays that way in a neutral position long term and takes what you give it, then yes, give this pad a try. Hopefully it helps you and does it's job.

I would say I would buy it again but I would also be open to something softer, more comfortable too. I don't hate it at all..Im just not in love with it.

All in all it's hard to knock this protein on the quality and ingredients..It's sweetened with stevia, lo-han and xylitol..so no saccharin or sucralose. title: If you are using a TENS for low back therapy - buy the belt.  It will save your skin and definitely aggravation!
text:
First off, it works. Buying online, I was a bit concerned. But it works fine. I've used a TENS device before by prescription and I had to apply the electrodes. Which was a pain in the arse if you have to do it yourself...think contortionist...MUCH easier to just put on the belt (using a bit of the electrode get).
This device delivers very gentle to a bit more deep therapy. I have severe low back pain, L4 and L5. Given my experience some years ago using a TENS and electrode placement--I decided this device was an absolute necessity to go along with my new TENS device. There's no way you want to have to apply the electrodes every time you have to treat your back. This is easy-peasy. This shaver uses replaceable rechargeable batteries so when the batteries go bad, I can just replace them. This is a plus comparing to other shavers I have. Although this is a 3-in-1 shaver, I don't see the need for me to use the other 2 functions. This might be a plus feature for other people.

The not so good parts:

1. The shaver cover is difficult to open for cleaning although very easy to put it back. I'm afraid one day I might break it while trying to pull it open. This seems to be a design problem.

2. The screen cover/protector can come loose easily. This means it can be lost easily as well. Therefore, not very suitable for travelling.

3. This shaver uses 2 AA size Ni-Cd rechargeble batteries. This is not good as Ni-Cd is the type of rechageable battery with "memory". As such, its battery life could be short. Wish it comes with newer type of rechargeable batteries that have no "memory".

title: Transition to Awesomeness = Complete
text:
I received this product at a discount in exchange for an honest review.

I have surfer's eye and yes, it is as cool as it sounds. While you probably wish you had it too, you should know that the surgery for it is not that big of a treat and will leave you with scar tissue in your eye.

Whenever the sun gets into my eye, even through my polarized sunglasses, the scar tissue in my eye becomes inflamed for a few days and I look like I've been drinking and fighting. Think Thanksgiving dinner at my Irish grandma and grandpa's house.

I have a patch that I'll use when working in the yard or sitting on the edge of a cliff but it is pointy (think Madonna videos- 1990) and it lets light sneak in where the patch meets up to the side of my nose. But with this new patch, NO LIGHT GETS IN!!!! It is indeed, a piratey Christmas miracle.

The patch is extremely comfortable (think sleep mask that only covers one eye) and it lies flat over my eye, forcing me to keep it closed. But even if I open it, guess what: no light is sneaking in.

Best of all, I look awesome. I want to wear this thing...always. I sit in the front yard and wave at the kids going by. Think Pirates of the Caribbean; only more awkward and less fun.

Peace.
